review_headline: Solid, excellent mouse pad.  Definitely recommend
review_body:
I was looking for a solid mouse pad for office work and after having some trouble with a cheaper, colored version settled on this one. I absolutely love this mouse pad and I'm thinking of getting a second one for home use. I work as an office manager so I'm on the computer a lot running reports, entering data, etc so I wanted something that would work smoothly with the other products that I had. First of all, this is a heavy mousepad that doesn't slip and slide easily around the desk. In fact, it is hard to get the mouse pad to move around at all. When you want to move this mouse pad you actually need to lift it up from the edge to move it around. I like the weight and the grip that the bottom has because it keep is from moving and keeps my mouse where I put it. The top is also harder than standard mousepads which makes for smooth tracking on the pointer. The wrist support is just right for providing a comfortable place to rest your wrist while you are working.

I would definitely recommend for office work and I think it would be great for gaming as well. I am considering buying on for myself at home for gaming purposes.

product_title: New Collectible Edition! 30 Various NYC New York Photo Postcards 4x6 Inch
review_body:
I am full of praise for this economical set of NEW COLLECTIBLE EDITION - 30 VARIOUS NYC postcards. At a current price of around eighteen cents apiece, you get --

Sturdy cards, suitable for mailing anywhere
No repeats
Classic four-by-six-inch format (10 x 15 cm), which mails domestically at a current price of $0.35, $1.20 outside the USA
Modern "bleed" (borderless) design
Bold composition
Up-to-date selection, including the new Freedom Tower (opened 11/2014 in the World Trade Center location)
A mixture of full-color cards (20 of the thirty in this assortment), black-and-white (eight), mixed B&W/Color (one) and one sepia, a charming mock retro take of the kind of horse-drawn cab that plies Central Park.

With the low price and the high quality both physically and compositionally, this set of 30 cards gets a high recommendation from me. Given the chance, though, there are a few things I'd have done differently in the interest of greater variety: This set is very much a first-time-tourist's view of Manhattan, emphasizing the Theater District, Empire State Building, Freedom Tower, and the Statue of Liberty. Now, I love Miss Liberty, but I don't think it was necessary to show her looming over the Theater District as a mere logo (one way or another, She figures into thirteen of the thirty cards in this set). Perhaps it would be better to "retire" that card, along with the multiview card that is hard to read and the one that unaccountably paints the Hudson River red, in favor of some single shots of other well-known sights, such as the Chrysler Building, the Cloisters, Macy*s at Herald Square, the George Washington Bridge, the U.N. building, or a view of Central Park with big hotels like the ESSEX HOUSE as backdrop.

I think it would have been better to identify a very nice B&W shot of the Brooklyn Bridge, as well as the Freedom Tower (especially since the Empire State Bldg. and the Statue of Liberty are identified).

This is not to overlook the fact that these cards are a tremendous bargain, and it does not surprise me that some people buy the set in advance of their Manhattan vacation, just to have ready when need arises. I myself like to send them to my Postcrossing recipients who ask for big-city views.

product_title: Amram Comfort Grip Standard Tag Attaching Tagging Gun BONUS KIT with 5 Needles and 1250 2" Standard Attachments Fasteners Barbs
review_body:
I've been selling my children's clothes at consignment sales for years now and have always priced the clothes using safety pins. I finally decided it was time to get a tagging gun and make my life easier. This gun sure did!

It was one of the less expensive guns that are out on the market, but I thought I would give it a shot. I am so pleased with this tagging gun! The instructions were very clear on how to load the tags into the machine and how to insert and remove the needle.

The only instructions that were not very clear was how to properly get the tag to go into the clothes. The instructions explained how to insert the needle into the clothes and pull the trigger but I kept having misfires. The tag would shoot out, but wouldn't go through the clothes. Having never used a tagging gun before, I didn't realize that you have to push the needle ALL the way through the tag and the clothes so it is flush and tight up against the base of the gun. The tag needs to be flush against the base. Once I figured that out, it's a breeze to use! Definitely recommend this product.

So far this is working great. I wish I could add a block (Black) list like I can make a Whitel list. I had about 12 numbers all ready to add to the block list. Ok, so after they call once more I can now block them. We have a corded phone that rings when we get a call. The

Our cordless is mounted on the wall, so the Sentry is hanging down below it on two 8 inch phone wires (hard to find today). This makes it easier to lift it up to add to the Block list.
ALSO Make sure you add the numbers just like they show up on your caller ID, or they will get your message to dial 0. When they dial 0 your phone rings and you can decide to answer it or not.
We are using it in basic mode as suggested for the first few weeks to build up the White List.

Overall, given the ink, it was a cheaper investment, or so I thought. While I am not losing monetarily I am definitely losing time and patience with this Brother.  When I first set it up it was working perfectly. I was able to print from my Mac OS X, my iPhone and iPad. However, tonight, after multiple reinstalls and troubleshooting, this printer has stopped working as well as it once did. Keep in mind it is only a few weeks old. My computer didn't recognize it, then when I realized there was a firmware update, while the computer sometimes recognizes it, it printed a 20 page document in 15 minutes. It paused after each page. My iPhone can no longer see the printer and, when I try to print to it it tells me to click OK so it can go into a deep sleep, thereby ignoring my print request.  I didn't change anything, I didn't add anymore programs just, all of a sudden, this reliable and great printer has become little more than an expensive paperweight . I am incredibly disappointed and if I had not thrown the box out I would be taking it back to where I got it tomorrow.  I have tried everything and so, apart, from drop kicking it out the window I am out of options. I hate to say it, because I used to love Brother printers and, while the older wired one I have is a workhorse, I cannot recommend this particular printer, especially if you need a reliable wifi printer, in fact, I suggest you search for a comparable and more STABLE printer, because this is certainly not it.

review_headline: Not so easy to print wirelessly
review_body:
Printer set up okay but you have to read the online manual to get the printer password and complete setup. Does not really print wirelessly as it turns itself off. If it happens to be on when you want to print from your iPad or iPhone great, as long as they can find the printer. Test printing from iPad on a Pages document that had some highlighting: yellow highlight did not print. Test sheet printed with both black and color and the printing was crisp and color good. You have to download the Canon app to get the thing to turn on when you want to print or either turn it on manually. Set up for the printing is a little complicated and we were unable to do it from a laptop, had to go to PC. There are a few Canon apps so be sure you choose the correct app for this printer. We have an older model Canon printer that prints wirelessly without an app, does automatic double sided printing and is great. Don't know why Canon had to complicate the print procedure with an app on this newer model. The description leads one to believe printing is powerful and easy. Frankly, wish there had been reviews available before we purchased. Don't think I would have chosen this model.
Update 8/26/15 gave it one more star. After countless hours of searching the online manual, and searching for problem on Canon website and popular search engine without results we tried the trial and error method. From PC or laptop, access devices and printers from the start menu and right click on the Canon 3600 icon, select printing preferences, maintenance tab, click on Auto power which opens a window to disable the auto off feature. Now you can print through AirPrint from your iPad. This eliminates the need for the Canon app which we could never get to work. Because this solution was so difficult and no help could be found and we never got the app to work I only increased the review by one star. We've had issues printing some pages with graphs from the Internet which print cropped or without line spacing. Still a work in progress!without line spacing. Still a work in progress!

review_body: The one thing I don't agree with is the fact that ink cartridges last forever on the one five start review that's first featured. If you use non-HP inks or remanufactured HP cartridges you are in for a really difficult struggle. Print jobs fail in error all the time even when using genuine HP inks. I am not using the wireless feature either and rely on a hard wired ethernet connection to this printer with a dedicated IP address, so that never changes. Regardless of the connectivity, the printer even when on, goes unresponsive and cannot be reached without recycling the power button. This is to date the worst printer I have ever used and it constantly requires me to run the HP diagnostics (Scan and Print Doctor) to see if it can determine what is wrong. I don't know why I keep using the utility at all because it can never determine what the issue is. Several power cycles usually fix it but even that is no guarantee. Then for the cost of the ink, I could have purchased several printers by now that don't use even nearly the amount of ink that this printer does. Worse than comparably priced Epsons which are notoriously expensive for ink. This printer should be sub 100.00, but I wouldn't consider buying one again or keeping one even if it was given to me as a gift. Save your money and buy a modern printer that supports iOS and Android devices along with a PC. This one doesn't work with Apple tablets or phones even if it says it does. And trying to configure the wireless setup for those devices is a total exercise in futility. I can't tell you how many times I have had to completely reinstall the software and drivers for the printer to get it to work again, and then only temporarily. You have better things to do than to deal with this product. BTW- I dropped this off a electronic waste/recycling I wouldn't have given this printer to my worst enemy. product_title: Avery Double Wired Shipping Tags, 13pt. Stock, 4 3/4"x 2 3/8", Pack of 1000, Manila (12605)
review_body:
I am about 60 years old, so I remember the days when tags like these were used with either a string or a wire like this one. These are exactly as I remember them, and they work great! The 1,000 piece package is about 18" x 12" x 3.5", which is bigger than I thought it would be. If you get this jumbo sized box of tags and are not using them at a rapid rate, you should keep in mind the space needed to store them and possibly consider dividing them into smaller boxes to more easily store them on a shelf or in your supply locker.

I use these for a number of jobs. For instance, they are great for quickly and easily putting my name and contact information on my extension cords and other items that cannot easily be directly labeled. I do videos and still photos as a side job and have quite a lot of this kind of gear when I go on site. I have a rubber stamp with my information on it which I use to mark the tags. This is much quicker than my old process of using business cards and a laminator for this task. Although those laminated tags are more durable than these paper ones, they were also a lot more work to make. These are so quick and easy that there is less barrier to getting started. As a result, all my cords and other loose items are tagged now.

I've also taken a bunch of these to work (Silicon Valley startup company) and have assigned a student intern to use them to label our inventory of cables, antennas, and other similar parts. These take ink well, and are sturdy enough that they are lasting fine so far.

There is a a version of this tag that uses a string instead of wire. Although that attachment has no sharp points to stick your fingers as the wire version does, I find that it is a lot easier and quicker to just twist the wire around the attach point than it is to tie knots in the string tags. YMMV.

These are super - they are just like those "old school" tags of past days. I think they are great and hope you do too.ope you do too.

product_title: Document Scanner
review_body: Great hardware.  I have scanned folded and crumpled letter and legal size documents, as well as various sizes of paper and cards like driver license and business cards.  All scanned well and quickly with few jams.  Software is good.  I already had Paperport 14, so I skipped that.  Canon's Capture on Touch is pretty good, once you figure it out and set up the profiles you want.  You can set it up to create a separate pdf for each page or all pages into one pdf file, color, B&W, greyscale or automatic.  I found that using B&W on a crumpled carbon copy on pink paper removed the color and the wrinkles.  Very pleased with the scanner and software.  Drivers are an issue.  I installed it on Windows 7.  When I upgraded to Windows 10 the computer could not find the scanner.  I emailed customer support and got a reply in a couple of hours (on a Sunday!) that there was no Win10 driver yet; as a current product it would probably get one, but no ETA available.  So kudos for a prompt response, a Bronx cheer for its content.  I resolved my driver issue by using a NextBook that is running Windows 8.1.  Driver and Capture on Touch work fine, and I set up the profiles to save to a folder on OneDrive.  Then I go to the Win10 computer and move the file to other folders on that computer.  It works, but I am looking forward to the Win10 driver.  Another reviewer indicates that Canon expects to release the driver in 2 - 3 weeks.  When the Win10 driver is released, and I determine that it works property, I think I will increase my rating to 5 stars.  I am debating whether or not to knock off a star for what appears to be an habitual delay in developing drivers for new operating systems that other manufacturers do not seem to encounter.  Googling revealed a similar delay in delivering drivers when Windows 8 came out.  UPDATE 8/29/15:  Windows 10 driver and software are out.  I haven't tried them because I dropped back to Windows 7.  There were just too many articles about Windows 10 phoninghome with all kinds of information for me to feel comfortable.  So I have given it 5 stars because it is a great scanner.

product_title: Tools4Wisdom Planner 2016 - 2017 Calendar 4-in-1: Daily Weekly Monthly Yearly Organizer - Purpose Driven Goals Planning Book - Personal Life Progress Journal Notebook (8.5 x 11 / 200 Pages / Spiral)
review_headline: Nice planner, just too big to be practical for a busy family.
review_body:
I recently purchased this planner and was very excited to receive it. I was searching for a planner that I could carry with me to appointments, games and work to help keep me organized for my busy family. I like how this planner breaks the day down by time increments and that it has a place on each day to write goals. I've found that to be really helpful actually. It seems if I write down one goal for the day, it makes it much easier to accomplish than if I hadn't written it down. I like that the planner seems to be durable and I like that the monthly tabs stick out so you can easily access which month you need to. The quality is nice, highlighters don't bleed through too much!
However, I only gave this a 3 star "it's ok" rating because it is really large and heavy - the size of a thick notebook (think 3 subject)! I had read several of the other reviews and knew it'd be the size of a notebook and thought that it wouldn't bother me ( I even went to the companies website to see if they offered smaller ones but they don't yet). So, I took a chance and purchased this one because the reviews were so great. However, since I've been using it for a couple of weeks now, the size really does bother me. The large size makes it impractical to carry with me. I have a medium sized purse and it doesn't fit in it. Since the purpose of getting this was to carry with me to have everything at a glance when scheduling new things, it really doesn't work for me. I can't carry it along everywhere while holding hands, pushing grocery carts, carrying sports bottles and chairs etc.etc. If it was smaller and I could slip it in my bag, I would probably give it 4 or 5 stars. So, I'm back to searching for a good family planner.
If you're not looking for something to keep with you at all times (unless you carry a backpack) then this is a good,easy to use, time manager planner.

product_title: Gold Metallic 8" x 100' Laminating Foil MyBinding GLD-80-8 Gold
review_headline: I figured it out, and it works great!!!
review_body:
I figured it out!!!

I read all of the reviews and although there were a lot of people disappointed with this product, I ordered it anyway. I'm glad I did, because I figured out what the problem was. You can't use a super porous style of paper. If you do, then the toner soaks into the paper too much. So, when you go to reheat it, there isn't enough toner on the surface of the paper for the foil to adhere to. You need to find a paper that has a bit of a gloss to it. I found a glossier style paper from Hammermill, that's made specifically for laserjet printers. I created a simple design in black, printed it on the glossy paper, then taped a sheet of the foil over it (making sure not to cover any of the design with the tape) and fed it back through the printer. When I fed it through the second time, it was with a blank document. All together, I thought the foil showed up beautifully.

FYI, if you use a laminator, then you don't have to tape the foil down. I wouldn't recommend running the paper through the printer without the tape, if the foil gets stuck in your printer, you'll have a really hard time getting it out. It might even ruin the printer.

product_title: Scotch Precision
review_headline: These scissors are great. The handle is comfortable
review_body:
These scissors are great. The handle is comfortable, the blade is strong, the open and close action is good, and the scissors work very well. In the 9 months that I have owned them, I have never experienced any problems.

These scissors are sharp enough to cut through paper with precision, and are heavy enough to handle heavy duty cutting. They can handle cutting through multiple documents at once, which is a nice feature that can save quite a bit of time. If you need to cut out the same shape from multiple documents, you can stack them together in a few piles depending on how many documents you have. Then you can follow the shape on the top document with the scissors and cut it out. The result will be multiple instances of the same shape from the different documents.

They also have nice action. This means that the scissors open and close with ease, but not too much ease. If the scissors opened and closed with too much ease, there would be less strength behind each cut. If they opened and closed with too little ease, it would be very difficult to use them. However, with these scissors, there is no problem with the action.

The grip handles are very comfortable as well. The grip is made out of rubber material, and the size of the two openings is larger than other scissors, which makes the grip comfortable for small and large hands alike.

Overall, I would recommend these scissors to anyone who needs strong, reliable scissors.

review_body:
So I got this in order to shred all my documents, mail, etc. and because I didn't want my garbage to always be full of my junk mail. So I did some looking around at paper shredders and found this one. The reviews all seemed pretty good and the price was right.

So after getting it I found out it comes in two pieces, the top and the basket part. All you do is pop the top on and your done. I put a little plastic bag in between the two for easy clean up when the bag gets full. I liked how it holds a lot of paper so you aren't constantly having to empty it out. Also although it doesn't shred them micro sized I liked how it shredded them at an angle so if someone would try to put them back together it would be very difficult since they aren't just all straight on the end. Finally I really liked how this was one of the only paper shredders I could find for a cheap price that can handle shredding staples and such. Also It can handle around 6 pieces of paper at once and I have never had it jam on me yet, and if it ever should there is the reverse switch to un jam it.

I really liked this shredder and found no problems with it other than that having it shred micro sized would be better, but this is good enough for home use. I highly recommend this if you should need a shredder.

product_title: USPRO® LM393 Sound detection sensor module for Arduino Intelligent vehicle smart car
review_headline: Great sensor for the price - just beware the output is digital not analog!
review_body:
This sound sensor works great for the project I'm using it for. I gave it four stars instead of five because it comes with no documentation whatsoever and even online documentation is difficult to find and usually wrong. Once I figured out most of the info out there in internet land is wrong, I was good to go. Another clue is the LM393 comparator which is - duh - digital :) There is a tiny light that blinks when the sound pressure level exceeds the threshold you've set with the potentiometer. When that light blinks, it's setting the output pin high. It doesn't get much simpler than that. I found several sets of instructions about this and other virtually identical sensors online and they are flat wrong. The output is not analog. You need to connect it to a digital input and test when it goes high in your code.

Also, one of the answers states that this is a microphone with an analog output. It's a sensor - meaning above or below threshold - not a microphone, and there is no analog output. It's either on or off. I'm using it to test the presence of a very loud bang and nothing else so the threshold for my application is set very high.

product_title: Click 'N Dig! Key Finder. 4 Receivers. Wireless RF Item Locator Remote, Wallet, Keyfinder. (Free Extra Batteries) New Model: E4
review_body:
I had purchased a set for my in-laws who were always losing their keys and was contacted by the seller to receive a second set in return for a review. I was not paid for this review.

I've had this set for a few weeks and, of course, had to put it through the paces to see if it really worked as advertised. I'm pleased to say it came close! I did not experience an 80 ft range but I was able to trigger the device from a different room than I was standing in. My husband hid the receivers throughout our house for me to find and I did so with ease. The sound was loud enough to hear and the flashing light did help locate it seconds quicker than I might have otherwise. One receiver was buried in the cushions of our leather couch and under a blanket. The receiver activated but it was very faint. To me that is a good trade off because you don't want the sound to be ear piercing, either. :-) It would be neat if the sound increased each 3rd time you pressed the button on the remote.

As others have mentioned, they are a little bulky/large but as technology improves, I expect the size to decrease as well. I do wish there was a smart phone appl that I could purchase so I could activate the receiver when I am away from home and don't have the remote. Or a smart phone appl that would locate the remote so I can find the item attached to the receiver that I misplaced. :>) Yep, we can't have it all but at this price I'm thrilled to have some assistance with finding items I commonly misplace!!

product_title: Nemosine Singularity Fountain Pen, Fine German Nib, Magenta (NEM-SIN-13-F)
review_headline: Great starter pen with few drawbacks
review_body:
This was my first foray into the world of fountain pens. I knew going into this that this wasn't the best pen out there, but a good starter pen, and I have to agree!

The color is beautiful, first of all. A nice bright magenta, leaning a bit more cool than warm. It has a nice feel in the hand and the cap posts nicely on the end. It is a screw on cap, which has its benefits, but also its drawbacks. I find that the pen dries out quickly if I leave it uncapped for too long, and screwing and unscrewing the cap all the time is just a little annoying.

The nib is nice enough in my opinion. It lays down a nice line of ink for the most part. I do find a little scratch on it when I push it upwards, but we're going to fuss at that with some polishing papers later on to get that taken care of (thank you You Tube tutorials!). I think with a little work, this is going to be a great pen, and one that's definitely gotten me a bit of attention at work when others see it!

Overall, I'm quite fond of the pen. The fact that it came with 6 cartridges AND a converter really sold me, as it lets me get into ink as well without having to buy a separate converter on top of the pen at one time.

review_headline: Fit in three wallet styles, photos included
review_body:
I sectioned off my review into two sections. First being my testimonial; why I personally need this product. Second is my actual review. If you don't care for why I personally needed this please skip ahead to my review.

MY TESTIMONIAL:
As a recent victim of credit card identity theft I was happy to review these sleeves. When I first found out my credit card information had be stolen I had to understand what had happened. Was this an online based scam (I don’t use my card online) or did someone local steal my credit card information? In my case someone local had stolen my credit card information and used it to make a counterfeit version of my card. They attempted to use the counterfeit version of my card at a grocery store only 20 minutes from where I live.

How they stole my credit card information is something I will never know. This is a card that rarely gets used. It’s not used out of my eyesight. I didn’t use it at a restaurant where someone could walk off with it and copy my information. After talking to my bank the only thing I can figure is that someone used an RFID scanner to scan my card while it was in my purse.

These RFID Blocking Credit Card Sleeves by Sefcard give me the piece of my mind I was looking for after this happened. I’m still leery of how I use my credit card. I do feel better though knowing they are actually safe in my purse.

MY REVIEW:
I tested these RFID Blocking Credit Card Sleeves in three wallets. One man's leather wallet, a woman's clutch style wallet, and a metal case wallet. They fit all three styles. (Photos attached)

The only thing I’ve found about these RFID Blocking Credit Card Sleeves by Sefcard is sometimes the corners are over glued. You have to push your finger into the corner to allow the card to fit. (Photo attached)

I honestly recommend these RFID Blocking Credit Card Sleeves by Sefcard to anyone who is looking for piece of mind and security. It’s a hassle dealing with banks. It’s unsettling knowing no mater how hard you proactively protect yourselves the thieves are just going to keep getting smarter. This is one small, inexpensive, way we can fight back.

product_title: Avery Big Tab Insertable Plastic Dividers with Pockets, 5 Tabs, 1 Set, Assorted Fashion Designs (07708)
review_body:
I picked these to use in my data collection binder where I need to keep different forms and groups separate. I love the colors: pink dots, black dots, blue stripes, lime stripes, aqua herringbone.

The plastic appears to be fairly rugged even though it's very thin. I've tried to stretch out the holes and tugged at the seams and the plastic is flexible but strong. I'm used to a sturdier divider and the pockets are rather thin and flimsy until you fill them with papers. It will take a few weeks of regular use to see how these hold up.

The big tabs are nice, since I can make the divider labels bigger (and more legible for me). It's easy to get the labels in and out of the tabs. The tabs are translucent, so I find that I have to write darker or with a thicker pen (Sharpie or labelmaker) so that the print shows through.

My only warning is that, if you don't have a large enough binder, the tabs will stick out of the sides which might cause them to get bent or mangled. I've found that you need a binder with a cover that's 11 - 11 1/2 inches wide in order to fully contain the tabs. I tried them in 2 different Avery One-Touch binders and the binder covers were entirely different widths.

review_body:
I have had back problems most of my life, I am 62 and now have spinal stenosis and arthritis along with knee issues. I have been overweight most of my adult life and have recently lost 65 lbs. That said, I now have less fat on my butt area so when I was offered this cushion for review I jumped on the chance, almost literally.

The set up I have on my desk is different than most in that the monitor to my computer sits high and my desk chair only goes so high. Plus the underside of the cushion is made of non slip material so the cushion stays in place without sliding. The cover on the cushion is made of a nice soft material and it does come off for washing.
I have neck issues, after two spinal fusions, and the Cush Comfort cushion enables me to sit at the right height so that my neck is at a more normal and comfortable angle. I immediately noticed when I sat on it that my butt felt a lot better and does not get sore. I sit at the computer for some days more than 8 hours doing my blog stuff, I no longer work due to a disability, and I need to be comfortable.
I even have problem reclining on my couch watching tv so that I have been taking the cushion to sit on there. It is the best cushion I have used and I have tried a few different ones. If you have spinal or even coxyx issues, give the Cush Comfort cushion a try. Plus the price is reasonable, I have already paid over $50 for a cushion that did not help. So definitely worth the price. I received a Cush Comfort Non-slip Memory Foam Seat Cushion for my review and my thoughts are my own.

product_title: Pentel Mechanical Pencil, Quick Dock, 0.7mm, Blue (PENQD7EC)
review_headline: Great pencil with one issue that can be worked around
review_body:
Great mechanical pencil with a long eraser and comfortable to write with. The four star rating is due to the fact that you are supposed to replace the lead housing (entire barrel) when it runs out of lead. You can refill/add lead to it if you carefully insert the lead into the writing end one stick at a time. Also, after prolonged use, the paint and words begin to chip off the barrel, but this does not affect performance. The writing end is not always extended so it does not have a permanent sharp point that pokes holes in clothes and flesh as there is a two stage mechanism to expose/retract the actual lead. This pencil is worth the money if you manually refilled lead instead of paying for the replacement barrel that costs as much as the original pencil.

I bought four of these, one for myself and one for each of my three kids. They are robust and save a ton of money versus traditional pencils if it doesn't get lost and if you are willing to refill it one painstakingly stick of lead at a time.

review_headline: Just the Ticket for Students' Schoolwork Binders!
review_body:
These AVERY BIG TAB POCKET INSERTABLE PLASTIC DIVIDERS are just the ticket for loose-leaf binders used for schoolwork. Each divider consists of a pocket that will hold a very thick class handout--up to 35 sheets, anyway--and still turn smoothly along the binder rings. Once inserted, the loose pages stay in the pocket, because the pocket front slants upwards all the way to the top binder ring.

The dotted, striped, and diagonal decorations are cheerful. Each pocket has a different design or color, so you can identify your notebook sections at a glance. These pocketed loose-leaf-binder dividers have large tabs that extend beyond the cover of a standard binder. I'm not keen on things that stick out of a loose-leaf binder, but these tabs are more or less okay because they're made of flexible (and presumably durable) plastic. Also, there isn't room for the tabs inside the binder cover if the pockets are going to work for holding lots of loose papers.

These plastic dividers come with a paper sheet of blank tab inserts that is perforated for easy separation of individual inserts. The sheet is are suitable for printing, using MS Word or Avery's online templates. The tabs on the dividers have notches that make the printed tab inserts easy to slide in. The notched tabs are also designed hold the tab inserts securely.

product_title: Casio MS-80B Standard Function Desktop Calculator
review_headline: Calculate THIS:  Casio 'MS-80B' Mini Desk Calculator [with ON/OFF buttons]
review_body:
This Casio MS-80B portable desk calculator is one nice little piece of home office
equipment. We'll start with the statistics and then head down for a brief review of
the MS-80B.

Width: 4-1/16 inch
Length: 5-3/4 inch
Height: 3/8 to 1-1/8 inch
Keys: 1/2 by 7/16 inch (Number & most function keys)

"On" / "Off" Buttons
Large 8 Digit Display [ 3/8 inch height digits ]
2-way Power, Solar and Battery
Tax Calculations
Currency Conversion
3 Memory Keys
Profit Margin Percent Calculation
Square Root Key
Key Roll Over
3-Digit Comma Markers

I like the low key, muted gold, color of the calculator and how easy the buttons press
down under very little pressure from the fingers. The display sits at a nice angle on
the desk and the numbers are a large 3/8 of an inch high which are easily read from
2 to 3 feet away.

The face-plate on the keyboard area is metal and provides a nice contrast to the plastic
display area that tilts upward from the keyboard. I could easily see the LC (Liquid
Crystal) black digital-like numbers even under a bright fluorescent lamp on the desk.
The display is not back-lit so you will need an external light source to use the Casio
MS-80B.

All I had to do to start using the calculator was sit it in the sun for a few hours and, voila,
let the calculating began. Of course, not like the calculating on the 'Game of Thrones'
series; but calculating for you and me so we can balance the finances and do the taxes.

This model does have separate ON and OFF buttons, yet it will power off after a few
minutes if left unattended or blatantly ignored. By the way it is the Casio Model 'MS-80S'
that does NOT have an OFF button. The 'MS-80S' is almost twice the cost.

I do not see any obvious way to replace the battery on this unit. There are two visible
screws on the back of the display and, I assume, two screws underneath the rubber
pads on the back of the base.

Overall, a very nice portable desk calculator for home or a small office. I like the looks,
the feel, and the price of this solid unit and that is why it gets 5 stars.

This unit works very well except for one extremely annoying feature. I give it one star in hopes the manufacturer will read this review and make a much needed improvement.

The annoying feature is --- there is no buzzer to tell you it has reached operating temperature. It takes maybe 7 or 8 minutes to get there. And I hate to be tied up waiting around for it to reach the required temp. Right now the only thing that notifies the user that it is ready to go is a modest little green light,. What it needs is a nice loud repetitive alarm clock style buzzer so that I can go about my other chores while the laminator hots up. product_title: sharpener
review_headline: Super Sharpener for High Quality Colored Pencils - Kid Tested, Mother Approved!
review_body:
My nine year old child told me yesterday, "This is THE BEST pencil sharpener I've EVER had!"

If you knew how many different kinds of pencil sharpeners we've tried, you would know that this is high praise indeed.

We're colored pencil connoisseurs in my house; we use only the best - Derwent Colour-Soft, Prismacolor Premier, and Lyra are some of our favourites. We don't even bother with Crayola or similar anymore because we can't stand the breaking "leads", waxy-pale colors, and uneven blending.

So you can imagine that we are also rather particular about what we sharpen our colored pencils with. Sure, I use the standard brass Made-in-Germany two-size sharpeners when I have a place for the shavings to drop, but for a kid, you want a sharpener with a built-in receptacle for the shavings. And like I said, we've tried so many I can hardly count them. (BTW, don't sharpen your high quality colored pencils in an electric sharpener - it wastes valuable pencil and can gum up your sharpener, particularly with the oil-based pencils.)

This sharpener, I believe, is made specifically for the Prismacolor colored pencils, so it really delivers: pigment sticks ("leads") don't break, wood is not chewed up, pencils are sharpened EVENLY all around, with minimal waste for maximum point. The receptacle is on the small side, which is good for smaller hands, but you have to empty it after sharpening about 10 pencils.

I only hope I didn't get the ONE good one...(it's happened before that we reordered a decent hand sharpener only to find that what we THOUGHT was a decent sharpener was actually a fluke). But we will definitely reorder this sharpener; in fact, I'll probably buy a few of them to keep on hand.

As always, your mileage may vary, and I didn't get a free sharpener in exchange for my honest review. (I wish I knew how people got those deals...)

review_headline: A great Journal for years to come.
review_body: I received the Miquelrius 600-page Journal on time through Amazon's delivery service.  This is an impressive volume that, at the rate of writing a page-long entry almost every day, I "guesstimate" will last me two years, if not longer. The supple leatherette cover feels close to real, well-treated leather.  The elastic strap is an appreciated feature to secure the closed pages.  For these reasons I give the Miquelrius 600-page Journal high marks.  I subtract one star because 1.) there were two minor scuff marks on the copy I got—not severe, but just noticeable—and 2.) there is no page sash for marking one's place in this volume, which would be welcomed for a long page-count Journal like this.  But, I can just find a bookmark.  Overall, this is a high-quality Journal that I look forward to using and preserving for posterity.

product_title: HP Envy 4500 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner and Copier
review_headline: A true wireless printer for a fair price!
review_body:
What's most impressive about this printer is that you get so much for a fair price. I've always been a fan of HP printers because I've found them to be the most user friendly for the non-techy types (like myself) and this printer didn't disappoint. Setup was a breeze; you don't even need to open the instruction manual. The disk prompts lead you through setup and printing test pages, and as an added bonus you can opt to set up via the internet, which ensures the most up to date info HP has for your printer. The printer can be setup with its own email address, which you'd use to print with when you're anywhere. This is a pretty radical feature for me! My old printer had "wireless" printing but that apparently was just code for "may print from phone or laptop within your house." But this printer lets me print from anywhere, which is pretty cool. Just yesterday I purchased tickets from my phone while I was in a store and just printed them right there.

The print quality is excellent for a home printer, but I expect nothing less from HP. The scan feature is also very straight forward, but if you have to modify paper type/size for printing, you have to do it from your computer which is annoying but certainly livable. It does make a fair amount of noise while printing, but I've yet to own a printer that doesn't so I don't mind it or find it louder than your average printer. Overall, I am really excited to have this printer on my desk and quite satisfied with it so far. I received this printer for review.

review_headline: one of the worst places in the country for credit card and ID ...
review_body:
“I received this product in a discounted price in exchange for my honest review”.

We live in Southern Florida, one of the worst places in the country for credit card and ID theft. A few months ago our credit card number was stolen just before we left town for a week long vacation. I spent hours on the phone dealing with it while I was on vacation and even more time once I got home. No we didn't lose any money but what a headache and inconvenience! After reading many, many reviews of a number of different wallets we selected this wallet for several reasons.

2. Other reviewers who purchased this wallet said they tested it and it worked. A number of other wallets we read about the buyers said those wallets didn't pass their tests.
3. My husband loved the flip up pocket for the driver's license. He has to show ID at a number of places he goes into for work sot this is a great feature. In playing with his new wallet I noticed that you can fold/position the ID pocket on the outside of the wallet so you don't have to open and expose the contents of your wallet when asked for ID.
4. Quality. Other reviewers raved about how nicely this wallet is boxed/packaged and the quality of construction and materials of the wallet. We agree 100%. In the reviews of other wallets, the reviewers said they were inexpensive and worked great but didn't hold up. Why waste money on a wallet that isn't likely to last a year.
5. Functionality. Everything fits nicely in this wallet and isn't too bulky. This wallet has nine slots. Some others only have seven.
6. Price. Another wallet sold here on Amazon that looks identical sells for $39.99

I read everything I could find before ordering and was impressed enough that I bought two of these wallets, one for my husband and the other for our son. Now that the wallets have arrived and we can actually see them and have transferred his stuff, I am so glad I ordered two! My husband and I both highly recommend the Dante RFID Blocking Genuine Leather Wallet.ght two of these wallets, one for my husband and the other for our son. product_title: Sentinel Pro FMC120P 12-Sheet Micro-Cut Shredder
review_body:
A shredder is a necessity these days for reasons I don't even need to get into. But what you need is a shredder that is up to the task. I have tried many shredders and they typically all suffer the same fate - early failure due to a low capacity. I believe this shredder has the capacity and power to handle normal household shredding needs.

The Sentinel Pro FMC120P can shred up to 12 sheets at once and you don't even need to remove staples or small paper clips. There is even a slot for DVDs/CDs.

I tried it with typical stuff - a credit card statement, bank statement, etc. it handles multi-page documents with ease. The final shredded product is micro cut. There are basically three types of shredders: strip cut (long strips), cross cut (3.9mm x 50mm) and micro cut (also cross cut but 1.9mm x 15mm). Micro-cut shredders provide maximum security.

Emptying the FMC12P couldn't be easier. There is a slide out bin that collects the shredded material. I use a plastic liner to make removal easier. The bottom of the unit features casters so it can be rolled about when needed. A built-in sensor prevents you from further shredding if the bin is full. This shredder also features an overuse/overheat sensor which prevents burnout from shred-a-thons.

Some of the shredders I have owned in the past would easily choke on paper clips or staples. Most of them would choke on more than 3-4 pages at a time too. I have burned out shredder before too by shredding for more than 2 minutes. The Sentinel seems strong enough to handle tough or prolonged jobs and does so with added security.

Overall, I am very pleased with this shredder. I use a Fellowes PS70-2CD which does cross-cut and 15 sheets but I think this Sentinel Pro is on par with that and has micro-shredding. I would recommend it.

product_title: Brother MFCJ870 Wireless Color Inkjet All-In-One with Scanner, Copier and Fax Printer
review_headline: Ours Does An Excellent Job Printing Photos !!! Well Pleased !!!
review_body: First, let me say that our machine is USB connected; regardless of manufacturer, I have never had anything but headaches from wireless connections. Also, all printer and scanner commands have been initiated from the desktop; except for straight copying (which it does flawlessly) I have not yet touched any of the buttons/commands on the printer itself and may never have reason to.  I selected some random text from here and there and printed them. The results were as neat and crisp as any I have seen; what was supposed to be black is a nice coal black. I used whatever default settings that were already set. Paper was Georgia Pacific 20# 88brightness acid free "copy paper" from the local Walmart.  After reading all the reviews, I was afraid photo printing might not be quite so good as I had hoped; BUT, at least with the printer we got,  that is definitely not the case; I am WELL PLEASED with the results of the photo printing we have done. During the initial set-up, it requested that I select a photo for a test printing; so, I chose a photo that had a lot of detail and many different colors. I did no initial preparation to this photo and printed it straight from the file-folder using whatever default settings Brother had already selected for this test. I was expecting to be disappointed, so I sure got a nice surprise; the very first photo printed in this unprepared for trial run came out as good as anything we have had printed at any of the usual sources such as the kiosks at the chain stores and Walmart Online. Although the print quality was excellent, it did trim about an eighth-inch of the image from all sides of the 4x6 print; I expect this is on account of me using a straight-from-camera full-size 39.99" x 59.99" 72-PPI image file. I then took that same image file to Photoshop Elements 7 Full Edit and resized it to exactly 4 X 6 300-PPI and sharpened it with high pass sharpening; no other changes were made. I then printed this file from Elements byselecting File > Print; in the print dialogue box I selected "printer preferences" and that brought up a Brother print preferences dialogue box where I chose "vivid" and "enhanced color management (I think it said)"; clicked "Okay" and it immediately began printing. The resulting print of this purposefully and properly sized image file printed in it's entirety, with no lost detail around the edges and the colors were dead on perfect. Needless to say, I am well pleased with the photo prints from this machine.  You MUST place the photo paper in the tray FACE SIDE DOWN.  Now let's try scanning a couple of 5x7 photos : I selected two photos that had a lot of detail and many colors; one was a cherry-red U.S.Marines Humvee all decorated with various colored insignia and sitting at a car show amidst many brightly colored vehicles; the other photo was of a Christmas Eve family gathering with a Christmas tree, brightly colored packages, wads of crumpled paper and bows lying all over, and several family members; both good candidates to show me what this Brother scanner could do. I first scanned  both photos with the Brother, saving them as 600-dpi TIFF images; I labeled them Brother A and Brother B. I then scanned them with our old battle-scarred HP Deskjet F2210, using the same format and labeled them HP A and HP B. Other than choosing image file type, no other adjustments were made to the default settings. The Brother performed the task in about 1/4 the time that it took the old HP. When scanning, the HP always sounds like shot-rock going through the crusher at the quarry; it has sounded like this for years and every time I hear it I expect it to come all to pieces. In comparison, I barely heard the Brother. The scans from both machines automatically went into the same dated folder in "My Pictures" Once my test images were scanned to digital files, I viewed and compared them at full-screen. The images from the Brother were much sharper than those from the HP; in a side-by-side comparison, the HP scans were quite soft compared to the much sharper ones of the Brother. The only negative I could see was that the Brother rendered the deep bright red of the Humvee with a slight orangish cast; I really do not know why, as it rendered the bright reds of the Christmas packages and decorations quite true to original color. I have spent many grueling hours this overly rainy spring/summer scanning shoebox-fulls of photos to digital with the old HP and now the wife has suggested I do it all over again with the Brother --- it is that much better.  I do not like that hateful flimsy paper tray, nor do I like the haphazard way that it slides in/out; maybe it will get better as I become used to it.  These are the things I wanted a printer/scanner to do and I am happy so far with what I see; I hope the honeymoon lasts.   I am so excited with how well our particular machine prints photos !!!  Update: 13-July-2015: I have since been given some 8-1/2 X 11 glossy photo paper of unknown brand. I loaded this face-down in the regular paper tray.  In "printer preferences", where it gives type of paper options, I selected "Brother BP71", my reasoning being that the printer itself probably cares little what brand the paper is and that there may very well be some incorporated degradation of quality when "other brand" is selected; I figure if the printer firmware thinks the paper is Brother brand, then it will do it's utmost best to impress me. In the printer dialogue box, there is a choice between " allow Elements (or whatever photo handling program you are using) to control colors" and "allow printer to control colors"; I have experienced  the best results by allowing the printer to control colors. When printing photos of this size, I usually remove the plain paper from the tray and load the one single sheet of 8-1/2 X 11 photo paper, FACE DOWN, in the paper tray and all works asplanned; however, on the rare occasion that the machine fails to pick up the single sheet, I put a few sheets of plain paper underneath it and it will then pick up the single sheet of photo paper, leaving the regular paper safely in the tray. The reason I load photo paper only one sheet at a time is that I seldom have reason to print more than one photo at a time; and, if I load more than that single sheet of photo paper, in all the excitement I will probably forget to change back to regular paper and then print some multi-page document or other on the expensive photo paper.  I don't know why many reviewers claim that this machine can only print photos on 4 X 6 photo paper; we have had no difficulties whatsoever printing photos on 8-1/2 X 11 glossy photo paper by loading it in the regular paper tray.  27-November-2016__Update: We have discovered an 8-1/2 x 11 photo paper that works wonderfully with this printer; Epson "Value Photo Paper Glossy"; 49-lb  9.1 mil We get ours here from Amazon, 50-sheets about $7 It feeds wonderfully through the "roll-over" mechanism and the resulting prints turn out well.  Although we haven't tried it yet, other all-in-one owners claim that the Costco "Kirkland Signature" paper also works well.  We have found that this printer does not get along well with Canon GP-601 Photo Paper Glossy, with about two of three sheets having disastrous results, the rollers losing traction about midway during the process with a portion of the sheet getting ink smeared all over.  We have not yet found a 4x6 paper that did not perform well; it has printed good on any brand that we have ran through it.  Our prints look as good as any we have had done at any of the chain stores.  The only Brother paper we have used are the stingy three 4x6 sheets that came with the printer; Brother paper is ridiculous expensive and way out of our budget    >>> INK <<<  Genuine Brother ink is far too expensive, plus the printersays the cartridges are empty when there is still about 3/4 of the volume left; what a rip-off. I found an easy way to fool the printer into using all the ink; just Google it for loads of tutorials. We are currently using Blake ink, available here at Amazon; 4-blacks and 2 of each color for $18; less than we paid for a single genuine Brother cartridge. Regardless of manufacturer, these companies could give these printers away for free if the recipients used a couple changes of ink per year.  I have just received a package of bulk ink that I will use to refill the cartridges and see how that goes; BCH brand; six 100cc bottles; three black and one each of color, $16 right here at Amazon; a 100cc bottle of ink will refill these puny ink cartridges for several years of frequent use.   I hope this information is helpful.

product_title: Epson Perfection V39 photo Scanner
review_body:
For researchers, the Epson V39 is the ideal size for travel and meets the requirements of most libraries and archives as a flatbed scanner without automatic feeder. It's fairly fast at about 20 seconds per scan . . . from the beginning of the scan until the wand returns for the next scan. The problem is . . . this scanner makes two scan passes for each image. That takes 40 seconds per image. The image is clear so that 5th generation carbon and mimeographed copies are not further compromised.

The included software is minimally efficient. Once each scan is complete, one must move the image to the folder of choice. This gets tiresome for a researcher with limited time. Also, I find the cover lid a bit flimsy with awkward hinges.

Therefore, it is only logical to compare other scanners for optimum performance. The Canon 220 is priced almost exactly the same. The scan needs just one pass. In just 20 seconds the image is saved and the software is much easier to use. The image is clear and detailed. The lid is substantial and the hinge feels solid. Also it looks and feels almost identical to my Canon 210 which I have had for a few years and have abused endlessly in travel. it is still in good shape.

In conclusion, my choice is Canon!

product_title: V-LIGHT Halogen Desk Lamp with 3-Point Adjustable Arm and Dimmer Switch
review_headline: Can't recommend.... gets really hot, flickers on low setting, cheap switch, energy hog...
review_body:
This is an "old technology" style halogen bulb that was popular back in the 1980s in those black floor "torchieres" that many of us owned. They are cheap ($3 to replace) but waste energy and produce a LOT of heat. When I saw the size of this fixture I assumed it was a MR-16 halogen, much cooler when burning. The minute you turn this thing on it's like a heater-- lots of heat emanates from the light itself and you don't want to get your hand anywhere near it. The switch, this is different than the switch in the current product description, is different (see attached photo) and feels really cheap as you turn it. With halogen I had expected a nice dimmer that would smoothly adjust to the exact brightness you want, not a switch that clicks <low> (and flickers) and high (bring on the Sahara).

The black chrome is an interesting design choice. I prefer the classic regular chrome.

You can now get desk lights with LED's that look great and only consume 3 W of power --- the fixtures are less and those LED's last forever. Not sure why one would want to buy this fixture with it's unique special-order halogen bulb that you could fry eggs on.

Sorry, can't recommend this lamp.... there are many better options on the market. Hope this helps!

product_title: Icellent Silicone Lego Molds / Ice Cube Trays, Lego Inspired Building Bricks and Mini Figures DIY Molds for Chocolate, Jello, Hard Candy, Fondant, Crayons, Candles and Soaps (Set of 4 Molds)
review_headline: There are so many fun thins you can do with these. They are easy to use and clean as well.
review_body:
My 10 year old is a huge Lego fan. We are having a Lego themed birthday party for her next month, so these are turning out to be huge lifesavers. I have used similar silicone molds in the past and love how wonderful they are, these are no exception. Here’s why I love them:

• Easy to clean: I have already thrown these in the dishwasher multiple times and they come out perfect every time. I have scrubbed them out to clean them, but with all the crevices and small spaces I much prefer the dishwasher.
• Unique: We have done some experiments with these trying to figure out what we want to do for her birthday, but pretty much everything comes out looking cool because Lego’s are cool. I took our last experimental batch of chocolate to a friend’s because I don’t need a bunch of it laying around my house, they were so impressed with how cool it turned out. These are very good replica Lego’s!
• Dishwasher, freezer and oven safe: This gives us such a wide variety of projects we can do with the molds. I’ll briefly mention next some things we’ve tried.
• Projects-
-Melted chocolate: See picture. This was her first choice for her birthday party. We got chocolate coloring (it’s not regular food coloring, its base is oil instead of water). Then we melted white chocolate down, mixed the color in and poured it in the molds. It turned out great! We plan on doing this on top of cupcakes and potentially a few in goodie bags wrapped up nicely. Advice: I figured this out towards the end. Make sure to use plenty of coloring. I didn’t use enough and you can see that it’s more pastel. Also, tap the molds against the counter a few times to make sure the thick chocolate gets in the little holes. The more melted the chocolate is the better. Sometimes they still don’t fill the holes entirely, but it really helps.
-Ice cubes: This is a no brainer, but she did want to put coloring in the ice so you can see the Lego better. I’m sort of anti artificial coloring, but I figured for a party it would be OK. See my test run ice Lego’s in the picture. Advice: Don’t over fill, it’s super easy to do. I prefer the bigger Duplo 2 x 4 brick mold for this. I tried making purple and it came out horribly. My biggest surprise was the colors mixed as I picked the molds up and some of them actually turned out really pretty. I only did green, blue, red and an attempt at purple, so you can see the other mixtures are due to some colored water moving around and mixing. My best advice for this is to put the molds on something flat and sturdy and fill them there, then put them in the freezer on that. When I picked the molds up they sagged a little in the middle since they are flexible, then the water mixed. Putting them on something hard would’ve been better. This is why I do a test run.
-Crayons: I haven’t made crayons with this, but I have with a similar mold. This was one of my daughter’s favorite projects ever and it was so easy. We took her leftover crayons from last year, broke them up and put them in the mold. Then baked them in the oven (I forget the time and temp, but I think at 270 for like 25 minutes) until they melted. If you Google it you’ll easily be able to find some instructions. They turned out amazing and only took like 45 minutes to do AND my daughter had a blast! That’s an all around perfect scenario for me: cheap, easy, happy kid, no electronics. Yay! I am getting another set of these just for crayons for the goodie bags at the party (I hope they don’t get them mixed up with chocolate, I’ll label them as crayons or chocolate so they’ll know). We liked mixing similar colors, like pink, red, orange and yellow. My daughter also made theme sort of crayons for some kids she tutors. She did themes: Forrest = brown + green, Beach = blue + tan, girl = pink + purple. She did one color on one side and one color on the other, so they can flip it around. Just an idea. She’s going to use the larger 4 x 2 brick mold and the smaller irregular shaped mold for the crayons, I think the minfigures are too shallow.

Oops, I had no intention of writing a novel about these. We just really do like them. This has been a fun little product to get us planning some DIY Lego party things. review_body:
Nice option for semi-durable outdoor display. They do hold up in the rain and to people touching them. Orange fades in the sun to yellow after six weeks of use outdoors. Haven't tried red, blue or black.

We find that if we slightly depress the tips the entire time while drawing long lines, the color applies more boldly.

These colors are easily scratched off after they dry so when I need to correct a small line without damaging everything around it, I use a small, flattened bamboo stick (like you would use for nail care) to gently scrape off the ink. Or you could also use your fingernail.

Facial tissue and window cleaner are effective at removing these colors. I lay the sign flat on the floor and spray directly with window cleaner and then with my finger, rub the window cleaner around a bit on the lines to be removed. You can see when the lines begin to smear and are ready to be wiped away. Paper towels work fine, but don't get the board quite as clean.

product_title: Brother Printer MFCJ4410DW  Business Smart Multi-Function Inkjet and Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner, Copier and Fax
review_headline: This printer covers all my personal and business needs!
review_body:
I been waiting forever to have a new printer for use at home. I've had random laser printers that were re-tired from work, when they ran out of toner, i'd get another, so on and so on. I usually do most my printing at the office, but the heavens have granted me the wonders of telecommuting. I soon discovered the need for a good quality printout for reports, proposals, etc. This printer covers all my personal and business needs.

Printing:
Right off the bat, the printing wasn't so great to the point where I was concerned. However, I really just needed it for my random print jobs for my home office. Overtime, it worked it's way out. Even on basic copy paper, this printer output's print outs beautifully. I was surprised when someone who received a printout asked if it was printed on a laser printer. I've never came across a printer that prints the paper horizontally, so it's pretty unique, I'm sure it helps with the speed.

The print output tray is connected to the paper tray so if you need to reload, pull those important print out's off the output tray! I'm worried about the longevity of this tray as it seems kinda flimsy, like I'm going to knock into it the wrong way and it's going to break. So far, no problems with me bumping into it as I push the output tray back in.

-- It prints Two Sided DUPLEX!, which in my opinion a must in a printer. Let's save some trees people, print on BOTH sides of the paper. A lesson my late grandfather installed on me as a child forever ago. It's worth the short delay. If you want to print both sides for a presentation, you better be using 24lb paper or else the ink will bleed through a little bit on paper of lesser quality. If it's to be conservative like me and want to save trees and your just trying to save paper on print outs you need to reference for a few hours, scribble on and throw out, then go ahead with the standard 20lb copy paper. The bleed thru is minimal and not distracting to work off of.

--Aftermarket Printer Ink doesn't work. Brother printers check and make sure their legit Brother OEM replacement cartridges. I was REALLY disappointed when I ordered ink from YoYo Ink and they didn't work on two printers of this model after two shipments. The prices don't seem to terrible for Brother OEM ink though so I guess I can't be cheap.

I CAN FINALLY PRINT FROM MY iOS DEVICES!
This was an added plus and embarrassingly a surprise. I usually read up on everything before I buy. After all the research I looked into, its either not well point out or I overlooked it in excitement at a printer within my budget and of a trusted name. I wasn't sure before purchasing it if I could, but it wasn't a major factor.

Scanning:
It was a top feeder, which is usually what I prefer to use with documents. It scans very quickly through the feeder, much faster than an
HP 8500 All in One. It can scan double sided print outs as well using the the feeder.

Copying
It does that quite well.

Faxing:
Faxing in 2015? I prefer to send the document via email, the system can send an email or scan it to your computer. However, I did purchase one of this for one of my companies retail locations-- and they report is faxes quite well. I personally only have a cell phone, and no land line to fax from so I don't have much hands on experience for sending and receiving until I visit that retail location that I gave one too.

Compatibility
If your in IT, you'll appreciate Brother's wide range of drivers to work on many platforms. I use ONLY Brother brand laser printers at ALL my companies retail locations because they work great with our custom Point of Sale and limitations of the platform powering it.

Connectivity
It connects to Wi-Fi and LAN, and to iOS devices and more.

The Goodies
A basic,but responsive and small touch screen display. The style is attractive decorated with a glossy black smooth finish.

All in all, a great printer for the price. I have no complaints as of yet. When I do.. I'll be back, trust me...yle is attractive decorated with a glossy black smooth finish.

All in all, a great printer for the price. I have no complaints as of yet. When I do.. I'll be back, trust me...

product_title: Kensington Bluetooth Presentation
review_headline: A mixed bag, but generally good.
review_body:
There is a lot to like about this presentation controller, and a few things that will drive you nuts! Let's deal with the positives first.

It's a nice, sleek little unit, and it fits nicely in the hand while giving a presentation. It isn't burdened down with a bunch of buttons--just a four-way rocker for next slide (right), previous slide (left), laser pointer on (top), and blacken screen (down). I like that simplicity. On my Mac and Windows laptops, it works from 10 to 15 feet away, which is all I need. It comes with a nice carrying case and a recharging cable. And left to just that, I'd give the unit five stars. Here's why I knocked off a star:

A few reviewers have complained that the unit won't hold power--that you have to charge the unit just before you use it or it will be dead when you start your presentation. That's not really the case, but I understand how they came to that conclusion. The unit does not have an LED to let you know it is turned on. There is a small LED that flashes when you turn the unit on, and again, more quickly, when you turn the unit off. Until you get the hang of the flashing frequencies, you might very well think you had turned the unit off when you hadn't. That's a bit of a pain.

The second problem is with pairing. I had no real problem with my Windows laptop, but my Mac (running OS 10.10 'Yosemite'), paired it as an 'unknown keyboard'. A search through Kensington's FAQs uncovered a note to restart the Mac after pairing, at which time it would reappear in the Bluetooth device list as a mouse, and that turned out to be the case. But, that's another pain.

So, when I travel with this controller, I bring along a little cheat sheet with the details on pairing to both Mac and Windows, in case I end up using someone else's laptop for my presentation, and how to verify that the unit has been turned off. Perhaps Apple has spoiled me, but I don't feel like I should have to do that.

One final minor annoyance: The recharging port for the unit, a micro USB port, is in the midsection of the unit, and the top and bottom sections slide together while presenting and cover up the port. That's nice when it comes to protecting the port from dirt and grime, but if you forget that you have to slide the top and bottom apart a bit to expose the port, it can take a few minutes to find it.

Even with all that said, I think this is still a better Bluetooth presenter than most of the other units out there, and it is a good value for the money. Note that it does not include a Bluetooth dongle for the laptop on which it is used, so the laptop will either have to support Bluetooth natively, or you will need to buy a Bluetooth dongle separately and install its drivers on your laptop. And note that the controller won't work with phones or tablets, since it has to emulate a mouse. review_headline: Maybe the Worst Printer I've Ever Owned
review_body: This printer is virtually identical to model 7525 when is exclusively sold at Costco. I've looked at the two versions in person and can't tell a difference except for the model number on the front. I assume they change the model number to prevent "best price guarantees" having to match Costco's price.  I purchased this HP printer at Costco because my last HP printer was extremely temperamental, but this one isn't any better. Given the current state of printer technology HP shouldn't be producing printers this unreliable. Initial set-up wasn't as easy as advertised, but was doable. It worked flawlessly for about a month before the problems started cropping up.  First, even though it shows it's on the network my devices are completely unable to locate the printer.  This is a constant problem when the printer comes online from hibernation mode.  The only way to get it discoverable by my PC's and Mac is to turn the printer off and then back on.  At which point it's back in business.  This process worked for a couple months, but then I discovered that when I turned it off using the power button it wouldn't turn back on. Seriously, what else could go wrong.  I've fiddled with it for 10-15 minutes at a time trying to get it back on when we urgently needed something printed and the only thing that works (and even then less than 1/4 of the time) is to unplug the power cord from the back of the device and wall, wait a little bit, and then plug it all back in. IF I'm lucky, at that point it will power back on.  More often than not it won't.  If I try the power button again a few hours or days later, it will usually turn on, but by then whatever we needed to print in the first place is long past due. This is the most insanely frustrating device I've ever owned.

product_title: Pilot Mechanical Pencil Automac, 0.5mm, Black (HAT-3SR-B)
review_headline: Exceptional: The best of the Pilot Vanishing Point H1005 and the Faber Castell Alpha-Matic
review_body:
The Pilot Automac is in essence a combination of two of the best general purpose mechanical pencils ever made: the Pilot Vanishing Point H1005 and the Faber Castell Alpha-Matic. If you know pencils, you know those two pencils. Both have been out of production for years; in many ways the Pilot Automac is better than either both in specification and in practice.

I bought this pencil a few years ago when my venerable Pilot H1005 retractable tip pencil started to break down and I discovered that my back up supply was out. It was only then that I found out that Pilot no longer made the H1005 - I'd used that model since the early '80s as my daily writing tool. The H1005 had the right functionality and price to be a daily writing tool.

I'm old enough to have used mechanical pencils when they were for drafting and so have used a wide variety. My favorites have always been the Faber Castell Alpha-Matic and TK-Matic. Many still say they were the finest mechanical pencils ever made - they were expensive in the 80's and have only gone up in price used. The TK-Matic is an ideal drafting pencil with extended point. The Pilot Automac compares to the originally more expensive Faber Castell Alpha-Matic which was designed as a general purpose mechanical pencil, but to me the Pilot actually functions better. I bought my Alpha-Matic new in the late 80's but the auto-advance function was never as smooth as what I've found with the Pilot. With the Pilot automatic lead advance is completely smooth and unobtrusive and feels more natural than the Alpha does.

A note on automatic lead advance pencils to those who aren't familiar with them: unlike manual advance pencils, with automatic lead advance pencils you should barely be able to see the lead when you look at the tip. The sheath that holds the point of the lead will push against the paper when you write and give way to the lead so the lead writes. The magic is that as the sheathing is pushed back, it automatically grabs the lead and the next time the pencil is raised from the paper even partially, the lead is automatically advanced. So you never have to feed the lead until the lead runs out. The only time you have to manually advance the lead is when the lead is too short to be advanced - about the same time you'd have to move to a new piece of lead in a manual advance pencil.

To me the Faber Castells were both too expensive and impractical as a daily carry-around writing tool. One thing that the Automac has that neither Faber Castell had is a vanishing point - with the Pilot Automac you can retract the lead and metal sheathing point into the casing of the pencil like you would for a pen. This makes it a practical daily pencil. So the Automac matches the functionality I was so accustomed to with the H1005 and which largely made it my carry-around go-to pencil: it doesn't poke holes in pockets.

The Pilot is heavier and thicker than the Alpha or H1005, but not in a negative way. Its build is solid with excellent attention to detail. I bought my Automac here for a little more than twice the price of the H1005 yet it's so much more.

The Automac has exceeded any expectations I could have had - it is an exceptional pencil. The ultimate testament isn't words, but actions: this has been my daily writing tool ever since it arrived. Like it's forebearers, it has performed flawlessly and reliably. Highly recommended.

review_headline: Is your Printer from outside of US? Then do not buy the cartridge even if Amazon.com says it is compatible with your printer.
review_body:
Read this if you bought your MFC7860-DW not here in US but in India. Here's my experience not on the product per se but on the customer service that I received from an Indian reseller on (Amazon.in). I give a 5-Star rating to Zilla for customer service. Here's why:

Printer: Brother MFC-7860DW; purchased from an authorized Brother dealer in HYDERABAD, India - back in 2012

Placed an order for a Brother TN-450 toner cartridge on AMAZON.COM from US and sourced it through my relative in 2014 April-May as my toner was running out. Continued to use the one that came with the printer until it stopped printing any document. That's when I opened the package from Amazon only in Dec 2014. Though on Amazon.com it says its compatible with my printer model - IT DOES NOT especially if your printer is from another country. SO PLEASE WATCH OUR AND READ this IF your printer is sourced/bought from an another country. Though printers are of the same model, they are not just different in voltage (110v vs 220v) but also some of their accessories like the cartridge, Brother has designed them differently.

And, how did I get I figure it out? After calling the mobile number (on a Sunday 06/28/2015 at 10AM) on Zilla's product page on Amazon.In. I told the gentleman that the toner cartridge TN-450 was not fitting in the drum unit of my BROTHER MFC-7860DW and he told me that there could be some design changes between the US model and the Indian model AND that is the only reason why the US cartridge is not slipping into the drum unit of the Indian printer (left side slips in but not the right side). After carefully examining the pieces I do see the design difference between the two cartridges. Right side of the cartridge from US was not slipping in because of the protruding plastic piece that is placed at different location. After giving a thought, I heated a thin steel rod on a gas stove, melted the slots on the drum unit, slipped the cartridge into it. VIOLA....it went in smooth and could hear the locking sound of the US cartridge inside the Indian printer drum. Inserted it into my India printer, turned it on and could see the printer functioning like brand new.

Why this long story? Coz I wanted to shared my success story with others who may have had the similar experience and figuring out how to get this done. While that's the primary intent, I also would like to THANK wholeheartedly for listing a mobile number on the product page so customers like me get instant call support. Prior to all this indigenous innovation, I tried calling BROTHER Service center here in Chennai in Nov-Dec when I initially tried using the US cartridge and experienced this incompatibility issue. I was asked to try returning the cartridge and see if Amazon.com will refund my money or buy a new one from them costing around 4500 to 5000 INR.

However, Zilla person who spoke to me, did not do that or tried to up sell his products. Instead he asked me to take it to a local printer shop and see if they can help me. He gave instructions to find out the difference and see if I try slipping in the cartridge into the drum unit while he was on call with me. That too on a Sunday.
