product_title: Case-it Mighty Zip Tab 3-Inch Zipper Binder, Neon Blue, D-147-NEOBLU
review_headline: We are running 50:50 in terms of durability
review_body:
I purchased this late in the school year with about 6 weeks to go before summer break. It was a replacement for an identically sized binder from the same company -the only difference is the color. Unfortunately, it is the second replacement I have had to buy this past school year -the previous one was a direct replacement for my other daughter that was purchased back in December. As some of their classes required 3" notebooks as well as either a separate accordion file or an enclosed file system, the Case-it seemed to fit the bill. In past years, I have tried other zip-book systems (including previous styles/models of this product) but none of them ever proved to be consistently durable enough to last a full school year. Since each daughter needed (2) of these units (3 classes per notebook), I was hoping that this year would be different. But alas, out of the (4) notebooks that I purchased, I have had to replace (2) of them. In all fairness, one of my daughters is harder on her things than the other - hers is the notebook that I had to replace in December. The other daughter, however, is quite conscientious with her supplies and the notebook still failed to survive the school year.

The pros for this item are its size, the zipper system which seals in all of the paperwork, the zippered pencil/supply area, and the file system that is accessible both internally and externally.

The cons are price given its reliability. Out of 4 notebooks purchased, only half made it through the school year needing replacement. None of these were "main" notebooks - each was used for less than half their classes and were definitely not "stuffed to the gills". As per the other negative reviews, the rings can tend to loosen up and the zippers seem to be a weak point. Also, the mesh area for pencils and pens can and do tear - some more easily than others. There seems to be a 50:50 chance of getting a good binder. The good ones are great but it gets expensive quite quickly replacing the poorer units.

So... needless to say, I will continue to search for a more rugged binder - and one where the durability is not a matter of luck.at but it gets expensive quite quickly replacing the poorer units.

product_title: Chair Mat for Hard Floors | Polypropylene Chair Floor Protector | Colored Floor Mat for Office and Home | 100% BPA, Phthalate & Odor Free | 30"x48" | Multiple Colors
review_headline: Disappointing. Overpriced and made for kids.
review_body: My wife has a customized pink office and I thought this would be a great fit seeing as how it was the only pink chair mat I could find but be warned it is deceivingly small! If you notice in the picture they used a kids chair to make it seem bigger and I think this was very misleading. A normal office chair will have its legs come right to the edges leaving no room to roll around which is the point of a chair mat. Double check those measurements on your floor before buying.  Also, it comes with no instructions or documentation at all from Office Marshal such as which side is top or bottom. I assumed the side with the two already peeling stickers (one was a bar code the other sticker stating it is made in Israel) was the bottom but with those removed this mat has no logos or markings at all. Neither side seems more "non-skid" than the other. These also usually come with basic instructions for weighing down the corners and leaving it out in heat to settle.  Finally it has no spikes on the bottom forcing me to purchase a regular clear mat as an under layer on the carpet. I then laid it vertically to allow back and forth rolling at the least as I have no interest in returning this in the fairly large box it comes in. I expect it to deteriorate quickly since she will probably be rolling over the edge onto the plastic one repeatedly. All in all I have 2 mats now and spent around $65 to compensate for the bad design. I suggest they add "Kids" in the title.  Update: I decided to return it. It looked really tacky laying on the second mat and she complained that the chair was sliding way too much on it and that the wheels of the chair would simply never settle. I thought this may be due to the clear mat beneath it but when I removed it the same result occurred. This mat honestly seems like a piece of cheap plastic being repurposed for this task compared to the many brands specifically designed for this purpose. It also takes much longer to settle and straighten than standard chair mats! The only good thing I have to say is it is a nice color.

product_title: HP Paper, EcoFFICIENT Copy Paper, 16lb, 8.5x11, Letter,  92 Bright
review_headline: Thinner paper than usual. Constantly worried about paper jams.
review_body:
As most every other review out here has said, this is thin paper. Make no mistake, it won't look/feel like "regular" office copier paper. If you need thinner paper, that's fine. However, you should seek out the instructions and/or specs for your printer to see if this will work. This is 16lb rated paper, and my printer's manual says it can take paper from 17-20lb paper. This is thinner, and so far I haven't had jams, but it's in the back of my mind as a possibility because a) I've seen so many reviews saying it jams, and b) It's below the officially rated numbers my printer will accept.

However, if your printer is set up to use this kind of paper reliably, it will work for you. You do get more pages per sheet, and the thinness can come into play depending on WHAT you are printing. Things are far more visible from the other side of the paper. Printing on both sides of the paper might not be recommended, as it might end up looking like a mess (again, depending on what you're printing) with "visible bleed through" on both sides.

To me, the addtl pages you get in the ream aren't worth the jam possibilities, and the issues of printing on both sides of the paper - which to me is a more eco friendly thing than just having thinner paper.

product_title: Hallmark Signature Collection Wedding Card: Live, Laugh, Love
review_body:
This is a really lovely wedding card that has a lot going on. I have made my own cards over the years and this is a very well made card.

The corners have four raised die cuts in silver metallic (be careful when putting this card in the envelope so you don't snag these as they are certainly higher than the rest of the card.

The next layer is white and is coated in a very fine blue/green iridescent glitter. This layer is also raised above the surface of the card, so again, take some care in putting the card into the envelope. This layer has a wedding cake punched into the card and the words "Live" "Laugh" and "Love" are also punched.

The top of the card (which is below this layer) is in silver and shows through on the punches. The metallic silver tone is the same as the raised die cuts in the corners. When looking at the card altogether, you see a three dimensional representation from high (die cuts), medium, white layer, to low (silver backing) that gives the card a rich and elegant look. The wording inside the card matches the color of the silver and tops the whole thing off beautifully.

The card looks expensive and has an elegant, fragile quality to it. If you are planning on mailing this card, you will need to include extra postage as there is no way it can be machine stamped. It is a card that I would be proud to send to a couple on their wedding day and I recommend it to anyone looking for an elegant card for such an occasion.

product_title: HP Envy 7640 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Photo Printer (E4W43A)
review_headline: Problem making copies.  Otherwise good printer for price.
review_body:
I have had this printer for a few months. Bought it at Best Buy, and the first one I got was so flaky Idecided it it was defective and returned it for a replacement of the same model.
I have had the replacement for a few months and it works very well with one glaring exception: About every other time I try to make a single-sheet, flatbed copy, it tries for a minute or so, then says "printing cancelled", with a moving circle on the display screen and stays thereeither forever or until I disconnect and reconnect the power and try again, whichever comes first. The next copy after that always works first try.
For me this has not been a huge issue because I very seldom use it for copying - mostly printing, scanning, and an occasional fax. I have it connected to an iMac by USB and a Windows laptop via network router.
I have decided to keep it until either further problems develop or my copying requirements increase. For the featuers I mostly use it is a very good printer at an excellent price (got it for $50 off list at my local Best-Buy.) But I would NOT recommend this printer to a friend because the problem seems to indicate bad firmware, therefor poor testing, and because I expect most users use the copy function more frequently. Not sure if this will be my last HP printer, as I have had 3 or 4 before this one and was quite satisfied.
Meanwhile I check HP website for a firmware update about once a month. I don't see how it could be a driver problem because copying is (or should be) totally independent of any network or connected devices/computers.

product_title: INFINITER XP-5 4-in-1 Ballpoint Pen with LED Light/ Stylus for Most PDAs/ Red Beam Presentation Pointer
review_headline: nice laser pen, horrible battery life
review_body:
We bought this pen for our cat. As much as we were spending on cat lights, we could get this for the same price AND be able to see it on sunny days. It works really well except that the PDA stylus never worked, which doesn't matter for me, but it may for many of you. It looks more like it should be a highlighter than a stylus, but it doesn't highlight either LOL. Also, I had read that these batteries were very short lived. I did not believe them. I have used the product for 4 days for about 10 minutes per day (off and on) and they are dying already. What was once a wonderful bright beam is now a faded, hard to see in the light one. Otherwise, I really enjoy the laser light. The ink pen does work (but I can't imagine much ink in it as there are 4 batteries that take up space in there), and the white, flashlight like lite (great for a doctor checking pupils) works just fine too. It has a nice weight to it and feels solid. It came in a very nice silver outer box (that has the barcode sticker on it that says made in Taiwan) and an interior black box with a fold over lid. it could be given as a gift. The pen is encased in a black styrofoam mold to hold it and the batteries in place. It also came with 2 "other products" leaflets and why Quarton is the best (can also be seen on their storefront), and an operating leaflet with specifications (in English and German).

I found it interesting that when I click on the link for this product from my orders, the page no longer exists (it has only been a week). My product: INFINITER XP-5 4-In-1 Laser Pen/Light/Stylus, Black (P151-51004) and the response I get: "Looking for something? We're sorry. The Web address you entered is not a functioning page on our site Go to Amazon.com's Home Page" I don't know if it is just a glitch or if the product was removed and re-categorized, because when I search for the pen, I find it this: "INFINITER XP-5 4-in-1 Ballpoint Pen with LED Light/ Stylus for Most PDAs/ Red Beam Presentation Pointer by Infiniter Be the first to review this item" Both are sold by Quarton USA. And I always read the reviews and the only negative thing I remember is about a short battery life, so I am not the first to review the product. Just food for thought, as those little things always make me curious. I paid the same price it is now being sold for, but I got Prime free shipping, which is no longer offered (and now ships for a fiver). Maybe they had to resubmit the pen as a new product to remove the Prime free shipping?

I give this a 3 for PDA stylus not working and horrible battery life, minus one point for each.

review_headline: Can't program using Comcast VOIP service
review_body: I purchased a CPR Call Blocker V202 because ever since we switched to Comcast VOIP we’ve been receiving many more unwanted calls than we used to. I chose this model because the Call Blocker website and Forum stated that it was improved over older models to make setup easier for US customers using services (like Comcast) easier. Unfortunately, I can’t get it to work. The problem is that in order to program the unit you have to use codes (like ##7#) to do so. These codes (which are input via your phone system) seem to conflict with the Comcast network codes. Using them fails to put the Call Blocker into programming mode. There is no way to tell it which numbers to block. There is a feature that is supposed to help you work around this problem (i.e., pushing the “Block Now” button for 5 seconds). This seems to work for about 2 seconds, which is not enough time to input the information before the system gives you an error. Overall, the device is severely limited  by not being programmable without using your phone/network which may not be compatible with the programming process.

I am pleased with this folio and will definitely recommend to my friends.
It works exactly as described and I was thankful to have a clear description upfront on the do's and don'ts.
For example, I was glad to know not to use the pouch as long-term storage for documents-- as the print might transfer to the bag, but that the folio can be folded when I use a smaller work bag. It's not rigid like the other folios.

I am an interior designer and this bag is flexible and resilient enough to carry around my carpet, laminate, paint samples and drawings as I go to and from client meetings. I now prefer to use this bag over other regular thin file folders as the others get beat up so quickly and their sharp corners are really annoying. This folio goes in and out of my bag smoothly and doesn't crease.

The magnet buttons are strong enough for me to stick the bag to the refrigerator door or metal filing cabinet - though I probably wouldn't leave my iPad or stone samples in it while doing so.

The bag is completely see-through, front and back, so it's easy to identify the contents no matter which way it is facing in my bag or hanging on my file cabinet at work.

I was unsure about the double layer fold over at the top, but now I realize that is what gives it the extra spill protection, so now I prefer this design - I can place my client's paperwork by my cup of coffee and not worry about spills!

Overall, I highly recommend this bag and am considering giving to all my clients as a year-end gift.

review_body:
This is a great pen. The nip is finer than a medium, but the ink flows well enough that it doesn't skip. I'm new to fountain pens but have found that finding good ones can take some patience, Pilot has done awesome for the pricepoint, on this and their Varsity disposible pen line.

It does come with a rubber converter, but save yourself the heartache and possible leaks and get the plastic pilot converter. The rubber one works in a pinch but I struggled loading it full with ink- there is no way to completely fill the converter by filling it through the nib, and not really a way to see how much ink is left. I tried multiple times filling from bottled ink and thought I succeeded, went to work with it the next day to have it work for a paragraph, and I opened my pen to find a completely empty converter. I threw the disposible cartridge in there and it's worked beautifully ever since. Since fountain pens go through so much ink weith daily use (this one isn't as bad as others I've used) and I hate the thought of throwing away a cartridge every time, I will definitely be using the converter. While I'm not a fan of having to carry around my bottle of Noodlers black (in a Ziploc), I'm not sure there's another way I can travel without disposables.

The pen itself has a nice weight and the cap clicks gently but securely. The grip is small, hard plastic but with a good lip to keep fringers from sliding down and getting inked. The price is well enough that if it does get misplaced (or stolen, based on the compliments I've gotten) I can put another one on my Wishlist.

product_title: Grandstream GXP1400 Small-Medium Business HD IP Phone
review_headline: Decent IP Phone for the Money
review_body:
All in all, it's a decent IP phone.

Pros:
- The price is definitely right
- Ease of setup/use
- Nice web interface

Cons:
- The audio (on the receiving end) sounds rather tinny. I've heard callers tell me I sound like I'm far away.
- The phone has a tendency to drop audio for 20-30 seconds during a call. The call stays connected, but the audio is gone, both ways.
- I will note, that since I've upgraded the firmware (which takes a little work to do) I haven't noticed the audio drop anymore.
- 10/100 PC port

Summary:
For the price, it's definitely a decent phone, it does work as intended (once the firmware is updated). Mainly I chose it because I wanted to test how IP phones would handle on my network, to upgrade off ATAs, and to see how well it would integrate with Asterisk as some refurbed Cisco phones were giving me difficulty. I do plan on trying some of the 2130's to see if there's an improvement in the audio on the receiving end, as that is my only real issue with the GXP1400. Other than only a 10/100 PC port, and lack of PoE.

product_title: HP 1513ni Multifunction Color Photo Printer with Scanner and Copier (Ink Not Included)
review_headline: Don't let the Lack of Ink on this Printer Make you Pass it By!
review_body:
Generally, when you buy a new printer, the ink cartridges provided are only 10% to 30% full. That's the catch! Low price on the printer with very little ink makes you purchase the more expensive ink quite quickly! Shop around! I was able to find this printer with no ink for $27 and free shipping.

Save money on this printer by buying it without ink, then, search for the re-manufactured (refilled) ink cartridges at less money than new (check out House of Toners at $21). Even still, if you want brand new ink, the HP cartridges run around $26. Compared to other printers, the $26 for brand new is still pretty low. However, the ink from House of Toners works great.

As far as the printer? Electric can openers cost nearly as much as this printer, so how can one complain? It's simple, and easy to operate. I did notice it prints slightly slower in normal speed than my previous, more expensive printers. But the draft mode prints quickly and the loss of print quality is hardly noticeable. For basic home office printing and the such, it's wonderful.

_____________________________________________________________________________________________________
Update July 10, 2015: One month of constant operation. I'll bet I've run nearly 300 pages through this printer. Absolutely no complaints. Not only have I gotten very nice printed pages, but I have also run full-sized color photos on regular paper with very satisfactory results. I don't recall experiencing as single paper jam! This is one of those rare examples of when less-is-more.

Quite honestly this has been the best of all of the Bluetooth conference phones that I have tried and I have tried all the major brands under $300.

---My Use---
I use this as my mobile and home office conferencing system going solely over my cell phone.
I generally have anywhere from 5-25 people on the call. (1-5 on my side of the call)
We generally all sit anywhere from a foot away to 5 feet away.

---My Impressions---
I have great clarity as long as my phone signal is good. If the phone signal is bad, there is nothing this thing can do about that.
Everyone I have asked says that they hear me and anyone in the room with me, very well. Obviously with the same caveat as above with the phone signal strength.
Even on battery the response has been very good. The battery can go for a long time. I have not ran out of battery and have calls last for 2+ hours.

I see a few one stars. It could be any number of things from a bad batch to people not understanding how to use it properly. My company has 6 of these and all have the same review as I do.

product_title: Brother HL-L2340DW Compact Laser Printer, Monochrome, Wireless, Duplex Printing, Amazon Dash Replenishment Enabled
review_headline: No ethernet connection, no ability to setup wi-fi without a cable not included, none problems with wi-fi connection.
review_body:
I rarely return products but this one may be a record for the quickest return. Got it yesterday, started to set it up and was stumped when I couldn’t find a place to plug the Ethernet cable in to connect to my network. It advertises itself as a “small office” printer for 1-5 years. Thus networked. But apparently they neglected to include the standard networking port that is a 5 cent part these days and is the best means to network a printer. Okay, I figure, I’ll give the inferior wi-fi printing a shot even though I have read many reviews here that there is a bug with the printer that causes it to get locked in “deep sleep” with wi-fi printing and require hard power resets. But unless you have a small minority of very new wi-fi routers, it does not come with the ability to enable wi-fi without first a hard-wire attaching it to a computer and installing some bloatware. By this point I’m think this thing must have been designed last century but whatever, I am determined to give it a shot. So I search for the cable to connect it to my computer. Turns out it’s not included. So then I get a standard USB cable of my own. No dice, because the printer uses a non-standard female connector port so it requires an unusual USB cable. Perhaps it’s not unusual if you are USB-connecting to a printer these days, but who does that?

So that this point my only option to install this printer is to order a special cable to do a one-time connection to a computer to setup the wi-fi. Are you kidding me? Who ships consumer electronics these days without everything you need to make it work? If I’m going to have to wait days for a cable I will only use once, I’m just as well off returning this half-product and getting something that actually connects to a network and works out of the box.

Having read thousands of reviews on Amazon over the years, I am ready for the “it’s your fault for not knowing it didn’t have an Ethernet connection” and “where did you read that it included the cable” comments from fans of this product. Yes, possibly, but I don’t agree. In this day to send a product that requires a cable and doesn’t include it is so unusual that the description should have noted you would need a cable not included. It shouldn’t be on me to have to scour the web for some product information that notes this little footnote. As for the Ethernet connection, you can by $40 printers that include them these days. It’s pretty much de jure for “connected” products. Even my TV’s, DVD players, cable boxes, etc. all include them, let alone an actual “network” printer. So, again, I think it was a reasonable expectation it would be there and they should really note its absence. Duly noted now.

Heck even if it last only for 2-3 years, it is cheap enough to buy a new one.

review_headline: Super sticky, easy to remove backing, works well with inkjet printer
review_body:
I purchased these for a crafty purpose: I print out Hyperdex planner circles, which I then punch out and stick into my planner for time management. Previously, I bought [[ASIN:B0000C0CJQ Avery Sticker Project Paper, White, 8.5 x 11 Inches, Pack of 15 (03383)]], so I can compare the two.

The Avery Sticker Paper is thicker than these shipping labels; I can't see through onto the next page of my MoleSkine planner when I use the Sticker Paper, but I can somewhat see through it with these shipping labels. However, the shipping labels are significantly stickier, and it's much easier to remove the backing plastic on them. The shipping labels are also significantly cheaper (in bulk - I paid around $25 for the box of 100).

For my purposes, I'm really happy with this particular product. If you don't want any see-through effect/need a thicker paper, I would recommend the official Sticker Paper.

Both types worked fine in my top-feed inkjet printer. :)

4 stars only because they're so thin; otherwise, they would be 5!

review_body: The one star is for the "sold by" supplier and not for Epson.  My personal warning regarding who in particular supplies the product when you purchase it is: do NOT purchase it if it says it is Sold by: Beautiful Ink.  The product I received was in an Epson box but the box was difficult to open - maybe it was re-glued?  There was a 3/4" x 2" label on the outside of the box with product description including the word "New" on it and a long barcode - assuming this is the supplier's barcode - I'm thinking most credible suppliers do not add a label onto an Epson box.  The pouch inside was not a standard manufacturer's pouch:  It was not tightly vacuum sealed like Epson does it and it did not have the tear-notch in it (had to cut it open with scissors).  There was ink on the outside of the cartridge underneath the yellow removable tab (which by the way did not seem to be applied in the usual manner) - have never had this happen before and I have purchased Epson inks for many years.  Don't know yet if it is going to make a mess inside my printer.  Bottom line is that the product, when it is a true Epson manufactured/sealed product, is a good one - just don't buy if the "Sold by" supplier is Beautiful Ink.

product_title: M-Audio MobilePre USB Audio Interface
review_headline: the bigger brother of the FAST TRACK interface with PRO TOOLS software
review_body:
the M-Audio MobilePre is a USB interface product by AVID, the same people who make and distribute PRO TOOLS recording software. it is essentially the bigger brother of the Fast Track MKII with an added XLR/TRS Combo input on the front and 1/4" line ins/outs on the back.

this interface can be used with a wide range of recording software or "DAW's"
FREE versions of PRO TOOLS called "PRO TOOLS SE" or the latest "PRO TOOLS First" software for Windows & Mac can be downloaded from the manufacturer's website(AVID) or you can use it with a wide range of other programs such as Audacity, Fruity Loops, Sony Acid, Cubase, Reaper, etc. if you are more comfortable. the device drivers for any computer or laptop can be downloaded from the manufacturer as well.

the interface itself is fairly basic and not complicated to learn or use at all. 4 knobs on the top control line levels and volume, +48v switch power for microphones if needed. a headphone output, line outputs to speakers and 2 inputs for guitars, microphones, keyboards , or any other line level sound.

the mic pres and A/D converters are pretty good for the price and if your starting a small home/podcast or mobile studio this is a good small lightweight interface. if you only need the 1 input and basic RCA outputs i would suggest getting the smaller FAST TRACK.

product_title: iGearPro Voice Activated Audio Recorder - Premium Digital Voice Recorder  - Multifunctional Portable Rechargeable Dictaphone MP3 Player (8GB)
review_headline: A great, handy voice recorder. But if you already have the right app on your phone, stick with that.
review_body:
I’ve been wanting to give a voice recorder a shot lately, mostly to have a recorder on the go for when I come up with new material, or if I’m having a good conversation with someone that we could record and put up somewhere. With my plans for starting a podcast constantly getting pushed back, I felt that smaller recordings might be the way to go for now. iGearPro just happened to contact me recently about trying out their voice recorder, so of course I jumped at the opportunity. The bottom line is that this is a pretty decent little recorder, but if you have a good app on your phone or even iPod, you may as well stick with that.

iGearPro’s recorder is very small and slim. It can easily fit in any pocket, even the little credit card one on most jeans. You slide the power to on, let it take a second to get ready, and then you’re all set to start recording. Press the red recording button and talk away. When you’re done, press it again and the recording will stop and save. This little device holds 8 gigs of audio, which is pretty impressive for the price. You can easily play and skip between tracks, It’s easy to learn how to operate the menu, even with the tiny screen, and the included instructions make everything a breeze.

Charge time is fast. After it finally ran out of power, I charged it back to full in about two and a half hours. I have an iMac and when I connected it to the recorder, it didn’t give me any problems. Recordings are saved as .WAV files, as expected.

Unfortunately, when I played back a 10 minute recording I did, the audio skipped several times here and there. It wasn’t terrible, but it was pretty annoying for a word to get messed up for a second. It kinda sounds like when a radio station scratches out any profanity in a song. I tried a few shorter recordings, ranging form 30 seconds to 4 minutes, and eventually something would mess up again. If you’re looking to buy this for interview purposes, I’dgo with something more reliable. And for what it’s worth, the included earbuds are pretty bad. The first time I put them in to listen to something, I actually said “oh no” out loud. The do their job though, and that’s what counts.

I actually feel a little bad about giving this recorder 3 stars. It’s a solid product, very well-made and holds a lot of audio. There are worse products like this out there, so it’s worth trying out if you really need it. I’ll keep it around just for ideas and stuff that I can record for a minute or two.

product_title: Brother MFCJ870 Wireless Color Inkjet All-In-One with Scanner, Copier and Fax Printer
review_headline: Fast, simple AOI with awful noise and flimsy hardware
review_body:
This all-in-one (AIO) from Brother replaces my trusty old Canon MX892 since it stopped printing no matter what I did. I needed something that scans and prints quickly and easily. No use for fax at all. The Brother MFC-J870DW does both well.

GOOD:
- very fast printing. Faster than the Canon.
- good print quality, on par with the Canon
- fast, accurate scans, on par with the Canon
- so far no driver conflicts (Win 7 laptop) or issues.
- replacing cartridges is fast and easy. There is a dedicated small pull-out tray on the front right. With the Canon you had to open the hood and mess around with the cartridges that way
- nice LCD touch screen with intuitive menus
- LCD panel can be swiveled upwards so if you put the Brother on a desk and you're standing up, you won't have to crouch down to see what you're doing.
- much cheaper ink compared to many competitors in this class.
- easy installation and use of Brother drivers and software

BAD:
- it is LOUD. It's so loud, I'm docking this 1 star. It sounds like a 1990's cheap Lexmark printer, but possibly worse. The Canon was not nearly as loud when printing or scanning.
- it's flimsy, so cheaply made, that this deserves another star taken away. Compared to the Canon, this machine feels like something that cost maybe 1/3 as much to manufacture. The lid likes to fall off if you open it to put down paper to copy or scan, there is no way to properly secure it to the rest of the machine (via a closed latch, for example).
When the machine prints, the whole thing shakes a bit. I believe that the flimsiness is part of the reason this device is so loud when it prints. The Canon is a beast, much heavier and bigger, with thicker and better quality hardware that apparently contains much of the noise the printing hardware makes.
The automatic paper tray feeder on the Brother is thin and cheaply made as well. The front paper cassette (takes regular paper and has a separate tray for photo paper) is just shoved in there without any secure mechanism. On the Canon, you slide it in and it "clicks"and stays in place, even during heavy printing sessions or when moving the device itself. Everything about it with the exception of the surprisingly good LCD touch screen control panel, the whole thing feels very cheaply made. Not appropriate for an office with high profile clients judging some of your professionalism on the qualify of your work gear. I also don't see this hold up to regular abuse by multiple co-workers. This really is just fine for occasional use by one person at home/home office.

OTHER/SUMMARY:
Cold boot to print time (time it takes to send the print signal, machine to wake up, and start printing) is about on par with the Canon, possibly a tad faster.
When you turn this machine on for the very first time, it'll go through what appears to be an excessive amount of time "cleaning" (Cleaning what? It's brand new....). That is where the noise starts. You hope it'll get better but it doesn't. This is about the noise level and sound frequency you can expect every time you print with this thing going forward. If this is in your home office, expect to wake family members 2 rooms over. I made the mistake to set it up at 2 AM at my home office and that's exactly what happened. For 10 minutes or so, the Brother would be "cleaning", making noise the entire time.
After this was done, I was able to connect it to the Wifi, which was a very fast and painless process.
Download the newest drivers for your machine directly from Brother.com, don't bother with the included CD. Setup and installation is very easy. Brother has a bundle that contains all drivers and software you need, or you can pick and choose what you want to download and install. The full package is about 143MB
Like all printer manufacturers, the software will put a bunch of icons and shortcuts on yourcomputer and in the tray that you may never use. And, also like most other manufacturers, expect the software and driver to eat up some of your computer resources constantly, whether you're actually doing anything with the device or not. Brother's drivers and software appears to be in line with Canon's printer drivers and utilities in terms of using up background processes. You can also set most of the software like the Control Center, Help, and Status Monitor to not automatically start after you start up your Windows machine.

Printing, scanning, hooking it up to Wifi, and general basic use are all pretty straightforward with the Brother. I haven't tested all features yet but for what I know I need to do regularly (simple prints, simple scans), this machine will do OK.
The excellent printing speed, general ease of use, and low cost of ink make this a very good device for the price. The unacceptable noise when printing and generally flimsy hardware knocks an otherwise excellent rating down 2 notches.

product_title: Casio FX-CP400-L Graphing Calculator
review_body:
A major disappointment. I purchased this calculator because I'm accustomed to using Casio calculators and I like the quality of their products. Well, every chain has a weak link and the Casio FX-CP400 is Casio's weakest. First, I would like to state that I am very comfortable using a stylus and touchscreen and as a person who owns a Casio FX-115ES PLUS, I'm also accustomed to Casio's calculator layout. Neither of those things proved to be helpful. I will describe the problems I encountered as a numbered list.

1. USER GUIDE/DOWNLOAD/INSTALLATION: Casio seems to assume that I have owned this calculator before and that I should already know exactly how and what to install from the installation CD. Yes, it's a CD. I have no complaint there because my computer has a CD drive. Problem is that Casio is not even slightly helpful with telling you how to install, what exactly to install and why. Each time I installed an application, I had to disconnect and reconnect the USB cable or the "Flash memory" could not be found.

2. UNRESPONSIVE TOUCHSCREEN: Twice this calculator's touchscreen became unresponsive. I waited. And waited. Nothing. It would not respond to stylus or finger. My only recourse was to turn the calculator off and on again. Who needs that kind of problem? A touchscreen device with an unresponsive touchscreen is best known by its other name, Paperweight. I paid $140 for a paperweight. Thank goodness for refunds.

3. VARIABLES: The problem here is that I can simplify a polynomial on paper faster than I can enter it into this calculator. Variables are in one tab, numbers are in another tab, fractions and radicals and in a different tab. I spend more time changing tabs than it actually takes to use pencil and paper to solve. The variables should be A-Z on a physical keypad. What's the point of having a stylus if I still have to use the physical keypad to find...wait for it...numbers. Yes, the numbers are the very last tab.

Conclusion: If you're planning on buying this for your children to take to school or use for homework; you're better off sending them to school with an abacus and an Etch-A-Sketch. This calculator will not help them with math, it will further frustrate them. This product is time-consuming and burdensome. I just now learned that this calculator isn't allowed on most test (SAT, ACT, CLEP) while other CAS calculators are allowed. product_title: MCO55937 - Easy Trap Flip Holder, 4quot; X 47quot;
review_headline: The 3M Easy Trap Duster system is the only extra wide alternative ...
review_body:
I do own & use this item, but it was not purchased through Amazon or one of their Marketplace sellers...

The 3M Easy Trap Duster system is the only extra wide disposable sheet alternative to a Swiffer duster I've found, and is twice as wide the the hard-to-find Swiffer XL. There are some significant differences, but you essentially get the same results. The sheets are thinner, use a different material and have some sort of sticky stuff applied. The sheets are perforated in six-inch increments and you use whatever length corresponds to the 24", 36" or 48" flip holder you purchase. The sheets are aggravating to handle, as the sticky stuff gets all over your hands, but the adhesive-type stuff does seem to help in picking up loose particles. Unlike the Swiffer, there are no slots to tuck the sheets into to hold them in place. Instead, the 3M holder has a Velcro-like strip the runs the length of the facing edge of the holder. While this sound like a good thing, there's nothing to hold the sheet onto the holder surface that contacts the floor. If you raise the "broom" up off the floor, there's nothing to keep the sheet from flapping around.

Now to the actual flip holder. It has a terrible design flaw that results in breakage every time. I've gone through four of these 47" versions and they all broke in the same spot where the pivoting handle head is attached by rivets to the long plastic "broom" that holds the sheets. Eventually, the plastic breaks and you are left with the holder part and no way to re-attach the handle.

Overall, I would rate the entire system a bit higher, but the flip holder itself WILL break over time and that's why I rate the holder at two stars. If Swiffer made a four foot version, I'd much prefer it to the 3M. Unfortunately, this seems to be the only choice if you are sweeping a large area and need better pick up of fine particles than you can get with a standard dust mop.

product_title: Pilot BeGreen Precise V5 Rolling Ball Pens
review_body:
Pilot BeGreen V5s are a pleasure to use. The lines are very fine and ink flow is consistent and fast enough to avoid skipping. I'm left-handed and don't have a lot of problems with ink smearing. I like that they are made from 89.2% recycled content. The grip is not the greatest for me but that is totally subjective and everybody has different preferences so your results may vary.

The large green "BEGREEN" section on the pens is a bit over-the-top. It's enough that I know that I bought something that is made from recycled materials. I don't need to advertise it to the world at the expense of the aesthetics of the pen.

I have had these for 10 months and mine still work but I don't write with them daily (for my daily writing I usually reach for a Uni-Ball Signo UM-151). You can also buy ink refills to ensure that you will be using these for a long time to come. They are worth checking out; especially if you already know you like the Precise V5 and are interested in the BeGreen line.

I suspect that the rubber layer is simply too heavy and pulls away from the cushion.  In any case, I now have three Armousepads which are useless.  Incidentally, the stuffing inside the cushion is real sticky.  I tried to tape the seam, but the cushion material won't hold the tape.  I hope they can fix this flaw because, otherwise, I absolutely love the product!

product_title: Alvin Professional Parallel Glider Metric
review_body: I received 2 of the 24 x 36 mats as a birthday gift and my cutting table needed a bit more to cover it entirely.  I had ordered another brand in what was supposed to be 9 x 12 and the brand was not of the quality of Alvin.  These are exactly as described.  The 9 x 12 was exactly 9 x 12.  I also check that the markings on the mats are exact and the Alvin brand is.  Even more impressive, once you line them up side by side, the distance between the markings across the mats is also exactly right.  When side by side, the edge marking on one mat is 1 inch distance to the edge marking across to the next.  You do need to line up the mats to be the same direction.  I set the logo to be in the upper left as each one is laid out on the table.  That's a very, very good indication of quality.  The other brand was not even 9 x 12 - it was not quite 8 3/4 by 11 and the markings weren't properly spaced meaning they failed the 'ruler' test.  I can recommend this brand without any hesitation.  I did have to leave the large mats out for a full 24 hours to air out.  Note:  For those new to cutting mats, the dimensions of cutting mats refers to the overall dimensions and not the lengths that the markings go out to.  A 9 x 12 mat will have marking lines for 8 x 11 or should have.  I also recommend using a trusted ruler or measuring tape to double check any mats markings to make sure they are true.  Thanks to trial and error over the years, I learned not to assume they are.

TLDR:
+Plastic does not feel cheap
+Worth the price
+Does not break easy, though it is definitely ~possible~ due to plastic upper body
+RETRACTABLE AND POCKET SAFE
+Attractive challenger the the Pentel Graphgear 1000
+WAY cheaper than Rotring, which is more likely to break at the tip than the body.
-Upper is plastic
-Like all graphing pencils the eraser is not great, opt for a click pen eraser or a MARS plastic block eraser.
-The screw on tip (not the pipe) can become loose on occasion though it is rare and has never fallen off, and also has long threads inside to prevent this. I have attached a photo to show both the length of the screw with the piece removed to show just how hard it would be for it to fall, and to show the length of the pencil compared to a Lamy safari and an eraser.
-I wish the upper was aluminum so it was stronger without losing is forward heavy weight.

I wanted to wait a month or two before reviewing this, and I have found that it is of surprising quality. Many of you have heard of the declining quality of Rotring since the 90s and as such I opted for this in place of the Rotring 800 which is substantially more expensive. The Rotring 600 is only slightly more expensive though the lack of a retractable causes problems for people like me- the people that SHOULD be these brands target markets as we write infinitely more than almost any profession- and that is students. I carry a Lamy Safari, Clic-Erase pen eraser, and this pencil with me constantly. The wobble mentioned was all but absent. I really did not notice any play, though it does rattle near the eraser, it does not do so when writing, only when shaken while in the deployed position. The shift mechanism is sure and effective. The plastic upper feels quality and has a nice matte finish. This light upper leaves the weight at the bottom which I actually prefer. While it may not be quite as rigid, solid, or hardy as some expensive fixed pipe pencils it ties the Pentel Graphgear 1000 for best low-price pencil, sacrificing the metal upper for a better grip, and much better aesthetics. The shift mechanism is absurdly good and due the "Z" shape of the track it can be deployed and closed in one fluid motion and stays locked (provided you fasten it entirely, don't pin human error on the product.) The mechanism should be standard for retractable pencils in my opinion. -This version, while well-tested and known to be reliable, is an older model that uses a CC for illumination. As such, the CC contains mercury and requires special disposal at end of life. A newer, fancier version of this scanner uses LEDs, but it also retails for about $1K!

review_body: I have a Pro 715 and these work great!  I can't vouch for this vender, I purchased mine from Walmart website and have had no problems at all. It's where your printer will print various patterns. If they don't print properly...do a head cleaning. Some people don't like to do that, since the process uses ink...but it works most of the time. I will certainly purchase more of these cartridges in the future. Lexmark is just too expensive and I've gotten bad cartridges  buying directly from them as well. This is a good set to try the cartridges out. Buy them from Wally World since they have a physical store and take them back if it doesn't work for you.

product_title: AT&T dect_6.0 1-Handset Landline Telephone
review_body: I love this phone!  I've had several cordless phones over the years but none come close to this one for features and ease of use.  I especially love the caller ID announce, which gives you the name of the person calling once it shows up on your caller ID.  It makes it so easy to know who it is before you get up and go to the phone and realize it is NOT someone you want to talk to.  I also like the feature that allows you to turn off the ringer and direct calls directly to the answering machine during certain hours, like when you're in bed or eating.  This is also one of the few cordless phones/answering machines I've seen that is actually wall-mountable, although the base is more than slip-resistant enough to place on a desk or other flat surface without it sliding around every time you pick up the phone or check the answerer.  The screen is plenty large and clear for older, not so good eyes and the screen and numbers light up for easy use during low light times, like at night. product_title: Brother Printer MFC-L8850CDW Wireless Color Laser Printer with S Copier and Fax,
review_body:
My previous color laser printer was also a Brother (MFC-9440CN), so I expected the MFC-L8850CDW to be just as good and hopefully a little faster. It surpassed my expectations by an order of magnitude and it's THE fastest color laser printer I've ever seen. The print quality is superb too and the automatic duplexing works flawlessly. My girlfriend needed to scan a 30+ page, double-sided document that was primarily black & white, and this printer scanned and printed every page flawlessly and so fast I couldn't believe it.

It is also a LOT quieter than my MFC-9440CN printer, which is/was a LOT louder and took forever to warm up. The MFC-L8850CDW warms quickly and is rather quiet, in terms of large printers. I also ordered a full set of the high capacity toner cartridges at the same time I ordered this printer. Brother quality cannot be beaten and during the 4+ years I used the MFC-9440CN, I never had a single problem with either the printer or the Brother brand toner cartridges.

My Brother MFC-9440CN color laser printer was still working fine when I ordered the MFC-L8850CDW printer, but it needed a whole new set of toner cartridges, so I decided to bite the bullet and go with a newer/faster model. I could NOT be happier with this printer. It's FAST, the print quality is absolutely perfect, the auto duplex feature works flawlessly, faxing works flawlessly, as does walk-up copying of documents. The scanner is REALLY fast and produces very high resolution images in Photoshop.

One of my favorite things about this printer is that it's not nearly as heavy as the MFC-9440CN. That thing is a boat anchor but the MFC-L8850CDW isn't nearly as heavy. I took it out of the box and set it on our printer table all by myself ... and I'm 62 years old (young!). I had ZERO issues installing the software from the CD and since I'm very familiar with Brother's well designed user interfaces and menus, I had no issues configuring all the settings to MY specifications.

I can HIGHLY recommend Brother color laser printers to anyone who might need one. I recommended one to my 85 year old neighbor, he bought one of their small office color laser printers online, and he couldn't be happier with his buying decision. My girlfriend's brother is an attorney in California, and Brother printers are the ONLY printers he buys and uses, both in his office and at home. I'm just as sold as he is.

Shipping was incredibly quick and I had my new Brother printer within a couple of days of placing the order. Amazing. It's a BIG box and it comes very well packed and protected. The documentation says you should get someone to help you take it out of the box, although I didn't need to. For you lady's out there, I recommend getting someone to help you. It's not light at all and you might just break a nail.

I would buy this printer again in a heartbeat. There's NOTHING I can complain about with this printer. It's a Brother, "the best" is what I always expect from them, and so far, that's exactly what I've gotten. GREAT printers!

product_title: Sale !!! H&L Office Mid Back Mesh Executive & Managerial Computer Desk Swivel Office Chair with Headrest and Flexible Arm Rest
review_body:
This is the worst "executive chair" I have ever seen. Everything up the the armrests is fine, but the back of the chair makes it impossible to sit in properly. It is not uncomfortable, it is impossible to sit in. In short, NO lumbar support, no shoulder support, headrest is where your ears should be.

Starting from the bottom up. The lumbar support you see in the picture is literally just for show. It is a hard plastic panel that cuts across the back of the chair frame so it is a good 5 inches from the fabric. If the mesh gave way enough to use this, the mesh would break and it would be terribly uncomfortable anyway.

The upper part of the back curves back so far that if you put your weight on it properly you'd be staring at the ceiling.

The headrest, oh my goodness. It is the farthest forward part of the chair back by at least an inch and is not adjustable. For a 6' person with good posture the headrest in its highest position digs into my shoulder blades. All the edges of it are hard plastic so however you angle the headrest it will dig into something. Rotated all the way up you can finally sit mostly right, but now the plastic edge digs into the bones of your lower neck.

Based on some of the "it is fine" kind of reviews they must have changed this chair to make it into a torture device recently, because everyone in my office tried it and all agreed it was the worst chair they'd ever tried to use. The uselessness of the headrest is really not a matter of opinion. Without it the back leaning way back and lack of lumbar support makes it a sad but functional task chair, making it worth about $20.

Do not buy.

product_title: Tel-Sentry V2.2 Smart Automatic Blocking, Block All Spam Calls, Election Calls without Relying on Black List
review_body:
Included with the call blocker are the instructions (including a version 2 supplement) and a phone line cable. Two AAA batteries are needed for the device but not included.

After discovering my telephone’s ability to block soliciting was limited to twenty numbers, I have been in search of a solution for the harassing phone calls that come daily. I have tried a couple different blocking solutions and I have yet to find one that has all the features I am wanting. So how does this Tel-Sentry blocker stack up? This is the 2nd version of this blocker and since I did not try the first, I cannot say exactly what differences or improvements were made and I can only comment on this version versus my experience with others.

Since I have a phone that the instructions recommend the parallel setup, I connected that way. My phone service is through a cable company operating through a cable telephone modem but working through my standard phone line outlets with a phone that is one main base and 5 cordless headsets. The blocker is connected to that main wired phone base through the splitter in order to maintain my caller ID. I can’t say how well this will work with other phone types and telephone providers.

The instructions are pretty basic and I think lacks some details but it is sufficient at getting everything set up. The call blocker has an Accept and Reject button which can be used to create a known “good” caller list and a bad “black” list. You can program a “good” list into the blocker but I found that a bit more work since there is no ten digit keyboard. In addition there is a mode for callers not on either list that force callers to go through a process that gives a warning to get through to you. The warning voice can be put in English/Spanish or German. Luckily you can disable that mode completely. In this case, I think the device is a bit too complex and unnecessary with some features. I would prefer not adding a good list as most of those are programmed into the phone book of my phone and don’t feel it is necessary to add them into the device. An easy way to program numbers with a numeric keyboard that you already know as solicitors to me is more beneficial than programming a good list and having an accept button. These days most callers, even those that know you will not wait to get through by pressing 0 and will just hang up.

The device itself is good quality with sturdy buttons and does effectively block numbers. This blocker has the ability to block (and accept) up to 9999 numbers each which should be sufficient for a long time. The display is clear and easy to read with the display indicating the number of accepted calls/rejected calls, date and time, and whether voice warning message is selected or off. The device has 6 buttons, including the voice warning selector, accept, reject, home and arrow keys. The buttons are clearly marked. Even with my issues with the device, it is fairly easy to use and even more so if you disable the advance mode, which turns off the warning voice and allows this to be used just as a blocker.

This device works well as a blocker but I think needs to add an easier way to add numbers you want to block (such as adding a keypad on the device) and the white list I don’t really think is necessary as most people already have those numbers programmed into their phone. I am also not crazy about the voice warning message but at least that can be disabled.

This write-on 5-tab divider for classification folders is a heavy duty cardstock with reinforced holes. They hold up well to the up and down motion of checking paperwork. They also hold up well to the riggers of adding paperwork to the classification folder. Because the holes are reinforced with copper, they are more durable and hold up to more wear.

product_title: Pilot Namiki Falcon Collection Fountain Pen
review_headline: The Pilot Namiki Falcon I order was the Fine Nib in silver Rhodium trim
review_body:
I'm fairly new to the fountain pen community so please take this review for what it's worth. The Pilot Namiki Falcon I order was the Fine Nib in silver Rhodium trim. The pen is VERY light. If you're someone who prefers pens with weight, this isn't the pen for you. But for those who do not mind light weight pens, you can write for hours with minimal to no fatigue. The flexibility of the nib is about what I expected, based on the various reviews I've read as well as the videos I've seen on youtube about this pen. However, at first it was a little stiffer than I initially assumed it would be. I'm in the middle of learning Spencerian writing, which is one of the reasons why I was interested in this pen. I was looking for something I could use as an every day writer as well as add a bit of flare to my handwriting. Some reviews have reported concerns of the pen skipping, or railroading. From my personal experience so far, this had only occurred when I was flexing the nibs to it's maximum width for thick lines. It doesn't happen often, but it can happen from time to time and only if you're trying to create the maximum thick lines the pen would allow. Outside of this, the pen writes like a dream without skipping once.

The ink flow is fairly quick and wet, but not overly so. And the nib feels quite smooth on quality paper.

The only reason this pen doesn't get 5 stars is because of 2 things. The first being the ink capacity. The cartridge converter that comes with the pen does not hold a lot of ink, which is disappointing. If you write a lot, as in if you're a student or writing is a part of your job, you will have to refill ink in the pen before the day is out, at least once. The second reason is more of a personal taste. The Fine Nib isn't as fine as I had hoped. For something like this, I was hoping for a really fine line that was thinner than what this nib provided. So I'm currently in the middle of returning this one and purchasing one with an Extra Fine nib.

However, I'm quite sure that for most people, this nib would suit them all right. Amongst fountain pen owners, this may be common knowledge, but for the rest of you who may not know, the Japanese pens tend to have nibs that are almost one size smaller than the western nibs. This would mean that a Japanese Medium nib would be closer to a Western Fine nib and a Japanese Fine nib being closer to a Western Extra Fine nib. Now this does not mean it's a one to one correlation. You'd have to get the exact measurements of line thickness to be sure of what to expect. So please be aware.

In any case, I do love this pen and I'm looking forward to getting it in an Extra Fine nib. I hope this review helps.Fine nib.

product_title: Epson WorkForce WF-2630 All-In-One Wireless Color Printer with Scanner, Copier and Fax
review_headline: Pretty average at everything except at guzzling ink.
review_body:
After having the WF-2650 for about a month I feel it has some good and bad points.
* Setup was pretty easy even for a tech shy senior like me. I did use a cable rather than a wireless setup since it was easier for me.
* I love the enclosed paper feed tray. It keeps the paper neat and avoids the problems of a top feed where sometimes a foreign object would fall in.
* The unit does not take up much space, fits easily on top of a 2 drawer file next to my desk.
* it is certainly not the quietest unit when printing but is tolerable. Print speed on B&W is pretty fast.
*The print quality is good but not exceptional. After using both the scanner and printer functions I feel it is kind of average. Have not used it on Photos yet.
*The ink cartridges appear exceptionally small. I have printed between 30 and 50 pages of mostly E Mails and it is already calling for me to replace the
Black ink cartridge. After getting a pretty good amount of pages from my Canon MP 460 this is a disappointment. Could prove expensive.
Overall it is a decent machine for the money. It does about everything you could want in a personal or perhaps very small office environment. I guess I am just kind of bummed by how few pages it prints on a cartridge. I could understand it more if I were printing very high quality documents buy all of my use has been on average looking E Mails.
Bottom line is if I had to replace this unit tomorrow I would probably be doing a lot more research on other machines.

review_headline: I've used a lot of mechanical pencils, and this is by far the best.
review_body: As an engineer, I write A LOT. I've tried every mechanical pencil imaginable. It's almost a fetish. I have hundreds at my home. I'm a big fan of the [[ASIN:B000GAU2RU Pentel Graph Gear 1000 Automatic Drafting Pencil, 0.5mm Lead Size, Brushed Metal Barrel, 1 Each (PG1015A)]] for drawing or drafting. I find that the tip of its cousin, the [[ASIN:B000SBSAYE Pentel Sharp Automatic Pencil, 0.5mm, Black Barrels, 2 Pack (P205BP2-K6)]] series will become loose and wobbly and slippery when sweaty. , When I need to write fast or make calculations, I prefer the Pentel Sharplet-2. This is the best of Pentel's line, in my opinion.  It has a simple design and it's really the only pencil I've been able to use for extensive periods without being uncomfortable. If you're a student or write a lot, this would be the only pencil I recommend. (Eraser refills can be found readily on Prime [[ASIN:B000TY06T2 Pentel Mechanical Pencil Eraser Refills, Z21, 3/Tube, PK - PENZ21]] but you should probably be using a dedicated eraser such as the [[ASIN:B001Q4HQVU Pentel Hi-polymer Block Eraser, Large, 3 Pack, White  (ZEH10BP3-K6)]] or if you prefer stick type [[ASIN:B0006HXI74 Paper Mate Tuff Stuff Eraser Stick (SN64801)]] and its respective refills [[ASIN:B001PMJUA8 Paper Mate Tuff Stuff Eraser Refill, Small, White]] all of which work great and are available through Prime or as an add-on.)  It has an eraser cover, which I usually leave on because it adds a slight bit of weight that provides a nice balance for the pencil, it also reminds me to use a dedicated eraser because you'll burn up the included one rather quickly. I also leave on the pocket clip mainly because I use it and keep the pencil in my front pocket, but I also find it harmonizes the balance of the pencil and provides a nice area for the pencil to rest between my thumb and finger.  The end screws on very firmly and I haven't had a problem with it coming loose. The blue/black is a nice color scheme (.5 is black/black and .9 is yellow/brown). If you write a lot like me and own a plethora of mechanical pencils, the Pentel Super Hi-Polymer bulk pack of lead refills is a good bargain [[ASIN:B000DN86RS Pentel Super Hi-Polymer Lead Refill, 0.7mm Medium, 2B, 144 Pieces of Lead (50-2B)]] and will last you a lifetime. (Be sure to choose appropriate hardness, HB is standard - I have used up to 4H in this pencil)  I prefer the .7mm because I write heavy and like dark marks. I do however, frequently use the .5 and .9mm for different applications. I use the .5mm when I need more precision such as drawing free body diagrams, or engineering sketches. I use the .9mm when working in the oilfield sometimes wearing impact gloves and writing in a tally book.  Lastly, if you're buying the bulk 12-pack, they come with a sticker on each pencil that leaves a bit of residue that may take some goo-gone or cleaner to remove.

product_title: TOOGOO(R) HERO 616 Fountain Pen Hooded Golden Nib Black Barrel Small Vintage
review_body:
It is an Okay pen for a good price. Please do not buy this pen if you have not ever tried fountain pen and/or want to get the first pen. This is NOT how a good fountain pen feels like. And remember, that this is a cheap Chinese Parker 51 look-alike, so do not expect high quality here.

I bought this pen because I was looking for a cheap light pen i could take with me without any worry to lose it or brake it.

It arrived nearly 1 month after I bought it (I do not know exact period) - no tracking available. It was reasonably packaged. Arrived with no damage, which is very nice.

The pen itself looks good. If you do not mind the cap, it looks 7/10. The cap is not bad either, but the clip is really sharp (it is a copy of the Parker Arrow) and is crafted poorly.

Pen is easy to disassemble (good thing) and is very easy to clean (it has a sac. It is not as easy to clean as a converter, but is not much harder either). Mine was very scratchy, and very wet. Tuning the nib to get reasonable result took more than an hour (I am not the most experienced tuner, but the pen was too cheap to take to any specialist). product_title: Hot Newest Ipad 2/3/4 Case Shockproof Rugged Hybrid Armor Series Dual Layer Protection Case with KickStand and Built-in Screen Protector for Apple Ipad 2/3/4 (Red)
review_headline: Great protection for a good price, with a few knocks.
review_body:
I'll start with the pros...
Fits the iPad 2 like a glove, very rugged and probably could take a great deal of shock or a good drop. Bought this to put on our kids' iPad and it has weathered some abuse and came out strong. I have taken it apart once to clean it and check the iPad inside, and the iPad looks like the day we bought it. It completely encases your tablet save for the camera holes, charging/data port, headphone jack, speaker and mic holes and a hole to reach the volume lock switch. It has a nice kickstand (which only works in landscape orientation, not portrait). The buttons all function pretty well. I will also say that despite the screen protector not being a cling or attached to the screen by adhesive, the touch screen is still quite responsive.

Now for the cons...
First of all, ours didn't come with instructions on how to put it on... It's not brain surgery, but it does take some light engineering skills making sure you get the tabs in the right places (one of which broke when taking it apart to clean it) and the silicone wrap pushed in everywhere it needs to be. Also, without the instructions, it made remembering how I put it together tricky, couldn't remember how to deconstruct it and fumbled with it for a while during the aforementioned cleaning. The headphone jack, which is located on the top edge of the iPad, is situated at one of the thickest parts of the case, and some of those 90 degree type headphone connectors might not work perfectly, although we don't use headphones with it much, so I can't say for sure. Not impressed with the screen protector either (it's a thick plastic film and is NOT affixed to the screen itself, but rather is part of the case) and lacks the clarity of a glass or cling type screen protector. I'm considering cutting out their plastic screen protector and getting some tech glass for it. Lastly, we bought the "red" version of this, which is kind of red but in certain light almost looks more of a magenta in my opinion.

All in all, I would definitely purchase this again. You get an extreme level of protection for an expensive iPad at a great price and the good far outweighs the bad.

Tip for those who already own one of these and need to take it apart to clean it. On the screen side of the iPad, gently pry the red silicone away from the black plastic so you can lift up and unseat the little tabs (4 in all) that are near the corners on the longer sides of the screen. Once you have all 4 tabs out, you should be able to unclip the black plastic screen protector from it (at the middle of all 4 sides), remove it and the rest should be fairly self explanatory.s more of a magenta in my opinion.

All in all, I would definitely purchase this again. You get an extreme level of protection for an expensive iPad at a great price and the good far outweighs the bad.

review_headline: good for gel pens, don't last as long as regular ballpoints, though
review_body:
These are some of the better gel pens I have used (I have several of the red "fine point" ones on my desk). The tips don't get gummy and the grip is comfortable. The lines formed are clean and crisp without any bleeding and, unlike felt-tip pens, the shape of the tips doesn't get distorted over time (since these tips are metal). The "fine point" ones do not make the thinnest line ever, but they're an excellent thickness for proofreading documents -- dark and thick enough to show up even if all you're doing is adding a missing comma.

I have not yet been able to break any of the plastic clips on the sides of these pens (I play with pens and have broken the clips on a lot of other pens, so this is actually a concern to me). The pens like this that I have used have not bled or leaked. I think the ink dries quickly and without smudging. To be fair, I have only used these on regular "office" type paper (i.e., no glossy finish). Mostly I use them to mark up printouts of documents, either to make note of important passages or to edit/proofread.

However, like all gel pens that I have ever used, they seem to run out of ink or stop working sooner than I would expect -- that is, when there is still a visible amount of ink left. These last longer than most gel pens I've tried, and the writing is very smooth when they work, but I do often have to throw them away when they seem like they should still be good.

review_body: we had a working HP MFP laserjet but wanted to upgrade to color. AirPrint from my Ipad/iphone works well.  paper makes a diff as well so I buy the heavier, 24 lb HP Laserjet paper,  98 bright, glossy finish so that we can duplex. yes, gotta love the duplex feature, saves paper and make it more professional.  you don't have to use HP paper but I just happened to like it.  We also accidentally discover you can print great glossy photos using Canon Selphy paper.  it looks like Costco finish, very close to the Dye Sub technology of the Selphy printers.  good enough for passport and ID.  of course color copy works great. we don't use the fax function.  big investment, yes; is it worth it, totally!

product_title: Brother P-touch PTP750W Wireless Label Maker
review_headline: Works great if you get it all installed...
review_body:
This printer works great once installed. Installation on a computer is horrible. ABSOLUTELY HORRIBLE. But once you get it installed to your liking it does work very well. I'm still giving it 4/5 stars overall, but I know that many people will never get past the install. You can still us wifi direct from a phone and P-lite software on a computer with a usb cable even if you don't go through the horrible software.

I know this is a book and a half, but this is not only a review but also a help for getting going with this. Let me explain the easy ways first:

The manual talks about wifi direct and putting the printer on your wifi network. Basically wifi direct means disconnecting your phone/tablet/computer from the internet and connecting directly wireless to the printer. If you put the printer on your network, it's a lot easier to print from you phone/phones because you don't have to disconnect from your normal wifi and connect to your printer. But to put the printer on wifi means the complicated install. If wifi direct and phone/tablet are your only devices, it might be worth the hassle and works very well. I only have an iphone so I've not tried the NFC, but it looks like the NFC is only a shortcut to downloading the app and doesn't have anything at all to do with connecting.

You can also plug into your computer with a USB cable and almost immediately use the P-lite software that is included on the printer itself as a "usb drive" built into the printer. You don't have to install anything. Unfortunately, this P-lite software has the least amount of features and wastes more tape than the phone app or the full computer software. You have to have almost an inch at the beginning of the label before your type starts and unless you play with it, it wants an inch at the end too. It's ok to print a quick label on a new computer, but I wouldn't want it all the time.

So that's wifi direct and P-lite. The third way to use this is to connect it to your wifi router and use it as a network printer. You still use the same app on phones/tablets but you don't have to reconnect to it to print a label. Multiple computers/phones/tablets can also all use the label printer as long as they're on the same network. You can use the full feature computer label software through wifi. It all works nice once you get it going! IF you get it going.... (Dun, DUN, DUUUNNN)

******************INSTALLING THE SOFTWARE******************
There's no disk included. The manual says to go to "http://support.brother.com" which then you have to find the support section for this PT-P750W printer. It took me, a computer tech, more than an hour to get this going on a wifi network. It's completely ridiculous! I don't even understand what brother was thinking. There is no one file complete install and update like every other printer I've installed in the last 5 years. You have to download all these separate programs and figure out which ones you need. What the crap? If you aren't techy, and wifi-direct/P-lite isn't good enough for you, expect to hire a tech to set this up for you. The installation is zero out of 5 stars. Yes, it's that bad. There are holes in the instructions and you just have to install many stupid things.

I've only installed it on a windows 7 pc, but it seems to be the same installation files for Vista, Windows 7, Windows 8, and Windows server. There is no XP support. The Mac files are different and seem to be packaged together some, but I can't help you there.

Unless you only want to do wifi direct from an iphone or just use the P-touch lite software, you need to install the ones in the "you should install" section below. To set up the printer on your wifi network, you have to install the driver and printer settings tool on a windows computer first. There is no way to connect the printer to a wifi network using only a phone/tablet (might be able to do wifidirect and then open a browser and browse the printer wifi direct ip--so convoluted that I'm not going to try).

You should install these 3 on your windows computer:
Printer Driver -- in the middle of the install it will ask you to plug in (with usb) and turn on the printer. Also make sure the P-lite green light is off. Press the Plite button to turn it off or this will not work. Yes, you have to have the usb printer driver installed on a computer to be able to setup the printer on a wifi network with the "Printer Settings Tool". You can use the printer as a usb printer only using the full P-touch editor on one computer (and then skip the Printer Settings tool). I hate how much explaining this takes.

Printer Settings tool: It doesn't even say this is what you use to set the printer up on a wifi network, but that's what this is! This doesn't work unless the printer driver is installed and the printer is plugged into a usb port on your computer (and turned on). This is how you configure the wireless and update the wireless direct password.
You really need to be able to set this up as a static ip on your network if you're going to be putting it on your network and printing from phone/tablet. The phone/tablet app will not find your label printer on the network and so you have to be able to input the ip and if you don't set a static ip, the ip number can change. Really if you have no idea what I just said, you may need a tech to set this up on your network. If you don't know how to set your printer ip to static, you can see what your printer's current ip is in this tool on the "wireless lan" tab under status. At least on the iphone/ipad version you put the ip address by going to the gear, click on printer, choose the PT-P750W, click set manually at the top, and put your printer's ip. Yes this is all horribly convoluted.
One of the reasons others are saying the printer won't stay on wifi is probably because of a changing ip. The other reason is because the printer has an auto shutoff after a set period of idle time. You can also set how long after use the printer powers off in this Printer Settings Tool. This doesn't seem to be a printer that's meant to run 24/7. the longest setting on the "auto power off when AC adapter is connected" is 12 hours. The default is one hour. It's not sleep mode, the printer will just literally turn off.

P-touch Editor5.x -- Many more features than the lite one on the printer itself. Someone better than the phone/tablet version but comparable still.

Other things you can install:
P-touch Update software -- enables you to download the latest updates for your printer firmware and the P-lite software.

Things you don't need to install but are in this printer's software list:
-Driver Deployment wizard. Not sure exactly how it's supposed to work. Comes with no instructions. Really don't understand it or it's use and lost interest by the time I got to this.
-BRAdmin Light and BRAdmin Professional- I only used the professional version but these seem to be tools for configuring a brother network printer that's already on your network. What? Yes they have a separate utility to configure brother printers after they've been on the network. I just don't understand why this is here--just use the Printer Settings tool. Again, I lost interest by the time I got to this.
-Firmware Update Tool and P-Touch Editor Lite Update Tool -- I did these, but it seems that the P-touch Update Software will run a check to see if there are new firmware/lite editor updates and install them for you. That's much easier that downloading them individually. Since I had no instructions or guidance, I did things the long way.

***************the Printing review******************
So if you can get it installed it works great. You can print nice looking labels and there are lots of options in the full software. You canpick fonts, add pictures, etc. Everything looks kinda jaggy till you turn on high resolution, but then it prints a little slower. I think the slower is worth the better labels. It's still not amazing laser sharp, but it's a lot better.

The templates in the full software are kinda weird. There is a spices section that has 8 spices (including salt and pepper). You can't edit the words on these templates either. If you want us to print spices labels, at least give us a full set or some generic ones we can edit... There is a good mix of professional, hobby, and personal use labels but some of the choices are just weird. I think if more of the labels had an editable text spot that they could be more useful rather than being a one use template.

There are a lot of color choices for the labels themselves. They're all two color labels. There is a background color and a text color. There's colors on white, black on clear, and color on color. There are specialty tapes for iron on labels or tamper evident labels. And there are label tapes from an eighth inch to an inch wide (the 1.5 inches wide labels won't fit). None of the brother label cartridges are cheap, but at least there's a good variety.

***************Conclusion***************************
If you can get this installed it's a nice printer. My wife is using it a lot these days. If you don't need tablet/phone support or network sharing, you can the get usb only wired printer for about half what this costs and with a much easier setup (Brother PT-P700). I've installed a lot of brother printers and it's been years since I've seen a printer that was so complicated to install.
