product_title: Alvin DM03 Draft-Matic Mechanical Pencil .3mm
review_headline: I highly recommend this mechanical pencil to anyone searching for a reliable
review_body:
I highly recommend this mechanical pencil to anyone searching for a reliable, long-lasting, and precise writing, drawing, or drafting utensil. I have been using this Alvin Draft/Matic model in all types of applications for over a decade now and I honestly can not imagine myself switching to one of the various competitors that I have tried. In the eleven years that I have been using this device I have owned two, the first of which I sadly lost a couple months after buying it and the second one is currently sitting on my desk.
I was first exposed to this mechanical pencil by my sister while she was studying to be an architect in college. It was an indispensable tool of her's while she was learning how to draft. At that same time I was studying ceramics and I would often borrow her 0.3mm Alvin Draft/Matic to make rough sketches of sculptures or pottery that I wanted to create. I loved how precise I could get with the 0.3mm tip so I quickly purchased one of my own and since then I have been using it for almost everything.
Throughout the years I have tried various other brands of 0.3mm mechanical pencils such as Staedtler, Pentel, and Uni. Each pencil had it's own various perks but in my mind none of them seemed to standup to the Alvin Draft/Matic's feel and quality. This is why I strongly recommend this model to anyone in search of a reliable, long-lasting 0.3mm mechanical pencil.

Pros:
It is built of rock-solid construction.
The pencil has a very precise tip/nib with a good barrel length.
It has an excellent grip even with sweaty fingers.
Very long life.
Thoughtful features: lead density indicator, nib-clearing needle hidden in eraser, protective cap for eraser.
Good weight and balance.
Does not produce unnecessary fatigue of the fingers or hand.

Cons:
Lead density indicator is somewhat loose making it easy to accidentally adjust.
Non-retractable tip is easily bent if the pencil is droppedhowever it easily bends back.
Somewhat useless eraser is only good for emergency use.
Although not necessarily a fault of the pencil, it can be quite difficult to find 0.3mm lead as well as replacement erasers. I generally go to drafting/blueprint shops or art supply stores.

I tried all of the recommended after market toners for the Xerox and found none that would do color without caking up or smearing. It must need a very specific temp for fusing properly. This Brother printer has turned out to be the workhorse. The genuine toner does a much higher page count than the Xerox and it is cheaper. It has also done well on aftermarket toner. Although I did have one aftermarket black cartridge that got tossed last week as it would leak toner and was dumping black ink throughout the print job which was totally unacceptable. My next printer will be another Brother.

product_title: Outop Colorful Pen
review_headline: Bright colors, but scratchy/inconsistent ink flow. Good for gifting/casual use.
review_body:
The pens arrived a few days earlier than I had expected them to, so that was great!

The pens, quality-wise, were not up to my expectations, though I should have seen that coming from reading the other reviews.

Pros:
* Bright, vivid colors!
* There are twelve of them!
* Cute design, I love how the pen-tip area looks like a crystal.

Cons:
* The pen-tip area keeps unscrewing. It seems very loose, so I keep having to stop writing to twist it back on tighter.
* Very scratchy, so you can't write continuously. Many times I'd have to stop writing and scribble on a piece of scrap paper to get the ink flowing again.
* The ink comes out unevenly. Sometimes it comes out very light because it's stuck, and then it comes out like a "spill" and bleeds through the paper.

My overall impression: I'd use these pens for casual use. Since they're inconsistent and don't write smoothly, I wouldn't use them for any serious projects. The colors are bright and cheerful though, and the pens are cute, and the pens aren't that expensive either. If you were thinking about a cute gift for a friend, this would be it!

product_title: Wolverine F2D Super 20MP 4-In-1 Film to Digital Converter, Convert 35mm, 126, 110 and Super 8 into digital in seconds.
review_body:
When I opened up this package, this device looked like a rather inexpensive toy, almost like a toy block a kid would toss around. It's made of a lightweight plastic and doesn't feel like it has a powerful scanner or digital converter, but it does exactly what it says it does. All I have to test with it are 35mm slides, but it does accommodate 120 and others according to the description and does come with the necessary accessories. There are two different slide cartridges that you slip your negative into and simply slide the cartridge into the unit and with a couple of clicks, you've captured the image which is saved to the unit's internal memory. There's also a convert button which loads the images directly to your computer.

When I first plugged the unit to my pc via the accompanied USB cable, the pc did not initially recognize the device and you couldn't see it as a drive option that you could click on, but after I converted several photos to my pc, eventually it did show up as a "No_Name" external drive without the need to download any software. There are no disks or setup software like a printer so it doesn't show up in my options as a Wolverine scanner or anything other than "No Name", however in the printer setup page, my PC does recognize the device as "Coach 100".

As for photo quality, it looks exactly as I imagined it would. Most of my negatives are old school from 10-20 years ago so I suspect the faded quality is from the age and condition of the negatives and not the conversion from this device. The colors are slightly muted but there are some simple color enhancement options for red blue and green that you likely won't use since they drastically alter the negative's image.

Overall, it's very simple to use, almost too simple since the buttons are used to click back and forth. Initially, it's a bit confusing because there isn't a "Go back" button as you're clicking through the optionsand I found myself accidentally powering off the device before I figured out how to return to the previous menu, but I worked through the quirks. Capturing each individual negative is going to take a really long time to convert, especially if you have a string of images on a negative, however, and it would have been ideal if the device took the whole slide with 4 or 5 images on it and scanned them through. That's not the case, but it's a simple load, adjust and convert functionality.

review_headline: Unreliable, difficult to set up and use, arrogant customer service.
review_body:
After about 2 weeks of use, the scanning/copying unit broke. Now, scanned images come out blank, as do copies. Customer service failed to fix the problem over the phone. Returning is impractical for us, and we would not want to rely on a unit with inherent problems. So, will use it for printing (while it still works) and purchase another unit for scanning and copying.

Other difficulties we encountered so far:

1. Printer visibly chews up envelopes. A workaround we tried is to use custom paper size, manually enter the size of the envelopes and choose one of the heavier papers. Still envelopes get chewed up and printing is misaligned. Not a great first impression.

2. It took us several attempts to install updated drivers and firmware. We followed all steps carefully. Software finally decided to work, we hope it lasts longer than the scanner part.

3. Customer service seemed to us to be following a script and wasting time, taking 15 minutes to collect useless info before we even got to fixing anything. The agent interrupted me several times when I was speaking and told me to let her speak.

Conclusion: We had nothing but trouble with our unit. Would not consider buying again. If you think the above problems will not happen to you, we wish you the best of luck.

product_title: Digital Galaxy HDMI 720P HD Video,   2800Lumens, 5-Inch TFT LCD Panel, 70W LED Lamp LCD Projector (DG-757)
review_headline: It's awesome to have a few friends over and be able ...
review_body:
I bought this projector somewhere around JUN2013. It's now MAR2015 and the projector is still running strong on its original bulb. It's true that the picture isn't absolutely stunning, but as a 22 year old guy with no wife or kids, it fits my needs perfectly. I have it hooked up in the living room sitting on a book shelf and connected via some splitters to a wide variety of consoles from the original NES to the PS3/360/Wii U and it plays all of them perfectly. It's awesome to have a few friends over and be able to play a game like Mario Kart where each of us has a portion of the screen that's bigger than any other TV most of us own.

My only real complaint is that the channel searching feature for cable TV didn't seem to work for me. Instead, I had to manually figure out what frequency the channels were on and put them in manually. This was a bit of a pain, but I don't really watch that much TV anyways and it remembers your channels even after having the power removed from it, so I don't really care.

Entering text is extremely tedious, especially when you are trying to type function names, which are case sensitive.

review_headline: Better than 3800 Epson, maybe better than 3880
review_body: Pro 10 replaces an Epson 3800.   Pro-10 replaces an Epson 3800. Friends have the same problems with 3880 that I had with 3800. Those Epsons and this Canon seem to produce equally good prints (Canon supposedly has a fine detail advantage but I can't see it).  Canon paper transport is obviously far more reliable than Epson with a variety of soft and hard-surfaced papers. Canon seems a lot slower. Canon's wireless has been too much hassle so I've gone over to USB (may have to do with printing huge files since my wireless office printer works fine).  I don't think anybody has mentioned that Canon Pro-10 really does have the equivalent of Epson's wonderful ABW printer driver (allows  subtle print tones...I relied on Epson's ABW for a certain sepia/brown and Canon produces it the same way but apparently has no name for this printer driver).  3800 had gigantic ink tanks but that meant I needed to spend $450 to replace the set at $45 each. Canon may be more expensive over time  due to smaller ink tanks but they only cost $15 each ...a set costs $130. For that reason Canon's smaller tanks make more sense for my low volume purposes (maybe 50 letter size per month with a few 13/19).  Canon has a "gloss equalizer" that does seem to minimize gloss differential on glossy and luster paper.  Probably contributes more with some papers than others.    I gave 4 rather than 5 because the wireless was a hassle...though that might have to do with my particular DSL/router.  I don't think I could ask for better print results.  Incidentally...all I care about is B&W  :-)

product_title: Finestra Value Gloss - Glossy Everyday Photo Paper, 8.5 X 11 Inches (200 Sheets)
review_headline: It is cheap paper but your still may not be getting what you paid for.
review_body:
I go through anywhere between 500-1,000 sheets of photo paper a week for my digital imaging business. I normally use other brands but after talking with these guys over the phone I tried this value paper. If you need this for anything professional do not use it. The paper is curled without any ink on it and once you put ink on it the problem just gets worse.

To note for those it matters to this paper has no branding on the back of it as of the time I used it and none of the higher quality paper that Finestra Arts carries has it either again from the time I last used it.

I have tried every possibly setting and spoke with Finestra Art over the phone on this issue and it just is very poor paper. It works best with top feeding printers as any that feed from the bottom may have issues feeding the paper. I ran into this constantly.

What finally did this paper in for me is while running in through one of my printers that feeds from the top is the paper got caught in the print head as it was going back and forth and after getting this out it had damaged it where the printer just will not longer print correctly. The paper is so curled up that some printers while going back and forth putting the image on the paper hits the corners and when it did this on the printer of mine it just ruined it.

I read the reviews carefully before buying paper and try to get any information that I can from them. This review is not to bash Finestra Arts paper. They do have some very good quality paper that is in a higher grade but if you want paper for your business or have a printer that cost you a good amount of money that you cannot do without I would stay away from this paper. Use a higher quality paper from this company or use another brand of photo paper. There are many others that work well such as Kirkland, Ilford (it is costly) and Inkpress paper just to name a few.

I hope this review helps anyone looking for photo paper. Again if you do not care about the quality that much or use very little paper this may work for you. The image on the print is decent but the paper will not come across professional to anyone. Again I do warn this could damage your printer but it seems others have used the paper with no issues on that.

product_title: Victor DC300 High Rise Collection Sit-Stand Desk Converter 28 x 23 x 15 1/2 Black
review_body:
I was very skeptical as this desk converter only had one review. I went ahead an purchased it due to it being Prime eligible and I know that since it was fulfilled by Amazon that I wouldn't have any issues returning it. I now have no interest in returning it and just about everyone in my office wants one. This is an amazing alternative to forking out $1,500 on a full sized desk.

I am giving this five stars overall as this desk conversions has exceeded my expectations, but that is not to say there could be some improvements:

Pros:
1. I am 6' 5" and at it's highest setting it is perfect for me.
2. The hydraulic system which converts from sitting to standing and visa versa is smooth and effortless.
3. There is a slight bounce when typing, but the addition of the tension supports is a great idea and solves that problem.
4. For the most part, very easy to set up.
5. It allows for vertical and lateral monitor tilting, which several more expensive competitors did not have.
6. Keyboard tray is nice and large and is now holding my keyboard, mouse with mouse pad, a picture frame, rubber band and paperclip holders, post its all over the place, etc..
7. It is a solid piece of furniture that does not feel flimsy at all.

Cons:
1. Tightening the nut which controls the monitor tilt is a little frustrating. As you tighten, the monitor wants to move with it. I would recommend having someone else hold the monitor at your desired position while they tighten. I would also recommend using a socket wrench as the little crescent wrench just does not cut it.
2. I think little predrilled cutouts where the support legs could rest in on the underside of the keyboard tray would be helpful just to ensure they stay in place (mine have no moved at all since using though). Just a thought :)

I would highly recommend this for anyone that wants to get off their cadunk and hopefully avoid the forming of blood clots. I hope they stock some more because we are coming for them!lots. I hope they stock some more because we are coming for them!

review_headline: Shredder is OK but AMAZON has no business in this business.
review_body:
Reviews were all over the map on this shredder. Particularly it stopping working. We let our five year old shred our 2003 to 2011 taxes. She was a ruthless beta tester. "snapped" back down. So while it's a battle ready product, it only gets three stars. Amazon is not in the business of shredding paper. There are numerous other companies that this is their livelihood. Amazon simply went to China (who has duplicated a number of products) purchased on in bulk, and they are selling it to us directly. Not the right way to treat the merchants who were selling shredders on Amazon before Amazon decided to make their own shredder the number on ranking product on the worlds third largest website. So, two stars to Amazon for the ethics violation...

review_headline: Multi-function printer has great features at low cost
review_body: Multi-function printing devices are a remarkable buy---getting a printer, copier, and fax machine  all in one compact unit. Couple that concept with pricing that competes with single-function printers and you can understand their popularity. This model by Brother has features galore, such as printing from small memory cards directly, allowing for automatic multi-page document feeding, offering a choice of printing color documents in B&W, and using separate cartridges for color rather than the typical tri-color single cartridge. Construction is excellent even though some flimsy plastic elements are used. However, they apparently are adequate for their purpose and cause no difficulties in use. Printing quality is very good although the default settings tend to make photos look "soft" in their colors. (Extra settings are available to make adjustments.) Copying can use paper of standard 11" depth or 14" legal size. Caution note: In the initial setup you must use the low-capacity starter cartridges that are furnished. Putting them aside for emergency use and substituting standard ink cartridges just doesn't work. The wireless connection to multiple computers is simple and the fax connection to a telephone or answering machine is explained in easy-to-follow instructions  All operations are extremely quiet and the large-size illuminated screen  provides a keyboard and touch commands that conveniently handle all functions.

product_title: Brother Printer MFCJ4410DW Business Smart Multi-Function Inkjet and Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner, Copier and Fax (Certified Refurbished)
review_body:
This is the third Brother printer I have purchased. Two older ones are for the home office and this one for my motorhome. The two at home are hardwired and work fine. I bought this one for the motorhome so it could be in a cabinet, out of the way and operate wirelessly. It would (will) be a huge pain to have to run wires. If you own an RV you know there is no easy way.

Here is the application. I have my RV at my sons house next to a detached garage. We ran an ethernet cable from his router to a very good (Amped AP 20000) access point in the garage. I have excellent strength on 5.0. After two goes at installing the driver print driver wirelessly I also bought a DVD drive to download the install software from the CD. Long story short, the printer sees the network for the access point but will not / cannot install it to operate in the wireless mode. After two phone calls to the Brother help line,(and on hold for nearly 30 minutes each time) I was told the printer must be located no more than 15 feet from the router (not the access point). The tech made it clear that the printer WILL NOT operate from the access point and MUST BE within 15 feet of the router. The printer is currently sitting on a table 12 inches from my laptop. The laptop has perfect wireless capability and the printer does not. How can that be? This means the printer is not really wireless or the wireless function is a joke. If it were not such a pain to return, I would return this and find a printer with actual wireless capability. Instead, this will be my last Brother product ever, and I will make sure to communicate this to others so they do not make the same mistake I did.

review_headline: Beware, does not save MP3 files as claimed!

The recorder functions well and the audio is good. But the informational material said it can save in MP3 format, and that is a lie. If I had known, I would not have purchased it.

The info with this claimed it saved MP3 files. What they don't tell you is that it saves in Sony proprietary format. Then you must download, install and use their converter application, on Windows only. So as a Mac user, I was really upset that they misled me about this.

And before you WIndows users feel smug...be aware that you are only one upgrade away from losing the ability to save as MP3. How long will Sony support this application on Windows? Windows 8? Windows 10? No one knows... I'd bet it won't be as long as the recorder lasts. Then you'll have a paperweight if you need MP3 files.

So my advice would be to get one that actually saves MP3 files, not Sony's proprietary format. Sony is the King of Proprietary. Avoid them!

review_body:
Completely serviceable and comfortable as a replacement for my LED TV. Absolutely amazing for its price. Not ridiculously bright but bright enough to watch during the day with some blackout shades. product_title: BIC Kids Pencil - Blue Barrel, (1.3 mm) 1-Count
review_body: My daughter does not hold her pencil correctly. Despite repeated attempts at correcting her, she goes back to her bad habits at school. The teacher does not force her to hold the pencil correctly, and they don't teach handwriting like they did in the "old days", so I have been fighting an uphill battle. I got this pencil set through Vine and she absolutely loved using it--she thought the pencil was cool, loved the size and the color. I am thrilled, she's getting muscle memory from using the pencil, and all is well for the first month. Problem is, once she went back to using a regular pencil or other writing device, she went right back to her old, bad habits. So, while this worked for a little when she used it consistently, it did not change her behavior, so I am not sure it accomplished it's purpose. After the novelty of the pencil wore off, she stopped using it and went back to regular mechanical pencils. Go ahead and try it--perhaps you will get better long term results. For now, I will continue to battle on my own.

review_body: In order to make it not slip, the product uses, what are essentially, rubber bands on the "feet" and the page holders.  That is what the orange color is on the arms in the image of this product.  If you have a toddler in the house, I would rate this product 1 star, because the toddler will remove the rubber bands making the product useless.  If you are a single person or a person with older children, I would rate this product 5 stars.  So i averaged it and gave it 3 stars.  I am using it for our homeschooling, so my son can practice his typing.  We use it to hold up "Scholastic Children's Encyclopedia" type books.  For single sheets of paper, you will have to attach the paper to a clipboard and then put the clipboard on the stand.  Or put the paper in front of another book.  As for turning pages, the arms easily move back and forth, so you can just move the arm forward, turn the page, and then move the arm back.  Any book holder is going to work the same way, and have the same problem of blocking text.  But these arms are clear, so don't think it is a problem.  The only way to get around that would be a magnetic page holder, but one, you would still have to move the magnets, and two, that method would not work for books.

product_title: TeckNet Gaming Mouse Mat
review_body:
I got introduced to Tecknet when I bought their wired gaming mouse (which is awesome, by the way), and their customer service department was nice enough to reach out to me about my purchase. It made a really good impression on me, and so when I got this mouse pad today, I was expecting the same quality product and service. And by God, quality is what I just got.

Style-wise, this mat is very simple. Matte black with just the company logo (the letters have a little grip, due to being rubber, but not enough to interfere with use), it is not flashy nor is it supposed to be. It does have a stylish embossed border, which though not visibly prominent (due to also being black), gives a good feel to the wrist and the slightly raised edge it provides serves as a physical border for the mouse while using it.

Size wise, this thing is awesome. The extra-wide design allows for great side-to-side movement and control, and the length is also very nice. It's not obnoxiously big, though, and the low profile of the mat makes it seem smaller than it is when you aren't using it, but absolutely massive when you are.

The bottom has great grip to it, and even holds on my super-slick desk. Most pads I buy tend to slip a lot on it, bu this one stays put; I really like that.

The Casio FX-115ES Plus is a good non-graphing calculator that does most everything I need it to, lots of functionality, good screen resolution. One thing to note: the FX-115ES Plus, both the unit and the slide-on hard cover include small ridges on them at the top and bottom. In many calculators these are rubber and are there to ensure the calculator doesn’t slip or slide around easily when it’s being used sitting on a table or similar surface. That’s not the case with the FX-115ES Plus – it’s just all plastic molding and the faux ridges do absolutely nothing to prevent it from moving around. Not a problem, after all the calculator is $15, just an annoyance.

product_title: Casio Inc. HS8VA Standard Function Calculator
review_body:
Had an older version of this model for years but recently it was submerged in water for a good ten minutes. As soon as I got it out of the water I could tell it was wet inside as it was not working, so I took it apart and dried the inside the best I could. Slowly some numbers began to work again but ultimately I decided that was as good as it was going to get and came online to get a replacement because it is by far the best calculator we've ever used. I was happy to find the same model, only newer, on amazon and for such a good price, so I ordered it right away and forgot about the old broken one.
Turns out, the wife knew I had taken it apart and dried it and put it back together and so she just picked it up and started using it thinking I had knowingly 'fixed' it. It was back to working good as new before the new one even arrived.

product_title: HP LaserJet Pro 200 MFP M276nw - multifunction printer ( color )
review_headline: (UPDATED) HP LaserJet Pro vs the Brother MFC-9130CW: Cost of Ownership is the big difference
review_body:
Be sure to read the update at the end! Important Firmware Update Available.

The HP LaserJet Pro 200 is pretty much the market competitor to the [[ASIN:B00C6MNP52 Brother MFC-9130CW]]. I have experience with both and I hope this comparison review will be helpful.

For those who just want the bottom line: both are capable small workgroup printers. You get faster printing and more capability with the [[ASIN:B00C6MNP52 Brother MFC-9130CW]] and based just toner price-per-page using brand-name toner the Brother is a lot less expensive over the long run.

The HP software package with the HP is typically bloated but less so than in older models. The Brother software package smaller and lighter.

One I find particularly annoying is the incessant nag window to validate your toner cartridges. I hate checking in with some central site whenever I change toner or inkjet ink so I don't want to do it. It did not accept my "decline" choice and kept coming back.

Both printers have similar specifications: single sided printing and scanning, wireless connectivity, Apple airprint support (works great), proprietary mobile connections, Automatic document feeder (35 pages), and print from/scan to USB. A 30,000 page duty cycle is the same for both. Both have nice color touch screens. Both are capable personal or small office multifunction units.

An important difference between is the HP LaserJet Pro 200 has a LAN port for hardwired connectivity. The Brother MFC-9130CW does not, but the generally more capable [[ASIN:B00C6MNQ92 Brother MFC-9330CDW]] does along with duplex printing.

But in specs Brother wins in most ways: 19ppm compared to 14ppm for the HP. Paper capacity of the brother is 250 pages compared to 150 for the HP, and print resolution is higher for the Brother MFC-9130CW.

The big difference in Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) is the cost of toner. This both with the included toner cartridges and replacements. The HP comes with "demi-toner cartridges" with a capacity of 700 pages. The Brother comes with "starter" toner cartridges with a capacity of 1000 pages - 42% more included with the Brother.

Note: I had originally reported the Brother came with full standard cartridges. This was true for one a client purchased just after the MFC-9130CW introduction. Thanks to kdaj for bringing this to my attention.

A full set of standard toner cartridges is around $300 for the HP. High capacity cartridges for the Brother (2500 pages black and 2200 pages color) cost same, that's an effective purchase price differentiator of at least $150 in favor of the Brother!

[[ASIN:B009XF3HJY HP color toners]] (just one size) have a yield of 1800 pages. HP has a [[ASIN:B008M11XOG expanded black toner]] cartridge available with a 2400 page yield, Brother [[ASIN:B00ELR1LTM color toners are 1400 pages]] standard, [[ASIN:B00EPOH406 high yield is 2200]]; just one size [[ASIN:B00BR3WWY6 black toner with a 2500 page]] yield.

In favor of the HP the output on the Brother holds 100 sheets compared to 125 on the HP. The non-expandable memory on the Brother is 192MB and 256MB on the HP.

I setup the HP with a wired connection and it was instantly recognized on the network. The Brother's I've setup are the same. Wireless setup for both are comparable.

The HP LaserJet Pro 200 color MFP M276nw comes with a pretty typical HP software suite. It installs a large amount of software which isn't as large as I have seen in the past. The install was relatively quick for HP MFC's. The Brother software suite is a lot lighter and a very easy install too. Both provide printer monitoring and a good level of control. Both drivers updated the firewall for accessing the printer.

Another area of differentiation is in scanning. The ADF works well and automatic scanning of documents is reasonably fast and the quality is fine. HP used to set a standard for fine control in scanning. That is sorely lacking from the included software which seems to have only brightness, contrast and cropping. No gamma or other controls which HP used to provide. HP has really "dumbed-down" the scanning interface to the point where most control is lost.

This isn't an issue of most documents, but shows most in scanning photos (I mean real photographic prints from the days of film). Some photos look fine (generally glossy photos) but matte finish photos seem to come out with high contrast and loss of dark detail with default scanning settings. Trying to adjust the contrast, brightness and cropping does not result in improvements. The same photo on a Canon Lide scans worlds better!! An iPhone photo of the photo is worlds better!! I can only hope HP will read this and fix this issue.

That said, its focus is in scanning documents and in that I have no complaint.

I think it's pretty clear that the HP is generally a capable multifunction device but, the Brother competitor the MFC-9130 is a better value. Even more so if you plan to do a lot of printing the Brother is a big winner right out of the box since it comes with full toner cartridges.

In real world use the HP LaserJet Pro 200 is close to as good as the Brother, but the Brother is as better value. The HP costs less to purchase but the aforementioned included demi-toners makes it less of a bargain. When toner capacity vs. cost is considered the total cost of ownership is in far favor of the Brother and only gets more you print. This is based on brand-name toner cartridge pricing.

Print quality for both is very close. Scanning the same. Both are easy to use from the console.

The bottom line is that while capable the HP LaserJet Pro 200 color MFP M276nw has significantly worse value and TCO than the [[ASIN:B00C6MNP52 Brother MFC-9130CW]]. In my experience both the HP and Brother should have similar useful lives. Maybe a little longer for the Brother.

Because it's a fine multifunction but less economical than its Brother competitor (MFC-9130CW) I'm only giving it 4 stars. If you have a strong preference for HP printers you might want to consider it 5 stars but take a look at the [[ASIN:B00C6MNP52 Brother MFC-9130CW]] before making up your mind.

UPDATE
We have run into an issue with the Laserjet Pro 200. We have come to the conclusion that the printer will sometimes not wake from sleep without being shut down and turned back on. This is true whether trying to print through the wired LAN or wake up the device from the touch screen. The unit remains unresponsive until either the power plug is pulled or the power button is "long pressed" (more than about 10s) to power it off.

We installed the latest firmware (as of late last week) and it seems to make not difference. The HP support forums have multiple people reporting the same issue and the consistent advise from HP was to assign a static address to the printer instead of using DHCP. We had a fixed DHCP reservation setup, but we setup the printer to have a manually configured address in the printer settings. No change. The problem still happens.

While this is annoying it happens infrequently enough and the workaround is simple enough we will live with it a while. For a multi-user office this issue could be a deal-breaker. Until this issue is fixed I'm dropping the rating on this printer to 3 stars.

UPDATE
HP released updated firmware to address the issue where the Laserjet Pro 200 will not wake from sleep mode for network printing. This is great news as it addresses what has become a MAJOR annoyance over the past months. There is also an important security fix with the OpenSSL library.

Here is the lists of fixes/changes in this firmware I found on the HP web site.

* Fixed a vulnerability issue (CVE-2014-0224)in OpenSSL versions 1.0.1e.
* Updated WIFI binary codes regarding to the power consumption efficiency.
* Fixed a 79 error when printing certain documents.
* Eliminated Smart Install feature.
* Fixed an issue where secondary DNS entries may not properly match the address returned by DHCP Server.
* Resolved a fax quality issue when Fax Resolution is set to "Photo".
* Fixed an issue where the printer would incorrectly respond to a switch sending out router advertisements for a VLAN.
* Fixed an issue where network connecting printer might not wake from sleep mode.
* Fixed an issue where the "Black and White" printout of a JPEG image might be inverted

Because this fix resolved the most aggravating issue I'm bumping the rating back to 4 stars.

We have run into an issue with the Laserjet Pro 200. We have come to the conclusion that the printer will sometimes not wake from sleep without being shut down and turned back on. This is true whether trying to print through the wired LAN or wake up the device from the touch screen. The unit remains unresponsive until either the power plug is pulled or the power button is "long pressed" (more than about 10s) to power it off.

We installed the latest firmware (as of late last week) and it seems to make not difference. The HP support forums have multiple people reporting the same issue and the consistent advise from HP was to assign a static address to the printer instead of using DHCP. We had a fixed DHCP reservation setup, but we setup the printer to have a manually configured address in the printer settings. No change. The problem still happens.

While this is annoying it happens infrequently enough and the workaround is simple enough we will live with it a while. For a multi-user office this issue could be a deal-breaker. Until this issue is fixed I'm dropping the rating on this printer to 3 stars.

UPDATE
HP released updated firmware to address the issue where the Laserjet Pro 200 will not wake from sleep mode for network printing. This is great news as it addresses what has become a MAJOR annoyance over the past months. There is also an important security fix with the OpenSSL library.

Here is the lists of fixes/changes in this firmware I found on the HP web site.

* Fixed a vulnerability issue (CVE-2014-0224)in OpenSSL versions 1.0.1e.
* Updated WIFI binary codes regarding to the power consumption efficiency.
* Fixed a 79 error when printing certain documents.
* Eliminated Smart Install feature.
* Fixed an issue where secondary DNS entries may not properly match the address returned by DHCP Server.
* Resolved a fax quality issue when Fax Resolution is set to "Photo".
* Fixed an issue where the printer would incorrectly respond to a switch sending out router advertisements for a VLAN.
* Fixed an issue where network connecting printer might not wake from sleep mode.
* Fixed an issue where the "Black and White" printout of a JPEG image might be inverted

Because this fix resolved the most aggravating issue I'm bumping the rating back to 4 stars.

Hope this helps someone.

product_title: Canon LBP6030W Wireless Monochrome Printer
review_headline: Great printer for the price but challenging setup
review_body: I've been using this printer for a couple of weeks now after purchasing it from a big box office supply retailer.  Opted to go with this model instead of a more expensive version that offered duplex printing.  I have had several Canon printers since 1994 and they have always been good to me.  This one appears to be no exception so far.  That being said I only gave it five stars due to what I consider to be seriously difficult installation instructions.  The printer itself was OK but the wireless installation instructions left a lot to be desired.  It was only through a lot of trial and error and quite honestly dumb luck that I was able to install this thing wirelessly.  I am using it via USB to a desktop and wirelessly to a Windows laptop and also to a MacBook.  I also do printing via Google Cloud Print.  The fact that I can connect via USB AND wifi simultaneously was a big plus for me.  I know that for some printers it's one or the other depending on the printer.    One issue that I encountered after installation that gave me a lot of headaches was the printer would go offline wirelessly after a few hours.  Then, when you tried to print via wifi the printer could not be discovered by my laptops.  I was unable to locate anything about this in the printer documentation (all online by the way).  Interestingly, another Canon inkjet that I have installed wirelessly NEVER does this.  It has been working fine for years with no hiccups.  Fortunately through a ton of Google searching and reading various forums I was able to come up with a fix that (so far) seems to work.  I was skeptical but so far so good.  The solution involved entering into the web-based setup of the printer and setting a location for the printer (which is blank by default).  I'm not tech-savvy enough to know how or why this did the trick but ever since I did that it has not dropped off of my network.  I will update this review later if I encounter any issues.  I would also like to hear from anyone elseif they had this problem and what they may have done to rectify the situation.    Update 2/15/15...I went out of town for several days and did not use the printer wirelessly for a week.  Went to print the first page today and lo and behold it didn't print.  So I guess the fix I described above isn't going to work after all which is what I figured.  A power cycle of the printer brought it back to wireless life.  However, this is inconvenient as the printer is located on my second floor and shouldn't be necessary.  If anyone experiences this and has a fix I would love to hear about it.

product_title: Hp Designjet T520 Wireless 24-in E-printer
review_body:
Here is a warning to anyone considering this printer (and potentially any other large format HP printer) for banner printing. This printer will not pause in the middle of a print job when one of the ink cartridges is depleted. It will cancel the job and eject whatever it was printing regardless of how far along it was.

We bought this printer to replace an Epson Stylus Photo 2200 which we used to print banners up to 80 inches long. The Epson has a feature which I assumed was standard to large format printers like this. If an ink cartridge ran out during a print job it would pause to let you insert a new ink cartridge then resume the job seamlessly. You would not be able to tell where the print job paused.

However, as I said the HP Designjet T520 does not have that feature. So in our case if it runs out near the end of printing an 80 inch banner the banner is ruined and we just wasted 78 inches of paper. If you don't want to chance that this means you have to replace your ink cartridges before they are fully depleted. I can't say I'm surprised as I'm sure many would agree HP is really in the business of selling ink.

With that said, the features it does have are very impressive which is why I didn't reduce my rating to 1 star.

review_body:
I like this device and do recommend it. I am currently on my second one having left my first at the dinner. This new one has opened my eyes to something - this pointer may have a 2-3 month effective lifespan.

I thought my previous one was working great right up to the day I lost it (3 months after purchase.) But having this new one, I can clearly see, feel, and hear just how the performance of my previous one had degraded over that time. This newer one sharpens in a fraction of the winds as my previous one. There is considerably less play between the body and top, and a much smoother rotational glide while sharpening. Compared to this new one, my old pointer felt like it was... rubbing the lead to a point, whereas this new pointer is clearly slicing and shaving--the way it crunches the lead is almost therapeutic!

Either way, this thing works great and I use it A LOT! This time around I'll be watching closely to see how the performance changes over time. It just may be something I'll have to replace at 6-8 week intervals if I want to maintain maximum performance.

If anyone else has long-term (3 months+) experience with this pointer, I'd love to hear what you think.

But what the heck. I made it work. Now I can flip that pack easily from either shoulder with a couple of clicks.

product_title: Pack Of 2 Beto Replacment TZ221 TZe221 black on white Tape for Brother P touch Labeler
review_headline: ONLY buy Genuine, Authentic Brother tapes from Amazon.com (avoid Marketplace)
review_body: Do NOT purchase these lousy Beto replacement tapes. Both tapes in the double pack did not evenly flow through my P-touch 1280, resulting in unsynchronized clear laminate crinkling over the white base paper and completely jamming up in the label maker. Even after I worked out early on, that after every TWO labels printed, you had to pop the tape out of the machine, tighten the tension on the tape (are you old enough to remember sticking a pencil into an audio cassette to wind pulled out tape back into the plastic casing? Yeah, like THAT with the label tape) tape would still wind around a spool inside the PT-1280 and badly crinkle the labels. In all, I lost over 7 feet of a 26 foot long tape or 27% totally wasted product. Seriously. I measured. Even with constantly adjusting the tension, the black letter-making tape portion would crinkle just a tiny bit, resulting in a lost letter every so often. Laminate didn't always line up with the white label portion, leaving you with a sticky, exposed strip at the top of the label. A total nightmare. Just buy the authentic Brother tapes directly from Amazon.com. I tried to purchase "Brother Tape, Retail Packaging" which described "Genuine Brother accessories in retail packaging" from seller Sienoc but instead received "Compatible replacment label tape" (sic) so don't even trust Marketplace sellers to send the GENUINE AUTHENTIC tapes. I haven't tried the new "compatible" ones - they do seem different (and perhaps better made) than these Beto tapes. I've used 5 or 6 of the "real deal" Brother label tapes and never experienced a single glitch, so from now on, I'll only buy the authentic Brother tapes and I'll only trust Amazon.com to deliver.

review_body:
As a hopeful aspiring filmmaker hoping to one day go pro I go to a lot of meetings and take even more notes... or, at least, my lady/assistant does. I just do the scheduling. One of the largest challenges to me is note taking and planning as we have to schedule personnel, prop acquisition, location scouting and securing, casting, etc. and that's a hefty task if you don't have a full staff at your disposal. Note taking is critical to maintain cohesion and any form of order in a project and the LAST thing one should be worried about is what they're taking notes on.

I've used the AT-A-GLANCE meeting planner and loved that and, having tested the Padfolio, I can safely say that it's OK. It's built durable like any other AT-A-GLANCE product but the pages seem more graph paper with \\"notes\\" printed on the top, as if the company had a paper surplus and used it to make this product. Don't get me wrong, the binding is superb and it's what we needed, but it just didn't wow me like other AT-A-GLANCE products. The layout could be a lot more friendly for notes but it seems more suitable for basic sketching.

I'd still recommend AT-A-GLANCE products, just that this one is not as good as the others.

review_headline: As always these have been fantastic. Highly pigmented with no odor
review_body: As always these have been fantastic. Highly pigmented with no odor, even after hours of full-time use. They virtually never smear, the only instances I have noticed smearing as a full-time university student is when the highlighters are used over freshly written gel-ink pens or fountain pen ink. Using a anti-fraud ink pen eliminates thus issue entirely. If freshly printed pages haven't fully dried, there is minor risk for smearing. Book pages of all types of paper work well and won't smear. However, thin pages are at risk for bleeding of ink. I would not recommend this for bibles or textbooks that have unusually thin paper for pages. Standard book paper and vellum-type paper work beautifully with these highlighters. The turquoise and purple are a bit dark and are not as easily read through as the others, but still very usable. The blue is a tad dark, but not in the way the turquoise and purple are. And better yet, the main colors of this series which are most used have refill stations that can also be purchased. The stations are cost effective long-term and you don't have to purchase new highlighters. These highlighters are well crafted, light, and comfortable to hold. They have a standard-sized tip. I have not tried making copies of pages that have been highlighted to see what colors are retained or not, though the packaging says that all the colors will disappear when copied with the exception of the turquoise and purple.

review_body: I bought this pen before becoming familiar with fountain pens in general, so I didn't realize what to expect. I put Audacious Red Waterman ink in it, and it wrote immediately. I really like the twist loading of ink - it works great. At first the ink was a bit heavy on paper, but after a bit it settled into its normal ink flow, which I like very much. I can't feel the flex of the nib, but it does lay a slightly variable line width, making writing much prettier.  I wouldn't push on the nib much - it immediately lets more ink out than you want to see, slightly blobbing your letters. The only real complaint I would have is that the nib, while not scratchy, is not the smoothest in the world either. I prefer nibs as close to buttery smooth as possible, so that makes me a bit prejudiced. If you don't mind a small amount of paper \\"feedback\\", this pen gives you some very nice looking handwriting.    UPDATE: After receiving a beautiful Parker Sonnet fountain pen I recently purchased and comparing it to this pen, I realized that this pen actually writes very comfortably, and quite smoothly. I particularly like the narrower grip, and its light weight.  I'm quite happy that I purchased it!

The construction is all metal and nothing fancy. It has a removable rear spring loading mechanism that pulls totally out, put the staples in and push it back in and hook it. product_title: Brother HLL8350CDW Wireless Color Laser Printer
review_body: I had a 2008 Dell 3110cn Laser color printer that really worked great I had no complaints. Was going to purchase toner for it but thought I should look at a new printer with new features and compare the price. After a lengthy research I decided on this printer because of the features and great reviews, I have never had a Brother printer before.  I also have had HP and Canon all in one ink jets, with a canon as my current all in one. I am a fan of the ink jet quality but did get tired of having to buy new ink on a regular basis.  HP's are pretty expensive for ink. I love the speed of the brother, I printed a five page color document in 27 seconds from clicking print to finish where it took my fairly new Canon ink jet 45 seconds. When I compared the quality of the print I felt the sharpness of the black text and the color to be better on the Brother. I was very happy with those results. The one thing that does bother me, almost to the point that I'm not sure if I can live with it is the paper curl. My Dell Laser had zero paper curl, my ink jets have zero paper curl. The brother has quite a lot, I tried it on 20, 24, 28lb paper and on photo paper, all come up with a pretty good amount of curl. I'm not sure if everyone is having this issue or if maybe mine is defective. Hopefully I will find out soon. So for all the positives I do give it 4 stars, take away the paper curl and it would be 5.

review_body:
It's okay. I'm not going to return them as I have taken a long time to figure out how many I needed to re-do my entire filing system. I was going for a uniform and clean look. My cabinets are dark java (almost black) & most of my office furniture & accessories are black. I wanted an organized look.
PRO: They arrived quickly
They included clear plastic tabs so you can label them (see also CON).

CON: They are not really \\"black\\" as stated. They are more of a faded black (like when something that was a true black that's been faded out in the sun).
They are flimsy. They are not reinforced so they can rip if not careful (i.e. when you insert the plastic tabs to label them or if you have a heavy file folder that you put into it).
The clear plastic tabs that came with them were completely the wrong size and you end up ripping the hanging file when you try to insert them into the holes. Solution: You have to trim the plastic tabs (just right, takes a few tries) to get them to fit. Very annoying and tedious process when all I want to do is re-org my files, not create a craft project. I bought 4 boxes of these and all the plastic tabs were like this. I ended up buying Pendaflex clear plastic tabs separately and those worked fine. Not impressed since they came from the same \\"company\\".
Finally, a few (6 to be exact) were \\"damaged\\". The white rod that you hang them with was twisted & unusable or the top fold of the file was \\"factory sliced\\" (looks like a production run error) & when you hang them and try to put anything in the file, it rips it completely. So had to throw those 6 away.

They are better than my nasty green ones I replaced them with, so I'm not going to hassle with a return, but I'm not a fan.

Edited to fix a couple of grammar errors. :)

product_title: Vupoint Magic InstaScan PDS-ST420-VP Sheetfed Scanner
review_headline: Great product with a few quirks
review_body:
I had a very specific purpose for purchasing this scanner. I have been doing a lot of Family Tree work and am planning a trip to Ireland to visit distant relatives. I presume they will have photos and documents which I would want to copy. I could use my DSLR camera to take photos of photos, or my smartphone can do the same. Taking photos of photos requires careful attention to light and reflections. A scanner would be a better solution.

I wanted a small, light weight, and portable scanner. After several hours of research I selected this one. Now that I have it in hand I can see it was a good choice.

Pros:

- The PDS-ST420-VP is designed and manufactured so it has no sharp corners, it is light weight (13.8 oz. without batteries)

- The materials used to fabricate the scanner are of good quality.

- The little unit is nice looking. It would look good on any desk.

- It takes AA alkaline batteries which are readily available all over the world. You can even use rechargeable batteries. Many users report the batteries last at least the 200 promised by VuPoint, and up to 1,000 by one user. I hate the trend of designing in lithium batteries that can't be replaced by the user. Lithium batteries deteriorate over time and would begin to fail after about two years. Most of VuPoint's portable scanners have lithium batteries.

- The LCD display shows the level of charge remaining in the batteries.

- The scanner is small and easy to slip into a backpack or briefcase. ( 10.6\\" (L) x 1.6\\" (H) x 2.6\\" (W) )

- A built in slider can be used to guide a document or photo into the scanner.

- The scanner is very quiet while scanning.

- It turns itself off after 2 minutes of non-use to preserve the batteries.

- After setting the time and date the date items were scanned is stored in the PDF or JPG file.

- It scans very quickly; a few seconds regardless of settings.

- Using a microSD card is great for me. I can slip the microSD card into an SD card adapter, then put the SD card into my desktop or laptop. Further my phone has a microSD card slot so I can put the card directly into my smartphone to view or email files.

- Using the supplied SCAN Direct software on my PC I can scan directly into the computer. A microSD card isn't even required when scanning directly to the computer.

- A calibration card is supplied to be used with the calibration process on the scanner. This adjusts the white balance so colors are more correct. This process does more than set the white balance though. When I first tried the scanner all photos had thin white lines all up and down the scanned image. I thought I was going to have to send the scanner back due to these poor quality photo scans. But the Calibration process eliminated that problem.

- A cleaning card is also supplied. Insert it in the paper/photo scan slot and it cleans itself.

- The buttons and status display are self explanatory and easy to use.

Cons:

- Inserting a document or photo correctly takes some care. It is easy to insert the document or photo a bit crooked and have a messed up image. You don't know this unless the scanner is connected to a computer, or you insert the microSD card into a computer to view the images.

- The supplied SCAN Direct software, that allows scanning directly into the computer, is feature shy. I didn't find a way to save all files to the hard drive, only one at a time. I could not resize the SCAN Direct window on my computer. There does not seem to be a means to set Color or Mono, set the DPI, or set the PDF or JPG when scanning directly to the computer. I sent an email question about this to VuPoint and they confirmed there is no way to control the settings when scanning to the computer via USB. To me this renders that feature nearly useless unless those default settings work for you.

- The LCD panel showing the scanner status is quite small. I finally memorized all of the status icons. I can't read them without a magnifying glass.

- Dots Per Inch (DPI) is selectable 300, 600, 900 dpi. But only 300 dpi is the native optical resolution. 600 & 900 are interpolated which means it really scans at 300 DPI, then more dots are filled in with software to simulate 600 and 900 dpi. If you scan at 900 dpi you won't get a better image than at 300 dpi. For documents 300 dpi is quite adequate. For photos 300 dpi is marginal.

- As many other reviewers have reported the scanner resets the settings to 300 DPI, Color, JPG every time you turn the scanner on. That is an unfortunate design but we're stuck with it.

- As others have reported there is no way to scan multiple documents into a single PDF file. Each page goes into it's own file. I confirmed this limitation with VuPoint in an email exchange.

Image Quality:

Scanning documents provides more than adequate image quality.

Scanning photos is another thing. I have two other scanners. One is a dedicated flat bed scanner with a native resolution of 1200 dpi. The other is an all-in-one scanner/printer/copier with a native resolution of 600 dpi. There is no way this VuPoint PDS-ST420-VP scanner can produce scanned photo images as good as either of those. The question I had to ask myself is will the quality be good enough for my purposes. I bought the scanner to scan photos primarily.

Black & White photos come out pretty good. If I scan at 900 dpi I can then do some sharpening and other adjustments on the computer. For B&W I'm pleased with the results.

For color things aren't as positive. The scanner produces color images that are way too saturated, underexposed, and lacking detail. Corrections can be made on the computer with a bit of work but, as expected, I'll never get the same quality as my other scanners.

For color photos I would give this scanner a 6.5 on a scale of 10, 10 being best. It isn't great but it is acceptable for my purposes. I expect to visit Irish relatives where they will pull out a shoe box of a couple of hundred photos. This scanner will allow me to quickly scan in all of the photos without disturbing the visit.

Once my trip is over we will likely use this scanner to reduce the amount of paper in the house by scanning in our receipts and other documents used for tax returns.

Would I recommend this scanner? It really depends on your end use. For simple, quick, light weight, small, portable scanning I couldn't find a better scanner than this one. If you don't mind a built-in non user replaceable lithium battery then VuPoint has some higher quality portable scanners. If all you are doing is scanning in receipts this would be a pretty good option although selecting a different VuPoint scanner that is powered by AC or USB would be more practical as you don't have to worry about changing batteries. Once my trip is over we will likely use this scanner to reduce the amount of paper in the house by scanning in our receipts and other documents used for tax returns.

Would I recommend this scanner? It really depends on your end use. For simple, quick, light weight, small, portable scanning I couldn't find a better scanner than this one. If you don't mind a built-in non user replaceable lithium battery then VuPoint has some higher quality portable scanners. If all you are doing is scanning in receipts this would be a pretty good option although selecting a different VuPoint scanner that is powered by AC or USB would be more practical as you don't have to worry about changing batteries. If all you want to do is scan photos, and you care about the highest quality, this isn't a good choice. For my particular situation I will live with the shortcomings and am happy with my choice.

product_title: HP Q8842A Color Laser Glossy Photo Paper, 4 x 6 Inches, 100 Sheets
review_body:
I was a little surprised when I saw the finish on this paper. I won't say the finish is actually dull, but to me, it hardly passes for matte, much less glossy. I've used a lot of various glossy papers.

I just bought an expensive HP printer through Amazon very recently and I bought this paper to try out with the new color laser printer. I have to say that images do look pretty sharp and clear when printed on this paper. But the paper is not glossy, and that might detract from the overall appearance.

In some ways, the paper looks like real photo paper that older photographs used to be printed to. I'm talking about the paper photo prints that you got (and can still get) when you take 35 mm film in for developing and printing. And I think some of my prints look better than most of what I got from the photo labs. Photo lab quality can vary a lot.

A couple of negative things about this paper is that it seems to often be overpriced and hard to find. If you do a search for it on the Internet (using the product number) you will come up with "no longer available" or something like that quite a lot. I can't even find it on HP's own website (http://store.hp.com).

I think I'm going to try some different photo papers and see if I can do better.

product_title: Epson Expression Premium XP-610 Inkjet Multifunction Printer - Color - Photo Print - Desktop
review_headline: Short-lived, noisy, hard to use, baffling.
review_body:
This printer has many baffling design decisions. Here are some examples.

To print, you must manually open the front of the printer and pull out a paper receiving tray that's inexplicably connected to some resistive gear mechanism. This may feel like you're disassembling the printer, but you're not.

To refill the paper supply, you must pull the front of the printer by its hinges. This extracts the paper tray, which is also the bottom-most component of the printer, so you're guaranteed to scratch up your desk surface every time.

Although the printer will connect to Wi-Fi, it turns itself OFF after a short time instead of going to standby, meaning that you have to manually walk up to it to turn it on to print anything.

Every time the printer turns on and off, it goes through a complete song and dance, making a racket before printing anything.

The software is laggy and hard to use.

This printer didn't last a year. After complaining about its ink being low, it refused to print any cyan out of a new cartridge.

The only reason this printer got two stars instead of one is that its scanner is decent, and its print speed is quite respectable.

product_title: Mighty Bright XtraFlex2 Book Light
review_headline: Not worth the small savings over geniune item
review_body: As others have mentioned, this is a knock-off and not a true Mighty Bright. I've only had mine a few days and it works OK, but I didn't realize it was coming from China when I ordered it. When I discovered that, I ordered a real Mighty Bright Xtraflex2 from another web site in the US because I was in a hurry. With free shipping over the holidays, it was only about a dollar more and I received it in just a few days. As it happened, they both arrived on the same day, but I'm glad I ordered the second one. On the surface, the knock-off looks very similar, but one thing I noticed is that the goose neck on the authentic lamp is much better. It stays in place no matter how you bend it. The knock off does not do that. It will stay bent to some degree, but tends to spring back a little. I purchased mine to mount on a treadmill console, so that I can read while walking in the evenings. The fact that I would have to wrestle with the neck/head to keep it in position is a deal breaker. I have since put the knock-off in my tool box and have actually used it successfully for putting light on a project I was working on outside after dark. It works and while I'm more or less satisfied with it, it is certainly not worth saving a few bucks. Make sure to order the true Mighty Bright to avoid disappointment.

product_title: Canon Office and Business MX922 All in One Printer, Wireless and mobile printing
review_headline: Fantastic for pictures and all in all a well rounded printer.
review_body:
When I first received this printer I had buyers remorse. I've been so used to laser printers that it was hard to adjust to slower printing speeds and a noisier machine. It also takes longer to start printing and if you pause between jobs the printer goes through this whole noisy process cleaning it's printing heads. Also, the words are not as \\"crisp\\" These things bothered me and still do but the reality is that this is my home printer and I print maybe 10 pages a week so speed isn't really the priority and having the ink/energy saving mode on is ultimately a benefit.

Having the built in scanner is very nice. The few items I've scanned have been fantastic. The color was sharp and there was text recognition technology. The ADF is pretty fast and the pages are centered and all in all this scanner is way better than a xerox I bought for my office 3 years ago.

The duplex printing isn't all that good as the paper is printed, sucked back in and printed on the other side. It can really slow down a print job.

It took a little bit to set up my wireless printing properly (I had an issue printing from the chrome browser on my S3). Ultimately I just resorted to google print and print through the cloud. It now works fine.

But here is the reason that I'm starting to fall in love with this machine. If you want to get a printer that prints fantastic photo pictures this is your machine. When paired with the Canon Photo Paper Plus Glossy II the prints are amazing. They are on par with anything I've ever gotten from Walgreens or Shutterfly (grayscale pictures are a bit grainier). Now I don't have to worry about downloading pictures online and then ordering prints (which we never get around to doing). You can also print from your phone using the Canon Easy-Print App.

My opinion is that it is very difficult to find a \\"perfect\\" printer. So many people have so many different needs that it is impossible to service them all at an affordable price. For the $90 I paid I feel like I got really good value. Yes there are many minor quirks I have to deal with but overall it has all the functionality and need and then some.e I got really good value. That was according to the manufacturer customer support (in China but very responsive within 24 hours). I was using a memory stick that had a continuous loop of the VS and according to them there was no work around. review_headline: Arc 100 vs SanDisk Ultra II - VALUE DRIVES for HD Replacement
review_body:
Several of the major SSD manufacturers have come out with what I call "value drives" These are built to have a lower price point sacrificing of some speed and durability and warranty during compared to most of their higher performing brethren.

They offer significant improvements in performance and power consumption when traditional mechanical or hybrid drives. This is their target and they meet that need well and economically.

The Arc 100 series from OCZ is an example of this. Others are the Crucial MX100 and [[ASIN:B00M8ABFX6 SanDisk Ultra II]].

I got the Arc 100 as a drive to upgrade an older Dell Optiplex desktop PC. I had done a similar upgrade to a Dell Precision M6300 Laptop with the SanDisk Ultra II. So before I put the Arc 100 to its final purpose I cloned the Sandisk Ultra II with Centos 7 on it in the M6300 onto the OCZ Arc 100 and put it in place of the Ultra II. I then ran some tests and used it for a while to see how the Arc 100 ran compared to the Ultra II.

Both were pretty close in apparent speed copying big files and lots of small ones. The M6300 is sata II, not III, so that could be a factor in how much speed improvement I could get. But these drives are made for value and as a hard drive replacement. Either will operate very well.

The Arc 100 and Ultra II close in price. I've seen them within a dollar or so in price, but at the time of this review the Ultra II is about $15 more than the Arc 100. Both have 3 year warranties. The Ultra II claims power max writing power of 4.5w and idle power of 85mw. The Arc 100 claims "active" power of 3.45W and 60mw idle. In practice I could tell no difference in battery drain rate on the M6300 laptop.

So my bottom line is either drive is a great upgrade for a system with a traditional mechanical or hybrid hard drive for a desktop or laptop system. I would not recommend these for high performance use in servers or gaming machines.

The Arc 100 hits its target upgrade market accurately. It's a SSD value drive that will meet a lot of economically minded user's needs. For that I'm handing it 5 stars./>

review_body:
Pros: All-in-one functionality; Wireless capable; Photo printer; On-screen interface
Cons: Fragile wireless; Ink use; Problematic print head, Noisy; Complicated interfaces

Bottom line: Not recommended. There's a reason this model has a 1 1/2-star rating. I used to swear by HP printers but this one has been a disappointment.

I picked up this one to replace an excellent all-in-one that fell victim to a lightning strike after 10 years. This one had all the features we were looking for but was relatively new at the time so there were no reviews.
We had no problem using different MS Operating Systems (XP, Vista, 7 & 8) and it seemed to work fine; albeit noisily.
The wireless transmitter/receiver conked out shortly after the warranty expired but I created a workaround using a spare wireless router. Changing the print default was a daily occurrance. Despite repeated attempts to set the defaults in the OS and printer, it seemed that the next day it was right back to color and high definition. No matter how much or little printing we do, the ink tanks require monthly replacement - and they're not cheap. Possibly due to increased ink use, the print head clogs about every nine months and requires disassembly and overnight soaking.
Truthfully, I'm tired of screwing with this thing.
Oh, how I wish our far thriftier 8450 could fax and scan.

It frequently prints poor quality and needs to have go through a self-cleaning process.  In addition, though it says it will accept photos via the usb port, it has never recognized anything I've put in the usb port.  I can't tell you how many times in the middle of work or homework projects, I have wanted to throw this thing out the window.  It's totally and completely unreliable.  I am researching new products for a replacement.  I want a printer that works most of the time.

product_title: Canon Office Products MG5620 Black Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner and Copier
review_headline: A great all-in-one printer, but not enough ink for serious photo printing.
review_body:
The Canon Pixma MG5620 is an all-in-one printer with scanner, copier and printer capabilities (no fax). The main headline here is that this printer uses Wi-Fi to your home network, so any device (PC, Mac, tablet or smartphone) can print documents or photos to your printer.

Since it's from the team at Canon and part of the "Pixma" line, photo quality is a priority. This will make borderless photo prints up to 8.5 x 11 inches on a variety of photo papers. There is a typo in the description of the "Print" specifications on the Amazon product page that claims this printer can handle larger paper sizes like 11 inches x 17 inches and 13 inches x 19 inches, but that is an error on the Amazon page.

Wireless printing is relatively easy to setup, but I will caution Mac OS and iOS users that the folks at Apple have a hard time getting any of their devices to play nice with printers. I usually have to restart my wife's MacBook Air or my iPhone if I want to print something or the print job will not be sent to the printer. I have ZERO problems using PCs or Android devices with this printer ... so it's a problem with Apple, not Canon.

The photo quality coming out of this printer is fantastic. Unless you are very picky about your prints you'll have a hard time seeing a difference in photo quality when comparing the prints from this printer to prints from a photo lab.

My only complaint about this printer is that the ink tanks are too small considering that this is being aimed at people who want to print photos. Photos (particularly borderless photos) consume a massive amount of ink and if you print a large number of photos that use the same color then you'll quickly run out of ink in one or more of the ink tanks/cartridges.

For example, when I printed some photos from a beach vacation with lots of blue skies and blue water the cyan ink cartridge ran out. When I printed a bunch of night shots with black skies the regular black and pigment black inks ran low. The size of the ink tanks wouldn't be a big deal if this was a work printer and you just print a bunch of pages of black text, but if you're primary purpose for this printer is to make photographs then you better buy a bunch of spare ink cartridges.

If Canon made this same printer with tanks that are twice as large then I would have given it 5 stars. Canon does offer "XL" ink cartridges that are larger, but they don't hold much more ink than the standard cartridges. product_title: Doinshop New Cool Concise Delicate Jinhao Shooter Series Fountain Pen Sliver Medium Nib White
review_headline: Yep it's a knock off but it writes really well.
review_body: I've recently started collecting fountain pens, right? The vast majority of my collection involves super-inexpensive pens made in China (don't judge...I'm on a budget) which, if chosen with care and flushed before first use via a drop of grease-dissolving dish soap in a bowl of water to remove the residual factory machining oils left behind on the feed, will write just fine. When I saw this painfully obvious Jinhao copy of a Lamy Safari I thought "wow, that's crass and all copyright-violating...wait, it's less than 4 bucks with free shipping? Oh okay why not, then" and bought the sucker. I seem to recall when I first saw the listing for it on Amazon that it used a #6 nib like all of Jinhao's other pens. Turns out that's not the case. When it showed up in the mail (took about 3 weeks) I found that it has a narrow, short nib "almost" like a Lamy pen but not quite the same dimensions, so don't buy this thinking you can put a Lamy nib on it. But for what it's worth, after I gave it the aforesaid flush-out cleaning, I put some Noodler's "Cactus Fruit Purple" ink in it and it wrote just as nice and smoothly as an actual Lamy does. It writes with a sort of medium-fine point....if you really tried to get me to be specific I'd have to say it's more "fine" than "medium". But the ink flow is just fine, it's as comfy in the hand as a Lamy Safari, the line it lays down is consistent and, yeah, again, it writes smoother than you'd expect for a $4 dollar knockoff. So far I think they only come in white. Also, it uses a standard type converter rather than the Lamy pens which can only use proprietary Lamy converters, and the pen's barrel is missing the little ink windows that Lamy pens have (Lamy does that so you can tell at a glance how much ink is left in your converter or ink cartridge...and by the way, ink cartridges are the Devil; please do your wallet *and* the environment a favor and get a converter & use bottled ink) so you could use this as an "eyedropper-fill" pen if you wanted to. Feel free to contact me for instructions on how to do this, or go to any YouTube video blog about fountain pens like sbrebrown or Goulet Pens and you'll find all kinds of help on topics like that. Bottom line...yeah, it's a shameless knock off of a better pen, but for the money it writes really good, and if you lose it or it gets stolen from your desk at work, oh well, you've lost a $4 pen rather than your $150 Pilot Falcon fountain pen or what have you.his as an "eyedropper-fill" pen if you wanted to. review_headline: Outstanding vibrant paper and great bang for your buck.
review_body:
I have been using this paper for year. It never fails to deliver bright, crisp, clear results. The colors are well saturated without being overdone. I am a professional photographer and though I don't use this paper for fine art printing (and I don't believe canon even intended it for fine are printing) I do use it professionally. I photograph student theatre and print the cast photos up on this paper. I do fund raisers for shelter animals and print the photo advertisements on this paper. I always send my studio clients home with one print from our photo session and I typically print it on this paper. I can't begin to tell you how many times a client has asked me how much I paid for my printer because they can't believe the quality of the print I am sending home with them. The fact is that I pair this paper with a fairly inexpensive can multifunction printer.

For high end exhibit prints I use fine art paper although I am fairly certain that folks would be just as happy with a print on this paper. It really is that good.

BOTTOM LINE: if you have a canon printer and you use canon inks, you will be thrilled with the results. I am sure that this paper would hold up equally well when paired with other printers but since I don't have other printers I don't want to make that statement.
