product_title: Canon MAXIFY MB5020 Wireless All-In-One Color Printer with Scanner, Copier and Fax (Airprint and Cloud Compatible)
review_headline: Canon Maxify MB 5020 vs. Epson WF-4630 vs. Canon Maxify MB 2020
review_body:
We picked this copier to use in one of our home office areas. We have another Canon Copier (MB2020) and an Epson (WF-4630) in use and we did a brief comparative analysis for those looking at other options, here are our thoughts:

· Overview

o High Performance Business Printer, All-in-One with cloud connectivity (Wireless-Print-Copy-Scan-Fax-Cloud Link)
o Wireless printing and scanning from computer, tablet & smartphones.
o Cloud Link connects with services such as OneDrive, Dropbox, Evernote, Google Drive, Twitter, Canon Images to print or save scanned images.
o 30,000 page peak monthly duty cycle
o Size in Use approx: 18 1/4 " (W) x 24 " (D) x11 1/2" (H). Note Depth includes paper out put tray extended. W/o it extended it’s about 18” with letter size paper in tray. Height goes to 13” with feeder lid open.
o Weight is about 25 lbs
o Included is a quick setup guide, CD w/ SW, power cord, phone cord, warranty/safety info, regular ink cartridges (one of each, total 4), and printer.

· Features

o 3.0” touchscreen LCD, works well but could be a little larger.
o Auto 2-sided printing
o 250 sheet tray capacity
o 50 sheet Auto Document Feeder (ADF)
o Paper sizes: 4" x 6", 5" x 7", 8" x 10", Letter, Legal, U.S. #10 Envelopes
o Max Paper Size : Flatbed: 8.5" x 11.7" ADF: 8.5" x 14"
o Max Resolution: 1200 x 1200 dpi for optical (flatbed) & ADF.
o Print Speed: Black:ESAT: Approx. 23.0 ipm and Color:ESAT: Approx 15.0 ipm
o USB port for photo uploading or scanning to USB flash drive.
o Individual color cartridges (Black, Yellow, Cyan, Magenta), with two sizes regular and XL. XL provides more economical printing.
o Print resolution claimed at 600 x 1200 dpi
o Supports access point mode, which you can connect to the printer wirelessly from a computer, tablet, smart phone even if you don’t havea wireless router.
o Supports operating systems from XP to Windows 8.1 and Windows Server. Always check to make sure you have the right OS.

· Product came very well packaged and protected in a sturdy cardboard box. Inside, the accessories and documentation were all together and contained in a smaller cardboard box.

· Installation and Operation:

o Directions are easy to follow on the quick guide. There is no paper manual, it’s on the CD or Canon has on-line manuals which are better than the CD manual.
o Ink cartridges I found to be easy to install sliding in and snaping in place. Cleaning of print heads took what seemed like a long time, 7+ minutes and alignment of the heads another 3+ min.
o One big concern was there is a warning notice in the box that says not to remove an ink cartridge until a new one is prepared to be installed. Once you remove an ink cartridge, the printer will not operate even if the removed ink cartridge is just reinstalled. AND if the removed ink cartridge is just reinstalled and stays un-removed the printer may malfunction and need to be repaired. This just seems wrong and a poor design. Probably put in place to prevent people from using after market cartridges. But I could see the wrong ink cartridge color installed in the wrong slot, then what? You can’t remove it and re-install it. Or if you bought the wrong ink cartridge inadvertently, pulled the empty one? You can end up with a “bricked” printer for a period of time until you had the right ink cartridge.
o One quirk was that the language selection did not follow the guide, it asked me after the printer head cleaning and alignment vs before per the quick guide.
o Another strange thing is that the paper tray come flush with the unit, but to use it, you have to expand it until this clip snaps in place. At that point the tray is sticking out about 2 ¾ for standard letter size paper. The output paper tray holder then coverit up. To change to legal size paper you have to unclip it and slide it further out.
o Also, something annoying is every time you remove the tray you have to register the type of paper you have loaded in the tray. I guess it can’t recognize what size you have in.
o Connectivity was easy, via ethernet (wired LAN) or wireless LAN. I connected via wireless to a laptop running Windows 7 Professional, a desktop running Vista, an iPhone 4 and an iPad. Connection to the wireless router was seamless with WPS setup. The first computer I connected, I printed a Test Page and noticed that every 2 1/8” I had a noticeable streak through black text. I printed a few more and it did the same. So I went into setup and ran another “clean” of the heads. After the second clean the streaking went away.
o Via an iPad I printed a double sided email w/ no problem.
o An issue I would think for small businesses and home users is that the ADF cannot handle 2 sided originals without you flipping over and re-feeding the paper. This seems like a big hassle if you're copying/scanning/faxing a large number of double-sided sheets.
o Also, the lid when closing it is like spring loaded in the last couple of inches and slams down if you are not careful.
o The printer automatically went out and checked for newer version of the firmware. It then notifies you via the LCD to install the latest firmware update. This was very easy and seamless, just follow the prompts.
o The CD I loaded into the desk top. The initial user interface to walk you through the install was nothing to write about and took about 15 minutes. The SW itself is ok.
o The scanning function worked great uploading directly to the desktop or onto a USB Flash Drive.

· Comparison Test: Epson WF-4630 vs Canon Maxify MB5020 vs Canon Maxify MB2020.

o I ran a simple test, printing a jpeg image and scanning a photo.
o The Canon’s do run noisier than the Epson.
o Results: As expected the MB5020 and MB2020 were pretty much identical in clarity, colors, contrast, etc. However there was a difference between brands (I view the EPSON WF-4630 comparable to the MB5020).
§ Color photo printing: Epson had brighter colors and printed lighter so dark features in a photo stood out better. It was also faster. But where there wasn’t much difference like someone with blond hair standing beside a white wall you would get less contrast and definition. The Canons however had better sharpness and detail, probably because they had better contrast or wider range of color.
§ Scanning a photo, the Cannon was slightly better as the colors were just slightly more vibrant. I scanned at 600 dpi, photo, and all of them onto a flash drive.
§ Text printing the Epson was slightly better.

· Summary: I was surprised by the Canon not-so-good design of the paper cassette holder, the whole ink cartridge potentially “bricking” the printer, and some of the other weaknesses (can’t automatically handle double sided originals). You have some better options out there. If I could give a 3.5 stars I would, the only reason for giving it a 4 star is the comparison test I ran vs the EPSON where the images were slightly better.

4/5 stars.

product_title: Canon MAXIFY MB2320 Wireless All-In-One Color Printer with Scanner, Copier and Fax (Airprint and Cloud Compatible)
review_headline: A real workhorse for not a lot of money
review_body:
I've been using a Brother MFCJ6920DW Wireless Multifunction Inkjet Printer with Scanner, Copier and Fax for about a year, so I had something to compare with the Canon MAXIFY MB2320.
Cutting to the chase, I like the Canon better than the more expensive Brother machine.
The Canon seems faster than the Brother and makes better color prints. It was easy to set up and I had it installed and running within an hour of its arrival on my doorstep.
As one other reviewer mentioned, it was prone to dropping the Wifi connection early on, but I just woke it from a two-week slumber to print an email and after the electronic equivalent of some yawning and stretching, it dutifully spit out the hard copy without demanding to be re-started. I'm not sure what changed, but I'm happy to be done with what I considered the only serious shortcoming of an otherwise great machine.
Like some other reviewers, I was surprised to find the paper trays don't slide in flush with the front of the device. I'd rather that they did, but that's a minor cosmetic detail.
It's also easier to print envelopes on the Canon, but I wish the machine would accept more than 10 #10 envelopes at a time.
I installed the Canon printer app on my iPhone and it works perfectly.
As a scanner/copier it works every bit as well as my Canon flatbed scanner. Making multi-page pdf files is a breeze and had me hunting around my office for more documents to digitize.
Considering the price, the Canon MAXIFY MB2320 is a very impressive bargain.

review_headline: Here's a good tool to add to the took box - that ...
review_body:
No more taking the office scissors to the garage! Here's a good tool to add to the took box - that will be up to "shop" tasks. These scissors have comfortable grips that fit even my big hands.

I have to note that as-new, the blade sharpening seems a little rough. I expected to see a really smooth blade, but it's less precision than I would expect. However, cutting some very thin coated paper, it was a perfect cut. On to the harder stuff.

They are effortless to use and cut through a variety of materials easily. Project one included open foam sheeting and some really thick closed foam strips. They will also cut cardboard easily - the thicker blades don't bend like standard consumer types when cutting thick materials.They will cut thin sheet metal though I'm not sure that I want to do that often with these - but they will do when you need a small amount of trimming. I tried cutting some polypropylene rope - lot of strands in it and though it takes some work, like with any scissors, these seemed to make quicker work of it with the apparently sharper blades. Again, the thickness of the blade helps here, standard scissor blades will bend on this rope. It slices with ease through plastic banding that straps heavy packages together. Plastic sheeting - even really thin stuff - is also easily managed (sometimes the really thin stuff will not get cut by cheaper scissors but will just spread the blade apart).

Anything you would attempt with regular scissors can be done well with these.

The ruler is a great idea - until you try use it. To me, it's backwards - the measure should start not at the tip, but near the pivot point. The typeface they used for the number is way too stylish - if you saw these numbers on a Stanley tape measure you would never buy it. With a little practice you can use the markings without the numbers.

The non-stick feature seems to work. I tried cutting cellophane tape, packing tape and duct tape with no issues. Usually duct tape will hang on to my regular scissors, but these definitely didn't stick.

Finally, while this is not a feature that counts for a lot, they look good in a shop. The black and gray definitely belong in a shop. There's no practical value, but sitting next to a Stanley box cutter with similar colors, it looks like it "belongs:" Small detail, but I like it.

product_title: BestDealUSA USB Laser Scan Barcode Scanner Bar Code Reader White Hand Held
review_headline: Low cost, dependable, and easy to use!
review_body:
My current brand name scanner cost well over $130 when I bought it and I thought this would not compare to it at all. I was wrong.

I use this at a cellphone dealer, where many of the barcodes on the phones can be quite tiny, or in the case of the iPhone boxes, tiny, and faint (some iDiot - see what I did there? - decided they should have grey barcodes on a white background) which some scanners have difficulty with. Also works perfectly fine with huge barcodes (at least half a foot long) like you see on some shipping labels.

I have had 0 problems with this scanner after using it for a few months. The manual is written in Chenglish, and not very helpful, but if you've ever used a scanner before, you won't need it. It is completely plug and play with no programming needed. Has a VERY bright green LED at the top (I ended up using electric tape to cover 2/3rds of it as it could almost substitute as a flashlight). The build quality is really great, I've thrown it down a few times and never had to worry about it breaking apart as it feels pretty solid. It's also very ergonomic and feels great in the hand.

Would recommend this for any small business that doesn't want to invest a lot of money into equipment. I'll definitely be buying more when I begin to upgrade my other computers which currently use PS/2 scanners.

review_headline: Great for wood blocks and cutting boards
review_body:
Exactly what I was looking for. Make sure you have a clean, dry cutting board or wood block, then apply a coating of this stuff with a cloth. Let it sit overnight and wipe it down in the morning.

I live in Arizona where we don't have much in the way of humidity and untreated wood will dry out, crack and split. I used mineral oil in the past, but I was applying it all the time to keep the wood treated. The addition of the beeswax makes the treatment last a lot longer and the cutting boards seem to be even more waterproof.

product_title: Digitone Call Blocker Plus
review_body:
I have two of these and have recommended this gadget to everyone I know. I have one at my parents' house (over three years) and one at mine (over two years). The parents are elderly and had been bombarded with sales/survey/scam calls. This little box solved most of that problem. It did take a few months to add all the area codes, etc., but it's been nice and quiet for years except for occasional spikes when the telemarketers shift to new numbers. Adding Nomorobo has helped bring the number of those calls down.

At my house, I have Ooma, which permits personal blacklisting, has a community blacklist and global area code blocking. Maybe one call a month gets through. However, this political season has been rough. We've been bombarded with calls from assorted numbers, usually from our local area code. I couldn't do a global block on the area code and was tired of playing whack-a-mole, so I got fed up this morning and changed the setting on my Digitone to invited callers only. Problem solved.

The instructions are not great, but understandable. I recommend printing them from the website as the included instructions are printed in a font so small that you will need a magnifying glass to read them.

I did not purchase my units on Amazon as the price was significantly cheaper elsewhere.

product_title: Brother MFCL2740DW Wireless Monochrome Printer with Scanner, Copier and Fax
review_headline: MY BROTHER ALWAYS HAS MY BACK!!
review_body: As a user of Brother laser printers for the past 10 years in my medical office, I swore I would only buy Brother when I needed machines for my home.  The MFC-L2740DW does not disappoint.    Obviously, if you are reading this, then you know all the features of the machine, so you are probably deciding between models.  This has all features/specs and even some better than the competitors in this price class but when you add in the solid track record of Brother machines, this is a no brainer.    This machine is fast and extremely quiet when compared to previous models.  Brother must have changed their cooling fans because they do not run as long or nearly as loud as previous. Also the sound of printing is considerably quieter as well.  Scanning function is faster than most scanners I have used in the past with immediate upload to wireless tablet/phone if desired.    AirPrint works extremely fast with all iPhone/iPad models that are AirPrint capable and the wireless/wired network connect is painless to set up.    Absolutely perfect for home use but I would not have a problem using this in a small office setting that doesnt demand an extreme workload. Also, toner cartriges for this model are cheapest I have ever paid for toner.    Oh yeah, and the touchscreen is awesome. The only thing, and I mean ONLY thing I have a problem with is that on the older models and some current as well, you were able to copy at the press of just the start button. Being there is no start button, you first have to select \\"copy\\" from the home screen then have to enter the number of copies then start. Really no big deal but it would of been nice to keep that function.    Overall, just a great machine.

review_headline: Cushion part of handle wears and peels off in chunks
review_body:
At first, I loved these scissors. They have sharp blades that cut smoothly through fabric and many other materials well. The blades don't stick at all and the handles have a comfortable grip.

However, as time passed the cushy orange "comfort" part of the handle started to peel off just from normal wear and friction against the user's fingers. Every other scissors I've used with the same type of cushioned comfort material has never done this. The material came off in peels at first, then a couple of small chunks. So disappointing. Eventually the blades dulled, too - which can definitely be sharpened - but I don't know that I'll even bother considering the state of the handles.

This happened to both pairs of scissors I got from 2 separate stores. Very disappointing. They were great while they lasted but not worth the price for the use I got out of them - would not purchase again.

product_title: Epson ES3000 Ultra Portable Projection Screen (V12H002S3Y)
review_headline: Epson calls the ES3000 the "Duet Pro" and it's perfect for my home theater
review_body:
Epson calls the ES3000 the "Duet Pro" and it's perfect for my home theater. I wasn't going to remodel the room, and rearranging it for a wall-mounted screen wasn't practical, so a tripod model made more sense. Most of them look like they belong in a church basement, but the ES3000 is very attractive and the construction quality is excellent.

Although it is true that the top and bottom edges of the screen curve forward, this is noticeable only when sitting off to a side while the screen is still relatively new. if you leave the ES3000 open for an extended period, gravity eventually flattens out the screen nicely, to the point where the curl is very minimal. See the picture, taken at an angle. Calibrating my projector, which has a full set of adjustments, the color accuracy came out perfectly for the Rec. 709 standard, according to an X-Rite i1Display meter.

I have used the ES3000's width setting to lock in 4:3, but now I just leave it open for 16:9, regardless of what I'm watching. The screen opens to its full 80" diagonal width and it stays there. I haven't had a reason to use the carrying case, but I have needed to take the screen down on occasion, and I appreciate how quickly and easily this can be done.

review_headline: Cute idea, but unfortunately pretty useless
review_body:
I had high hopes for these rubber cable/cord organizers, but the adhesive attached to the back is cheap, and hardly sticky at all! I attached three onto three different surfaces (manufactured wood, metal, and a plaster wall), and after about one day of use, ALL three fell off! I can understand getting one dud in a box of six, but three?? I wasn't willing to take my chances after that.

This is very upsetting for me because I really wanted to like these! They're super adorable and are firm, yet still flexible enough to hold any cords (up to 6mm in diameter). They come in a pack of 6, in three assorted colors (neon pink, lime green, and highlighter orange) and have a rubbery, silicone-y texture which make them flexible. It's too bad the adhesive is so poorly made... they should use better quality adhesive, or better yet, make the sticky surface reusable with a suction cup. Once these babies fall off, you won't be able to use them again, which is a bummer.

I would not waste my money on this!

product_title: Stanley 8” Piranha Premium Titanium Scissor with a Non-stick Blade and Ergonomic Handle, Gray/Black (SCI8TINS)
review_body:
The review sample that I received is possibly the best pair of general purpose scissors that I have ever owned. There are a few things that I don't care for, but they are more a personal preference. I'll get those out of the way first.

At the top of my list of 'rathers' is the rule on the blade. I wish the numbers started at the fulcrum instead of the tip, That would make measured cuts more easy since you are not subtracting in your head while cutting. I do like the thick lines and the high contrast against the black, titanium finish. Second is the action is a little stiff, although I am sure that will correct itself through use and breaking it in.

What I love far outweighs the 'rathers' and at the top of that list is the sharp edge blade, the fact that it is titanium and will not easily dull. Another subtle feature is the slight - but effective - texture on the handle and loops. They are non-slip even when wet. Finally, the points when the blades are close are not as acute, making these safer when carrying them. Don't get me wrong, the points are very sharp when the blades are opened or even slightly separated.

Overall, these seem practically indestructible, and I am betting that the edge will retain its sharpness even after months of heavy use. If you could only have a single pair of general purpose scissors I recommend these.

product_title: iGearPro USB Voice Recorder - Portable 4GB Flash Drive Digital Audio Recorder with 15-Hour Battery Life / No Flashing Light When Recording
review_body:
I must admit I have a fondness for devices that can be used for... unexpected monitoring. :) Getting the chance to try out the IBSound USB flash drive and digital audio voice recorder made me happy. In short, this is a very good product that gives me some nice options in various situations.

This looks like, for all intents and purposes, a normal USB drive. The 4GB size is good enough to hold a fair amount of content, so using it for that purpose alone is fine. There's a slide switch on the one side that pushes the USB head out of the unit, and that's a nice touch that keeps the plug from being damaged. The other side also has a small slide switch, and that's what activates the voice recorder. When you slide the small switch forward, it puts the unit in voice record mode. There's a (very) little red light that shows when you first turn it on, and it switches to blue when it's recording. The lights are so small that's there's little chance anyone would see them. When you plug the unit into your computer, you'll see a folder that has all the Windows media files of the recording. Plugging it in is also how you charge it. There's no charging indicator, so it's hard to tell how full or empty it is, but I'd just recommend keeping it plugged in most of the time "to be sure" it's ready to go.

The sound quality of the files were excellent. I can see using this during conferences to aid in note-taking during important sessions. It would also be a good tool to record yourself during speeches and talks, as you can easily play back the recording for feedback on how well you did. And of course, without any statements about the legality of such actions, it would be great to make sure certain conversations could not be misrepresented later. :)

I'm very happy with the IBSound USB drive, and I'm glad that I have it in my USB thumb drive collection for those "certain situations" where it will come in handy. :)

review_body:
Did not fit my Brother HL-2270 DW printer!!!!!

This thing does not have the same gears that grab toner from the toner cartridge to distribute it onto the drum. Instead, toner is pooled into the sides of the drum and eventually into the body of the printer. No matter how many times I reset the drum and cartridge units with each other, and back into the body of the printer, this drum unit pooled up toner, jammed the printer, and made a grotesque mess.

I vacuumed the inside of the printer and cleaned the rest as best I could with alcohol swabs, I put my OLD Brother drum back in using the SAME toner cartridge, and aside from the warnings to replace the drum which appeared on my screen, it worked fine. Clearly, it was the replacement drum from EPS that was crap.

I stayed away from the really low priced replacement drums (some on Amazon are as low as $14.00) because I thought by paying a little more, I'd get a better product. This was not the case.

product_title: Ipevo CDCU-04IP VX-1 Internet Conference Station for Conference Calls and Remote Meeting
review_headline: This has a good quality of sound
review_body:
A solution for anyone who likes to Skype in a group.

I know this is intended for business calls, and I intend to use it for that sometimes, but I find it's also very helpful for Skyping with a group of people. Typically, for a virtual meeting or a Skype call, the microphone is on the computer, or somewhere on the camera. And the speaker is also somewhere on the computer. With this device, a group can be gathered around the microphone with it on the table in the center. Everyone can look towards the camera to see the person with whom they are chatting, but the sound comes from the microphone in the center of the table. And the microphone input for each participant is also in the middle of the table.

This has a good quality of sound, and it as very easy to hook up. The microphone can be muted, and it's also possible to have just one side on, or all four sides of the microphone on. Has a volume control for the speaker. The device is powered by USB and it has 5 ft of cable for the USB and for plugging into the headphones port of the computer. In a few office settings, it might be nice to have a longer cable for conference use, but for home use, it's perfect for me.

There is a non-stick pad on the bottom to keep it from scooting around the table.

review_headline: Small price to pay for something so valuable.
review_body: I bought these not only to protect myself from credit card fraud and identity theft, but to protect the cards from wear and for my own personal safety. I'm not sure if everyone pays attention to detail but here is my advice. When you open your wallet at the market, store, and other public places, people notice what you have in your wallet. When ever anybody opens their wallet at the supermarket I always notice how many credit cards and department store cards they have. Now if I pay attention how much attention do you think criminals pay to your wallet. The RFID chips in credit cards and ID cards, holds all of your sensitive info such as card numbers, expiration dates, names, addresses, etc. I did a little research and you can buy RFID readers and writers for $25 from china, I'm not a credit card genius but with all these department stores getting hacked. I think the credit card is a little outdated as far as security. It's reasonably priced and a no brainer for anyone traveling or looking for added security.

product_title: Epson Expression Premium XP-820 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner, Copier and Fax
review_headline: Good as personal printer but not as a small home office printer
review_body:
Rating 3 1/2 Stars

The printer is made for light duty printing. The printer will satisfy anyone looking for all in one printer for occasional printing of documents and photos.

Pros.
Easy Setup - Plug in the printer, locate your wireless network, and enter in the key. I would recommend going to Epson's website to ensure you have the latest drivers

Cloud Options - In my opinion this is the biggest pro. You sign up for an Epson connect account and register your printer. You can email a print job to the printer. Scan to the cloud is the feature I use most for scanning documents to PDF. I wish Epson include OneDrive

Photos: I have higher end photo printer but for a good quality photo this printer does a great job with the two black cartridges.

Cons:
INK: If you plan to a large amount of photos the cost to own will be high. The ink cartridges are small and eat through the ink quickly.

Small Paper Tray: This printer does not hold a too much paper and you will be refilling it often.

Slow print speeds. This is not a fast printer. I also have a Workforce printer, which is much faster.

Document Feeder: The document feeder can be finicky. I have paper feed multiple times.

This printer is for someone who will have low volume printing and enjoy having good photos.

If you are looking for a small home office printer look at the workforce line

product_title: Canon PIXMA PRO-10 Color Professional Inkjet Photo Printer
review_headline: After several months, not worth the money and the cost of the ink.
review_body: I have had this printer now for several months and primarily print photos of various sizes through photoshop and documents.  Although it does print outstanding BW photos, I am less enthused about the color.  I find the color prints to be be darker and less saturated than the photos appear on my computer screen within photoshop.  I have to overcompensate on the brightness and color saturation in photoshop to get the print to look like what I expected it to look like in the first place.  This shouldn't happen, it should accurately print the image that is on the computer screen.  I also have a beef with the labeling of the paper feeds.  When trying to first use the printer, I assumed the rear tray to be on the back of the computer where in reality, it is the front of the two feeds and on top of the printer (as I learned from Canon Tech Support).  The start up instructions don't label these.  I don't know what the one is called on the rear of the printer.....the front feed?  Also, the paper feed on the rear of the printer has never worked properly.  If I put a stack of blank paper in the tray, it will try to feed all of the sheets at once rather than one at a time so I end up having to feed one sheet at a time, putting the second sheet in when the first is done printing, etc.  Finally, I don't mind that the printer is printing slower than other printers however, I do mind the 20-60 seconds of whirring noises the innards make while its thinking of printing something after I've pressed the print button.  For the price of this printer and after reading all of the hype, I expected this printer to function better and produce better color prints w/o having to turn the photo into a caricature of itself.  Maybe mine is a dog, but I won't buy another.

product_title: Epson WorkForce WF-2630 All-In-One Wireless Color Printer with Scanner, Copier and Fax
review_body:
I am thoroughly enjoying this printer. I got it up and running in less than 15 minutes. It isn't much harder than plugging it in, popping in the ink, putting in paper, and running some software. No extra cables are included If you want to use the printer through direct USB, you do need to buy a printer USB cable. If you want to hook up through a wired network connection, you need an Ethernet cable. And so on for a fax. I wanted to hook up wirelessly, so I didn't need to buy anything. (I did pick up a printer USB cable anyway, in case of emergencies.) If you are hooking up wirelessly, you can use Wi-Fi or WiDi. I used Wi-Fi on a Windows 7, 64-bit, AMD machine.

The printer tray holds 150 sheets had has an engraved guide so that you can set it correctly to your paper size. The printer itself will have you confirm paper size and type. I have had some small issue with paper jamming the first time I load it. The tray isn't the nicest, and I don't like that you're supposed to remove it completely when you reload. For some reason, they set it up so that you load paper away from the paper instead of into.

The print quality is nice. It isn't comparable to my photo printer, but I'd happily print out casual photos on this machine. It is also extremely fast, even when printing on both sides of the paper. Although it is ink jet, it comes close to laser speeds. Each ink cartridge supposedly lasts 220 sheets. That's a very nice number; however, I haven't managed to print out 220 pages yet.

I like the scanning and copying functions. The fax, however, is useless to me. (I wouldn't even know how to set up a fax line.) Scanning speed is similar to most other scanners I've used. As always, it is quicker at lower quality.

I've had no issues with the software, either on my PC or on the printer. There is a downloadable user guide if you get into a tight space.

product_title: Pilot Vanishing Point Metallics Collection Retractable Fountain Pen
review_headline: Best Fountain Pen I've Ever Used. Without A Doubt!
review_body:
I ordered this as I was looking for my next long-term fountain pen. Somebody recommended this one to me, so I decided to take the plunge and check it out.

I am extremely impressed with the pen's build quality. I have the black matte one, so it feels very sturdy, assuring, and comfortable. I know there's a clip down the barrel, but because of the way I hold my pen, I actually don't find it uncomfortable whatsoever. It feels perfectly fine for me when I write with it. I especially like how the clip is in a different place so the pen will be aiming upward whenever you have it clipped away in a pocket or something. I also like the added value of how the pen comes included with an ink converter, so if you have any ink lying around, you can load it up manually.

The pen is extremely versatile and portable. I carry it around regularly with my pocket notebook (a grid-dotted Leuchtturm1917), and I find that it works extremely well. Alongside that, I use it with another couple of notebooks. One is a CR Gibson journal that I use for organizing ideas for my stories and novels, and another is some off-brand notebook I use for studying other languages. It works well with all the paper that I've tried it on, with the exception of modern Moleskine paper. Of course, that's the fault of Moleskine themselves and not the manufacturers of this pen.

The pen feels quite sturdy, and I can say if you want a long-term fountain pen you can use for years to come, you will get an excellent value with this one. The best part for me is that I seriously feel like this pen makes me want to find excuses to use it. It just feels that excellent.

review_body:
I ordered this screen for my new theater room after reading all the good reviews posted by other buyers. I received the screen in 2 days after placing the order (Great work Amazon)

I declined to mess with it and wanted to return the item since the issue seemed like a know issue and the product description had no mention of having to adjust the product in order for it to work properly.

I asked the process to return the item and I was told to file a claim which I did.

Apart from the motor issue, the screen did look like it was well made. I projected a bluray movie and it looked phenomenal. Too bad the seller didn't want to earn my business.

My 2 cents: Stay away from this product and this seller and spend a little more to order a better product from Elite cos it seems like the motor issue is a known issue.

review_body: If you're meticulous about having clean cases for your reloads, this works. About  an hour in the pins with a dash of dish detergent and they come out better than 5 hours in dry treated walnut. Reason being it not only cleans the outside, it cleans the inside of the case as well as the primer pockets. Instructions tell you to add a small amount of Lemi-Shine but I can't see a big difference either way. A little messier than dry treated media because you're working wet and you have to let the cases dry but to me it's well worth it. Works very well even on dirty, stained range brass. I use 2-1/2 lbs of pins in the HF 3lb tumbler but should have gone for the dual drum. I've processed 5000 rounds so far and I'm convinced. The picture is some dirty .30 cal after 45 minutes. Another plus was not having to listen to the noisy vibratory cleaner since tumblers are much, much quieter. Maybe I wouldn't recommend this method to the occasional reloader but if you want really clean cases, this works.

product_title: PILOT "Elite 95s / Deep Red"
review_headline: Love it! Pilot just seems to know how to make pens.
review_body:
I love my new pen. I am a bit of a fountain pen addict and my collection is getting a bit ridiculous. I loved the retro-styling of this pen and as I understand it, this is actually a reproduction of the old "Elite" model. If you look at other listings that are from the USA you will notice a slight difference. The U.S. version has a simple upper-case "E." This Japanese listing is different in that the "E" is replaced with the model it was designed after and it says "Elite."
Cool design is one thing but it need to write well and it does; very well, in fact. I am suprised how smooth this EF nib is. Flow is perfect. Although many fountain pen users seem to love pens that dump gallons of ink on the page, I prefer a reasonable amount of flow so I can see the color of the ink. This pen hits that sweet spot of never skipping or hard-starting and not being too wet either.
This pen is very light! Be prepared for that. Unposted it is practically weightless. I have medium sized hands and I can actually write wight this pen unposted. Many with larger hands will need to post the pen because it is very short without the cap. Speaking of the cap; it is a very interesting friction fit that just seems to glide into place. I love putting it on and taking it off. There is no click, just smooth smooth smooth until it hits the stop. I fly a lot and so far no leaks or issues with this pen at all.
Here is the one and only gripe I have; the pen does not come with a converter. I know the price is excellent considering you are getting a gold nib but how much does it cost to throw a CON-20 in the box? Not sure if this is how they all come or just from this seller. I recently purchased a Platinum 3776 Century from a Japanese website that doesn't come with a converter even though I have seen plenty of review videos of the same pen that all mention the pen comes with a converter. I suspect some of these sellers might be pulling out converters to sell separately. This one came sealed in plastic so that is most likely not the case hear. Regardless, a converter would have been nice. It did come with a single black cartridge. If I could knock off a half star for the converter issue I would but I don't want to take away from the review of the pen and its performance because I really do think it is great.

product_title: Canon Original 104 Toner Cartridge - Black
review_body: A lot of people complain that this cartridge is small and runs out of toner too fast... I disagree. I have found that when the printer says to replace the cartridge because the toner is low (or out), ignore it. Take the cartridge out of the machine, gently shake it side to side to redistribute the toner, and place it back in the printer. You'll have to put up with the flashing light and/or messages for awhile but hopefully you'll get use to it like I have. When your page comes out completely blank THEN it's time for a new one. I believe printers are set up to calculate usage by counting pages, but it really depends on what's being printed on those pages. On average I get 2,147 copies per cartridge with this shake/replace method and am very satisfied with it. It's the only one I trust in my Canon printer!

product_title: Canon PIXMA MG3522 Wireless Inkjet Photo All-in-One Printer - Print, Copy, Scan
review_headline: Cheap but hard to set up
review_body:
I bought this printer to replace a basic Canon printer (IP2600) that I had used extensively for over five years. This model used the same ink as my second Canon printer MG2220. The MG2220 and MG3522 look similar but the MG2220 has a more complex button layout and also has a LED display. The MG3522 looks like a cheaper quality printer.
I spent close to three hours to get the wireless to set up for my PC and laptop.
For my PC, I couldn't get it setup without using a USB cable although the software had the option to setup without it. Once I got it working, I disconnected the USB cable and it worked fine.
As for my laptop, at first it connected without the USB cable but I mistakenly installed the software where the printer would send Canon my printer information. I uninstalled everything and restarted. It wouldn't connect and I uninstalled and re-installed many, many times. Finally when I saw that my web browser wouldn't connect, I realized that the Internet connection had been disabled. I had to reconnect and set it to auto connect. After that, the installation worked. Now I have both my PC and my laptop connected to the same printer.
I read about some who wrote that the paper jams. My MG2220 (which looks identical) has never jammed. I don't use the duplex printer and I wonder if that causes it or whether the printer jammed with normal printing. Since I print very often, I'll see how this printer holds up very soon.

product_title: 16X150mm Glass Test Tubes with Cork Stoppers, Karter Scientific 201B1 (Pack of 10)
review_headline: Corks too small--won't fit; tubes 13mm inside; corks ~13mm
review_body:
Corks do not fit. I see some reviews now that indicate similar problems, but at the time I put these in my shopping cart, I didn't notice any such reviews. The cork stoppers sent are just too small. Even if I can force a stopper to go in, it will only go in about 1/8\\", and that's with pushing so hard I'm afraid I'll break the tube. Makes the test tubes useless.

One other issue is the packaging. All mine arrived unbroken, but I'm surprised. At first, it seemed like good packaging. A box within a box. The interior box had paper, and the tubes were inside a padded envelope. But when I opened the envelope, all the tubes were just in a plastic bag loose together, rattling against each other. But, they DID all make it.

If the corks fit, these would be fine. The tubes are just what I needed, but I can't use them if the stoppers won't fit. I'm not confident that trying to exchange them will solve the problem.

I think the seller needs to send out new corks that actually fit these test tubes--maybe they just made a mistake & put the wrong size corks in a few packages (the corks were just all loose in the box).

---Update---

I started looking through other reviews and found several references to corks not fitting. Plus, some folks apparently had the tubes break when trying to force the corks, which is what I was afraid of. It doesn't sound like anyone with the wrong size has gotten a resolution. It does seem like some folks got the right corks.

Amazon customer support has been somewhat helpful (offered free shipping if I buy other corks, etc.), but since they didn't sell this item, Lake Charles Mfg did, they can't really fix the problem. I can try to contact Lake Charles.

I hoped to just find some other corks in the right size, so I measured the test tubes and the corks I received. The test tubes are only 13mm internal diameter (close to 16mm outside diameter--I'm not sure which was supposed to be the16mm in the item description), but the corks have a small-end diameter of about 13 mm and large-end diameter of 17-18mm (maybe cork size #5?), so they obviously are not going to work with these test tubes.

Cons:

product_title: AIE AIE-300 Impulse Handheld Bag Sealer, 12" Max. Seal Length, 2 mm Seal Width, 500 Watts, Exceptional air and watertight seals on most plastic materials up to 6 mil, Food and non-food applications
review_headline: Bought Impulse Sealer on Impulse, But no Regrets
review_body: Bought this from a site that starts with an e, because the seller gave me an awesome discount.  It arrived shrink wrapped and new in box. The unit came with 2 extra teflon sheets and 2 extra burn wires. I like that it's made of sturdy metal, so it won't move around on your table when your trying to seal something. The sealer comes with a black plastic clip to hold the sealer down for storage. Don't pitch that plastic clip, because you can re-use it to hold the handle down for storage when it's not in use. Plus it's easier to carry the sealer with the handle pressed down. I threw out the black twisty tie and attached a large velcro strap around the power cord to make it convenient to store and unwrap when I need it. The unit seals those metallic ESD bags and bubble wrap like a champ!! Leave the setting on 5-6 for everything and you should be fine.  Instructions are clear and understandable even though product is made in Taiwan. I tried being stingy and got a China sealer and the instructions were in broken English with bad grammar. Those China plastic sealers are so flimsy and cheap, that I wouldn't count on them lasting very long. The China sealer, also bought on that e site, lasted a couple months before it gave up the ghost and would spark every time I pressed down on the handle. Lately, China has been putting out a lot of sh*t, which I don't understand considering Apple products are made there. Therefore, go with Taiwan if your on a budget because it appears they have tighter quality control standards. Plus you will be able to understand the instructions.  I chose this model, because it bears the UL symbol, so hopefully it won't catch fire on me since it has supposedly been tested at the factory and passed some standards. The cheapy special from China did'nt have the UL sticker when I bought it and the cord looked rather paltry compared to the thick 3 prong cord you get with this unit.  In summary, good impulse sealer with the features I'm looking for, has betterTaiwan quality compared to China, and UL listed for piece of mind. Hope this helps in your search for the perfect seal.  2015 Update: This sealer continues to provide an excellent seal and I haven't had to change out the burn wires or brown padding yet.

It's really handy in helping me get an overview of what my entire month looks like. On the actual pages, it's simple. Monday-Sunday with 7 open lines. I use this space to write in appointments and as a 'to do' list. The pages are thick enough- I use a regular ball point pen and it doesn't bleed through. It's light and totally small enough to keep in my everyday purse. I've had it for about 3 weeks and to be honest I'm not super careful with keeping it safe. product_title: Epson Expression XP-410 Wireless Color All-in-One Inkjet Printer
review_body:
It prints and the ink is cheap, but quality wise, its awful.

After about a week of printing documents (maybe 1 or 2 a day) it started streaking and made weird white lines through all of the text, making it unreadable. I had to go into the printer utility on the computer and use the "clean heads" function. I had to run it about 5 times before the prints looked readable again. I have had to do this a few times, and I am using the recommended Epson ink, not a 3rd party ink.

Recently it has started printing the pages out of alignment, so the text prints somewhat diagonally on the page, instead of vertically. I have not been able to figure out how to realign the print heads.

As far as printing pictures goes, the colors don't look very good at all.

Its a cheap printer, and it acts like one. And while the ink is fairly cheap as well, it goes FAST! order 3 or 4 replacement blacks if you are printing documents often, as the ink goes quick!

Overall, I would not recommend this printer. The price is right, but the quality of the print, even for rough drafts, is pretty poor.

product_title: Sophia Global Remanufactured Ink Cartridge Replacements for HP 45 23
review_headline: I contacted Sophia Global who sent me another single cartridge which is working great. The second cartridge of this order works
review_body:
This is a package of 2-HP-23 Color cartridges for a HP Deskjet 812C printer. One cartridge would not print and I think it's because whoever made it labeled it for HP-23 using the wrong cartridge. (This is the reason for a 4 vice 5 rating) The contact are not those of a HP-23 cartridge. I contacted Sophia Global who sent me another single cartridge which is working great. The second cartridge of this order works as well as any HP-23 cartridge I've ever used. These cartridges are definitely worth the money and Sophia Global stands behind their products.

Update 4 Aug 17: I kept the second cartridge mentioned above beyond it's 2 year warranty. When I did use it the yellows started fading then the reds after only a few prints. I order 2 more of these cartridges on 26 Apr 17; Received 1 May 17; Installed/tested 1 May 17. Within a few "Draft" mode prints (spreadsheets) I noticed the reds were really faded. Colors that didn't require red continued to print 'ok' until a few days ago. I tried "Best" print with only minor success. I don't do a lot of color printing and when I do I normally use "Draft". When I print in 'black and white' only with a Sophia Global HP-15 cartridge I get straight lines and excellent print quality in "Draft" mode. With the above color cartridge active (printing) lines were wavy from the start though alignment settings showed straight lines. In "Best" mode, I got straight lines. I normally get a year or more of my color printing from each cartridge. This 1 May 17 cartridge didn't really last a month. I just kept getting what I could out of the cartridge until today. I just installed and tested the 2nd of my 1 May 17 purchase. It seems to work 'ok' in "Draft" mode but the red is showing yellow lines, not a solid red color. I haven't tried "Best" mode.
I usually praise Sophia's cartridges but recently their HP-23's aren't meeting quality standards. So far, their HP-15 black cartridges work great - hope the 2nd of my last purchased HP-15's doesn't change that. I'm dropping Sophia Global's HP-23's to 3 stars at best right now.

review_headline: Pass on this; get the full sized punch instead
review_body:
This is really not worth getting and I strongly recommend holding off and getting either the full sized Arc or Circa punches. There are multiple problems with the portable one. Just to cite a couple, the bottom rubber cover has a tendency to come off,releasing the little bits of paper. Moreover, the punch presses unequally and does not create sharp cuts. You can't even cut holes in a single sheet of paper. One of the two premium punches not only punches a single sheet easily, but 7 or 8 as well.

Of the two premium punches, I strongly recommend the Staples Arc over the Levenger. Most of the time the Levenger items are more expensive and are of much higher quality. In this case the Arc and Levenger items are almost precisely the same price, but the Arc is of much higher quality.

review_body:
This is my first experience with a projector outside of the office and using one for powerpoint presentations. I couldn't be happier. I've connected this little Epson EX-7230 (this is not the wireless model) via HDMI cable to my laptop. Setup was extremely simple, there is a quick start guide included and I was up and running quickly.

I'm using the projector mainly for use with my travel soccer team. We meet weekly in a clubhouse room to look at game clips and review some slides. Much nicer than the old whiteboard! The kids have been wildly impressed obviously. For me, the small, portable unit is PERFECT. The small carrying case actually fits easily in my laptop bag with my laptop, not too heavy. The set up is so quick and easy, we're up and running in no time.

The picture is frankly AMAZING. Watching the game videos in particular is as good as watching them on my tv rather than projected on to a white screen. Crisp, bright and very clear. You could very easily use this to project and watch movies at home if you wanted. Projecting my power point slides the unit is equally clear and bright, and the display is still sharp whether in a dark room or partially lit.

Really, I could not be more impressed by this projector. Highly recommended!!!

review_headline: Holds well and comes off without leaving residue
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:moUOHQRLS4WOIJ]]I love this stuff. I own both black and white daffer tape and found numerous uses for it. Because it sticks well and comes off clean. The black tape is good for repairs, in many cases it is hard to see. White tape lets me write on it so I can label things (like packing boxes).

Gaffer tape is a fabric tape with a strong adhesive. It is often used during theater and stage work to hold things together and then easily remove. It is similar to duct tape, but a major difference is that it can be removed cleanly because it uses a petroleum-based adhesive rather than rubber adhesive used in duck tape. However, duck tape is easier to produce so it is cheaper. However, if you need to remove the tape without leaving gunk behind gaffer tape is what you need.

This tape is provided by Gaffer Power.

review_headline: What the heck has gotten in to me.

Who would ever thought I'd ever write a review about pens, VOLUNTARILY?! I don't even know myself anymore. Except that I love these things. Heck I never knew I could have that kind of a relationship with a pen. I lent one to a classmate on the first day of class (Hey, I am a very lend-friendly person, plus it's a friendship maker) and an hour after class as I sat on the train home I realised what had happened. I literally walked 3 cars to look for her (since we both take the same train back) to ask for it back. Like some seriously deranged person, what the heck! Sadly, I could not find her. Perhaps it was a good thing for our friendship. No one likes a person who remembers that you borrowed their pen and hounds you for it. But now I've learnt my lesson.

Decoy pens.

Use these Uniballs on your own, and when someone asks for a pen to borrow, give them the free crap you get from your mum's office or your eye doctor. Decoy pens, I'm telling you all. Didn't hear this from me.

review_headline: This is the large printer paper you've been looking for
review_body:
OK, I have been shopping for paper like this for a long while and finally found it. Wide-carriage InkJets capable of printing on 13\\" wide paper (such as the HP DeskJet 1220C) have been around a long time, why is it so hard to find regular paper for them? So now for the particulars... Paper came in a largish box. Paper was shrinkwrapped between two stiff pieces of cardboard to protect it. Paper itself: 20 lb
Brightness: ~95
Texture: Very smooth

(Comparison made to Staples 24 lb, 98 bright \\"Bright-white Inkjet Paper\\")

Suprisingly, this paper is more opaque than the heavier weight Staples paper, and about the same as Staples \\"Professional Double-sided Matte Paper\\". So it won't work for tracing and it's too light for photographs (use the Staples \\"...Matte Paper\\" for big photos and keep lots of spare color cartridges on hand).

But it is great for general printing!

On the inside front cover is a file folder capable of housing many documents.

On the inside back cover is the three ring binder, itself, which can be easily removed if necessary.

It's a great organizational tool, whether for your home office or school, but not something I'd recommend bringing to your day job.

review_headline: AT-A-GLANCE 2014/15 School Year Weekly/Monthly Planner 5 X 8" Size (601-200A)
review_body:
This is a grey spiral 5.50 x 8.50 Inch notebook style calendar for July 2014-June 2015.
Cover - The pink robins on the dark grey front with pink inside covers & month tabs would keep most men from wanting it to use it themselves, but very cute for women without it being too cute. It's made of a weird neoprene (soft plastic)? that can bend a bit but will crease like cardboard if bent too much.
It has a laminated 3 year (2013-2015) single page reference as the first page.
Month View
There's a tab for each month that takes up two pages, giving 6 lines per day in square form.
Weekly View
Between each month pad is several pages for the weekly view. Each week takes up two pages, Monday to Sun, 8 lines each, giving room for specific tasks/assignments, etc. though there could have been more if they put less empty space showing the month on top.
Holidays - it does list major holidays in the month & weekly view.
Contacts - Why is it not tabbed? Which gives you 5 lines, 5 contacts per page & there are only 6 pages. Better then nothing, but not much of a contact list.
Notes - 6 pages back to back. Not much at all. Barely worth calling this a planner, it's a more glorified calendar.
Event calendar - 1 page for Jan - Dec unspecified months. Looks thrown in.
Holiday List - laminated single page listing all major US, Canada & Mexican holidays that include religious ones for Christan, Jewish and Islamic holidays. They also list ones not as popular like Holocaust Remembrance day, Pearl Harbor & Kwanzaa. I am pleasantly surprised how many national/well known religious holidays are listed.

product_title: Five Star 7 - Pocket Expanding File, Reminder Tabs
review_headline: Lots of uses, well constructed - very pleased
review_body:
I am very happy with this file folder. I have previously had ones the closed with velcro and one with a rubber band like loop. I disliked the velcro immensely due to the noise (especially during meetings). The rubber band was great until it got stretched due to using it full for a prolonged period. A zipper is a really happy medium between ease of use and security.

The file folder is very expandable. I do not feel that the zipper will be too limiting in that regard.

The pop tabs are useful - especially because they are color coded and are visible when full & closed.

The pen loop is a little too snug for me, but is a nice added feature that could be improved upon.

The clear cover is not necessarily something that I needed - but I it it accessible from the front, which is useful for adding last minute items.

It seems durable, but only time will tell. My last one (with the elastic bungee closure) got brittle with age (>5 years) and did have several tears that made it a little unattractive for use. I think the kid factor would have brought the use down to 1 year as I was not throwing it in a backpack & locker.

Bottom line: Equally useful for me and my high school son. That's a rare item. My 5th grader now wants one. So...that's a pretty wide audience. I use these for work (keep separate projects separate during meetings without having to open binders repeatedly) and home for things I cannot necessarily file and forget (school organization/paperwork, health, home remodeling projects, receipts etc...) - that said this is great for temporary filing (things that either need to be filed, or need to be kept transiently).

product_title: Fluid Mesh Task Chair by Allseating
review_headline: One Of The Worst Chairs Ever!
review_body:
if i could rate this chair lower i would. I wrote a review of the chair many years ago that appeared on some other sites. i wanted to write a updated review.

i own two of the Allseating Fluid chairs. although there are some very nice features these chairs are so poorly built and designed it doesn't really matter how good any of those features are.

Build quality is a huge issue. both my chairs came is with stripped screw faces and creaked like the ship was going down out of the box! the seat slider design is really bad! the seat slides forward and backward on two metal plate carriers. the problem there is they left so much room that you will have play in the chair leaning from left to right. there is also tons of play in the arm rest system. there is no tension system for the seat mesh which stretches and is not as elastic like as the Aeron chairs.

Design: a lot of the build quality grips are also design issue. i don't want to go over those twice. so here i will talk about strictly design related issues. if you notice the seat pan lip is not flexible. they used a hard plastics that does not give in any way. this is really bad since it puts a lot of pressure on the back of your legs. if you opted for the optional seat slider you could position yourself where there isn't pressure on the back of your legs. otherwise the result could be discomfort as it is in my case. it is really hard to focus because i find myself constantly adjusting to stay comfortable. that eats up valuable time. lumbar support is ok. again like a lot of the components of the chair there is some or a lot of play in them. the issue with the lumbar support is that uses a plastic latching system that sometime doesn't latch.

Support: if you have gotten this far you understand i have had pretty much a issue with ever part of the chair besides the casters! well maybe i was unlucky and got two lemons. i contacted customer support about the issues and even sent them a few videos to help illustrate the problems i was having with the chairs. The rep from Allseating i exchanged E-Mails with said that is a how all the Fluid chairs are and there wasn't anything they could do.

the major mistake i made was not sitting in the chair before i purchased it. i figured a chair that cost this much has to be well made and comfortable. well i was wrong! i would avoid Allseating products.

product_title: J.Herbin Fountain Pen Ink
review_body:
As with MOST fountain pen ink, I love this. I'll say my only issue is the price, but the nice bottle and how it's a conversation starter on my desk make up for it.

This ink is very close in color and properties like the J. Herbin Bleu Nuit. This is a shade darker and behaves a tad better. The coolest thing is this ink is somewhat like an iron gall ink because it goes down a light, bright purple but dries to a... I'll say presidential blue. This makes writing even more fun. It's a pretty saturated ink, especially for J. Herbin, so minimal if any shading in the bold nib I use it in. Smaller nibs may change that. It dries fast and has minimal feathering on the VERY cheap recycled paper I take notes on and no shading on my very good notebook paper. This ink also is water resistant I'll say. It does run and smear some, but I can still completely read what I put down and MOST of the ink stays put. If you let it sit longer than I did, it'll probably behave even better if it gets wet.

If you like a darker, but still visibly blue, ink, then get this. It has a bit of purple in it, as evidenced by the color change, but shockingly it doesn't look very purple after that. It flows very well and behaves even better. If you can overcome the premium price, J. Herbin has made a great ink

product_title: AT-A-GLANCE 2014–2015 Academic Year Thomas Paul Weekly and Monthly Planner, Wirebound, Teal, 8.5 x 11 Inch Page Size (628P-905A)
review_headline: this planner is really fantastic. I was previously in the habit of printing ...
review_body:
If you want a lot of writing space, this planner is really fantastic.

I was previously in the habit of printing calendars using my printer, and a single page for each week. I'd struggled with finding planners that would work for me, because they mostly were more like agendas (to track what to do at each moment of the day, rather than more broadly what needs to get done) and they didn't offer nearly enough space to track the things I was concerned about comfortably.

This is the full size of a typical notebook. It gives you a two page spread for a monthly calendar, and a two page spread for each week. There are tabs to let you jump to the month you want.

There's also a couple of pages for contacts in the back, which is not really something I ever liked much in a planner. Particularly not NOW, when my mobile phone does the job of tracking contacts. Fortunately, they pretty much just have lined paper there, so you can use it as more pages for notes if you want. There are also extra pages for notes.

I feel better about things if I have somewhere to write down (by hand) what's supposed to be going on. While I use online tools to track some things, somehow they are emotionally not enough to make me feel like I have a handle on what I'm doing. Most planners don't work out great because I end up feeling like I don't have the space I want, which is why I took to printing pages. This seems like it's going to be perfect for my particular needs.

There are potential big cons, depending on your priorities. It's MUCH bigger than many academic planners I've tried to use (which were made pocket sized), so it'll take up a lot more space in a backpack or whatever than those. The fact that it divides days into am/pm makes me feel like it's more of a university and up planner than one made for students and teachers who are starting something new every hour. Or for parents who aren't directly following the school schedule in their activities.

The design is very nice, the cover feels extremely good in person. I've noticed that the highest quality pen that I had handy tended to write dark enough on it that you could see through more than I'd like, but all of the rest of my pens (including gel pens) seem to be fine so far.

The high quality and excellent feel, of course, contribute to a price tag that may not be palatable. That's totally understandable, especially when it's so easy to print a couple of pages of your own to track the current week at any given time.

For my part, I think there's a pretty good chance I'm going to be buying these in the future when I need more planners. One of the things I didn't like about just printing something is that it wasn't particularly... pretty or tidy. I sometimes felt like it'd be nice to get something bound and pretty so that it would feel more satisfying to use it (kind of like when I occasionally buy a higher quality notebook than I normally use, to coax myself to write more in a particular area). This is more expensive than most, but if it does help me to stay on top of the things I need to do, over the course of a year it'll be extremely worth it.

product_title: Canon Office and Business MX922 All in One Printer, Wireless and mobile printing
review_headline: Some good things; some bad things
review_body:
Got this for $75 on a lightning deal. Ability to print worked for one day. Can't print anything now. Keep getting a general error message without any hint as to what the problem might be. So I'm back to using my old printer.

The main menu is confusing. If you hit the wrong button, it takes much longer than you would expect to get back to where you were. The scanning software seemed to be pretty good. At least the results were good. The popup interface worked well with a couple of exceptions. The auto-detection of multiple photos in a single scan never worked right. I ended up just scanning the entire glass and then extracting the individual photos in Photoshop.

After many years of using HP printers, I've purchased two Canon printers recently. Both were at a bargain price. So far, I'm not happy with either Canon.

Update: It wasn't easy, but I figured out that the printer was no longer connecting to the wireless router. I followed the printer's directions (on the little display) for reconnecting, but that didn't work. Had to deviate from their instructions and try different ways of connecting via WPS. Was eventually able to to do it. Sorry, don't remember exactly what worked. Upgrading this from one star to three stars.

Update (Nov 2014): Beginning to use this more. It scans text documents to searchable PDF much faster than more expensive (but older) HP models. Upgrading from 3 to 4 stars.

Update (Nov 2014): The software for creating searchable PDF documents is horrible. Pretty much impossible to do an accurate copy/paste in a scanned text document, so search results will not be reliable. Haven't figured out the best way around this, but probably will end up scanning or printing image documents and then letting Adobe Acrobat Pro do the OCR. Or try letting Acrobat do the scan from scratch. Back down to three stars.

Update (January 2015): Discovered more problems: (1) It will scan 100+ pages into memory, but when you go to create the PDF, it gives you an error message saying it can't create a file of 100+ pages. You can't delete pages to get under 100, nor is there any other way (that I can see) to save the scan. You lose everything. You have to do the entire scan over again, making sure you stay under 100 pages before stopping. I scan 100's of pages all the time for single PDF files, so this is a huge negative for me. Down to 2 stars just for this one. (2) I have to reconnect to the wireless router all the time. I think it's easier to just use USB; (3) this ADF has trouble picking up pages unless they're in perfect condition. Several times I've had to give up on a document and use a different scanner; (4) Several times I've been unable to continue scanning via the PC. I have to go over to the printer, hit buttons, and then they tell me to go back to the PC and continue the scan from there. Would be nice if once you got going on a scan, you could just control everything from the PC. Aside from these negatives, it does scan multiple pages quickly and the image quality is good.

Update (late January 2015): Just found an extremely useful feature that my HP scanners don't have. In the scanning interface, you can adjust the contrast/darkness of text. This is extremely helpful when working with PDF's (or other documents) that have light, difficult-to-read text, which I get all the time in scans. This feature alone (for me) makes the printer worth having around. With my HP's, I'd have to, page by page, edit the contrast in Photoshop before printing. product_title: Satechi F3 Smart Monitor Stand with Four USB 3.0 Ports and Headphone / Microphone Extension Ports
review_body:
I have had this Satechi F3 smart monitor stand for a couple days and I absolutely love it. At first, I didn’t really think I would have a need for it but after testing it for a couple days, I have really come to appreciate everything that it offers.
Out of the box, you will find the stand with 2 “U” shaped aluminum legs (which you must use) and also a USB cord to connect the stand to you laptop or desktop or whichever device you want to connect it to, and also a microphone and headphone jack so that you don’t have to reach all the way to your computer tower to connect. These you connect under the actual platform, so that the wires can be hidden (which is a fantastic feature giving so you don’t have a clutter of wires on the desk.
The design of this stand if very clean and sleek. This increases the amount of space on your desk as you are able to store things underneath the stand. I store my wireless keyboard and wireless mouse under there when not in use. The aluminum legs give it a nice finish. You have the option of 2 heights with the stand (but keep in mind that you MUST use the stands! The top is made out of a rough surface plastic material which gives it an overall impressive look. The only thing I wish they had was a top that also came in a black color.
This stand functions very well. On the front you will find 4 – 3.0 USB ports and also the other end of the microphone and headphone jack to connect those into. All the ports work very well, and I tested the speed of a 3.0 USB flash drive and didn’t notice much difference in the data transfer speed test. This is very neat as you can easily increase the USB port capability of your computer. And you don’t even have to bend down and reach behind the back of the tower to plug your devices into!
Another thing which I really like about this stand is the versatility of it. I can put my external monitor on it while connecting it to my laptop so that I can use all the ports and prop upmy monitor to a better eye level. Or, I can prop up my laptop/tablet and use my wireless mouse and keyboard to control everything. So it is very versatile.
Overall, I really enjoy this product and have already found many uses for it (which I didn’t think I would). It looks good, functions well, and adds a cool, yet useful, feature to my desk. product_title: Epson WorkForce DS-40 Wireless Portable Document Scanner for PC and Mac, Sheet-fed, Mobile/Portable
review_headline: Literally changed my whole work flow on the road
review_body:
The wireless portable color scanner is one of those devices that has changed my entire workflow.

In my work, I have to sign dozens of documents per day, and I am on nearly constant travel. The WorkForce DS-40 has come to my rescue. I have a large, hi-res, non-portable scanner at home, and it works well enough when - I am at home. But, if I am running from one airport to the next, or at a hotel far away from a support location then are few alternatives. (One workaround was to take a hires photo and then just use tools to crop and format the document.)

The DS-40 works anywhere. All that you need is a WiFi capable computer (or i-device). You feed the document into the DS-40 "narrow end" in. Apparently it can take up to 36" long documents, but I never go past 14". Color is a wonderful feature for a portable scanner too as it lets me scan in and share briefing charts with my folks.

My principal uses of the DS-40 are ensuring my signed documents get to my staff and sharing presentations from the road, but the DS-40 has other potential uses, e.g., business card scanning, sending personalized notes, etc. Really, its applications are only limited by your imagination.

There are a couple caveats that have to do with practical matters - not limitations or issues with the scanner. The scanner uses 4xAA batteries. I don't know how long they last exactly, but it is probably best to have a back-up set on standby if you are trying to scan something critical. The other main warning would be that this operates in an unsecure mode across WiFi (it does not matter that your WiFi is password protected - the data being transmitted is still unencrypted); so, just be mindful of sending sensitive information in a public location using this scanner.

Thank you Epson for making my busy, travel-filled work life much, much easier!

In service,

Rich

review_body: I agree with a few post that software and scanner manual VERY confusing, but yes its possible to setup one button/scan operation..... If you dont care about price Fujitsu will be your best bet, but if your weekly volume less than 2000 pages and you want to save 300$, Xerox 5445 is a very good option ( especially with current 3 year advance exchange warranty included). review_headline: Decent looking reliable Fountain Pen for $15.  Good pen, great value!
review_body:
This review is for the Pilot MR Animal Collection Fountain Pen, Matte White with White Tiger Accent, Fine Nib.

After several days of using this, I have this to say about it. For looks, it's an OK looking pen. I think for a little bit more, they could have made it much nicer looking.

The nib, which is Fine, writes on the thicker side of Fine. If you write with the nib upside down it will lay down a finer line.. The nib is a bit scratchy. Not a lot, but a little bit. It lays down a smooth steady line with no skipping. Other than right after I put the ink in, I haven't had to prime it at all. It is always at the ready. The nib is steel and not very springy. You won't get a lot of variation in the thickness of your writing by pushing down on it harder.

I like that it can use the converter or the cartridges. I prefer cartridges and 12 of them are available for cheap here on Amazon. But a converter is supplied if you like to use your own inks.

The cap posts securely and the pen has a nice feel and weight to it.

The pen comes in a nice, but not elegant box, complete with 1 ink cartridge and instructions.

Overall, it's a solid pen that writes well, and for $15 it is a very good value for a reliable fountain pen.

product_title: Kum Long Point Pencil Sharpener with Pointer
review_body: There must be something seriously wrong with me, but I can not get a pencil sharpener, electric or not, to work to save my life.  I grind a new tip for the pencil and it comes out either half covered with wood or with new tip already broken off.  I grind some more.  Same thing.  Pencil gets shorter and shorter, no usuable tip.  THIS pencil sharpener puts an end to this crazy problem I'm having.  It works like a charm.  First you put your pencil in the hole that removes wood from the tip, but leaves a fat, unsharpened tip.  Great for coloring pencils.  Then you can put your pencil in the second hole, which leaves the remaining wood alone and only refines the newly exposed tip.  It works EVERY time.  Problem solved.

product_title: Happy 40th Birthday DVD Greeting Card: A Flickback Decade DVD
review_body: *****    Disco apparel of course, as we are reminded in this engaging DVD compilation of the incredible 70's.  Studio 54 was everything to celebrity and so was this decades musical notoriety from the Bee Gees to the Village People.    The Beatles break for solo success while the Supremes, Led Zeppelin, Eagles, Elton John, Rod Stewart, Chicago, Bob Marley, Donna Summers, The Sex Pistols, Blondie, Police, Tom Petty/Heartbreakers and infinite scores of talent made the music of the '70s so dynamic. Tragically, we lost some of our best; Janis Joplin, Jimi Hendrix and Jim Morrison all only 27 years old at death.    Can't forget the Apple 2e, Commodore, Space invaders, Pong ... while the Cray 1 smashes computing power records for R&D.    Popular movies included Star Wars, Jaws & II, The Godfather and Saturday Night Fever claimed the disco craze.    Gloria Steinem promotes women's equal rights, while more women find their way to heads of state in Israel, UK and India.    Nixon banned cigarette advertising, sends 50 thousand more troops (w/ cigarettes) to Vietnam, while 13 students at Kent State are shot during a demonstration. Vice President Agnew is sentenced for bribery & tax evasion, the Watergate scandal ends in resignation. Vietnam War Paris Peace Accords are signed on January 27, 1973.    The first heart transplants are performed.    Arthur Ashe became number one seed in tennis while Billie Jean King trounces Bobby Riggs in a highly anticipated \\"battle of the sexes\\" tournament.    Ali takes Foreman in the world championships.    The tearful decline of muscle cars and compression ratios find Detroit's dismal introduction of the Vega and Pinto \\"ignito\\", for a couple of MPG points.    A new Ford Maverick was $1,900, the Honda Civic produced 50 horsepower, the VW Rabbit ('78) made its debut and, AMC continued to produce epically ugly cars w/ the '75 Pacer.    Hertz wishes it could forget they hired O.J. Simpson for their national ad campaigns.    This \\"Dungeons & Dragons generation\\" 1970s DVD is solid with wickedly cool nostalgia. A splendid indulgence.    Cheers,  Marcel B.    *****  Disclosure: I have purchased this companies products for many years and occasionally review new products from them at no charge.

review_headline: Great journal book for fountain pen wielding travelers
