This is more like a four and a half stars product- coming from a long line of cheaply made paper notes with horrible paper quality and finish that fell apart in a month or so, I was originally quite conservative in my expectation.

I'm happy to inform you that this note goes above and beyond what I expected. I'm a heavy fountain pen writer and travel in rough environments often, so any notebook I end up using for daily journaling needs to live up to some really high standards most consumer quality paper goods doesn't seem to be able to match most of the time. This notebook completely surprised me. The quality of the paper is good enough that my thickly laden Lamy Safari with fine-medium nip is capable of writing on them without worrying about smudges or spill over into the back of the page. The spine and the requisite finish and binding are also excellent, with no niggles or any weakpoints I can identify that could cause earlier than expected damage to the notebook structure itself.

All in all, highly recommended!

This machine is now going to the garbage and I'm going to try Scotch brand which has way more positive reviews than this one and from the reviews I read Scotch's customer service seems to be great. product_title: Epson WorkForce WF-3620 WiFi Direct All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer, Copier, Scanner
review_headline: Absolutely Professional with the Highest Standards and Quality that you would expect, HIGHLY RECOMMENDED
review_body:
The Epson Workforce 3620 is a fabulous machine. It took me several months of research to finally decide which model to purchase, after much research and review I finally decided on the 3620 or the 3640. I finally realized that both machines are practically identically except that the 3640 has the capacity to load 500 sheets of paper in two different trays, while the 3620 with only one try can hold 250 sheets. They are both priced at the same level, so the decision of which to chose would come down to a individual choice, depending on your print usage.
I must admit that setting up the printer was a bit tedious and it took sometime to complete, my only disappointment so far is that the instructions and user guide needs to be vastly improved, its obvious that not much time and thought was put into creating a user friendly, easy to follow instructions guide or manual, the minor details were not properly explained and that in itself creates more confusion and time constraints in setting up the printer. For example in Step 2 "Turn on and configure", the first few prompts on the touch screen were easy to follow but when you get to entering the date feature, I got stuck because there is no feature for you to select indicating that you are done, all I was left with is a blinking light on the last number in the year, there is no "OK" or "ENTER" button that allows you to continue with the Time prompt, it just leaves you hanging, then no matter what key you press, I was just not able to complete the date and time. So I had to call tech support and even the technician I spoke to was not able to quickly offer any solution, until he placed me on hold to get advise from his supervisor, then he finally had me select the but with the Arrow, which is actually the return button, so it appears that this is return button performs the function of "OK" or " ENTER" allowing you to continue with the installation, it was only then that I was able to continue to entering the Date. It would have been so much easier if this minor but important detail was noted somewhere in the manual. Other than this somewhat minor glitch, the rest of the steps went smoothly, but it did slow down my momentum as I tried to find a solution on line, I went to Epson website and spent many hours just trying to find a answer. I was not able to find any discussion or solution so that was when I decided to call tech support.

I would still highly recommend this printer over any of the competitors, the print quality is excellent and the color copies are very professional. You also have the ability to send and receive fax so with this printer you have the ability to run your complete home office

product_title: Panasonic Link2Cell KX-TG7875S DECT 6.0 1-Line Bluetooth Cordless Phone with Enhanced Noise Reduction & Digital Answering Machine
review_body:
I purchased the Panasonic KX-TG7871, received and installed on 6/19/14. Initially I was very happy with the product. I purchased the five handset version and all worked acceptably. The link to cell feature was the main reason for getting this model and it did indeed work with very little setup. Whenever my cell is in range all of the handset will ring and take the call if answered. The voice quality over the link to cell was less than I had hoped but was within acceptable limits. The text message alert also worked great by ringing all handsets twice and each announcing \\"text message\\". I had not appreciated how nice this feature was until getting to use it for a few days. The only thing that could have made the text notification better would be if it read the txt, but it's more than ok the way it is.
Now the bad part, yesterday on 8/5/14 the device lost power. The handsets all had an error stating that the base station was off. All of the extended units seem fine but serve no function without the base station. After checking the base station it was indeed powered off. Unplugging and plugging back in, changing outlets yielded no results. I believe that the station itself is fine but as a dead power supply. The power supply for this phone is a proprietary plug and outputs. What I mean by proprietary outputs is that the power supply uses two sets of wires with two different currents that terminate in a plug resembling an rj11 but slightly different. This makes using any other supply near impossible. I am just over a month so amazon will not offer replacement (not that it is their fault). So now I am left trying to battle customer support or engineering a new supply. A few searches on the power supply model has shown that one month lifespans out of these are not that uncommon.
I very much regret choosing this brand.

Update 8/6/14
Called tech support and have mixed opinions. The first irritation was suffering through the automated phone system.This is hardly unique to Panasonic so it's hard to fault them for this. The second headache was that I had to be transferred to several departments during the call. With the third transfer I was sent to parts department who could help if I was willing to pay for the parts needed, if I wanted it covered under warranty I would have to call another dept. After calling the support number again and getting through the auto phones I reached a tech that was able to help.

The current status of my issue is that I have just shipped the dead unit back (at my expense) and am awaiting its return.

One positive that I can say is that every human from support that I spoke with was extremely polite and pleasant. Even the rep that incorrectly transferred me was polite and the transfer could have been an honest mistake. All in all, aside from the automated director phone system, i was very pleased with Panasonics support. This could change when and if I get my phone back in working order, but as I have just shipped it out today, expect it to take at least a week or two.

product_title: 2015 Organized Mom Family Weekly Planner wall calendar with columns for 6 people, plus perforated shopping lists and extra organizational features
review_headline: Happy to see this in the USA
review_body: After the BusyBodyBook planner went out of business, I had to go to the UK to find a family planner that met my needs.  The Organized Mum Family Weekly Planner Calendar became my go-to planner to organize my family's schedules.  Now, I'm happy to report that Boxhouse Publishing has come out with an American version of this planner, and the planner has been tweaked a little for American users.  This 16-month calendar begins in the middle of Aug. 2014 and goes to the end of Dec. 2015. Unlike the British version, the American one begins each week with Sunday instead of Monday.  The days go vertically down one side of the page, and then there are spaces in a horizontal grid for each member of the family. There is room to track the events of up to six members of the family. The spaces for each day are bigger than other family calendars you find in the U.S.  U.S. holidays are also listed. Some very nice features of this calendar include a weekly "Things to do" section and a "Shopping list" with perforations so that you can take these lists with you. The calendar itself has perforations, so that if you want to rip out the week, you can (I don't like doing this because I like to see the history of the year all together).  There is also a plastic cover that you can write on with a dry-erase marker for those appointments or schedules that repeat weekly (dry erase marker included). Overall, I've been extremely happy with this calendar/planner over the last couple of years--that is why I was willing to pay overseas postage for it.  I am glad that I can buy the calendar locally now.

My replacement bulb that came from a different manufacture, lasted 1100 hours and 8-10 months also. My third bulb, the same, 1200 hours, 8-10 months. I happened to be on Amazon and came across this bulb and read the reviews. The reviews were mixed, but for the price, I thought I could give it a try. I am definitely against trying to go the "cheaper" route with everything I purchase, knowing that you get what you pay for. But having to buy a new bulb every 8-10 months, at $300+ is crazy. I watch everything, all the time on my projector. Anyhow, I purchased the bulb in the summer of 2013 and it was amazing! Now, it isn't as bright as the bulb that Epson uses but the bulb is 100% identical, physically. I wouldn't be surprised if it is the same manufacture. It is just a bit dimmer but maintains the same amazing picture quality and color. You also have to take into consideration; if your projector is always on its brightest setting, you will burn your bulb out ALOT faster. I leave my projector on somewhat of a dimmer setting. This bulb has lasted me 14 months and over 3400 hours! I couldn't believe it. maybe I got lucky, maybe my next will burn out fairly quick, who knows. My bulb just burned out this morning and I bought two. Some of the customers have had unpleasant experiences with this bulb, but it is the same case with customers of the bulb that Epson uses. Just a con that comes with having a projector. If you love your projector as much as I do, I definitely recommend that you give it a try.

product_title: Epson WorkForce Pro WF-4640 Wireless Color All-in-One Inkjet Printer with Scanner and Copier
review_headline: Amazing small office/workgroup printer-replaces multiple devices and does more
review_body:
I used to work in an office with 22 people. We all shared an HP color inkjet and an HP workgroup laser printer on the network. Both worked great, but we also had to hook up a scanner to someone's PC, and we had a stand-alone fax machine that was actually a Canon all-in-one...you get the idea, it was lots of equipment.

The Epson WF-4640 would replace all four of those machines with one box, and do a better job on most tasks. Here's what I tested:

* Color Inkjet printing: As good as any four-ink color printer.
Very good for business graphics, good for photographs.

* Black and white document printing: Nearly as good as a
laser printer. You have to have a sharp eye to see a difference,
and even then you will probably decide it is good enough.

* Two sided printing: works great. This is a pleasure if you
have ever had to do it manually.

* Scanning: Multi-page scanning works great. 2 sided scans!

* FAX: multi-page fax works great.

* WiFi: Set up fine, no problems. Another Epson wifi printer
that I use sometimes needs to have the password reset
every time the power fails, but that hasn't happened since
I started using this one.

I haven't tried printing from iPhone, and I don't know how long the ink tanks last. Epson claims that the cost is \\"Up to 50% lower printing cost vs. color laser,\\" which would be nice, but those kinds of comparisons can be complex to do right. But wow, this thing does a great job at all the basic tasks.

After using this printer for a few weeks, I decided I didn't need a black laser printer any more. The output is that good. Unless you need 6-color or 10-color photo printing, all the users on your network will be very happy with this machine.

product_title: Swingline Metal Fashion Stapler, Full Strip, 20 Sheets
review_headline: Good for a new stapler, though not quite as good as the Swinglines of yore.
review_body: Oh Swingline, legendary stapler of film noir and American office lore! I remember as a child riding the subway past the Swingline factory sign in Queens. The factory closed in 1998, but the Swingline stapler remains an icon of American manufacturing prowess, a simple but durable instrument that lasts, like the IBM Selectric. While Typewriters are no more, every office desk has a stapler, and you hope it's a Swingline. Though they are no longer made in the USA, they are still the best at that simple task. This one, the Metal Fashion stapler, is a competent example of the breed, if not the best. It's certainly blingy, with its shiny chrome body and blue translucent plastic highlights. Those cosmetic touches do nothing for the performance of the stapler, but might make it easier to identify in case yours gets stolen (its a common problem - just watch Office Space) Performance wise, it's OK. Not on the level of the  old, heavy black Swinglines, which were also good as hammers, but OK. I use it every now and then for light tasks. But if I have a lot of stapling to do, I get my antique US-made one. It's probably 50 years old, but it still works better than any new one I've seen. If you must use a new stapler, this one is pretty good. But if you have a choice, find an old one. It's easy, since they last forever.

review_body:
Bought this to extend the Panasonic KX-TG6592T 2 handset phone because of having about 40' between phones, and the base being 1st floor, handset being on 2nd floor. I have another Panasonic 5 phone setup and the base is directly below my 2nd floor office on the 1st floor. There are times that the phone looses contact with the base, so I thought I'd play it safe and buy this extender with my new phones. Had some cutting out and base contact issues right after setting up the phone, so I fired up the extender and put it about 25' away from the base on the 1st floor and everything has been fine since.

BTW, I read and printed some instructions from another review of this unit that complained about no mention of the PROGRAM button in the manual. Found that to be bogus, and the instructions given in the review were WRONG! The unit is designed to go into program mode immediately upon plugging it in, so there is no need to hit the button. I followed the manual to a T and found it to be very simple to set up and get working perfectly. The PROGRAM button is mentioned in the troubleshooting section of the manual to RESET the unit, basically starting from scratch, after you've done the initial setup. YOU DO NOT NEED TO PRESS THE PROGRAM BUTTON the first time you turn your unit on.

I have 2 green lights (no amber or red) at 25' from the base and didn't try going further because that's where a convenient outlet is, and the unit cleared up all cutout and base range issues. Very happy with it, and was surprised at how small this unit is.

product_title: Canon Office and Business MX922 All in One Printer, Wireless and mobile printing
review_headline: Really nice printer but it can be a pain to setup on a wireless network
review_body:
This printer got excellent reviews from Consumer Reports and the price of the ink and printer are great. Seems to print quick and well although I have not yet printed any pictures. The problem was with making a reliable wireless connection. It took me about eight hours between tinkering, a phone call to tech support, and searching the internet for a solution. Also, Cannon includes a CD-ROM for installation but neither of my laptops have CD drives and the Cannon website was not very straightforward as to which software to download. I was finally able to get everything working after I found a trick on a tech web site.
Here was the solution for me:
(1) On the printer go to Menu>>Setup>>Device Settings>>Lan Settings>>Other Settings>>TCP/IP Settings>>IPv6 - Chose No
(2) On the printer go to Menu>>Setup>>Device Settings>>Lan Settings>>Other Settings>>Wireless LAN DRX Setting - Choose Disable

product_title: Epson WorkForce WF-3640 Wireless Color All-in-One Inkjet Printer with Scanner and Copier
review_body:
Let me start by saying I've had this printer for a month and I haven't used all of the features - it's that awesome!

Installation and connection with my laptop and wireless network was super easy. It didn't take long to get things connected and set up to talk to each other and our network has only been disconnected once when someone flipped a switch (little hands!) unbeknownst to me. If you've ever set up anything wireless, you can set this up in a snap, too.

Printing is beautiful. You can select multiple types - photo, black and white document, text and graphic document, etc. I have printed everything from flyers for a workshop, to passport forms, to simple task lists and they all look great. I have used it to print several templates from my Corel program and all of the graphics and text fonts are as clean as they appear on my screen. I don't have color bleeds or blurry lines.

Scanning documents is beyond easy. I have gotten so many things now saved to my laptop it's ridiculous. I have copies or birth certificates, ID cards, and so much more. You lay the page down, select scan to computer, and then you can even choose how you scan it - photo, PDF, etc. It's INSANE how much easier this printer has made keeping my documents secure!

Copies look AWESOME and with the 2-page print, there's no more guessing which way to flip the page to get the back printed, either. I know that's easy for some people, but I always print at least one page upside down before I get it. Now I just set he page(s) to be coped in, and let 'er rip! This comes in REALLY handy when I want to make stuff for the kids, or need to duplicate workbook pages, etc. It's so much les cumbersome this way than with other printers.

Overall, I am in LOVE with this printer! I haven't tried the fax because I don't have a landline in my house, and I am sure I will play around with it more, but for now, I haven't found anything a small home / office needs that it CANNOT do. This is a solid investment!

product_title: Hahnemuhle Fine Art Pearl, Fiber Based, Bright White Inkjet Paper, 285gsm, 8.5x11", 25 Sheets
review_body: I make prints from a simple Canon 1P4900, a hybrid text and photo type printer using this paper with mixed results, which may be due to the printer technology rather than the paper.  This is a high quality paper stock with a low gloss sheen. When printing B&W, some prints are excellent, reproducing the deep blacks in the photograph. What I do not like is that some prints reproduce the blacks and greys as shades of purple. When I print in color, some prints are excellent, reproducing bright colors with plenty of light behind them, other prints which appear adequately lighted on the monitor reproduce in more somber tones that do not live up to the original image. I have tried several adjustments to my iPhoto app and my Canon without success. I conclude that this is a high quality paper, possibly a five star paper, but that you need more sophisticated systems to tune your photos and print to it's maximum capability. Possibly Photoshop and a professional grade photo printer will do the job.

product_title: Epson XP-310 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner and Copier (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
I got this Epson XP-310 printer for my home computer printing needs a few months ago after an older Canon printer recently died on me. This printer is a good deal at $60 considering it has a printer, scanner and copier all in a single unit. Locally, this item sells for the same price, but the store did not have any in stock. The only negative issue I have is the separate ink cartridges don't last very long and you really need to keep at least a few extra ink cartridges on hand and they are not very cheap either. Print quality is acceptable and photo printing quality is pretty good. I gave this printer a 4 of 5 stars due to the fact that the ink cartridge issues I described earlier dropped it down 1 star...but overall a good general printer/scanner unit and well worth the price.

DECEMBER 2014 UPDATE: I have now had this Epson XP-310 scanner/printer over 5 months of moderate uses of mostly printing out emails. One new negative issue arose....when I load paper into the printer's backside, when I print, the paper seems to skew a bit sideways and not perfectly straight up and down...but at a slight angle and I slid the plastic thingie to keep the paper straight up and down right up against the small stack of blank paper for future print jobs. It's a minor issue but an annoyance. Ink cartridges seems to last about as long as rival printer's ink cartridges. I been using aftermarket cartridges with no major problems so far. Print quality is still acceptable/pretty good in many cases. It's easy to use for the most part. Once in awhile, this printer will \\"stall\\" and I have to power it down and restart the printer to make it work, but that's happened just a couple of times. I was tempted to drop it another star from 4 to 3 stars, but overall, this printer/scanner is working out okay. The scanner works great, and I use that fairly consistently and the software is typical Epson on the computer, fairly easy to navigate. If you need a decent printer/scanner and will be printing quite a bit, probably should get the next model up on the Epson line up since it's just about the same price. If you just print emails and/or periodic photos in color, this printer/scanner should do just fine. I will keep the rating at 4 of 5 stars.g quite a bit, probably should get the next model up on the Epson line up since it's just about the same price. If you just print emails and/or periodic photos in color, this printer/scanner should do just fine. I will keep the rating at 4 of 5 stars.

product_title: YR.Seasons Hero Extra Fine Nib Fountain Pen + Black Bottled Ink
review_body: This is carbon ink, see [[ASIN:B00I452N1C Hero Carbon ink Black]], it should be mentioned in the description so people are aware it could potentially clog their fountain pens if they are not careful. Look at the 234 number.  I believe the safer ink number is 204, have not been able to confirm that yet.    I guess the pen that comes with this ink is probably designed for carbon ink, I cannot confirm because I don't read chinese.    UPDATE:  I have now verified the pen is a [[ASIN:B00I17WZA2 Hero 9296 Accounting Ultrafine Fountain Pen]].  I left the pen in an upright position for two days unused.  That was enough to cause the pen to start skipping.  I was able to restore the flow only after rinsing with hot water and forcing water through with a bulb syringe.  Now it writes again like new, but this seems like a confirmation that the pen is not especially designed for carbon ink, seems to be only a normal fountain pen, a good one and very smooth for a extra fine nib, but just normal.     (Before you ask, hot water is a trick sometimes used with some Hero pens to assist with initial disassembly of the pen for cleaning purposes, especially with a Hero 616.  While that was helpful to clear up residue inside the pen, I was not able to disassemble the pen, either I need better instructions from a fountain pen forum, or it seems the pen is designed to me semi-disposable, not intended to be repaired or to receive deep maintenance).

product_title: Rubbermaid Reveal Power Scrubber
review_body: People ask me what it's for. I say "For a little while." But, unconventional me. I used it for the usual "around faucets", then one day I saw a tiny spot of dark something - maybe oil on my otherwise pristine carpet. So I put some Woolite on the spot and with the pointy implement either cleaned it off  or drove it in right down to the sub-floor - either way, it looked perfect after I sponged it off. I then cleaned the implement  with some bacteria destroying hand soap. product_title: Canon Office and Business MX922 All in One Printer, Wireless and mobile printing
review_headline: Here is my fair review of the Canon PIXMA MX922 and why you should consider buying at your local store
review_body:
I was searching for a new printer since the cheap replacement ink killed my Epson WorkForce 633 and it was a fast printer for document printing. I came across this printer when I was searching for auto 2-sided printing printers and it was surprisingly ~$20-30 cheaper than HP and includes a 2-sided ADF scanning, which all competitors lacks, but given this printer have a lot of bad reviews, I better off buying from BestBuy or OfficeDepot locally so that I can return it easier in case of trouble. My decision saved me a lot of hassle.
Since I don't have a car, I took a bus to BestBuy and carry the printer on and off the bus twice and took me 1 hour to complete the journey. When I gone home, I realized that the printer box may have been opened, but the receipt marked as new. When I opened the box and power on, I found out the printer lacks a first time turn on set up, Driver CD, sample picture paper, some manuals and the ink missing. Also the printer showed an error code telling me that the ink tanks are all empty. So I called my friend to drive me to BestBuy to get another one. The manger says that they never heard of it and they will investigate. If this was to happen on an Amazon purchase, it will take me 2 weeks before I can get back to work again. That is one star off.
So let's get something clear here
1. Canon's printers are not famous for fast or anything. It performs like a snail for document printing even document mode and fast mode is on and quiet mode is off . If you want a fast printer, get a laser printer or look elsewhere. You will just give it a one star review and return it.
2. This printer first time turn on set up is the most complicated compare to all the printers I have used. It is harder than setting up a wall-mounted TVs. If you hate following instructions, look elsewhere.
3. This thing is little bit wider than Epson and HP, look elsewhere if you hate it.
4. The inks are more harder to find compare to HP, look elsewhere if your local store does not carry Canon ink.
With all those non-sense out of the way let's get to the review.
Expect printing/copying speed for all your stuff as slow as a cheap printer you find from Walmart. If you tune the driver/settings a little bit it can get faster. Just give yourself a coffee break while your printer is printing.
The 2-sided ADF is a really handy feature that no other offers at this price point and you will love it.
Auto 2-sided printing should be a standard for all printers.
WLAN/LAN set up is easy
Google Cloud print and E-mail printing service set up is easy, just allow the printer to print out the necessary document, and follow the instruction.
Functions like printing templates (Included: folder paper,graphing paper, etc.) without computer is convenient and you can download more via the printer interface, not like HP with coupon printer and angry birds.
There is a second paper tray for you to put some smaller papers,like photo papers, only complain is cannot put normal paper into it and print normal stuff.
Included DVD/CD printing tray.
2 black ink tank(1 big and 1 small)
Buttons only lights up depending on what function you are using
Easy night operations
The last complain is that Canon don't pack all the drivers and software into 1 package. Instead you have to download all individually.

There are more functions I need to explore but for ~130 it is a bargain compare to other offerings.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Updated 10/4/2015
I'm on the my second set of ink. The speed of the printer have degraded by 10-20 seconds. Sometime a minutes.
At hot temperatures, printer will show Master error. Unplug the power cord, wait for 1-2 hours. Plug it back in and it is up and running again.
It is quite annoying so I demoted the ratings.
Overall, I feel like a printer that can last more than two years had already exceeded my expectation.had already exceeded my expectation.

product_title: SOL Corp (Non-OEM) 4 Pack OPC Drum Refill Kit Use In Brother DR-110CL DR110CL Drum Cartridge for HL-4040CN MFC-9440CN DCP-9040CN Series
review_headline: Just buy the drum unit if you don't like to tinker
review_body: There were no instructions and no rubber gloves provided for this product. Also, no videos on YouTube. However, I saved about $200 by not having to replace the entire drum. Sure, I sat at the dining room table for about 2 hours to puzzle it out. In the end, I performed a successful rebuild on all four PCR rollers for a DR-110CL (drum) on my MFC-9840CDW. No more black blotches on my papers! I was so proud of myself! The trick is to remove the metal plate on the wire side of the drum unit, gently snap off all the gray plastic end caps, remove the tension pins, and remove the shaft pins on both ends of the rod. After you get the rod out you can remove the old PCR roller and insert the new one. Leave the paper on until you are all done reassembling the drum. I consider myself very handy, but this job was tough! Just buy the drum unit if you don't like to tinker.

product_title: HTC TOUCH PRO 2
review_headline: Unique Tilting Screen and Vivid Display!
review_body:
WE LOVED:
SCREEN, KEYBOARD, WIRELESS FEATURES, TOUCH FLOW 3D LAYER, SURETALK, TILTING SCREEN, BUILD QUALITY

WE DISLIKED:
RESISTIVE SCREEN THAT IS EASY TO SCRATCH, AVERAGE BATTERY LIFE, LARGER FOOTPRINT, NO FLASH FOR CAMERA

BOTTOM LINE:
FANTASTIC BUSINESS AND ENTERTAINMENT SMARTPHONE THAT UPDATES ON THE ORIGINAL HTC TILT.

EXTENDED REVIEW:

THE HTC TOUCH PRO 2 IS THE NEWEST WINDOWS MOBILE SMARTPHONE FROM THE TAIWANESE MANUFACTURER, HTC. THE PHONE PACKS SOME VERY POWERFUL FEATURES ONTO A COMPACT PACKAGE. THE SMARTPHONE WILL COME TO ALL MAJOR US CARRIERS, SUCH AS AT&T, T MOBILE, VERIZON, AND SPRINT. GSM VERSIONS WILL BE QUAD BAND WORLD PHONES. ALL VERSIONS OF THE PHONE WILL INCLUDE 3G, WIFI, AND BLUETOOTH. IN OUR REVIEW, WE USED THE AT&T VERSION.

HARDWARE:
THE HTC TOUCH PRO 2, OR TILT 2, IS A MEDIUM SIZED PHONE. ON THE FRONT, THE PHONE IS ABOUT THE SAME SIZE AS A IPHONE. HOWEVER, SINCE THE SMARTPHONE ALSO FEATURES A SLIDE OUT QWERTY KEYBOARD, IT IS PRETTY THICK. OVERALL, THE PHONE ALSO HAD A NICE WEIGHT, THANKS TO THE MATERIALS USED. THE PHONE SPORTS A 3.6 INCH RESISTIVE DISPLAY, THAT SHOWS OFF VIVID COLORS. BELOW THE SCREEN IS A TOUCH ZOOM BAR(FOR WEB AND PICTURES), AS WELL AS FOUR SHINY BUTTONS. THEY TAKE YOU TO THE START MENU, BACK TO THE HOMESCREEN, AND TALK/END KEYS. THE BUTTONS ARE EASY TO PRESS, BUT DID NOT HAVE MUCH TACTILE FEEDBACK. THE FRONT DISPLAY IS ALSO VERY REFLECTIVE OR MIRROR LIKE. PLEASE NOTE THE AT&T VERSION OF THE PHONE LACKS A FRONT VIDEO CAMERA. THE LEFT SIDE OF THE PHONE HAS A VOLUME UP/DOWN KEY, AS WELL AS A PUSH TO TALK BUTTON. THE RIGHT SIDE HAS A SECOND MICROPHONE, AND A NONMAGNETIC STYLUS.ON THE TOP IS AN ON/OFF KEY, AND THE BOTTOM HAS A HTC CHARGE AND MUSIC PORT. THE BACK HAS A LOUD SPEAKER, AND THE 3.2 MEGAPIXEL CAMERA. YOU ALSO GET A SPEAKERPHONE BUTTON. INTERESTINGLY, ALL THE BUTTONS ARE BUILT ON THE BACK BATTERY DOOR, SO WHEN YOU REMOVE THE DOOR, YOU CANNOT ACCESS THOSE FEATURES. THE PHONE ALSO HAS THE MICRO SD CARD BEHIND THE BATTERY DOOR (HOT SWAPPABLE). THE PHONE HAS AN 1,550 MAH BATTERY. THE QWERTY KEYS ON THE PHONE ARE SUPER LARGE. THE LETTERS ARE ARRANGED IN THE SAME FASHION AS A KEYBOARD FOR A COMPUTER. THIS MADE TYPING MUCH FASTER. THE LETTERS ARE ALL BACKLIT AND HAVE EXCELLENT FEEDBACK. I DARESAY, ALMOST EVERYONE WILL LOVE IT. THE TOP ROW IS ALSO DEDICATED TO SYMBOLS OR NUMBERS (ON DIFFERENT VERSIONS). THE SCREEN CAN ALSO TILT UP FOR A BETTER ANGLE IN TYPING.

SOFTWARE:
INSIDE, THE TOUCH PRO 2 RUNS WINDOWS MOBILE 6.1 PROFESSIONAL EDITION(FOR VERIZON, SPRINT, AND UNLOCKED), OR 6.5 PROFESSIONAL EDITION (AT&T). 6.5 IS A MUCH BETTER SYSTEM WITH THE NEW FINGER FRIENDLINESS. HOWEVER, HTC ALSO ADDED TOUCH FLOW 3D TO MAKE IT BETTER. YOU HAVE A BOTTOM BAR TO ACCESS ALL THE PHONES FEATURES, LIKE INTERNET, PHOTOS, WEATHER, ETC... THE PHONE ALSO INCLUDED OPERA MOBILE WEB BROWSER OUT OF THE BOX. THE PHONE WAS AS A WHOLE RESPONSIVE AND FAST(670 MHZ PROCESSOR). OTHER FEATURES INCLUDED GPS, LARGE ON SCREEN KEYBOARDS, SCREEN HAPTIC FEEDBACK, AND A ACCELEROMETER. IF HTC STOPPED HERE, THEY WOULD HAVE MADE A STRONG SMARTPHONE. HOWEVER THEY MADE IT BETTER WITH SOMETHING CALLED STRAIGHTTALK TECHNOLOGY. THE PHONE HAS NOISE CANCELLATION DURING VOICE CALLS. ALL YOU NEED TO DO IS PLACE THE PHONE ON IT'S SCREEN, FACE DOWN, AND THE SPEAKERPHONE WILL COME ON. PICTURE QUALITY WAS DECENT, THOUGH NOT GREAT, AND BATTERY LIFE WAS ON THE SHORTER SIDE. HOWEVER WITH ALL THINGS CONSIDERED, THE HTC TILT 2 IS A SOLID CHOICE FOR ROAD WARRIORS LOOKING FOR A MODERN WINDOWS SMARTPHONE.

If you put in third-party cartridges you are besieged with warnings about how you're not covered under warranty for whatever happens as a result of using such cartridges.

The second issue is that the printer sometimes decides to make weird noises and cycle itself for what seems like an hour. It cannot be shutoff or reset. You simply need to wait until it decides to start working again. When printing large documents the printer needs to think for 10 minutes before it even starts printing.

review_headline: Great to use, durable, and absolutely adorable!
review_body:
These pencil cases are great to use, durable, and absolutely adorable!

I got the pastoral set shown in the main thumbnail with some hesitation as the same sets showed up all over Amazon and there were so many options. I tend to be more hesitant in those cases, especially when I'm not familiar with the brand. The set had such a great value though (4 for $3.57 at the time of this review, they were almost double that when I bought them!) that I decided to go for it. I'm really glad that I did decide to go with this pencil case set!

Some things that really impressed me:

SHIPPING- These came a LOT sooner than I expected! My friend also ordered some pencil cases from China which took weeks to get delivered and the expected delivery date on these were 15-25 business days which translates to about a month. I was so impressed when it arrived after only a short period in time! My order history says 2 days, but I think it may have been a week? Either way, I was very surprised when it arrived!

DURABILITY- I've been using a couple of these to store all of my writing utensils that I use for college (there are a lot) and I've used them, as in actually opening and closing them up practically every day for about a month and a half and they are still working perfectly! The zipper is like new and the bag itself is holding up great.

SIZE- I've also used the bags to hold some make up and brushes in addition to all sorts of writing utensils. One bag can hold 4 highlighters, 5 pens, 1 eraser, and a small flashdrive without a problem. One bag can also fit a round blush/foundation compact as well as mascara, liquid eyeliner, lipstick, and a brush! Just note that with the compact, it doesn't allow the bag to widen very much because it's almost too big.

review_body: I've been a loyal Epson fan for the past 20 years. I finally called Epson and they agreed to send a replacement. They sent a printer..the blank ink cartidge was only half filled. By the way, when you return the printer for replacement, be sure you're using Epson ink because they do ask that you include the ink cartridges with the printer. I went online and I see many Epson users have noticed the issue with the ink. Don't buy it unless you're willing to spend a lot of money on ink. Goodbye Epson! You've just lost a very, very once loyal customer!  Update: Epson has already sent me two replacements. Just got the 2nd replacement, it came with a set of new ink cartridges. I printed out two test print pages and it told me that I needed to replace the black ink. How can that be? I called Epson support and was told that the print uses more ink when it's setting up the ink. A whole cartridge? I've already spent more on ink than the cost of the printer. And most of that money went down the drain when I had to put the printer thru so many cleaning cycles when the printer didn't print properly. This printer is baaaaadddd news!  Update: Received the THIRD replacement printer from Epson! Pretty much same problems, won't recognize the ink catridge, then showed ink empty after printing 3 pages. Called Customer Support again! Mentioned that it'd be ridiculous to send me another replacement printer to Hawaii, shipping costs more than the printer I initially bought. THEY offered to send me an upgrade to an XP-820 which I received about a week ago. Am waiting for the power cord...hope it'll work. product_title: X-ACTO XLR Electric Pencil Sharpener, Gold
review_body:
Purchased this x-acto pencil sharpener to replace another broken x-acto pencil sharpener at work.

Plugged it in, and put a pencil in the opening... No go.

Did some troubleshooting, determined that a tiny piece of plastic within the front cover was broken off, this tiny piece of plastic is responsible for depressing the 'safety switch' which functions to only allow the sharpener to work if the cover is in place.

In my mind, this extremely small and fragile plastic tab could be an engineered flaw that, while likely not designed to break prior to the first use... may be designed to break all the same.

After some jury-rigging (really safe thing to have to do to a safety switch, mind you) I did get the thing to work; though it was very underwhelming. The motor is so weak it sort of defeats the purpose of having an electric sharpener.

I really wish I could say this sharpener had some redeeming qualities, but it does not. Even after repairs it doesn't function on a level I would consider acceptable for an electric pencil sharpener. Beware.

review_headline: Still waiting for an Android smart IP Phone
review_body:
I had an IP + DECT phone before for home landline. The small size is perfect and it's wireless. The HD voice is fantastic, like DVD vs HD. I returned it because the interface is too bad compared to a smart mobile phone. I created the "ideal" home IP phone out of an old android phone and a big retro blue tooth handset for better acoustic.

The GXP1400 has the right price for me to add an extension and as a backup which does not need wifi. It will also be easier for kids who didn't have a smart phone. I can also call on a computer on ethernet cable as a backup but that will be too much involved otherwise.

It's not too big for home use, 8 by 8", though I prefer it to be much smaller. The plastic is solid and the phone have enough weight not to slip. There are 4 rubber pads so the phone stays stable on the desktop. All the connectors plug straight into the back, so that you can't put it flat on a table without using the stand for inclination. The screen and the UI is rubbish compared to a 4" smart phone. Without backlight you will have difficulty viewing unless you config the lighting around it and the phone stays at the same place all the time.

The web browser interface can config everything except for the telecom provider registration! On the old discontinued phone I tried at least there are over a dozen of providers preinstalled on the phone. You just need to enter your ID and password. For this 1400 you have to enter everything by the 10 phone keys!

1st I changed the passwords to all cap so I can enter them and hope that the all cap URL is recognized just the same. Then I remembered in the good old days on mobile phones you can text with numbers, both cases and even punctuations on the 10 keys. What a pain to enter callcentric dot com twice with all lower cases.

I did it so many times before this 1400 so I just enter what I think it should be. (All androids in our home are also extensions.) I left out the proxy entry and the phone seems to reboot forever.

My provider has instructions for Grandstream but not this particular model. I tried a few times. I think you need to reboot after you save the settings. The 1400 don't let you let you see old passwords so you have to enter it every time you try something else. I changed my password. My provider doesn't display the password on the website. That's how much I'm frustrated. I thought the U on the screen was V !

I tried a few more times with no hope of success. Then all of a sudden the phone say registered. These were the fairly standard settings that I intended to enter all along. Still have no idea what exactly gone wrong.

The 1400 will be wireless as I have an wifi routers than are turned into wireless bridges. The router box is a lot smaller so if you don't mind carrying the 1400 around the router isn't an issue. Or I will be adding ethernet over powerline adaptors, which is superior in going through walls.

As for the screen and UI I don't intend to use it much. I can use my smartphone to see who's calling, custom ring tones with names and hopefully speaking caller ID for SIP phone will work someday. I can also initiate calls on the 1400 from my contacts list on the browser and perhaps on the mobile phone too.

product_title: Panasonic Landline Telephone
review_body:
At first I liked it fine. I was able to successfully pair the system to my cell phone and the sound quality was great. But then, after 10 months of trouble-free service, the unit self-destructed. Both of the remote handsets ceased working at almost exactly the same time. The screens were blank and there were no dial tones (my land line was still connected). The lights on top of the handsets were flashing which, I understand, means the batteries need charging. But they wouldn't accept a charge. Except for the flashing lights, it was as if there were no batteries at all in the units. Installing new batteries did not rectify the situation.

I'm guessing that the chargers somehow actually DISCHARGED the batteries. When I placed the handsets into the cradle in the console, they immediately responded. So there was a strong possibility, in my mind, that the remote chargers were defective. I sent both handsets and chargers back to Panasonic under the warranty. l soon received two replacement handsets and chargers, which are working fine (so far).

Now here's the problem: The two units were sent back to Panasonic under their one-year warranty program. But what I received in return were two refurbished units with 90-day warrantees. It would appear that Panasonic doesn't have enough confidence in their products to issue a longer warranty period. If the replaced handsets and chargers display similar faults I'll be looking elsewhere for a competitor's product.

review_body:

For those that are not aware of this, the best way to make and receive high quality calls is to setup the Quality of Service (QOS) settings correctly and to connect the Ooma to your DSL or Cable modem first, then to your wireless router if you have one. You can configure QOS by typing http://172.27.35.1 in your web browser, then go to the "Advanced" tab. Type in your average internet speed and the Ooma Telo will allocate bandwidth when you make and receive calls so that your calls won't sound problematic in case you have a very bad internet connection.

Other than that it was worth the switch!

product_title: Ooma Telo Free Home Phone Service
review_headline: Hawaii (808) Numbers Unavailable, Horrible Customer Service
review_body:
I am currently sitting on hold with Ooma. I have been on the phone for over 40 minutes and have been trying to set up a Hawaii number and get answers about Ooma premier for over an hour (online + phone). This is after the hour of research I put in prior to purchasing Ooma and thinking this would be a great solution.

Context: I own a vacation home in Maui. We wanted to offer free local and long distance calling to our guests and have a second line for those inquiring via phone about the property.

Research: Nowhere on Ooma's site does it indicate any complications with obtaining an 808 phone number. The premier service is advertised as being able to either forward a second phone number's calls to another number or go directly to voicemail.

Reality: I was told after speaking with four Ooma representatives (two who were supervisors) that obtaining a Hawaii number is very expensive for their company and could take up to 3 months to obtain. After asking if I needed to physically do anything to the Ooma once the number was received, I was told "yes", I would need to reboot the Telo. When I said that I wouldn't be on-island to do so, I was then told, "well, we can do it from here if you call us and as long as the Telo is connected to electric and internet." It's a solution, but its hardly what was advertised and this took me well over an hour to resolve. I'll update when I get the 808 number to share the final outcome.

The second question, regarding the second phone number (NOT line, Ooma is very clear on this...over the phone) via the Premier service to be used for our inquires was another disappointment. In order to have a second number that has different settings (i.e. call forwarding or forwarding direct to voicemail) from your main number, you have to purchase an additional Ooma device. Nowhere in their advertising is this specifically stated. To get this clearly answered, I had to ask the question at least5 different ways and one supervisor was so condescending in her response that I asked to speak to another supervisor because I didn't appreciate her tone or understand her explanation. The supervisors were so immersed in the Ooma lexicon, that they had extreme difficulty explaining to a layperson who had never used their services before.

As a person who runs a successful small business and who is very tech proficient and makes recommendations to clients about the technology and tech services they should use for their organizations, I was incredible disappointed in the quality of customer service Ooma provided and their disrespect and misrepresentation of their product.

I am keeping the Ooma on the basic service plan to see if the 808 number issue gets resolved, how, and when. At that time I will decide whether or not I will continue. However, given the other VoIP options on the market, if this is "the best" I fear what the competition is like and may be forced to keep them. That said, there's a lot of room in this market for a top tier option and I'd be willing to pay more to have it.

product_title: Sanford Parker - IM Fountain Pen, Gold Trim (1760799)
review_body:
As an avid fountain pen user (I've got 50+ pens), I'm always on the lookout for a good pen value. This pen is pretty inexpensive, but it is not worth the money.

I won't spend too much time talking about the aesthetics of pen. I personally find this pen to be a surprising combination of boring and unattractive, but looks are very much a matter of taste.

As for writing, the pen was a major letdown. I have purchased $6 Chinese pens on eBay that have written circles around this one. While I haven't experienced as many of the ink flow problems that other users have experienced, there are a few things about writing with this pen I don't care for. The nib is very small for the size of pen, which can require holding the pen either too close to the paper for proper hand position, or holding the pen on the step-down between the barrel and the section. Writing with this nib is akin to writing with a roofing nail: it is one of the most unfinished writing tips I've ever used on a fountain pen. While it wasn't scratchy for me, it was very rough, even on super-slick, fountain pen friendly paper.

Be aware that, if you want to use bottled ink, you'll also need to buy a Parker converter as the IM doesn't come with one. Since Parker uses proprietary converters, you can expect to pay upwards of $10 to get one. (I, fortunately, had one already from another Parker pen.)

Overall, I wouldn't recommend this pen for a first-time fountain-pen user. And my experience with Parker nibs is that their quality control can be all over the place. Some will write well, others will feel like you're writing on sandpaper (which was the case with my IM). There are a lot of other pens in this same price range or cheaper that will give a much better writing experience.

review_headline: Useless feeder, expensive ink, questionable print quality
review_body: Edit: I have had to come in and edit this review to a lower star rating -several- times as I use this printer. Formerly, the only pro I gave it was that the wireless function worked great; however, the wireless function has now stopped working for no reason, and I have to plug the printer in to use it. Edit 2: I just tried printing out my first photo; I set quality to high, used photo paper, and made sure the ink levels were sufficient. The photo came out smeared and unusable. I'd remove another star from my score if only I could...  I find black ink runs out very quickly; I ran out of the sample cartridge within a week or so, and the replacement I bought only lasted a month (and I doubt I printed much more than 50 pages in that time). Black ink is only about $12, but I'm still not thrilled to have to replace it so soon. The color ink levels are doing much better (I have yet to buy a replacement for the included cartridge).  I bought this model especially for the scan feeder, but honestly, it works no better than the glass. It feeds extremely slowly.  Finally, print quality is not great. I noticed lines on my printed-out PDFs-- I figured it might just be a problem with the files. However, the printer just now left a big line through an amazon return bar code I printed on it. Totally unacceptable.  I would not recommend this printer.

review_headline: That works great. One slight problem was that the files arrange ...
review_body:

My other recorder has the middle button lower that the out\er, and the outer is square, so it works better. Best might be for outer to be diamond shaped, so the points are in the best direction to press. I can only put temporary, not permanent, index marks into files I downloaded, only noes I recorded. However, It stays where I'm positioned when I switch folders or change batteries, so it doesn't need index marks very much.

You may want to do what I did - download the user's manuals for the devices I was interested in buying. Now that I bought it, the manual on my computer is the one I look at if in need to. I can find it easier that the paper one and search it.

product_title: HP OfficeJet Pro 8720 Wireless All-in-One Photo Printer with Mobile Printing (M9L75A)
review_body:
I have always preferred HP printers over other brands for many reasons. They are usually well made and don't feel as though they are entirely constructed of plastic. The Pro 8610 is typical HP in that regard. It is big - like the older models - and sturdy. The setup didn't take me as long as some of the other reviewers said it would, which makes me think I may not have done it as thoroughly as I was supposed to. I, like others, had some problems setting up the fax feature - so I never got through that.

The prints do come out quickly! I will give it that. For my purposes, the best ink coverage occurs with smooth white 24# paper. You really have to experiment with the paper you use to get the best effect for the type of printing you do most. It appears to me HP has done something here to conserve ink, which is a good thing, unless it compromises quality. In my case, I do a lot of heavy color printing. I have to reproduce 8x10 full-color artwork, one after the other, sometimes for hours. Sounds as though it's a tough test for a printer, but I have been doing this on my HP Officejet 6210 All-In-One for years and years and it has been a champ. I absolutely do not see the 8610 being up to the job. Truthfully, I have tried a lot of other printers just to see if I could find one I could use concurrently with my 6210 to share some of the burden. I want the 6210 to last as long as it possibly can, because they just don't make them like this any more.

While the 8610 is advertised as a color photo printer All-In-One, it's use for me will be limited to (quickly!) printing letters and documents and occasional throw-away-quality color pieces. I would say I was being too picky about the quality of the color prints if I hadn't had the good fortune to own a 6210 all these years. HP has spoiled me. But considering the 6210 cost over 400. when I bought it and this one is way less than that amount, I can use the 8610 for its strengths and keep my 6210 for its superior color printing.

product_title: DBPOWER BL-18 Portable Mini LED Projector with USB SD VGA HDMI AV Multimedia for Party,Home Entertainment,20000 Hours Led life with Remote Control
review_body: Before I cover my experience let me state that this review is for the DBPOWER LED Projector 1080P HDMI USB Black, BL-18 LED projector:    BEWARE THAT AMAZON IN THEIR USUAL  APPROACH HAS LUMPED ALL REVIEWS WHICH INCLUDE 4 OTHER MODELS THAT CAN BE SELECTED FROM THE SAME PAGE AS THE BL-18 AND LUMPED ALL THE REVIEWS WITHOUT SEGREGATING SPECIFIC REVIEWS. SO TAKE THE \\"FAVORABLE\\" REVIEWS WITH A GRAIN OF SALT IF THEY DO NOT SPECIFY THE ACTUAL MODEL THEY ARE REFERRING TO.    I was looking for a low-cost - under $ 150 - projector that I could use for a small gathering that didn't cost hundreds of dollars.  And I did not need high lumen output or an extremely large screen since the viewers would be within 5 to 6 feet of the screen at a table in a room that could be darkened.  I did realize that most low-cost projectors such as the DBPower LED Projector 1080P are poor performers.  However, in spite of some unfavorable reviews, most reviews on the projector were generally favorable so I took a chance to try it out with the following results:    Size, weight, design:    The projectors size is very compact, not more than 9\\" x 9\\" square and about 5\\" high.  Weight is very light, too light infact: if a solid or stiff cable is attached to the unit it easily walks around the table if the cable is touched or moved - like the old AT&T Princess telephones of the past that had the same problem until AT&T installed lead weights into them.  The projector is constructed of a piano-black glossy plastic.  Fingerprints are easily and readily deposited and while this has nothing to do with the unit's ability to project images, it's something that I noticed very quickly. Controls and video inputs are on the sides with menu and other buttons on top. Ergonomics, aside from the feather-weight of the unit, are generally good.    Ease of use and Hookup:    The projector came with a composite RCA cable and a sparsely printed pamphlet that is for the most part useless.  Connecting the unit is relativelyeasy though once you realize that first you must hook up the projector to a video source, turn on your source and the projector, then fiddle with the menu button on the top of the projector - which on my unit seemed very temperamental - and then hope for the best. I have much experience with more expensive projectors and this unit was for some reason very finicky - but eventually I got an image out of it.    My Video Source:    The projector accepts a composite video, VGA video, and surprisingly an HDMI video input as well.  I tested the unit with both an HDMI and VGA source, both from laptop computers with a VGA and/or HDMI output.  Both input types produced an image for my tests, but I did not try the composite video input.    Image Projection and Focus    This unit was capable of projecting a relatively large image, as much as 50\\" or more - but not very usable as will be explained in the next section.  Although there is a lens-cap to protect the projector's lens when not in use, this model has no lens focus assembly like most other projectors, neither can the image be electronically focused or zoomed.  After all, what can you expect for under $100, right?  The only way you can focus (or zoom) an image with this projector is to move the projector closer or farther from the screen - or move the screen closer or farther from the projector.  If you're able to achieve focus, moving either the projector and/or screen a hair off will require re-positioning to regain focus - a tedious, frustrating, and not very reliable process.  In addition, this model projector does not have any height adjustment to alter angle, etc, so you will have to really position it perfectly to avoid severe keystoning (this projector has no controls to adjust keystone).    Image Quality and Brightness    Probably the two most important aspects of any projector are its image quality and brightness.  The larger the image size required and distance the projector is from the screen the brighter it has to be for a given rooms' brightness.  As I said most projectors in this price class do not perform very well usually because of either an image quality and/or brightness level issue. For the BL-18 LED model there is no lumen light level stated but the LED Wattage is indicated as 100 WATTS.  You'd have to convert 100 WATTS to Lumen to get the lumen but even doing that would not be accurate since most WATTS to LUMEN are for incandescent bulbs and not LED lamps. So at best conversion is an approximation. 100 Watts roughly corresponds to 1600 lumen - which is actually quite bright, especially in a darkened room - but as you'll discover later in the review I got no where near that level of brightness.    The relative quality of image, i.e. sharpness, color relationships, produced seemed reasonable, though colors were very washed-out and not anywhere near movie-quality.  When switching between my VGA and HDMI sources I could easily see the differences in image quality.  But overall, Image quality was more typical of a badly performing projector used for meetings, etc.    As for image brightness: I tested this projector in a dark, not dim, or dimly lighted, but totally dark room with no windows and all lights out, with the projector on a table not more than 5 feet from the screen which was a whiteboard about 48\\" x 36\\" in size - not a large screen at all.  The whiteboard coating has a BETA (the ability to reflect or amplify light) of 1.1 - meaning it will provide an approximate 10% increase in reflected brightness as opposed to using a plain white surface.  Because I was in a totally dark room I had to use a flashlight occasionally to actually provide temporary light while manipulating things then turning off my flashlight when not needed to regain darkness.  While there are some good things this projector has (small size, weight, portability), I am truly sorry to say that unless there was something severely defective about the unit I received my battery powered flashlight (a standard \\"old fashioned\\"  flashlight with an incandescent bulb with 2, not so fresh double-A batteries) was significantly brighter than the image produced by this projector.  In my totally dark room, my unit produced a barely view-able image which was for all intents and purposes, not usable.    Summary:    Frankly, unless my unit was defective, I can't really imagine how the other reviewers gave favorable reviews for this particular model - unless the reviews were fake.  Because of the very poor performance from this unit I had to return it.    Customer Assistance:    The only positive thing about this experience is that customer support was good:  After contacting the seller (via Amazon's internal system) I was soon in communication with a \\"Karmen\\".  To be fair, Karmen did offer to send me a different unit (same model) - an offer I did not take - and then later offered to send me a more costly unit for a slight discount off its regular price - yet another offer I did not take.  I would suspect that the more costly unit might have \\"done the trick\\" but unless my unit was defective I was not interested in testing additional units (and taking yet another chance and having to ship back yet another unit).    The only down side to this experience was the time lost testing, repacking, and shipping, and the $12 I spent to return the unit.  I'll chalk that up to experience.    Final thoughts:    It would be unfair to say that any projector purchased from DBPower is a clunker.  I strongly suspect it was the particular model I selected (or a defective unit) and that other slightly more costly models from BDPower would have been a better choice perhaps.  But as they say, \\"once bitten twice shy\\".

product_title: Sky Blue Silver Embossed "EVERY CLOUD HAS A SILVER LINING" Journal / Notebook / Diary, 256 Premium Quality Lined / Ruled Pages, 5x7"
review_body:
I bought this without perusing the description and was under the wrong impression that this was made by Eccolo, as this appeared among the list of many Eccolo journals that have similar looks and size. However, these are actually made by Fine Keepsakes, one of the sellers of those Eccolo journals on Amazon.

Despite this not being made by the bigger brand, I think this will function well enough and has a nicer design than most Eccolo journals because of the actual "silver lining" that goes around the embossed cloud. It looks very clean-cut and adds a nice touch that subtly stands out, unlike Eccolo journals that have only two tones of color.

However, there are a few differences:
- Unlike the Eccolo journals, this does not have rounded corners, both the cover and the papers.
- This uses slightly thinner paper, but very slight so I doubt there is much difference in usage. I haven't written on both papers yet.
- The first page (the spread immediately inside the cover) does not have a pattern printed on, and thus looks less polished/luxurious.

I haven't actually used this journal yet so I cannot comment on some important aspects of a journal, such as how the paper takes different inks, how flat the journal lies - it doesn't lie flat initially, but I haven't tried to break the spine - and how durable it is. However, from observation I can say that the paper quality is not terribly lacking nor the binding too stiff or weak. The lines are not too dark, nor too light (for lighter lines, go with Peter Pauper Press).
Although this journal is slightly lesser in quality than Eccolo journals in these ways, this journal is also slightly cheaper, and looks better in my opinion.

This is not one of those high-quality journals to write in with fountain pens and pass on as an heirloom. But its size, cheap price and unique design (if you appreciate this sort) are enough for me to like it as a decent, portable journal to carry in my backpack and write in with everyday sharpie pens and gel pens.

review_headline: Great Projector for the price when you understand the limitation.

I connect this to my tablet and open up the bible app and poof it is there. I did open up a game to see what it would look like. I didn't expect much but i was impressed that i got that type of picture for this little machine and the price i paid for it. Granted i purchased another projector for my wife’s slide show because i knew this machine would not give the best image. In other words this is great for simple and small projects. If you are looking for a projector for major projects, movies, and any quality then this is the wrong machine. If you are looking for something to share documents, reading etc then this will do just fine. I would suggest you purchase Mini HDMI connection to get the best quality that this machine can give. review_body:

What I didn't expect, was to find the outer packing box to be halfway opened, and the inner box taped shut with 4 pins missing.

I know, I know. It's really a petty thing. But, when you are sold a certain number of items and some are missing, it can get under your skin.

I'm sure my world won't end over 4 missing T-pins, but when it's late at night, and I'm trying to block out a knitted lace shawl that took me a year or more to knit, and it's a gift for a very special person, and I need 4 T-pins to finish blocking the last side or the shawl will look like one spot is crumpled, what do you think I'll be muttering under my breath about the company that shorted me those pins? It may not be pleasant.....

So, that's why I'm only rating this as 4 stars instead of 5. If you say 100 T-pins are enclosed, then please don't only send 96 pins.

product_title: HP LaserJet M5035X Multifunction Printer Q7830A#BCC
review_headline: Very good hardware but not so good firmware
review_body:
Bought this machine for small business with multiple users. Installation instructions are sketchy and insufficient. Installing printer on local network and copy part was very easy and required no help. However, installing scanner part (to get the output to the user’s PC) was nightmare. I spent several hours trying to figure out myself ( the attached “help” CD was like blank, did not give anything and the printed installation guide was, well written by somebody who possibly had no idea what the machine is), I called HP Support. The person at other end was very knowledgeable and eager to help, but it took her a long time to install scanner on my PC even after using remote desktop. When this was accomplished, I tried myself to connect other PCs, I spent hours before calling HP support to find out that clicking “OK” and “apply” was not enough. What the installation required was click “OK”, next “apply” and hold your breath, once more “apply”! Few tips for HP to make better installation guide:
• Use better quality of paper for installation instruction (toilet papers that I use has better quality)
• The installation manual does not mention about creating a folder on destination PC, why?
• The installation steps should be in the bullet point format not like as an essay, it will just take less than an inch of your valuable (!) paper
Bottom line, great Laser/MF printer to buy under 2k. However, if you are planning to use the scanner part (on network), do NOT attempt to install yourself as the very important steps are ignored in the installation guide. Call friendly HP Support line

- Have a vacuum nearby. Toner is messy, but if you have a vacuum hose nearby, you'll stay nice and clean. It also helps clean out the cartridge before refilling.
- Tap the cartridge out completely (you have to clean it out before refilling) to make sure no plastic bits from the hole you drilled are inside.

product_title: AmazonBasics 12-Sheet High-Security Micro-Cut Paper
review_headline: Excellent shredder in a number of ways
review_body:
I had satisfactorily used Amazon Basics cables and batteries previously, and am happy with my judgment of upping the ante and ordering this shredder. After several months' use, I am very pleased with this 12-sheet Amazon Basics shredder. It shreds quickly to quite secure-enough-for-me pieces, and is as quiet as I hoped -about as loud/quiet as my beard trimmer. I am especially pleased that it is healthier and neater than my old machine which yielded paper dust upon shredding and when emptying. It also looks nice, and is very easy to use and empty. It has jammed only when I put in too many and/or too-thick sheets, and the reverse mode has easily cleared the jam -easily enough, that I don't worry too much about the exact number of sheets I'm inserting. It has never jammed using credit cards nor CDs -in fact, as you might expect, they go through significantly easier than 12 sheets of paper -which go through fine. I've never considered stacking CDs to shred, so I don't know nor care what a CD capacity might be. I replaced a 15-year-old $80 shredder that jammed easily with less sheets, was very loud, and by-produced dust.

Note, that when left on Auto, the machine is still on, consuming power, (and) using (up) its circuitry -however minimally- to immediately engage when loaded. BTW, I would guess the LED is probably consuming less, and marginally-additional power, than the readiness state itself. I leave my unit on only when I expect intervals to be less than about 15-20 minutes.

I am uploading a couple of photos to illustrate the LED On indicator, and paper/CD/credit card shreds.

review_body:
The HP-35, my first calculator, cost $400 + $24 tax. The Casio cost 1/10 + no tax! (I discovered that in FL it is still possible to order without tax from Amazon if the dealer is outside of FL. Amazon began taxing FL residents at the beginning of May.) It is amazing how much more the Casio can do compared to the HP=35, especially in view of inflation!

I tutor math, and this calculator does about everything required for high school math including AP Calculus, College Algebra, Pre-Calculus, and other subjects. If more students knew about this calculator, it would soon outsell the TI-84. Of course, if you think you have to have the latest full-color back-lit screen to show of to your friends, then go ahead and spend OVER 3 times as much ($125). But if you are a secretly partly nerdy or fully frugal or both, the Casio will not disappoint.

The Casio actually comes with a manual specifically for this model instead of a computer disc or a web address.

The screen is smaller than 9860, but contains all the same information, which is more than the TI-84. (The X-axis is longer; it can display two full cycles of sinX in radians when each pixel = 0.1 unit on both axes.)

The 9750 does not have the math input option. That would be the only reason I can think of right now that would justify spending more money for the 9860.

The 9750 does not have the spreadsheet or the e-act features of the 9860, but I seldom use them.

product_title: SVGA 3LCD Projector
review_body:
This is a review of the Epson VS330 3 LCD video projector. The VS330
was designed with business use in mind, and falls toward the mid range
of Epson's line of "value" priced projectors. It is light in weight,
but is no light weight when it comes to features - with the very
unfortunate exception of not having any sort of auxiliary audio output
.

The fact that the VS330 is aimed at the business user rather than the
home theater viewer shows up in the 4:3 aspect ration and the 1024 X
768 native picture resolution. For home theater use one would want
16:9 or 16:10 aspect and at the very least 720 resolution, with 1080
being preferable.

This is a light weight projector, clocking in at just a hair over 5
lbs. It, the remote and various cords could probably be easily carted
around from office to office if Epson had only seen fit to include a
carry case or pouch. The decision not to include one is almost as
baffling as the decision not to include an audio "line out" jack as I
mentioned above, a decision which really puts a cramp in the style of
this otherwise very nice little projector.

Other than that missing audio out jack the VS330 sports a very nice
selection of inputs, including HDMI, RCA, computer d-sub, and S-video.
There is a mono speaker built into the VS330, but you are not going
to get booming volume out of it.

One of the business features included with the VS330 is what Epson
describes as "Plug-and-play 3-in-1 USB projection, audio, and mouse
control for instant setup" The CD that comes packaged with the
projector has software for this control that can be installed on both
Windows and Mac computers. As luck would have it, the only computer
that I have available to me at this time use a Linux OS, so I was not
able to test those features.

Now granted that this model is aimed at the business user, I really
didn't have much in the way of business work to test this projector so
I put it through its paces as a replacement for the 40" flat screen TV
in my (very) modest home theater setup. Keep in mind that this is not
the recommended projector for this use. The native picture aspect and
picture resolution are not what one would want if she or he were
picking a home theater projector. An Epson projector similar to the
VS330 but designed for home theater use would be the PowerLite Home
Cinema 725HD 720p 3LCD Projector which sells for about 20% more than
the VS330, but is much more appropriate for use in the home theater.

The first thing that I plugged into the VS330, even before starting on
the home theater equipment was my smartphone, using a MHL micro usb to
HDMI adaptor that I had purchased here. It was kind of mind blowing to
see the screen of my HTC One blown up to 72". I streamed a couple of
TV shows, and while the picture quality wasn't the same as my 1080p
flatscreen, the quality was certainly good enough to display to a room
full of people. Carrying your documents or video files on your phone
rather than on a computer is doable.

Next I unplugged the HDMI "out to TV" cable from my A/V receiver from
the flat screen and plugged it into the VS330. What an improvement!
I know that it could be better if I had the proper home theater
version of the projector, but even this one produced a beautiful
picture projected on my living room wall. A word of warning here -
When I first temporarily set the projector up, it was sitting close to
me at about face level and I happened to be in the line of fire of the
exhaust fan. It gets too hot to sit where that blows on you...

I set up a more permanent mounting setup this morning and I have just
fallen in love with thehuge and quite detailed picture. Of course
with the video coming out of my A/V receiver I still am getting Dolby
5.1 audio just like I always have. I have a Roku box for online TV
services such as Hulu Plus, Netflix and Amazon Prime and my "regular"
TV is high def/Dolby Digital broadcast signals that I pick up and
playback on my TIVO DVR. Oh, I almost forgot. I wasn't really happy
with the focus of the VS330 until I discovered that the video noise
reduction default setting is "on". Turning it off much improved the
focus of the projected signal.

My takeaway on the VS330 is that it is a sweet little projector at an
affordable price. It is quite light weight, seems sturdy and can be
set up easily a quickly where ever the user needs to project a video
from a computer or other device. I would give it 5 stars except for
the lack of any audio out jack and no included carry bag. I give it a
very strong 4 stars.

review_headline: My Previous One Was About 15 Years Old
review_body:
I had a Seiko SSII label printer.It just stopped working in the middle of a label. I checked all the usual and came to the conclusion it was just done. I have a lot of label materials for that printer, so I wanted another just like my old one.I went looking for a used one on e-bay. Much to my shock and amazement, an old one costs nearly as much as a brand new one. That was also when I realized that my old label printer was from 1999. I was using Windows 98SE then.

After I determined that my existing supply of labels would fit a new printer, I ordered the 620.When I upgraded to Windows 7 in 2010, I upgraded the Seiko software. When I loaded the new software, it converted my labels file. I was surprised, but happy, of course.

The new software compared to the old is as night and day. Wow, how the software has grown up! The new stuff is in color, and you can do so much more with it. As someone mentioned, it is much easier to load the labels in the printer. My printer is white, whereas it looks grey in the picture.

I always loved my old Seiko label printer, and now I love this one too. I hope it lasts as long as the old one did.

review_body: I am a notary, and sometimes have to scan many pages at a time in a short period of time. The scanner I have can only scan 8 or 9 pages at a time, very slowly. I purchased the first one a couple of months ago.  The first time I tried it out, it began jamming after about the third sheet of paper.  I called tech support and they offered no help at all. I returned the first one and ordered a second one, thinking the first may have had a glitch, or had been damaged or something.  The second one is doing exactly the same thing!  The thing jams on about the third sheet, and starts pulling two or three sheets in at the same time.  The only way I can get it to scan more than one sheet, is to thread the sheets in on at a time (very slowly).  I did not pay $300 to do this, so I am through with the ADS2000. My less expensive copier/scanner/fax machine can do the job better for me than the ADS2000.  At least I can put 9 pages in the old one, and not have to worry about it jamming.  I am very disappointed with my purchase.
