product_title: CANON PIXMA iX6820 Wireless Business Printer with AirPrint and Cloud Compatible, Black
review_headline: Prints are beautiful, I'm just not in love with the design
review_body:
I found the set up a bit problematic. It has one push connectivity which did not work for me. Epson is making printers with touch screen interfaces that make set up a dream, and so this one really is not up to par, IMO, for it's price range. Then I couldn't figure out how to get the ink in. I wasn't born yesterday - I review printers ALL the time and I have worked on several corporate networks doing all kinds of printer support and repair, and there I was, I couldn't figure out how to get the ink in. It wasn't that hard really, I've just come to expect the ink station to move over when I open the lid. It's really just a matter of mashing a button. But why?

It's big, and the paper tray stands up on the back, for the feed. The top isn't completely flat. I don't like this design. I like my paper IN A TRAY and the top of the printer to be flat, so I don't lose any surface space in case I want to put a book down. The trays just work better for the feed in my experience - this one is typical- it sometimes pulls just fine, and other times it takes 2-3 sheets with it. In fact, the whole design of this printer just seems old and well, cheap, to me. I've got a wide format Epson Xp-950 and it's flat, and has index cards all over it right now- and it has the nice touchscreen that makes tasks so much easier.

Also, with the normal paper feed, it just doesn't hold enough to call itself business. My Epson workforce holds 500 sheets per tray. That's more like it.

As I am writing this, a complete refill of this ink - with Cannon - is $65. Each cartridge runs about $16.

With the wide printing, it does blueprints fine. The print quality is very good and sharp. That's my main use, but I did print an anime poster to test and it looked great, with accurate color reproduction and no skipping or fade apparent.

It prints photos nicely- with good paper and the right settings they look as good as any, but once again, it suffers from lack of a decent paper feed, IMO. I mean, I expect to have to hand feed 11x17s.

There's this software that comes with it - it lets you print calendars and such - as long as you have genuine Cannon Ink it in. It's really going to be about useless to anyone that is handy with graphics software. It reminds me of those EXPERT software packages that make calendars and put graphic frames on pictures. It's annoying too, because by default it likes to live down in the taskbar by the clock, and will fly up and out and tick me off, and who needs another useless bloat TSR? (Programs that load automatically at start up, using system resources.)

It works, it prints lovely, it just fails in comparison to other printers IMO. I've got 3 wide formats- this one, an Epson, and an HP. This is my least favorite. The listprice as lower but if you can afford a bit more, get a better designed printer. I think in the long run you will waste less paper (I had trouble with standard, not 11x17) and save a bit each time you buy ink.ean, I expect to have to hand feed 11x17s. product_title: Brother MFCJ870 Wireless Color Inkjet All-In-One with Scanner, Copier and Fax Printer
review_body: I've had this printer for about three weeks. It replaced a Dell printer that my wife was talked into buying when she bought her laptop. The Dell was possessed by demons from the very beginning and we could never get the Wi-Fi to work with both our computers. I shopped around and settled on this one because of the ratings. I took the time to read through the manual on how to set up the Wi-Fi and set it up as a network printer. I loaded up the software on both computers and just like magic both computers could pint. You have no idea what a blessing that was. My wife is a teacher and prints quite a bit so when it don't work I have to! Untold hours were spent fighting the demons in the Dell. This printer is fast, quiet, and relatively small. I've had no issues what so ever. Some one complained that it isn't built very sturdy. If you have a habit of treating things roughly or take your temper out on stuff then this not your printer. It is very well built but not robust. If you give it some respect it should last for years. Print quality is very good. So far paper handling has been perfect. Printing from my Kindle Fire is no problem with the right App. It is capable of so much more than I've used it for so far but everything I've asked of it has been performed flawlessly. The manual isn't the best but it is good enough that you can figure things out. If you don't spend time in the manual and just plug it in and go, you will never get the best this machine has to offer. Bottom line is, I think it's a great printer. Seems pretty stingy on ink too. Being able to use after market ink without hassles is a big plus also. A very big thumbs up!

product_title: PRO Call Blocker - Ver 2.0 - Incoming & Outgoing Telephone Number Blocker
review_headline: This device has brought peace to our house...
review_body:
We got this little box back in September of last year. It has performed excellently. The device itself is small...4 inches x 3 1/2 inches and about 1 1/2 inches tall. It is also very lightweight. The display screen on it is small and could be difficult to read for folks with poor vision. You may want to keep a small magnifying glass near it.

First: Ignore the instructions that come with it...you will go crazy. Go to hqtelecom.com for a much, much better set of instructions.

*once again...ignore the enclosed instructions...*

Once I got it set up (took about 5 minutes), blocking numbers became a no-brainer! My provider is Comcast and it only allows 12 numbers on the block list. Pretty funny that...considering there are already 100 numbers on my current block list on this device. Once a number is on the list, your phone doesn't even ring once. Done deal!! When a new number comes it, it rings. Then, just push the blacklist button if the number isn't known to you. That's the last time you'll hear the phone ring on that number...how cool is that? Or, if you've been away from home, you can page thru the numbers that called...if you see an unknown number, just press the blacklist button and you will see 'Save...Succeed' on the readout.

You can also block up to 10 area codes. (I currently have 2 on that list...just make sure you don't know anybody in that area code...lol...) You can also block prefixes in a particular area code! I have a few of those, too. Many telemarketing companies
use an entire block of numbers. You can kiss them goodbye, too!

I have looked for a device like this for years. It was money well-spent.

product_title: J.Herbin Fountain Pen Ink
review_headline: Mesmerizing Color... Fantastic Ink (beware it's a new formula though - golden sheen no more - see EDIT)
review_body:
First things first, it is true what other reviews said, this has been reformulated, so there won't be much of a golden sheen to your red (at least there was none that I could see. But maybe it truly makes the ink safer for fountain pens, so I won't complain if I can safely use it in some expensive pen.

Even though, a little sticker on the plastic wrap around the package warns you that this ink is very saturated and that oyou shouldn't leave it lying in a pen reservoir forever... (hence I'll wait a bit until I dare put this in my Diplomat MB 149). And saturated it is! The red is deep and strong, and yet it gives off a nice shading. The color is mesmerizing. It's the red of all reds!

It's expensive, but it's not like I am going to write novels with this, or take minutes in business meetings. I may use it to annotate here and there, and do a few drawings and letters. So, even though it is pricey, I can see this mottle lasting me quite a few years.

Last (and maybe least of all) the bottle is kind of cool. Antique-looking little cube. I was afraid the red waxy knob would have to be broken, or the string cut... but as it turns out, it's a rubberized coating on the cap, and the string does not attach to it, so no wax seal to break-off. The bottle will look cool even in a couple years.

3 MONTHS EDIT --- The gold sheen is indeed there, but you need to shake the bottle quite a bit before filling, and it only works if you have tremendous flow, and areas where the ink can pool and concentrate (using an italic or a flex nib for example). Also depends on the paper. Unsurprisingly, the sheen shows better with high quality paper...

review_headline: Do you like clogged pens? Buy this ink!
review_body: Noodler's inks for fountain pens are my favorites, but their inks for highlighters are NOT. The formulation of these inks include very fine pigment particles that clog pens and seem to react with the felt of the highlighter pens to coagulate in the barrel of the pen into a semi-solid. The pen that came with this ink was no exception. But, if you use the pen with a dilution of Noodler's fountain pen ink, it makes a reasonable highlighter (of course don't expect UV fluorescence from most fountain pen inks!). So the one star here is for the included pen. The ink is a total waste of money in my opinion.

product_title: Quartet Magnetic Combination Calendar Board, 17 x 23 Inches, Dry-Erase and Cork, 1-Month Design with List Frame
review_headline: It was good until it warped.
review_body:
I thought this would be nice for a nonprofit office that I volunteer in. When I received it from Amazon it was in great condition, but then I put it in my car to take to the office and it was parked outside on a very warm day. The heat warped it so badly that it won't lay flat against the wall now. I gave it four stars because the circumstances under which mine warped are probably fairly unusual, so I doubt that this is a common problem with this product.

Aside from the warping issue, it's a very nice write-on calendar board. It has room to write the date and one or two brief things in each date square. It also has space at on the side to write additional notes and a cork strip at the bottom which is very convenient. We were using a write-on calendar sheet that thumb-tacks to the wall, but it was hard to write on and never cleaned off completely so after a while it began to look pretty shabby. This one is better in every respect - it wipes off cleanly and looks terrific. Maybe I'll glue-gun it to a piece of masonite to flatten it back out and then hang it. I guess if it were made a little more substantially it wouldn't have warped, but then it wouldn't have been under $20 either. Bottom line: it's a nice calendar board for the money.

Biggest complaint: I tried to trim the wrap, as it was about 1 1/2 feet too long for my cord-end-to-power-strip length, and that was a mistake--fabric frayed instantly, unevenly, unsightly and badly, even though I used very sharp scissors and a very straight cut. I ended up taking it off, using fabric glue to seal the end, and it worked fine from there--just make sure you're prepared if you want to trim it!

Overall I'd say I'm pretty pleased but the two problems mentioned above meant I had to go through the hassle of unwrapping and re-wrapping (I know, it doesn't seem like it'd be that big a hassle but I had more trouble with it than I'd expected). I was unhappy about the fraying but the fix wasn't too difficult.

product_title: Straight Talk Wireless Home Phone
review_body:
I purchased this unit in December 2013. Set up was a breeze and my old land line number was ported within 48 hours with no hiccups. My phone bill was about $68 per month, now I pay $17.17 (including tax). It does work when power is out but only if you use an old school corded phone. I have two cordless base units attached so that I can have a cordless phone in almost every room in the house. It looks a bit odd to see both bases units next to one another, but who cares?

The sound clarity is good. I made a long distance call when I first got this unit. The person I called had no idea I was not using a land line until I told them.

I do have one complaint. When making outgoing calls, you sometimes have to redial the number several times. For some reason the calls won't go through. You get a recording that says "Welcome to Verizon wireless" and it proceeds to tell you that your call did not go through as dialed. So far that has not been a big issue, but it is kind of a pain in the neck. Also, the redial feature on my phones are hit & miss, meaning that sometimes the calls go through the first time, but sometimes you get the Verizon message mentioned above.

This unit is for phone calls only. You cannot hook up to alarms, internet or the "I've fallen & I can't get up" thingies.

You do have to purchase the phone card each month. You can buy it online, at a brick & mortar store, or you can set it up on the straight talk website and have it renewed automatically each month. That is what I did, and I have not had any issues with that.

FYI: I do live in a rural area surrounded by lots of trees. I have absolutely no problems picking up a signal.

product_title: Canon Office Products IP7220 Wireless Color Photo Printer
review_headline: Carefully Read All Reviews - The 4 Stars and 1 Star are Very Similar!
review_body:
I purchased this as a replacement for my IP4500 which was fast, quiet, and excellent at printing both text and photos. I am returning it because it is slow, noisy, and is not excellent at printing.

I purchased the printer for very light home use and although this printer got many bad reviews and I wanted a printer with a rear paper feed, choice was limited and I thought I could get used to the negatives over time. I decided after 2 days that I would not want this printer even if it was free. The LONG and NOISY start up time and the slow printing are unacceptable to me. My IP4500 was rated at 34.5 decibels while the IP7220 is 44 decibels. It is not only louder, but makes noises during set up and close down that sound like a woodpecker and grinding gears. It also vibrates, as other reviewers have mentioned.

Yesterday I spent much time on the phone with Canon. According to the techs I spoke with, Canon has made changes in print speed to save on ink. They have switched to opaque tanks so that people won't use refill ink over buying new Canon tanks, as refill ink is sometimes not well filtered and causes problems in the printer. Canon has pretty much phased out back feeding paper option - there are only 2 models of photo inkjet printers that feed from the back, and they are both office machines that take 9X13 paper and the rear feed is therefore necessary. They had no idea why the rear feed is discontinued and seem to be unaware that many people prefer it.

Consumer Reports and PCMag both gave the IP7220 very good reviews and having had such good performance with the IP4500, I chose to take with a grain of salt the fact that User Reviews on Canon's own site gave it an average of 1.8 The Amazon reviews seemed pretty evenly distributed, but on closer reading, the complaints of slowness and noise were mentioned pretty consistently from 1 star through 4 star ratings.

I think that a video review of the printer would be really helpful - not an un-boxing and features review, but a \\"let's see and hear this thing printing both text and photos\\" review. In this case, \\"a video would be worth a thousand words\\"!lly helpful - not an un-boxing and features review, but a \\"let's see and hear this thing printing both text and photos\\" review. In this case, \\"a video would be worth a thousand words\\"!

product_title: HP Officejet 6600 e-All-in-One Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner, Copier and Fax
review_body:
I don't recommend buying this product. The printer looks good but suffers from two very serious design flaws that make it unacceptable:

1. Cartridges deplete even when you don't use the printer. I haven't touched my printer in over a year, and when I used it last, everything was fine. I just booted it up to use it again after a year of it doing nothing but sit there (powered off, no less), and as soon as it booted up, the display told me that ink was 'depleted'. I couldn't understand how, since I had never used it in over a year.

2. You can't print in black & white if even just one of the color cartridges is depleted. In my case, the display told me I had magenta, cyan, and black ink, but the yellow cartridge was depleted. No problem, I thought, I'll just print in black and white. The printer wouldn't let me. I can't think of any valid technical reason why the black cartridge couldn't be used when the color cartridges are out, so I'm going to assume this decision was made purely out of greed on HP's part. For this reason, I will never buy another HP printer ever again. They just lost a customer.

But since this morning it won't print because of a \\"paper jam\\". Trouble is, there is no paper jam. It will print, from the computer or printer console: the Printer Status Report, the 3-page \\"HP Network Configuration Page\\", etc. But NOT any document/s that I need to print out. Yet it insists there is a paper jam. But please do not take my word for it, it would appear, that when I googled \\"hp officejet 4630 false paper jam\\" that I am certainly not alone. There doesn't appear to be a manual \\"reset\\" button that I can find either. If I find one & it works, I will immediately revise this review.

UPDATE/UPGRADE TO 3 STARS: ☆☆☆ (forgot to enter a date) Still frustrated & annoyed I decided to try again, still had the paper jam notice but yet another status report printed without problem and on a whim I tried to copy a document, this also worked ok. I shut the printer off (unplugged also) & left the room for a couple of hours. Came back, tried again. Paper jam notice gone & everything printed perfectly. Hope it lasts.

UPDATE: 4 STARS ☆☆☆☆ July 10, 2014 Has been working just fine. Had a couple of real paper jams which were easy to clear & appeared to be the paper sticking to itself rather than a printer problem. Still no more phantom paper jams. Am feeling pretty good about this now.

UPDATE: July 30, 2014 I had a problem with the instant ink program which turned out to be my own mistake and NOT the printer. I mention this fact because I had to call HP Cloud Services to try and find a solution. While I am embarrassed I am impressed with the HP customer service and although the fault was entirely mine I appreciated the quick response and help. I wish all customer services were so good. Printer still working great by the way.

product_title: Samsung Electronics SL-M2825DW Wireless Monochrome Printer
review_headline: did not need the cd for windows or linux
review_body:
not sure what the cd offers. I grabbed the latest win7 drivers from the website and used the control panel to add_printer, followed the prompts and things worked fine. on linux, I connected the usb cable directly and that worked fine (able to print pdf files from linux just fine).

one area that was confusing: the paper tray has a plastic stop tab that pulls out BEYOND the end of the paper tray and unless you do that, your usual US letter paper won't fit. it was not obvious I had to do that and the plastic looked like it would not go beyond the end of the tray but it did and that's how you fit a full US letter page in the printer tray. this is probably why that one poster had problems and always had to keep filling the 'low capacity' tray.

I have not tried wireless yet. not sure I plan to. wireless is not secure and I dont' want hackers submitting print jobs and consuming my toner and paper ;) wired ethernet works great and is secure so I'll use that.

unit is very small and lightweight. classic simple looks. would be nice to have a display instead of just buttons but this keeps cost down.

only just got it yesterday so I don't know its reliability, but linux works great and win7 install was simple enough. I like having a network printer for under $100.

update: I just put the printer on the wired network and tried to have linux (latest ubuntu) find it. the standard gnome guis were able to find the printer and it was easy to make it the system wide default. you can even set the default to be double sided (double sided printing is VERY cool with this printer; it half feeds a page and then sucks it back in again to print the other side before ejecting it all the way) and when you go to a command shell and 'lpr file.pdf' it just plain works! no worries about linux and this printer, at least with usb and wired ethernet. again, I have not tried wireless yet and I'm not sure I really care, to be honest.

review_headline: Don't buy!!! This printer is a total piece of junk

Our old HP photosmart printer, which was only three years old, completely stopped working, so my husband bought this as a replacement. It seemed like it has a bunch of great features... if only it worked. The first HP6520 he bought printed a couple of pages, then gave us an error that there was a paper jam. But there was no paper jam. We tried everything to get rid of the error, going through the manual, watching troubleshooting videos on the internet, calling HP, etc. Finally my husband took it back to the store for an exchange.
The replacement is only marginally less crappy than the first. Regularly my laptop can't locate it's wireless signal, so I have to manually go over and reset the printer by unplugging it and plugging it back in. Even with that, I still almost always get errors. So I've taken to hooking my laptop up to it via USB to print (which totally negates the whole point of the printer supposedly having wireless capabilities). Once the printer does start to print, over 50% of the pages are mis-fed and the printing only shows up on half the page. I literally have a 0% success rate after many, many trials of getting this printer to print any document without having to go back and re-print the mis-fed pages once or twice more.
If this had just happened once I'd think we'd just gotten a lemon. But two lemons in a row? I can only conclude that HP produces junk and really couldn't care less about their customers. Last time we buy an HP product ever.

product_title: Sony MDR ZX100/BLK - headphones (MDRZX100/BLK) -
review_headline: Good Sound For The Price, But Requires Tone Control Bass Boost.
review_body:
Sony MDRZX100 Black Headphones, by Sony.
These inexpensive, closed, 30mm dome headphones are a bit shrill, and unless you have some tone controls available, the bass is minimal at best. Forget up-front thumping bass, -as even with your bass controls cranked up, the bass is barely adequate. These headphones are not very good with music sources that don't have bass tone controls, -like your basic computer. On a Sony CMT-EP505 MICRO HI-FI, I had to use the ROCK setting to cut some of the highly directional shrillness of the POP setting, and I had to press MEGABASS to get adequate bass response. The sad part is that the bass is very clean when boosted, but you have to be able to boost it. In rating these headphones, I give the sound a rating of 4 out of 5 stars. The design gets a rating of 3, as the clamping pressure cannot be relieved by bending the plastic headband outward, just above the ear cups. The poorly designed bass response was also taken into consideration. The ear pads, with the sprayed on finish on top of foam, can get a bit sweaty after a while. To lessen the clamping pressure, I extended the headband as far as possible, and added a bit of padding (6\\" of 3/8\\" thick, 1\\" inside diameter self-sealing foam pipe insulation) at the top of the headband. Headband pads can be bought, but the hot water pipe insulation was all I had available at the time. I suppose that I could have sacrificed an old wool skating sock, with the end cut off, and folded halfway inside out, to do the same thing. Without the added padding, all you can do is move the ear cups lower on your ears. The construction rates a 4 due to the limitations of the adjustable plastic headband. I also wish that there was an option to change the on-ear pads to large or extra large around the ear pads, as your head can handle long term clamping pressure better than the folds of your ears can handle it. Comfort gets a rating of 4, tied into the issues of small sweaty pads, and a plastic headband that cannot be bent outward above the ear cups to relieve the clamping pressure, without breaking the headband completely. With the padding, the comfort was acceptable. Thankfully, the headphones are light in weight at 4.23 ounces exclusive of the cord. Adding the ratings, we get a rating of 15 out of a possible 20, or 75%, a score of \\"C\\", and three stars overall. Are they worth buying? At the price of fifteen dollars, yes, but you have to adjust to them and work around their limitations.

review_headline: Awesome Pen for a Good Price! I Love it!
review_body:
Lamy pens are probably my favorite fountain pens.

Miss Timmons, my third grade English teacher, was right, I had no business trying to communicate in the written medium and should stay with guttural sounds and thumping my chest. (and absolutely NO more throwing my poo).

I got this sharpener at the beginning of the semester, and we've never looked back. The tip produced by the sharpener is longer than what I've seen other sharpeners do, but you get used to it. Mechanichally it seems ok, but it sounds like there are plastic parts inside that could break at some point. The tips produced are even but sometimes seem to be off-center leaving  think film of the wood on the pencil. I've noticed, that if I twist the pencil a quaftdr turn before lifting it up, this problem is usually fixed. You want to make sure to empty the container before it fills up, otherwise you will be cleaning shavings for a while. Overall I'm happy with it, the most annoying part is where it doesn't cleanly cut the wood around the center. However,  big pro is that it sharpens the softer colored pencils just as well as the harder 2HB pencils.

review_headline: Oh man, I'm in love with this flashlight, and I own about 8 Surefires.
review_body:
Surefire's are great but this Fenix blows them away and at a much better price point. I will most likely never buy Surefire again.
Don't get me wrong, I'll keep my Surefire's but the price is not worth it. This Fenix offers so much more and it's an awesome looking light. I thought my Flury was powerful. It's weird, the Flury is heavier and has that huge reflector, thought it would throw much more and wider light, not so, not even close to the Fenix. And the Fenix throws far. And you can go all the way to 850 Lumens. It does get hot at that setting. The Fenix is much thinner and lighter but not cheap feeling, in fact to me it looks and feels SO much better than any Surefire I own. If you're going to spend this kind of money on a light I highly recommend checking these Fenix lights out. If you don't like it you can send back. There is one thing I don;t like but I've only used it one night. I really wanted this light because of the switch on the barrel and the tail cap. Sometimes I like to hold my light at a right angle from the hip. You cannot do that with taillight switche unless you turn them on first. The Fenix barrel switch only controls the light settings. It it not an on / off switch. You have to first turn on the taillight switch and then cycle through the settings via the barrel switch. This would of been a deal killer for me but it's still a great light and after using it in the dark tonight it's a keeper. Really wish they would have a setting where you can turn the light on with the barrel switch.
When you cycle through the brightness levels and then turn off the tail switch it does remember which setting you turned it off from. So, if you cycles through, turned of the light via the tail switch at 850 lumens, it will come on at that setting. Pretty cool. But note, the barrel switch is NOT an on/off switch. This may be a deal killer for you. I still want a light that is only a barrel switch or either or, tail or barrel. Hope this helps in making your choice:-)
I need to check their site and see if they make a barrel switch only light. Or maybe someone here can recommend one.

review_headline: UPDATE -Great for what I bought it for - Great value
review_body: After having this printer for 5 months, I have changed my rating from 4 to 5 stars. I think I have found true happiness with this printer. Workhorse, cheap to operate, great two side scan, copy, AND print. Now going to update my marketing collateral materials with two side card stock because I have this printer. Terrific value! Original review follows:    I was interested in replacing my current Brother Laser with a new all in one laser that had a two sided scanner. But it was VERY (like really, really) heavy, and I wasn't too keen on the prices for replacement toner cartridges and drums. Then I found this . . . two sided scanning, wireless, inexpensive replacement cartridges, and not too heavy (one woman lift, easily).    Install: The one criticism I would have is there is too much bloatware, takes forever to install CD, and it appears, that, for what I need, most of what was installed could be skipped. But the software controls are fairly intuitive and easy to use, once installed. Cartridge install, too, was a little tricky (had to be done in exact sequence, when asked), but again, doable. Also, paper loading is from the long side in the tray (in a landscape position), which again is weird and counterintuitive, but workable once you understand that this is what is required.    Since I mainly bought this for the two sided scanning capability (its a second printer for me), I have to say that this feature is awesome. Easy, easy. It even asks if you are done before it closes the file (in case there are pages you want to add).    So I would definitely recommend this printer for the kind of stuff I need it to do, i.e., two sided scanning, copying, and printing - and the printing on a fairly low volume basis.    As other people have noted, its not a great graphics printer in the \\"photo quality\\" sense. Colors are not especially true to what's shown on the screen - a little washed out. But good enough for most business uses. Printing is also pretty slow. And it does have alarge footprint (it will do 11x17\\" paper).    But I am happy so far.

product_title: Fellowes Powershred W11C, 11-Sheet Cross-cut Paper and Credit Card Shredder with Safety Lock (3103201)
review_headline: Good, but be careful what you shred with it.
review_body:
This is a solid product.

I initially was very disappointed that it stopped working after about 9 months. This was due to the sensor being blocked.

Be careful NOT to put sticky paper in there, i.e. Amazon tags that you pull off of your boxes. It won't break the machine, as they can still be shredded, but a wad of sticky shredded paper builds up around the sensor, only allowing the machine to be run in reverse.

I was annoyed as I thought the machine was fragile and broke. This was not the case - as I said, it was just that the sensor was blocked.

The area around the sensor (which is a little plastic piece that gets depressed as the paper goes in; it's at the center of the paper opening, set down inside) can be cleaned with a knife or other small instrument.

DEFINITELY unplug the machine before you try to clear it out and still I would never use fingers to try to do it, they're probably too big anyway. Aside from that hangup, the product works very well.

product_title: uni-ball 207 Impact Gel Pen
review_body:
These refills worked for my purposes. Uni-ball has more than one refill. Some refills (like this one) have a longer plastic section between the metal tip and the ink tube. These tend to go into "click" pens. The plastic section was white. Others have a shorter section with a flared lip. That type goes into "stick" pens. Those had a green section. This refill shows the longer white plastic section (the type I wanted). The package I received had a green section. At first I was disappointed b/c I thought I had ordered the wrong thing, then I compared them to the other green tipped refills I had. While the plastic section is green instead of white, it is long and has not lip (like the white type). It looks like maybe Uni-ball may no longer be using the white/green tip to differentiate between click/stick pens and maybe all the tips are green now. Who know? This same refill at the depot of office supplies local to my house still has the white tips (but only in blue and in the thinner ink tip so I ordered them here).

I'm happy with the refill. I mentioned the color thing in case anyone else runs into this situation and might find it helpful.

product_title: Brother Printer HL2270DW Wireless Monochrome Printer
review_body:
We originally bought this printer because my wife and I are both college students and needed a new printer and preferably one with duplex (automatic double sided) printing. This printer is equipped with both a wireless and Ethernet connection although you can only use one of them at a time. because I'm a nerd, i hooked this puppy up straight to our wireless router with a cat5 cable. it was not very complicated to set up as a network printer either. (but then again, i am a nerd, but I'm fairly confident my mother could have figured it out as well) it prints well and is able to be managed via my laptop and my home network. I can set defaults like toner saving mode or automatic double sided printing from my laptop and I don't have to steal my wife's computer to tweak the settings for when she prints. it is also very nice to not have to go and plug in a cord every time I want to print something. now I can stay at the table click print and it magically appears on the printer in two seconds. although that may sound incredibly lazy, it is non the less fantastic!

one negative thing I did notice is that if you use the thicker print paper, the first few pages will print okay but subsequent pages will leave toner trails down the whole page and make the print job look like crud unless you change the defaults to reflect that you are using thick paper instead of normal print paper. and that is the extent of my negative comments about this machine.

My wife and I are happy with this purchase and after over 1000 pages run through this printer (i just checked the printer report, not a made up number) it is still working swimmingly.

you will not regret buying this printer if you want a reliable black and white laser printer and you can see yourself using the bells and whistles it is equipped with.

I would love to give this stapler 5 stars. However, it looks like 4 stars is what it is getting from me today.

Pros:
- easily staples through 20 pages
- love the great low price
- the color pops, giving your boring office some personality
- lightweight, unlike those heavy Swingline standard staplers
- almost never jams up- almost

Con:
- When the staple strip gets down to 3 staples is when the jamming starts.

The con isn't too bad.... I just end up taking the last 3 staples out, and place in a new staple strip. Problem solved.

If I have the option arise between purchasing a Bostich vs Swingline. I will go with a Bostich.

product_title: Brother MFCJ450 Wireless with Scanner, Copier and Fax Inkjet Printer
review_body: I just received this printer 3 days ago, the shipping was fast it only took 2 days to arrive.  It is impressive for what it is. I got it for 80 bucks and i am very pleased with it.  It is good for making copies and scanning and every day printing, i would not use it for printing pictures though. I bought it because i had to replace my old Lexmark.  I like that it is a full bed scanner and that the paper is easy to put inside of it.  This thing is heavy and i am very careful when moving it around.  I think that the best feature of this printer is that it is wireless. Hooray! no more USB cables. :D It also does 2 sided printing automatically. It was easy to setup to my network and both of my computers are able to print through it.  The scanner also works well and it does full color copies. UPDATE! I want to warn you that under any circumstances if you are considering buying this printer to understand that i believe Brother now has proprietary cartridges for this printer meaning that if you try to use \\"COMPATIBLE\\" cartridges they will fail. I spent 25 bucks here on Amazon for compatible cartridges and my printer did not recognize them, each cartridge has a little chip in it that communicates with the printer and while these other non Brother cartridges may have worked in the past, they are not working now! I kind of hate that it it will cost me more for 5 high yield ink cartridges than i paid for the printer itself but that is to be expected as high ink prices are how these companies really make their money. I am very happy with the printer but the ink costs way too much and i am locked out of buying the cheaper alternatives together at this point. So you are warned. product_title: New York Toner Laser Toner Drum, 25,000 Pages- Black Brother Compatible DR-520 DR520
review_headline: Jams on duplex printing - but fixable
review_body: I give this compatible drum unit a 3 rating because of its price only. From other reviews I expected it would jam on duplex printing, but knew what to do about that thanks to D. Lee-Wo's review. Be sure to keep your old drum unit for swapping parts from this unit. A couple things to keep in mind when you swap the drums. First, never touch the new drum's surface. Second, minimize light falling on the new drum. When out of the cartridge for more than a few minutes, cover the drum cylinder with paper. Do not make any attempt to wipe clean the new drum. Third, there is a spring clip inside the drum cylinder that the rod may hit when re-assembling the unit. DO NOT FORCE the rod through the drum cylinder. Rather simply insert the drum's rod from the other side of the drum and the spring clip will clear the rod. You should also replace the rubber roller beneath the drum. When all back together, test your printer before discarding the old parts. When done, your old drum cartridge will get this unit's drum cylinder with its own shaft and plastic gears and the lower rubber roller with it's own white plastic bushings. Hopefully this vendor will resolve this duplex printing problem. But I'm okay with doing 10 minutes of assembly work for a $17 drum compared to up to $200 at retail. By the way, the prints with this units drum installed are very nice - I think this drum unit would consistently get high star ratings were it not for the duplex jamming.

product_title: AmazonBasics 12-Sheet Cross-Cut Paper/CD/Credit Card Shredder
review_body:
I tried to give this a chance - when I received it, I was immediately unhappy with the power for a 12-sheet shredder, and the cheap plastic that it was made from. It was also slow, slow, slow. The so-called \\"cross cut\\" was actually 2-inch strips, not small pieces. But given the number of reviews and the price, I decided to keep it.

I don't have things to shred everyday, but when I do, the shredder is probably in use for 1/2 hour at a time. I bought this shredder in December 2013, and used it about 6 times since. I was shredding ONE, empty, regular-sized letter envelope yesterday, when it just stopped shredding - mid envelope. The shredder still had power, had not overheated, and allowed me to run it forward and in reverse, but it would no longer accept paper, and wouldn't eject the envelope. I tried emptying the basket, and cleaning out stray paper from the blades, but it wouldn't work again.

I looked up other reviews and saw that this issue had been reported many times before. Since it is still under warranty, I contacted Amazon and they sent me a label to return it to them for credit.

I immediately reordered a Fellowes - I had one for YEARS and it was built like a tank. Don't waste your money on this shredder - if you do significant shredding and need a reliable machine, spend a few extra dollars and get something better.

product_title: Symbol LS2208 Barcode Scanner Kit Includes: LS2208-SR20007R - CBA-U01-S07ZAR Cable - 20-61019-02R Stand
review_body:
I have a small online retail business and use a barcode scanner when filling orders. I had been using the following $40 TaoTronics scanner for quite a while:

http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B006LVO56W/ref=wms_ohs_product?ie=UTF8&psc=1

But recently started using very small barcodes on some products and thought the LS2208 (due to it's great reputation) would do a much better job. I was wrong.

Pros:
- The LS2208 can scan items more rapidly than the TaoTronics scanner, as long as they are the correct distance away (see cons)

Cons:
- Whenever the computer is turned on, or woken up from sleep mode, the scanner emits three very loud beeps of increasing pitch (low, medium, high). These beeps are incredibly annoying and can be heard through a ceiling and two walls. I contacted Motorola (see con below) and they said there is no way to disable the startup beeps. Very annoying to hear all throughout the day.

- Motorola support is terrible. When I had a question about the TaoTronics scanner, I emailed the Amazon seller (who put me in touch with the manufacturer) and I got my question answered the same day. The first challenge with Motorola support is getting in contact with the company. They don't have a support email listed anywhere on their website and it's difficult to find the appropriate contact form. Then, after submitting the contact form on the appropriate Motorola division's website, the email gets forwarded to a different department where they create a ticket for me (which they email me to let me know), and finally a few days later I get an email from them. The first time I contacted them I just had a very simple question and they wanted to set up a phone appointment and answer it! The second time, it took just as long, but they answered the question in their reply email. Motorola really needs to improve their support system.

- Unlike the TaoTronics scanner, the LS2208 won't read a barcode unless it's within a certain distance range of the scanner (there's a diagram showing the specifications in the manual). I can scan a small barcode with the TaoTronics scanner with the barcode almost touching the scanner, all the way to the surface the stand is on, but with the LS2208 I have to get the barcode's distance from the scanner "just right" in order for it to read. For such an expensive scanner, I thought it would be better than the TaoTronics one, but it's much worse in this regard.

- When the computer is put to sleep, then woken up again (which I do a lot), the scanner doesn't wake up properly. The scanner won't read anything and the laser blinks every second or so. To get it working again, I have to lift the scanner off the stand and then set it back down again.

So to sum up, when I wake my computer up from sleep I:
1. Hear three loud, annoying beeps
2. Have to lift the scanner of the stand and then set it back down before using it
3. Have to position the barcodes just the right distance from the scanner in order for them to read

Motorola will not be getting any more business from me.

product_title: MagicJack Plus + Free 6 Months Subscription to Magic Jack Service
review_body:
I bought a house and realized my cell phone did not work inside, every conversation I had was like talking in morse code. Every conversation ending with - "your phone sucks" and me yelling back "then quit calling me!" A month into my new new home, i started house phone shopping, so i could make and recieve calls from home too.

I was skeptical about the MagicJack and the promise of a home phone line for $20 a year. I was worried about reliability, interferance, it not working at all. I read a number of reviews and talked with friends who had friends with the MagicJack and decided to try it because the appeal of $20/year vs. $20/month was too good to resist. Worst case scenario, i'd wasted a few bucks, i find it hard to justify 2 monthly phone bills, and since my cell isn't going anywhere, paying for a landline seemed silly.

I received the Magicjack and (once i got the right kind of phone) got it hooked up and ready to go. I just got a cordless phone, simple, nothing fancy. Make sure it's not one that's part of those wireless sets though, cause then you can't plug it in! It needs to have a phone jack attached to it. it was simple installation on the PC - then i moved it to my wireless router, plugged in the jack, to the phone router and power - and i had a working phone line almost immediately.

I sometimes have to reset the MagicJack, by unplugging it and plugging it back in. I don't know why, it just doens't work sometimes. But it works MOST of the time. I don't drop calls, I can walk through my entire house - with is 2 stories with a basement, outside, it works just fine. My friends and family that call me are quite happy with it too because it eliminated the e - i - e - i - o conversations. The only thing to remember is to dial the area code when dialing out or to it. And it works great!

I most definitely recommend this as a cheaper alternative!

review_headline: Works well but takes some practice
review_body:
Read the quick guide carefully and follow the steps in the exact order. Installing the drivers can get snarled up if you skip a step or change the sequence.

After you install Silverfast, go to the website and down load the latest update. The version on the disc is out of date and very slow.

Documentation kind of sucks. It is in the form of QuickTime movie clips and also some PDFs. I'm old fashioned and prefer big fat manuals with TOC and an index. Nonetheless, its all there in the movies. Maybe no one but me reads manuals any more.

I found best results are if you minimize enhancements and keep the contrast fairly flat. Then any enhancements including dust and scratch removal can be done in Lightroom, Photoshop or other image processing software. These all have better tools than Silverfast. or at least tools you are more familiar with.

Get a squeeze type dust remover like the Giotto Rocket and use it.

If you set ppi to 7200 you get very smooth scans but slow scans and huge files. You need to give some thought to your purpose. Maximum image quality vs speed and convenience.

product_title: HP Prime Graphing Calculator
review_headline: The first hour with my calculator
review_body:
Ok, I've had a love affair with HP calculators and RPN since I was 14. Still have my 15c, probably use it for
the rest of my life. HP calculators remind me of what a great company HP used to be.

So here is my first hour with the calculator. I instantly turn on RPN. I decide to try out the CAS. I find the 500+ page english users guide and head to the CAS section and I type in the polynomial root finder example exactly as shown on page 53. The equation is 2x^2+3x-2 with roots (-2 and 0.5).

..... one hour later I realize the example has many typos, 1) shift-alpha turns on caps, the CAS uses lower case only, 2) the screen graphic shows 2x^2-3x+2 (which has imaginary roots) but the screen shows (-2 and .5). How is that?

Update: I installed the connectivity kit, and the virtual calculator, and got updates for both. Next I tried to update the firmware for the calculator, BIG mistake. the connectivity kit
bricked the calculator with messages like \\"unknown command\\", then \\"update failed\\". the calculator only shows the \\"x^2+y^1=1\\" splash screen. Searching around I find a solution at educalc (search for 'hp prime rom update').

product_title: Fujitsu ScanSnap S1300i Mobile Document Scanner
review_body:
Our office was a sea of paper needing to be filed or scanned then shredded. In the hope of going paperless, I've had a flatbed scanner (without sheet feeder) in for many years, but scanning multiple double sided documents is so laborious that it just never gets done, leading to the piles of paper.

Decided to purchase a multiple sheet / double sided capable scanner in the hope of improving the situation. After reading many reviews, settled on the Fuji.

I'm extremely happy with it. Probably only scanned a couple of hundred pages, varied bills, documents, etc, so far. The scanner itself has performed flawlessly - no feed issues at all. The software, of which I'm really only using the core scanning functionality and not the organizing part, seems fine. Auto orientation detection mostly works well, scan quality is fine, OCR/searchable PDF also works (although I turned it off due to the extra processing time). I'm simply scanning to PDFs, and moving those into my existing document folder hierarchy.

Perhaps most importantly though it's so easy to use (open scanner, insert doc, press the button on the scanner) that I actually use it!

I'm using it on a Windows 8 desktop PC.

Will update this review if I encounter any problems.

product_title: Obihai OBi110 Voice Service Bridge and VoIP Telephone Adapter
review_body:
My unit lasted about one year and three months. I wrote customer support to help me troubleshoot, describing the problem, and they did not even attempt to help. They told me to buy another unit. Many emails later, still no help troubleshooting.

I researched, and found others that had the same problem, and a new power adapter cured their problem. During those emails mentioned above, and asking them 3 separate times to sell me another power adapter, they simply refused, finally telling me to buy any 12v power adapter from Radio Shack. (BTW, I supplied links to posts in forums that had people describing the same problem as me, and the cure, which was a new power adapter from Obihai.)

NOTE: The first time I asked them to sell me an adapter, they ignored the question. The second time, they told me they would not give me another adapter because my unit was out of warranty. The third time I asked, after reminding them I had been asking them to sell me an adapter, not give me one, that is when they told me to go buy an adapter. - Before I had asked the third time, I had looked around some. I did not find one with the correct size plug and the same power requirements. On the Internet, I found some used adapters for sell, but I wanted to buy a new one.

More than once, they told me to buy a new unit, without even trying to help me troubleshoot. ... Pathetic! ... This, also, after I had asked them about whether a new unit would even work after Google Voice stopped supporting (Obihai's use of) XMPP in May, 2014. - They ignored that question, also!

In one email, I aksed them to describe how to reset the unit, seeing as how I had found two different descriptions of how to do it on the Internet (and wanted to make sure I was not missing 'something'). Yes, they ignored that question, too.

As for the time the product was working... I could never get rid of the echos, and voice clarity was not very good.

Simply, I would not be writing this negative review if they had, at least once, actually attempted to troubleshoot with me, and had not been so indifferent to simple questions I had asked them.

product_title: Quartet Magnetic Dry-Erase Calendar, 1-month, 11"" x 14""
review_body:
While this calendar is a fair size for the price (really, $7 ain't bad), there are two things which really dock this calendar down a few stars. The adhesives it comes with for the magnet backings are 3M, but are not powerful enough to hold the calendar on the fridge. It slides down on its own, so I've managed to keep it in place by buttressing other magnets underneath. Thankfully, it doesn't fall completely off the fridge.

It's nice that it comes with additional magnets, but, since the calendar is quite tiny as it is, there's really no space to put the magnets on if you're going to write all over the calendar, so we've moved them off.

We use this board primarily for meal planning, and my wife and I constantly have to rewrite our plans once we've started them because we forget that the week starts on a Monday in this calendar. It may not seem like a big deal at first, but considering almost every calendar we use starts with Sunday it becomes quite the nuisance after a while. I have no idea why this company decided to start it on a Monday.

So, because this calendar can be stuck onto a regular wall, it's not bad on that part, but like most families we got this dry-erase board to use on the fridge. We still use it daily, but there are far better options, even if they do cost a bit more. The fact that this slides down the fridge and starts the week on a Monday seriously flaw this otherwise budget-friendly planner.

review_headline: Good Printer, But Don't Depend on the Wireless
review_body: I've owned this printer for over six months now.  I have mixed feelings about it.    Pros:  Excellent print quality  Reasonable ink usage  Relatively inexpensive ink  Canon came through on the rebate making the end cost very attractive    Cons:  Huge!  Wireless functionality is near useless  Paper handling is terrible <---- See Edit Below    ****Edited 11/20/2014  It turns out that the paper handling issues I had were apparently a defect in my printer.      After putting up with it's paper feed problems for over a year, I finally bought a new one.  The print quality and price (after rebate) were so good I was willing to try again.  The new one has no paper handling issues.  I can't say if the wireless works on this one.  Now that I've run the USB cable I don't really care about wireless any more.  I guess Huge! is still a Con since it's size made the original one cost prohibitive to return for repair/replacement.    I really like this printer.  I purchased it again even after being so frustrated with the first one's problems, so that tells you how much.  I added a star to my review.        Original Review Starts Here....    Print quality is great.  I use the printer for AutoCAD line drawings and it is much clearer and better defined than the old Epson it replaced.  I can't speak as much for the photo quality, but it looks great to me.  It doesn't seem to be too thirsty on the ink.  So far I've replaced black and red more than the others - which is true to the type of line drawings I create, so that seems legit.  I like that it uses separate tanks for each color, keeping the cost down.  But it does have a lot of tanks for those who print more multi-color stuff than I do, so it could get expensive there, I guess.    I use this printer with Windows 7 on a home network.  The printer wouldn't stay on the network.  Six feet away is a Canon MX860 that never misses a beat, so it isn't signal strength.  At first, it seemed it was just \\"sleeping\\" after periods of non-use andnot waking up.  But sometimes it would lose connectivity during a print.  I have since given up on wireless and attached a USB cable.  Solves the problem, but unfortunate that it won't serve the purpose for which it was designed.    And the paper-handling is horrendous!  I print almost entirely on regular thickness 12\\" x 18\\" paper - very rarely on something as thick as photo paper.  I can't find any paper thickness adjustment on the printer, and I've set the paper type setting in the printer properties accordingly.  Still, it feeds multiple sheets through at a time, sometimes grabbing additional sheet halfway through a print.  I can fill the paper tray and be out of paper printing a five page document!  If it manages to complete at all, as the extra paper sometimes clogs the feed and requires a manual reset.    So what you're left with is a printer that is VERY large and supposed to be able to be put anywhere and accessed by wireless network, but won't work reliably.  So you have to have a large space to put it close enough at hand for a USB cable.  But you'll want it close by because you'll have to babysit it, watching every printout to add paper or correct it's paper jams.    I've found a space near my desk that works for me.  And the print quality is so good that I put up with it's Diva personality.  Just make sure you are able and willing to be as accommodating before you buy one!

review_headline: Quality of toner as good as the factory one
review_body:
The toner is as good as the one that came with the factory cartridge and the parts fit perfectly on my HL-2270DW's starter cartridge. Unfortunately the solid toner light didn't go away despite trying to reposition the actuator gear, the one with the arrow pointing towards the bottom of the spring, in addition to making sure that the reset gear's flags had the correct orientation, and therefore I couldn't print until I found the following solution. Steps found online to 'reset the toner sensor':

- Open the front cover and leave open while completing the following steps.
- Turn the printer off.
- Hold the 'go' button (or "start' button) while turning the printer on. All panel lights should be on.
- Release the 'go' button (or "start' button).
- Press the 'go' button (or "start' button) 2 times.
- Pause. All panel lights should be on.
- Press the 'go' button (or "start' button) 5 times.
The toner light should be off. (error may be flashing)
The paper light should be on or flashing.
- Close cover. The ready light should be the only light on.

These steps are compatible with HL-2240 printers and most likely others as well.

A quick search on google for your printers model followed by the words "toner cartridge reset procedure/sequence" might provide additional information.

product_title: Canon PIXMA Printing Solutions MG5520 Wireless Inkjet Photo All-In-One Printer, Cloud Enabled
review_body:
This is a typical quality printer from Canon, by that I mean it will surpass other printers by other companies in this price range (Better build, photo quality, and durability)
For print quality and speed, I don't think you can go wrong.

Some Amazon reviewers have recommended other Canon models due to noise and speed, but I think you should see them in person before you buy. One of them is enormous and weighs three times as much as this one and is just much larger in size. Unless you're in a huge office with a massive desk space I think its impractical for home use. Also on some other Canon models available right now, I don't think it's as easy to get around the menu and operate the front panel controls. Also a couple models have a combined color ink tank which you DON'T want. These horrible combined tanks are harder to find aftermarket ink replacements. The smaller individual color tanks are cheaper to replace and give more yield, and there's lots of good off-brand ink tanks available. For these reasons, the Canon MG5520 here is the best choice.
I also think claims about print speed and noise are unfounded with the 5520, its plenty fast. It does make some noise but nothing more severe than other inkjets I have owned.
I actually preferred my Canon MG5320... if you can still find one, that's the one you want. Its a little smaller, and just as fast with utterly great print quality & loads of good aftermarket ink available on Amazon. Trouble is the big box stores are selling out of these for newer (not better) models.
The 5520 is noticeably better on the 'draft' setting than my 5320, this may be its best feature so far. Its actually usable for many print jobs whereas the draft setting on the 5320 was totally unusable it was so light.
The 5520 here has done away with the rear tray which was reserved for glossy paper and such. For me that's a good thing, because now I only need to load paper in the front. Some people may see this as adowner. Technically its an eliminated feature.
The display screen is a little smaller font than the 5320, but still very nice and usable. It does not tilt adjust for viewing like the last model.
Just when you thought Canon's software (and Epson, and Brother) couldn't take over your computer any more, behold the MG5520! The software puts a giant, ugly icon that is a six inch by six inch (yes I'm serious) letter \\"L\\" shape on your desktop littered with mini icons and features. I am unable to move it. The good news--you can click it to minimize it to a tiny one inch square icon that sits in the lower right corner above your Sys Tray, and call it up when needed. In this mode its very doable.

Other people have cited an unusually long warm-up time with the 5520. Again, not seeing this at all... no different than my 5320 or the Canon 3300 series. There is a way in the settings to disable the Auto-power-off... thereby allowing the printer to sit in low-power stand-by mode all the time, so when you're ready to print each day there's no pesky warm-up period when you turn it on. I'm only seeing it take less than a minute anyway from power-up to be ready to print but for some people this may be problematic.

Canon seems to charge more than anybody for ink tanks, so I recommend checking out some aftermarket ones here on Amazon and try a few. I haven't had a problem and I've used numerous aftermarket choices for ink on previous Canons. Check the reviews and you'll be fine.
Since Canon charges so much for ink and this printer seems to have less features but the same quality as predecessors, I've got to go with four stars on an otherwise fine product.

The only thing I don't like about it is that I'm measuring approx 2.0mm avg, which is actually better than most (which tend to be 2.05mm), and every other filament I've ever had has similar measurements, so perhaps my measuring technique is off.

Overall, an amazing product and I apologize for my earlier poor review, it was my own ignorance which led to the product being used improperly, and not a defect of the filament. review_headline: The pen... it is the fulcrum of things best not spoken of.
review_body:
I found this pen in a box of old papers and effects of a former colleague of mine. It seems the university cleared out the dear old man's quarters rather unceremoniously, and left them in something of a pile near the wastebin in the Old Commons.

At first, I felt fortunate that a student happened by and found the battered oaken box to be interesting, if not its actual contents. Apparently, the lad is studying something they call "communications", which I can only assume is a discipline involving recent developments linguistics or semiotics. The modern academic world is full of new wonders, and I can only imagine what such investigations into the very nature of the sharing of ideas are bringing into the world for the betterment of all. My mind races at the thought of some new method of representing relationships of meaning that casts off the shackles of the written or spoken word. If such tools had been available to the greater lights of academia of the past centuries -- Rudolph Otto or others in psychodynamics, for instance, or M. N. Clarke and other pioneers of the study of the mind. The intellect that could embrace mastery of a subject so intrinsic to the life of the modern man, and so arcane in its intimacies, as communication itself must be a prodigious one indeed. Ah, well, he is a student at the beloved Miskatonic, so it is not open to question that he is a stand-out, as immodest as it is for me to say.

At any rate, I believed it even more provident that the young prodigy shared his quarters with the son of a former student of my department, who recognized the box as belonging to my colleague. I hope, if I may speak plainly, that this young lad can benefit from association with his room-mate and perhaps surpass his father -- my former student -- in diligence, if not intelligence. His father's exegesis of Blennheiser's "Neue Physik fur den Neuen Xenobiologie", or Kratomastos' "Κίνδυνος από άλλους κόσμους" were quite dull and uninspired, showing the sort of stripe that has led the man into the fields of aviation and "aero-space" and other such fancies. Exposure to his new companion, and isolation from his dilettante father can only do the son a world of good -- though it may take some time, as the description of the box and effects that came to me was couched in terms like "nifty", and the pen itself by some reference to diseased wood. "Gnarly", I believe was the term.

My faith in my good fortune was unshaken when correspondence with Miskatonic, aimed at returning the box and contents to my associate, revealed that he had simply not shown up to class one October morning of two years past. After further investigations, I learned that the disappearance, coupled with several recent complaints of odd noises and strange bursts of light, originating in the Professor's office at unseemly hours, had led to the termination of his tenure, and the ensuing mucking out of his quarters. The administration spoke of students, particularly of the fairer sex, cancelling their tuitions that June, and refusing ever to return to the school. The whole matter smelled of the backroom-politicking familiar to any veteran acedemician at institutions of higher learning, and I had concluded this was the case after some further inquiry.

It seemed that the only witness to the disturbances that the faculty could put me in contact with was housed in the sad and loathsome halls at The Elizabeth Arkham Centre for the Criminally Insane. I could scarcely be blamed for reaching the opinion that Miskatonic's administratiion staff were toying with me. This, especially after I visited the poor lass at Arkham itself. The tale she told -- from her elation at being chosen to be the old man's assistant, to the things she described seeing through a particular mirror in his reliquary -- only served to reinforce my fears that my beloved alma mater, in its ignorance of the nature of the brilliant man's work (and none too insignificant contempt for his genius), had led itself down the primrose path in believing this poor waif's mad ramblings.

It was only then, in despair of reuniting the box and its owner, that I overcame my distaste for intruding into another's private things, and opened the box. Inside, to my horror, I found some surprisingly detailed diagrams -- schematics, almost -- of the very blasphemies of which the poor young assistant had raved. What I saw among them, even though reduced to two dimensions in their representations, spoke of things that could not be. Shapes that dare not exist. Forms that would lead Plato himself to despair of his life's work -- for no "god" worthy of any whiff of divinity could gaze upon such things in their fully realized form and remain sane. They trouble me even now, and I have thrown myself feverishly into pursuits as far from academic research as I could find to occupy my failing psyche. Still, they trouble me -- and even in the simple lines and square angles of the furniture or other trifles I build, I find in them the hints of strange angles and absurd geometries. In seeking to occupy and still my mind, I seem to have left myself open to the intrigue of domains never meant for the eyes of mankind. I tell myself it's simply my inexpert handling of the plane, mitre or jigsaw and that these things -- these abominations I create with my own hands -- are not the artefacts of that horrible place in the dark places of my mind.

Have I mentioned... there is something nagging at me. The fulcrum... the centre-piece... THE PEN! Ah yes. The pen. In searching through the box I did find the damned thing. Such a fine instrument. Tooled in gold. It's nib the model of perfection. To call it "gnarly" is a shameful thing, only fitting of the low and base mind of the son of a space-man. It is so beautiful, I am brought to tears. I weep. To write with such a thing as this is to know joy. To draw or draft with it, the essence of what it is to be a man of ideas and intellect. Had Gianlorenzo Bernini such a brush or chisel? Had DaVinci such a marvel? Degas? Escher, Bosch or Magritte? That this world continues in all its harmony and chaos proves that they had no such device.

And yet I cannot bring myself to touch it. If I remain focused and will my hand to hew to the world laid out by Euclid and Descartes, my thoughts wander and insanity beckons. If I lose my focus, my thoughts sharpen and I find I can work out by sheer intellect the mysteries that dogged Poincare, Foucault and Heidegger. But when I do, my hand becomes the fool, the slave, of this wicked instrument, and creates images that profane and defile the Earth and all its beauties. I cannot, and yet I must.

Quisnam vadum defleo mihi?

I am lost.

review_headline: One Of The Best Purchases I've Ever Made
review_body: This thing is absolutely amazing. I'm using it with a Mac (I just bought it) and it has changed my life. I have it set to automatically scan to a local (non-Cloud) notebook in Evernote. At the end of the day, I drop my receipts into it, hit scan, stick the receipts in the shredder and I'm done for the day (as per Publication 522, the IRS now allows scans, so it's fine to do this--see IRS.gov for details). When my bank statements arrive, I reconcile the personal expenses and delete the scans. Business scans are reconciled and filed. I'm a songwriter and I also carry an Oxford At-Hand Note Card Case wherever I go. Each evening I scan whatever cards I'm carrying into a Evernote notebook. Then I file actual the cards, never to be looked at by me again, in a huge index card box which is guaranteed to provide hours of entertainment for and derisive laughter by my loved ones after I'm dead.  This could not be easier. I love this thing. I suffer from mild dyslexia and TMID (Too Much Input Disorder) and this thing gives me hope. The Windows software includes a copy of Adobe Acrobat. I can't imagine why I'd need it. Possibly the best 400 bucks I've ever spent.  IMPORTANT UPDATE: If you own an iPhone, there's now an app that allows you to wirelessly scan documents from this thing directly into your phone. Not sure if there's an app for Android. It is easily one of the most useful apps on my phone and ups my opinion of this scanner to well over 5 stars.

review_headline: Big disappointment - wrinkled envelopes and poor color
review_body:
This printer was a big disappointment. While it is fast and the print quality is good, I had two big issues. The first is that business envelopes come out seriously wrinkled on one end. Large, squarer envelopes (professional Thanksgiving cards) came out with the printing completely skewed. The second big issue is the color. I use a Pantone blue color for my logo and other presentation materials which is a darker blue - close to navy. This color prints as a bright sky blue on this printer.

After 3 months of working with Xerox (many support calls, onsite support visit), I have learned that this printer has no adjustment for tension, or for color. Because I bought this through Staples, the best Staples will do is exchange it for another printer (that's after much complaining). However, be warned - the tech didn't know of any printers less than $1200 without these issues, and he wasn't even sure of that one.

Final warning - the printer is new and hardly anyone knows anything about it. All in all, a horribly painful and expensive lesson. I will be donating it. I obtained an HP Laserjet Pro 400 for $200 less than this printer, and after a month, has no issues. The blue isn't exact, but i can live with it - it's pretty close. Envelopes come out perfectly.

review_headline: Wouldn't use a modern Canon pixma printer (dye ink) without these
review_body:
I have used Canon inject printers for many years. I think they have the best software and drivers for network printing of the big 4 companies. I've used them all. My favorite for printing pictures is Canon. Now Canon says that their inks in the pixma printers won't fade etc. The problem is that every new generation of printers that Canon comes out with, the ink tanks get smaller and smaller. I had been having the cartridges refilled at Costco, but that was 7 dollars plus tax for this tiny tank. Again, ridiculous. So now I buy a bulk pack of tanks from Blake, and when I start to run low on particular colors, I buy just this 6 pack. The printer still goes through a lot of tanks, but at 2.5 dollars a tank, it's not as painful. I've been using printer with Blake inks for a year and I've had no bad nozzle checks. The color is compatible with the built in canon color profiles, and photo prints are very good. They are even better if you profile your combination of paper and ink with something like a color monkey. I have to recommend these inks highly to canon users.

This combo pack will last quite a while. I find that I am not going through the black inks as quickly, so I purchased the 6 pack of just the cyan, magenta, and yellow when I start running low on them. http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B008LDI8RA/ref=cm_cr_ryp_prd_ttl_sol_0

review_body:

Biggest problem: Wireless setup is difficult, and at least once a day it loses its connection to the network. You find out when you hit print on the computer and its offline. No other printer I have ever seen has such connectivity problems (on an excellent Wireless N signal).

Biggest problem number two: Someone at HP has this bizarre idea that we want lots of popups all over our computer every time we even think of printing and that we like hitting okay all the time.

Biggest problem number three: It guzzles the most expensive ink in the industry and HP has used software that, unlike competitors, makes it hard to use third party ink.

When it prints, it prints fine. But if you don't want to get frustrated once a day, grab a Brother (I like my 3 brother printers far more than my two HPs) or a Canon. The ink is cheaper and the interface is better.

One plus that gave it two stars rather than one - the HP print app on my cell phone DOES work with the printer (better than my computer does).

I can still guess which column is Sunday, Monday, etc. however, this omission leaves the possibility for error that I'd rather not have; I ended up jotting in the days of the week where they should have been.

product_title: 3M Knob Adjust Keyboard Tray, Standard Platform
review_body:
Needed a keyboard tray for my glass desk and this was the only product that I found that was "drill-free".

Installation was easy - the choice of a velcro / mounting tape attached on the deep end of the tray was rather odd, but unlike the other user reviews that I've seen, I'm not sure why that would cause the tray to fall out? The weight of the keyboard is support by the front portion of rail unit, which latches over the front of the desk (They should have included tape for this side to prevent the unit from moving sideways and extra plastic inserts for the screw in portion of the install for ultra thin desks - i improvised...).

As my desk table top is rather thin, I had to insert two soft erasers on the inside end of the rail unit to reduce the wobble. However, a moderate amount of wobble and lateral movement remains, largely because the tray to rail assembly doesn't fit as well as it should and is slightly loose.

Glad this product exists - 3M could make it perfect with just a few simple fixes.

The Good:
- installs on glass desks
- quick and simply
- good spring mechanism for adjusting height and angle

The Bad:
- Tape / velcro portion isn't a great idea. They should have give us a large rubber stopper to attach to the desk which the angled rail can rest on...
- Tray is slightly too narrow for my mouse + macro keyboard
- Slight wobble during use

On other units that I use this change is a menu item, usually reached after scrolling through a number of menus to switch from one USB mode (charging) to another (connecting but not charging). product_title: Pilot Prera Fountain Pen
review_headline: Pilot Fine Nib is equivalent to an extra fine from other manufacturers
review_body:
I have had a Cross ATX Extra Fine fountain pen for many years--I just love the aesthetics of the pen...shape, weight, colors, and texture of the finishes. After nearly 20 years on a computer keyboard, I decided that I'd like to work on my penmanship (which has sorely suffered from lack of use).

Got my groove back after note-taking with the Cross for several days, and decided to look for other fountain pens. I heard that Pilots/Namikis were fantastic, and that the nibs were one level finer than that of other manufacturers. So, to match my Extra Fine on the Cross, I ordered this Pilot Prera in BLACK with a FINE nib.

Wow. This Fine nib on the Prera is probably .5x finer than my Cross Extra Fine! Ink flow is smooth, consistent, and creates an extremely clean and neat look to my lettering. I really really like it!

Yes, the barrel is a bit short, but my hands are small enough that it doesn't matter (such that I don't HAVE to post the cap if I don't want to).

Like many reviewers, I find the clear barrel intriguing and aesthetically pleasing. That Pilot used a translucent white cap liner is a puzzle as it completely detracts from the concept of \\"see through.\\" Yes, this pen is far lighter than my all metal Cross, but for an everyday writer that I want to carry around with me this actually works better.

I was originally interested in the Pilot Vanishing Point pens (the retractable nib and sealed compartment make it both unique and practical), but I wanted to start with this Prera to see what all the fuss was about first. As it is, I am thinking to pick up another of these Preras!

UPDATE 01.31.14:

I ordered another Prera in BLUE with a FINE nib. Both sold from Amazon.

Strangely, my 2nd experience was a bit different from the first....

Black/Fine came with the ink cartridge in a small ziploc baggie. This black pen had no stickers on the barrel nor tabs on the clip.

Blue/Fine came with the ink cartridge rolling around loose underneath the pen--it was NOT in a ziploc bag and it had *exploded* (not a nice way to greet a new pen). The cartridge tab was pushed or pulled inward, much like it would look if you had tried to attach it to the pen. I immediately wondered if the pen was used...but close inspection could not confirm that even though the tines did look to be not quite as tight as on my Black/F pen. Additionally, there was a little F sticker on the barrel and the Pilot tab was on the clip.

The writing experience seems to be the same with both pens (smooth, with an extra fine line), however, so I'm pretty happy except for the lack of ink cartridge due to the fact that it exploded inside the case.
