product_title: Canon Pixma iX6520 Inkjet Printer (4895B002)
review_headline: Once you go Pixma.... Clean simple design
review_body:
I got this printer to replace my 5 year old Canon Pixma IP3500; which after all this time has finally had some breakage of parts I may not be able to find to fix it myself and as you all know the parts may cost more than just buying a new printer. So I decided to stay with a product that has given me great service with very little problem other than what you would typically run into with home printers. Plus I always wanted and needed a larger print format such as 11x17" for the graphic design part of my business. I didn't get one back then because they were a little pricy which is why I had the IP3500 which only printed up to 8.5x11". The IP3500 still had a great print quality that couldn't be matched as far as I'm concerned.

I couldn't be happier with this purchase of the Canon Pixma ix6520. It has the back feed tray; which is a must for me; and the fine 9600dpi photo technology. The IP3500 had fine 4800dpi technology; so this ix6520 is a step up for me. I'm a graphic designer and photographer so I was looking to keep the fine technology that Canon printers offer and also a printer that can support larger print media such as 11x17" prints for the graphic design part of my business; like mailers, posters, menus, etc.

I also liked the idea that this ix6520 is a dedicated printer only! I don't really like the all in ones because if one thin goes bad on the unit and you have to send it out you don't have anything. I'm just old school when it comes to multi-function products. I always felt when it's a dedicated product more time goes into perfecting one thing instead of five. Much like this ix6520 is a great printer because it's a clean simple design with nothing else on it's mind but a great print quality. Don't get me wrong; the all in one printer are great for the average home user and a small office. For this group of people I would recommend a Canon printer as well.

product_title: Simplyitem © Black Toner refill kit + chip for Konica Minolta MagiColor 1600W 1650EN 1680MF 1695mf
review_headline: Well, it works, but you MUST be careful and take your time...
review_body: First, the toner cartridge fill plug is delicate--remove it carefully. If you tear it or deform its shape, the new toner LEAKS from around the plug, as I found out. A couple wraps of teflon plumbing tape around the plug before reinserting it solved the problem of the tiny tear I created trying to remove the plug from the cartridge. The tear in the edge of the plug looked tiny to me, but to the toner it was a GIANT opening. Second, toner is an extremely FINE powder and it is determined to get all over everything. The nozzle cap shown in the photo went in the trash right away once I discovered that squeezing the bottle even a TINY bit released clouds of fine black toner into the air (there is not a good seal between the funnel cap and the toner bottle, regardless of how tightly you screw on the cap). So, I took the toner cartridge to the kitchen, propped it in an empty container in the kitchen sink (anything will do, to support the cartridge and keep it upright, refill opening facing UP, of course). I inserted a kitchen funnel into the opening and carefully emptied half the toner powder into the funnel and used a turkey skewer to carefully work the toner powder down into the funnel hole, and into the cartridge, gently tapping the edge of the funnel with the skewer to cause powder clinging to the funnel walls to fall through the funnel hole into the cartridge. I then did the same with the rest of the toner still in the bottle. Worked fine, and since I wasn't squeezing and/or shaking the bottle, there was no toner powder all over. Pay attention to the chip. You COULD put it in upside down, but careful examination of the chip hole in relation to the printer cartridge screw hole reveals the proper way. Minolta could easily have offset the chip mounting hole to make the correct way more evident, but then more of us would be doing what WE'RE doing, meaning that fewer of us would be buying overpriced OEM cartridges with new chips factory-installed. So, my newly-refilled toner cartridge seems to be working fine, and a couple test pages did not smear, though I intentionally tried. Saved lots of money, for about half hour of work. Next refill will take less time, as I will use the tricks and precautions I learned with this first refill.

product_title: 1 X Bluecell 10 pcs Silver Color 5.5 Inch Aircraft Key Ring Holder Wire
review_headline: Perfect for key rings and securing straps to bags
review_body:
I grew up around an aircraft mechanic's hanger and recognized the cable type immediately. It's used as linkage on the controls of small airplanes and is strong, light and rustproof. Not mission critical for keychains but a nice lightweight alternative to heavy key rings. If you only have a couple house keys, keyring weight is no biggie. I drag around nearly two dozen keys so being able to organize keys on lighter and fewer key ring holders means a significant reduction in weight and bulk. I ditched my heavy key rings and never looked back. As long as you tighten well, they won't unscrew and are secure. If you're paranoid and don't plan to remove keys, a dab of Locitite Red will ensure it will never unscrew.

Since there are 10 of these in the package, I had several left over and found they make great safety wires for camera bags and instrument case straps. I've had a strap hook accidentally open on a bag full of photo gear and the works fell on the floor. Thread one of these through the D-ring and strap end and you have a perfect safety wire, insuring your goodies won't hit the deck when the claw hook gets bumped.

The product I received appeared flawless and worked perfectly for its intended purpose. After 6 months of use I've had no problems with rust or failure. Great little gismo, ideal for both keychains and as a safety cable for straps, bags and other gear.

review_headline: Very happy with Ooma - so far.
review_body:
OK, I just got it today and within 10 minutes had it working. Very easy setup, just follow quick start instructions. The Telo should be powered up BEFORE connecting it to the modem/router. Like others have said, the lights will flash, etc. After the lights are all blue, I hooked it up, then went to the Ooma website to set up my account, configure the Ooma settings and look at other options.

I have AT&T Uverse and a landline with AT&T, so I plugged the Ooma into the modem/router, then plugged the wireless phone base into the Ooma.

While configuring the Ooma, I wanted to port my number and one of the questions I needed to answer is what type of internet connection I have. I knew it was DSL, so I did contact AT&T to ask if I would have to have a \\"dry loop,\\" but they said no because, even though my internet and landline share a wire, the internet has it's own dedicated pair. There is a one-time porting fee of $40, but it is waived if you sign up and pay in advance for a year of the Premier service. I will update this review once my number is ported over and I find out if it is set up correctly.

Ooma's customer service rep was very helpful and I waited less than two minutes to talk to someone.

I did try out the Ooma. I called my husband's cell phone and the call was very clear, as good as the landline. Then I hooked the POTS back up to use until the number is ported over. We've had the same number for 20 years, so we didn't want to change it.

Incidentally, I had called AT&T on Dec. 31 to make some changes to my service for the purpose of reducing my bill. During that call the customer service rep asked why I had not changed from a landline to a VOIP system. I didn't know that AT&T had a VOIP system, so she explained it to me (two plans, (1) $25 and 200 minutes/month or (2) $35 and unlimited). I told the CSR I would discuss it with my husband and she was supposed to call me back later that day. We were going to switch over to AT&T's VOIP system, but she never called back. I had already looked at Ooma and had been trying to convince my husband to try it. After the AT&T CSR didn't return the call, my husband was ready to spring for Ooma. Then today when I contacted AT&T in regards to setting up my Ooma, the CSR asked what VOIP system I would using and how much it would cost, so I told her and said, \\"You can see how much money I can save with Ooma.\\" Then she tried to sell me on the services included in AT&T's VOIP plan, so I told her that I could get a basic package from Oma where I would have to pay less than $4/month that had more services than AT&T's basic pkg, but I was upgrading to the Premier pkg for a total of about $14/month, and that I was looking forward to stopping sales calls with Ooma's blacklists, something that AT&T isn't concerned about. I hope I put a bug in her ear about AT7T's prices, that they are just too dang high!

I will update again after I've used it for awhile.

I've added numbers to my personal blacklist and have had a reduction in robocalls, unwanted sales calls, etc. My number has been on the national Do Not Call list for years (and updated), still I have gradually received more and more unwanted calls and AT&T really had no options to stop them. I have also lodged complaints about some of the calls at the Do Not Call site numerous times over the past few years, (especially Card Services, which changes names and numbers frequently. I think it's about as much use as writing the numbers down and throwing them away. Ooma has changed that for me. As the calls come in, I check my history and update my blacklist. Using the Ooma interface at the Ooma website is easy and I like seeing a history of all calls. I received my final bill for the AT&T landline, so now I have no phone bill to pay for the next year (I prepaid a year's service). Thank you, Ooma!

review_body: I read the reviews first and definitely made use of the advice that others gave. However, since I didn't have any on hand, I used very thin nails and just nailed each corner into the wall. With the added thickness of the foam board they are both easier to secure and have enough depth to more than account for the depth of a push pin. review_headline: Really good quality and fast too
review_body:
This is my second one, having bought one for the bargain price of £200 at staples, thrashed it 2004-2007 until I damaged the belt and it was uneconomic to replace. That gave superb photo results on laser glossy paper, colour laser paper and 160gm card. I then switched to a canon 5000 in 2007 but that went badly out of register in November 2013 so I bought another 1600w on ebay almost new for £49!

Pros:
Compact cube about a foot square
Paper tray is open and sticks out: the canon 5000 was always a filddle pulling it out and then slamming it back in for loading or changing paper or double-sided printing. I really like the open tray as you can change stock very easily and double-sided is a doddle. You're also always aware of how much paper you have left - no suprises!(if your're deft you can reload while printing...
Blindling fast 20ppm in B/W - unlike the Canon 5000 which is slow on all settings
High quality photos on good 100gsm colour laser paper
Easy to refill toner carts - refill and chip two or three times easily
You can get a Remote Panel program where you can tinker with the settings and get the last drop out of the carts.

Cons
A bit noisy as it has to make three passes for each page in colour - printing loads at night in the lounge or on the desk next to you is not ideal - cover it with cushions!
The usual miserly starter carts, but mine went on quite a long time even though it was still on the starter carts and second hand.

Overall recommended. Must get another cheap one for spares!

product_title: Canon PIXMA Printing Solutions MG7120 Wireless Inkjet Photo All-In-One Printer, Cloud Enabled
review_headline: This is a big intiminatng machine!!!
review_body:
This is Canon's latest all-in-one printer/copier/scanner for home and small business use with all the bells and whistles. It has the six ink cartridges, two paper trays for different sizes (but with an unfortunate limitation), and best of all it accepts wireless input from just about anywhere including the cloud. Thus, if you are looking to upgrade your old bottom-of-the-line HP all-in-one as I was, this may be the one for you. However, it is probably overkill for many people and you may get a surprise, as I did, to see how big the thing really is when it arrives. The pictures on line all make it look so small and sleek next to models from other manufacturers but in fact it has quite a large footprint and it weighs in at about 15 lbs. It is quite low, however, and so will fit comfortably on a shelf needing relatively little headroom.

Set up is easy, in principle, but like all these devices, can be fraught with difficulty when something goes slightly wrong. It is important to follow the directions closely and make sure you have the correct router password for it to connect to. Once set up, however, it is quite straightforward to use it from any computer or iPad with internet connection, and that is the really nice thing about it. On the down side, of course, there are so many options for printing on different types of paper with three different qualities, etc., that some time must be spent setting up default options to make sure you get what you want every time without wasting too much of the expensive ink.

The bottom line is that this printer has everything the average home user is likely to want. I must say, however, that I was a little disappointed in the quality of the first photograph prints on plain paper that I made compared to what was possible with my old HP. They are, of course, better with photographic paper but still not as sharp as some I have seen from more expensive professional printers. But then, perhaps it's the photos I am trying to print taken with my point-and-shoot Canon cameras that do not quite have the focus and resolution needed to produce the best results with this relatively low-cost printer.

product_title: Fellowes Powershred 99Ci 100% Jam Proof Cross-Cut Paper Shredder
review_body:
I've gone a lot of years with the 60 and 70 dollar \\"office shredders\\". That means I've endured a lot of years of headaches. When my latest office store brand shredder burned up and stopped working, I decided to invest in something nicer. I did quite a bit of research before deciding on the Fellowes brand. The 99Ci fell in line with my needs for a lot of reasons. It is the perfect size for my office and it sits nicely at the end of my desk (where my former shredder was sitting). It also fit my budget.

I am still blown away by just how good this thing is! I was skeptical about the \\"jam-proof\\" claims and, yes, I did have to give it a try. I very seriously have not been able to jam it with any batch of paper. The opening where the paper is fed controls the volume. You can't push more in than it can handle. On a couple of occasions, the machine would stop \\"mid-shred\\" and I would think, \\"ah-HA!\\". But it wasn't jammed...just assessing the situation. In those couple of cases, it would stop, reverse slightly, then take the rest through without a complaint. My old shredder required manual operation for reversing in situations like that and usually I would wind up yanking big chunks of partially shredded junk mail out of the feeder.

I use my shredder primarily for junk mail and some office docs that are printed, used briefly, then can be trashed. I love the fact that his machine can take an entire glossy envelope from a credit card company and completely shred the entire envelope and contents without me opening it. With past shredders I was reduced to opening the unwanted offer and feeding individual sheets in order to avoid the dreaded jam.

So far I've been through three full bins of shredded paper. I love the easy opening front load bin. I am using standard 13 gallon white trash bags in the bin and they are great. Note about the window at the front of the bin: you can only see the level of shredded material if you are using clear bags or no bags at all. I'm using white, so I don't have the visual as it is filling. That is really not a big deal for me. I normally will pull the bin out and do a little hand compressing when I get the fill indicator light.

I am very happy with the quality and the performance of this unit. I would recommend it highly for any home office or small office.ags at all. review_body:
I had to write a review after reading some of the other reviews here. I have had all around good experience with this printer. I bought it nearly 6 years ago and it works great until this day.

My experience thus far:

Pros
Fairly quick scanning, printing, copying, and faxing
High resolution printing (compared to some newer printers I have used)
Wifi works great!
Maintenance is very minimal (not a replacement part in 6 years)
Easy to use
Easy to understand interface
Software (Productivity Studio) is very flexible - allows multiple scans to be compiled into single file for faxing or converting to PDF
Software also supports OCR and PDF conversions
Auto detection of paper size and thickness changes - compensates automatically

Cons
As many others have pointed out, this thing eats ink. Look to spend around $25 for black and $33 for color cartridges.
Spooling hung on me when I upgraded to Windows 7 64-bit. Quick call to Customer Support walked me through the fix.
If you are already on Windows 7, you may have to request an original drivers disk to get fax and OCR support.
Online download from Lexmark.Com for drivers does not have Fax or OCR drivers. (I lost my disk and had to install on new PC)

Overall, I cannot complain about this printer too much other than the ink it consumes. Ink pricing is very consistent with many other newer printers. You simply have to purchase more ink more frequently. I paid $250 or so when it first came out and wifi on printers was up and coming. It has met my needs and anytime I've ever had to call support, they have always been very friendly and helpful.

review_body:
Made a leather sleeve with a slot for a Zebra mini pencil to hold this notebook. I keep in my other back pocket, it balances my wallet out, and I wanted to have a place to jot down any idea that struck me, anywhere.

It is what I expected from RITR, having used their products before.

Top 5 reasons why this should be your "EDC" notebook:
RITR's smallest bound notebook. Still very useable.
Handy ruler on back cover, both inch and metric.
Handy standard/metric conversion factors on front cover:length, weight, temp, volume, speed, and fuel efficiency.
"Universal" format is a cross between grid paper and ruled paper, good for writing and sketching.
Paper is all-weather, with the right writing instrument (pencil, or "space pen") will write in very cold & wet, and will stay on the paper.

On the other hand:
The paper has a slight texture to it. At first it really bothered me, but I got used to it. Feels like a powdered latex glove.
Erasing pencil marks is only partly effective, words will still be legible.
Heavy erasure appears to diminish the water resistance in the area erased, water soaks in, but paper doesn't break down.
Writing while the paper is wet doesn't always work 100%. Pencil works better than space pen while wet.

Overall:
The cons are nitpicks; after all, normal paper wouldn't stand a chance under wet conditions.
The tradeoff for waterproof-ness is incomplete erasure. Fine trade in a pocket notebook I think.
In my humble opinion, pencil is the way to go with RITR. Even though you can't count on erasing, the main benefit of pencil here is being able to write while the paper is wet. In my experience, writing through beads of water with a space pen doesn't make a strong mark, and some of the ink is then suspended in the bead of water, which then spears.

Found out recently that a company called "Form.Function.Form" makesa product very similar to the sleeve that I mentioned earlier, called the "architect's wallet". Of course I'm partial to mine, theirs uses a Moleskine notebook. But maybe if you are looking at this, it might interest you.

review_headline: Dont spend the money on the kit

Just order the balloons. The kit contains heavy duty balloons a base and a piece of styrofoam to work as an insulating base and clips to close the top of the balloon when you fill it with water. It also includes tea lights.

If you want to use them, you need several days preparation. The instructions say freezing the balloons outside works best if the temps are 20 F or below. If you want to use your freezer, you will probably be able to create one at a time. They are heavy as heck also.

We've had fun freezing them one at a time - our winter in the mid atlantic states hasn't been cold enough to do it outside. I froze the first for 8 or 9 hours and it was a thin shelled sphere that has survived the day in the low 40s. We filled the next balloon with quite a bit more water and froze it for about 18 hours and it is thicker shelled but not as solid as the pics.

We are having fun with this and recommend getting the balloons only - not the kit. You can probably fashion a base, whose only purpose is to maintain the shape and prevent the bottom from freezing solid, from items you have at home.

product_title: AmazonBasics 8-Sheet High-Security Micro-Cut Paper
review_body: This was a 2013 Christmas present from Santa.  Apparently he thought I needed to organize my office.  I was actually very excited to have this and set to shredding some old documents.  After two old credit cards, 20 pieces of paper and five old duplicate check books..(yeah, I'm that guy... I still use checks) it started smoking.  I understand this is only an 8 sheet shredder and was doing no more than three pieces of paper at a time.  The duplicate checks were run through in batches of five or so.  All things considered I did not put this shredder to a \\"heavy\\" load, in fact, I would consider it well under what it should be able to handle.  My next step is to print a return label and get a \\"real\\" shredder.  My advice....stay away from this one and buy something a little more durable.    Update: 12/23/14  - After the smoke cleared -     I was able to shred documents two at a time. A \\"real\\" shredder should be capable of more.  Regardless, given the amount of shredding I do (less than 40 sheets per month) I decided to keep this unit and limp along rather than go through the hassle of a return. Seemed to work out over the course of the year. The 30 days return policy expired.  And on 12/18/14, the one year warranty did as well. Perhaps the stars were just not in my favor when I ordered this or the person manufacturing it had a bad day, I don't know but the machine is now completely dead.  It started going through its death spasms prior to the warranty expiration.  Maybe it was telling me to \\"get out!\\"  It started with the \\"auto\\" function not working - ergo sitting idle until it was fed paper.  I had to physically turn it from auto to \\"off.\\"  Shortly thereafter it just refused to come on unless I held my mouth just right and stared at it.  And now....It's dead.  The warranty is up and I am SOL.      Folks....do not buy this shredder.  It is a waste of money and will only cause you heartache and frustration.  And the the wife/spouse/partner will be upset because the documents are piling up and....anyway don't be that guy/gal.

product_title: Canon Office and Business MX922 All in One Printer, Wireless and mobile printing
review_body:
Photos print with little dots across the images. They appear in the direction of movement of paper through the machine and there are about 20 columns of these dots. They appear across non printed areas. This rules out an issue with the print cartridges. I believe the feed mechanism inside the machine is damaging the paper on the way through. I went through all the troubleshooting tips including one for prevention of paper abrasion, which increases the clearance of the print heads. As I said, the dots cross non printed areas, so I don't believe the issue has anything to do with the print heads, but I tried it anyway. I filed for a replacement unit, and I will post my results with the second one when I receive it.

Update for second printer:
The second printer I received was actually worse than the first one. It has the exact same defect with printing little dots on the photos, which indicates a production problem of these printers. This second printer actually stops during printing. When I print a full page photo, it stops five times. I guess it needed to think about how bad the photo was going to look when completed. I saw all the negative reviews (and quite a few positive ones), but when the price changed from $120 to $69.99 it convinced me. Now, I am convinced $69.99 was too much.

Amazon has been awesome about the return of both of these printers. They do want me to pay the shipping to return the extra ink cartridges I bought for this printer, but never opened.

review_headline: Delightful design, almost perfect when it works, but it's fragile
review_body: I eagerly awaited this pen, and I received it as a gift shortly after it became available.  First the positive.  It's beautiful, the design is clever and works well (when it works, see below), it writes well and in general is a pleasure to use.  it is large, but I have large hands so that's not an issue for me.  Since the body of the pen is a cylinder with no tapering it's not highly ergonomic, and it did take some time to get used to it. I don't care much about such things, but the wooden case that the pen comes in is quite tasteful and nice.    Unfortunately, I've had to send the pen in 3 times for repair.  The first because the palladium finish started to peel off, the 2nd and 3rd times because the twist to open mechanism failed.  I think they replaced the entire pen the first time because the mechanism felt different after I received it.    I treat all my possessions, including my writing instruments with care - no dropping, no forcing, and I routinely clean the nib.  I waited a long time for this pen to be released and I'm disappointed in the quality of the instrument.  When it works properly it is a pleasure to use, but it's frustrating to need to keep sending it in for repair.  In the great scheme of things a $300 fountain pen isn't all that expensive.  Still and all, for that kind of money it should work properly.    I will say that the folks at Lamy have been easy to deal with - I think this is a QC or engineering issue.    Update - 12/26/2014.  Since I got the pen back the 3rd time 11 months ago, it's worked properly.  I don't do anything out of the ordinary, just clean the nib in vinegar every month or so.  increasing rating to 4 stars.  Will update again if issues arise.

product_title: Epson C11CD28201 Expression Photo XP-950 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner and Copier
review_headline: Limited amount of reasons to buy this printer
review_body:
Oh Epson, why oh why is there such a need to develop a new printer every year? Like many of you, I've been a longtime Epson fan, starting with their first generation color printers, all the way up to the most recent Artisan line. Sadly, with each new printer, Epson managed to screw things up little by little. In the case of the Artisan, they managed to milk the line for several years - starting with the 800, to the 810, 835 and finally the 837. By that time, they realized it was time for something new, so they released the Expression line.

The XP-950 is supposed to be the top of the line, but it lacks the ADF (document feeder) and fax found on the cheaper XP-850. The only major difference is that this one does 11x17 borderless (more on that in a moment) and that it has an "innovative fold down" lid.

Setup is like any other Epson - a lot of plastic and foam to unbox, but nothing out of the ordinary. The printer comes with starter ink, and its initial setup and prime will leave you with about 85% of the ink left. It features a dedicated photo paper tray, and thankfully Epson did not fiddle with the excellent CD/DVD printing tray.

Software setup was not too bad under Windows 8, I did try the wireless as well, which worked fine. Printing from my mobile device was equally easy to setup, but essentially useless as I rarely need to print off my phone.

Print quality is the real issue here - prints are NOT as crisp and streak-free as on my old Artisan 800. For a printer that is supposed to use the newest generation inks, I'm quite disappointed in the end-result. I used an assortment of papers, including original Epson photo paper, Canon paper and Costco branded papers. At the absolute highest quality with best premium paper, I'd call the results nothing higher than "acceptable". Black and white prints on "normal" paper are very fast, but not suitable for business use.

All in all, I think this is acase of the Quicken effect - release a new product every year, regardless of what kind of new features you can come up with. At the very least, they could have improved the touch screen, but everything on that end is the same. Just more plastic, and of course - newer ink cartridges. Disappointing.

product_title: Hewlett Packard HP Color LaserJet CP1210 CP1215 CP1217 CP1510 CP1515N CP1518NI CM1312 CM1312NFI CM1312NFI MFP Four Color Toner Refill Kit with Reset Chips and FREE Hole-Making Tool. Refills CB540A, CB541A, CB542A and CB543A. Manufactured by Toner Eagle. FREE 2 Day US Shipping.
review_headline: Excellent product and successful re-fill for HP Color Laserjet CP1518NI - Hints and Tips I discovered
review_body:
Hi,

This is a great product, I have a HP Color Laserjet CP1518NI but expect the kit will work just as simply on your cartridges as it did on mine. Here are a few of my experiences and opinions that may help you when your product arrives.

I would suggest when burning the hole for refilling the cartridge that one stay a little (1/8\\") one eighth of an inch below the top and keep the heated cutter head angled downward a bit so you don't cut through the top of the cartridge and continue on and cut a hole in the top of the housing, I did this but had no problem sealing it with the generous amount of tape they provide to close the refill hole.

Be careful when sealing the hole that you do not tear a hole in the relatively thin foil adhesive backed tape. When finished sealing the housing give it a good cleaning and look for any small leaks around your tape line ( I had two upon final inspection) but they were easily sealed by adding another layer of foil tape around the entire perimeter of the original hole. The toner chamber is not pressurized or under a vacuum but is susceptible to leakage due to small vibrations and general printer movement. Its not super-critical that the hole be absolutely air-tight but one should take care that to gently shake the cartridge and furthermore gently blow on and around the sealed hole to detect any leaks before reinstalling it in your printer. Careful as I was with the tape-job I found two small pinhole leaks in my tape job and simply adding a little more tape to the leaking area fixed the problem.

When replacing the new PROM chips in the housing I simply squeezed the plastic retaining legs in with a pair of small needle nosed pliers and removed the original chip with a pair of tweezers.

Instead of using the included double sided tape which turned out not to be thick enough to reach the bottom of the IC and the top of the housing I simply placed a very small drop of superglue on each edge of the new IC and chassis ends made sure it was dry before reinstalling the cartridge. Note that the IC's dont seat all the way to the rear of its mounting area, take a look at a cartridge that still has the IC's installed and you can clearly see how far back into the little port the chip goes before it is fully seated. As far as polarity there is only one way to install the chip, the small bulbous (Epoxy potted chip) goes on the bottom, you cant miss!

Upon initialization of the newly filled cartridges I had a report of a \\"Shipping retainer needs to be removed from CYAN cartridge but a simple removal and re-installation of the cartridge cleared this error).

In the HP printer utility I received a report of 2200 black and 1400 color pages remaining. I ran a routine cleaning from within the HP app and began using the printer , No errors, beautiful smudge free, brilliant, bright, vivid colors on common 20 weight office bond paper, as expected from a color laser jet!!!

I am super impressed with the value, quality and ease of use and installation of this product. I give it 5 Stars , In my opinion the kit is easily worth many times the thirty some odd dollar cost. It took me around 1.5 hours from start to finish for all four cartridges.

This is an install, test, use and report analysis, so long term usage and reliability remain untested, but I certainly do not expect any problems down the road and feel comfortable reporting on the product in the first few hours of usage and am nearly certain that it will continue to provide trouble free printing from the refills.

On another topic, the toner is water soluble and was not nearly as \\"Messy\\" as some would lead you to believe. I did it in my kitchen and cleanup was not a problem anywhere a little of the used or new toner spilled, just take your time, cut a large hole in the screw on tip so the toner flows freely from bottle with a simple tap on the edge of the bottleto refill the cartridge.

On each cartridge before reinstalling in printer I inspected the green fuser assembly underneath for any spilled toner and gently cleaned it off by first gently blowing it and then very gently wiping it off with a very very very damp cloth followed by a dry lint free cloth, the cleaning wipes the provide in the kit are excellent for this!

As a matter of safety and good electronics bench work principles, I would place the cartridges on the cleaning wipes when working with them. On the bottom of the cartridge the fuser remains unprotected and is vulnerable to scratching or damage when working on the assembly. Simply holding it cradled in your hand with wipes covering the bottom of the cartridge will prevent any scratches or inadvertent damage to the very fragile assembly when you are doing your refill.

Enjoy!

Jerry H.

product_title: LAMY Safari Fountain Pen Charcoal Ex-Fine (L17EF)
review_headline: my first fountain pen and I'm a little underwhelmed
review_body:
My expectations may have been too high. But I was expecting this to glide over paper very smoothly. Instead, it scratches the paper. Also, the ink flow is uneven, sometimes not coming out at all on certain strokes. This may be to poor handling on my part, but really, a pen this expensive shouldn't require too much user knowledge. It should just work. I should note that I'm using Noodler's Black Waterproof Ink, as suggested by other members here. I get the feeling the ink is not the problem.

It's definitely comfortable in my hand. However, I prefer to not attach the cap to the top when I'm writing, as that seems to shorten the area my hand can come into contact with the pen for true comfort.

I have not noticed any leaks and this pen has traveled in my briefcase for more than a month (as of this writing). I store it tip up, as that is just the easiest way to store in my briefcase.

The refill converter works well in this pen.

EDIT: After reading and watching videos on this and other fountain pens, I decided to take the Safari apart and clean it with tap water. It seems to have made a big difference as the ink runs smoother. The scratchiness is still there, but I don't find it annoying. Perhaps I merely got used to it. Also, I tried writing with the cap posted to the back of the pen and after a small adjustment period, I enjoy this much better. I just have to make sure I line up the clip on the cap with the \\"LAMY\\" logo on the pen.

I've increased the star-rating of this pen, with this update.

As an aside; if you're really interested in fountain pens, look for a few website forums on the topic. There is a lot to know about these things and having that knowledge makes owning one a much more enjoyable experience for me.

product_title: Canon CL211XL Ink Cartridge
review_headline: Canon Ink Cartridges are the Best
review_body: I love Canon and Canon products, so I stick mainly with them, especially with printers, cameras, and camcorders.  These are at a lower price, slightly, than the local office supply store, and I get them delivered to the door for free with Amazon Prime.  What could be better?  I use only Canon ink cartridges because many years ago when I was just beginning with my use of computers, I thought that compatible inks would be a great way to save money.  Long story short; I ended up having to replace my printhead which the "compatible" inks ruined.  That was $75.00, and awful lot for a $125 printer, but worth it because it's Canon.  Don't get compatibles. product_title: Brother Printer MFCJ825DW Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner, Copier and Fax
review_headline: Great all pupose printer that works well with all operating systems.
review_body:
I chose the Brother MFCJ825DW because I needed a printer that will work well with various computers with various operating systems over a network. Anybody who uses Linux knows that their printer choices are limited to about two manufactures. I chose the Brother over the other brand due to the lower ink costs.
The printer has a somewhat smaller footprint than the other all in one printers I have owned. The scanner feature seems to work well, whether you are using the sheet fed scanner to scan documents or the flatbed scanner to scan photos. The only downside to the sheet fed scanner is that it is not duplex. The printer also prints well, either documents or photos. The printer can print documents in duplex. Some reviewers have complained about the quality of photo prints. I think the problem may be that the printer has many quality settings, such as draft or high quality, and if the print quality setting is set incorrectly, you may get poor results. Also, some reviewers have complained about the printer losing the wifi connection after being idle for a period of time. When I installed the printer, I upgraded the firmware while I was installing the drivers. Perhaps that is why I have had no issues with the printer dropping the wifi signal despite the fact I have had it on for several weeks.
Driver installation under Windows is pretty straight forward and painless. The printer comes with a driver installation disk. However, if you have an Internet connection, I would recommend going to Brother's website and downloading the driver. That way you will have the most up to date driver. It is also a good idea to upgrade the firmware at the same time to avoid the wifi issue noted above.
Driver installation under Linux is a bit more work than under Windows. Fortunately, Brother provides detailed instructions on their website for both Debian and Red hat based distributions. Just follow the instructions on Brother's website and you printer will work just aswell under Linux as it does Windows.

I bought the ScanSnap with the bundled software (ie, the Magic Desktop & Rack2Filer & Adobe Acrobat X). The bundled package was only $40 more than the solo hardware option and I think is well worth the money.

The speed and overall operation of the ScanSnap is once again, SIMPLY AWESOME!!!

review_body:

You can also plug it in directly to your computer and it should install by itself. You don't need the cannon software. I think printer all softwares are useless. I also use it to scan to USB flash drive if i want to scan multiple files using the document feeder. You can save all the images to one PDF file if you scan to USB. review_headline: Best bang for buck in class - 16 bits per color capable
review_body:
Outstanding print quality, well built, quiet operation, competitively priced and good USA based Canon product support. Canon drivers have ability to handle 16 bits per color files output from Adobe Photoshop and other image processing software. This gives smooth color gradients when using a wide color space like Adobe RGB on large prints. The XPS driver is needed for this capability to be activated and it is available on disk and from their website

Only negative so far is after installation from disk, I tried to updated all the drivers and PC software by downloading them from canon USA website. That messed up the network and printer profiles I had working, so the printer would not communication with my pc over the wired gigabit network any more. I had to call Cannon support which was good in walking me thru the process to get the network connectivity back again. Support is all USA based with good English speaking and knowledgeable staff available 10 am - 10 pm.

I got the network connectivity active but had multiple printer icons in my devices and printers folder and I ended up using the Restore function in Windows 7 64bit OS to wipe the install clean and start from scratch. Knocking one star for poor software update installation instructions and expensive inks. Ink cost is lowest in class compared to other printers when using the for $ / unit of print area metric, other printers inks are lower cost based on $ / volume of ink in cartridge, but they use up more ink in the cleaning and startup process, so that does not count for me.

review_body: I needed a small document shredder, mostly for junk mail and receipts.  This one had the best price and good reviews so I gave it a try.  About a year later, it's still going strong! It doesn't accept too much paper at a time--four sheets is the max--which is fine for light home shredding.  The only bummer is that the slot on the top is less than 8.5" wide, so you either have to tear or fold the paper you're going to shred so that it will fit through the slot. If you save a lot of documents to shred at once, this can reduce you to one or two pages at a time, but it's not terribly inconvenient. It says it can accept one credit card at a time. product_title: Panasonic DECT 6.0 Link-to-Cell via Bluetooth Cordless Phone with Answering System
review_headline: Great phone system.  Feature rich, good sound quality, battery life, expandable, cell-tethering.
review_body:
Have had this set for about 5 or 6 months now. Replace a V-Tech setup I had. I've also had Unidens.
I really like this set.
Range is great. I don't really know the details of DECT vs the legacy technology but I have a 1/2 acre and can talk anywhere on my lot - perhaps 150 feet from the house. I have the base station upstairs to increase the range.

Headsets are nice with most used features on dedicated buttons or simple directional arrow shortcut buttons and/or on-screen menu.
Sound quality is great both using handset and speaker-phone mode. Speaker phone on base or handsets is equally good.
I use the Bluetooth "tethering" and have my iPhone registered with it so I can place/receive calls on either. It doesn't really seem to have a true 2-line capability but you can conference the cell with the landline, etc. Those features I don't use a lot and they'd take a little playing with to get it down. The cell line can be configured to ring with a distinctive tone and via the bluetooth will actually play the same ring as what is configured on your cell (not sure if that works with all makes/models I can only speak for the iPhone).

Battery life on the handsets is excellent. I've never run out of juice and I have days where I spend 5-6 hours on the phone when working from home with minimal time between calls (no recharging). That was one of the reasons I replace my other system - batteries were going.

I like having the full function base station as my primary desk phone too - I prefer using the base speakerphone when I'm at the desk, but nice to be able to roam uninterrupted and use speaker anywhere.

Displays are clear and subdued color (amber backlighting).

Most common programming/configuration functions are available via menus and navigation buttons, but there are a number of other programmable features accessible via feature codes. I like that there is that degree of flexibility,but if I have a small complaint about this system it would be that: that some of these (like ringer volume) you have to go get the manual to remember some 3 digit code to set.

product_title: Epson EX7220, WXGA Widescreen HD, Wireless, 3000 Lumens Color Brightness, 3000 Lumens White Brightness, 3LCD Projector
review_headline: Very nice unit.  Great picture.  Some drawbacks.
review_body:
The Epson EX7220 is a nice combination of performance, ease of use and portability. The 16:10 aspect ratio is a good choice for both meeting presentations and video viewing. The brightness and clarity are both first rate.

The best qualities:
1. The android app works really well (on my Galaxy S3) allowing a slideshow type presentation of select file types such as JPG and PDF. Both devices need to be connected to the same network for this to work.
2. It is very light and portable.
3. The lens cover and adjustment feet are simple and effective. I know that should be a standard expectation but I use a Viewsonic projector that makes those simple features difficult to operate.
4. The 720p resolution and brightness are a vast improvement over other business projectors I have used.
5. The remote works well and is easy to use. It even works when pointing away from the projector at the screen – a common habit for presenters.
6. Wireless connection was quick and simple.
7. If you have used any other projectors, using this one is very simple.

The things that could be better:
1. While connected to the wireless network, the voice and picture were out of sync while streaming a movie from my PC which was streaming the movie from my NAS. Playing on the computer without the projector worked fine. I was unable to resolve this issue other than by directly connecting the projector to the PC.
2. The Android app does not project file types I frequently use such as Microsoft Office files – including Power Point files.
3. The fan seems a bit louder than other projectors I have used. Perhaps this is because the fan is forward facing and I am usually standing in front of the projector.
4. A laser pointer on the remote would be really cool.
5. The wireless connection is via a detachable (included) dongle vs. internal.
6. Wireless connection requires the installation of software to discover the projector.

While I’m not ready to drop my big screen TV for a projector, the picture quality and brightness of the Epson EX7220 is impressive and will make business presentations and inservice trainings, especially those with video, really stand out.ojector.

review_headline: Excellent grinding sharpener for home or classroom
review_body:
This fast and efficient grinder-style sharpener performs as advertised. It has an easily removable shaving reservoir with an auto-shut-off switch, which might make this a good fit for a classroom as well as a home office.

The feature that stands out with this product the most is how it is able to detect when sharpening has completed. Upon inserting a dull or new pencil, the sharpener will begin grinding the pencil to sharpness. When sharpening is done, you can feel that it stops grinding. It seems to work every time. However, if you insert the sharpened pencil again, you will end up grinding it down further. This is one of the biggest issues with sharpeners like this -- the way they will grind a pencil down to nothing in seconds. I think this product solves that problem well.

Removing the shaving reservoir is very easy. There's a sort of bubble catch in the front that allows you to easily grip it for removal. It then slides right back on and clicks into place.

The product is about the same size as any of these sharpeners -- about 2 man-sized fists.

review_headline: Easy operation with clear instructions now
review_body:
Refilling the toner cartridge is an easy operation, but care must be exercised. The instructions now are quite clear and easy to follow. I would add, though, that when replacing the chip which counts the number of pages printed, you do not need to break the two plastic welds holding the cover, as explained in the instructions. Instead you may carefully pry off the other side of the chip cover where there are two locking tabs by prying the cover over the tabs. Carefully remove the old chip with tweezers and replace it with the new one. The new chip is oriented so that the notch in the chip is away from the body of the cartridge with the four contacts up.

My printer is working beautifully.

product_title: Brother MFC-5890CN Professional-Series Color Inkjet All-in-One with Networking and Large-Size Printing
review_body:

I have spent over £300 on ink cartridges - if the unit is moved or knocked, the ink sensor thinks that the cartridge is empty and WON'T do anything unless you put a newly filled cartridge in, sometimes it won't even detect the cartridge so you have to pop the cartridge in several times before it will register.
Now, for the print heads....
WHAT A PILE OF ABSOLUTE RUBBISH, words cannot describe how bad this printer is, I am left with £250 missing from my wallet, and another £300 from the genuine inks, the print heads are completely misaligned for no reason and by performing the tests, it won't align them any further so the printer is basically useless!!! I called Brother and they said they can fix the problem but for a cost of £299 + Delivery fees, THE PRINTER COSTS LESS THAN THAT RETAIL!!!!

In a nutshell:

DO NOT BOTHER WITH BROTHER PRINTERS, BUY ONCE, PAY TWICE.

review_headline: Just what I was looking for
review_body:

In this area the Nortel was as good as Polycom, and I would have considered Polycom but they don't manufacture phones with features that I feel are needed for a home office.

After a week of use I can say the Aastra has exceeded my expectations. The speakerphone quality is excellent. The only negative I have so far is that the 3 keys that are used for scrolling and volume seem flimsy compared to the other keys. On the positive side I like that the phone takes up less desk space than the Nortel. And I like that I can create customized labels for the 6 programmable keys to match the standard keys.

Overall the phone retains the Nortel look and feel, and the setup menus are almost identical. A couple of reviewers have indicated that they have had problems long after buying the phone. I suspect that the problems I had with my Nortel phone were due to a power surge on the phone line. The new phone is connected to a VOIP modem so I doubt a power surge will ever make it past my Monster surge protector, cable modem, wireless router, and Vonage adapter to the phone.

I had also hoped to have multiple ios devices be able to scan from the device straight to the ios device, that doesn't work like that either. Very backwards and behind the times in ways like that.

sounds negative I know but once you come to grips with the shortcomings, it does what it's intended to do and does it fantastically. it's quick, not many errors and super convenient. I have not been able to find a easy way though to scan multiple documents in one run that have nothing to do with each other and then easily split then up into separate files when done. beyond that, I have begun scanning, cataloging everything in the house and have really gone a long way towards being paperless. While it didn't natively let you install the software to a network drive, I was able to get around that issue and now my documents scan to my nas and I have remote access to those files from my mobile devices anywhere, everywhere...

product_title: Pilot Metallic Permanent Paint Marker, Extra Fine Point,
review_headline: Excellent specialty marking pens- for fine metallic lines, writing and decorative work; ideal for marking wine bottles!
review_body:
These are excellent marking pens.

They produce a fine line in the appropriate metallic color.

If you have not used them before, I suggest you try them on some scrap paper beforehand, so you can become familiar with the characteristics of these pens.

They use liquid ink, which is delivered through a fine hollow tube. The ink delivery is controlled by a valve, which is opened when you depress the writing point against the paper, or whatever other surface you are writing on.

The ink is stored under pressure in the metallic reservoir.

Here are some tips:

1. Shake the pen before use, to mix the paint.

2. Hold the pen vertically, with the point downwards, and gently press the point against some scrap paper, to prime the system with paint.

3. Write carefully- it does take some practise to match the speed of ink delivery with the speed of writing. Write too fast, and there's not enough ink; too slow, and it's blotchy.

4. Take care to avoid damage to the writing point.

5. Don't break the plastic to metal seal on the pen.

6. Store the pen upright, with the writing point downwards.

7. Wipe the writing point with a tissue after use, to remove excess paint.

With care, these are very useful markers- ideal for writing special invitations, and other like usage.

I use mine to write on wine bottles- the results look attractive, and the marking is permanent.

They can be hard to find, as they are a specialty product.

But for the specific use they are designed for, they are worth finding!

review_headline: NE Image Black toner for the KM 1600W
review_body:
Not a good option for your printer. I am upset with the purchase. The toner produces a black dust over the print. Not something that you get with OEM, & not something I had an issue with, from another vender here. I'm sure they changed to the crappy stuff as well.
Black dust isn't acceptable when you're making anything you want to look good. You may have it on lesser laser printers, but not on the KM line.
I will say this, that on plain, cheap copier paper, you can't see the dust. On everything else, YUCK! Just because the color of the toner is black, doesn't mean that it will be a replacement. When I did the distribution shakes, after filling, I ruined a pair of pants, because the toner leaked out. I just figured the seal is getting weak (this is my third refill).

What really irks me is that I looked at what others had said, when I asked a question.

If you can live with the dust, fine, but the way it goes on the "paper" isn't all too good either. It's not a full black, more of a slate, & images just don't seem to fill in like they should. Of course, colors are muted with a black dust overlay, in that dirty artsy kind of way. You bought the KM 1600w because it prints pictures very well (or because it was cheap), don't expect this toner to help do that.
I may just go back to using the OEM black, with someone's (see my reviews elsewhere) color, as that worked out quite well. I will say, that if you're printing all black on card stock, to cut tags, you should be fine. The dust won't matter, unless you want white in that black.
I haven't tried this on polyester paper as yet, but will give it a try soon. I'm sure that it will burn, as the previous cheap black toner has done (enough to damage the fuser unit). Seeing that it melts in the fuser, I'm not all to quick to do that. I may just print my polyester sheets & labels in the second KM printer (w/OEM toner).

Anyhow, if you can live with crappy dust (like a few other lasers produce), go ahead, I'm sure this is that toner anyhow. It certainly isn't anything close to KM's OEM toner in the least.w other lasers produce), go ahead, I'm sure this is that toner anyhow. It certainly isn't anything close to KM's OEM toner in the least.

review_headline: These SUPERB Post-It Flags Have So Many Uses!
review_body:
For me, I was recently shopping in a local market and stumbled across these Post-It Flags. The first thing that popped into my head was: Wow, I can use these for so many purposes! And so I brought this home to test them thoroughly! So I HIGHLY recommend these to you for the following reasons:

1) Amount in package has a very generous amount of 100 flags. With the 5 colors that contain 20 flags per color this is great for organizing things to copy, certain types of file folders that need a flag etc.
2) For me, I found something very useful about these: I use them as two types of paperback or textbook BOOKMARKS:
--Locked in Stone Bookmark – I place this on my all time favorite page in a book and to make the Bookmark stay on there FOREVER, I simply re-enforce it with a piece of Scotch Tape (clear) on the inside of the page and seal it down tightly.
--Regular Bookmark – A bookmark type that for NOW is my favorite page, but as I progress in my reading, I want to remove the Bookmark and place it on a NEW page for a NEW Bookmark – This one I DO NOT add any Scotch Tape to, I have found that I can actually re-use these several times throughout my reading of one book.
***I also COLOR CODE the bookmarks (Flags). For the Locked in Stone Bookmarks, I place a PINK Flag and for my Regular Bookmarks I place a Yellow one…this is just my personal preference but it works great for me.
3) As for the other colors, I like to use these when I run of the Yellows for my NEW Bookmarks and just continue to use the Pink Flags for the Locked In Stone Bookmarks as I just have a few of these.

These Flags I also use for my home office desk’s paperwork. If I need to address something very soon (like pay a bill) and it needs my attention, then I place a GREEN flag on this to associate the green with green dollar bill…

Highly recommend this to ALL!

review_headline: An excellent bargain for quickly verifying ethernet and phone lines. It saved me tons of aggravation down the road!
review_body:
I'm building a house and I have ethernet pre-wired through through the house. After the house was wired, I used this tester to determine if all the wiring was good.

First of all, the probe at the top (left side of image,) is extremely helpful. I have about 10 ethernet cables in the house. While I could use trial and error and go through 10 cables, I used the probe and get audio feedback of which cable I was connected to the other side. One of the cables indicated that there were four pins not matching. If it wasn't for this tester, I might not know and end up having transmission issues down the road. We use these at work where they are used to transport heavy items daily and they hold up well. Not quite as good as the really heavy duty non-adjustable carts, but well enough. I brought one home to use for the weekend and my son loved it. He works weekend festivals and must often tote a load of supplies and a canopy tent for a quarter mile or more, sometimes over grass. The small cart he used before could not handle it, and would often get stuck in the grass.

When his former cart broke down, he bought one of these. It has worked out great for him. Not only does the adjustable length work out great and over all types of terrain, but he often helps others with lesser carts who would otherwise be carrying heavy items. If you use one every day and only on pavement or hard surfaces, and don't need the adjustability to carry large items and don't mind the weight, you would probably be better off with a heavy duty welded convertible hand truck, but if you need something other than small hard wheels to carry larger items, the Rock n Roller is the best choice I have found.

product_title: Epson Expression Home XP-400 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer, Copier, Scanner.  Prints from Tablet/Smartphone. AirPrint Compatible (C11CC07201)
review_body:
The XP-400 is an attractive-looking all-in-one (but notice it does not do fax) that's easy to set up for Windows PCs. The Wi-Fi setup is also guided if you use a Windows computer. I never tried the phone/tablet hookup.

As with most Epson home inkjets, though, it can take forever to get ready to print something, especially if you have not turned it on for a few days. I don't know if it's the bootstrap part of the firmware or the needs of the printer to thoroughly clean the print heads each time it's turned on, the wait can be maddening. It also runs through the ink cartridges rather quickly, compared with an older Epson I have as well as my Canon workhorse all-in-one. (The Canon also takes a long time to get ready, if left powered-off for a few days.)

I personally recommend if you buy this printer, use it to print photos. You cannot print black-and-white documents without the color inks, and the printer does go through ink a little too fast, but it does work well when you want to print good-quality photos -- and in that case, a few minutes of waiting is not as bad as when you need to print a book report or Excel spreadsheet to hand in.

product_title: Crayola Marker Maker
review_headline: Great activity for a rainy day!
review_body: The Crayola Marker Maker is a fun and engaging craft activity for the whole family.  The kit comes with enough supplies to make 16 markers which fit into 2 boxes of 8 markers each, making this a great activity for two children to do together.  We opened the box on a rainy afternoon and had the assembly completed and directions read in about ten minutes.  That is certainly a reasonable amount of time considering the number of components provided in the box -- the marker maker contraption, 5 pieces for each marker, 2 beakers, 3 bottles of ink, a color chart, tweezers, and 2 boxes and a set of labels for the completed markers - but ten minutes is a long time for young children to wait patiently when there are very tempting items like ink and small plastic pieces lying around.  To avoid having to forcefully disassemble markers that have been incorrectly assembled by little impatient hands, I recommend that an adult get everything set up before calling the kids to the table.  The recommended age on the box is 8+.  I would say 10+ without adult supervision (due to the strength required to operate the press and the logic required to make sense of the instructions) and 3+ with adult supervision.  My 4-year-old son and 8-year-old daughter both loved making these markers.  The red, blue, and yellow ink can be used alone to make bright primary color markers or can be combined to create different shades of purple, green, and orange.  Here's how it works:  ink of the desired color(s) is squirted into a beaker, the foam core of the marker is placed into the beaker until the ink is absorbed, and the core is then moved to the marker barrel that has been loaded into the press contraption.  Firm pressure is applied to the handle of the press contraption until the barrel, tip, and end plug of the marker snap together.  After a couple of minutes, the ink will be absorbed into the tip of the marker and the marker will be ready to use.  My children enjoyed all aspects of this activity:selecting a color from the color chart, measuring and pouring the ink into the beaker, assembling the marker components, designing the label for each marker, and coloring the box for the completed markers. And believe me, in an office situation, a non-smelly floor mat is a wonderful thing. Heck, in any type of situation that's a wonderful thing!

After all, the description of this mat holds its size, 36 x 48 inches, so it's quite easy to take a tape measure (or even a yard stick or ruler) and mark out that same area around your desk to see if the mat will work for you or if you need to size up. Its small size won't be a problem if you do your homework first.

Because this mat is made for hard floors, it doesn't have the little nubbins on the back like those mats made for carpeted areas (which is good because they wouldn't work and simply break off, but I just mean there's nothing on the backside of the mat to hold it in place). So this mat will slip around a bit on a hard floor, but it's only an issue when you're walking around and maybe catch your foot on it until you get used to its presence. When you're sitting down at your desk, the mat stays in place, allowing you to roll around in your chair quite easily. And I tell you, that in itself is quite something as my home desk (which is where I've got the mat) sits on tiled floor made from those big 12 inch square tiles which have been eating up the wheels on my chair. With this mat, though, I can roll around like a maniac without leaving ugly black marks on the floor from where the chair wheels have shredded.

Frankly, for the price, I don't see how you could go wrong with this lightweight yet quality mat.

product_title: HP Photosmart 7510 All-in-One with eFax Printer
review_headline: HP should be ashamed to sell this kind of junk
review_body:
I can't imagine how HP engineers can face each day knowing that they put out products that are this awful.

My wife uses this printer in her office. She is a light printer user, maybe 10 to 20 pages a week, mostly black and white.

Here are the stats:

Over the life of the printer (about a year), she has printed 1303 pages on plain paper and 11 on photo paper. During this time, we have used 6 black 564XL (larger and expensive) cartridges, 3 cyan 564XL, 2 magenta 564XL, 2 yellow 564XL and 2 photo black 564XL. The total ink cost has been around $350 for 1314 pages printed. That works out to about $0.26 per sheet. Considering that most printing is black and white, that is on the high side. Where does the ink go? Are there secret cleaning routines that are dumping ink? Are the reservoirs in the cartridges microscopic?

The more painful issue is that we are constantly buying cartridges and the printer is always out of ink. On average we are changing a cartridge every 85 sheets or so! From my point of view, it seems like I am replacing a cartridge about every week while my wife asks me why the printer is always out of ink and what did I do wrong that she can't print again!

HP advertises the 564XL black cartridge as good for 550 pages and the color cartridges as good for 750 pages each. Based on that we bought the printer. They are not even close.

Suckered again by HP.

At work we have stopped buying HP printers altogether and have been very happy using Brother for the last couple of years.

There is also an irritating feature in the scanning process whereby the machine automatically assigns a 3-digit serialized extension to whatever filename you give to the document or photo (or whatever you scan).  In other words, if you want to name a file something like \\"Report 131004\\" the file name assigned by the machine will be \\"Report 131004486\\", those last three additional digits representing the current serial number of the number (486) of scans you have made.  Irritating and there is no way to deal with this other than to go back later and \\"rename\\" each file.  The only positive thing about this printer is that it does seem to be economical in its use of ink cartridges. product_title: Spracht ZUM DECT 6.0 Headset
review_headline: A good DECT headset for keeping a call going while far and wide in your house
review_body:
Spracht HS-2012 ZUM DECT 6.0 Wireless Headset with Base Station is a good example of a product that seeks to fill the niche stated as \\"what if you wanted a wireless headset for use with a hard land line, but wanted greater range and security than produced by Bluetooth?\\". As such it's a nice looking unit that performed very well for me all over my house and out into the driveway -- it's basically a dialless cordless phone in the form of a headset, and the range and performance is very similar. As had been noted, the Spracht is not interoperable with base stations made by other makers that require the ability to manually enter a pairing code. The Spracht works only with its own proprietary base station, that is paired with the headset by pressing a sequence of buttons until status lights flash confirmation of pairing. In between uses the Spracht base station serves as a charging station and rest for the headset.

Outgoing calls must still be dialed from either the base of your land-line phone, if that's where the dial is, or from the original headset of the land-line phone, which must be attached to the base station for the Spracht. A tad inconvenient, but there doesn't seem to be any other \\"plumbing\\" solution. That said, the system works well. This would probably be more useful to people in an office, for long conference calls or, at home, for compulsive multitaskers who also want to chat chat chat. I liked it and had a good experience using it. A little expensive for what it is, but RECOMMENDED.

First, the CallerID on the outside LED screen is completely unreadable unless you take the phone off the hook and angle it toward you. But by then you've answered the call, defeating the purpose of reading the CallerID.

Even more annoying, the useless CallerID screen necessitates four AA batteries (not included) which will eventually run down and need to be replaced, causing hassle in my life for no useful purpose.

The other thing I don't like is the numbers on the outside. If you put the phone under your ear, balanced on your shoulder, the tones will sound during your conversation. Sony thoughtfully included a keypad \\"lock\\" switch...but I don't want to have to unlock the keypad each time I dial, then relock it to talk on the phone. That's why, for time immemorial, the numbers on this style of phone are on the INSIDE of the handset. Perhaps for some, the ability to dial with the phone on the wall is a plus...but not for me. I would always remove it anyway as I find dialing an object in my palm easier than an object on the wall.

The other thing I didn't like is that the \\"message waiting\\" light keeps blinking even after I've listened to my voice mail. This is probably because I have several other phones in the house and I listened to the voice mail on a different phone. Still, the constantly blinking light makes the message waiting feature useless.

Since all the modern features on this phone are useless to me (CallerID, Voice Mail waiting etc.) I decided to get a vintage Trimline from 1990 on Ebay for $25 and I am happy as a clam. It works great, doesn't need batteries, works in a power failure and looks great.

Back to the Sony phone:

PROS
*Very nice quality and build; extremely hard to find these days in corded wall phones!
*Works during a power failure.
*Great sound quality

CONS
*CallerID screen impossible to read without being at the perfect angle--which mostly means taking the phone off the hook, ruining the purpose of seeing who is calling before answering.
*Numbers on the outside of the phone is bad design. To talk on the phone without risk of accidentally pressing them, you can use the keypad lock key but you need to remember each time.
*Requires batteries
*Message waiting light keeps blinking even after you check voice mail. Probably caused by having multiple phones--but how many people are really going to have this Sony as their only phone? For me, the wall phone is mainly a power failure backup.works in a power failure and looks great.

We (my husband) wanted to replace it with an expensive Lexmark printer/scanner/copier/faxer/can opener.  The thing sucked. Finally, five years ago, I bought the Canon Pixma MP560 on black friday for $48.  I love it.  It works wirelessly with our Mac and laptop pc, and never argues with them.  It prints photos (via the Canon app) from our iphones and ipads, and even pfds if we save them in our camera roll.  You have to make sure to select regular or photo paper if, like me, you keep both stocked in your printer.  I think the photo quality is great, although I only print 4x6 photos or the occasional 5x7.  We have moved this printer, in a moving truck across umpteen mountain ranges from Wisconsin to Alaska via the Alcan highway.  All of the paperwork for our move was printed, scanned, and re-sent using this printer, and we never once had a problem.  I frequently use the scanner and copier for recipes and knitting patterns, and the detail is always very sharp.  It's in perfect shape.  My husband disconnected this to take it to work with him for a week when their office printer failed, and it interfaced with their network and handled the higher volume beautifully.  I guess my only problem is that it's five years old, almost six.  I want a new one, with all the new bells and whistles, but I can't justify buying one since this one still works like it was just out of the box.  Dang it.

product_title: Canon Office and Business MX922 All in One Printer, Wireless and mobile printing
review_body:
The 922 may or may not be a wonderful printer, but unfortunately, it doesn't meet my needs, and I wasn't able to figure this out from any of the specifications or written description prior to purchase.

I've owned predecessor Canon multi-function printers for a number of years, and loved them. I was in a hurry when my 860 died, bought online from Amazon to take advantage of the overnight delivery option so I could be set up before leaving on a trip.

Unfortunately none of the copy on the 922 indicated that the new paper cassette is front-loading, nor does Canon's website include photos which so indicate. Equally unfortunately, when I came to Amazon's website, thinking I'd already researched the product, I missed the photo above which does show the cassette to be front-loading. I did read every word of copy, however, none of which mentioned this feature change.

I have a printer drawer, and cannot load paper into the cassette without lifting the front of the machine. Equally a problem for me, I regularly print checks and need to be able to load less than full pages of checks. None of this is a problem with a rear-loading paper feeder. But I could not make it work at all with the 922.

I prefer a rear-loading paper feed for two additonal reasons: Typically, they permit the use of heavier papers, cover stock useful for certain purposes like programs. Nowhere in the Canon or Amazon specs did I find any reference to permissible paper weights. But more important, front loaders in my years of previous experience are far more prone to jamming. And repeated jamming can misalign internal parts, leading to early printer death, given the cost and inconvenience of service.

I am so sad to have to return or donate this printer. I use Canon cameras almost exclusively, liked the software, have enjoyed the easy compatibility of photo files/Canon papers/and printer.

I'm particularly disappointed that the information on Canon's website doesn't note the front-loading feature in any way, and that it doesn't appear in the written descriptions on Amazon either. product_title: Floortex Ultimat Polycarbonate Chair Mat
review_headline: Finally, a chair mat that meets its rating
review_body:
I've been buying chair mats locally at the obvious office supply stores for so many years. They all carry a lifetime warranty, but none of them last very long. While it's important to make sure you buy a floor mat rated for the proper thickness of carpet (including the pad beneath!), my experience is that none of the mats will hold up longer than a year even if you do so.

For example, I have a carpet in my home office that's low-pile and certainly no thicker than 1/4" and the pad below it is about 3/8", a total of less than 3/4". But *every* chair mat I've bought for the last several years that says "For carpets up to 3/4 inch" develops cracks within less than a year.

And these things aren't cheap! I've been successful a couple of times at returning the mat to the local office chain, but this last time they told me to mail it back to the manufacturer. Umm, that ain't gonna work - for a number of obvious reasons. So I decided to look elsewhere and decided on this mat here on Amazon.

Even though this unit says "for Plush Pile Carpets More Than 1/2 Inch Thick" and not "... up to 3/4 inch", it must be nearly twice as thick as the 3/4"-rated floor mats I've been buying locally for years. And when I sit in my chair I can feel the difference. It is much harder and stiffer - stronger - it does not give at all to my weight - no comparison.

Also, I checked one of the local store's website and, lo and behold, there's the same mat there. I don't know why they don't make these available in the local stores, and now I don't care either because at $130 and free shipping to my front door, this one is both $40 cheaper and the same Make and Model. That's a no-brainer.

It hasn't been a year yet, so ultimately I cannot prove that this unit will not crack within that same amount of time. But at this point, I'm pretty darn certain, and I'm happy to pay double what I've been paying for those cheaper units because this will surely last more than twice as long, and will be a pleasure the whole while.

A word of caution: when the unit arrives and you've unboxed it, it will be rolled and tied with a poly strap you will need to cut. When you do so, STAND BACK, as the mat is very stiff and will spring open forcefully! The other option would be to have two people hold it while cutting the strap and release it slowly. Just a word of caution to be aware.
