product_title: Pilot Namiki Falcon Collection Fountain Pen
review_headline: A good pen with a Fine (not flexible) nib.
review_body:
I am a regular fountain pen (and an occasional dip pen) user since school days, and I have a variety of pens including some high quality pens. Most of the time I write in an ordinary style, but I can write in a calligraphy style using an italic or an oblique nib.

I bought this beautiful looking pen with a view to having my first "flexible nib" fountain pen, for daily use (dip pens are fantastic but you can't carry them around). I wanted a modern pen as opposed to an antique/used pen, and I chose a Soft Fine nib.

The Soft Fine nib is slightly finer than the usual fine nibs we get in the UK. The pen has a wonderful ink flow. The nib gives a little, but is NOT a "flexible nib". Posting the cap on the body makes the writing lighter and better. The line width variability, a key feature of "flexible nibs" is imperceptible. (The writing is nothing like the sample writing shown on the website. In fact I felt misled, but I won't return the pen.) It writes like a pen with a rather nice fine nib; but the scratchiness is distinctly audible, although reduced after writing some 200 pages of A5, so far. Recently I had to complete a lot of forms and the fine nib was excellent for the purpose. Also the SF nib deposits less ink on paper compared to say a M or OBB. With so many notebooks sold with somewhat thin paper, it is an advantage that this nib does not soak through, and one can write on the reverse side of the paper.

The refillable ink converter has an infuriatingly tiny capacity. A disappointment for a pen that carries the founder's name - Pilot should re-think. Cartridges have their advantage, but with such a wonderful range of inks now available today, users want refillable pens. (Since bottled ink is far from cheap, I don't see manufacturers or retailers making less money selling bottled ink as opposed to ink cartridges. So why not provide decent size converters?)

It is a good pen with a Fine (not flexible) nib. Without a good size converter it is not practical/dependable enough for daily use. Over priced, I think.nib. Without a good size converter it is not practical/dependable enough for daily use. Over priced, I think.

review_headline: Fits A Lot More Than I Expected When I Drilled A Hole In The Back
review_body:
This Safco Scoot Desk-Side Printer Stand is perfect for someone like me, who has too many things on my desk. I have two printers (a regular to save on ink and a photo printer), an Epson perfection scanner and other items cluttering up my computer desk. When you add these two printers and scanner to my tower, screen, keyboard, speakers, mouse, surge protector and 7 port hub, it's just a crowded mess. One of my printers has always been kept on a small under the desk stand, but it's always in the way. It's much nicer having a mobile desk-side printer stand to get my photo printer out from under my desk.

This stand is heavy duty, as the directions say you can put up to 100 pounds on the top and 50 pounds on each shelf. It takes at least 30 minutes to put this together. The middle shelf is adjustable to what 2 shelf heights you need, and this ended up being really great for my needs to de-clutter my desk. The 4 wheels are easier to lock into the legs, when you stand it up and push on the stand, and 2 of the wheels can lock, so the stand doesn't move. There is a large side pocket that you can put on either side to hold paper or notebooks and I found it great to hold some of my photo editing and art software in.

It's really great that this stand has metal vented sides, so you can put other printers or scanners on the shelves. This stand being 20\\" x 26\\" x 26\\" can fit most printers and scanners not only on the top but on the inside shelves. The only thing I had to do was cut a hole in the back metal for the cables and cords. I used one of those inexpensive drill bit hole saws made for metal or bi-metal and a variable speed drill. I cut a 2\\" hole in the back, which is perfect for the cord and cable on my scanner or printer. I believe Amazon sells several of these metal or bi-metal hole saws, as I bought a Vulcan brand one a few years back for only $11.00. They even make Impacted Rated Hole Saws that actually pops out the metal disc leaving a super smooth finish, but just for a hole in the back that no one will see, my cheap Vulcan hole saw is fine.

Once I adjusted the middle shelf to a lower position, I found it large enough to actually put my Epson scanner on and it leaves me enough room to open the lid to over 12 inches. I put my larger photo printer on the top, and with the lowest shelf I have room for my packs of paper. This stand fits a lot more items than I ever expected- freeing up my desk space to only my regular printer. The adjustable shelf and vented sides made this possible to add both a scanner and large photo printer on this stand. I only needed to drill one hole with my inexpensive Vulcan bi-metal hole saw in the back with my drill to accommodate the cord and cable to add another printer or scanner on the shelf. This sturdy stand freed up a lot more desk space than I expected and I love the fact that it can be mobile or locked into place. product_title: MagicJack Plus + Free 6 Months Subscription to Magic Jack Service
review_body: I've had a lot of problems with magicJack.  Most were probably my fault for trying to use it connected to other buildings, don't do it.  They are very sensitive to lightning and storms.  I've been through 4 magicJacks because of this. One other problem was AT&T's fault when I transferred my phone number.  They really messed me up and now I can't receive local phone calls from AT&T phones to my magicJack. It's a long story.  The only reason I am staying with it is because it is saving me about $500 a year in phone bills.  If you don't mind getting a new phone number that magicJack will issue you then you should be OK.  It was the transferring of the phone number that didnt work out as planned for me.  Oh, one other thing, 7 digit calling is over when you switch to magiJack.  Most phone systems are switching to 10 digits anyway but 10 digits are all you can use on magicJack.  People who call you will have to use 10 digits too.  I can only receive local calls if they use the 1+my 10 digit phone number when they call from an AT&T phone.  In other words all local calls to me are long distance calls.

review_headline: Works as well as the Epson branded inkjets

I cleaned the printer heads and ran the alignment check on the printer, and then printed a test page. Crisp text and nice color saturation - everything looks great!

I recommend these remanufactured ink cartridges as a solid alternative to the much more expensive [[ASIN:B003LD5QIE Epson DURABrite T127120 Ultra 127 Extra High-capacity Inkjet Cartridge-Black]] and [[ASIN:B003K1PH7W Epson DURABrite T126520 Ultra 126 High-capacity Inkjet Cartridge Color Multipack -Cyan/Magenta/Yellow]].

product_title: Westcott Paper Trimmer With Titanium Bonded Cut And Score Blades, 12"
review_headline: A small caution for laminated papers
review_body:
Overall, I like this little trimmer. I have to agree with the reviews that it is a bit lightweight (less durable) and that the print of the grid and numerals are subject to rubbing off with use, as opposed to trimmers where the print is molded in. However, this is a trimmer, and subject to infrequent exposure to moisture, washing, etc. under normal conditions. Not the same as my kitchen measuring cups, where embossing is at a premium for pretty much all users. For the dedicated scrapbook hobbyist: yes, you might want to get a heavier duty (and LARGER) trimmer.

I did have the opportunity to try this trimmer out at the same time that I was breaking in a new laminator. Considering that the trimmer is advertised as being able to slice through FIVE sheets of standard 20 weight printer/copy paper at once, I thought it might be fun to try trimming some laminated (single) sheets of 20 weight paper laminated with both \\"3 mil\\" and the thicker \\"5 mil\\" standard laminating sheets. (I only cut through the plastic - if you cut through the paper-sandwiched part of a laminated sheet, you open and hence ruin the seal.)

With the 5 mil, cutting through was a a bit of chore and in fact I couldn't keep up enough steady pressure to do it cleanly - one layer cut and one started to pull away. A second pass cleaned the edge up reasonably well, but overall I'd call it a fail, with careful subsequent attempts somewhat better but not always clean through from top to bottom. 3 mil was better, but still challenged the blade in terms of the pressure I had to apply, leaving me wondering if repeated use on even thin laminate might not greatly reduce the blade's useful life.

The best thing for my money about this trimmer is that you can load the slicing and the scoring blades and line them up out of the way on the one end or the other such that you can use the one you want for the task at hand. No changing out blades!

Photos and card stock on hand cut nicely for me; see other reviews here for feedback on the longevity of the titanium blades - clearly satisfaction varies based on usage, but unless I find myself with a task at hand that is so unusually large as to make this trimmer seem undersized and underpowered, I think I'm happy. It's sharp, it stows, and yes, I cheat and use a ruler (sometimes a T-square) to draw a cutting line on the reverse of many projects, so I don't need a bigger unit with a longer placement edge for squaring things up. I just need a reliable tool that will stow in a small space in my (home) office. review_headline: Exactly what I was hoping for...
review_body:
I have been searching for an electronic notepad for quite awhile. I was getting tired of endless post-it notes on my kitchen counter consisting of grocery and to-do lists. I wanted a neater way of keeping track of all of the errands I have to run.

I came across the Sharp WG-N10 in my hunt. It was exactly what I was looking for. It is for sure, the pioneer for this type of technology and seemed like the absolute best choice for me.

It is very easy to use. It is 4.5\\" x 6\\" which is perfect to carry along with me as I run my errands. It comes with an understated cover with a holder for the stylus pen and a USB cable. There is an eraser tool which allows you to erase whatever you have written and it performs exactly like a pencil eraser. The eraser tool also has the three thickness options.
You have a thousand pages to write on and can save anything you jot down. A full charge lasts 30 days. Another great function is being able to erase an entire page at once.

Even though all of the instructions and functions are written in Japanese, I spent 20 minutes playing around with it and figured most of it out. Watching the You Tube videos in advance (also in Japanese) helps as well. I know there are additional functions I will eventually discover after using it for awhile.

The instructions that come with this notepad are in Japanese as well as ALL wording within the notepad itself. The company that I ordered it from on Amazon, ALEXCIOUS informed me of this upon ordering it. I decided it wouldn't be too much of a problem after I watched a few tutorials on YouTube. product_title: Epson WorkForce  All-In-One Wireless Color Inkjet Printer WF-2540, Black
review_headline: Replace Ink Software has Serious Glitches
review_body:
We have had the printer for about 6 months. The quality of the print outs is fine. Nothing wonderful, but certainly reasonable for the price.

My issue is with the replace ink software code. The printouts were working just fine, no fading at all, and we got the alarm to replace the ink. We did it. Then after 5 pages the alarm came up again. As last time, the actual printouts were just fine. No fading or skipping. However, the printer will not print at all unless you replace the cartridge. Once you get the 'out of ink' alarm, the printer is rendered completely useless. I am not sure why that is, but it is. Anything we try to print is put in the queue for after the new cartridge is installed.

On the Epson website, this is a common question. The only answer is: \\"Re-install the ink cartridge\\". So we removed and replaced it 5 separate times. No luck. Clearly there is a glitch in the programming of the ink replacement code.

The one I ordered to replace the last one I installed has not even arrived yet!

In the last week, we have invested $60 on black replacement ink cartridge-and we are just not using this printer heavily at all.

As I type, we are trying to locate our old Canon printer. It is 6 years old, but at least we will be able to use it.

product_title: Ooma Telo Free Home Phone Service
review_body:
This review is for Ooma service - not this Ooma device.

I purchased Ooma for $200 in 2008 - the device was called Ooma Hub and it is a white box. Under the contract when I signed on, I was entitled to FREE LIFETIME phone service, yes, totally free service. From the date of my purchase, I have not paid any monthly service, per my lifetime contract terms.

Sometime after my purchase, Ooma apparently started charging \\"applicable monthly taxes and fees\\" for their \\"totally fee phone service\\". (Despite the name, the bulk of this monthly fee has nothing to do with taxes and more to do with Ooma fees). However, I'm guessing the buyer is aware of this monthly fee at the time of purchase. What the buyer may not be aware of, is that the terms of the \\"free service\\" can change at Ooma's whim.

I called this morning to buy a replacement device for my hub and was told my \\"lifetime\\" contract\\" is now null and void. I was told I need to \\"renegotiate\\" the contract if I replace the hub, and with that, now start paying a monthly Ooma service fee.

There is nothing in my written contract that says the \\"lifetime free service\\" becomes null and void when the device dies. This contract was for my Ooma account - not the plastic hub box.

HERE'S MY NOTE TO YOU -- if the contract terms are permitted to change whenever you have to replace your device (Ooma customer rep said this is 2-5 years), you too will have your contract terms changed and you will be required to pay whatever the prevailing Ooma fees at the time are, regardless of what your contract says. And there's nothing you can do about it.

I asked what the new telo box does that my current device does not that justified a monthly fee, and there was nothing different.

I'm tossing this service. 0 stars for this disreputable company.

GREAT HINT! Someone else shared this with me .. will now share with you.

Take one of those plastic tabs that tie the end of loaves of bread or oranges etc .. stick the plastic tab on the sticky edge of the end of the tape .. store it away .. next time you use the tape .. and EACH TIME after you make a cut .. BEFORE you let go of the tape .. plop that plastic tab onto the sticky edge of the tape and you are good to go!

product_title: Kodak P811R Personal Photo & Negative Scanner 8x10" Photo Size, USB 2.0 - Red
review_headline: Good little scanner, as long as you don't operate with batteries.
review_body:
Pros:
Small, portable, and very easy to set up and scan.
Uses SD card (so no need to plug into a computer to scan items).
A 2G SD card is included (which holds quite a few files at the resolution provided by this scanner).
Can scan even the thicker photos (many of the family snapshots from the 1950's and 1960's are on something similar to card-stock or even cardboard).
It scans negatives too (with included attachment).

Cons:
While this scanner has a battery compartment, it can only scan three or four items in a row when powered by the batteries. After that, the scanner jams and hangs. Powering it off and back on can sometimes get you one more item scanned, but I found that if you have a batch of more than 3 items to scan, it is best to just plug it in.
No ability to increase the resolution (not really a big issue when just trying to digitize items for archival purposes, but don't expect to be making files that you can then print as posters or even significant enlargements).
Does not seem to scan transparencies (slides).

Overall I like this scanner and it meets my needs perfectly for archiving generations of family photos. I would have given it four stars if it worked better on battery power. I wanted to give it 3.5 stars as it is, but the rating system seems to require full stars, no halves.

product_title: Samsung Multifunction Xpress SL-M2875FW Wireless Monochrome Printer with Scanner, Copier and Fax
review_body:
This printer works good when it works but when it doesn't it's annoying. We specifically bought it because it's WIFI capable - we could plug it in in a centralized location and then use it from any of our systems as we needed without having to have any specific system turned on all the time.

Turns out this printer after some time of non-use [say a few days] basically drops offline. The status light shows it's on and connected to WIFI but printing will not work, scanning will not work, it cannot be seen on the network. Pressing the 'wake/power' button or the 'start' button will not fix the issue - the *only* solution I've found is to unplug it and plug it back in.

Additionally the ScanToPC software crashes regularly on all systems it's installed on. I had an HP Printer with the same features for years and not once did the ScanToPC software ever crash. It always crashes at the worst time too - giving a presentation from your laptop? BAM - Error message in the middle of your screen.

The hardware works well - it's the firmware and the software that seems to be buggy. I'd hope for an updated/improved version but I can't even find the *correct* drivers for this printer on Samsung.com. Even if I go to the driver download page from the specific model I have - it still gives me 'Universal Print Drivers' which work for printing but not for scanning or any of the other features the printer comes with - it seems the only way to get this software is from the CD and, as we all know, software delivered on-CD with a product is almost always outdated.

I've considered trying to return the printer but no longer have the packaging materials, etc - it's too much work for what we paid. We'll simply be keeping this in mind the next time we're shopping for printers that Samsung - while the print quality is good when it works - isn't a good print/fax/scan system to have for a small office.

review_body:
[[VIDEOID:mo27MDA1ATHYEXE]]I was so impressed with how well this works that I decided to create a short video for my review.

I've seen TV commercials advertising products like this but it wasn't until recently that I decided how handy it would be--especially since you don't need to have it hooked to a computer to scan! I decided to purchase one with the docking station because I was concerned that perhaps the free-hand scans may be difficult to do well. I also liked the fact that this one scans up to 900 dpi using the wand, and even higher when it is docked into the station. I've only scanned in about 15 items but I found using the wand very easy.

If you watch the video you can see the results! The color scanned a bit intense on the glossy photos (these were photos of some of my art work) but right now I'm not overly concerned because I know I can adjust that in Photoshop. Earlier I had scanned some color images from a text book and the color seemed very accurate in those. I'll need to scan a few more to see if this is a consistent issue or not.

The main reason I brought this is to use with my art students. In the past I've had them scan some of their art work on a traditional scanner--but it was a lengthy process with one scanner and 24 students waiting in line. Now they will be able to quickly feed their work (if it is smaller than letter size) into the auto-feeder, or they can hand scan it with the wand. Most of the items I have them scan are black and white drawings so if the color is off a bit it won't matter.

Now that I know how well it works I'm sure I'll be able to think of a lot more uses for it. I have a faculty meeting tomorrow and it seems like a perfect way to scan important documents I'll be receiving . . . and after work, perhaps I'll visit the library?

Overall, I'm very impressed!

review_body:
I'm a person who spends long hours at the computer, so I'm always on the lookout for products that minimized back strain and shoulder soreness, and this product look like just the ticket. However, after both my husband and I tested it, we came to the conclusion that it really only works with specific chair types.

The product itself is well made. The cushion is wide enough that it'll stretch across most chairs, and it fastens easily with a wide strap and clasp system. You can either slide it down the back of the chair or clip it around and, once it's in place, pulling on the strap's slack tightens it. The cushion is firm with just enough give, and it felt good on my back.

The problem we ran into had to do with our chairs. My husband and I have different desk chairs, but both of our chairs have curved mesh backs. When the cushion was in place, it did support our lower backs, but it also had the effect of pushing us forward, causing discomfort for our upper backs. The only way I could sit with my back all the way against the backrest was to push myself back with a fair amount of force, which wasn't at all comfortable. I think if you have a straight back chair, this cushion might be just the ticket. But I didn't find it compatible with a curved chair.

product_title: Brother Printer HL2270DW Wireless Monochrome Printer
review_headline: Connection: Failed (Error : TS-07)  restored w/good but tedious live support from Brother
review_body:
use: light home use

problem: Connection: Failed (Error : TS-07) occurred several months after initial purchase and install. e Printer inexplicably lost wireless connectivity. The solution was not that difficult but involved far, far too many steps than I think it should have to fix.

print quality, speed, features: darn good for sub $80 printer on sale

solution: Initially I went to the Brother site and followed the re-set steps which involve pushing buttons on the printer including one recessed one on the rear. Since there were no changes to the Brother software on my computer and the printer self test report gave a fault of no comm to router I assumed that the problem was in the printer. This may be true but the solution requires one to uninstall the PC software!!, connect the printer to the router via ethernet!! briefly and a whole mess of other step not required during the initial set-up. PITA!

The self help directions of the Brother site for the particular fault code tell you to push the re-set button on the back for a specified number of seconds (not too many). Despite this the fault continued and the self help diagnostics are not enough for most to get up and running again.

Ultimately if wireless connectivity is lost, you need to know how to print the correct self diagnostic reports by pressing the go button a certain number of times and go through this complex re-set procedure that will require 90 minutes with tech support.

I ws instructed to un-install the Brother software on my pc. Was asked for the oem disc!!! Figuring that I wanted to re-install the latest drivers I asked the tech and she guided to the correct pages. As it turns out however the latest vs online is from 2011 anyway.

As of 7/2013 the latest software package was still from 2011 on the web site.

Dozens of steps were involved. I suspect that very few end users are going to be able to repair this fault on their own without live support from Brother. Fortunately the India based agent was very good which was a surprise. Most of the time spent was waiting for software to load and carrying out the steps. The CSR never put me on hold +++++++++++

The fault may have occurred as a result of numerous power outages here but there should be auto repair software built in to repair onnection failed error TS-07. Unfortunately the process is not self repairing

Do not but this printer unless you have the time and patience to deal with repairing erra TS-07

review_body: I'm one of those people.. I just cannot help myself. I like my pens to have a fine point, not bleed all over the place, and not bleed through the paper. Finally, Sharpie has made me happy. I like the really fine point mechanical pencils as well. If these are the things you like then you should love these pens. They have felt tips, so you do not need to "bare down hard" to get the ink to come out or maintain a fine line. I discovered these when they came out while working at an office supply store, since then if I have a  choice these are the only pens I will use. I keep them in my purse, backpack, and desk. This pack is an assorted pack with "fun" colors. They also have just blue, black, red, or a combo of blue and black. I say they do not bleed like other pens, because most other pens are ball-point and these have felt tips. review_headline: Cheap, mass-produced plastic--and I love it!
review_body:
The Etekcity is a bottom-of-the-line mass-produced Chinese piece of plastic, and I love it. I've carried it daily for a week now, and I couldn't be happier. It records well enough for any reasonable purpose, it lasts forever so I don't have to think about turning it on or off, and it has made little to no impact on my daily life. I just toss it in my pocket and it works. I couldn't ask for more, especially for $12.

There's just one switch: ON / OFF. It's either recording, or it ain't. After switching ON, there is a small (10s) delay before recording starts, and after switching OFF there is a 2s delay before it's ready to be switched back ON to start recording again.

The mic faces outward on one broad-side of the USB stick, so when I put it in my pocket I make sure that side is facing forward.

There is a light that actually shines through the mic opening. It's bright enough to see when you look at the naked device, but would never show through a pocket. The light blinks red when charging, is solid red when charged, and blinks blue when recording. When you start recording, it goes solid red, then blinks red, then once recording begins it starts blinking blue (10s). When you stop recording, it shines solid red until it's done finishing the recording file (2s). If the battery is low during recording, the light will begin to blink red again.

The recording files are stored in a folder on the root of the drive simply called \\"RECORD\\" and are named successively \\"REC001.WAV\\", \\"REC002.WAV\\", etc. Each file is limited to 2 hours in length, which is about 329MB per WAV file. In other words, it can record much longer than it will last on a single battery charge. If you recharge it without deleting the existing recording files, it will store about 22.5hrs of recorded audio before it's full. I've just been wiping it every night when I plug it into my desktop PC to charge.

As far as I can tell, there is no way to set the date and time stamps. They start sometime in the year 2000 and go from there. I have found some mentions of editing a \\"tag.txt\\" file or using \\"SetTime.exe\\" to write the correct current time, but all combinations of tactics I've tried to accomplish this have failed.

The battery life is as advertised: about 14 hours on constant record. To make sure I can record all day on longer days, I started to turn it off when I was at work, since I sit at my desk for hours doing things that aren't boring but sound really boring in audio-only.

Recording quality is excellent. It does pick up a lot of pocket noise, so walking or tapping on my leg generates a lot of sound. But, when I'm speaking with people, I can still hear the voices even if I'm walking along. If, for instance, I were sitting in my truck at a traffic stop, I'm confident even voices outside the truck would be recorded clearly. product_title: Doxie portable scanner for going paperless with rechargeable battery & amazing software
review_headline: Fast easy to use scanner, great for price
review_body:
I have tried multiple scanners over the last couple of years, and with all those I have tried under the $250 point, I have had issues with very slow scans, crashing while scanning, and incompatibility with my linux laptop.
The Doxie Go has a pretty decent scan rate, about 5-6 seconds to scan a page at 300dpi, the scans come out in great quality, and since the scanning is all handled inside the unit, there are no software incompatibility issues with the PC. The Doxie software is nice, but if it doesnt work on your pc, you can view the scanner like a camera and copy the files off, or use USB or SD card to scan to instead of the internal memory.

The only annoyances I have found, if you want to do a lot of scanning, like over 80 pages, and need to charge and scan at the same time, you have to buy a separate charger. Otherwise it charges off usb. Second, I sometimes have an issue feeding a page straight. it does not have a lot of a lead up with the tray. Not a huge deal as I just rescan the item if it is too bad. As I got through a few more and got more used to the best way to feed pages it became an issue less often.

Summary--
Pros:
-Quick, high quality scans
-No compatibility issues
Cons:
-Can be difficult to feed some pages straight
-have to buy separate power adapter to scan while charging

review_headline: promising design but fragile and lead jams frequently
review_body:
I like design, especially retractable point and the fine precise line well supported by sleeve so that it doesn't wobble.

However TWO FLAWS preventing me from giving it as a gift or recommending it wholeheartedly to others.

(1) It is FRAGILE: outside is metal but inside is brittle plastic, including the threads that hold it together.
DON'T put it in your pocket, purse, shoulder bag or brief. The pressure of items moving around can cause the plastic inner to snap - happened to us twice (2 out of the three pens we purchased for office and home use snapped in the first 30 days!).

(2) The frequently jams as it reaches the final 1/2 inch of the lead. By frequently, I mean at least once in every 5 leads. This has occurred with all three pencils we purchased. And once jammed, it is VERY DIFFICULT remove the jammed lead. It requires a wire or needs that is less than .3mm in diameter - this tool is not supplied by Pentel. You can use one strand of a breaded speaker wire.

I will continue to use it - but will handle it very carefully & transport it in a hard shell pencil case or eyeglass case (needs to be 7" long) Despite these two limits, when it works it performs better than any other .3mm mechanical pencil we have tested.

review_headline: I Passed Advanced Algebra Because Of These Tabs.
review_body:
So I've always struggled with organization, ever since i was old enough to put on my own shoes. I'm 17 not and I still have organization issues and it's gotten to the point where my lack of organization has prevented me from doing well in school (particularly math) because my notes are not organized.

I got the idea to do away with the typical spiral notebook and opt for a composition notebook. This way I'm not tearing out pages that i need for notes. Then these wonderful tabs come into play. I put them at the top of the page I'm writing on and write the subject on the tab. After weeks of note-taking the tabs add up and here is the magic: if I want to review a certain concept, I don't have to frantically flip though my spiral notebook! I can just look at the tabs that I've strategically placed on the edges to find the subject I want to review!! This may sound like a common sense idea to some but it has changed my life and the way I look at things!!

So as for the actual tabs: The colors are lovely, they don't smear after you've written on them (providing you wrote on the correct side, the more textured side), they are definitely sturdy, much more sturdy that post it notes. In my opinion it's definitely worth the money. Wish there were more in a pack! Quality Product.

product_title: Epson Expression XP-410 Wireless Color All-in-One Inkjet Printer
review_headline: Decent Printer, but Epson really needs to work on their "touchscreen"
review_body:
This printer follows the past couple years of Epson design, but adds a few new features to keep up with new devices and ways to print. I have to say that even though we've had a Chromebook for nearly 9 months, I never bothered to add a cloud printer until this printer. Similarly, having airprint and the ability for the printer to create its own ad-hoc network to other wi-fi devices pretty much ensures you'll be able to print from just about anything.

That said, the downfalls are typical for this price range. The paper feed extends upward from the back of the printer rather than being a tray that feeds from underneath. Also, the output has the pull-out style 3/4 page width tray. So the product picture differs somewhat from how it'll really look on your desk.

The touchscreen really isn't what we think of as a touchscreen these days. The full color portion of the screen is NOT touch sensitive. Instead, there are buttons to the sides of it that are touch sensitive. It's a bit like saying a microwave has a touchscreen - that's how similar they are.

Print quality is ok. Not outstanding but typical of most printers. Better paper yields better results. Scanning and copying is very easy, though I haven't been able to get it to recognize my home PC in order to scan directly over wi-fi, which is strange because my other Epsons do it with no problem.

Overall if you need a low cost all in one that can connect and print from a wide range of devices, this is worth looking at. review_body:
I always buy the Pilot G2 Gel Ink pens, and for good reason: they work great. They write smoothly and clearly. I only recently recently discovered that there are subtle differences among the numbers for these pens, however. For example, I usually buy the "07" version of the pen, but the last time I tried the "05" wondering what the difference was. Apparently, the lower the number, the finer the point of the pen.

For my uses, the "05" (Fine point) was just too small of a point; it was a bit more difficult to write with and the lines were obviously thinner. Therefore, I went back to the "07" (Medium point).

I generally don't use these too much in a given day so they tend to last me a while. However, for a more moderate user (someone who uses pens just about every day, but does not write too much at a time) they will last a shorter time. Of course, the best way to know for sure is to just try them out and see for yourself.

review_headline: This is one fantastic personal printer
review_body: IMO, the quality of this print is good enough to write important reports, proposals, presentations, offerings, etc. out in real life (business). It showed up here just in time for a run of 325 one page reports that I would normally do on my LaserJet4, so I added color and of course this was quite an improvement.  The first drawback I encountered is that the single paper tray only holds about 150 pieces of paper, so I had to reload twice. My LaserJet4 would have reliably printed all of them unattended while I ate breakfast, even after 25 straight years of light to moderate use. This LaserJet Pro is definitely a light use printer; do not expect a color version of the early HP LaserJets. This prevents it from being a good shared printer in an office. That being said, it works without problems, the output is spectacular, and the reliable wireless feature improves ease of use around here on our intranet. The contrast between these two printers when running is noticeable. The old LasterJet4 sounds solid like the industrial strength printer it is, while the LaserJet Pro sounds like plastic parts in motion. The bottom line for me was that I bought the Pro 200 for one 7th the cost of the LaserJet4 twenty-five years ago.

product_title: Ooma Telo Free Home Phone Service
review_body:
We purchased Ooma on Black Friday, November 2012 so it's been in service a little over six months. It worked fine until we had an electrical storm about ten days ago and afterward it wouldn't work - no power light from the unit to the router . I called customer service and they sent a replacement unit which arrived today and it seems to work fine now. I mention this because their customer service always has been helpful and responsive. I see a lot of complaints about Vonage customer service, for example. They programmed the unit especially for me. I just had to connect it snd plug it in. I don't think they used to do this for replacement units causing users to complain.

I've learned a couple of things about Ooma that might be helpful to prospective users. A good high speed broadband service is essential. If you don't have sufficient speed and bandwidth, calls may be dropped or simply not be transmitted at all or be sent to voice mail. A cat 5e or 6e ethernet cable seems to work better for connecting the Ooma unit to the router than does the cable that Ooma provides. These are essential - you may not be happy with the service, otherwise. It is still good to have a back-up line or cell phone available for emergency use during a power outage.

The best thing about Ooma is the cost savings. We save about $50-70 per month on our international long distance plus what a land line phone cost us. Basically Ooma costs us about $25 per month , including premium service, plus the initial one time cost of the unit.

I gave this four stars because I'm not certain of the quality of the Ooma unit since it had to be replaced so soon.

review_body:

Using only an old Sony digital recorder and this, we have several class-A recordings just from our first tries. I'd totally recommend this as a starter box for anyone! If we can do it, you can do it! (recorder recommendation: WS-600S Olympus)

UPDATE: Tried the modified Sangean, you can't modify the new ones so you have to find older modified units on sites like a certain auction site. The modified Sangean however, scans too slowly for me and you get a lot of 'trash' noise. We love the Spirit Box P-SB7 and I'm getting a ton of quality recordings from it. It works scanning both forwards and backwards, and I like the faster scan rate as you tend to get more reliable results instead of worrying that what you are hearing is actually something from a radio station. I've gotten a lot of multi-syllable replies, many 3-second replies, and lots of what I would classify as Class-A and B recordings. This box is so much fun and we get great results.

UPDATE II: With extensive testing on the Sangean, we now get 4 and 5 word replies (some sentences) with the Sangean. My only complaint is that trying to edit out all the background noise on the Sangean leaves tracks that are very faint and hard to hear. It's MUCH easier to edit out the background noise of the P-SB7 recordings and have something you can share and have others understand.

review_headline: good item if u want a standard wall phone
review_body:
I bought this for my 88 year old grandmom whom has hearing problems(so do i). My mom was complaining that she tries to call her and she doesnt hear the phone mainly because she has a hearing problem and both the other phones are in the other rooms and was unable to locate a wall phone to replace the modular phone jack that those old phones used to use.

First off the back of the phone says \\"Made in china\\" . When i ordered it this stated made in USA. Just so you know. Other than that that didnt bother me.

Secondly I had the phone on the loudest setting and it wasnt loud at all therefore my grandmom couldn't hear it ringing. I barely was able to hear it ringing. There was no buzzing sound like these other people claim either.

Thirdly the volume was okay it wasnt great however she was able to carry on a conversation with my mom.

One other thing the handset cord is extremely short. I owuld say no more than 12 inches long. Wasnt a problem for us but some other people might have an issue with it.

I had to remove this phone from the wall and re-install a regular cheap slimline type of fone which rings loudly. Mainly all you have to do is get a small telephone line that connects between the modular jack and the module in the back of the phone. Its available online or at most 99 cents stores.

Installing and uninstalling this phone was simple provided you have that old plate with a modular input between two screws or nails where the phone will mate with.

Youre best bet is to pay a little more and go to an online company that makes phones and devices for hard of hearing people. Its called Clarity.

I slso suggest you shop around for the best price on this phone or any other device.

review_body:
Don't buy. This machine will suck your wallet dry the same way it sucks ink from the cartridges. I know inkjet printers periodically go through a cleaning cycle to clean the heads but this machine is ridiculous!

I tried to get a simple answer from Brother Tec Support, Live Chat and finally a supervisor. I just wanted to know what the factory default setting was for the machine to cycle and clean the cartridge nozzle heads. I could not get the truth from any of them because I believe they know it was set to cycle way too often. Shame on Brother for making the machine clean itself when it wasn't necessary just to sell more ink. The firmware update seems to have helped but the ink is still disappearing and there is no way to adjust how often the machine automatically cleans the heads.

The print quality is not very good. I only paid $89.00 and I knew I wouldn't get the same quality I do from my Brother DCP 7020 laser printer but I have had less expensive inkjet printers with better results. The wireless was easy to set up and the fax and scan worked well but I paid more for cartridges than I did for the machine in the first year and I only used it a few times a month.

I love the Brother DCP 7020 but will never buy another Brother machine again because of the way I was treated by the Brother representatives.

product_title: AVantage Plastic AV Cart Adjustable from 16" to 42"
review_headline: Buyer beware and be careful when assembling
review_body:
This review is for the AVantage 4-in-1 Electrical AV cart. I chose this product after reading reports of problems assembling the Buhl AV cart, which has support posts made of extremely light plastic that will crack during assembly or use. It turns out, this model has the same weakness. I will offer a suggestion to others who buy this product or the Buhl cart. I believe some of the posts I received were damaged upon receipt, but I chose to use a different size post to assemble this product. Still I called The Library Store (from where I purchased this cart) and they offered to replace the cart, but after two calls I never received anything.

THE BAD:

The support posts (the variable length legs that allow you to configure the cart and shelf height) are the most fragile pieces of plastic you can imagine. The instructions suggest using a rubber mallet during assembly, but after reading reviews of the Buhl product, I decided to use the mallet as a last resort as it would surely crack the posts if too much force is applied. I carefully assembled the product knowing this, and when it was almost together, I had to use the mallet to level the top. The first light tap cracked the first post. Another post cracked at some point that I didn't even notice. So I took the posts out and tried another approach.

To get around having to mallet this thing, get yourself a can of silicone spray lubricant. Spray each post before seating them into the shelf. Turn each post as you apply pressure until the post is seated all the way. I used a generous amount of spray and each post went in - no mallet needed. Worked for me.

Once you have it together, you probably won't want to take advantage of the adjustable configurations, which require you to disassemble and reassemble using another size post. The posts were tough to get in - they will be tough to get out too. For this reason, the terms \\"adjustable\\" and \\"4-in-1\\" should be followed with \\"at your ownrisk\\".

THE REST:

Aside from the posts, the assembly is simple. I am now using this cart outside for occasional use (backyard movies) - so I am not too concerned that two of the posts have cracks. The cart is lighter than the metal ones I looked at, and I don't have to worry about rust (which is good since it is now outside use only). The shelves are solid and feel durable, but with its fragile posts you have to go easy on loading it up. (And I don't recommend doing stunts on this thing.) The attached electrical outlets work fine and make it easy to plug in three AV components. The casters are good quality, and two of them include locking pedals. All in all, this is a good product for occasional use but I would look for a more solid unit for regular office use.

product_title: Ooma 100-0301-101 Telo Wireless Adaptor
review_headline: Unstable, Poor Call Quality Using Wireless
review_body:
I purchased the Ooma Telo unit two months ago and with the many problems I was having, I thought I would have to return the unit until I realized the problem was with the wireless adaptor.

First of all, the setup was a breeze. I easily connected to my wireless router and verified that I had a strong connection. I activated the Telo base unit and I was off and running. The problems then started immediately. I noticed frequently that the Telo unit was flashing red and had lost connection with the server. Call quality was atrocious. There was a severe artifact and echo in the speech coming across the line. The worst part was that there was a 2-3 second delay in the audio so that the caller and I were constantly talking over each other and eventually would have to hang up and use the cell phone. I tried moving the Ooma unit to try to improve the signal, but there was no improvement to my problem.

Conclusion: I installed the Ooma Telo base between my modem and router and now the service works perfect. If you can avoid using this wireless adapter and instead install using an ethernet cable connected to your modem or router, I highly recommend it. This 1-star review reflects my feelings about the adaptor only, not the Telo unit or Ooma service.

I have seen many people complain that they installed a new toner cartridge only to be told that there is still no toner in the machine, and Brother support will only give out the steps to manually reset the toner if you can prove to them that you have just bought a new Brother toner cartridge. If you run into this issue, here are the steps to manually reset the toner:

Open the front cover of the printer
Press and release the \\"clear\\" key
Press \\"start\\", then press the up arrow until you see the number 12 on the display
Press \\"ok\\", you will see \\"accepted\\" on the display
Close the front cover, your toner cartridge should now work

product_title: Philips LFH9380/27 Rechargeable Pocket Memo Digital Diction Recorder with Slide-Switch Operation and SpeechExec
review_headline: Good machine but would be better with a tutorial
review_body:
Good dictation machine. I use this primarily for dictating letters, notes and pleadings in a legal office. It works about the same as an old cassette tape dictaphone that I still have as backup. Our office is transitioning to the fully networkable electronic version. The big advantage here obviously that it is completely electronic and networkable. We set the storage file to a Dropbox file in the cloud and I can be anywhere and I plug the machine in and it is saved where my assistant can get it immediately. Because it is saved in a. Common file I can tell when the dictation is pending. In progress or done.
It is not without its quirks but with a little Experience you will learn how to make it work for you. The machine must be set up properly and the default is pretty close to what I need. There are modes that will start a new file every time the slide switch is switched from pause to record. And there are alternatives on how the slide switch is set up. What is lacking is a good tutorial. I would love to see. Little video on what all the options are and how they can be adjusted to fit my particular needs. There is an online help file but this doesn't really help as much as it should.

product_title: Optoma WXGA, Mobile LED Projector
review_headline: Do Not Buy for Conferences/Business Meetings
review_body:
Before I start my review allow me to disclose a few items first. I work in the Audio Visual industry and I service a wide variety of events, mostly corporate business but I also service social events as well. I work for a large global company so I did not have to pay for any of the equipment I use on a daily basis. The equipment that people rent from my company is on the high-end side of the spectrum and the clients pay a proportionate rental fee to rent said equipment for their events. I do not work for any projector manufacturers nor do I work for the companies that sell them.

If you're a meeting planner or if you are the meeting facilitator looking to purchase this projector for trainings or meetings, this review is for you.

Basically, don't waste your money.

I am compelled to write this review because I came across this projector today and I was shocked at just how awful it was, even more so after the client informed that this projector was NEW. The client rented accessories from my company but chose to provide their own projector because of cost and once the Optoma ML500 projector was set up and ready to go they asked for assistance from me because it was so dim. Turning out the lights in the meeting room helped but they weren't sold on having the room so dark for their presentation.

They also tried to make the image bigger by using the Zoom feature on the remote, which the remote didn't work so we used the buttons on the projector to navigate. The Zoom feature isn't a true zoom, there is no button or slider to make the image bigger or smaller, you have to physically move the projector to make the image larger or smaller, the zoom the guy was using was just zooming in on the image which is not useful at all.

How dim the projector was, for being new, was shocking until I read that it was 500 Lumens. 500 Lumens under fluorescent or can lighting equals a total wash-out which means you are not going to be ableto see the projected image no matter the colors of your Powerpoint. (His Powerpoint background was white and accented with a bright blue and orange, all good colors for a presentation as long as the projector has a good lamp). So this projector is useless under ANY kind of light. The room this group was in didn't have windows, just artificial light.

I understand this review is vague, only addressing two main problems, but it's geared more towards meeting planners or persons who are purchasing this for meetings or trainings. One of the most important aspects of a projector is the zoom and the brightness and this projector has neither. Your attendees will not be able to see the screen unless the room is pitch black and if they have to take notes? Forget about it. The fact that there's no zoom means the projector could be positioned a mile away from the screen in order for it to fill in a standard six foot screen which equals needing a longer VGA to reach the front of the room or you're sitting in the back behind your class.

Whatever the cost of the Optoma ML500 is, save it and buy a projector that is 2,000-3,000 Lumens MINIMUM. Yes, a larger-lumen projector will be bigger and more clunky to travel with (perhaps ship it ahead of time?) but your attendees, customers, business partners will be able to see what you're actually presenting. I'm not going to lie, when people show up with crappy, dim projectors that no one can see and it can't fill up a screen even when you move the unit to compensate, it can send a negative message.

I hope you found this review helpful. Again, I don't work for any equipment manufacturers, I've had my hands on many brands of projectors and notice I didn't endorse a single one here, I felt compelled to write this review after seeing in the flesh how terrible this projector is, $700 for 500 Lumen is a complete rip off.

review_headline: Great Product But Keep Away From Kids!
review_body: We recently purchased the MC14MX and are very happy with this product.  It does everything it promised. The micro-cut shredder is far superior in doing this than the traditional cross-cut shredders.  If you receive bank statements in the mail, then you should be concerned as well about this.  The MC14MX does an excellent job and the easily removable lower compartment makes it a quick snap to take the \\"confetti\\" to the trash can.  The wheels make it very easy to move.  No shredder is silent but the MC14MX will not have people around you running for ear plugs.  I cannot tell you how impressed I am with this product.  However, it's lacking in one important feature.  Since it does its job so well, this is not a safe product to have around kids especially toddlers.  There is no finger guard as there is with other shredders.  I just don't understand that.  If I am harping on this, it's because I called the manufacturer and was told by them that this model had a finger guard.  Since our young grandkids occasionally visit us, we have to keep the shredder in a closet when they come.  We're also purchasing the Plug Lok! - Safety 1st product which is available on Amazon to keep them from being able to plug it into an outlet in case they find it in the closet.  We believe in keeping track of what the kids are doing but little ones can get into trouble so quickly even if you just turn your back for a second.

product_title: Epson WorkForce Pro WP-4020 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer (C11CB30201)
review_headline: Not a bad inkjet printer, but don't believe the high print volume hype.
review_body:
It seems the high page yield Epson is flaunting with this printer is mostly a gimmick. Unless you aren't buying it for the laserjet comparable yields, or can get by with very faded printing (even from greyscale) in the printer's economy mode, stick with laserjet.

I've been using an HP laserjet for years. And while it's held up well, and been pretty reliable, $80 per cartridge (full SRP is actually at or over $100 depending on who you ask) was just rediculous. I'd tried recycled cartridges, but what you're saving in cost, they more than make up for by not putting nearly as much ink in the cartridge. I only got about 150 good pages from the last replacement cartridge I bought. So, when I saw an inkjet advertising the same print yield as my laserjet, but with original manufacturer cartridges that cost about the same as the recycled cartridges I've bought, I was intrigued.

I commenced reading reviews, both user and \\"professional\\", though the term \\"professional\\" should be used very lightly these days, as it seems most \\"professional\\" reviews have devolved into little more than product publicity for the manufacturer, evaluations based on specs rather than actual experience with and testing of the product. Aside from your typical bad units seeming a bit overly represented in user reviews - which is common online, if not understandable that a disproportionate number of people with problems would feel compelled to go through the trouble of writing a review, compared to those finding the unit to perform to their expectations - I found the reviews at the time to be convincingly positive. Enough so that I figured I'd give it a try, afterall, the entire printer cost only a little more than one of the four cartridges I needed for my HP.

I have no extensive expertise with printers: my experience is mostly limited to the dozen or so models I've personally owned over the years. I've only printed about 50 pages with this Epson thus far as well, which is hardly a test of the build's reliability or even the ink capacity of the starter cartridges it comes with. BTW, if you don't already know, the starter cartridges included with this printer are estimated at only 1000 pages for black and white, not the 2400 (black and white) or 1200 (color) pages the standard XL cartridges are supposed to be capable of. I'm still on the starter cartridges.

I should also qualify this by saying that I'm going on the assumption that the 2400 yield number being so aggressively advertised only applies to printing in greyscale, in fast, economy mode, not normal mode, which is probably closer to the quality most might expect. I couldn't find any clarification in the literature either, what little there is. Remember when printers used to come with 1/2 inch thick books telling you everything you actually needed to know?

Text in fast economy, greyscale mode is very faded. Rather than black, it's a medium gray that looks about like a laserjet on an empty cartridge, or more precisely, like when I keep printing with the laserjet, well past the point it says to change the cartridge, because my replacement was bad or out of stock and recycled cartridges aren't very good about warning you ahead of time when they're about empty.

The Epson's normal mode is what I'd reasonably expect of economy inkjet printing, based on other inkjets I've owned. So, it seems Epson didn't reinvent the wheel, nor are the XL ink cartridges the reason for them being able to tweak the numbers for inkjet to be in line with your lower end laserjets in terms of print capacity. It seems they're just using a lot less ink, which really shows in the quality of the print job. I tried printing a couple coupons off the internet in economy mode; they were so faded, all but the barcode was illegible. Generally, text is dark enough to read, if the font isn't too small or thin. And I don't think it's too light for shipping labels, but Ihaven't confirmed with the USPS that their scanners can pick up the barcode or not. Based on the intensity of black, I'd assume if printing in something more realistic, like normal mode, you'd need to half your page expectations. This is probably not the best printer for photographs, though the high quality setting does look reasonably good from what I've seen of it's handling some simple graphics.

The printer is extremely fast, at least spitting out the pages themselves is; preping the print seems to take just as long as most others. I also expect the print jobs use less energy than any laserjet, and assuming you don't turn off the printer when not in use, I suspect it uses less energy in standby too, as it doesn't run automated checks every so often like my HP.

I'm not too thrilled about having to get a special device to be able to reprogram the ink cartridges just to be able to use all the ink you're paying for. But, if I didn't consider printers solely on the grounds of unwanted or unnecessary design constraints, there wouldn't be any to choose from.

BTW, these cartridges also expire and Epson recommends replacement after 6 months, whether they're depleted or not, for best print quality anyway.haven't confirmed with the USPS that their scanners can pick up the barcode or not. I'm bothering to write a review because we recently changed modems and our network name and password changed. Everything, including the printer, had to be reconnected to the wireless network using the new information. Trying to get the Brother printer to find the network was a long and painful process.

Here's what I learned:

1) The key element is to re-set the printer to the factory defaults, as described in the Quick Setup Guide.
2) Go ahead and delete the printer that's already installed, since the re-set installs the drivers all over again and will name it Copy 1. Then you'll have to select Copy 1 to print from.
3) Follow the directions to set up the printer as if it's a new install, including inserting the driver disk.
4) There is no separate process for changing the SSID network name or inserting the new password--at least, none I have discovered at my level of computer (in)competence.
5) I never needed to use the new password, because the printer went and found the new network and connected to it once I followed the setup instructions exactly.

Remember: re-set to the factory defaults before trying to connect to the new network.

The printer has 4 or 5 tiny spring contact wires reaching upwards on the right side (viewing the front of the printer) designed to contact the corresponding gold plated pads on a 0.3" x 1.2" printed circuit board glued into a cavity molded into the bottom of the cartridge. Reliable connection depends on the thickness of the adhesive keeping this tiny board in place. Removing this little board and re-installing it with an additional thickness of a double sided tape on its bottom corrected the problem. product_title: Fellowes Powershred 99Ms 14-Sheet Micro-Cut Heavy Duty Paper Shredder with Auto Reverse (4609001)
review_body:
I wonder if Oliver North had a shredder this capable? In all seriousness though, this is the best shredder that I have ever personally encountered. It can shred 12 sheets of paper at a time, and reduce them to micro-cut pieces of 2 x 14 millimeters each. It can shred paper, credit cards, and staples. However, it is not recommended to shred adhesive labels, transparencies, newspaper, cardboard, continuous form paper, paper clips, CD's, DVD's, laminates, file folders, X-rays, or any plastic other than a credit card.

What is amazing to me is how quiet this shredder is. I have used it with my toddler napping in the next room, and she doesn't flinch. It doesn't scare my cats either. I tested the SafeSense Technology, simply by gliding a finger across the paper entry port. The shredder immediately stopped. This shredder has a 9 gallon bin, so frequent emptying will probably not be necessary for most users. It came with a few sample trash bags, but I am currently using just a standard kitchen trash bag. It also comes with a small sample size bottle of Fellowes shredder oil. To keep any shredder running at optimal efficiency, it is crucial to oil it on a regular basis. The sample bottle of oil is enough for a couple of uses, but after that I highly recommended purchasing the reasonably priced [[ASIN:B00006I58N Fellowes Shredder Oil, 12 oz. Bottle with Extension Nozzle (35250)]]. The manual recommends lubricating each time you empty the bin.

I was surprised at how large this shredder is. I am not sure of the exact weight, but the shipping weight (with the packing materials) was 55 pounds. By my measurements (with the casters attached) the shredder is 25.5\\" high, 17\\" deep, and 11\\" wide. Honestly, this level of shredder is probably overkill for most average home users, but it would be ideal for many businesses.

As a final note, when I opened up the box, I could not find the owner's manual anywhere. I assumed that the manufacturer forgot to include it. But after I shredded a big pile of papers, I opened up the waste bin to see the progress. Much to my chagrin, I found the owner's manual, sample trash bags, and sample oil half buried under a pile of paper shreds.

This product does not work as well as a regular landline (POTS). SKIP THE WIRELESS ADAPTER!

1. PRICE. I am not sure the total price of switching the telephone line for $40, the premier service ($120 but no $40 switch fee), etc. is worth it. If it lasts a long time, I guess it will be less expensive, but I will have to wait a long time to break even. At this point, I have $250 bucks invested- It will have to work about 1.5-2 years to break even. The time it takes to work on this and set it up adds to the cost.

2. SETUP. Setup is not that hard, but this is a complicated system. Ooma Telo requires you to connect an ethernet cable to the device to made changes and set up Ooma Telo via a computer, which is not included with the product and is a hassle to set up. If you lack a portable computer, I would not buy Ooma with Wireless adapter.

3. QUALITY. We had many complaints about call quality. I called Ooma and they told me they did an adjustment on my device, but that did not completely fix the problem. They said my wireless adapter was working fine, despite the problems. Do not use OOMA for your business, especially if it is not connected via a ETHERNET cable to your Router.

4. MY SOLUTION. I replaced the Wireless Adapter with a WIFI EXTENDER and an Ethernet cable directly to Ooma. Since my Wifi Extender works much faster than the Ooma Wireless Adapter, the sound quality is much better. However, it takes a while for the Ooma to get going, so there are weird sounds on the line in the beginning of calls.

product_title: Smead Organizer File Folder, 1/3-Cut Tab, Letter Size, Assorted Colors, 3 per Pack (85785)
review_body:
This product fills a need when more than a single folder is required but less than a large accordion file. I have a couple of small projects that generate lots of receipts and keeping them organized, for tax purposes, is quickly becoming a problem. This small group of attached folders appeared to be the perfect solution.

Open on three sides, to avoid small receipts from sliding/falling out, I find it necessary to keep the organizer in a drawer or file box, rather than on my desk, as I'd planned.

The quality of the paper seems lighter than a normal file folder. And, although I understand the thinking behind having two, one inch holes in the body of the files so the contents may be viewed, and an empty file quickly identified, for this particular item, there are only a few individual sections, so the holes seem unnecessary. No one should be endlessly paging through, searching for an empty folder. Small thing, but the holes contributed to the already flimsy feeling of the organizer.

The product information claims the files will expand to three-quarters of an inch, but I think that would unduly strain the integrity of the folder, so I would plan on less than that - perhaps one-quarter to one-half inch per section. Again, because of the light-weight feel of the organizer, the instinct is to treat it more carefully to avoid a tear or split - another reason to avoid over-filling.

Personal taste, but I find the colors muted yet attractive. The idea of the organizer is appealing, and this design is almost perfect for my needs, but it would have been more useful if the sides were enclosed about half way up so the contents of the folders wouldn't easily fall out. Happiness with the product will clearly rest with its intended use.

product_title: Swingline Auto Feed Paper Shredder, 60 Sheets, Cross-Cut, 1 User, Stack-and-Shred 60X, Black (1757572)
review_body:
I've been using this shredder for several months and it has not jammed once. I use it to shred old bills, financial statements and insurance documents for the most part. I stack them in a folder and when I get a big enough stack I load them into the Swingline. With my old shredder I had to hover over it, feeding in 2-3 sheets at a time, which was a hassle when I had several papers to shred.

I've loaded it with as many as 30 pages at once. It rips through staples with no issue and the pages do not need to be 100% flat, as all of mine were creased at some point. product_title: OBi202 2-Port VoIP Phone Adapter with Google Voice and Fax Support for Home and SOHO Phone Service
review_headline: Obi202 and Google Voice Work Great. I wish I would have dumped the cable company long ago.
review_body:
This is actually a review of both the Obi202 and Google Voice and how they work together. I have been using this for about 3 months for my home phone. I used it for a few weeks with a test number prior to porting my home phone.

I have had the same home phone number for almost 25 years so I was not in a rush to port my number and I definately do not want to lose the number. So I set up a secondary number using Google Voice to test the Obi and Google voice. I made quite a few calls over the course of a few weeks and was very happy with the call quality. Porting my home phone number to Google voice took longer than I expected but my home phone worked throughout most of the entire process. It took two weeks to port my home phone from Charter to T-Mobile. (I borrowed a T-Mobile phone and bought a prepaid card.) It took 23 hours and 43 minutes to port the number from T-Mobile to Google Voice. Cost $10 for T-Mobile prepaid card, $20 to Google Voice to port.

Pros:
1) Good Call quality
2) Easy set up
3) Easy to hook into house wiring
4) I love Google voice and the ability to block calls
5) International calls are Cheap ($.02 a minute to Hong Kong)

Cons:
1) Time consuming to port a home phone number
2) Ring sounds weird ( I tried different setting and gave up without spending much time on it because it is not that important to me.)
3) Google Voice caller ID shows number only not name
4) 911 Service has to be purchased from a 3rd party
5) The OBiON app worked with a iPod touch on our home network but did not work with an android device on the road.

Technical knowledge required: Similiar to setting up a wireless router.

review_body:
I've been using Epson printers for years now, and I've found them highly reliable and very user friendly, and this Work Force 3520 is no exception.

~Set up~
For the most part, this is the most complicated process for most people, since setting up a wireless printer for the first time can seem confusing. However it's actually very easy when following the step by step set-up guide included in box. When first installing this printer, there are more steps than when you install the software on each additional printer. You set up the network connection only once, then you just add additional computer from which to print from. So even if you have 5 computers in different rooms in your house, they can all be set up to wirelessly print from this same one printer.

The trickiest part is usually hooking the printer up to your wireless connection. If you have a password set up on your network (your wireless signal in your home from your router) take note when logging this Epson into it of whether or not you are typing the letters in capitalized or not. My Epson defaults to all capitalized letters and my network password is all lower case. Something as small as this can keep your printer from accessing your network. However, once connected, my printer has never once dropped the signal, and always stays connected to my network.

~Printing and ink~
Printing has always worked perfectly from my Epson 3520. It has all the typical settings for changing how much ink you use each time you print. As others have mentioned, the ink does go fast, but I've found it goes through ink at about the same speed as any other printer I've owned. The reason the Epson seems to go through in faster is because Epson offers more budget friendly ink cartridges, which have less ink, but also cost less. To prevent running out as often, I order the High Capacity ink cartridges that are made for this printer. They cost more, but also last a lot longer. The reverse printing feature works well, and I haven't had any issues with the feeder eating any of my papers when it's pulling the paper back inside.

~Scanning~
Wireless scanning seems to baffles a lot of users, and I can understand why. For years people scanned by going to the printer/scanner, opening up the lid, placing the paper inside and pressing scan. When scanning wirelessly, it doesn't work this way any more, because you can have multiple computers set up to one printer. The Epson doesn't know what computer it's supposed to be scanning the document to. Instead, now what you do it go to the computer you want the document scanned to, open the Epson Scan program and launch it. At this time you will have scan options for previewing the document and sizing it and such. Then you press a scan button on your screen, and it sends the signal to the Epson to begin scanning the item/document in the printer. After it's scanned, the image is then sent wirelessly to your computer and saved into a file. This sort of backwards scanning can be confusing if you're use to just pressing a scan button on the printer, but it's actually very easy to do. I scan constantly with this printer, and have had no problems with any dropped signals or anything like that.

~Copying~
No need to even us the computer for coping. It works just like a copy machine. Just place the paper in the scanner, press copy and chose black and white or color. There are a ton of other options as well, should you want to tweak the image of what your coping. You can lighten, darken, enlarge, make smaller, set to double sided, and change how many copies you want of a single page. All the features of a full sized scanner are included in this printer.

~Faxing~
Just place the papers in the feeder and dial the number you want to fax the papers to. It has features like redial and a conformation screen to let you know if your fax was successfully sent. The pages feed in on their own, andthe Epson can tell when you've set papers into the fax feeder and begins the faxing program. Every time I've used the fax feature, it's worked without any issues.

~Conclusion~
The printer can be set up both wirelessly or with a regular wires in connection. Once set up, I've never had to really think about it again. It just works. It prints everything I've needed and buying the high capacity ink cartridges keeps me from running out very often. I scan constantly and once you've gotten use to how the wireless scanning works, it's pretty darn easy to do. Coping is effortless. Just the press of a button. OVERVIEW:
------------

This phone and its 2 cordless handset equivalent (KX-TG6672) are at a value sweet spot among cordless phones with great features. We've had ours over 2 years without issue and I highly recommend it.

PROS:
------

In order of importance to me:

- (1) Has HEADPHONE PORT (2.5mm) on each handset like most Panasonic cordless handsets, and the sound quality using the port is excellent. I use a quality comfy 2-ear headset (I use a Turtle Beach one for this) for long or important calls.

- (3) The SPEAKERPHONES are loud enough and fairly high quality for a home phone unit. Certainly not office conference speakerphone top quality but again very good for a home unit.

- (5) DECT 6.0 for best privacy/security and least interference (DECT 6.0 is rather commonplace these days, not the stand out feature it used to be).

SUGGESTIONS:
---------------

- Test yours out in-depth soon after arrival so you can exchange it easily if you get a lemon. Talk to someone on a good land line phone from the base unit and from the cordless handsets, test the speakerphones, test out the answer machine even if you won't use it right away, etc.hich we did.

product_title: Canon PIXMA MG8220 Wireless Inkjet Photo All-In-One Printer (5293B002)
review_body:
This printer is a beast when it comes to features. We love it because it wirelessly connects to our home network. It produces excellent photographs. It is quiet and relatively fast. It's unique touch buttons on top take some getting used to. The buttons you need will only light up when you need them. After a few months it's transparent to us. The very small capacity paper tray is frustrating if you're doing a lot of document printing. Since we don't, it's not a deal-breaker for us. However, I could see how a student that's always doing papers would get frustrated at always having to refill the paper tray. We use the rear tray for photo paper and just put more back there when it gets low. However, the printer will sometimes pull from the rear tray based on its settings. So we have to watch out for that or we'll end up with a web clip (i.e. a coupon from a screen capture) on photo paper instead of plain paper. If it prints an image of any kind it will pull the photo paper. So just remember to change your paper source before printing.

As for ink it drains it quickly. Whether it's photos or documents it flies through ink. I recommend printing documents at a fast ink or draft setting to minimize use there. But photos will still pull ink quickly and rightly so because they're good photos. Once the warranty expires we'll probably switch to a refillable system that costs half as much (almost $70 for all the Canon ink this thing needs and that lasts us just a few months with light printing).

Here's the bottom line: photo quality great; ink usage high; paper capcity low; network connectivity great; speed is fast; it's quiet.

product_title: HP Deskjet 1000 Printer (CH340A#B1H)
review_body:
Pros:
-Inexpensive Printer
-Easy to set-up
-Relatively high quality printed image for price

Cons:
-Ink is expensive
-No wireless capability
-Doesn't come with a printer cable

This is a good printer for someone like me: someone who doesn't print often, but needs an inexpensive, reliable printer next to my computer for those few times when I do need to print. I bought this printer about 3 weeks ago on Amazon, it was delivered fast and well-packaged (as is usual for Amazon). I have printed about 15-20 pages since I've had it, all black and white. The image quality is good for my purposes.

I did initially have a problem with the set-up, but determined that the problem was a bad printer cable. This printer doesn't come with one: if you have one you know works, you'll probably be fine. I bought a cheap one from Amazon, which was faulty, but I returned it to the seller and got a full refund. A new (much more expensive) printer cable from Radio Shack solved the problem immediately.

To address some issues I've read about in other reviews: I've never heard my printer \\"self-clean\\" in the middle of the night or anytime for that matter. Mine has a \\"stand-by mode\\" that it goes to after about 5 minutes, and then shuts all the way off after an hour or two. I have to physically turn it back on if I want to print something (which is fine by me... as I said I don't print often). I just checked the ink levels and the reviews are right: Ink is used pretty quickly. I show about 10-15% used from the original black ink cartridge, but the color cartridge is 100% full. I have purchased a high capacity black ink cartridge from Amazon, it was about $25 (which is almost as much as this printer cost). I expect I'll get about 100 pages with the printer cartridge that came with the printer and hopefully 200-300 with the higher capacity cartridge. If so, that will likely get me through about a year or so. I hopeto not have to replace the color cartridge in that year.

Bottom line: This printer would be a good choice for someone who occasionally prints, and doesn't mind turning the printer on each time and can put it near their computer (no wireless). If you've got a printer that just died and already have a printer cable, and the above describes you, I'd recommend this printer. If you print a lot, you should probably spend more on a printer to find one with less expensive ink cartridges. I'll update this review with any pertinent updates.
