review_body:
I purchased this Epson in hopes that it could accomplish two things for me: Print decent quality prints and scan multiple page documents. I must say, it does both better than I expected!

I am a professional photographer and also a licensed Realtor. I wanted to be able to print decent quality 8X10's and 11X14's (or larger) at my home on the wedding day in order to have something to display at the wedding reception that night. I spent about 15-20 minutes configuring the printer and setting the contrast and color I wanted in order to match my already configured IPS monitor. From some of the other reviews, I was expecting OK prints, but I was surprised and very happy with the results. Images were sharp, clear and great quality! I printed 3 13X19 prints the night I setup the printer and several 8X10's and all of them have been very nice and clear. They aren't quite as nice as some of the pro labs I send my high end work to, but I am completely satisfied with the clarity and quality of the images. Setup correctly, I think the quality reflects professional work. I have only printed with Gloss paper (not my personal favorite, just what was available at the local office store) but I have ordered some lustre and matte paper to try and I will update my review with those results. So far I'm very happy with the quality for Gloss.

As for scanning it works great. Wireless network scanning is nice because I use every one of my USB ports on my machine and am happy that I do not need to add another device. It scans a 10-15 page contracts relitively fast at 300dpi and I like that I am able to save them as a PDF right from the scanner. That saves me time having to convert them later.

All in all, I'm very happy with this printer so far. I love the image quality of the photo prints and I'm happy that the scanner works so well through the network.

product_title: Fisher Space Pen Bullet Chrome Finish, Gift Boxed
review_body:
I truly love this pen as much I can love something that I can buy with a credit card.

I started using Fisher’s Space-Pens since 1998. Once, when in an airport (outside US) in line waiting for immigration, I had to fill a very lengthy form and we all were using the walls as support; there we learned that the normal pens will work for some time, and then the ink will stop flowing. Later, on the same trip, we went to the Science Museum and I found the Fisher pen and I bought the Zero Gravity and fell in love with the technology.

The design is such that is very short when closed but long as a standard pen when in use, and as the “weighty” part is closer to the writing tip and full metal construction; the balance is very nice (IMHO).

I carried it in my pocket with my wallet. When I leave home, I pick up the wallet, keys and my Fisher Pen.

This is my fifth one, because I gave away my previous ones to friends. I don’t think will give up this one though, the first ones were of a better quality (IMHO), I notice roughness at the tips of the pen I got that I didn’t with my first ones, they used to be smooth. Not a deal breaker.

The chrome model is much more durable that the other finishes and is the only ones I currently use, after discarding the bronze finished one after the bronze finish flaked (after one year of pocket carrying) and some rust started to shown up.

Do not over tight the pen after replacing the cartridge and change the O-rings (there are two) every three years or so, cap the pen but do not exaggerate, the O-ring will keep the cap secure, and you will have a companion for life (provided they will continue manufacturing the cartridge).

I also use Fisher cartridges in my “non-Fisher” pens as my Rotring and Sheaffer.

The cartridge is not as smooth writing as my fountain pen (that I use daily) nor as a gel or roller ball; but will not run or leak, will ever work, the ink cartridge will last longer and most important for me, I always have it with me when I’m out of the house.

product_title: Brother MFC9325CW Wireless Color Printer with Scanner, Copier & Fax
review_body:
Printer was easy to set up for network operation and occupies a portion of a kitchen counter (the most used part of the house). I had both wired and wireless network connections available but chose wireless because it is immune from lightning induced surges that appear on long runs of internet cable and did not appear to slow the printing operation.

The big surprise was the scan function which automatically sent the scanned image (PDF) to the appropriate computer (the one that the printer software was installed from) without the necessity of running an app for that purpose. A notification chime sounded and the image was available for whatever in the scanned images folder.

The only feature the printer lacked was duplex printing which I find really useful for saving paper or printing small books like user manuals.

The color prints are very acceptable and print as fast as monochrome. I printed a 175 page book that I was editing, complete with lots of color images and was amazed how fast the pages streamed out.

Finally, the Brother printers I have had seem (based on very limited experience over the years) more reliable and longer lived than Epson, Canon or HP (which all make decent products.)

I know it's not a woman's place to offer suggestions, but if you guys added a spoon attachment to these pens, it would be the greatest thing since sliced bread (which, incidentally, comes in much more handy now that I make my boyfriend so many sandwiches)!

The only downside I can see is that the ink is black. That color is dark and harsh on my feeble lady-eyes, and it frightens me. Please, BIC, make these pens with a softer color ink. Lilac would be nice!

product_title: AT&T TR1909 Trimline Corded Phone with Caller ID
review_body:
I bought this phone at a local store. I was looking for a basic landline phone that was inexpensive and this one seemed to be a good choice. Overall I am satisfied with this phone and my purchase. The phone has a lot of features. It requires 4 batteries to make full use of the memories and added features visible through the LCD window. The instructions suggest replacing the batteries every 6 months so numbers stored in memory wont be lost. The batteries also add weight to the phone cradle. The LCD window is difficult to read unless you are in bright light. The line coil between the handset and the cradle is short as is the line between the cradle and the phone jack. For these reason the phone seems designed primarily to function attached to a wall. It will work as a desk phone though. Both line cords are replaceable and a person can purchase longer cords.

The sound quality is very good, voices are loud and clear and the volume can be adjusted on both the ringer and the phone itself. This is a fine phone and a good buy at this price. It is similar to other phones such as RCA and Uniden available at this price point. When I was shopping I debatted whether to get this phone or a Uniden, they were close in price and features. This phone is made in China for AT+T.

review_headline: wount open use a rubber mallet
review_body: This recession applies to all sentry safes with an electronic lock and a separate handle to open it.  After 3 years of usage the safe refused to open sporadically. Even punching in the right combination using fresh batteries, the handle to open the door could not be pushed down. Sometimes it opened, sometimes not.  Sentry customer support knows about the problem and provided the following instruction to solve the issue:  \\"Try the following if this doesn't work it might be necessary to drill open the unit:  If the safe still does not allow entry, but hears a click - if the safe is not bolted down, I have the customer tip the safe on its back and leave for 12-24 hours. This allows all the air pressure built up in the gasket to release. With the safe on its back, lift up on the handle as if the safe were upright, enter the code, and bring the handle down.  If you can't hear the click after trying lift/push or if after laying the safe on its back didn't allow entry, lift the handle up and give 5 quick, firm taps to the right of the keypad on the door with a rubber mallet. After tapping, keep the handle up, push in on the door, enter the code, then bring the handle down. This should allow entry.\\"    Unfortunately this is not a joke. I followed the instruction and the door opened indeed. Luckily I did not mount the safe to the floor so I could turn it.  I looked into the door from inside and was amazed by the cheap and bad quality I saw. The locks of all Sentry safes with an electronic look have a general design issue, that results in clogging the electronic lock after some years of usage.    There are groups who talk about the issue:  idoneitmyself.wordpress.com/2010/05/07/opening-a-sentry-safe-with-a-rubber-mallet-some-wd-40-and-a-screwdriver/  [...]    My Advise:  Stay away from this type of safe. It looks like for a real safe some more money must be invested. It does not help at all to lock away your belongings like passports and documents, if you have no access to itany more.

review_headline: Warning - Misleading Product Name- Not the Same
review_body:
This is NOT the same ink used in the \\"Sharpie\\" ultra fine point permanent marker.
Sharpie Permanent Marker ink is waterPROOF and highlighter PROOF.
Permanent Marker ink *does* bleed through paper.

The Sharpie *pen* ink is merely water RESISTANT and highlighter RESISTANT
i.e. just another fiber tipped pen, only slightly better than a Pilot Bravo or a Flair.
It does not bleed through paper,
but it lacks most of the properties that make a Sharpie *Permanent Marker* useful in the first place.

Marketing these under the \\"Sharpie\\" brand name is misleading.
They are not the same product.

The packaging and the re-use of a known, established product name makes it difficult
to determine what the newer product does or does not do.

It has now stopped because it believes it is out of toner after just printing 40 clear and crisp pages without any indication that there is any problem with toner other than an inaccurate low toner message which I had been receiving within a few days of setting it up and proceeded to ignore as it was printing beautifully and was until this afternoon. That's between 750 to 900 pages from the cartridge and it is still printng fine until it stopped.

This is clearly a Brother scam as the machine does not need toner as it just printed 40 pages beautifully. It has been telling me it is low on toner for several weeks. As I recall it was within five days of setting up that I was getting this message. I will contact Brother service and if I don't get satisfaction I'm returning it because of the \\"out of toner\\" scam on these new machines. review_body:
As with many other people, I bought this for my Pilot G2 pen. I got the G2 about a week before and was very impressed with the writing style of the pen with the stock insert, and was highly anticipating an even more impressive writing experience with the Mont Blanc insert.

Got the insert, trimmed the rubber stopper on the back and plopped it into my G2 with no issue.

Started writing. Right off the bat, I had to do the \\"Swirly\\" thing to get the head unstuck. And even still it skipped. After a few minutes of troubleshooting, it finally started flowing smoothly.

However, the writing experience feels grainy compared to the G2 Gel insert that was in there before, which was smooth and felt like you were writing on a cloud. Side-by-side the clear winner was the G2 insert in overall smoothness and reliability.

A week or two went by and I was still using the MB insert just to see if it got better over time. It was okay for a few days. The ink doesn't smear and it looks fine, but it skips every now and again.

There's a reason why the inserts are cheap, and the pen bodies are spendy. All the work Mont Blanc did went into engineering their fountain pens and pen bodies, not the cheap rollerballs. In the end; just use the G2 inserts with your G2; they write better overall.

product_title: Canon Lasers Color imageCLASS MF8380Cdw Wireless Color Printer with Scanner, Copier and Fax (5120B001AA)
review_headline: Easy set up, Fast print speed, decent color image
review_body:
I must admit that I got spoiled with the big color copier at work. It's a $25k Canon ImageRunner C3220. Although it's 6 yrs old, the print image is almost as real as the original. Obviously, when I was shopping for a home copier, I was a bit disappointed. The print quality generated was nowhere near a $25k copier can produce. I know I need to lower my expectation.

Primarily I was comparing between 3 models : HP LaserJet Pro 200 (m276nw) $250, LaserJet Pro 400 (m375nw) $450, and Canon MF8380cdw $350. Canon was a clear winner in every aspect.
First off, HP color print quality was fuzzy and inconsistent.
Secondly, HP print speed was rated slower than Canon 8380cdw's 21page.
Thirdly, Canon offers duplex printing.
Fourthly, Canon is on sale.
Print quality from 8380cdw was acceptable compared with a $25k copier. However, for $350, I am happy with what I am getting. The print image was way better than HP PRO 200 and 400 in the same class.

Set up with Canon CD Utility was quite simple. I just set up the printer with Wired LAN. The utility walked me through every step, I was able to print and scan in less than 10 min. I have not tried to set up Wireless yet. Don't think I need to.

The only down side is expensive toner. Each color toner is $120 x 5. I guess that's how Canon make money selling the copier with heavy discounts. Most likely, I will be using generic toners to reduce TCO. Assuming if the copier broke from bad toners, it will be cheaper to buy a new one that's faster and cheaper than repairing it.

product_title: Kodak 10B/10C Combo Ink Cartridge - Black/Color - 1 Year Limited Warranty
review_body:
I bought my Kodak printer with great expectations. Cheap ink was their big claim. The ink that came with the printer lasted about 9 months. I do not print much. Bought this combo pack figuring it would last a year or more. I usually only print B/W mailing labels and I set it to "Draft Quality". Imagine my surprise when after about 5 months it told me I needed more ink. These cartridges should have lasted longer, as they were bigger (supposedly) then the ones that came with the printer. Contacted Kodak to see if there were other issues. Waste of time. Got the run around with India and gave up. In the course of speaking with them, pulled up data that showed with all the ink, I had printed a whopping 87 or so pages.......on draft quality. Oh, and just so you know, every time you turn the printer on, it 'primes' the print heads, so even if you just use B/W, the color disappears at the same rate. Can you say RIP OFF?

Replaced it with a Samsung B/W Laserjet. I have upped my label printing over the last few months and still have 90% of the initial cartridge ink.

I will keep the Kodak as a scanner and a reminder to not believe marketing hype.

product_title: LD Remanufactured Epson T125 Standard Yield Ink Cartridges: Black T1251, Cyan T1252, Magenta T1253, Yellow T1254
review_headline: Update: Now Used for two month
review_body:
Now that I've used the product for a couple of months I must of necessity downgrade my previous review. I still feel the product is a great replacement/alternative to the OEM item, especially in terms of cost. It fit and worked perfectly right away. The black ink seemed comparable in every way to the OEM. I've not had a chance yet to use the color I bought because the cartridges haven't run out yet.
However, regarding the performance of the cartridge.... since we don't use our Epson NX230 everyday, it can sit for several days inbetween print demand. Then, when we send a new job, the black ink cartridge (the OEM replaced by this LD Remanufacture) produces lines, broken print, and blotchy patches. Now, all I've had to do so far is send the printer into a head cleaning and this issue is immediately resolve . . . I can resume printing and all looks great. The issue is, I NEVER had to do this with OEM cartridges.

So, it remains to be seen what sort of problem this may become once I replace all of the color cartridges. They (being OEM) work flawlessly without any print defects regardless of how many days or even weeks between printing. There is simply something real different about LD's printer ink component that makes it a "cheaper" ink in terms of this clogging or drying out quality. If you can work through that inconvenience and don't mind performing a head cleaning each time you use your printer (IMPORTANT: this is after it has sat for days), then the LD cartridges seem to make a good alternative to OEM. They're certainly a much better price.

I'll update this with an additional comment after I've replaced all of the color cartridges and worked with those for about 60 days.

Jeff

So basically, get this recorder if you're trying to decide whether or not you need a recorder at all. Then, if you find that you actually need a recorder, return this one and upgrade to something more legit.

product_title: Panasonic DECT 6.0 Corded/Cordless Phone with Answering System, Metallic Gray
review_body:
The great variety of opinions on this phone may be due to its many features, with ratings based on the functioning of the features for which you bought the phone (as mine will be). If, for instance, you bought it only for the speaker function, you may not care (or notice) whether the call blocking works or not. I think we can agree, though, that sound quality matters to everyone. I found the sound quality of this phone intermittently very poor, sometimes making it impossible to continue a conversation or be heard above the static. The speaker function has also been poor from the outset (tinny, distorted sound, not loud enough even in a silent room). There are more than 40 reviews giving the phone a single star, and most of these mention poor sound quality, yet various people have seen fit to argue about the reviewers' experiences or claim it must have been \\"just that unit\\" when obviously, by the number of negative reviews and their common references to poor sound quality, the problem is more widespread.

Sound quality aside, I bought this phone for call blocking, and expected to get what is specifically noted in the advertising: \\"Block Unwanted Calls - Store the Caller ID info of ANY AND ALL UNWANTED CALLERS into your phone's Call Block list so that you can eliminate future pesky calls. After the information is stored, those unwanted callers will receive a busy signal when they call you again.\\" This is simply false advertising, since the phone blocks only 30 callers - so \\"any and all\\" is deliberately misleading. If you have been plagued by these kinds of calls, you already know that the Do Not Call list is disregarded and that 30 won't even make a dent in the number of scammers/criminals/debt collectors looking for their next victim. Even for those calls that can be stored and blocked, there is no mention in the advertising of the fact that the phone will still audibly ring once before the call is blocked. The only way to get around this is to use the silencer, but that is not an option for people who need to block junk calls but still remain reachable by family members in the event of an emergency. In short, if you have a real junk call problem, this phone will, at best, block a small percentage of the calls.

product_title: Epson WorkForce B11B194011 Pro GT-S50 Document Scanner
review_body: Recently, I read dozens of reviews of various scanners on Amazon.com over several days, and I really wanted to buy the sleek NeatDesk scanner.  I use the smaller NeatReceipts on an iMac at the office to keep track of my boss' expenses.  I also considered the Fujitsu ScanSnap.  But I didn't want all of my items to be in proprietary files in their file cabinets.  So, I bought the Epson GT-S50 based on enough good reviews, that I could return it to Amazon if there were issues, because it is a TWAIN scanner, and does duplex scanning.  I have used the GT-S50 on my PC for a few hours today; set up was quick enough although the installation process did not automatically start on my machine for some reason.  Easy enough to work around if you have installed software before.  So far I have scanned bank statements and their reconciliations (love that you can skip blank pages), a bunch of old photos, and a 50-page document into PDF that my husband can copy/paste sections of into his genealogy program.  No problems at all, I am glad to report.  Speed-wise, I was pleased; the 50-page, 1-sided, document took roughly 2 minutes to scan at 300 dpi and pop over into the file I designated.  Because I am not doing volume scanning for a business, this speed is great.  I especially like, and am more impressed, that I can set a resolution and file location BEFORE the scan.  This was especially convenient for the photos.  On my flat-bed scanner (HP Scanjet G3110), I am forced to set a scan resolution for every scan, one page or photo at a time; it is impossible to change the default resolution.  Back to the GT-S50 - so far the software has remembered the scan resolution I chose, which was 300 dpi.  I did not install the PaperPort software only because I do not want to do OCR at this point.  I have OCR software for another machine.  I also purchased the offered warranty on this product in case further down the line I have problems.  The price for the Epson is very close to the price for theNeatDesk, so I felt good about spending the money.  Sizewise, the scanner has a fairly small footprint; I was surprised at how heavy it is.  I am looking forward to scanning books and magazines that we are currently storing in the closets.  I am greatly interested in minimizing the paper stuff we have been saving and hauling around for over 30 years.

review_headline: Generic carts from a far away supplier not a good thing
review_body:
I am familiar with and have used rebuilt/refurbished carts before, even refilled some myself. I also was a copier and printer tech for 32 years, the last 16 at Samsung reseller. There are three common things you run into. The drum, the drum cleaning blade and the charger. If any of these are not perfect you get black lines. This is why it is important to be careful when buying rebuilt carts. It is not an uncommon thing for them to need exchange for one of these issues, even right out of the box. The issue is when you buy them on the web. These are the greatest value for the money, but they carry the risk of not working right and returning them is a hassle.
This is what happened to me. Right out of the box the cart was no good. It is dark on the sides which usually means a re-used drum or a bad charger. The seller did refund my money and was supposed to send me a return label, which never arrived. I expect that almost all the time, these arrive fine, but I had bad luck, and when that happens, it creates hassles.

review_headline: Great product and great customer service
review_body:
I was initially skeptical of buying this given the price, but there really isn't much else like it, so I ordered it anyway. It is very configurable for nearly any office type chair. My plan was to use it for gaming, with a mouse on the right side and a Logitech keypad on the left and it works great for that.

It is well-built and feels like a natural extension to the chair. Too much so maybe because after having it for about a week, I leaned over to pick something up and pushed down on the end of it and it snapped one of the hinges. The other hinge of the same arm still worked and I was able to line up the broken part so I could still use it, but after another two months the other hinge finally gave way too, and I was without my right armrest.

I emailed the manufacturer and told them what happened and asked if it were possible to just order the right arm because I didn't want to have to re-purchase the whole thing. Within a day via a very nice email they authorized a free arm replacement (+shipping). I thought this was a great gesture for something that was completely my fault and I fully recommend this product and the manufacturer.

These days, I'm just very aware of where the arm extensions are, so as not to repeat my mistake.

After going through some of the reviews, the only con that I have experienced is when I lean back in my chair, the mouse will slide off the back arm extension. To fix that, I put a black rubber-band around the base near the hinges and the mouse stops nicely before sliding off and I don't even notice it's there. Also, the pad works just fine with optical mice, no need for a different pad.

Another issue I ran into is a few times the blue light would start flashing orange. The only way to reset it is to unplug the unit. There are also times where I will put a few sheets in the scan, hit the scan button. All the sheets will scan and after the last sheet goes through, the scanner keeps running. I have to unplug the unit to get it to shut off.

I am sending this back to Amazon to get a replacement. Other than this issue, I really like how it scans and the software package. I am hoping that it is just defective hardware.

product_title: Pentel Arts Pocket Brush Pen, Includes 2 Black Ink Refills (GFKP3BPA)
review_headline: Perfect replacement for brushes/ink for comic-makers
review_body:
I love the look of comics/manga inked with a brush, but I find traditional sable brushes are too pricey and they don't have enough spring for me. Plus, its potentially very messy and clean-up is annoying. Brush pens are no alternative at all: they have no give, require too much pressure, and the ink quality is washed out and gritty and bleeds like crazy.

Here's what you want: the Pentel Arts Pocket Brush. It has a great, durable synthetic bristle that actually has individual hairs! That means great line variation for not much pressure, it holds a lot of deep black ink in it's belly, and you can get a great ragged edge if you want. The tip comes to a super fine hair-width point that's just sopping with ink, so you can do super-fine detail too. Ink cartridges are cheap, the ink quality is fantastic, and it's very comfortable to hold.

One con: If you're used to a longer brush handle, you may find your hand blocking the drawing as you work. It took me a little bit to adjust by holding my hand more to the side than directly above, but the brush lays down the same this way.

product_title: Philips DVT1000/00 2 GB Digital Voice Tracer with 2 Built-In Microphones Voice Recorder
review_body:
I have to say that there are very strong pluses and minuses to this voice recorder. First,if you are looking for something that you just hit the record button, rewind it and play it back that this is not the device for you. I have a Sony Digital Voice Recorder that looks the same without all the bells and whistles featured in the Philips that is simple to operate.

First, when you open the package, it tells you that it has the ability to record all types of files such as .mp3,.wav. etc. This already improves the sound quality. It has dual microphones so it can pick up anywhere in the room. The sensitivity level of the microphones are amazing and it picks up everything clearly across the room even for soft spoken speakers. The sound is clear. It does not sound like someone is talking in a tunnel or like the Charlie Brown teacher.

You can hook up this device to your computer via the USB cable that is included. This makes it very convenient to save files from the recorder onto your computer or the ability to hear it played back on your computer. You can also upload files onto your recorder. The packaging claims you can use this as a timer and an alarm. However, I cannot see anyone using it for this when we all have cell phones and other devices that have this feature that is easier to work.

It says on the packaging that there is an instructional manual loaded onto the recorder itself but I had no idea how to get to it and the pictures that it showed were not self explanatory. This leads me to my next complaint. The package includes a quick start manual which has several languages. Most of it is easy to see what is being described but some of it has you scratching your head. Also, there is no explanation of the symbols and pictures on the recorder which would have been helpful. On the website there is a very detailed instruction manual which is a PDF file and 60 pages long! So if you have some spare time to read all this and figure outall of the features, then more power to you. However, I am not that patient and I just wanted something simple to operate. I do not need to launch the next space shuttle or have my recorders make coffee (hmm...) but I did need some idea as to how to operate this device.

My fingers are rather tiny (kid size) and yet, every time I tried to hit the rewind button to playback the recording my finger hit the record button and recorded over the initial recording. This could be a very negative thing if I missed something important or if I needed to have this information. I tried hitting the directional button on the very edge with my fingernail and it still hit the record button. I see other reviewers have had an easier time and can work it so I do wonder if it is my particular device or me. Probably the latter. I was able to somehow rewind and play back the recordings a couple of times so I am thinking that it is definitely my problem.

This recorder is a good size that fits into the palm of your hand easily and in some cases is smaller than a cell phone. It can be put into any backpack, briefcase, handbag, or pocket easily. I see room for improvement especially in the area of the instructions and the directional button.

So, I will be going back to my Sony device which is all the recorder I need. Simple to use, self explanatory and while it may not have the sound quality or the microphone sensitivity of the Philips but so far with the Philips' buttons, I would not even get to hear the recording anyway.

I give this 3 stars because I know there are probably some wonderful features that I have yet to discover. The sound quality and the microphone sensitivity are that good!

product_title: HP Laserjet Pro M451dn Color Printer (Discontinued By Manufacturer)
review_body:
I bought the HP M451dn printer after doing a bunch of research. However, none of the reviews explained that this printer only comes with 128mb of memory. Within a few days of operation one of our sales guys kept getting \\"out of memory\\" messages. The standard memory places (Crucial, Newegg etc) did not carry the extra 256mb memory modules. HP sells it for almost $600! I found what I needed at Parts-Quick.com for $13.99. The person I talked to was very helpful- a former HP person. I now have 384mb of memory and no problems. The memory you will need is CB423A HP 256MB DDR2 144-pin DIMM Code: EV_CB423A at Part-Quick - It was only after I did hours of research that I found Parts-Quick. The same module is available from Parts-Quick through Amazon but the Amazon description does NOT mention the HP M451dn as a model that this memory works with. review_headline: Great Ink at a Great Price
review_body:
Five Stars because the HP 38 Light Cyan Pigment Ink Cartridge was shipped immediately and arrived promptly in good condition. If you use HP 38 ink in your printer, you must have all eight colors in the HP 38 series for your printer to operate properly, so price is a big consideration. Buying blind can cost you more for a complete set of inks, including more than one cartridge for the light gray and a couple of other colors that are used up faster than the others, than a new printer, and in fact I have heard of people that simply buy a new printer (of a different make) because it's cheaper than the inks. Amazon has a selection of vendors, but be wary - I recently picked the lowest price for each color, mostly from one vendor, and when I went to check out I found that this particular vendor charged $9 per cartridge for shipping and handling, making them the most expensive vendor on Amazon.

I stock up on inks only occasionally. The trigger event is when the warning light on the printer for a particular color comes on, and I don't have that color ready to change. When that happens, I check out what I do have, flesh out what I need to have a complete set including two of light gray, light cyan, and light magenta, and order them all, usually on Amazon. I like genuine HP inks on Amazon because that's where the price, Amazon Prime free shipping, vendor reliability, and prompt delivery all come together. I need genuine HP inks because I have this printer for studio-quality color prints and I depend on it for my most-invested hobby, and I don't have the time or patience to deal with cartridges that require color re-calibration or don't provide the color fidelity that I expect of an 8-ink printer, or that don't last as long as HP 38 ink cartridges. One of the reasons that I selected this printer was the combination of quality prints, low cost per print, and long life of the ink cartridges, a rare combination.

I recommend genuine HP 38 inks to anyone with a printer that calls for these inks, and recommend Amazon.com as the first place to check for best price. At one point during finals, I printed a document around noon, got frustrated, got back from the computer labs, went to bed, and woke up to the sound of printing at 6:30 am, processing a document sent hours ago.

I also realized that the paper got easily jammed because one of the rollers (I'm not sure what they're called, but they transfer the paper from the tray) were slower than the other, causing the paper to be drawn up crooked. I was impressed by its handling of ink, but the paper didn't make it out of the printer without being extremely damaged on one side.

Once again, after contacting customer service, they couldn't find out why and how, and refused to claim it as their own fault.

Now I just dream of the day I get a new and functioning printer. review_headline: Great VUPoint portable scanner with dock
review_body:
Used it first day opened box to scan over 140 photos at newly found cousin. I am not a gadget geek or techno geek, just a genealogy geek. The dock works great, it needs to be connected to a power source-computer or laptop or better yet the handy dandy USB adapter to electical outlet. I plan on covering the box it came in with paper or fabric because it will keep it safe and has a handle for carrying! It is light weight. The wand is sturdy enough that scanning is easy and works over photos in mats, and works on rounded book pages (book pages that do not lay flat). (I used a pen type smaller wand years ago and found it terrible, scans all wiggly because of going too fast or too slow and difficult to have a steady scan due to size.) I was very happy to use this wand and have it scan beautifully the very first time. Quality great. When hooked up to computer just one push of the button and it opens MY PICTURES and ready to download, very quick. Can keep scanned photos on the microSDHC card or delete them. I scanned in color mode as I was scanning black and white and color photos. All were great: great color, black and white were great. Tried black and white in Mono mode did not see a difference. Scanned over 3 1/2 hours without running out of the charge. 43 MB used for all my photos. It says it scans fabric, I did scan a colorful mouse pad, it worked!
I bought mine through Sears as it came with a 16 GB microSDHC card and adapter/reader so it was ready to use right out of the box. (needs charging first-made cookies while charging). The adapter allows you to read the micro card out of the wand if so desired. I am very very happy with this product and highly recommend it to genealogists, I scanned photo front and back of photo with the writing information, sure beats writing it all down, saves much time. It is also a quick way to scan home photos for preservation and sharing as well.

I properly chose the 3mil size for the 3mil laminator paper I had with the regular paper. The feed mechanism is self-feeding, so it's not like you could really \\"do it wrong\\".

So the art project didn't turn out exactly as desired and if this is the \\"quality\\" I question why someone would own their own, versus just going to a 24hr Kinko's that does a substantially better and higher quality job.

product_title: Epson Stylus Pro 4900 Standard EditionPrinter
review_body:
I bought this printer a couple of years ago when they were deeply discounted following the Japanese tsunami. I am not a professional but can afford to indulge my passion for photography by working hard at my day job. Given the deep discount I splurged on this machine. It is large requires two people to move it, uses expensive ink $100 a color, but produces beautiful images.

Right out of the box I had some issue that I finally called Epson about. I was told to send it back and they would send out a new one. Mind you I had just had a couple of friends help me move his up the stairs to my attic workspace. None the less,I did send it in (not UPS by the way but freight delivery) and they sent another though the packaging was very different. i suspect like many people I received a refurbished unit. It did however work until a month ago when it developed a clog in the black jet that the internal cleaning system only made worse.. After trying a number of Internet remedies I finally dragged this monster 65 miles to the Epson authorized dealer. They informed me I would need a new print head at $1300 and he was giving me a discount!

C'est la vie. The bottom line is this is not a casual use item. Part of the issue may have been that it sat between
projects. Despit Epson claims of virtually eliminating clogs they haven't and a search of the web will provide you with a plethora of hits regarding this problem with this unit. This printer is kind of a thoroughbred that may give you years of enjoyment with upscale care. People suggested humidifiers, temperature controls, etc, or you may,like myself,end up shooting it in the head and moving on. Normally I would look for a completely different manufacturer after an experience like this. Sadly, by general consensus, Epson does make the best printers out there. I'm looking at the 3880 and would suggest it to the advanced hobbyist like myself.

product_title: LD Remanufactured Hewlett Packard #14 Ink Cartridges:C5011DN Black & C5010DN Tri-Color
review_headline: I Had To Return This Item
review_body: I ordered this item for use in a HP cp1160 inkjet printer. The printer reads an expiration date code from the ink cartridge, and if the cartridge is expired, the printer will not operate. When I installed the remanufactured tricolor cartridge to replace an empty one, the printer did not recognize it as a valid cartridge and did not operate. Replacement with a factory-original tricolor cartridge restored proper operation.  Perhaps the idea of remanufactured cartridges is a good one for printers that do not have the expiration date code "feature", but it is not a good idea for the HP cp1160. I do not know if other machines that use the same cartridges would have the same problem. Since the printer is old and ink cartridges are getting hard to get, I will replace it soon, but definitely not with one made by HP! The prices for factory-original HP cartridges are very high, and I feel that the expiration date code "feature" is just a scam to sell more expensive ink cartridges.

product_title: Epson WorkForce WF-2530 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer, Copier, Scanner, ADF, Fax. Prints from Tablet/Smartphone. AirPrint Compatible (C11CC37201)
review_headline: Expensive Ink Prices - HOW TO USE REFILLS
review_body:
Nice all in one printer, but cost of ink cartridges is very high! I wish I had known beforehand. For me, it ran about $79 /month. I can't support that. So, here's a few tips on how-to refill your new Epson WF-2530 with refillable cartridges.

First, buy from an online supplier a refill kit for yellow, cyan, magenta and black cartridges with auto-reset chips. The kit should include good quality ink, the equivalent of Epson DURAbrite, and syringes. You want good quality ink, as it's refined and less likely to clog the print ports.

Press Copy button on console.
Press Menu button.
Press down arrow on console to scroll to Maintenance.
Press OK.
Press down arrow to scroll to Ink Cartridge Replacement.
Press OK.
Printer will say Replace Cartridge.
Cartridge carriage will position itself outside its bay.
Lift open the printer case.

Lift out original Epson cartridge if this is the first time putting in a new, refillable cartridge. Later, you can refill the refillable cartridge without taking it out of the carriage.

Shake briskly the capped bottle of ink.
Fill syringe with color needed.
Poke syringe needle right into fill hole, or through rubber color plug on refillable cartridge. (Depends on what brand you bought where the fill up hole is.) It's a straight forward thing, tilting the cartridge during fill up is optional.

Fill cartridge to the top. It takes about 3 syringes or 15 ml ink.
When done, press filled cartridge firmly back into carriage, if first time.
Press OK on the console.
Printer will check say Checking...
Ink not recognized, proceed? Choose Yes or 1.
Printer will again say, Replace Cartridge. Ignore that.

Turn off printer. (Don't press stop/reset button, it doesn't help.)
Wait 15 seconds. Turn on the printer again.

The first time a new refillable cartridge is put in, and the printer is restarted, the printer takes a long time to settle down. It may hover silently and click a bit.
Don't worry. It will settle into copy mode after about two minutes.
Next time, it will behave as normal.

Print a test page. Test pages always take a long time for the printer
to think about. Just wait, it will print out. If the print looks faded or blotchy, do a head cleaning and try again.
The next page should be okay.

review_headline: Good scanner, but why over $300 now?

Just warning you.. I bought this in 2010 for $99.00. I'm not sure why this is listing over $300.00 now??

Why am I posting this now? Well frankly, I haven't used the scanner that much until recently. So after finally using it extensively, I went back to my \\"Prior Orders\\" and clicked on the link, and to my surprise it showed a $384.00 price tag. This scanner is nice, but NOT worth that much. The $99.00 I bought it for almost THREE years ago (in February 2010) seems much more reasonable.

The quality of the scanning images is decent, and it has decent speed (though not super-fast). It also has several methods of delivery (i.e. mail, PDF, printer). There is no duplex option, so if you have bulk-scanning to do, this is not for you. Also it did not seem to auto-crop some of the smaller images I scanned -- this may have been due my failure to configure it properly, or it may be a flaw of the scanner - not sure which.

Bottom line is, while this is a very old scanner, it still does the job well. But please do not buy this for anything more than $100.00, and especially for over $300.00 - I'd hate to see someone get ripped off like that.

product_title: Epson Expression Premium XP-600 Small-in-One® Printer - Epson C11CC47201
review_headline: Ok printer, bad support and airprint is not definite w/PC
review_body: I purchased this printer so my mother could airprint from her ipad and iphone. It took a long time to install on the computer (hers happens to be an Acer laptop with Vista on it (uhhhg). I installed it to work wirelessly and it did with the Acer. I've tried multiple times to get aiprint to work and it did appear as an available printer on both our iphone and her ipad for about ten seconds then it disappears. I was able to print a photo from her iphone, then have never been able to print anything again. The Epson support system is a joke. If you try to get help hey just keep linking you to the instruction manual, which I had a hard copy of that came with the printer and it is despicably lacking in information, especially for trouble shooting. For help with airprint they link you to apple's website that says \\"check with your printer manufacturer\\". From what I can tell with other peoples' reviews, the airprint feature will only work when the printer is hardwired into the main computer you installed it on. Useless since my mom doesn't want to leave her laptop on all the time just so she can randomly print things.    NOW - for all you MAC users there is a possible answer. Handy-print ([...]) is a nice little bit of software that will unlock ANY printer and allow airprint. I did this at home with my old HP all in one that I bought before airprint existed. BUT my HP is installed on a mac mini. Handyprint is not available for PC - they say they are working on a version, however, so keep checking back. You can download handyprint for free. To keep it after the trial period you just have to donate $5. Totally worth it to me to make my non-airprint printer work with my iphone/ipad. If you have a mac try it and if it doesn't work just don't donate.    Another word to the wise - Epson wants you to install all this crazy remote-email-print software. I didn't but then most of the functions on the printer wouldnt work so I had to download them and sign up for all this stupid crap (like an email address just for my printer so I could print by emailing my printer - such unnecessary horses*** - just make airprint work!!!!!!) to get it to work.    The printer is a nice printer, and it works great otherwise. I love that it was separate ink cartridges so you don't waste ink like in a tricolor cartridge. The wireless printing from the laptop it was installed on works great. Good luck!

product_title: ViewSonic PJD5123 SVGA DLP Projector (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
Had it for a year and still works, used for 950 hours up to this day, so averaging about 2.5 hours a day. I mainly use it for shows and movies, but also play PC games on it sometimes.
Pros: Great for movies and shows, Very bright compared to cheaper projectors, runs for hours (I've gone as much as 12 in one sitting,) can get very large projection, and the heat output is great for winter.
Cons: Not ideal for games as the level of detail isn't very refined. Colors and picture settings can be tricky to get right and there's not really a perfect setting. The larger picture you project, the larger pixels will be. Difficult to read small text (like chat boxes) at any screen size b/c of the poor pixel blending. Only one audio input (for standard computer speakers) so if you have A/V cables you'll have to buy a male to 2 RCA female adapter.

Overall, I recommend this because it cost less than a very small LCD Television and has great quality.

product_title: Canon PIXMA MX892 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner, Copier and Fax
review_body: Let me first say that I had a Canon  MP 530 for 4 years and it worked flawlessly for all this time. When it finally recently  broke up, I did not think twice and I got another Canon, this one Pixma MX 892. Nice looking, excellent features. Loved the wireless connectivity and the quality of the printing. BUT: for me there were 2 unacceptable aspects: every time the printer is idle for more than a few hours, and every time you shut it down, it takes a very long time to start up again. It looks like it performs a head cleaning which takes a long time. So if you need to print something quickly at that time, just forget it. By doing this, the printer also uses a lot of ink, which is definitely unnecessary. I called Canon and they said that's the way it is and there is no other way to change the settings. I've had the printer for 10 days, used it very little and I am already low on 3 of the colors. The ink cartridges are about 30% smaller than my older model and even buying compatible ones, I can see tat it would be quite expensive to maintain this printer. Furthermore the Canon cartridges are totally black on the outside: one cannot see the ink level and to me this seems like another trick from Canon to make one replace them whenever the printer says 'ink low'. Before I could see the ink level and I could judge if there was still ink enough to print a few more pages...I am returning it and I hope Canon will stop making products with all these money-making tricks.

product_title: MagicJack Plus + Free 6 Months Subscription to Magic Jack Service
review_body:
This is the second time that I've tried Magic Jack. This review covers both the original Magic Jack and the Magic Jack Plus. First time, audio kept cutting in and out so I ended up having to repeat myself alot. Very annoying. I spent literally hours and hours chating with their customer service, and everytime they said technicians were aware of the problem and that it should be fixed within a 24 hours. Never was fixed, UNTIL about the 11 month. Than it seemed to work perfectly until the subscription ended and service was cut off without any warning whatsoever. Since they bill your card automatically annually, and I had changed cards during that time, they had no way of knowing, but that is what emails are for. They do not notify you that they are going to bill your card, they just do it, which is wrong imo. So I renewed it through the chatline thinking they fixed the problem and everything would be fine. Shortly after renewing, I started losing calls to my mom every time, even though it worked ok with everyone else. Calling my mom long distance was the main reason why I wanted Magic Jack. And so I ended up going through the same crap spending hours all over again with their customer service. Finally after 2 months, I told them to just cancel the service, and when I asked for a refund because they couldn't fix it, they refused. About a year later, I saw a renewal charge on my credit card, even though I had canceled the service 10 months ago, I had to deal again with their chat line to get a refund, but I bet I spent at least 12 hours total on their chat line.
About 2 years later, they came out with Magic Jack Plus which doesn't require a computer after the innitial set up. Desperate as I was for cheap phone service, I decided to try again. Believe it or not, I was losing calls again just 10 minutes in to the conversation. Almost like it was on a timer, but this time it was with everybody. Naturally, they couldn't fix it, but after a couple months, I realized that if I unplug my computer from the internet before I called someone, it started working fine, yet they couldn't figure that out. Today, Magic Jack just quit working completely with no warning. That's it! Never again!

product_title: Samsung SCX-4729FW/XAA Wireless Monochrome Printer with Scanner, Copier & Fax
review_headline: Hard to set up wireless, paper tray is weird
review_body:
The most frustrating thing a printer can do is jam the paper. By that measure, this printer is the most frustrating printer I have ever used in my entire life. I have decades of experience putting 8.5 by 11 inch paper into a laser printer paper tray. All of my experience is for naught with this Samsung printer, because the paper tray simply doesn't like normal sized paper. I know that seems a bit imprecise, but there really is no better way to put it. The paper doesn't sit in the tray properly, it seems to curve upward, and even if I am very careful, when I close the tray, the paper jams. I am not exaggerating when I say that this printer has caused my frustration meter to explode into yelps of rage. [SEE UPDATE!]

Compared to the paper problem, the wireless issues really don't seem so bad. It's very difficult to get the wireless set up, especially on a Mac computer, because the installation software seems to hang all the time. But I didn't select this printer for its wireless capabilities, and I simply use it plugged in with a USB cable. I suggest putting it in directly anyway given that the scanning it functions do not work wirelessly.

The print quality is fine, but at this stage in printer development I expect nothing less from a major printer manufacturer. But I also expect a paper tray that works, and this one simply fails that test. I do not recommend this printer unless you enjoy collapsing into fits of rage and despair.

--
UPDATE, Sept. 2013: The paper doesn't jam anymore. It was entirely user error. Silly me, I'm used to all paper trays acting pretty much the same way. Not so on this machine. You have adjust a plastic guide on the REAR of the tray, which lets the tray extend out behind the printer, and then you can put the paper in all the way. Paper doesn't curve, nothing jams. I've upped my stars from 2 to 4. I still can't get it to work on wireless, but as a fast laser printer and nice scanner, it works great.

product_title: Epson Stylus NX625 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer, Copier, Scanner (C11CA70271)
review_headline: NO, NO, NO, A THOUSAND TIMES, NO.
review_body:
Okay, I want to make a couple of points for anyone considering buying this printer.

The printer works about as well as you could expect for the price, though it constantly runs out of ink with only moderate use, even the so-called high capacity black ink cartridge - by the way, in the printer utility, you can check an option that will allow you to continue printing in black when one of the colors runs out. Without that feature, I would have thrown this printer, along with its overpriced ink cartridges in the trash - and the paper feed is unreliable and I often have to waste time removing the device from my computer and reinstalling it just to get it to come online and print - but those issues are not what prompted me to write this review.

It is, of course, reasonable in the world of computers and peripheral devices that one may have to download new printer software after an upgrade to the computer operating system, so when I tried using the printer shortly after upgrading the OS on my Mac, and I soon realized that the printer was not responding due to some new malfunction aside from the the host of other malfunctions I had already experienced with this printer, I went online, did a little research and understood I was going to have to upgrade the printer software. So I went to Epson's download site and downloaded the new software compatible with my operating system, meticulously following all the instructions on how to install it. After carefully installing the new software, per the written instructions Epson had furnished along with the software, I then tried to add the printer but my computer would not recognize it and prompted me with a message that I would have to contact the printer manufacturer. So I did that.

I called Epson and explained the problem, describing everything I had done to try to complete the install. The Epson technician explained to me that he knew EXACTLY what the problem was - I had corrupted files in theregistry on my computer. (Oh No! I thought to myself.) But no worries - he explained that he could solve this problem by accessing my computer remotely and removing the corrupted files. He assured me he would have everything up and running in only 15 minutes. What a relief, I thought to myself. He then me asked me for my credit card number. I paused momentarily at that request and then asked him what he intended to charge me for this service. (Frankly, I felt it should be gratis, under the circumstances.) He answered \\"$79.95.\\" I said, \\"No thanks.\\" He hung up.

So I pondered the problem awhile. I would have bought a new printer before paying $79.95 for help installing the software. I told myself that the solution would probably come to me. Myself must have heard that suggestion because it then answered me with the idea to open my application folder and delete all the Epson application files. I did it and then I went, once again, to settings and tried adding the printer and it installed to the Mac without a hitch. It is now working as well as ever, which isn't saying much.

Epson was actually trying to lock me in to a $79.95 charge for what only amounted to deleting my old Epson application files. Rather than extending one of it's own customers the courtesy of some advice on how to resolve this issue very simply and easily, the Epson man talked to me long and fast to make this magical fix sound like a job that only a skilled, highly advanced, Epson-trained computer technician could possibly manage. It's basically a scam, a ripoff, a fraud, a flimflam. How can I possibly give more than one star to a product under those circumstances? (There should be a choice for zero stars - or perhaps minus stars.) When we buy a computer product, we're trusting the manufacturer not to rip us off when we turn to them for help when their software will not install. I can only imagine how many Mac users had the wool pulled over their eyes and paid the price.

No, I would not recommend the product under those circumstances.

review_headline: Best choice for Mac based multi-function machine
review_body: I run Mac OSX 10.7.4, which replaced my PC. Unfortunately, my older Cannon copier/scanner/copier/fax would not work with the Mac. So when my Canon machine gave out (probably the 5th one I have owned from Canon), I went shopping for the best multi-function laser printer/copier/scanner/fax machine I could find. I wanted something with a good document feeder, that would handle legal sized documents. I looked on Apple website, figuring they would sell the machines that worked best with Apple. Not such great reviews there from the users of the products they sell (Canon, Epson, etc.). Next, I did a Google search to find what other people recommended. Brother came up quite a bit, so I went on their website and determined this product was a good fit. I read the reviews on Amazon. The result is a machine that does everything well, as advertised. When I had a few questions (after my purchase), the Brother customer service was first rate. I am very happy with this product, as well as Brother. As usual, I am also happy with my shopping experience on Amazon.    To address a few negative reviews, here is what I noted from my experience. First, this machine does draw a lot of power, so if your circuits are not up to it, that could be a problem. This, however, was not a problem for me (note that I am using a battery back-up surge protector, which I believe helps). Second, if you are printing wireless, you cannot also do it on a wired network. It is either the wireless network or the wired network. Note: if you are scanning to your Mac, the wireless does not work in that direction, so you must be hooked up with a cable for that task.    Also note that I was surprised to receive my machine so quickly, after only 3 business days following my order.    My only slightly negative comment is that the software for scanning, etc. could be a little more intuitive.

product_title: Set of 8 Remanufactured T0540 T0541 T0542 T0543 T0544 T0547 T0548 T0549 Ink Cartridges for Epson R800 R1800
review_body:
First off, the cartridges shown in the photo are not what was sent to me, which would be no big deal if they worked as advertised. Unfortunately, the design of the cartridges is flimsy and I already broke one of the spring loaded thumb snaps that hold them in place, AND these cartridges are extremely messy due to an air hole on top that you have to remove a tape-like tag from to relieve air pressure. Maybe it's my altitude (6000+ feet) but each of these cartridges either splattered or oozed ink all over my hands, printer and counter top. Once installed I got 2 or 3 photo prints out of the printer but the colors were all off, so I cleaned the nozzles and aligned the heads again and again without success. When I'd finally get the two or three clogged cartridges starting to work another one would stop working. I've used half the ink in these cartridges (they're clear plastic so you can visually tell) just trying to unclog them and I still haven't gotten a single print out of the machine. To make matters worse, Epson essentially nags you to death every time you try to print by throwing out a window that says you're not using real Epson ink and you're voiding your warranty. Thanks Epson.

It's downright silly how much money Epson wants for their ink cartridges and the prices keep going up ($19 each at the local Office Max!). So I figured this would be an inexpensive experiment and in my mind, this is a giant FAIL. The Epson R1800 has been an excellent large format printer but I'm guessing that it's about at the end of it's life cycle judging by the premium cost of true Epson Ink. I may simply retire this printer and replace it with an all-in-one for day to day documents and small photo printing and send out the large format printing to the local print shop or even Walmart(!).

Bottom line, AVOID these print cartridges and save your 15 bucks and all the hassles that go with it!

product_title: Samsung Electronics CLP-680ND Color Printer
review_body:

I have printed Word documents, Excel files with grids on, pictures, charts and graphs and the prints are sharp and the text is very clear; it shows lot of fine detail in pictures. It feels great to use laser printer after using inkjet printers because the cartridges will dry out if not used regularly. You don't have that problem with this printer.

Installing the printer is effortless using the CD, and it works well with Windows 7. This is not wireless in the true sense of the word, since it requires a direct Ethernet connection to the network. In this regard, the manufacturer offers an explanation to one of the reviewers and blames on a third party. The statement says; \\"Please know that this model was originally incorrectly identified as a wireless printer. The incorrect title was caused by an error supplied by a third party content company, and was not an error on Amazon's part.\\" This explanation is unsatisfactory because the manufacturer bears the responsibility for the product description.

This is not a multi function printer (MFP), and it is a large and heavy machine. The consumables are expensive. There are many printers like Hewlett Packard LaserJet CE866A that can also copy and scan. This may be important if scanning and copying is necessary, especially if you are a small business owner. Overall, this machine gets four stars for quality, performance, features and ease-of-use.

product_title: Brother PC-Connectable Label Maker with Auto Cutter (PT-2430PC)
review_headline: Good label maker... tip for saving tape
review_body:
It does a great job at making labels. The on-board software is sufficient enough for most people.

However the BROTHER corporation deserves criticism. It appears that BROTHER has designed this label maker to waste incredible amounts of tape. Note the cost of replacement tape cartridges. If it weren't for tape waste I'd give this product 4 to 5 stars. At one time I tried the full version of the software just to see if the I could control the amount of feed before printing started. There are TONS of other settings. Nothing though that allows one to prevent the unnecessary waste of tape. It has to be a deliberate decision. The amount of waste between labels is so incredibly bad that I'm taking time to write this post.

I have discovered one way to get around this customer-be-damned approach to selling replacement cartridges: Make several labels at a time by typing in your text and inserting a couple spaces, print, and cut with hand-held scissors. You will save incredible amounts of tape with this approach, especially during big projects. For people looking for a decent label maker to get things done at a decent price, this tip is for you. The decision-makers at BROTHER can go jump off a cliff.

It's a good label maker. But take a minute to look at the competition to see if someone has built a better label maker by a company that wants to deliver value to their customers.

product_title: Learning Resources Healthy Helpings MyPlate Pocket Chart
review_body: Have you ever said, \\"Don't play with your food!\\" to your kids? Now there's a way to let them play with it! The Healthy Helpings Pocket Chart is from Learning Resources and it's a great way to encourage children to learn more about the foods they eat (or should be eating). Based on the guidelines of ChooseMyPlate.gov, this great learning tool helps children recognize not just the foods they eat, but the food groups those foods belong in. The plate diagram on the pocket chart helps children and families visualize healthy food portions too. There are 90 real-life photo cards included with the chart and the cards have the name of the food printed on the picture side. On the back side is the name of the food group that food belongs in, so children can make a guess and self-check their answers. The food groups are marked by color and the food groups on the back of the card match, so reading is not required. The Healthy Helpings Pocket Chart comes with an activity guide for parents and teachers. My preschoolers thought it was so much fun to put the cards in the pockets on the chart. Made of heavy-weight vinyl and stitched-on pockets, the chart is durable and will hold up to many little hands. The cards are made of a glossy heavy-weight card stock. The top of the pocket chart has metal grommets so you can easily hang it up. This kind of a learning toy can be used for all ages of children, from preschoolers through elementary. Children can work alone or in groups to build a healthy plate for all three meals, find foods beginning with a specific letter or food group, or use the cards and pocket chart to build a food theme over several weeks. Open-ended educational materials can be used in many ways. Disclosure: I received this product at no charge in exchange for my honest review.

product_title: HP Officejet 6500 Wireless All-in-One Inkjet Printer
review_headline: HP 6500 Printer Stopped Working After 2 Years & Waste Ink
review_body:
As of four days ago, my HP6500 Printer suddenly stopped working, displaying the following, \\"Ink System Failure.\\" I had this printer for 2.5 years now, and I had just printed something the day before it stopped working. It said to turn the machine off and turn it on again, and I did (several times in the last few days), and it still won't return to working condition. On the first day it malfunctioned, I took the ink cartridges out and cleaned the ink system with dry towel and it still didn't work (as recommended in the manual). I then wiped it down with a moist towel, and it didn't work. Then I rinced it and all this ink gunk came out of the ink system (with the cartridges removed). I then let it dry for three days before trying it out, and again it didn't work. It seemed that the printer wasted a great deal of ink as it drained into the printer when it wasn't printing. I did notice that this printer uses up ink very quickly even when I buy the extra large (XL) cartridges. The ink cartridges are super expensive, and I bought a lot because the machine would run out quickly. So, now I have all these expensive cartridges for a printer that no longer works. Based on what I read of other owners, they had the same situation with this printer lasting only about three years.

When it was working, the software would suddenly stop functioning on the computer, and I had to reload the software in order for the wireless capability to function again. This happened several times, especially when I had critical documents to print and in a rush such as once trying to print my tax return. It seems that this printer drains ink while it is not printing, and the ink sits inside the ink system causing a major malfunction. Being that I have all these ink cartridges (multiples of every color) left that I purchased, I figured I'd buy the same cheap printer somewhere to use up the ink I have, and it turns out no major chain sells this model any more. HP doesn't even sell it any more probably because they realized this printer is bad on ink and stops working after 2-3 years.

I'm a bit disappointed because I always trusted HP and even recently bought an HP laptop. Now I'm concerned as the HP brand seems to be losing its quality. I will probably never buy HP again. The company forced out its last major CEO, stopped selling its tablet and had to write off millions of dollars recently because of financial mismanagement. It is sad to see such a great brand fall. Don't buy this printer if you are looking for one. If you own it, don't buy the ink until you truly run out because you'll end up having lots of unused expensive ink if your printer ends up breaking down. I trusted HP because there was a printer at work that lasted nearly 14 years; thus, thinking my printer would outlast any computer I have, and it turns out to not be true. Upset and sad at HP.

product_title: HP Officejet Pro 8600 Plus e-All-in-One Printer (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: I bought the HP Officejet Pro 8600 Premium (the same as the 8600 but with two paper trays)because it had an automated document feeder that could hold 50 pages.  I was using a Fujitsu Scan Snap 1500, which holds less than 20 pages, and was hoping to reduce scanning time. I also thought I could save money buying an all-in-one machine.  Big mistake. The product specs say it scans at \\"up to 11 ppm.\\"  That is only true if you scan at 75 dpi in black and white, which leaves you with a scan that is barely legible even when scanning simple black and white typed pages.  If you scan at 200 dpi - which is ok quality, but not great - you get 3 pages per minute!  If you want to scan at a higher quality dpi, the document feeder can not be used.  Instead, you have to manually place each page on the glass, go through the cumbersome scan process with every single page.  For comparison, my Fujitsu scans 20 ppm at 600 dpi.  If you are looking for a scanner, just buy the Fujitsu and buy a separate printer!  If you do decide to buy this printer, note the 14 day return policy and test it out the day you get it or you will be stuck with it!

product_title: Brother PC Connectable Labeling System with Carry Case (PT2730VP)
review_body:
I have not needed to hook this to my pc, so this review is for standalone service only. I have used the Labeler to make numerous labels for cabling and other household devices. The specialty wire/cable labels hold on very well even outdoors throughout the year and the seasons. Label generation is very easy using the keyboard. To save label waste, I prepare all of my wording in advance and turn off the cutter until the last label. When I have finished I use scissors to cut and separate and thereby save a lot of wasted label blank that would be generated if I let the machine cut each one. There are enough built-in fonts to generate tight text or very blocky readable text. Bold or italic, it all worked very well. They keyboard is a little rubbery, but you're making labels, not typing a novel. For standalone it is great. If I can edit this review, I will add to it when / if I use the PC interface. As of now, I would buy again.

***UPDATE*** I finally had occasion to hook the label maker to my pc. I downloaded the latest software from the Brother website. Despite the instructions on the original paper label pasted over the USB port, you actually have to have the label maker powered on and connected to the USB port before you can load the printer driver. The Editor and Updater will load without the label maker connected though. The software works well. I would not call it user friendly, but it can be figured out without a lot of effort. You get more fonts available and it is easier to type on a pc keyboard. It worked very well and I was very pleased to be able to preview many different changes and options far more quickly than when standalone. My feelings stand. Recommended and I would buy again.

product_title: HP Officejet 6500A Plus e-All-in-One (CN557A#B1H)
review_body:
The boss bought this computer for the office to replace another HP which had just become too old. Fortunately, the computer we got didn't have that one bug where if it sits idle for 5 minutes, it totally freezes. UNFORTUNATELY, it did have 2 other huge problems. Every once in a while, like once a month, the printer becomes a ghost and basically appears offline to the entire network. It is clearly on and the printer claims to be connected to the network (I can see this on the little screen located on the printer), but it cannot be detected. Thus, I have had to reinstall the driver, delete the printer and install a \\"new\\" printer (the same one -_-) 10 TIMES!

Another huge problem is that it occasionally cuts off the bottom part of a document. This is not because the margin is too low, or because it does not fit on one page. It does this with PDFs, Excel workbooks, Word Documents and webpages! For example, if a document has 5 pages, the first one will be missing the bottom two inches. When I print it again, it will print fine. I contacted HP through the chat to tell them of this and all they did was lead me through a meaningless tour of \\"how to adjust your margins\\" and told me to print again. When I did print and told them it came out fine, they said, \\"Great, problem solved.\\" Noo, problem not solved because it does it out of nowhere. It has happened 4 times a day, and then stops happening the rest of the week and then it'll happen again. This can be a HUGE problem for businesses because you're having to print things again and again until they come out complete and thus wasting precious ink, WHICH BARELY LASTS AS IT IS.

End of rant.

product_title: Nettalk Duo VOIP Adapter
review_headline: You get what you pay for
review_body:
I bought this back in June, 2012. At the time I was raving over the product. Yes it had flaws, but for the price I could put up with them, or so I thought.

First the good points:
1. Easy to install. Just plug in power, Ethernet, and a phone, and presto, it works! That is wonderful.
2. The on-line set up is nice and has the features I would like, all included in the low price. This includes things like voice mail and call forwarding. The voice mail can be forward to an (one) email address. Also, it has a speed-dial feature for 10 numbers which is nice. They give you a complete record of calls received and sent, if you are interested, (but who cares since they are all free anyway.) International calling is about the only extra they charge for, but Canada is included in the basic plan.
3. It is a nice package. Easy to unplug and take with you if you travel. Not much larger than a pack of cigarettes.
4. I have sent and received faxes without much difficulty.
5. 411 and 911 support. They claim 411 information is free, but I never tried it.
6. No hidden fees. No 911 charge, no taxes. The purchase includes the first year's service with NO additional fees.

So with all that, how can you go wrong? As I said I recommended this to several friends who went out and got it. I was happy for a while. Yes, the voice quality was not great, not even as good as my cell phone, but so what? The price was right.

Well, it is now November and I just got rid of it. Here are my reasons: CALL/VOICE QUALITY!!
Sometimes, it is fine. Maybe 20%-30% of the time there are problems.
These include:
1. Echos. Sometimes you hear you own voice come back about a second later. This makes it impossible to talk.
2. Ringing, static, etc can be very annoying,
3. Delay in sending and receiving the voice. There can be about a second in the round turn. Sometimes it does not matter, sometimes it can really interfere with the conversation.
4. Tones can happen in the middle of the conversation. It can be like someone's two-year old is playing with the keypad while you are trying to speak.
5. The call just simple gets cut off.

Bottom line:
If you want a good quality, reliable phone, this is not the right one for you.
If you want really cheap and do not care about quality, this can work for you.

I got a Vonage phone to replace this. The difference is like night and day. Of course, it costs a lot more.
I am not sure what I will do with my Nettalk Duo device now.
I might hook it up as a second line. I can use that line for giving out to companies where it might result in solicitations. Sometimes companies need my number. This would be a good phone for that.

review_headline: Quality printing and a variety of features

Envelopes print perfectly centered via Word 2010. Of course the 4 cartridges are only setup cartridges so I would advise purchasing a refill of black 932 and all three 933 colors especially if you print a heavy volume of documents. Personally I don't print that much. Since I started using the printer, I have only printed 155 pages according to my printer status report that in turn reflects I have the following ink levels remaining in the setup cartridges: 40% Black, 10% Yellow, 30% Cyan and 25% Magenta. So for my needs it works. My only criticism is with all these inner mechanical parts, it seems to make a little more noise than I was used to compared to my prior printer. But its something I can get used to.

A lot of people complain about the cost of ink, but this has always been the case for these HP all in one printers. The more pages you print and the higher print quality settings you use, the more you will pay. Other brands might be more economical for ink so I would research them carefully before purchase if you have to print a lot of documents.

review_headline: Not enough scent to annoy humans

I purchased the product based on the reviews from others that it was strong enough to annoy humans. This has proven to be entirely untrue. If you hold the product up to your nose, it is repulsive. However, if you use this product on something like a tree, at 5' high, a human would have to be within 1 or 2 feet literally to be able to smell it at all.

Since this product is designed to repel cats and dogs, and their olfactory senses are much more sensitive, it might work for cats and dogs (although my dog is not bothered by it).

It DOES NOT work to repel humans from an area as some reviews have indicated, unless perhaps they are leaning ON the pole where you apply the product.

product_title: Powershred 63Cb Light-Duty Cross-Cut Shredder, 10 Sheet Capacity
review_body:
This shredder is designed for personal use. But that doesn't mean it's \\"cheap.\\" It seems to be a solid, top-of-the-line shredder. It's relatively compact, less than the height of a standard couch. It will easily hide, out-of-sight. But if noticed, it is very elegant (at least for a shredder): the top is a glossy black with a silvery-framed feeder. The switches are solid, suggesting attention to detail.

Note: this is a cross-cut shredder, not a particle cut. This means the shredder cuts paper into rectangular, parallelogram, or diamond-shaped (or lozenge) shreds, NOT tiny square or circular pieces. The latter would be required for highly sensitive (or highly paranoid individuals). A cross-cut shredder is not quite as \\"secure\\" but more than adequate for personal use (the pieces in this shredder are about 2 inches long by 1/4 inch wide).

I have not tested the \\"anti-jam\\" feature.
