product_title: Canon PIXMA MG3220 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner and Copier (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
Unlike some of the other reviewers, I didn't have any trouble setting up the Canon PIXMA MG3220 on my home wi-fi network with Apple computers and iOS devices. Duplexing is automatic, and scanning is just one sheet at a time from the platen, unlike my older Canon with a sheet feed.

The color quality is good, once the heads are aligned. Printing is a bit slow, but photos are worth waiting for. Like most printers at this price point, you need to switch between plain paper, photo paper, labels, and envelopes manually. I always keep my inkjet set to draft mode/grayscale to save ink, and have probably saved hundreds of dollars over the past 20+ years. If you plan to use this as a photo printer, ink costs could really ad up fast!

This is a good, very basic printer that will produce good photos. It is reasonably priced upfront (as most of these printers are) with fairly pricey ink cartridges as time goes on. If you have relatively modest printing and scanning needs, the MG3220 might fit the bill. But factoring in the cost of even one cartridge refill ($50) could allow you to choose another level of speed and features from Canon.

review_headline: Excellent product, but templates aren't very easy

I ended up going to the Avery website, using their online layout tool to make a PDF, then opening that PDF inside Adobe Illustrator and laying my artwork out that way.

It took me hours, and I do this kind of thing for a living!

NOW, I will say - the cards themselves are fantastic. Note that they are not Inkjet & Laser -- you buy EITHER Laser OR Inkjet. The papers are very different, and my Epson inkjet can't print on these laser ones -- but they come out great when you use them in a color laser.

product_title: Leuchtturm1917 Hardcover Medium Plain Journal
review_body:
I have been looking for blank journals with high quality for general note-taking and recording my ideas. Naturally, Moleskine products come to mind and they are prevalent in college bookstores. I had a few of them but rather disappointed with the paper thickness ans quality. Now I that have found Leuchtturm notebooks, I'm not likely to go back to Moleskine ever again. This notebook is superior in quality than Moleskine.

They have all the details that make it stand out and worth the purchase value. Pages are numbered - the page number font is rather fade and small - still looks like a blank page if you don't really notice. You even have table of content - really useful But some might find this augmentation unnecessary - though it doesn't compromise the aesthetic for me. Papers are thicker than MS and are less likely to bleed through - fountain-pen folks will love this. The papers are of paler hue though - I mean it is a bit whiter than somewhat yellow-ish MS. It also provides some perforated pages at the back, in case you have to tear some page of the book - I don't think most people will do that with a more expensive notebook like this though, but the details make it nice.

It is broader in dimension as well - about half an inch broader than the MS - I find this make it more comfortable to write (but could compromise portability if you have small pocket). Speaking of pocket, the back pockets are sturdy in this product. But they are harder to pry open compared with MS and I like the MS's pocket better - not that I use them a lot. The elastic also snaps a little sharper than MS, which I like.

In sum, this is a winning product. A bit more expensive but worth it. The only thing is the name is difficult to pronounce/remember. I am a trademark lawyer- and I know this is not a good name to use in American market. If they adopt a new Trademark, Moleskine is dead.

product_title: Parker IM Gold Brushed Metal GT Fountain-Pen, Gold Trims, Steel Fine Nib.
review_body: Parker is in my opinion the finest producer of economical yet elegant and well constructed writing instruments.  The I.M. is a large barreled, wide grip and weighty pen.  It has a very hefty feel and is comfortable to use.  The pen, barrel alone is light, but when the top is put into place on the end of the barrel the pen becomes proportionally well balanced.  I have owned both the ball point and the fountain tip and I have found that the ball point is almost flawless and is easy to use.  The only drawback is that the pen can at times write faster than you can think.  Meaning the flow of ink against the paper is copious and the tip can get away from you if you are not careful.  The fountain pen does not fall prey to the same type of flaw, where it does come up short is the fact that the nib has a tendency to dry while writing and will press through the paper if you are using thin or recycled material.  The nib is also very fickle about how you hold it.  Most pens especially Parker pens are very forgiving when you hold a fountain tip a few degrees off center but for some reason the I.M. is not at all forgiving.  Thus allowing one more way for the pen to find its way through the paper.  The pen for its design is a well balanced and comfortable instrument but can be unforgivably stubborn when not held in proper position.

product_title: Epson Artisan 730 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer, Copier, Scanner (iOS/Tablet/Smartphone/AirPrint Compatible) (C11CB18201)
review_body:
As of this writing, I've been using the Epson Artisan 730 wireless, daily, for about a month. Connecting it to my WiFi network following the supplied instructions went well. I've been printing from my Macs over WiFi with no problems. Print quality on paper and DVDs are great and the photocopier is fast and near silent in operation. Printing on both sides using the automated system works as advertised.

The only downside I'd say is that I can no longer run non-Epson authorized (thick) art paper through the printer as it is not a rear feeding printer but takes the paper from a tray in the underside bottom. I've tried to print on matte board but the printer won't accept the paper --- which my old Epson Stylus 1400 rear feeder had no problem accepting. As such, anyone who needs a printer that can print on thick card stock -- art-board, water-colour paper, matte board, (Designers you know who you are)-- should look for a traditional rear feed printer. I forgot to account for this when doing my research so I may have to purchase a rear feed printer in the future.

Other than not printing on thick card stock, this printer/scanner/copier is an excellent choice for home & home office user.

review_headline: Good but did not last one day without breaking.
review_body:

One minor issue (major for some people) is that this is not a calligraphy pen. You will not get the thin downward strokes and the thicker horizontal strokes. The resulting writing is similar to a nice biro so if you want a recognizable fountain pen writing this is not the pen for you.

The pen does come with the ink converter and ink cartridges and has a label on the outside with real writing initials on to show that it has been inspected.

However into just the first day of using it I had it in my pocket and without thinking lifted up the clip with a finger while the lid was still attached to the pen. With minimal effort the end of the lid snapped off and it took the clip with it. The pen is still usable but there is a hole on the end of the lid now. Might I purchase it again? Possibly. But I have lifted the clips on previous fountain pens priced at a similar price point and they did not snap off.

product_title: Kodak ESP 2150 Wireless Color Printer with Scanner, Copier & Fax
review_body: I have never taken the time to write a review before, so this just shows how passionate I am about this, DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY ON THIS PRINTER!!! I purchased this printer without reading reviews (my mistake), thinking I would save money as the cost was low (it was a black Friday deal) and the cost of ink was low and I would barely use it. I didn't have any trouble setting up, connecting it to my wifi or anything like that. The problem lies in the actual printing, which is what I need/want it for. For some strange reason it needs two separate ink cartridges, one for color and one for black yet you can't print unless both are full. I rarely if ever use color ink yet for some reason it will keep depleting, and when the color ink is low the black is not sufficient for printing. Faxes will not come through and I cannot print. It doesn't even allow the faxes or printing to come through in a lighter or hard to read version. Without Caller Id, I wouldn't know who was trying to fax me something. This is my first Kodak printer so, I don't know if they all work like this, but I do know that with my previous HP printers I never had this problem. HP used the color you needed and when black was low you could print in grayscale and print even more. This printer was a total waste of money. I will never buy another Kodak printer again! On and on the box it says something like \\"lowest ink cost,\\" however I am going to go ahead and dispute this based on the fact that you replace the ink way more often than you would any other ink cartridges. Oh, and another thing I'm not to found of is that you can't set it so that you can receive fax confirmations after you send a fax to someone. Yep, invest your money in another brand.

product_title: HP Premium Plus Photo Paper, Soft Gloss (100 Sheets, 4 x 6 Inch with Tab)
review_body:
Okay y'all, here's the deal, in my humble, and newbie's opinion (for those of you searching aimlessly for the right paper as I was not long ago). First of all, I new I wanted a semi-gloss type paper, as that's what we used in my high school (not all that long ago, but yes, I went FOREVER before finally getting a decent photo printer) photography/digital art class, and it turned out beautiful prints- and it's what I'm used to. So I went looking for more paper, when the glossy paper that came with my new hp printer ran out.

Anyway, I searched and cross-referenced to find the right size (4x6, obviously), finish, and rating. When I finally found 4x6 soft gloss paper, all I could find that was reasonably priced was this one, \\"with tab\\" which I'd never seen, nor heard of before. I read complaints about it, but I was thinking \\"tab\\" meant a small extension, maybe an inch wide by 1-1/2\\" long... NOPE. It extends the entire length of the bottom of the photo, and on my printer comes out at the top, and the serrated edge DOES NOT come off clean. I gave up after butchering a few pics, and started just waiting for them to 'dry' and then using my paper-cutter to cut the end off (you can surely imagine what a pain in the rear that is- and I'm sure not everyone has a paper cutter hanging around).

PLUS the whole NEED for a \\"tab\\" leads one to believe that even though it is soft-gloss paper, it needs quite a bit of dry time. Therefore, it's VERY annoying not knowing A: How long one must wait to handle the photo (and cut the d*mn tab off); and B: Is it okay to print multiple prints at a time..? Or will this smear the first print? And as I'm a bit over-cautious/paranoid, my printer and small table adjacent to it are covered in photo prints, as I'm back-logged in pics to print, for framing, scrap-booking, etc.

OKAY as for the QUALITY of the paper itself, THAT, my friends, is the reason it has earned its 2 stars. It is indeed a great paper. I really love it, actually. It's a nice, heavy weight that you can feel, in addition to seeing it in the quality print. I love the \\"Soft-gloss\\" finish. Seemed like maybe there were some incidents and they had to add that precaution. I realized I really didn't care about the battery backup feature. I don't use the unit to store numbers. I just want to screen callers before picking up so I just didn't insert batteries.

I spent some time trying to figure out how to set the time and date, only to find out it sets itself with the first call. To delete all the numbers, press and hold the delete button. You can use this unit to place return calls; I haven't tried that.

Another reviewer said the red light does not stay illuminated to alert you to new calls, but it does. It flashes until you view any new calls. Not real big or bright but it does its thing.

product_title: Brother TN450 High Yield Black Toner/2-Pack
review_headline: High yield - may be. But that TONER LOW popup is very annoying
review_body:
Like most people, I bought this TN450 when I purchased MFC7860DW as the feedback were consistent that the starter toner TN420 has such a short life.

Well, we have been printing+copying from this printer at the rate of ~100/150 page a week (normal full text page). To my surprise, this TN450 only last 5 weeks when the dreadful \\"Toner Low\\" popped up. That was not even half of workload that it supposed to be !!!

I know that it can still print several more pages. But that TONER LOW pop up is very very annoying. As it also show up on the PC screen every now and then (this is on top of my wife and kids keep saying . . . \\"Dad . . we've got toner low again !!!\\" I then order the refill kit and really examine how the reset gear work. So far, this simple plastic gear is THE ONLY thing that trigger toner low or toner life end message regardless of the actual amount of toner remain in it. As a test, I opened TN420 (after TONER LOW for 3 weeks) and pour out the remaining ink. My goodness, it was quite a lot.

So, for those who has not yet experienced this. When you get TONER LOW message, I suggest you order your refill kit to be ready when needed. Then continue to print until it won't print anymore or the TONER LIFE END message comes up. Then you refill it. In fact, I suspect that even if TONER LIFE END comes up, you may be able to just reset that gear without refilling the toner, it will still be able to print for a while (providing that you can endure the bugging request from your love ones when they see that toner low thing). This uneasy situation (induced by a poor design from Brother) is the only reason I take one star out. Otherwise, printing quality and price is pretty good and comparable to other Brother MFC model.

Now, I have my TN420 refilled and installed with the reset gear and the TN450 refilled/reset as well. I will update again in a couple of weeks.

product_title: Kodak ESP C315 Wireless Color Printer with Scanner & Copier
review_headline: Not A Great Printer, But Great Customer Support, UPDATES
review_body:
WIRELESS FUNCTION: \\"Iffy\\"-- worked fine connecting for a room in our home much further away from the router, with more obstacles, (that room's pc OS is Windows 7) but would not complete final connection step for a room much closer to router with less obstacles (that room's pc OS is Vista) weird; however, the ability to print remotely is extremely handy;
CLOUD FUNCTION: My husband uses an iPhone, and he has raved about the convenience of the \\"cloud\\";
PRINT QUALITY: just okay, really bad if printhead is faulty/defective; (please see my photos)
EASE OF ACCESS TO REPLACE INK CARTRIDGES: Very easy, just lift the hood and lift out old/slip in new; (please see my photos)
TIME BETWEEN NEEDING TO CHANGE THE 2 INK CARTRIDGES: Using the draft quality more often than the normal quality, the time between needing to change the black cartridge has been frequent, the color less frequent--it seems to drink up the ink quicker than my old HP Deskjet F4440, which is older technology;
SCANNING OPTION:This has worked consistently well with no problems;
COPY OPTION: This also has worked consistently well with no problems;
LED DISPLAY: Bright, easy to read and adjustable;
NOISE LEVEL WHEN PRINTING: Suprisingly, this is louder than we expected, not a quiet printer;
KODAK CUSTOMER SUPPORT: Very good! We didn't have to jump through hoops to get support for what is apparently a faulty printer head, and they are going to send us out a replacement printhead at no charge to us, so I am pleased to say that our experience with Kodak customer support has been a positive one.

OUR EXPERIENCE WITH THIS PRINTER:
I purchased this printer spur of the moment when it was on sale in a brick and mortar store about 8 months ago with pretty high hopes. I loved the idea of wireless printing, and with the Kodak name, I felt I would be able to print out some pretty high-quaility photos that I had been taking. When I had tried to the wireless function up in my art studio, which is about 30 feet from the router, with only one corner between it and the printer...our network was detected, but this printer never would connect. I followed the directions, and then the troubleshooting steps, but after an hour I was just too frustrated to give it another try. My husband decided to put it in his office, which is about 60 feet away between the router and his office, but was able to wirelessly connect right away. Since then, there have been no problems with it maintaining a good connection. Something we really love about this printer is our children can easily print their homework wirelessly with this printer. My husband loves the cloud features and has found this function to be very handy.
The print quality of photos has been just okay, nothing especially great, always using the genuine Kodak ink cartridges, which kind of suprised both of us. However, he uses this primarily for documents with only a small amount of images, so he was satisfied that it printed those out okay.
However, about a month ago, the print quality greatly deteriorated, leaving reds looking pink, yellow barely printing out, and some portions of the page missing ink. After having replaced the ink cartridges, doing the alignments, cleaning the print heads, last night, we went to the Kodak customer support site, found the printer's model number (ESP C315) and issue (poor print quality) from the drop down menu on the troubleshooting site, then followed the simple troubleshooting steps, At the end of it, the troubleshooter displayed that there is an issue with the printer that cannot be fixed by us, would we like to contact customer support, gave us a referral number, and the chat or email option.
We chose the chat option, and after answering a few questions, the support person told us that the printhead had a defect, and they would be sending a new printhead at no charge to us. The support person sent us an email verifiying everything. This morning, we were sent an email stating that this printhead is currently out of stock, but it would be delivered to us as soon as it was available.*SEE UPDATE BELOW*

IN CONCLUSION: While I would not buy this particular printer again or highly recommend it, I would certainly consider buying another Kodak printer (after doing research, and reading others' reviews) because I have found that the Kodak customer support was courteous and willing to replace what they concluded was a faulty printhead (at no charge or hassle to us 8 months after we purchased this printer). I didn't have to dig out my receipt or jump through any hoops, the Kodak support person seemed earnest in wanting to be sure we were satisfied. That (good customer support) is very important to me and keeps me open and willing to buy another product from a company that backs their products and is willing to send out whatever is necessary to remedy the issue at hand.

*UPDATE*: True to their word, Kodak sent us an email notification today that the replacement printhead has been shipped, only 2 days after the email stating that it was out of stock, but would be sent as soon as it became available. As I stated in my earlier review, I would certainly consider buying another Kodak product, as the customer service is hassle-free and true to their word if a problem with the product should occur. Also, if we find that the print quality is better with the new printhead is better than the regular print quality that we had up until the printouts became clearly defective, I will be sure to come back and *update this review and stars to reflect that, as I can't help but wonder if we never experienced great quality in our print jobs because the printhead that came with the machine was never fully up to snuff to begin with.

*SECOND UPDATE: The printhead replacement arrived within a week of first contacting Kodak support, even with the delay for the out of stock status, and it was super easy to take out the old printhead and putting in the new replacement one. We did not find, however, that the print quality was any better than the quality of the print jobs before any of the problems began. I am very impressed with Kodak support's easy, courteous and prompt customer support and because of that, would consider buying another (but different model) printer from them in the future. So, still 3 stars for our experience with the printer, but 5 stars for Kodak customer support.

review_body:

Outside boards are thicker and tougher, and should hold up to regular handling and shelf scuffing.
The pocket dividers are sturdy which means they won't tear just from getting things out of the folder.

Usage:
It's perfect for keeping track of those loose receipts and loose papers, especially small pieces of paper that you might want to include. However, it lacks a latching top cover. So I use a bungee cord to keep it compact when traveling. If you need an open file for your office that you don't plan to travel with it, this is for you.

Con:
My biggest complaint about the product is that it's just the slightest bit too narrow to put file folders in. And papers need to be securely stapled or paper-clipped together before going in if you want to easily get them all back out.

Summary:
Overall, if you don't mind the missing cover, this is a good product for the value.

review_headline: Scratches easily, beware using with Stylus Pro 3880
review_body:

Also there was a problem with microscopic white dots in dark areas. I found out the white dots are a known issue (which Epson tech support did not tell me about) resulting from paper dust coating the new paper which flakes off after the ink dries. This topic turned up in extensive forum research and has been a big problem for Epson. Each piece must be carefully cleaned of paper dust before printing. The printing surface is much too delicate. Extreme caution must be used as it scratches easily. Must be spray coated with Krylon Crystal Clear or Hahnemule spray to prevent dry prints from scratching, which adds considerably to the cost and production time.

I'm on my 4th replacement printer now and it is scratching the Exhibition Fiber paper, too. I now must send the paper back to Epson for a refund and look for a different, less archival, less desirable surface, probably resin coated paper that will run through the 3880 without scratching. This has been a big hassle for my business as I put much effort into marketing the archival and fine photographic quality of the 3880/Exhibition Fiber combination. Black and White prints made with advanced control of the 3880 on Exhibition Fiber do look great, until you notice the scratches. Bottom line: expensive paper ends up being more trouble than it's worth.

Would love to hear from anyone who's had similar issues with this paper and/or the Stylus Pro 3880, especially if you've got a solution.

product_title: uni-ball Jetstream RT Ballpoint Pen Refill
review_body:
I find that these pens are a lot more finicky about what kind of paper is being used compared to their smaller-tipped counterparts (e.g. 0.7s and 0.5s). They write excellent on more expensive printer-paper and individual sheets, but on some of the cheaper white notebook paper or yellow steno-pad paper I typically live on, these pens sputter and stutter to no end. They leave gross \\"blank spots\\" across all my characters and it's incredibly frustrating.

Additionally, it's worth noting that because of the larger tip, these pens glide across paper much more smoothly. This may be a plus point for some or a minus point for others. Because these pens have a tendency to leave blank spots, I would've preferred that they offer slightly more resistance to the paper -- something that is also solved by using a smaller tip. Nevertheless, this isn't something I'd detract any stars for.

Having said that, buy with caution. If you're uncertain whether these pens will write well on your preferred medium, I would suggest it's a safer bet to go with 0.7s or 0.5s. The smaller-tipped Uni-Balls I've used have had much better performance across a larger range of media than these 1.0s.

product_title: Epson Expression Home XP-400 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer, Copier, Scanner.  Prints from Tablet/Smartphone. AirPrint Compatible (C11CC07201)
review_headline: Light as a feather, but a piece of crap
review_body: I purchased the printer and noted that it didn't contain a printer cable.  I planned on using it connected direct with my main computer and as a wirless for the others on my network.  I had to purchase the cable.  The cost of the cable equaled almost 1/3 the price of the printer since it was on sale for $74.00 at Best Buy.  I'm glad I did since the cable is recommended when installing the printer and based on some odd problems others have experienced when attempting an install without the cable I'm glad I pruchased it.  The printer set up easily, and downloaded updated software AND firmware automaticaly from the internet.  I test printed a few pages and noticed that the paper feed did not have a movable stop on the left hand side as most printers do.  After printing the first page the next sheet cocked in the feed tray.  It did continue to feed straight, but the continued cocking of EVERY sheet worried me and I clipped a 1/4x1/4x1 inch piece of plastic using a large moveable clip to the feed tray. This kept the paper straight in the tray when loading paper for printing.  I use a program to monitor all installations and noted that several pieces of software that weren't chosen with the install were loaded.  I had chosen NOT to load any of the extra tracking software that came with the installation.  Frankly, it is possible that the additional tracking software was added by the Epson site since it must have reviewed what I had loaded from the disk.  Since these additional programs loaded on startup and took up memory I eliminated them from the download and kept the three items of software necessary to keep the printer and other features working.  The program I used is called advanced uninstaller pro and it removes ALL downloaded software that you pick including the stuff added to the registry that is usually not uninstalled by Windows.  I tried various features of the printer and all seemed to work well.  The print quality is good and the print speed is fair.  The printer is very light and seems very cheaply constructed.  I have not tried printing photos and don't intend on doing so.  I use a dedicated high quality printer for that purpose.  Considering what I paid for this printer it's a value even without the cable.  I wasn't happy with the software or site adding tracking software to my computer.  Update: The printer does "Automatic checking" to see if any software or firmware updates are required.  When this is done even if you selected NOT to download tracking software or removed it once downloaded by the site it will redownload the tracking software if you allow Automatic Checking.  Disable this feature to prevent the tracking software from being downloaded each time Automatic checking occurs.  It seems this happens every two or three weeks.  3/9/2015 Update.  I just downgraded the review to a one star from three.  If you haven't used the printer for a couple of days it prints every other line only.  You have to clean the heads each time and that uses a lot of ink in the process and the ink is expensive.  This is the worse printer I've ever owned

Setup was a snap. I plugged it into my Mac, and it worked right away. I used the free version of Express Scribe to play the audio and it did so flawlessly with my new foot pedal. I configured the pedal so I could use my left toe to depress the left pedal to rewind the audio, and the right foot to depress the middle pedal to play the audio.

Unfortunately, Express Scribe itself seems to have compatibility issues with Mac OS Mountain Lion - when I try to type in the text box for Express Scribe, the program crashes and asks to restart. Since, the Express Scribe website stated that this particular Infinity pedal would not work with the free version of Express Scribe but would work with the paid Pro version, I tried upgrading to the Pro version, hoping everything would work. But of course it didn't. :p

I now use Express Scribe (Pro) to play the audio (assisted by the foot pedal), and type out the text on TextEdit, which is the default word processor for Mac.

When the foot pedal is left plugged in overnight, it stops working with Express Scribe. But restarting the program and disconnecting-reconnecting the foot pedal gets it working again. This awesome and comfortable foot pedal has so far seen me through over an hour's worth of audio thus far, and does what it promises to do - it leaves my fingers free to type.

product_title: Franklin SCD-1890 Speaking Merriam-Webster's Collegiate Dictionary, 11th Edition
review_body:
Franklin SCD-1890 electronic Dictionary, is not my first e-Dictionary; but the first one which I'm unhappy with. Previous e-dictionaries, you get instant access to search word's meaning(s). While turning on the present e-dictionary you reach a menu whose options one rarely used and it requires superfluous manipulation to access the dictionary, which can get on one's nerves if you have to do it all over tens of times per day. The words search in the dictionary should be instantly accessible by default.
Additional problem exist when you need to search for phrases or idioms. You may result empty handed and this in spite the fact that the phrase you are looking for is there but inaccessible. I'll demonstrate my point with first hand experience: I looked up in the thesaurus for \\"spill the beans\\", found it and also found among the synonyms the idiom \\"let the cat out of the bag\\" tried to search the dictionary for additional meanings for \\"spill the beans\\" but the search lead me to the word \\"spill\\" and had to scroll several frames to the bottom to find the whole phrase printed there; my question is, why it can't be reached instantly? I faced similar happening while searching the dictionary for idioms: \\"off the wall\\" and \\"let the cat out of the bag\\". Regarding the search of 'let ... cat ...bag\\" in the thesaurus, you get the message: \\"no thesaurus entry\\" How come!? I just saw it in the thesaurus less than 5 min. ago. Another absurd encounter while searching \\"right on target\\" in both dictionary and thesaurus, they resulted in the same message:\\"Sorry, I can't help\\", while I saw this phrase before listed in the thesaurus as an antonym for \\"on the wall\\". Bottom line the information is right there but out of your reach during a search. It seems that this electronic device is incompletely programmed therefore unable to recognize ALL idioms and phrases as a one whole unit sentence; which makes this electronic device insufficient for cross word reference checks. After all this is the crux reason for which e-dictionary are design for to cross check instantly with the push of a button which is a time saving process , otherwise one can continue using volumes of books.
The Spelling Bee sounds like gibberish, needless to say that it's useless for spelling practice. Fortunately the dictionary sound much better and with new battery it sounds is very clear.
The section of 5-language dictionary is speechless (soundless) it doesn't even have a written phonetic pronunciation guide. The selected vocabulary is mainly for truism purpose.
I didn't face any problem reading the screen although many users did. While reading in bed I use an overhead light and everything is visible. The words in this dictionary are clearly and thorough explained and difficult and uncommon headwords have exemplified sentences to demonstrate usage. Some headwords also contain related synonyms for \\"fine tuning\\", which are listed sequentially with the explanation of common and different meaning and usage. The presence of these features causes me to elevate my evaluation from 1 star to 2 stars.

review_headline: OK, but not my personal preference.....
review_body:
This paper is just what it states it is; white 24-lb heavyweight paper. It works fine in my Hewlett Packard Ink Jet Printer [[ASIN:B0040XYTIW HP Deskjet 3050 All-in-One Printer (CH376A#B1H)]].

Even though I work from home; I rarely have need for this weight paper. I generallly use Georgia-Pacific 20-weight paper which is adequate for all my needs.

However, since paper needs vary based on use; this GP Ink Jet and Laser Paper in 24-lb weight/92 brightness is okay as heavier papers go. The paper has a nice heft to it and the color is fine. It did not jam and the ink did not smear.

There are unexplained ridges in the paper that I received. It made is seem perhaps the item was the result of a 'bad run' of paper, I have no other explaination as there didn't seem to be a good reason for this.

If you need 24-lb paper this would probably be acceptable, but if you are willing to pay the price for 24-lb paper, a quick look at your local office supply would probably yield better quality for the money.

However, what really gets to me is that there are no instructions.  Nothing to tell me to hold the button on the side of the unit to turn it on, etc.  Also, there is absolutely nothing to tell me how to insert the battery.  Positive end first or negative end first?  Why this is important is that most batteries insert into a device with the negative side toward the spring (which is usually at rear of the unit).  Whereas most battery springs are on the bottom, the spring on this unit is up inside the cylinder housing.  So do I insert the negative side first?  Heck if I know - because there are no instructions.  More to follow as I get the battery charged.

product_title: Kodak P811 8x10 Personal Photo and Negative Scanner
review_body: There are many reviews that say this product doesnt work right or it is hard to use, but it seems to me that most of the complaints about it are due to user error, not a malfunction of the scanner. I have scanned hundreds of photos so far and have had awesome results! If you take your time putting the picture into the scanner and make sure its lined up right(not that hard to do), it works great! There is a plastic sheath to use with photos that are bent, thick, damaged in some way, or very old and fragile. You can also use the sheath to scan any other paper items (recipes, business cards, etc).  I have not noticed any problems with color. Some of the old pictures have a red tint to them, but the original picture has that color. All of my scans look exactly like the original paper photo. If you want to be able to save your old memories, it does take some time, but it is well worth it! My mother in law is excited that she will be able to pass on ALL of her photos to her kids without having to decide who gets what picture. They can all have a copy EVERY picture she has! I would definitely recommend this scanner to my friends and family.

product_title: RCA 25110RE3 - cordless phone w/ call waiting caller ID & wireless headset
review_body:
Absolutely a great idea and I am not sure if there is any thing else out there quite like it (thus I bought another unit when the first one finally died). BUT . . . they built this thing cheaply (mainly the headset). Headset is flimsy. And the cheap rechargeable batteries will need replacing/upgrading soon.

Briefly this is a cordless phone with caller ID display. When not in use, the phone handset lives in it's charger stand. The phone handset receives its signal from a wall transmitter unit which plugs directly into an AC wall outlet and must also be plugged into your home phone jack. And . . . you get a headset. The headset also lives in the charger stand. When in use, it gets it's signal from the phone handset (which can be on your belt, or can still be in the charger stand). You can use the hanset to call out while using the headset. Very versatile.

User tip - if experiencing feedback in the headset - turn down the headset volume some - that should fix the feedback squeal.

review_body: I carefully read all the major reviews before buying this phone. They were helpful and accurate in general. After receiving the phone and using it for 3 weeks, we sent it back to Amazon. What happens if you are retrieving a message of a very sensitive nature and a client walks into the office and hears the message? product_title: Epson WorkForce WF-7010 Wide-Format Color Inkjet Printer (C11CB59201)
review_body:
I use this to print web pages and screen captures in full color on relatively inexpensive (compared to 13x19 anyways) 11x17 paper. The extra width and length make all the difference in the world for marking up designs or to see the bigger picture. The installation was easy, make sure if you are downloading the software to get the full package since the driver's only package doesn't connect over the Ethernet (as least it didn't for me). Speaking of Ethernet, it's a little disappointing that it doesn't have wifi and the the ethernet cable sticks out from the side of the printer decreasing it's clean line appeal a little. But those are still little things and the dual paper ports which allow two different sizes in either bay and a nice quality print more than makes up for it. I don't think I would consider this a photo printer since it only has four inks, but it handles those four inks superbly and most business applications will be well served.

PROS:
+ Nice clean prints
+ Big prints for a reasonable price
+ Dual trays, each can accommodate any of the supported sizes
+ Ethernet makes sharing easy

CONS:
- No WiFi
- Ethernet port is on the side making wire push out, would've been nicer if the port was on the back
- Driver only install didn't work on Win 7 over Ethernet, but full install did

product_title: Generic Compatible Ink Cartridge Replacement for Epson T060 (4xBlack, 2xCyan, 2xMagenta, 2xYellow, 10-Pack)
review_headline: Great price, functioned acceptably in Epson Stylus CX3810, squirted black ink on my rug..
review_body:
This ink comes at an unbeatable price. The print quality is not good, but this can be overcome by selecting higher print quality like \\"Photo\\" or \\"Best Photo\\" underneath the Properties button on the Print menu. It appears to use a lot more ink that way, but since this ink is so cheap I have no qualms about this.

I have two complaints, one minor, one MAJOR: First, the status monitor will always tell me there is no more ink even though I can still hear some sloshing around in there when I pull the cartridge out, shake it, and re-install. I recycle my cartridges, and I have to keep these in plastic bags because the supposedly empty cartridge leaks all over in the bag. Perhaps a chip resetter would correct this problem, but I don't have one.

My second, AND MUCH BIGGER COMPLAINT: All four black ink cartridges squirted a GEYSER of ink all over when I peeled off the \\"Pull\\" tab. The first time, I was not expecting this, and it ruined a pair of (luckily cheap) pants. I had black spots on my skin even after a couple of showers. It also got all over the carpet in my apartment, which the complex (even more luckily) chalked up to normal wear-and-tear. I took care to open all the remaining cartridges outdoors wrapped in an old towel, but only the black ones did this.

In a nutshell: Jack up your print settings, and these will still be a great buy. But for Pete's sake, open these inside a plastic bag or wrapped in a rag or something!

review_headline: My second Water Brush from Pentel
review_body: I love the Pentel Water brushes or \\"pens\\". I have a large tip I've used for quite a while, and just received the medium tip recently. These work very well...it takes a few uses to get used to the flow, but once you do, you'll see why these are better than the cheapy three-pack types. The brush tip is soft and delivers a nice steady flow of water, without over-doing it. You can fill the reservoir part of the way or fully, with just a slight squeeze, and have nice control over the saturation....especially when using water soluable pencils, as I do. I highly recommend getting at least a medium tip and a large tip, for a great little set of water brushes that aren't hard on the wallet!

product_title: Open End Policy Envelopes - 5" x 11 1/2
review_body:
I also got these envelopes for our wedding invitations, which is also planned to have a botanical/vintage/natural feel.

PROS:
*The \\"regular\\" size 10 envelope made it easy to set up my printer to print on them and I knew they were okay for a regular postage stamp
*The opening on the short end made it feel a little more special to me
*The color is exactly the \\"brown paper bag\\" look and texture I was hoping for
*I had no difficulty with the sealing glue

CONS:
*The opening on the short end made the width of the invitation a lot less forgiving than a traditional long-side opening is. I had 4 components to my invitation, held together by a very thin twine and it was a tight fit. Any thicker, and it would have been a disaster.
* The lady at the Post Office threatened that they would need additional hand-cancelling due to the short-end opening. Another PO worker disagreed with her (luckily!) and they took them at the regular rate. NOTE: This is done by weight, so while mine made the cut, if your invite is heavier, it may need additional postage anyway.
* I printed the addresses on a laser-jet printer, and for some reason, the ink didn't apply as firmly as I expected. I really liked the look of it, but I worry that it may wear off during shipping. I don't know if this was the fault of the porous paper, or my particular printer.

I would buy these again; I love the way they turned out!

review_body: I love my Ooma service. Very low cost with a ton more features than before with traditional phone service. And so far, it's been very reliable. Thanks Ooma!

review_body:

No additional software is required for file transfer. Some reviewers have emphasized that the file date format is non-standard (yyyymmdd). review_headline: Extremely disappointed and out a lot of money
review_body: I purchased a couple packs of the Avery light t-shirt transfer packs to customize our girl scout troop t-shirts for a huge event we would be attending.  We even choose to put our design on the t-shirt from the event to help make us stand out.  Because I had never used this product before I chose to do a sample test on an old t-shirt.  I followed all the directions including pre-washing, applying pressure for the recommended time, cooling time, etc.  My sample came out marvelously, so I preceeded to printout and place our designs on 21 shirts.  I had no issues getting the transfers to stick or even getting the paper off. I'm extremely disappointed and angry that we spent all this money purchasing shirts and transfer sheets, only to have them completely ruined by the use of this product. Note that this is not a perfect solution because you still get exposed to the light (around the opening of the glove), but I believe it's still better than nothing.
The glove is a bit tight yes, but that's so that it doesn't slide and messes up your nail polish. Personally, while I do not have small hands, I found that the gloves are still comfortable. The length for the fingers is appropriate and if it's too long, it can be adjusted without fearing that the finger parts will slide back down onto your nail.

The two cons I find to this glove:
- the thumb part which is shorter and less tight, leaving the thumb more exposed than the other fingers
- the quality is not perfect. I will upload pictures, and you'll see there are some threads sticking out and some parts need to be sewn better. That's not a huge problem and it's fixable, but I think they could have done a better job at it.

product_title: Swingline Paper Shredder, 12 Sheet Capacity, Super Cross-Cut, 1 User, Personal
review_headline: Easily the best shredder I have owned
review_body:
Now, I should say that my shredder needs are fairly limited. I just need to shed old checks, credit card statements, and similar paper. Someone with greater needs may well want to purchase a more heavy duty shredder.

Things I like about this shredder:

1. Compact, so it fits easily under a desk or table.
2. Easy to remove shredder bin. Too many shredders have the bin under the shredding unit. That design requires you to lift the heavy shredding unit and put it to one side -- usually spilling shreds of paper from the teeth of the shredder -- to access the bin. Then, after emptying the bin, you have to make sure that the shredding unit is properly placed on the bin. This unit has a slide out bin that is very easy to empty.
3. Cross-cutting leaves paper well shredded.

Minor drawbacks:

1. Relatively small shredder bin needs to be emptied frequently, but, as noted above, it easy to empty.
2. Can't be used for more than three minutes or so continuously without the threat of overheating. If it overheats, you need to wait 30 minutes to use it again.

So, overall, if you need a shredder for light home or home office use, you can't go wrong with this unit.

product_title: LD Brother Compatible TN-210 Laser Toner Cartridges: Black TN210BK, Cyan TN210C, Magenta TN210M, Yellow TN210Y
review_headline: Works beautifully in my Brother MFC-9320CW
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:moL9WO8Z04IESW]]I've not had any problems using \\"compatible\\" printer cartridges from LD in my Brother MFC-9320CW color laser printer.

When you buy a \\"compatible\\" cartridge, it will often look quite different from the OEM cartridge. This cartridge is no exception. It fits perfectly into the printer, but the design of the cartridge is different enough to be easily identifiable as a non-OEM cartridge. In this case the design is preferred since the cartridge I got had a, more or less clear back panel that allowed me to actually see the toner inside the cartridge. This is nice because for the first time I was able to actually see how much toner is inside the cartridge, and how much might be left once the printer alerts me that a toner cartridge is getting low.

Print quality is as far as I can tell exactly the same as using the more expensive Brother cartridges.

review_body: I previously had a Uniden Dect 6.0 three portable phone answering system. One for home office, bedroom, and family room. One phone went out of commission due to keys that stuck. product_title: Brother PT1290 Home and Office Labeler
review_body:
This label-maker is perfect for my small office needs; it uses up to 1/2\\" tape, prints clearly (the \\"italic\\" style is a bit more pixel-ey than the normal style), and, contrary to what many reviewers seem to have problems with, does not waste that much tape - if you set the margins to \\"narrow\\", or do multiple labels at a time with \\"chain print\\", there is absolutely no problem for me.
I love the different label styles you can create; they print clearly and add a little more \\"zing\\" to otherwise routine labels.
The only complaint I have is that I haven't figured out yet how to delete all the text at one time; I read through the instructions manual and can't seem to find this option, so it takes about 5 seconds to backspace through longer label text.
I've used Brother products in the past at my former workplace (don't recall the exact model number) and this one seems to have a very similar interface, just more options, which was great for me.

product_title: Brother Printer HL2270DW Wireless Monochrome Printer
review_body:
The printer was delivered very quickly and was easy to set up. I have a home network with a router and a seperate print server so I can print to my choice of printers from multiple PCs. The printer's included software not only installed the drivers, but it found and set uo the printer on the network, something that can be a little tricky.

The original toner cartridge is apparently a \\"starter cartridge\\" and began giving \\"low toner\\" messages after a few hundred sheets. I purchased a replacement but the original is still printing fine, just putting the annoying messages on the screen after each print job.

It's pretty cool that it can print double sided without manually reinserting the pages to do the other side. The paper comes out, goes back in, and comes out again with both sides printed.

BTW: The price was a third of the cost of my previous printer and it has more features and is much faster.

product_title: 1 X Wholesale Lot of 10 Credit Card Sized Wallet Magnifiers 3X Lenses by OpticLens
review_body:
I ordered these as a back up means of starting a fire while camping/in survival situation/etc. They do their job swimmingly. It took me two attempts and some patience to get a fire going but this was not due to the lens, just my experience with it. The focal point, when positioned properly, can be smaller than a pea. The lenses are made of clear plastic which flexes nicely and they come with a clear plastic cover to protect it from scratches. The cover isn't anything to write home about but it is there. The lens is also super thin and fits nicely in an Altoids tin if you were wondering. :p

In my first attempt to start a fire with one, I managed to burn a couple holes in some cardboard. Second time I got more material together, set it up better, and went to work. Did its job very well and I am quite pleased with the product. When focused correctly, a semi dark piece of material will start to smoke/smolder very quickly with enough sunlight. Hope this helps anyone looking to get it!

product_title: Learning Resources Real World Folding Geometric Shapes Set of 8
review_body:
You can use the flattened forms to teach symmetry and surface area with older children. There is an activity guide included that gives parents suggestions for discussion questions, such as, 'Which shapes have mostly rectangular faces?' There are many different activities in the guide, such as 'mix and match' where you remove all the 'nets' (the inserts) and lay them out next to the empty clear shapes and your child has to match up the flattened paper version of the shape to the 3dimensional plastic shapes.

These shapes encourage her to make real world connections with her environment, such as realizing that an ice cream cone and a party hat are both the same cone shape. I like that the shapes offer something tangible that she can manipulate in her own hands, versus just looking at 2dimensional drawings of shapes in a book. To me, this is much more meaningful, and therefore, more memorable.

I feel like she will have an advantage when she starts learning about geometric shapes in school. My daughter already asked me if she could bring in the geometric shapes for share day at kindergarten this week, instead of her usual choice, a toy. All in all, I feel very satisfied with this product and would definitely recommend it.

product_title: Kodak ESP 7250 All-in-One Printer
review_body:
Every Kodak printer I've ever had has been loud and slow, so I wasn't surprised this one was too. The reason I've stayed with Kodak is because I've never had any technical problems. For those who complain about ink costs, I'm not sure how you go through it so quickly because I'm an amateur photographer who prints about 100 photos a month and my ink needs replaced about every 3 months. product_title: Canon PIXMA MX892 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner, Copier and Fax

Here's why:
Wireless Scanning AT THE MACHINE

- You push the button, choose the type of scan (PDF, Image), and then you have the choice of choosing which network connected computer to scan to.
- I have an iMac (with OS X AND Win7 on it via VM Ware), a MacBook Pro, an Acer Laptop, a Dell XPS, and a clone PC
- If the computers are on and connected to my network, they all show up in a list to choose from
- You choose the computer, then press SCAN and it starts to scan
- I tried it on all my computers & platforms & it worked flawlessly! Great software!
- I absolutely LOVE Canon's MP Navigator. It pops up, the scan is saved into it, and you're ready to use the file. AWESOME!!!

Wireless Setup:
- Super easy! Tell the machine you want to use Wireless and it looks for wireless access points (routers)
- You select your router and enter a password if you use one (I do)
- It then connects and that's it! You're done!

To set up your computer to talk to the printer, just install the software & let it run through the install
- Your computer will detect the printer and whoala! You're ready to print (or scan or fax) over wireless!
- Canon definitely rocks in this department and setting up the MX892 over my MX860 for wireless was even simpler.

Faxing:
- Super simple. Plug in your phone line, and it's pretty much ready to fax

Printing:
- It prints quicker than my MX860 does
- The ink tanks look a little smaller and if it's like the 860 I'm sure it'll eat through them like water

Copying:

- Lift the lid, put something on the copy glass, select the # of copies, and press copy

Software:
- Canon's printing software has to be some of the best out there. I've tried lots of others and I'm hooked on Canon
- Super easy install, super easy to use, and it \\"just works!\\" Every time!

- I tested some of the downloadable templates on the printer

Thoughts:
- If you're looking for an easy to set up, easy to use Multi-function printer, then look no farther. Setup couldn't be simpler and it just works. Every time!
- The Canon MFP's do drink ink like it's going out of style (my MX860 actually EVAPORATED ink), so just use off-brand ink & call it good.
- The machine is smaller than the Epson Workforce or the HP 8600 series (shorter) although it takes up just about as big of a footprint. But I like not having to use a stool to use the top of it
- Time will tell how well this one will hold out, hopefully longer than the MX860, but I'm happy with it so far.

review_headline: Great Multifunction but making double-sided copes of 2-sided original from ADF can be tricky.
review_body:
Double-sided copying of a 2-sided original can be very involved. The process is not readily visible in the documentation that came with the Multifunction. These are the precise steps, buried deep within the epson forums:
[...]

After pressing Copy, you will need to make a settings change on the printer control panel. Press the Menu button, then select Paper and Copy settings. In this menu there should be 2 sided copy options, you would want to select 2>2-sided.
Be sure the paper is installed in the ADF before making your settings change.

Please note: as soon as the ADF is empty again the settings disappear. If you want to make another 2-sided copy of a 2-sided original you will have to repeat the process. I suppose this is done to make absolutely sure that you have something in the ADF.
You may also make a 2-sided copy from the scanner glass, which some might consider easier.

I initially gave this Multifunction a 1-star due to this issue, but the Epson phone technical support was so pleasant and professional. I had to give the company the best rating.

Some things to note:
DO NOT Print photos and expect them to look good on regular or even on Photo Paper, there WILL BE BANDING if you use the wrong software settings. YOU MUST set the print output to photo quality, High quality, best, with premium or glossy paper.
For plain paper the quality should be set to \\"Quality\\"
I Wasted about 10 sheets of photo paper, and did several alignments before figuring this out. Knowing how to do this I can say the photo quality is GREAT!!!!!
By the way, Alignments are manual, there is no laser alignment on this printer. If you are going to align, do so from the so from the software, you may get nicer results.

product_title: Epson WorkForce 635 Color Inkjet All-in-One (C11CA69201)
review_body: SUMMARY: I've used my Workforce 635 in a home office for a year and love using it.  However, I'd never use the fastest speed.    Compared to other \\"home use\\" printers I have owned in the past:    1. PROS:  --SOFTWARE CONTROLS: Easy and intuitive to create a multitude of personalized print setups with detailed settings, such as 50% print density.  (50% density prints light, saves ink, good enough for many home uses).  --PRINT QUALITY: Great in B&W and color, if you do not use fastest speed.  INK: A cartridge seems to last a little longer than other brands. Very easy to change cartridges.  Price for refills is reasonable.  --TWO SIDED PRINTING, COPYING, SCANNING: A wonderful \\"hands off\\" automatic control.  No changes to paper tray, no manual flipping of paper.  --SCAN: Easy to use, easy to store files on my computer, and easy to create email attachments. The printer gives options for .pdf and other file formats. You can control using printer buttons or using Epson shortcut to software controls on desktop.  --PRINTER HARDWARE CONTROL BUTTONS: A little control screen on the front of the printer tells you which buttons to push and provides menu options and instructions.  Very good design and easy to use.  --PAPER FEEDER: The tray provides manual settings (slides) for a wide variety of paper and envelope sizes.  I've had only one jam in a year, and that was easy to fix by removing paper from the back of the printer.  The printer is not fussy about how you load the paper; it seems to grab and suck in most anything without jamming.  --VIBRATION: Negligible if you don't use the fastest speed setting.    2. CONS:  ---FASTEST SPEED: The fastest speed changes the font to a small, low quality typeface.  I'd never use that font.  (However, the speed with good quality font is fine for my use.)  --NOISE: It is noisy, but I stopped noticing that after awhile.  It has a \\"quiet\\" setting which prints a little slower and reduces noise greatly, although I don't bother to use that setting.    3. SO-SO:  --PLASTIC CONSTRUCTION: It's cheap plastic.  However, the printer only cost $95 and the plastic is designed well.  It held up well for a year with daily use. No problems with the great two-sided scanner/copier feeder on top. The paper tray is difficult to slide in and out, but I'm used to it, and there's been no wear or tear.  --SIZE: The printer looks big and boxy when you see it on the shelf at the store.  However, it sits in the footprint of my old printer, and it's easy to get at the controls and the feeder.  No problem with size, but plan on having a couple feet of space above it, and you need to get at the back to clear jams.    October 2014:  I've been using it 3 years and I still love this printer.  Two irritating shortcomings: (1) The paper drawer can be sticky when sliding in and out (2) There's no provision to feed a single sheet quickly, so you have to pull out the sticky drawer, replace paper, readjust the sticky plastic bumpers if the new paper has a different dimension, and push the sticky drawer back in. But everything else about the printer is great!

review_headline: Works great at warm temperatures; no "fancy black gift box".
review_body:
I purchased this specifically for pointing out star constellations on camping trips. My impressions:

Works great and as intended. A bright, clear beam that can be seen from the side and used to point out stars in the sky. My kids loved it. HOWEVER, (and I believe this is the case with all laser pointers), the beam only works well at warm temperatures (say, the laser pointer itself at 70-80+ degrees and warmer). Pulling it out cold from my camping gear at night meant it would fluctuate brightness and intensity, or just not work at all to start. I could get it working by warming it up under my shirt between my arm and chest (brr!) to get it going, and then would have to repeat every few minutes afterward if it wasn't constantly in use. This wasn't too much of a pain and the fact that my 5 year-old loved learning about constellations made it worth it. I've only had/used this for a couple of weeks on different camping trips so I can't speak to long-term longevity, but for now I feel I got my money's worth.

A couple of inaccuracies in the product description:

It does come with 5 different heads that can be screwed on to make different laser designs. My kids loved these, and they were fun with decorating the campsite with dancing 'stars' at night. However, in order to get a straight beam you had to remove the head-- it didn't come with a head for a straight beam as advertised. I don't think this is an issue, but thought I'd mention it.

In addition, I received mine in a bubble envelope and wrapped in bubble wrap. It did not come in a 'fancy black gift box' as advertised, nor did it come with AAA batteries. review_body: Just your old basic roll of bubble wrap, perforated every 12\\". Item is 12\\" x 12\\" x 12\\" in box of same dimensions. Don't throw away the box unless you are going to mount it on rollers like the big boys do, because it makes for a nice dispenser if you fold it back up properly. Here's what you need to do: Fold the front and back flaps all the way down inside the box. Tape them to the bottom and sides of the box's interior with shipping tape if necessary to keep them in place so that they do not exert pressure on the roll, or just cut them off neatly. However, folding them down inside the box gives it more stability. Then position the roll so that it will feed out of the box over the folded-down front flap. You want the roll to pull up from the bottom (under the roll). (If you do it over the roll, it will bind and not pull out properly.) Once you have properly positioned the roll, pull out enough so that about half a sheet is hanging out over the front. Then fold the side flaps back over the top and tape them down with shipping tape, including the thin gap in the back. Pull the sheets out towards you, diagonally, through the thin gap in front. When it looks like you have about 16\\" hanging out, pull gently to either side to rip the perforation. Use both hands if necessary, since some of the perforations are not as easy to tear as others. It will pull out neatly in 12\\" squares and leave about 6\\" hanging down for your next use. This is a very important step, since if the next sheet falls back inside the box, you will have to reach down through the gap to pull it back out. Pull up vertically to pull out more than one square. Voila! You now have a nice, homemade bubble wrap dispenser!

product_title: Konica Minolta Magicolor 1600W Laser Printer
review_headline: Very happy so far. Minor headaches that come with all printers.
review_body:
I bought this printer because (1) It was cheaper than most laser printers and (2) I read that one guy's amazing amazon review. What a fantastic chronology over 2 years. Keep it up dude.

I've owned this printer for 5 months now. Prints great images. I am not a heavy printer by any means. I use it for the usual document. A few full color pictures here and there. Recently I used it to print full color, dark programs. Quality is really great. No smudges. No lines.

Minor bugs that will drive you crazy:
1) The first time I turned it on, it kept spinning and spinning and spinning. Lot of whirring noises. I thought it was broken.

2) It's not the fastest printer I've seen. Takes around 1-2 minutes to warm up. You tell yourself \\"1-2 minutes? This guy must be super impatient!\\". Well let me tell you: We live in the future now. 1-2 minutes feels like forever.

3) The Konica software drives me f-ing crazy. When there was an error on the printer, I had to go to the Konica website and download another program \\"remote panel utility\\". Through that program, you can alter additional settings like letting the printer print on low toner.

4) The toner cartridges can be tricky when installing. I got mad because of the (2) above and started being rough when removing the black \\"K\\" toner cartridge and pulled a wheel off the end of the cartridge. It was easy to fix. I got some toner on my shirt. Not a complete disaster.

All in all, I am very happy so far. I have been able to print around 60-100 full color 8x11 programs before the black toner ran low. It was my fault as the background were very very dark on these programs. I had to use the software to continue to print on low toner and eventually replace the toner. product_title: Promarx MegaBold Regular Pens, 1.6mm, Assorted Colors, 6 Count (BP05-AR6B06-48)
review_headline: These pens are mighty with a little "fighty"
review_body: I absolutely love megabold 1.6mm pens and sadly many of them do not measure up.  The Kittrich Promarx MegaBold Pens 6 count are lovely pens but sometimes can be a little problematic.  Remove the wax cap from the pen's nib prior to its first use generally helps out a lot to begin the flow of ink to the nib.  The ink is of a gel nature and it does flow readily and smoothly and because it is able to do this the pens will dry out quickly so it is important to cap them off between usage.  If you don't you run the risk of drying the nib out so it skips during use and drying out the ink prematurely.  Sometimes the nibs are not as well machined as they should be and that is grounds for return in my book.  This last batch I waited for a long time on back order and I would like to report the wait was well worth it.  Every pen in the pack writes smoothly and as it should.  Excellent!

product_title: AT&T 1740 Digital Answering System with Time and Day Stamp, White
review_headline: AT&T Rises  from the Ashes (Albeit in Chinese)
review_body:
5 stars for the ATT 1740. It's perfect. I was particularly thrilled because
there were a number of Amazon reviews that panned its predecessor,
the ATT 1739. All the bad stuff they said about the 1739 is groundless.
1) The sound quality is superb, 2) the setup and button layout is easy, 3) you CAN intercept calls
(that is, YOU CAN DO CALL SCREENING - that's a key reason to have an answering machine),
4) the unit's interaction with my telephone is flawless (no feedback). This is all based only on
my unit, but it's so good, that if it were to stop working in 6 months, I'd just go buy another one.

My main telephone is a 20 year old ATT 1545 Speakerphone + digital answering machine.
It served me well for 2 decades (it outlasted my marriage). It is built in the grand old style
of the Bell era monopolies. I've got it connected to a handset lifter and remote Plantronics
headset. So, when the digital answering machine board in the old phone went bad,
I was not about to replace it with any cheap, modern substitute.

The solution is just to turn off the answering machine internal to the old ATT 1545, but still use
it to make calls. But, I connect the ATT phone to my new ATT 1740 answering machine.
Works like a charm!

Yes, ATT no longer makes this product - it's actually made by \\"Advanced American Telephones,\\"
but so what. The Chinese need to eat. A word of advice to AAT and every other company making
products reviewed on Amazon. If you give a hoot, respond to every single negative review.
(My main goal is to improve humanity before the robots take over; see my articles on robotics, AI,
and cognitive neuroscience at bobblum.com (all free).)

product_title: Epson WorkForce 645 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer, Copier, Scanner, Fax, iOS/Tablet/Smartphone/AirPrint Compatible (C11CB86201)
review_body:
We have had this printer for two months. I did NOT set up for wireless use so can't speak to that. Setup for me went smoothly. Even though I'm quite familiar with computer equipment, I follow the manufacturer's instructions on any new equipment I get. There is a reason that instructions are included and things go better if followed. I did not use the driver from the disk but downloaded the driver from Epson as recommended by a couple of other reviewers and as an option in the setup instructions. The download was rather slow even though we have a broadband service but it did go smoothly. Overall, start(from the box) to finish, setup took about 1.5 hours.

I have NOT used the Fax or Scanner. Printing and copying are our main uses and I have been very pleased. Our biggest use is printing lesson material for a Bible Study group of nine people, printing personal tax and investment information and creating greeting cards for family and friends. So far the print quality including color has been excellent. Two sided printing works very well and the ink seems to dry very quickly. A small manual is included and gives instructions on using each feature. As I mentioned earlier, I read manuals and follow prescribed instructions rather than quessing and so far every feature I've used works flawlessly. One nice feature is that the paper tray is under the machine and the top piece of paper is protected from that ever present room dust and I like that especially if you don't print every day. Just seems like print quality will be better if the printhead does not have to print through dust.

Some things to think about are: 1) the footprint is rather large so it takes up some desk or room space 2) it is rather noisy when printing 3)some movable parts are made of rather light plastic that's adequate but not made for a person who is rough, careless or likes to slam things around.

This printer is an addition to our Canon BJC-3000 which I have had for many years. The 3000 has been a very durable, reliable printer for me but getting the ink/printhead combination is harder to find so it seemed like time to get a new printer. I thought about staying with Cannon but the reviews on these Epson 545 and 645 machines were so good, I chose to switch to Epson and the 645. The print quality over the years has improved greatly so it was a good time to upgrade.

I normally buy things from Amazon. I have purchased a Bosch tablesaw, Delta jointer, and Bosch mitersaw from Amazon over the years and my experience with them is really good. What I rely on a lot is the review process they offer. If you ignore the extreme reviews - good or bad, and read reviews written by people who have used the product for awhile and who really want to tell you about the product, I think you can make some good decisions on what to buy. It does take some time to sift through the reviews but they are really helpful.

I bought this printer from Office Depot for two reasons - it was cheaper than Amazon at the time I wanted it($99.00) and I had it that day which was important because I was having trouble finding the ink for my Canon printer at the time.

I will update this review in six or eight months with my ongoing experiences with the machine.

review_body: After 2 months in law school, studying 8-10 hours per day, my neck began to tell me what it thought of my habits. You don't need to know the specifics. I looked around and settled on this book stand (Jasmine) and have been completely satisfied. First of all, the stand is plenty large for my big law textbooks, and yet it handles the smallest of my books with ease. To address concerns:  1) The price--I really wasn't bothered by the price. Having read reviews, I knew that it was a composite or something, not solid wood. The base is plastic and does feel a bit cheap (read: light), but I have had ZERO problems. I just don't know how to quantify what is excessive for something like this, but I know that it has saved me a ton of pain, and is therefore worth it's weight in gold. I guess if you were just looking for a cookbook holder, you could probably find a cheap-o for around $10.  2) The page holders--I read some time ago that someone's pages had small indent marks from the clamps. Being a bit perfectionist about my books, this caused me some concern. The neck took precedence, and I took the gamble. The clamps can cause a bit of an impression on the page, especially if you move the book while the clamp is holding it. However, the marks are slight--not a deal breaker. In short, a non-issue for me.  3) Plastic Base and clip on back--I read that a few people were concerned about the clip (which spans the back of the holder to the base, keeping it upright). It's plastic and thin, but I didn't go slamming it around and I've had no problems. It holds my books just fine, and I don't have to worry about the thing falling down.  In sum:  The holder is light, which is actually kind of a benefit, and large enough to hold reasonably large books (No, not that ridiculously large dictionary in the library at school). The base is plastic, but I've had no problems, though I admit I'm not tossing it around to test its strength. The clips are conveniently placed and easy to reposition, andhave a coating so that you don't have sharp metal on your pages.  I love the book stand, it saved my neck. I don't know why I would ever read with a book sitting flat on a table again!  Good luck!

product_title: Sharp XEA507 Bar Code Scanning and Dual Receipt Cash Register
review_body:
I purchased this cash register for my son's Little League concession stand. It seemed like overkill for a concession stand, but they've had issues with volunteers charging different amounts and/or giving the wrong change. (and the president of the league really wanted a barcode scanner.)

You want to be very careful to follow the quick start guide to set it up correctly. Fortunately, I'd read someone else's comment on an older model Sharp cash register, so I was prepared. IMPORTANT: If you put in the batteries and paper, plug in the power cord THEN reach for the quick start guide (which I probably would have done), you would have already messed up the initialization. Then, I learned from another comment that in the main manual, it says something about setting up a clerk #, which I did. After that, everything worked well.

Setting up prices is pretty slick. You can go into programming mode, scan a barcode and it will ask you the price and the department number. I also went in and set up the name of the item at that point. (That part is kind of a hassle, since you're doing it on a number pad, so for the letter \\"C\\", you're hitting #2 three times.) You're other choice is to download the free program and input the data in the program. The challenge with the program is figuring out at that point which SKU # to put an item name with. To me, it just seemed easier to go about it using the number pad. One idea would be to put in a short name using the number pad, then go back & correct it in the program. I also setup a button for some of the common things like Soda/Pop, Popcorn, Hot Dogs, etc. (by setting up a \\"Popcorn department\\")

After trying it out, I purchased a second one for another window and found that transferring the data was extremely easy. I saved everything to an SD Card (like you'd have in your digital camera) on the register I had already programmed, put the card in the 2nd cash register and uploaded it. It took about 3 minutes and all of the prices/ SKU's / product names were in the 2nd register.

As far as using it, last Saturday was our first day of having the stand open. People were able to figure it out pretty quickly. Everyone that's used it thinks it's pretty cool and easy to use.
