product_title: Canon imageFORMULA DR-M140 Office Document Scanner
review_headline: A workhorse for the home office
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:mo1VUCDQ58FFEKW]]Updated May 26 2012:
###############

I've uploaded a video of this scanner spinning through 36 pages from its automatic document feeder (ADF). The scan was initiated from the control panel using job preset #2, which I configured to scan to PDF at 200 dpi. This resulted in a 58 page PDF document - some of the pages were 2-sided.

Points to note:
1. the paper flow path is the reverse of what you find on the DR-M160 or the ScanSnap.
2. it capably processed this stack - with a whole range of thicknesses and fold locations - without any misfeeds.

#########################################################

In terms of pricing and functionality, this scanner inhabits the space between heavy duty workhorses such as its older sibling, the [[ASIN:B005JZKKNS Canon imageFORMULA DR-M160 Office Document Scanner]], and home office scanners such as the Fujitsu ScanSnap series.

In the years since I adopted a completely paperless home office, I have used scanners at both ends of this scanner capability spectrum.

At the budget end, I absolutely adored my ScanSnap S510's form factor, its speed - both for scanning and PDF conversion, and its competent software package. However, it was very easy to double feed pages with no ability to start at the errant page, its Windows 7 64-bit drivers gave me frequent errors, and it did not include TWAIN/ISIS drivers.

At the premium end of the scale, the DR-M160 made the ScanSnap look like a dainty toy, and performed like you wouldn't believe. Its rollers exuded confidence and could zip through thick stacks of paper with no mis-feeds. Its top notch software included TWAIN/ISIS drivers, a resident scan program, full featured scanner interface software, and a PDF manipulator that was as functional as Acrobat Professional (but without the looks). Once I began to use the DR-M160, the ScanSnap was retired to a closet.

So how doesthe DR-M140 compare?

It can be considered as either a budget DR-M160, or a souped up ScanSnap.

Where it matches the DR-M160:
#######################

== It comes with an identical software bundle.
== It has the same output resolution (optical 150 to 600 dpi max)
== It supports single pass duplex scanning
== It can scan plastic cards
== It can handle paper sizes from 2\\"x2\\" up to 8.5\\"x14\\", with long document scan modes up to 118\\".
== Its folio mode lets you scan pages printed as a booklet (such as a social security statement)
== Its thin paper mode is great for handling long receipts (the ScanSnap needed a carrier sheet to do this).
== 9 programmable job configurations are selectable via control panel.

Where it lags the DR-M160:
##################

-- Not as solidly constructed as the DR-M160
-- No double feed retry (the M160 can automatically push back and re-feed any double fed sheets!)
-- daily volume of 6000 scans (vs 7000 for the DR-M160)
-- speed of 40 ppm (vs 60 ppm for the DR-M160), with letter sized paper at 200dpi.
-- 50 sheet ADF capacity (vs 60 sheet for the DR-M160)

What is different about the DR-M140:
########################

++ Has two paper paths - U turn for normal documents, and straight path (for documents that cannot bend such as thick sheets or plastic cards).
++ Is about a pound lighter and much more compact. Unfortunately, with the straight path, the paper exits from behind the scanner, negating its compact-ness benefits.
++ Has less stringent hardware requirements (Core 2 Duo 1.66Ghz, 1GB RAM, vs Core i7 2.8GHz 4GB RAM for the DR-M160)
++ Where the DR-M160 toggles feed modes in its driver (which I prefer), the M140 has a hardware switch. The non separation feeding mode is designed for documents that are attached at one edge - such as a folded page.

Conclusion:
#######

This is definitely a solid scanner that performs well enough to merit the Canon badge. In my tests, it performed as well as the DR-M160. Also, like the DR-M160, it is exceptionally versatile when it comes to handling a variety of scan scenarios (receipts, folded pages, business cards, etc.)

Unfortunately, the DR-M140 is priced too close to its bigger sibling to be a compelling proposition.

If the power and solidity of the DR-M160 are desirable, there's very little reason to stop at the DR-M140. The heavier duty construction of the DR-M160 is something to be experienced, and could be well worth the premium. On the other end, for lighter home office needs, the ScanSnap should be more than enough - at about half the price.

For me, the bottom line is that this space between the DR-M160 and the ScanSnap is simply not a very attractive place to be.

review_headline: Great printer so far ... system admin experience required for setup
review_body:
I've only owned the printer for a total of 6 hours, so my review of the printer's abilities will be short...

Print quality: Excellent (for what I need). Its quick, the quality of the images/text is wonderful (better than my 3 year old Lexmark Inkjet)

Scan quality: Excellent (again, for what I'm looking for). I scanned some artwork from my 2 year old and it looks great. The colors are vibrant and the scanned image looks true to the original.

I haven't used the fax... and probably won't anytime soon.

Now, on to setup. Geeze. I am so thankful that I have some system admin experience otherwise there is no way I would have made it through the process. It took nearly two hours! I ran through the Quick Start guide with no issues. The printer showed that it connected via wireless and should be good to go so I installed the drivers (from the CD) and attempted to run my first print job. Printer Status: Offline. Huh?

So, I did some digging. I had to change my IP (manually using the printer controls) from Auto to Static. I then had to create a new Port using the IP address (rather than the name) and change the protocol to raw. I had to set the scanner to use the IP rather than the printer name as well.

Really? This is expected out of the box. I have a simple home network - this should not have been so difficult.

Bottom line, I'm still glad I got this machine but I would warn others that you might have to dig deeper than you're used to and/or comfortable with in order to bring the printer on-line.

product_title: Wireless Portable Color Document Scanner
review_headline: Love the Availability of Color! Easy to Use, Great for a Small Office
review_body:
I've been using scanners since the 90's when color scanners had to do a three pass scan to get all the color in the final image. It was critical then for me to be able to scan photos and other items for graphic design with as clean an image as possible. Now I still have a flatbed scanner but what a pain to lift the lid, position the image, scan it, remove it, etc. If you have a bunch of items to scan, it's a real pain to keep reinserting items. Since most of my scans are for reference now, it is not as critical to have a super clean, immaculate scan.

I previously had a Neat Receipts mobile scanner. The limitations were that it only scanned in grayscale, it was hard to feed documents through and often didn't recognize that I had something loaded to scan.

So I was thrilled to be able to get this full color portable scanner. They call it portable but it still needs to run off a computer, it won't scan on the run and store the data until hooked up to a computer. However, it was easy to use, grabbed my documents easily, no matter what the size and pulled them through without trouble. If you put a pile into the slot, it will not pull one at a time but you can feed through multiple pages to be placed in the same document and it prompts you to see if you are done with that batch. There are multiple options for uploading your files to online storage as well.

It trims the file automatically and saves it which is good but also not so good. If you want to give it a specific name, you have to go to the file and rename it.
But good in that sometimes, you just need to scan quickly and don't want to be interrupted with dialog boxes.

It allows you scan multiple documents for a specified "job" giving you the ability to manage receipts and documents based on jobs/customers.

It comes with some pretty nifty software, one of which is ABBYY FineReader. This allows you to scan a document and import it to Word or Excel. It then converts the document to text maintaining columns and text size that is then editable. Very cool and will come in handy for me.

So far, it's been easy to use and fairly intuitive but you need to buy it for the right reasons - it is not a product like Neat Receipts that will read and classify your receipts but it is not selling itself on that merit. It is purely a product that takes up little desk space, to scan color or black and white documents or photos, and store them on your computer or online.then converts the document to text maintaining columns and text size that is then editable. Very cool and will come in handy for me.

review_headline: Yes it's cheap, but the ink isn't! Read on to hear about the rip off:

Honestly, this printer is a decent machine for the price. For the price it prints and scans OK quality stuff.

But that's where the good deal stops.

Besides the touch screen system being pretty slow, here's why you should avoid this printer:

It falsely depletes your ink levels. I do a lot of printing with black only ink. But apparently, that lowers the levels of the color ink drastically! And once you run out of color ink, don't worry because you've still got plenty of black ink left, right? Wrong.

Once it runs out of ANY color ink (cyan, magenta, yellow, or black) the printer essentially ceases to function (except for the scanner of course). When I contacted customer service, they told me that this is normal and happens as a result of the \\"technology\\" that the printer uses, and that if it did allow the printer to print, then the printheads would be damaged.

What a bunch of crap.

What they've come up with is a printer that will make them a little money from the units themselves, and a TON of money from ink sales.

Skip this one, and if you're like me, you'll skip Lexmark for the foreseeable future.

product_title: Epson Artisan 730 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer, Copier, Scanner (iOS/Tablet/Smartphone/AirPrint Compatible) (C11CB18201)
review_body:
Let me start by saying I am quite picky when it comes to products and I rarely have enough enthusiasm about a product to take the time to write a review. However, this printer is THAT good that I need to write a review so other consumers can take advantage of this incredible product.

My wife and I each have IPads, myself and two of my kids have Iphones, and I use an HP Windows based computer and another HP Windows based Laptop.

We were frustrated that despite the different apps and workarounds, we could not print to our HP Wireless printer with any regularity. It would constantly lose signal, or display \\"preparing to print\\" and most of the time the Apple products couldn't find the printer on our wireless network. It was extremely aggravating.

Also, I recently saved a ton of photos into DropBox which my wife can then access with her IPAD and she wants to be able to print them for scrapbooking.

I bought this printer for $99 (which is a steal!), hooked it up, it immediately found our network (has the better N technology), I entered the password and it was set to print. Just like that. Loaded the Software onto the main Windows computer and within about 10minutes had it printing from SD Cards, Word Docs and photos wirelessly.
I then set up the incredible EpsonConnect, went to the website, set up approved senders, changed the email to personalize it to us, put it in my phone as a contact and emailed a photo to it from my Iphone and within two minutes it had printed the photo onto 4x6 photo paper with awesome quality, along with a separate sheet showing who the email was from, date and time. AWESOME!

I then went to my wifes IPAD and printed a photo immediately from there, no muss, no fuss.

Pic quality on Glossy printer paper is great (I'm no professional but my wife even loved the quality) and it prints fast! Even at the higher quality setting!

Touch controls (not touch screen) are really easy to navigate and the kids can now email homework from school or laptops etc. and print it without disrupting what I may be doing on my work computer or printer. Really great!!!

If you really need a downside to know this isn't a biased review, its a little big and pretty dang heavy but I don't plan to carry it around the house, so not really worried about it.

Also, in the interest of full disclosure, the first one I got didn't print and Epson determined it was a Hardware Malfunction, which was a bummer. However, they walked me through a few steps and when they determined it wasn't \\"fixable\\" they overnighted me a new one and I had it a day later. The new one worked flawlessly and I shipped the old one back all at their cost. And they sent a new batch of ink cartridges with the new printer and let me keep the old ones so no real harm.

Seriously, if you want to print wirelessly from multiple devices, both Apple and Windows, and send things remotely and print great photos....this is the printer you need (and I've always only owned HP, so this switch is a big deal!)

Steve in Seattle

product_title: Brother HL2280 Wireless Monochrome Laser Printer
review_headline: Nice features, nice price, works well, but terrible software
review_body:
I was looking for a fast monochrome auto duplexing laser for a home wireless network so the Brother looked promising. It is indeed fast and the duplexing works well. Unlike some comments, it IS possible to connect a wired computer to a wireless printer as long as they share the same network. It has some major drawbacks however:

1) The starter print cartridge is tiny. Although it is considered to be an advantage to have a seperate drum, this is negated by the poor quality of third-party cartridges (unlike HP where good ones are available). A new Brother cartridge is ~$50

2) The software is incredibly awful. I am used to HP for my J5870 all-in-one which updated the interface to the point that it is a snap to use. Not so for the Brother package, which forces you to download a behemoth 128 MB file which is mostly c**p, and then subjects you to about 10 separate downloads, the function of none of which is clearly explained. I finally stumbled on the \\"Brother Network Connection Repair Tool\\" which is actually quite good at getting the wireless network to connect. It is quite finicky, with the printer going offline for no reason, so if you are not a computer geek, I don't recommend that you use the wireless setup.

3) The printer is noisy. This is why it should be located away from your workstation, which is after all the advantage of a wireless connection.

After numerous attempts to connect the winning strategy is:

1) Download the driver from the Brother website
2) Using the buttons on the printer, detect the SSID and then enter you pass phrase by hand (a real pain but only needs to be done once)
3) Set the 2280 as the default and use the Brother Network Connection Repair Tool to connect. That should do it.

I am sure that the Brother will work fine with a USB or wired network connection. It really is too noisy, however, to have on your desk

Brother need to get their act together and thoroughly junk their existing software in favor of a streamlined, intuitive, functional, all-in-one interface. It is only then will they have a chance at competing with HP.

Update 1/12/13:

I recently installed the Brother driver on my Macbook, and must admit that it downloaded and installed smoothly. Furthermore, the interface with my PCs has been stable. So, Brother, good job!

product_title: Samsung Color Laser Printer (CLP-620ND)
review_body:
After owning this printer for close to 9 months now, I can safely say I have had mostly problems with it. I bought this printer for it's claim to print on heavier card and index and cover paper, which it does not. After having several sessions with their tech support, I've come to the conclusion that their claims of printing on heavier stock are flawed. The manual specifically states that it can print up to 220 lb paper. This only jams paper tray 2, the tray specifically designed to print this heavier stock. It even jams 200 lb., 180 lb. and 160 lb. paper. Needless to say, I have wasted a lot of money on paper waste and a lot of time calling Samsung tech support.

Also, any thinner text paper, 80lb and below, that has even the slightest textured feel to it or has the slightest cotton content and is specifically designed for laser printers will not absorb the inks fully. Plain text on textured paper looks slightly mottled, sometimes it takes well, but most of the time it does not. Forget about printing any jpegs on textured paper that is specifically made for laser printers. You will only get a photo with pin holes in it where the ink does not take.

I have had great luck though on vellum papers specifically designed for laser printers. Never an issue. These papers usually don't agree with the more expensive laser printers in Kinko's & Staples but for this printer they are just fine, but for this positive attribute alone, I cannot recommend buying this printer. Another annoying thing this printer does is draw an incredible amount of electric power when it is operating. My lights flicker and I do not have this problem with any other electronic device in my household.

I bought this printer to make professional presentations at home and unfortunately it does not do what it claims it does in the manual and on Samsung's website. After the toners are finished, I will not be replacing them, but instead will be looking to purchase a home colorlaser printer that indeed does what it claims it does.

If anyone knows of a home laser color printer that they can recommend, I would appreciate a response please.

Thank you for your feedback.

UPDATE: 2 YEARS AND 3 MONTHS LATER:

This is finally going in the garbage. After putting up with this hunk of garbage for this long and investing in new toner to boot, I've had it. All prints now have roller streaks on them from the wheels being too tight to the page, even after calling 'support' several times. Also, all prints have a purplish tint to them, more non-support from Samsung 'support'.

Going with a Brother now after borrowing one and trying it out myself. This Samsung simply cannot compare to it AND it's $100.00 cheaper.

If I can give this printer no stars, I would.

Good riddance!

product_title: Epson Artisan 725 Color Inkjet All-In-One (C11CA74201)
review_headline: Very good for photos, not so good at anything else
review_body:
Provided you understand that it's not a true \\"all-in-one\\" jack of all trades, the Epson 725 is a printer/scanner worth serious consideration for photo use.

The good points first: It's excellent at photo printing. Rich, saturated colors and fine details emerge both on plain paper and on photo paper. It prints quickly and is easy enough to set up. It also has a very small screen and memory-card slots for use directly from the camera, without a computer -- nice in a pinch, but you'd never want to rely on this for regular printing. It's also a very good photo scanner -- surprisingly good for an all-in-one device, with high resolution.

The 725 is not a good choice as a general office printer, though -- the cost per page is bad enough for photos already (is the ink made of gold?), but with those tiny, pricey ink tanks and its minuscule paper tray you'll never want to use this for general text printing. The scanner lacks an ADF for office use and isn't fast enough to use for text or book scanning in any case; it's workable for an occasional single photocopy or scan, not regular office-style use. And the device lacks fax capability. For all these purposes you'll be much better served with a laser all-in-one like the excellent DCP/MFC models made by Brother at roughly the same price point. But the Epson is certainly worth considering for photographers who want a good scanner and who want to control their own printing process.

product_title: Epson WorkForce 545 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer, Copier, Scanner, Fax, iOS/Tablet/Smartphone/AirPrint Compatible (C11CB88201)
review_body:
I am using Windows 7 so I cannot comment about difficulties associated with the use of a Mac. I bought this printer to replace an HP printer that was almost identical in size with less functionality. The scanner on the HP died after about a year and wasn't worth the time or expense to fix. If you have previously setup a wireless printer then you will find that removing the packaging and tape strips requires nearly as much time as getting the printer online and printing. It does not come with any USB cable but such is not necessary for setup with a wireless router. I visually scanned the quick start guide and found that setup was very intuitive. I did need to view the picture that shows the proper orientation of the ink cartridges. Be careful to read and follow the instructions for unpacking the ink cartridges and make sure that you only remove the one strip and not the little plastic cover where the ink exits the cartridge. This will be pierced while inserting the cartridges into the printer. Installing the software was easy and I quickly had both of ours laptops connected to the printer and properly functioning. The total time to install the printer, install the software on two laptops, and configure everything was less than 60 minutes.

All of the features are as specified by the manufacturer. I like the 30-page document feeder. I also like the feature that allows you to remotely enable and disable FAX auto-answer mode. This may be accomplished from any enabled network printer. You may also send a FAX directly from any enabled, network connected PC.

Pros:
* Quick and easy setup
* Versatile 30-page document feeder
* Fully compatible with Windows 7
* Ability to wirelessly setup and control all functions.
* I find that the color LCD, keypad, and menu structure are very useful and intuitive.
* I have had no issues remotely printing even when the printer is in \\"sleep mode.\\" The printer recovers faster than the HP predecessor that it replaced.

Neutral:
* The printer is not as noisier as the HP printer it replaced. I wouldn't install either in my bedroom.

Cons:
* I agree with others that the paper tray is flimsy but, with care, it may last as long as the printer's useful lifetime.

KEEPING IT SIMPLE:

Any DC 2.4V rechargeable battery would work on a handset once the battery connectors are the same. Batteries with different mAh ratings are interchangeable.

The Milliamps Hour (mAh) battery rating is important - the higher the mAh number, the greater the strength or capacity of a battery. In other words, the higher the mAh, the longer the battery will last.

In fact, these 800mAh capacity rating Gator Crunch replacement batteries would last longer per charge than the 650mAh capacity originals that came with my phone ... and at a fraction of the cost :))

review_body: After reading a lot of comparison reviews, mostly on Amazon.com, I finally settled on this HP.  Previously I had been using an HP 1012 which suddenly failed. My computer is running Windows 7 64bit and I have a wireless router to which my computer is connected via a USB cable.  I did not want to run the printer as a wireless unit. I allowed him to run my computer remotely and together we worked on the problem for perhaps an hour and a half.  In the end he had to delete all traces of the previous installation and begin new.  This time we got the printer to work and it has worked flawlessly ever since.  I give customer support high marks but the installation should not have been this difficult.  It cost HP a lot of money to get me up and running.  The remaining question is durability.  I don't detect that it is cheaply made. Most cordless phones have a 2.5mm jack (if you're not sure read your phone's manual), so the product you need is \\"Sennheiser CCEL190-2 Headset Cable-Adapter\\". product_title: Montblanc Meisterstuck Classique Ballpoint Pen 164 Black with Gold Trim
review_headline: A classic pen - beautiful to look at, feels great in the hand
review_body:
Even if you aren't much of a pen geek (and, truth be told I am), you have heard of Montblanc pens. Like Rolex watches, Mercedes Benz cars and Armani suits, Montblanc brings to mind visions of elegance, style and class. Sounds like a lot to ask from a pen, but at these prices, there has to be something to the thing besides being able to sign that credit card slip or your kid's report card.

The pen - called Meisterstuck, German for Master Piece - has heft without being heavy. The \\"click\\" mechanism (twist, actually) is smooth and feels like it will work for decades. The clip has good tension so the pen won't hop out of your pocket but not too tight so that you damage the cloth if you pull it out and put it back a few times a day. The plastic is polished to a glossy finish but some how manages to provide a good grip - not slippery at all. Not sure how that do that! But the real value to a pen is how well it writes. That all comes down to the refill. And here is one of the reasons for 4 and not 5 stars. The standard \\"medium\\" refill is pretty bland. Nothing special happening here. If you buy a similarly priced Omas (sweet, Italian pen) you get a very nice refill - a unique blend of standard ink and gel ink. I love mine and wish it would fit in a Montblanc. I did find a good compromise - they make a broad refill that writes like it has gel ink but without the smear (lefty's will like that). But, again 4 star alert, their refills are very expensive and unique to their pens. Some great pens (e.g., Faber Castell) let you use Parker-style refills. This expands the choices - colors, ink types, points (find, med, broad) and comes to you at a relatively low price AND can be bought at just about any office supply store.

As mentioned by others, don't drop your pen. The plastic is beautiful but can be chipped, cracked or scratched. I had to bring mine to the local Montlanc store when I noticed the barrel was cracked - not sure how that happened. $50 later it was like new but the bloom was off the rose and I've been using it less and less ($50 would buy a nice Faber, Parker of Sheaffer).

Overall - this is a classic pen, possibly the most iconic in the world but there are other pens in this price range (and lower) that score more points for me. Interested? Then look at pens from Omas, Faber Castell, Sheaffer, Delta, and Lamy.loom was off the rose and I've been using it less and less ($50 would buy a nice Faber, Parker of Sheaffer). Overall - this is a classic pen, possibly the most iconic in the world but there are other pens in this price range (and lower) that score more points for me. Interested? product_title: KHOMO DUAL CASE Green Cover FRONT + Green Crystal Back Protector for Apple iPad 2 , iPad 3 & iPad 4 (The new iPad HD)
review_body:
I really fell in love with this case when I first spotted it here on Amazon. It's hard for me to find cases that I really like, and the vivid apple green really sold me. It's a shame though that the product is flimsy and, roughly two weeks later, now falling apart.

I own the iPad 3 so I was a little concerned that the case wasn't going to fit when I initially made the purchase. Thankfully it didn't take much to get the backing to fit into place. The front flap doesn't sit completely flat on the screen but the gap is so tiny that it didn't impact the iPad from going to sleep or waking up. Everything was fine up until two days ago when the covers top pin cap fell off. I pushed the pin back in again but I guess it's so loose that the threads on the pin won't hold inside the cap and eventually it slips out again. I haven't seen any fraying of the cover nor has the cover peeled off, but I consider myself rather gentle when it comes to using this case. The only other complaint is the fact that this already has a smallish crack near the lower left corner of the iPad. As I said, I do treat this device very carefully and haven't dropped it so it strikes me odd that the corner has that small crack in it. It isn't too distracting, but it only reinforces the fact that this case really isn't constructed well.

Why not use a gel or rubber backing instead? Hard plastic is bound to chip or break off over time due to stress and wear. At any rate, two stars. The color isn't enough to make up for the poor craftsmanship.

product_title: Epson Artisan 837 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer, Copier, Scanner, Fax, iOS/Tablet/Smartphone/AirPrint Compatible (C11CB20201)
review_body:
This replaced my previous printer, and HP Photosmart All-In-One -- aside from a weird technical/network challenge which I had to work through (and will address below), I love this printer and am happy with the switch.

PROS:
- Network-enabled printing. Users on your home or office network can access this printer via Wi-Fi, which seems like not such a big deal but is really cool if you have roommates or multiple portable devices from which you might want to print.
- Print quality is superb -- the best of any printer I've owned so far. I typically just print black-and-white but will occasionally run a color document or a photo and this printer performs very well. I wouldn't rely on this as a dedicated photo printer, however, and will go into this in the Cons
- Sleek appearance
- Touch screen interface is user-friendly (for most functions) and easy to navigate
- Software / driver installation is straightforward
- Decent paper capacity

CONS:
- Very large (takes up almost the entire surface of my credenza)
- Color printing eats a lot of ink, and...
- 6 ink cartridges (yes, you need all 6) may result in higher quality, but a relatively small black in capacity means you'll be getting more refills than you might be bargaining for if you bought this primarily for printing black-and-white documents
- Slow startup time
- Print-via-Wifi issues from some computers... see below
- Printed pages fall to the floor unless you fully extend the fragile tray

WIFI Printing was tough for me for a while. The first time I got this thing set up, my computer instantly detected and it worked great. The next day, however, I couldn't get it to print. The printer was on, and said it was connected, but my computer couldn't detect it on the Wifi network. I went online and read through a bunch of forums and ran through some driver uninstall/reinstall cycles that seemed to fix the problem. A little while later -- same problem!

Since then, I've noticed that when you go to select a printer to print your document, you'll probably see multiple \\"Artisan 837\\" printers on the menu. The one you have to pick is \\"Artisan 837 (Network)\\" if it's showing up. Sometimes the others work, sometimes not -- but by selecting the (Network) one I've avoided any issues with printer connection.

BOTTOM LINE: this isn't your printer if you just want something to run off black and white copies. However, if you plan on printing photos and/or color documents, and especially if you want Wifi connectivity and plan on using this printer from multiple devices, this is the printer for you.

product_title: Epson WorkForce 545 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer, Copier, Scanner, Fax, iOS/Tablet/Smartphone/AirPrint Compatible (C11CB88201)
review_body: Shopper Beware.  Overall a good printer if all you are printing is on NORMAL paper weight, the thickness of copy paper.  The Workforce series can NOT handle papers heaver than 24lbs in weight, which is the basic copy paper weight.  Paper weight is an indication of the paper's thickness which is the culprit.    Hidden deep in the printer's manual is the actual paper specifications.    Paper types Plain paper and paper distributed by Epson  Thickness 0.003 to 0.004 inch (0.08 to 0.11 mm)  Weight 17 lb (64 g/m2) to 24 lb (90 g/m2)    [...]    If you try to print on a thicker paper eventually the paper transport will fail causing the entire device to become unusable.  A slower learner, I've had this happen twice to me.  I was using Avery's Business cards when the device failed.  Since it was over a year old I am left with the only option of purchasing a new device.  Not pleasant experience.

review_body:

review_headline: Good product, I like it a lot - would recommend

Near the space bar, the case is raised about a 1/4 of an inch higher and it's slightly inconvenient to space quickly.
It's not a full sized keyboard like a laptop so don't expect super touch typing.

The product is great for casual typing and a great improvement over using the touch screen keyboard but I would get it if you type on it enough for the touch screen to be annoying but not enough for you to think that it's a laptop replacement. If you fall somewhere in between those this is your product.

There is no brand marks on the cover so it looks nice and untarnished by a cheap logo and it snaps together well with the iPad 2. It seems to use similar magnet technologies as the smart cover to turn on and off the device on close.

Battery life is great so far, running strong still after 3 days of use (about 1-2 hours a day). I haven't tried the Logitech one that this product resembles but I can't imagine it would be any better. For the price, it's a great deal.

If I were to have one last complaint, it would be that it's not the most user friendly in getting the iPad out of the case. The notches are pretty small and requires two hands to pry it apart sometimes.

product_title: Ultimate 555 Timer/Oscillator KIT (Through-Hole)
review_headline: Good as far as it goes
review_body:
The instructions were clear, spare parts were included, and it worked properly the first time I tried it. (Which really quite amazed me, since I'd never worked with SMT before, and speaks well of the quality of the product and its instruction.)

That being said..

I expected a little more general-purpose unit, rather than having to choose a particular range of output frequencies and pulse widths and solder in the appropriate components. I would prefer to be able to select the R/C components via jumper, and jumper a diode across the discharge resistor to decouple the mark time and rest time.

That's why 4 stars rather than 5.

I bought this SMT (surface-mount technology) kit without really noticing the 'SMT' part of the name. This was the first time I've worked with SMT components, and it'll probably be the last -- but that has nothing to do with the quality of the product. Having a tremor and suboptimal vision, I was seriously dismayed at the miniscule size of the parts. Fortunately I have a 'helping hands' stand ([[ASIN:B000E3276S Hawk MG8950 Helping Hand Magnifier with Stand]]), but a set of non-magnetic tweezers is virtually a necessity -- and I don't have any of those handy. At least when I inevitably dropped parts on the patterned rug, I could find most of them with a magnet.

product_title: fadf
review_headline: This CIS system does not save money with Workforce 1100
review_body: I purchased this CIS from the seller's site. The problem is that with the new Epson chips the printer stops printing whenever it thinks one of the cartridges is empty and there is no way to reset all colors at the same time. That means that if you are doing a print and the printer decides the Cyan is empty it stops printing and you lose the print. You then go through the reset procedure and start over and the printer will likely as not stop because it now thinks it's out of another color. It does not automatically reset by turning off the printer, you have to physically remove the cartridge and put it back in and it only resets the cartridge it decided was empty.  When doing large format prints on expensive paper the combination of the Workforce 1100 and this CIS system is practically useless. It's really a problem with the printer design but the CIS is sold without informing the customer of this limitation.  At the time of this writing there is no software either paid or free that circumvents this issue.

product_title: Ooma Telo Free Home Phone Service
review_headline: Not quite up to snuff - wrong - update!
review_body:
Some good, some bad. Installation was easy. Porting my number was easy.

The problem comes in with a short delay when speaking to someone. Its VERY short, but just enough that you wind up stepping on someone elses comments and often they wind up stepping on yours, VERY annoying. Voice quality is excellant.

I am a computer tech so I know the only thing I can control is the actions of my router. I will go into the router soon and give the Ooma device top priority on traffic, but I don't really think the problems there. If it is, I will report back.

If not............ 3 stars is as good as it gets.

I promised an update and here it is.

As I work in the computer field and am familiar with most devices, I hooked the Ooma in AFTER the router. Dummy. If I had read the directions, they say to place it before the router and I'm sure this would have eliminated the slight delay mentioned above.

For other reasons I still wanted it AFTER the router. But if you go into the router's quality of service section (Qos) and give the Ooma top priority...all is well - no delay.

So 5 stars for the Ooma and 1 star for the dummy (me) who thought he was past reading the directions!

Cheers

product_title: Panasonic KX-TG6582T DECT 6.0 PLUS Link-to-Cell via Bluetooth Cordless Phone with Answering System, Metallic Black, 2 Handsets
review_body:
I installed this phone this weekend and am amazed at it's versatility, functionality, and the care that went into the human interface. This is one beautiful piece of systems engineering and design execution! Kudos to you, Panasonic!

I've had numerous cordless phones in the past, but was motivated to order this system due to the \\"link to cellphone\\" feature. How many times have you, like me, sprinted from the room I was in to the room my cellphone was left in, only to miss an important incoming call? Furthermore, with an elderly relative who's ill, I've been concerned that someone would call me in the middle of the night on my cellphone with an emergency that I'd miss because I forgot to bring the cellphone up to my bedroom.

With this phone those concerns are a thing of the past. It VERY simply and straightforwardly links to a cellphone via its Bluetooth interface- when my cellphone rings my \\"home phone\\" rings- no call forwarding, nothing to remember- it just happens. It will just as easily link to a 2nd cellphone (but no more than 2).

I'd dump my landline in a minute (except my wife insists on keeping it for reasons undecipherable by me!) but this phone integrates our landline and cellphone access into a single multi-handset cordless system. And if/when I'm successful convincing my wife that we can lose the landline this will work strictly as a cellphone access telephone! I was also able to upload my cellphones extensive Address Book (why do they call it that when it contains phone numbers?) to this phone's base station and, consequently, to all of the satellite handsets.

The flexibility of this product is amazing. Tonight my wife and I were on a call using 2 handsets, via linking to my cellphone, when our land line rang- I easily and intuitively (without having to read the manual) was able to disengage from the call to answer the call on the land-line.

And, unlike some other cordless products I've owned, this easily switches between handset speakerphone to normal handset operation during a call, and the base can be used as a \\"virtual handset\\" for calling out (either on cell or landline)via its built-in speakerphone. (For those with impaired hearing such as mine, the speakerphone is sufficiently loud and has sufficient clarity for folks like us.)

I couldn't be more pleased with this system- so much so that I immediately ordered a 3rd handset and will likely order 1 or 2 more. This one's a keeper!

product_title: Canon PIXMA MG5320 Wireless Inkjet Photo All-in-One Printer (5291B019)
review_headline: The Good, Bad and the Ugly
review_body:
Good - Excellent price, fairly easy set-up, decent text (in "fast" mode), acceptable ink consumption (not great, not wonderful, just acceptable).

Bad - Fussy about paper and inks used. Forget cheap photo paper. You'll end up tossing the output.

Ugly - Can't use copy function from keyboard. Must actually go to printer and perform copying there. No fax.

UPDATE: 1/25/2016 - Still in use -- more so now than ever due to a change to Windows 10. Microsoft's latest OS "upgrade" temporarily sidelined much of my older hardware -- especially my Canon i9900 and Samsung ML 2250 printers and my old faithful Visioneer 8600 and Canon 8600f scanners (as well as a dedicated photo scanner by Minolta). The MG5320 was not fazed by the new OS. As for scanners, thank you VueScan -- who released a software utility that restored all of my (until lately) inoperable scanners to full use. Even my Visioneer, which ceased working when no driver was available beginning with Windows 7. product_title: Brother MFC-8480DN High-Performance Laser All-in-One with Networking and Duplex Printing
review_headline: Overall seems to work well, but Linux support poor
review_body: We bought this printer for our home office 4 years ago, upgrading from an HP LJ 6L and gaining scanner, fax and copy capability.  Features we wanted were network-based operation, duplex printing, legal size printing/copying, not ink jet (consumables are too expensive and ink bleeds if it gets wet).  We considered duplex scanning, but for the cost and only occasional use we passed on that.  We named our new Brother "Comrade".  The drivers included were troublesome, but after downloaded the latest from the Brother website, both Macs and PCs worked pretty well.  On occasion on the Mac, the scanning gets wonky and I have to restart Brother's Mac scan software.  Otherwise, connectivity has been good, just plug it and and it talks on the network.  It has stayed on and reboots have been rarely necessary.  On the other hand, at one point we tried to connect a Linux box and it was disastrous.  Plain text (lpr) works, but printing using PostScript often resulted in PostScript interpreter errors.  PCL caused the printer to lock up or get weird (after which other machines had trouble printing) and required power cycling.  I tried the drivers included with Ubuntu and the ones on the Brother website, to no avail.  The hardware itself performs well. Duplexing prints at half the rated 33 pages/minute (i.e., apx. 8 double-sided sheets, not 16).  The printer is pretty loud when busy, and the fan runs for another 10 minutes or so after it's done, then it quiets down to silence.  Occasionally a printed sheet gets pushed forward by the next sheet, so you find a random page of your document laying on the floor; extending the legal-size support seems to fix this behavior.  Paper jams: * Rare on standard stock * Consistent when using hole-punched paper when duplexing * Rare on hole-punch printing single-sided * Thick/odd stock requires getting the paper thickness right in the print dialog or it may jam, particularly when duplexing.  The printer obeys our requests to use a particular paper feed (envelopes in the manual feeder, letterhead in the secondary/add-on paper tray that we got) and type.  Note that when printing envelopes/thick paper, for best results select such in the print dialog-- it seems to feed the paper slower, apparently giving the fuser extra time to adhere the toner, and it also reduces jams.  Envelopes do come out wrinkly, unless you open the back door and do the straight-through paper path.  The scanner works okay, although it takes a moment to connect and get going.  After that, it scans along on its own, no hassles or jams.  The Mac scan setup is a little weird but workable; the OCR software pretty rudimentary.  If you want to scan to .pdf or .doc on a Mac, you'll need to get FineReader or other add-on software.  I haven't used the PC scan software, so I can't speak to that.  Copying and faxing we've only used a few times, but have worked fine when we've needed to.

product_title: Lexmark Prevail Pro705 Small Office Wireless Multifunction Inkjet Printer
review_body:
I'll preface this review by saying that I have an older Lexmark all-in-one (X8350) that, to this day, works great. Based on my experience with the older device and the numerous glowing reviews of the Prevail Pro705 I found (a year ago, anyway), I decided to upgrade; the Prevail was reasonably priced, came with extra-capacity cartridges and a five-year warranty. How could I go wrong? Well, I'll tell you...

At first, everything was great. Setup was an absolute breeze. Everything was installed and networked in under 30 minutes (I will say the instructions on installing the print head were a bit vague for my taste). Everything printed beautifully, and I was a happy camper.

After a couple of days, I started getting the \\"please wait\\" error on the device as it ran through its clicks and whirrs in order to ready itself for printing...it seemed to take longer to initialize if I didn't print something every day (which I typically don't). The print quality for the Prevail is very good - colors and blacks are rich and sharp, so I tended to overlook the delays, since this is a four-cartridge ink system (the older Lexmark is a two-cartridge system: \\"black\\" and \\"tri-color\\").

After the first month, I really started having problems. First, my black cartridge, according to the printer, needed to be replaced. My EXTRA-capacity black that I had been using for a month to print a grand total of 45 pages, mostly text. When I checked all of the cartridges, they ALL showed to be over half-empty. About a week after replacing the black cartridge, a page was printing out, and it was drenched in cyan ink; I got the dreaded \\"print head error\\" message, and I was dead in the water. To their credit, Lexmark's support was actually very good. The tech determined that the print head was bad, and he sent me a new one, along with 4 new extra-capacity cartridges and a return mailer at no charge. I got them very quickly, installed everything, mailed all the defective stuffback, and all was good. For about two weeks. Then, I noticed my yellow (just installed) cartridge was running dry... and on and on.

In the course of the year I had this printer, I went through four sets of extra-capacity ink cartridges (including the set I set back to Lexmark)to print out a grand total of 183 pages.

About two months ago, I decided that enough was enough. I went to a local merchant and picked up an [[ASIN:B005IVL0SC Epson WorkForce 645 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer, Copier, Scanner, Fax (C11CB86201)]], and it's a night and day difference. The Epson is fantastic! I found myself anxiously hunched over it, waiting for something to go wrong -- so far, nothing has gone wrong (other than a minor faxing issue, which was solved by turning off \\"ECM\\" - I think it may have been an issue with the fax machine to which I was sending, though).

I really , really wanted to like the Lexmark Prevail, but its many operational flaws made it far too difficult.

product_title: uni-ball Vision Elite Rollerball Pens
review_headline: 90% of a fountain pen's benefits with 0% of the hassle
review_body:
The pen --

The pen delivers a smooth, even flow of ink with minimal pressure. It's not quite as effortless as a fountain pen, but it's leagues ahead of any ball point. It has a good weight to it and the fine tip is great for people with small handwriting. The pen itself is very elegant and professional looking. The ink reservoir is sized generously: although it's tapered to fit inside the pen body, it fills nearly the entire breadth and length of the pen, not just a narrow tube in the centre.

I'm not sure this qualifies as a 'con,' but I don't like using these pens for anything with carbon copies. The pen stands up to the task just fine, but the amount of pressure involved just feels excessive for this easy-writer. Alternatively, if someone needs to borrow your pen, you don't need to worry about them mangling it as you would with a fountain pen. While I haven't tested this feature, the pen supposedly won't leak in flight, either -- unlike fountain pens, which must be drained and later refilled when you fly.

The ink --

I can't comment on artistic applications that involve multiple strokes or layers of ink, but for routine writing on notebook paper, the ink dries almost completely within 3-5 seconds. Smudging is minimal. It also won't bleed through the paper. I've even used this pen in the rain; while the top layers of ink smeared a little, the writing remained bold and I could easily read what I wrote later. I dunno if this stuff could hold up like Noodler's bulletproof inks, but the box says the ink \\"helps prevent cheque washing\\" and I consider fraud-resistant ink a must for cheques and other important documents.

Supposedly the pens can be refilled, but I haven't seen any refill cartridges (???).

Bottom line is if you want a pen that glides (relatively) smoothly over the paper, won't give you hand cramps, and -- while pricier than a box of ball points -- won't break the bank if lost or stolen, this is the pen for you.n, this is the pen for you.

review_headline: Just Ok! If you are looking for a deal, here it is!
review_body: I have purchased this toner twice now. Both times I was able to print just less than 4000 pages (3881 and 3721) before it needed to be replaced. I'm sure there was still more toner left in the cartridge, but I replaced them because they were dropping more toner (blobs or dark backgrounds) on the pages than needed. I have purchased many high-yield cartridges directly from Dell and as you approach the end of their life cycles the toner seems to just fade away rather than drop excess toner on the pages. product_title: HP CM721A#B1H 2140 Professional Quality Plain-Paper Fax and Copier
review_body: There is a good reason why this fax machine costs $65. You will be lucky if you can receive 100 pages before the tiny black cartridge runs out. product_title: Maped Essentials Letter Opener (037400)
review_body: I got this product for my mother who is physically handicapped.  She uses this product a lot and finds it quite helpful. product_title: Westcott iPoint Kleenearth Evolution Recycled Electric Pencil Sharpener, Gray (15085)
review_body: I was recently given the opportunity to test out the Westcott Kleen Earth iPoint Evolution Pencil Sharpener. Whenever I buy products for my home office, I try to choose products that have at least some eco-friendly attributes. You can bet that I was pleased to see that the base of this great looking pencil sharpener is made of recycled plastic. The packaging for the iPoint Evolution was not excessive, and it was very easy to open. I was able to set it up in seconds because all that you have to do is clear a small space for it on the desk and plug it in.  This pencil sharpener works very well, and I was surprised at how quiet it was. My pencils came out perfectly sharpened and the clear savings reservoir makes it simple to see when it needs emptying. Emptying the iPoint Evolution is easy, and there are a few ways to do it but I found that the quickest and neatest way is to simply unplug it, hold it over the wastebasket, and remove the lid before flipping it over to empty it.  Since I will be using this pencil sharpener in my home office, I would have preferred a model without a cord. That said, the fact that it needs no batteries provides a great advantage for people who want to use it in a school or office setting where it might go through batteries quickly. Its size also makes it ideal for settings where it will be more heavily used than I will be using it at home. In short, this is a great looking pencil sharpener that performs well and is suitable for home, school, and business use.

product_title: Westcott iPoint Evolution Electric Pencil Sharpener
review_body: Bought this because it looks great and the packaging promised sharp points (thanks to \\"titanium blades\\"). Although I paid much less than this listing price, it was still a waste of money. I sharpened three pencils as far down as possible without managing to achieve a good point. In fact, I could have whittled the lead with a jackknife for the same result. At first I thought the pencils were the problem, but not so. Save your money.

review_body: Definitely the best stuff among other products. I have used TM6000 for 15ys. I purchased TM6000b to replace the old one with monitor gone bad.

review_headline: do not buy this..sony no longer sells paper
review_body: I purchased this..and could use it as a boat anchor today..Sony no longer sells the paper that you can use to actually PRINT your pictures..I contacted Sony and they basically told me to F--- off... they didn't give a damn about the fact that I paid more than 300 for this printer...they no longer sell the paper that  you can use... and they have no intention of ever selling it again. They told me as much and then HUNG UP THE PHONE!

product_title: 5mw 532nm Astronomy Powerful Green Laser Pointer - Black
review_body:
This laser pointer is a lot of fun. Yes, if you take it outside at night and point it at anything in your line of sight (including the moon and stars) you will see a green laser beam of light that seems to extend all the way to that object. It doesn't really matter how far away the object is. If you shine it through smoke, fog, or light rain at night, it looks almost like a really long lightsaber from Star Wars, no joke. It's very powerful, and makes a very bright spot on whatever you are illuminating (on Earth). It seems to drain the 2 AAA batteries (not included) rather quickly... as bright as it is, I would expect it to.
It's too bright to tease cats with... it seems to mesmerize them rather than get them excited. Plus the laser will reflect off of your hardwood floors and make all the furniture in your living room glow green. This pointer is so fun that I honestly don't think I could use it in a professional capacity (for presentations) because I know that the instant I use it, everybody in the room will be thinking, \\"WOW! Did you see that?\\" and they would all be harassing me about wanting to play with my laser pointer. Buy it. This would make a great stocking stuffer.

product_title: Panasonic KX-TCA60 Hands-Free Headset with Comfort Fit Headband for Use with Cordless Phones
review_body: I recently purchased this headset on Amazon and it works as advertised so far. It's a basic headset, nothing special. I'm using it for my cordless Panasonic Dect 6.0 landline phone. I've had it for about two months and there are no problems at all. The sound quality is great. It doesn't have noise cancellation, but that doesn't seem to matter much so long as I am in an environment where there isn't a whole lot of background noise. The headset is adjustable so that you can wear it on both the right and left ears and the boom mic bends easily so that you can adjust the distance of the mic to and away from your mouth. I have no complaints at all and it is easily worth the $14 I paid for it.

product_title: Epson LabelWorks LW-400 Label Maker
review_body: this is a real nice label maker & uses label's of all sizes & colors. I made lables for my spice jars, & to lable dvd's. Also for my file drawers & files.

product_title: Bostitch SuperPro  6 Commercial Electric Pencil Sharpener, 6-Holes, Black/Silver (EPS12HC)
review_body: I volunteer as a tutor in an elementary school.  The classroom pencil sharpener (made in China) chewed-up rather than sharpened the kids' pencils.  I searched all over, and tried several new sharpeners (all made in China), but each broke within a week and were returned for a refund.  I was desperate to find an American-made sharpener.  I found this sharpener on the internet with raving reviews from other teachers, so I decided to try it.  While I originally thought this one was made in the USA, I discovered it too was made in China.  I wonder why the USA can't manufacture a good pencil sharpener?

product_title: HP 564 Cyan, Magenta & Yellow Original Ink Cartridges, 3 pack (CD994FN) DISCONTINUED BY MANUFACTURER
review_headline: Great Print Quality, Horrible Life Span
review_body: I will start off by saying that I absolutely love my HP PhotoSmart All in One EPrint Printer.  The functionality of the printer is amazing, and simply having the ability to print from anywhere in the world along with not having my printer hard-wired to my computer is amazing.  However, this is not a printer review, this is an ink review.  This is a great quality ink.  I it prints very accurate colors and photos look amazing! HOWEVER THIS LIFE SPAN OF THIS INK IS A NIGHTMARE!!!! Ive owned my printer for about a year now and i have bought ink at least 6 times now.  This is partly my fault because saw this printer and wanted it without looking into how the ink reviews were.  But still, there are other printers out there on the market that are capable of doing similar things with way better ink life-spans.  And yes, XL packs are available, but I am not sure if i am willing to spend almost $100 bucks on ink.  I hope this helps someone, I am considering buying another printer to use as my main one, and just having this one for the e-print and scanning functionalities.

product_title: Plymor 5" x 8", 4 Mil Heavy Duty Plastic Reclosable Zipper Bags
review_body: These bags are of excellent quality and are far superior to those found in walmart or other grocery stores.  They are 4 millimeters thick and feel heavy duty in hand.  The plastic seems used to be very sturdy and the volume is spacious given the size.  Mostly, I have used these bags for camping duties and my first aid kit asnd they have lasted for quite a long time with minimal wear.  Also, the zipping mechanism on these bags is MUCH stronger than the ziploc brand and the like.  They also seem to zip shut much easier and are easier to aline the zipper. However, when opening these bags, because the lock is stronger, you must be careful not to pull to hard as to not rip the plastice side seam.  I have not done this before but it seems like a possibility.  Afterall, these are still just plastic bags, they just are more equipped for harsher tasks.  One thing I would recommend would be to measure out the sizes of the bags to make sure they are the correct size you intend to purchase.  These bags are great for camping, first aid, general orginization and other tasks and will withstand a lot fo punishment before they break.  The price is also great for 100 of these bags.  Definitely worth the money difference from the 2 mil bags.  I highly reccomend this item.

product_title: Rolodex 66551 Rolodex Covered Tray Business Card File, 200 slotted Cards, 12 A-Z Tabs, Cherry
review_headline: attractive but not functional. slightly misleading photo.
review_body: This might be at place on a large modern office desk, but on my little writing desk it is bulky and awkward. I expected a more old-fashioned look and finish to this piece, but the picture is slightly misleading. The wood part of this item appears glossy in the picture but is actually finished in a matte natural fashion, without the 'yellowish' tint that would have made it match my kooky seventies desk. To me, this lessens the classic look I had expected. Still looks smart enough on my desk and feels sturdy, so that's only a minor complaint.   ~~MORE IMPORTANTLY~~, this organizer isn't very functional! Yes, it holds business cards, but the plastic part sets down inside the lip of the wood part, so the business cards have to be standing perfectly in order for the lid to shut without smooshing them. Frustrating if you like to collect business cards in yr rolodex, as I do, but a minor issue if you like using the index cards that come with the rolodex. Those stand straight rather well.   One more minor aesthetic thumbs-down is that each tab has two letters on it, not just one. I knew this in advance because it does say so in the item description, but I hadn't anticipated how much less organized this would make my business card collection appear. Meh. This was a *great* deal at the time I bought it, for under ten dollars, so it's hard to complain too much.

product_title: Optoma PlayTime LED Gaming Projector

product_title: Lucky Line 3 Way Pull Apart Key Chain, Silver, 1 per Card (71501)
review_body: I have been searching for a quick-release key ring that was a little more compact and would give me more than two separate rings.  After a lengthy search through tons of novelty or gadget keyrings I came across this item.  I was already using the typical push to release ring and found that it just made a large set of keys larger.    This key ring is perfect because:  1. It has no mechanism that has to be pushed to release or lock the rings back together.  Trying to fumble with a locking mechanism can be frustrating.  You simply pull firmly on the rings to separate.  There is an internal sprung ball system similar to what is used on socket tools to hold it together.   2. It helps keep your keys compact.  I have a Mazda flip key, work keys, house keys, and also carry a small knife and flashlight.  This ring lets me pull off the light or knife when I need to without carrying a long bulky set of keys that is uncomfortable in my pocket.  This item would also be great for camping etc. because you could tie multiple items, knives, lights, firestarters, and whatever else you need together with quick and easy access to whatever you need.  I like this little keyring, I bought two and I'm happy with this purchase.

review_headline: Two fatal flaws. I hate it.
review_body:
First, when the unit is operating normally, its lowest volume setting is too loud by a factor of 2 which is only good if you're hard of hearing. If you're not, this headset will probably damage your hearing until you no longer notice.

Secondly, the unit spontaneously stops working. It becomes necessary to disconnect the battery not just once but twice. I tried replacing the battery so that's not the problem. The result of accessing the battery so many times is that the cheap plastic cover will eventually loosen up and refuse to stay attached to the unit.

product_title: Wired Handheld USB Automatic Laser Barcode Scanner Reader With USB Cable
review_headline: you get what you pay for
review_body:

update:
We found this did not scan properly on a consistent basis, so I purchased a used Symbol scanner and now use this one as a backup and in the office where we only need it once in a while. review_body:

Once again everything indicated that wireless was set up but the printer couldn't be found. At this point there is a check box for setting up using the cable. I checked this, plugged in the cable, and the setup went through without any problem and after removing the cable wireless works. I would urge anyone to purchase a cable when you buy the  printer if you don't already have one.  The printer is a little noisy when feeding the paper. It sounds like it's about to jam up. review_body:
So far I am loving this scanner. It reads right into my open applications. I am a MAC user and this is the only scanner pen that works with a MAC. Set up was simple.

The \\"Pen\\" is not perfect. It often will read an \\"I\\" as a lc \\"L\\" or even as a \\"[\\" and such. Thus, you do have to review the text it inputs for character and spacing consistency. This is useful to me, however, as it forces me to actually read the material closely rather than just to \\"upload\\" it. This way I stay engaged with my writing even as I \\"record\\" citations.

Greater contrast on the source of origin yields better results as does working in brighter light. Start a little before the text you need so the scanner can pick up some clear space prior to scanning the first letter. This prevents the first word from getting mangled. Being able to track straight across the page and not at an angle or wiggling between lines also helps with greater accuracy.

But other than that, this is as good as it gets. I research and write for a living so this saves me a great deal of time. I certainly wish I had one of these in grad school!

review_headline: We don't even bother putting them away...
review_body:
I never thought I'd feel this way about a marker.
We have the set of thicker BIC Mark-It permanent markers, and those are wonderful and offer such a fantastic rainbow of colors and shades. These were a logical addition when my son's fine motor skills advanced and he started drawing more detailed pictures.
The colors are fantastic. What really impresses me is how nice and fluid they write. I'm used to the Sharpie ultra fine markers, and those definitely feel sort of draggy on the paper, but these do not.
The grips are a nice size. These aren't \\"chunky\\" by any means, but they definitely are thicker around than a typical pencil or those Sharpies I mentioned earlier. They do feel light, but balanced in the hand, which is important when the two \\"artists\\" using these both have motor skill issues, one has hypotonia, and the other has Rheaumatoid Arthritis.
We have spent so many hours with this set open in front of us, just doodling away in our notebooks. I found that I can really color in with a heavy hand (I have recently discovered the idea of Zentangles, though I'm more playing than practicing) and they do not bleed through the pages of a Moleskine Cahier (unlined) as much as my sharpies and my Micron pen have in the past. Of course, there are a few dots of bleed-through, but the BIC Mark-It's seem to not \\"traumatize\\" the paper as much when you are laying down ink... Of course, YMMV.
We are thrilled with this set. It is a bonus that it comes with organization in hand, in the nifty tri-fold clamshell case. There is just something visually pleasing about markers all in order, lined up nice and straight, that lets my creativity go wild because the tools are easy to access. The one issue I do have with these, which did not seem worthy of dropping a star from my rating, is that the pens can be challenging for me to remove from their spaces as they snap in. As we continue to work with them though, they seem to be loosening up.

product_title: USB Automatic Barcode Scanner Scanning Barcode Bar-code Reader with Hands Free Adjustable Stand (Black)
review_body:
After reading the reviews on this scanner, I purchased one. Really couldn't go wrong with the price, but didn't want a lot of hassle either.

Building an Access 2010 database for inventory control, orders and invoicing for our forthcoming online store. Because we have an inventory of over 1,500 items to be entered into our database I wanted to scan UPC codes into the (database) DB. In addition the scanner would be used for scanning UPC codes into an online service which will allow for product look up to get addition descriptive info and comparable market pricing.

Received the product promptly, in Amazons usual excellent packaging box. By the way, we are so impressed with the service we get from Amazon that it's become our number place to go to find products.

Setup was very easy and was able to figure it out without looking at the instructions. Oops, I got the bottom plate screwed into place, but had to look at the instructions to see that I had to remove the plate and install the vertical stand first and then screw the plate down into place. My error, hey who looks at instructions anyhow!

From reading the reviews I kinda dreaded attaching the scanner to the computer because of the encrypted instruction for scanner set up that was mentioned in some reviews. However, had my data entry form built in Access 2010 and the time came. By the way, if your planning on using this scanner with Access, make sure its a non numerical field or set the property for that field to text not a number field. Not much is said about this subject, so including it for others that may be looking. For Excel, click in the cell your going to scan into then Right click. Select Format Cells, Click the Number Tab at the top, then select Number in under the Category. To the right of that select 0 Decimal places. In Microsoft Word just place your cursor where you want the scan to be placed and use your scanner as you normally would. The scanner will place the number where ever you want.

Plugged the scanner into a USB port and gave Windows 7 plug and play time to install the correct driver automatically from their own database as there is no CD software provided with this product. Two beeps from the scanner were heard and pop up said, that the driver had been installed successfully. Placed my cursor in a Access text box that I had labeled UPC Code. Pointed the scanner at a UPC code on an inventory item to be scanned and heard a beep. Presto, the scanner had successfully scanned the UPC code into my entry from correctly. Checked the Access table and yes, the UPC code was in the storage table where it was supposed to be. Double checked the UPC code from the box to what was entered and it was correct. Yeah! I didn't scan any ISBN (book bar code) yet, so additional set up may be needed, but unsure.

I went to my online UPC look up service and placed my cursor in the entry box and scanned in the UPC code. Within a nano second I had a screen full of product pictures, info and comparable produce pricing. Wow! I am impressed! This will make product look up so much easier if my inventory has a UPC code on it.

The only con I can see is the distance between the trigger and the mounting cradle to allow me to pull the trigger is very small. Am saying this as I didn't want to pull the scanner out of it's cradle each time to scan an item. I have smaller fingers and would imagine larger fingers would be a problem. However, I also noticed that when the scanner sits in the cradle that the scanner is always on, so all I have to do is slide an item with a UPC code under the scanner and it scans automatically without pulling the trigger.

Unit is very nice looking, sturdy and seems to be heavy enough. You can't go wrong for the price!

Update: We purchased a second unit because the first one worked so well. Brand name was different on the new unit, but had the same results installing, operating, both computers using Win 7. We have so much inventory to enter that I now have my PC entering one product line, and the laptop entering another product line. Unit reads ISBN numbers very well too. When I power the computer up for the day, I hear two beeps from the scanner which is normal. Very nice unit!

review_headline: Doesnt work too well over USB cord
review_body: I've been using this printer for about a year, and it would always seem to go dead after it went to sleep.  I had to pull the power cord and let it reset (which sometimes took a few minutes) whenever I needed to print something.  I was about to throw this thing out before I went online and found a solution.  Someone in a forum had the same issue, and they said the fix was to use the CAT5 cable rather than the USB cable.  I then disconnected the USB cable and used a CAT5 cable to configure the printer as a network printer.  What do you know... the printer now works as it should.  It goes to sleep and wakes right back up automatically when its time to print.  Overall the printer works pretty good.  Its fast and the printouts are sharp.  After a year of occasional use I still have half the ink left.  You can view ink levels by going to the built in web interface (just type in the IP addy of the printer into a web browser).  It seems like HP didn't do a good job fixing all the bugs in this printer, so I have to give it 2 stars.  If it wasn't for the USB issue I had, I may have given it 4.

product_title: Bazic Mechanical Pencil Lead, 0.9 mm
review_body: I ordered a 10 pack of the student's choice BIC mechanical pencils and a 10 pack of this Bazic brand lead. First of all, I ordered (and payed for) the 10 pack of regular lead and got the 8 pack of \\"high quality\\" lead. At first I was disappointed because I got less than I ordered. Then I was happy because the pack I received is priced at 19.99 while the pack I purchased was only 3.99. I can't tell you if they sent me this package by mistake or if everyone who orders the basic gets the high quality. Alright, so I use the term high quality loosely. The first thing I did was write a test sentence with the lead included with the mechanical pencil. It's name brand lead and performed as expected. It was soft enough to write darkly but didn't break easily. It also was easy to erase. The first thing I noticed about the Bazic lead was that it pushed back into the pencil when I tried to use it! I was shocked. I double checked the sizes and both the pencil and the lead were labeled \\"0.9mm\\". I chose a different lead. It allowed me to write without retracting but would allow me to push it in without depressing the eraser, unlike the BIC lead which would not retract without depressing the eraser. Once I got the hang of using the lead, it was easy to write and didn't break easily. It was a little harder and thus, not as dark on the page. All-in-all I'm willing to put up with the retracting issue for the price. It's certainly not high quality, though.

product_title: Kodak ESP 6150 All-in-One Printer
review_headline: Do not buy Kodak ESP 6150 printer
review_body: I purchased a Kodak ESP 6150 AiO printer in March 2011 because it promised cheaper ink and at the time the reviews were good. The color quality was never great, but it worked OK. Then horizontal streaks started appearing in black and white printing. None of the built-in maintenance procedures helped. Eventually it hardly printed black and white at all, and the color also became poor. We did an online chat with Kodak in November 2011, which was OK, and the agent had a new printhead sent to us. After installing the new printhead, everything seemed better - for a while. The color stayed OK, but the black and white streaks returned. I found that if I did a clean printhead, it would print with only a few streaks. The next day, however, the streaks were much worse and required another clean printhead. When we receive the Kodak replacement, we plan to either sell it or give it away. I have no intention of buying another Kodak printer, ever. product_title: AAXA M2 Pico/Micro Projector with LED,  XGA 1024x768 Resolution, 110 Lumens, Media Player and HDMI
review_headline: Awesome parts, but dismal overall product
review_body: I got this projector last year for Christmas. Right out of the box I had a problem with the remote control. The projector has two volume controls, and one of them is only accessible via the remote control, so I couldn't use the projector for a few weeks while waiting for a new remote.   The fans in the projector are loud. Real loud. After a couple of months the fans also started to go on my projector. I had to send it back to AAXA (at my cost) to get them to fix it. It worked pretty decently on its return, maybe even a little quieter, but now its just as bad, with the fans making screaching noises.   The onboard audio is not loud enough to overcome the noise from the fans.   The crazy thing is, the projector works awesomely in every other way. It has a bright enough, and clear enough picture to make watching movies and tv pretty enjoyable. I have it plugged into a mini stereo for audio, and have that turned up pretty high to block out the fans.   The projector itself has played every type of media file i've tried, I had originally planned to attach it to my notebook and play through HDMI, but instead I just copy what I want to watch to a USB drive, and plug that into the projector.   It is amazing that they can make such a small projector, that plays so many audio files, but they can't put in decent fans. The unit does not get hot at all, so I imagine the fans could be turned down a whole lot. I'd guess that only one fan is actually needed.   If someone was to build the exact same projector, only with decent fans, then it would be a real all-star product. As it is though, it is a complete lemon.  I'm also not really happy with AAXA. Having to pay to get it fixed after a few months of use was pretty cruddy. Having it break in the same way again is just a testament to their quality. I would not buy anything from AAXA again.

product_title: Canon Pixma MX882 Wireless Office All-in-One Inkjet Printer (4894B002)
review_body: I used to have one of the earlier Canon Pixma models - the MP780, and that lasted about 6 years. This one is very similar but is even better. It's true that it is slightly 'plasticky' looking, however it's worked beautifully since I had it. What can it do?  Well basically, anybody can print to it if they are connected on the same wireless network (no issues with software or drivers on 64 bit Windows 7). The only cable you need for this thing is the power cable-everything else is wireless (if you choose). Anybody can scan documents on this thing too wirelessly. So this means you can put this printer just about anywhere and everyone can still use it.  Print quality looks good too.  So far so good, and hard to beat the price at this point (~ $150).  One other thing that has come up in reviews: it's supposed to be a relatively large all-in one printer, however I found that once I had switched out my old printer it seems about roughly the same size (i.e. OK, it is a bit bigger, but it'll probably still sit nicely in your old printer location).  UPDATE:  After several months I have found that this printer still works superbly. I am still on the original ink cartridges. I had no problems with installation if you simply go to the website and download the latest patches and software.  I can't comment on print quality because I generally don't care about that too much (as long as it's decent).  One other thing to note which I did not know when ordering this thing: you can actually scan in duplex mode too which saves you a large amount of time when generating .pdf files (i.e. put a large 2 sided document in the paper feed and simply press 'go' and walk away!). Very happy with this.
