product_title: Epson Powerlite 1760W WXGA 2600 Ansi Lumens LCD Multimedia Projector V11H361120
review_headline: Excellent Value For Presenters On The Go
review_body:
My wife is a trainer for teachers and throughout the year, she travels to various schools to present sessions on Singapore math.

As she can never tell what the projector situation will be like at the school or facility she visits, she has been borrowing projectors from her own school when she travels. This year, they mounted them all to the ceiling, so we were finally forced to buy one.

I wanted to get her something light as she's already typically traveling with her laptop and carry-on so I didn't want to add too much more mass to her travel load. At the same time, it had to meet various other criteria as well for brightness, resolution, and ease of use.

After recently having seen a Casio Slim XJ-A235 in person and being pretty much blown away, I was very settled on getting a Casio. However, the 2500 lumen XJ-A240 is nowhere to be found (out of stock almost everywhere online as of this writing) and I didn't want to buy up to the XJ-A250 or 245, which everyone seemed to have in stock. After researching portable projectors for a few hours, I finally found the 1760w, looked through the features, and decided to take the plunge, even with the lack of professional reviews online.

My biggest concerns going in was the fan noise as it was listed as being louder than the Casios which operate at 35dB normal/29dB Eco while the 1760w is listed at 40dB/30dB respectively.

However, I am pleasantly surprised. When you initially turn it on and when you switch from Eco to normal mode, the fan does kick up a notch, but it will settle back down into a very manageable state. In the absence of any sound? It would be kinda loud. But in a real world scenario in a classroom or conference room, it's not loud enough that you can't talk over it and not loud enough that you have to raise your voice. In Eco mode, it's not silent, but for all intents and purposes, it might as well be as it won't even be noticeable during a presentation. I've heard laptops with nosier fans that sound like a jet engine at takeoff compared to this projector.

Just to run through my other thoughts:

STRENGTHS:
+ Comes with EVERYTHING in the box. USB cable, VGA cable, power cable, remote, batteries, carrying case!
+ Cheaper than the Casio (though the bulb may not last as long)
+ Very light, compact, and low profile. Will fit easily into a rolling laptop brief along with your laptop.
+ Runs pretty quiet, IMO.
+ Lens has a built in cover that slides over it so that you can't lose it
+ Bright for the package. Can definitely use it with the lights on.
+ Price is great.
+ Sound is pretty good. Works over USB - my wife was a bit surprised when I played a video and sound was coming out of the projector. Better than the sound on her laptop.
+ Handled her desktop resolution of 1366x768 just fine.
+ It does get hot to the touch, but not so hot that you can pick it up and put it in the bag and go right after turning it off.

WEAKNESSES:
- USB connectivity is pretty slick, but lots of lag for video. If you're not using it for video, then the USB connectivity is pretty convenient as you can ditch the bulky VGA cable, but it'll really only work for stills. Video is fine over VGA.
- Automatic keystone means slight loss of real-estate. It essentially chops off the sides to get a rectangular picture, but it's definitely handy.
- Zoom is pretty weak; wish it had more range.
- Bag could definitely be better - more padding, a bit more space.
- Wish it had a dedicated button on the unit for switching Eco/normal - have to do it through the menu.

I can't report how well this projector would work as a replacement for a TV, but it's bright enough I think and quiet enough in Eco mode that you probably could.

Definitely a good buy for professionals looking to travel light or even as a full time, stationary projector. Can't speak for the life of the bulb, but it compares very favorably to the Casios in both brightness (even brighter, I think), sound levels, overall size, and features. Having now used both the Casio Slims and this Powerlite, I'd purchase this one again in a heartbeat.

UPDATE (10/31): Wife used it for two days straight at a conference she was presenting at. Reported back that it was \\"virtually silent\\" (quiet enough that it wasn't noticeable) in a room with 75 attendants. Said that it's the best projector that she's ever used, but then again, it's probably also the most expensive projector she's ever used given her normal pickings at school :) A great purchase and very satisfied.ze, and features. product_title: Dixon Ticonderoga Wood-Cased #2 Pencils
review_headline: Consumer Warning: Ticonderoga Pencils contain an FDA regulated Pesticide
review_body: Consumer be warned! Instead of one box of 96 pencils as ordered, we received 8 boxes of 12, and on each box the information this product contains MICROBAN, which is a brand of Triclosan, an FDA regulated Pesticide.  Triclosan is added to the pencil paint to \\"inhibit the growth of odor and stain causing bacteria on the pencil\\".  But then we read about Triclosan in Wikipedia and the New York Times (article: Antibacterial Chemical Raises Safety Issues, August 19th, 2011). Triclosan is under review by the FDA. Various studies have identified Triclosan as a possible hormone-disruptor, carcinogen, allergen and a pre-cursor to dioxin.  How many of us either remember chewing on pencils, or have children who do so?? Reputable companies should shy away from products with pesticides.  Further tidbits:  - Representative Edward J. Markey, Democrat from Massachusetts, has called for a ban on triclosan in hand soaps, in products that come in contact with food AND IN PRODUCTS MARKETED TO CHILDREN.  - In August 2009, the Canadian Medical Association asked the Canadian government to ban triclosan use in household products under concerns of creating bacterial resistance and producing dangerous side products (chloroform).  - A household paint manufacturer has voluntarily removed Triclosan from their paints.  - Colgate-Palmolive replaced triclosan with lactic acid in Palmolive Antibacterial Dish Liquid, and its Softsoap liquid hand soap has been reformulated without the chemical.  So make up your own mind.  For our part, our children will not be allowed to handle Ticonderoga pencils.  Neither in school nor in the home.  We are returning these items to Amazon for a refund.

product_title: RFID Blocking Rigid Shielded 2-Card Badge Holder (FIPS 201 Approved) by Specialist ID Sold Individually
review_headline: Discreet, RFID-shielded, impossible to get card out sometimes
review_body:
The pros: 1) Because it's clear plastic on the outside, this is discreet and not bulky - always a big plus with ID cards. 2) It's metal-backed inside on both sides, presumably to stop RFID chip from shouting its information to the world (at least to anyone with a scanner). 3) It's double-sided so you can put 2 ID cards in there. 4) The cards don't fall out easily, which is good (although this is also related to its biggest con). 5) Discreet loop on the back doesn't add to the visual weight of the holder.

Cons: 1) There is a little section (in the picture above it's over the woman's name) in the clear plastic where one uses the thumb to slide the card out, but it stops shy of the top of the badge holder. This feature is a bit TOO secure - the card may not fall out, but often you can't get the grip you need with your thumb in order to slide out the card. I have stood next to the card reader and tried everything - wiping my thumb on my clothes, breathing on the card, licking my thumb, wiping the badge... it is not exactly the coolest look, and doesn't make one look terribly professional :)
2) There is a little clear plastic loop on the back for attaching the badge holder to a lanyard or badge clip, and I have gone through several of these badge holders because that loop can snap right off.

In all, I'd say this is a decent badge holder, but not perfect. Maybe if the makers extended the thumb-tab to the top?

review_body:

They are stamped \\"700 mAh capacity\\" which is the same as the OEM battery pack, although most replacement battery capacity markings should be taken with a grain of salt, and are essentially meaningless.

review_headline: Great cabinet, but $319??? Big Lots has the SAME cabinet for $129...
review_body: (As of Jan. 19, 2012, this cabinet is still sold at Big Lots for the price of $129)  Wow, was so funny to see this cabinet pop up while I was just looking for a totally unrelated replacement \\"medicine\\" cabinet!! BUT THIS ONE-STAR REVIEW IS FOR THE PRICE ONLY, NOT THE PRODUCT!!!!!!!!!!!!  I bought this cabinet impromptu one day while shopping at Big Lots for Christmas wrap at the last minute. Until I can find something I prefer for the space I needed it for, I bought it for temporary storage for that area rather than keeping things in boxes and working out of them, which is horrendous. It's the SAME CABINET, same brand, but Big Lots had it on sale for only $129, not $319 (or $250 also from another Amazon seller!) I think even the non-sale price from Big Lots was lower, probably $149, $179 TOPS... I forget what it was, pretty much wasn't paying attention to that. But no WAY is this cabinet worth $319 or 250 bucks! (Currently, there is no other Amazon seller for less than $250). But as of Jan. 19, 2012, this cabinet is still at the $129 price at Big Lots (you can see it on the Big Lots website, but it's only \\"available in stores.\\"  I have to say, it's nice and BIG and not that difficult (for your son LOL) to put together. Let me give you an idea of the size: One HALF of ONE shelf holds a 20-roll pack of toilet tissue, or easily 10 towels.  The slight design on the front makes it look much better than plain white surface laundry-type cabinets that are so common. Honestly? It really doesn't look like a \\"cheap\\" cabinet, esp. from afar, and gives a pretty good presentation when you're just passing it. Only when you examine it closely or inspect it inside can you tell it's a put-together \\"Sauder-type\\" structure.  So until I stop driving the antique dealers crazy looking for a piece to perform as a toiletries cabinet that fits my exact dimensions, wood, finish, and style, this big \\"little cabinet\\" is doing the job quite nicely for a lousy $129. Perhaps I may go the route ofa custom cabinet that won't be antique, but that would be a complete bummer. I sort of prefer to keep this temporary cabinet and continue hoping :).... But really.... just go to Big Lots and buy this cabinet if you must have it or need it, but in no way is it worth $319-250. However, it's a steal at $129, and would be much more appropriately priced at around $149-179 on a non-sale day.

review_headline: Fantastic shredder, very quiet, actually shreds 17 sheets!
review_body: For some reason I thought this was a 20 sheet shredder and I gave it a shot with 20 pages of printer paper.  It stopped about a third of the way through and auto reversed for easy removal, pretty impressive jam prevention.  Then I tried one page less at a time until I was down to 17 sheets and it shredded it no problem at all.    The first shredder I received was non-functional but Amazon's return policy is fantastic and they replaced it at no charge.  How loud is this shredder?  It's about as loud as an electric can opener, perhaps even quieter!  This shredder is really heavy, about 50 pounds, and that is what sold me on it.  I figure the heavier the mechanics the more power it has to shred, and boy does it have power!  If you are looking for a heavy duty shredder I would highly recommend this one.  Just don't drop it from the back of a UPS truck and I'm guessing it will last a long time.  UPDATE:  Well I've been shredding like a mad man for days now and everything is running smoothly except I get an occasional error that says the bin is full when it's really not full.  I get the loud beeping noise and the red flashing light and the thing shuts down until I open and close the bin.  Very annoying and seems to be happening more and more.  I tried to vacuum the inside of the unit but it didn't help.  Not sure if this is a normal problem?  Or maybe there is a way to turn off the sensor?  I'm going to contact the manufacturer to see what they say.  I've also run it constantly until it basically shuts down from overheating.  I can shred for about 20 minutes striaght, which is a lot of shredding.  When it shuts down from overheating it just stops with no warning at all and whatever you have in the slot gets locked up tight and stays there until it cools down, and at that point it scares you because it will continue the last shred job several minutes later.    I'm still happy with my purchase, it's amazing how much this thing can shred!

review_body: First off, website was deceptive.  Unless you read the very, very fine print, you won't know that the base model of this \\"MFP\\" doesn't include a FAX.  How can it be an \\"MFP\\" without a FAX? You literally have to disassemble the ADF then tear out the jammed document bit by bit.  Finally convinced HP to send another ADF...it jams too...but only if original weight is less than say 22 lbs paper.  20 lb originals are very iffy for duplex copying...may jam, may not.  Third, variable output quality.  Actually, print quality is OK and one of the reasons I bought HP...none of that light-weight eyestrain typeface that comes standard on every Brother printer.  However, copies are atrocious.  There is no 'copy' setting that will produce consistently dark enough copies that can actually be copied themselves!  Finally, technical support that actually gives the US Post Office a run for its money in terms of indifference, attitude and stupidity.  Now today, my partner has informed me the printer jams on virutally every print job.  To clear, one must remove and replace the paper tray, open and close the toner door, then wait for printer to reset.  I'll sell ours today (eight months old, spare ADF, only 18k copies) for $500.  Still have the original shipping carton...hell of a deal.  My how the mighty HP has fallen.  Used to be the defacto standard of reliability & quality.

product_title: Print.Save.Repeat. Dell F362T High Yield Remanufactured Toner Cartridge for 5230, 5350 [21,000 Pages]
review_headline: Excellent product, oustanding customer service - almost
review_body:
This Dell-compatible cartridge was purchased and received (very quickly) in November 2011. Unfortunately, the cartridge was not needed until Jan 2012. When the item was actually installed, we discovered it was leaving a black stripe along the right edge of every page. Having seen this in defective cartridges for other printers (different makes), I realized that this could be a BIG problem (well over the 30-day exchange limit usually in effect with Amazon). It was an expensive cartridge (but much less expensive than the original brand) so I decided to defy the odds and contact the company. Now comes the outstanding customer service part: I sent an email, including a PDF sample of what I was seeing, and they responded within 2 hours (amazing!). They apologized and informed me that a new cartridge was being shipped immediately - no questions, no argument. I was truly taken aback - as anyone who has read the reviews of companies selling printer cartridges on Amazon will know, this can become a horrible nightmare. Instead, it was simple, fast and amazing.

The new cartridge arrived within 4 days. However, the installed cartridge began, inexplicably, to print correctly (no latent images or streaks). I contacted the company to suggest that we keep the now working-perfectly cartridge and pay them for the replacement - but they said \\"No - please send the cartridge that was having a problem back to us. We want to take no chances that it will develop a problem again. We also want to examine it to see if we can determine what went wrong.\\" Now THAT really was amazing - not only did they take ownership of the problem, but they demanded the opportunity to correct it. With the pre-paid label they sent me to return the \\"damaged\\" cartridge with, the cost to me was zero and the result was a perfectly working cartridge and a very happy customer (who will continue to buy printer cartridges from this company).

This product, and the company selling it, deserves your support. With this kind of customer service, this company deserves to be around for a long time!

UPDATE - MARCH 1, 2012

Some serious concerns have arisen concerning this company since I originally wrote this review. Although the cartridges are rated as providing approx. 21,000 copies, after buying five of these cartridges, we have yet to see anything close to that yield. Approx. close to 4,000 is more realistic (we print tax returns for approx. 5,000 clients during the tax season, using 3 printers (only one Dell) and a high-speed copier). Originally, we were purchasing the normal yield cartridges from Dell and getting the same yield (approx. 4,000) which was acceptable. The cost for the high-yield cartridges are more than double the cost of the normal yield cartridges. Getting over 5 times the yield for only 2.5 times the cost seemed like a great deal - but, again, the yield has been very disappointing. When this concern was related to the company, it fell on deaf ears - three emails have brought no response at all. Additionally, they have apparently discontinued their program of offering free return of the empty cartridges for recycling - three requests for the labels have also been ignored. So the empty cartridges are headed for the local landfill and we are searching for a new supplier or going back to Dell. A good price is only a great deal when it is for a good product and backed by good customer service - all of which are now in question concerning this company.

EPILOGUE - MARCH 19, 2012

After posting the above update, the CEO of the company contacted me and expressed his personal apologies to me and promises that the \\"wrongs would be righted\\". He explained that the unanswered emails were due to an employee's error, as well as a planned facilities re-location which caused havoc with some of their connections. I was assured that he would be monitoring this and that the employee now understands the importance of follow-through to make certain a customer is satisfied. In addition, I was also assured that the recycling of their cartridges was very important to them and, again, the labels should have been emailed immediately. I have since received copies of the intended email replies, including the labels for returning the cartridges to them at no cost to me.

To be completely fair, I was very surprised to get this response from the CEO of the company (who called me three times!). Obviously, they are very serious about wanting 100% customer satisfaction and earning customer loyalty. That is VERY refreshing, and encouraging, in this economy where so many businesses are cutting back in customer support.

After examining additional printer reports, we have also determined that, although it isn't up to what we had hoped, the AVERAGE yield of the cartridges is close enough to the average yield we received from the OEM cartridges (and the cost is significantly less).

As a result of this, we will continue to support this company with our business. Hopefully, they will continue to build their company on this kind of customer support!

I have let it air out in the garage for a week and the scent is just as strong as it continues to off-gas, so I'm going to be throwing it out.  Other than that, the pages are quite pretty with sweet pictures and pleasant colors.  The artwork is a bit more \\"busy\\" than I would prefer, but I would have gotten used to it I think and enjoyed the drawings.  It feels like an elegant planner, if not for the scent.

product_title: Swingline Large Rubber Finger Tips, Size 13, 12-Pack, (S7054033C)
review_body: For years, I've used these as a thimble when quilting.  Although they don't last forever as metal thimbles do, the rubber allows you to grasp the needle easily to pull through the fabrics, and to have more control when inserting the needle.  Similar items are sold in quilt shops at a much higher cost.

product_title: 100 6x10 Bubble Mailers, #0
review_headline: Very tight fit but really they work fine for DVD/Blu-Ray/Games
review_body: The quality of the sides and the adhesive is good.  They can be a really tight fit for certain DVD cases but I have yet to find one that doesn't fit.  Yes I really had to cram a few in there but there was absolutely no tearing and no fear in my mind of tearing.  Padding is adequate and I am really glad I bought these actually.  Best price and they do their job WELL.  If you have some kind of disease or something that limits your hand/wrist strength or something then you might have a problem since most DVD cases etc won't just slide right in.

product_title: August to August Calendar 2011-2012 Licorice
review_body: I've been purchasing these August to August calendars since the early 1990s.  Seems like much of my year runs on the academic calendar so it's pretty useful.  I love the organization of the calendar and there is plenty of room to write notations, etc.  Nice sized format and durable - I've lugged mine in a backpack and have taken them around the world.  You'll LOVE this calendar!

product_title: HP LaserJet 2055d Toner OEM# CE505A 2300 Yield - Premium compatible toner
review_body: The advertisement language (HP LaserJet 2055d Toner OEM# CE505A 2300 Yield - Premium compatible toner by HP) which leads one to believe that this is an OEM and not a re-manufactured part.  Take the time to read the entire advertisement and you will decide not to buy.

product_title: Canon CNNMP27D Standard Function Calculator
review_body: This looks like a good calculator, but I am not buying it from Amazon because they have lied about the list price to make this look like a bargain.  The exact same model is listed at $59.99 on Canon's web page.  I'm not saying that it isn't worth $59.99.  If that seems like a fair deal to you, then buy it.  I am just insulted that Amazon would state a list price that isn't true to make it look like they are giving you a deal.  Unethical to say the least.

product_title: Fujitsu ScanSnap S1500M Instant PDF Sheet-Fed Scanner for the Macintosh
review_headline: Mine came with Adobe Acrobat 9 Pro
review_body: I wanted to write a review for two reasons: 1) Because I love this scanner and I want to contribute to a 5 star rating, 2) because I know that many people are probably hesitant to purchase this scanner because of all of the reviews, and even specs on the Fujitsu website, that indicate that this scanner comes with Adobe Acrobat 8 Pro, which is NOT lion compatible. I decided to buy it anyway though and just bite the bullet for the upgrade; I think the scanner itself is worth $400--any extra software, especially since it is not REQUIRED for operation, I considered a bonus.  Well anyway, I was pleased to find out that my Scansnap S1500M CAME BUNDLED WITH ADOBE ACROBAT 9 PRO. No, I'm not confusing this with the windows version. I have the mac version, and it is Acrobat 9 Pro. They must have heard the customer complaints and started shipping the most recent models with it. Hope it helps everyone to know this! I was hesitant to buy for a while because of that, but I'm glad I did buy!  Thanks Fujitsu!

product_title: Crosley CR59-PI Princess Phone with Push Button Technology, Pink
review_headline: Love it, even after five years!
review_body: A lot of people complained that the phone broke easily.  I can't imagine what they are doing to it.  I've had mine for five years and it's still working just fine. It's a pretty phone, too, and you can actually hear with the receiver, unlike today's cordless models and corded models with those funny shaped receivers.  I also like that you can hold it between your shoulder and your ear and thus have both hands free to do something else with.  This is impossible with todays smooth, oddly shaped receivers.

product_title: Xerox ColorQube Solid ink Color Printer, Up To 40 Pages/min for Color and Black and White (8570DN)
review_headline: Ink costs more than the printer!  Trouble prone.
review_body:
I've owned Xerox Phaser and ColorCube printers for more than 10 years. I just got an 8570 as part of a warranty replacement for an older version. Xerox got tired of sending their tech out to fix the old one, and just gave me a new one. For me the bottom line is pretty simple: they're expensive to own.

GOOD
The print quality is excellent for business letters. It makes my small business look like a big business. This is why I keep the printer.

BAD
The printer costs less than one set of ink! [[ASIN:B005QG64BC Xerox Ink Genuine 8570 10 Pack Ink Set (4 Black, 2 Yellow, 2 Cyan, and 2 Magenta)]] And it takes 2 sets of ink to fill the printer.



Breaks down always. There's wax to melt, nozzles to keep clean, gears to synchronize. The inside of one of these things is incredibly complicated. I spend about $250 a year for a Xerox maintenance contract. I've never not used it. But hey, the Xerox guy comes out the next day and I keep a cheap backup laser printer, so breakdowns are only a problem if you don't buy the warranty.

product_title: duogreen Cordless Telephone Battery for AT&T/Lucent 3101, 3111,BT-8001, BT-8300, SL82118
review_body: The Duogreen battery is an excellent replacement battery when the originals die out. They are only rated at 700 mAh, but are able to hold a charge for several days. These are less costly than the OEM batteries and are even guaranteed for a year. There are cheaper batteries available ([[ASIN:B003IFMZAM Cordless Phone BATTERY For AT&T SL82308 SL82418 SL82618 TL92328 SL82318 SL82518 SL82658 TL92378 TL92378 SL82218 SL82408 SL82558 TL92278 TL76008]]), but those don't hold a charge as well and tend to die rather quickly. Duogreen is an excellent buy and in the long run, are more cost-effective than the cheapies.

product_title: Fujitsu ScanSnap S1500 Instant PDF Sheet-Fed Scanner for PC
review_body: It is wonderful because it scans both sides of a page at once.  You can scan pictures that are on flexible paper and see the back side where people sometimes write the names of the people.  It also will do longer paper than 8 1/2 by 11 sheets.  You don't need to change the settings it just copies the size the paper really is.

product_title: Panasonic KX-FAT461 KX-MB2000 Series Toner Cartridge Replacement
review_body: Newer toner cartridge that isn't available at the toner refill locations yet.  Better price than at the big stores, quick delivery, and purchased an extra to be stocked for next time!

product_title: Hawaii Map Blue Notebook Small
review_body: This little notebook exceeded my expectations 20 fold!  The double spriral binding is a plus and the covers are very sturdy.  The paper inside has a light blue tropical pattern on the top and bottom.  The paper is also lined for easy note taking.  Overall I was very pleased with this product

product_title: Sophia Global Compatible Ink Cartridge Replacement Set for Canon PGI-225 CLI-226 (Pack of 6: 2 PGI-225 Large Black, 1 CLI-226 Small Black, 1 Cyan, 1 Magenta, 1 Yellow)
review_body: just got this ink...after spending more than $60 a month on canon ink we decided to give this a go. we just received it and have printed a few photos and documents. had no problems with the compatibility when we put the ink in and it's printing just fine. can't really tell the quality yet as we have not printed a photo to compare it to with the more expensive ink. as of now however, we are happy and thankful to be printing for 1/4 of the price!

product_title: Panasonic DECT 6.0 Cordless Phone with Anwering System
review_headline: Call Quality is Bad, Bad, Bad!
review_body: Panasonic has always developed great phones over the years.  This phone set is the exception.  The call quality is muffled to other people with low volume and very muffled to your ears also if you've had a phone with better call quality.  I've even had some call drops despite the phone being 20 feet away.    The screen quality is different on every handset.  Some subtle shadows in different areas of the LCD screen.  I also don't understand its charging system.  I charged the batteries on my MAHA battery charger then put the batteries inside the phone and connected to the base(s).  It registered 1 bar of energy on the handset's LCD screen despite the batteries independently testing out at FULL strength.  The base would continue charging for several hours until it deemed the phone at full charge (3 bars).  This sounds like some iffy electronics going on with this system.  Needless to say.  It was the substantially inferior call quality and cheapness of the construction quality of the handsets that prompted me to return it.  Great compelling features, but nowhere near good enough to keep it.  I hope this is not a sign of Panny going downhill in the quality spectrum on its once touted products....

product_title: Melissa & Doug Child-Safe Scissor Set
review_body: My son loves it. He plays both a lot. Good product. I agree with others. The blue is very easy to use but not the red one.

product_title: T-9 ,Thai English, English Thai, Electronic Translator Speaking Pocket Translation Dictionary.
review_body: I bought the translator for my wife and she really enjoys it. It is simple yet efficent. The best thing that she likes about it is that it talks.

product_title: Avanti Christmas Cards, Festive Frog, 10 Count
review_body: I ordered two boxes of these, and think they're fun.  But, one of them has the \\"Peace\\" work in glitter, and the other one was missing it and just had the frog.  I didn't bother to contact the company, but I thought it was strange.

product_title: Brother 411 Brougham 10-Pitch All Daisy Wheel Typewriters
review_body: The new daisy wheel is perfect.  I paid the price for \\"quick ship\\" because I needed to use my typewriter ASAP.  Upon arrival,  I took the old wheel out, inserted the new one, and started typing.  It was amazing !!  Thank you, Amazon.

product_title: Projector Lamp 003-120242-01 / 610 330 7329 / POA-LMP105 for CHRISTIE LX380, LX450 / EIKI LC-XG250, LC-XG250L, LC-XG300, LC-XG300L / SANYO PLC-XT20, PLC-XT20L, PLC-XT25, PLC-XT25L
review_body: This lamp is of good quality. The price was good and easy to install. This was not the original equipment,  but works great for our church ceiling mounted projector.

product_title: Black Piano Keyboard Style Design Soft Silicone Skin Gel Cover Case for Verizon At&t Sprint Apple Iphone 4 4s + Microfiber Bag
review_headline: Black Piano KeyBoard Style Design Soft Silicone Skin Gel Cover Case for Verizon At&t Sprint Apple iPhone 4 4s + Microfiber Bag
review_body: I absolutely LOVE this case. I received it a day after it was supposed to arrive. I not only go this case w/ a microfiber bag they also sent me an extra case, PINK at that. I bought this for my iPhone 4s and it fits PERFECTLY. I would definitely recommend this to all my friends.

product_title: Monet Art La Jardin a Giverny Garden at Giverny MOUSE PAD
review_body: The mousepad is very pretty - I received many compliments on it. It adds a nice bit of color and cheer to the workspace.

product_title: ALLBOXES DIRECT SS-320 PICTURE/MIRROR PROTECTION KIT
review_body:

review_body: I like it it's easy to replace but doesn't last to long because my tv in on 24 hours a day a year is about how long it last

product_title: Olympus TP-7 Telephone pick up
review_body: It works exactly as it is supposed to. It is easy to use and doesn't take up any room to store because it is so small. I also like that the cord is long enough to reach without pulling.

review_body: I have had this telephone for about two years now and am going to trash it.  It has been the worst phone ever.  Will go back to my cheap Walmart phones...much better quality.

product_title: Plantronics M214C Headset with Adjustable Volume
review_body:
our first headset lasted 5+ years for two busy businesspeople using it 7 days a week. the wire finally frayed, but the headset was still working when we ordered this replacement.

replacement works great - just like its predecessor. affordable, comfortable, does the job.

ps - we rely on the mute button on our vtech phone - not the mute button on the headset it is not reliable.

product_title: WorkFit-S Sit-Stand Workstation without Worksurface, Dual, Aluminum/Black
review_headline: Excellent product, main con is that monitors are not 100% firm or adjustable
review_body: As everyone says, easy install (about 30-40 min). Easy to use. Makes day in front of computer much easier.   Unlike other reviewers, I have had no problem using a mouse in the mousepad (and I use the high-foot-print [[ASIN:B00008KWWF 3M Ergonomic Mouse, Optical, USB/PS2 Compatible, Large Size, Black (EM500GPL)]])  Using for a week, I stand about 3-4 hours a day now.  I don't have back problems, just wanted to not have to sit all day.  Note that one can buy an accessory, [[ASIN:B004U632OQ Workfit-s Worksurface]] to the ergotron desk. It provides working space to have papers or other items (say extra mouse) at keyboard height [I have not tried it].  The main complaint I have is that the monitors don't tilt and they do shake a little bit as I type sometimes.  I am typing softer now and it is not a problem at all 90% of the time now. I suspect that in a few weeks it won't be a problem.  I bought the hinged-monitor support (cheaper elsewhere) that allows me to rotate one monitor. that's is very useful when i want to show the screen to people sitting on the other side of my desk, and to achieve a more comfortable viewing angle.  A minor thing to consider: everyone coming to your office will talk about it.  Overall I highly recommend. My concern about shaking is probably not an issue for most users.

product_title: Ooma Telo Free Home Phone Service
review_body: Overall quality is very good.  However, results may vary depending on your location.  I still have lagging two way conversations, almost like half duplex. product_title: Sealed Air Recycled 5/16 Inch x 12 Inch x 100 Feet Bubble Wrap (91145)
review_body: The Bubble Wrap arrived within a day or two. Fantastic! It was carefully packaged and is of good quality and a good value for the money. Only difficulty is in getting it out of the blue and white box. It's wedged in there a bit tightly. But I'd buy it again.

product_title: 32GB Strontium NITRO 466X Microsdhc UHS-1 memory Card with Idrive Card Reader
review_body: This is the best graphing calculator to purchase for college math and science courses.  I've used it up through Calculus 2 now, and also in several Chemistry and Biology courses. I've had a few classmates who did not realize that until they could not use their $150 calculator when they needed it the most.    If you are looking for a calculator and unsure which model to get this one: works great, never a problem for instructors, and the most common calculator in use so easy to get help in its use if you need it.  I also work part time in retail, and amazon was cheaper even with my discount.  Amber Kincaid

product_title: X-ACTO Powerhouse Electric Pencil Sharpener, Navy Blue
review_headline: Motor failed after a few years of moderate family use
review_body: I've read the other 1-star reviews and I'm submitting this to add some visibility on the home use case. I got this for my family because I didn't want to clamp an old-fashioned hand-crank pencil sharpener to any of my nice furniture, or drill more holes in the wall. Unfortunately, it failed after only a few years of very moderate home use. I took it apart and discovered the motor has cheap plastic bearings. Once the rotor started bouncing against the stator, it wasn't long before the slip exceeded the ability to generate torque.
I recently purchased this item and the product was of poor quality. It was not properly filled with ink. They have made it right by sending out an another product. Thank you for making this right.

product_title: Bankers Box Holiday Ornament Storage Box, Large, Red/Green, 2 Pack (4654101)
review_body:
These boxes are okay once assembled, which is an IQ test in and of itself because the instructions (read pictures only) leave a lot to be desired. It took me about a half hour to assemble the two boxes, once I figured out what to do, and all of the pieces were accounted for.

However, I still do not know what is meant by 56 \\"adjustable compartments.\\" It is true that there are 56 slots in each box for storing ornaments, in two levels divided by a fairly thin cardboard. Each compartment is approximately 3 and 3/4 inch long, 3 and 1/4 inch wide, and 3 and 1/8 inch deep. Once assembled, there is no \\"adjustment\\" of the spaces, unless you were to leave out one of the cross pieces to create additional space, but then the total number of compartments would reduce.

My biggest concern is that that the cardboard cross pieces that create the compartments are the most flimsy, followed by the cardboard piece that separates the box into two layers. The end result for me is that heavier ornaments would go on the bottom layer and not the top. Insofar as the manufacturer's (made in the USA) claim that the box is \\"maximum protection for fragile ornaments\\" goes, not so much. I am using the boxes to store fabric, plastic, brass, and wood items; the only breakables I would put in these boxes are those I can stand to lose. This item would have received a three-star rating but for the fact that each box is worth only $5 to me, and they are currently selling for twice that much.

product_title: Noodlers Ink Fountain Pen, Hard Rubber (Ebonite) – Green-Black
review_headline: Not a pen typical of Noodlers ink
review_body:
My first impression of this pen when I received it was that it is one of the ugliest pens imaginable. product_title: Merkury Innovations M-KRL110 E-book Travel Light
review_headline: Don't buy this for use with Kindle (2011)
review_body: I purchased this for use with my new Kindle, the 2011 model, non-touch, no keyboard.  While the light is very bright, the clip is too big for the Kindle. I managed to clip it to the windowsill near my bed, so it's not totally useless for me, but I really wanted a Kindle light.  If you want a light for a Kindle, don't get this.

product_title: Mickey Spiral Notebook & Pen Set
review_headline: My daughter is happy with this one.
review_body: This item was not the reason for my purchase, but Amazon was a suggestion and my daughter is happy with this additional purchase as a supplement.

product_title: Canon PIXMA MG3120 Wireless Inkjet Photo All-In-One (5289B019)
review_headline: Nice printer--love the iPhone print program!!
review_body:
I took a BUNCH of photos for this review...they are uploaded above. (There are pix of the packaging, the accessories, the printer, the set up, the software, the iPhone app and various screens, and the finished documents.) CLICK ON VIEW AND SHARE RELATED IMAGES

When I first got this to review, I was thinking, \\"Oh, golly, another printer???\\" I have three already (that I have deemed worthy enough to keep) and I didn't need another one. I figured this meant I could give a pretty darned honest review. If anything, I'm really hard to please.

First, this thing is big. I know, it has to be, to have the scanner and all, but it is tall and relatively cumbersome to move.

It was difficult to remove from the box. I had to flip it upside down and carefully lift the box off of the printer. Don't let it tip over.

Once out, there is a TON of tape on this thing. Just when you think you've gotten all of the protective film, tape, and cardboard squares off, there is another one hiding. This is a good thing, because it has that very shiny, reflective finish, and you don't want to have scratches upon arrival. (A drawback to the glossy finish are the innumerable fingerprints and smudges that are apt to happen--you can see them in the photos and I was trying to keep it nice and pretty for you.)

Insert your CD with the software/drivers into your laptop...let it autorun.

As directed, plug it in and go...put the ink cartridges in (easy!) and have printer paper on hand for that test print.

I have set up so many printers, and yes, you can do it wirelessly--but it's ALWAYS easier to do with the USB cable. Without exception. So, I tried the wireless connection first (just for you all, folks!) but when it hung up (as it always does--here and at friends' houses, too), I resorted to the included USB cable. Piece of cake.

Except.

When the software says that it can't find the printer--wait another 30 seconds. It will find it.
Just don't touch anything and let it finish.

Once it's set up, follow the directions to run the test print.

During the set up process, I took my iPhone and went to the App Store. I searched for \\"Canon print software\\" and downloaded the Canon iEPP program.

I ran the test print sheet.
I printed a photo from my iPhone (see pictures).
I scanned a document.

The quality of the prints are really NICE. The speed is what impressed me--the sheets were printed very quickly (quicker than my Epson or either of my HP's) and this thing prints QUIETLY. Very nice.

I printed a 20 page document without issue. Colors of the photos are nice, crisp, and bright. The print is clear. The pages ran through quickly and didn't jam. And it was beautifully quiet.

The price of this printer is amazing for what it gives you. It's NOT a FAX (bummer, Canon!) but aside from that (relatively big) drawback, but the other aspects are really great.nce it's set up, follow the directions to run the test print. review_headline: Just what I was looking for!!
review_body: Great triple stand at a great price. I usually dont write reviews unless an item exceeds my expectations or is bad. review_body: I purchased this as a gift to my girlfriend who is a law school student. Now she no longer needs to lug all those ridiculously heavy books to class! product_title: Erase Markers
review_body: I wanted an economical but easy to use and stable dry erase marker for our conference room.  Green was the cheapest color (at 12 markers per box) I could find, and I felt secure ordering an Expo product since I'd used their markers for years.  The markers write smoothly and after about 2 months of use I'm still on only my first marker.  I use the product about three times a week for about two hours each time.  If this company ever offers a sale on black with free super-saver shipping, however, I'll purchase that instead.  A definite plus has been the absence of any intoxicating odor.  Overall, I'm satisfied with the product.

review_body: We use these types of devices throughout our company and are always looking for a better one. We found it right here. It's like watching TV compared to the little round ones we we using previously. The pair of lamps in this unit make it nice and bright. This magnifier lamp has a very nice action. When you adjust it's position, the mechanism feels nice and smooth - almost hydraulic. The rotation of the head is a little tight at first though.  And, the cover for the glass tends to fall down while you're looking through it, but it is easily removable if that becomes a problem. These little nuances are not enough for me to warrant a four star rating. This unit gets five stars from me and everyone here who has used it.

review_body: This item was purchased for my office at work. The mesh coat hook fits snugly on my three inch partition. Looks great!

product_title: Avery Foil Mailing Labels, 3/4 X 2-1/4, Gold, 300/Pack
review_headline: Very nice looking labels, but tricky to use
review_body:
These gold foil labels are beautiful. They have a very classy, elegant look. The quality is everything you would expect from Avery.

The only downside is that they're a bit tricky to use. Inside the package is a sheet of paper with recommended printer settings for several types of printers. Several of the printers listed in the table include a suggestion to only use the color ink cartridge, even if you're printing in black.

My particular printer (an HP 1610) is not listed in the table, so I assumed it was OK to use black ink.

The results look great, but even after letting the labels dry for more than 12 hours, the ink still smudges when I touch it.

With that in mind, I would recommend using the color cartridge even if your printer isn't listed on the settings sheet. I deducted two stars from my rating because color ink is very expensive and I don't like being forced to use it when I'm printing in black; that's what the (less expensive) black cartridge is for. I also don't like the fact that the color ink requirement isn't mentioned anywhere on the outer packaging. Customers deserve to know this information before making a purchase.

If Avery could remedy this issue, I'd gladly give these labels five stars.

product_title: 6 Pack (3xBlack + 1 of Ea. Color) Compatible Ink w/ Chip for Canon Pixma iP3300 iP3500 MP510 MX700 PGI-5BK CLI-8
review_body: I ordered these a few months ago for my Canon printer.  So far, all the cartridges work perfectly and I can't see any difference between this ink and the OEM ink.  What a fantastic value!  I am definitely going to order again!

product_title: Canon DR-3010C Duplex Sheetfed Scanner
review_body: Scanner works almost just as it says. Speed is great as long as the settings are on correctly (so it knows to scan for speed not higher quality). You can put in paper face up or down it reads both. So far I have found that the max feed is about 40 not 50. But that's still pretty good. When it jams or has to many pieces of paper, it's a simple fix not a huge to do. That is really nice. It will simply pick up where it left off. Would highly recommend if you need high speed scanner for business or home use.

product_title: Desktex Anti-Slip Polycarbonate Desk Protector, Smooth Surface, 29 x 59 Inches, Clear (FPDS2959RA)
review_body:
After using a variety of smaller plastic mats, I found this item. It covers the entire desk, fits perfectly, and has radius edges. (I guess it doesn't cover the entire desk, as those radius edge leave tiny corners uncovered, but that's no big deal and the radius edges are a nice safety feature.)

The mat doesn't slip, and its great for writing on. It does have a very slight pebbling, but not large enough to affect writing, and feels good. It also adds a very subtle frosted effect, but don't worry, anything placed under the mat is completely visible.

I'm considering buying another one.

product_title: Ion ISC12 Document Scanner
review_headline: Nice scanner, does what I wanted
review_body:

light

*****************

I don't consider this a negative unless you consider getting a piano and not being gershwin the first time or several times you try to play:) this is just a matter of practice and wiggling the book around and lining up the arrows that are on the sides of the scanner and realizing that is how much will be scanned, plus the scanning light is in the middle so you have to remember to start above where you want to scan and follow through all the way down.

For books I have found using the non skid kitchen mats that go under cutting boards also keeps it fairly steady so I can concentrate on using both hands to keep the scanner straight and not worry about the book sliding around.

However, in just a few days I can see how much my scans have improved. Don't be afraid to scan sideways either if that makes the fit easier, you can always turn a sideways picture straight with the software. Even go from the bottom up, which has helped on some of the pages I've tried to scan.

The clarity and quality of scans I'm getting make me happy. I have a ton of cookbooks and I want to scan them, upload them to [[ASIN:B00493WILI Living Cookbook 2011]] and make some room in my overcrowded house. This scanner is going to be a perfect help.

Also, because it is light, it could be easily carried to the library and copy pages from book that can't be checked out, it would be perfect for students, say you need to borrow someone's notes, you could literally scan them in a few minutes, hand the notes back, the notes are in the sd card, and bring them home to upload.

The only negative is the spines of the books have to be pretty flat and I could see damage, on the other hand, copiers I have used also require the book to be squished down.

The scanner comes with software, usb cables, batteries, a carrying case, a white cardboard to calibrate, easy to read instructions (and let me tell you, easy to read from me means something, I am so far from a tech wizard it's sad, and even I could understand this)

review_body: Back when I was in High Scool, this pen is considered as Asia's favorite pen and received the platinum award from Reader's Digest. I can't believe this is not available in retail stores here in the US. I showed my friends and let them use this pen and they were simply astonished! EVERY single one of them liked it. This pen could be a best seller if it were available in places like Walmart.  However, the tip is VERY prone to being pushed in, so be LIGHT when writing and don't push it. Also, don't drop it. EVER. The pen is useless if it drops point down becuse it will ruin the tip. Otherwise, in some cases, the ink inside will no longer be pure (i.e. form microscopic bubbles) and you might experience occasional 'strutters' in your writing.  This pen makes your handwriting look great, especially if you have a good one already.  One thing I don't like though, this pen sells for $2.50 a piece. product_title: Plustek OpticFilm 7600I SE Film Scanner
review_body: In a word, this scanner is absolutely phenomenal!  I am using it with Vuescan software (available separately from Hamrick) and I could not be more pleased.  I was trying to use a 12 year old scanner with no driver support for Windows 7 - losing deal.  Buy the SE version of the Plustek scanner (NOT the Ai version, as the hardware is EXACTLY the same - only the supplied software is different) and save yourself $150.00.  You can then buy Vuescan Pro for $80.00 (permanent license and frequent updates) and you are good to go.  7200 dpi scanning works great, but 3600 dpi yields more manageable files sizes.  The infrared scratch and dust removal system works very well (I had no idea how bad of shape my old slides were in), much better than Digital ICE or similar systems.  Not sure why lowball reviewers had an issue - if you use a scanner that is supported, it works great!

product_title: 5mw 532nm Astronomy Powerful Green Laser Pointer - Black

The green light seems more appealing to the cats and the larger size makes it much easier to hold and swish around without fatigue. I just ordered another one for a friend.  And for those of you who are considering using it for its intended purpose, I took it outside in broad daylight and the bright green dot was clearly visible on the side of the neighbor's house some two blocks away.

As a comparison, I would rate FedEx's \\"engineered\\" tape a 9.

review_headline: Love standing and my neck and back feel great!

I decided to try alternative therapies, including acupuncture, gentle chiropractic with the \\"activator\\" method, and massage. I bought one of these as my neurologist recommending standing at work (I am on the computer all day long.) I have now been standing for six weeks and I love it! Today as I was leaving my office I looked over at my Ergotron and said to myself, \\"I love you.\\" I have more energy, my lower back and neck feel great, and I have found I move around and interact with staff more due to the freedom of not having to get up and down from a chair. I also bought the optional desk surface accessory that goes with it and that makes it even better! Occasionally I take a break from standing and sit on an exercise ball with the Ergotron lowered to desk height. I also use a thick rubber mat to stand on. I highly recommend this unit, it was easy to assemble, it's very well made and it is very, very easy to raise and lower. I'll try to post a photo later. I have a 21.5\\" monitor with this unit.

product_title: 5mw 532nm Astronomy Powerful Green Laser Pointer - Black
review_body: I was looking for a laser pointer that was bright enough to see the beam of light, and this laser pointer was actually much brighter than I expected! I'm able to see the laser beam even in moderate ambient light. On a cloudy night I can point the laser beam into the clouds and I can actually see the endpoint of the laser beam on the clouds! Additionally on a starry night I can shine the laser beam towards the sky and the beam looks like it goes on forever! It reminds me of a lightsaber from Star Wars. If you really want to see the beam, toss some baby powder and make a little power cloud of it and waft the dust around and the beam will be super bright! This is a really fun product, additionally it is really sturdy and easy to carry with you. The only issue that you may have with this product is only if you use it a lot is that the batteries--they last many hours, but if you use this product as much as I do you'll fine that you will be replacing the batteries about every three or four days. Don't be alarmed if the laser beam suddenly loses it's vividness, that just means it is running low on power, so swap out the batteries at that point and it'll return to a very bright beam. Awesome laser pointer.

product_title: Epson WorkForce GT-1500 Document Image Sheet-Fed Scanner with Automatic Document Feeder (ADF) (B11B190011)
review_body: 2-1-12  I had my purchasing guy buy one of these for me in may 2011.  I use it here at work every day.  I am very happy with this scanner.  I have 11 bankers boxes of papers to scan to PDF; so far I am almost done with 6 boxes (~35000 sheets).  our building is very dusty and the papers are stapled in to small packets 3 to 50 sheets in size.  Some pages are bent, tattered, burned (by our welders), have dirty footprints on them, and in general are just filthy.  I pull the staples, separate the sheets, and feed them to this scanner a little each day.  I have run into the streaking issue some other reviews mention.  There are two scan windows, the flat bed, and a small strip of glass for the auto-feed part.  My strip of glass got a pc of dirt stuck to it which was the cause of the streaking.  After chipping it off with my finger nail and cleaning the glass strip with window cleaner, the scans were perfectly clear again.  Every once in a while I have to clean the rubber rollers or the pages won't feed correctly, but to be honest, I can't believe I can feed such dirty paper through without requiring more maintenance.  I tried the included PDF software, and although it's convenient, it didn't provide files that were small enough for me.  I chose to use Adobe to scan, refine, crop, and reduce the size of the files.  With several thousand files, I didn't want to settle for less than optimal file size.  I would say the PDF's from the included software are around 30% larger than what I can produce with Adobe.  I have since bought another of these for one of my co-workers.  I would definitely recommend this scanner.....especially for the price.  I find that I can fit no more than 40 sheets in the auto feeder if they are clean, flat, and in good shape.  I usually don't try to do more than 25-30 sheets at a time.

product_title: Cool Toner TN660 High Yield Page Mono Laser Toner Cartridge for Brother TN-660 Black - 1 Pack
review_body: I was a little worried about using a non-oem product for my wireless Brother laser printer.  I rely heavily on my printer not only for printing online coupons (which I do daily), but for printing my college assignments and book chapters as well.  I already knew how to install the cartridge because I had already replace the toner before (with OEM) and it's fairly easy.  Other reviews have stated problems with an error message, but I have to say that even with an OEM cartridge, I had problems with a \\"Replace toner cartridge\\" error message.   This packaged arrived promptly and was well packed.  Again installation was easy. product_title: Optoma PlayTime LED Gaming Projector
review_body: The pros:       First and foremost it is CHEAP.       Second it is versatile with a couple of in line couplers , phono cables and an hdmi to vga/ rca out you can connect anything across almost any room without loosing too much resolution.       Third it's led based so it has a lamp life of 20,000 hours. lets do some math 20,000 hours/ 4 hours a day/ 365 days a year= 13.698 beautiful cheap years of service.       Fourth it's manual focus is quick and easy.       Fifth is portability, to have an impromptu outside movie night all i need is my laptop this projector, an hdmi to vga cable and an extension cord.  the cons:       Not sure, maby the resolution, but i never have wanted to dish out for high res anyway.    The Story:    I purchased this product for my girlfriend's 18th birthday. i did a fair amount of research on the type of products that where within my price range. i was at first dismayed, seeing only \\"pocket projectors\\" or brand less presumably Chinese models. I have bought and been perfectly happy with Chinese products before, but this purchase was a little too expensive to take the risk. I ordered it and it came a day early, which didn't help in keeping the projector a surprise but worked out anyways. when the big day finally came she awoke to breakfast in bead and a bright pink hello kitty wrapped box. as soon as the cinnamon toast crunch was gone and the milk consumed her fingers quickly devoured my 45 minuets of hard box wrapping work.When she was finally down to the box covered with the products picture she had a look on her face indicating duality, one part excitement, the other concern for a box with the words \\"PLAY TIME\\" written in big bright letters across the top but we quickly hooked it up to the wii and watched an episode of scrubs with dozens of cords extending in every direction. We decided that before judging the projector we needed to hook it up correctly. it was off to Radio Shack. I purchased a 24 foot phono cable for $9.99 and an rca 3 phono in line coupler for $6.93. we returned home to begin the prosses of setting upour home theater system, comprised of the new projector, a wii equipped with netflix, and modified to play dvd's, and a surround sound system that i purchased at a yard sale two years earlier. I place a shelf a foot and a half from the ceiling on the wall opposite of our large white wall devoid of any shelves or pictures. next i placed the five speakers in the corners of the room. then i ran the speaker wire, phono cable, and an extension cord to their respective end destination all originating from the closet in which sat my desk. on the shelf above my desk i sat my surround sound receiver an wii and began the task of wiring. with all the speakers connected to the receiver i connected the red and white cables from the wii to the surround sound and attached the yellow video cable from the wii to the in line coupler i purchased and the end of the 24' phono caple to the other side of the coupler. i then ran the wire for the sensor bar through the ceiling hanging the sensor bar from the ceiling and having the other end emerge in the closet where i connected it to the wii. i plugged the phono cable into the video in on the projector, and the power cord into it's port and fired it all up. at a range of about 10' we had a clear picture that was 54\\" diagonally. the projector may only have a native resolution of 480 but for the price that's plenty for me. as far as the projector having only 50 ansi lumens, i was worried about the brightness, but with a pair of good curtains it's plenty.    the summery: If you want a cheap reliable projector buddy buy this product.

product_title: HP CM721A#B1H 2140 Professional Quality Plain-Paper Fax and Copier
review_headline: This will do for now...lower quality for HP.
review_body: My husband bought this HP FAX and I'm surprised he picked up one of their lower priced models? We usually buy the top of the line in this type of item since we do so much office type work.  But it's not terrible...it serves our purpose for now. If someone needs a FAX and doesn't have alot of money I think you would be satisfied with it. FAX seems to work rather well \\"most\\" the time.  Some times when I will try to FAX 8 pages or so it will jam or skip a page or two and that drives me nuts. Some times I sit in there and almost hand feed it just so I can get it done! I send alot of medical records and it will FAX a few pages and miss a couple pages and go on to the ones behind it. Ugh! So the doctors office would get only part of the records which isn't good. So many times I have to start all over again. It's frustrating. (My last HP FAX was awesome and it never ever had any problems...so I was spoiled.) Plus just for the fact my older more expensive FAX from HP had made copies so crisp and clear you could NOT tell which was the orignal from the copy...it was amazing!  Even on legal documents...you would have to look at it so carefully to make sure what copy you had in your hand.  Now from this HP 2140 you can EASILY tell which is the copy from the orignal. Cheap looking. It always looks rough around the edges. (Meaning the ink.)    Now as to making copies I am very disappointed.  :(  That is one feature I use often on any FAX machine and this one makes awful copies IMHO compared to my older HP FAX. Again...if you don't want to spend alot of money this will serve your purpose for most ppl. The copies are OK...just not crisp and clear like what I'm use too...but for the price we paid it's GREAT. :) The ink cartridge cost a small fortune...but don't they all...that's to be expected. I do get annoyed with how often this one jams for no reason. Then it says remove paper...yea right...easier said then done. It comes out but I don't want to ruin the machine.  And when it jams there is absolutely no reason for it!  It jams with just ONE page going through more often then I'd like to mention.  And maybe my husband didn't set this one up right but I've noticed when I FAX things it never tells me all pages were recieved like my old HP FAX machine did?  I'll have to find the manual in all fairness...that might be our fault?     It seemed like this HP FAX worked ok at first but the longer we've had it (8 months) we have more and more problems with it.  I am tired of all the errors it gives.  It no longer serves my purpose at all. The \\"Mode\\" button will not bring up the correct options to change contrast or to set to copy. I try to copy and it wants to dial \\"1\\" out when it's NOT even set to FAX. It is cheap so for some ppl I think you will be happy...for me personally I am going back to one of HP more top line quality FAX machines that have CRISP CLEAR copies and sends FAXES without jamming all the time!  We fight with this FAX machine more then we do anything with it.  It's really not worth it for us.  Hope others are having better luck with this then we have.  My advice would be to step up and buy a more expensive FAX from HP.  (I do believe in that saying \\"You get what you pay for\\".

review_body: Initially, I was looking to replace a digital scale from My Weigh that accommodated up to 15lbs and was a bit pricey at $40 without an AC Adapter.  In looking at the various scales that were Prime eligible, I ran across the 35 lb version of the Weighmax, but on delivery the LCD was faulty and I had to return it.  Then I found this 15lb version and it included an AC adapter and a 9 volt battery.  It only has one read out in lbs & ounces and no tare button.  The taring function is gotten around by putting whatever object you are going to place the item in and then turning on the scale.  That amounts to a tare option.  It works well enough for my purposes and now the question is the unit's durability that can only be determined over time.  The lifetime warranty is better than nothing, but really somewhat worthless because you have to send the scale back at your expense and if it is past one year you then have to pay to get it fixed.  At that point, you might as well as buy a new one because these basically throwaway electronics just aren't worth repairing. review_body:

review_headline: After 50 years, Lawyer Still Likes X-Acto products
review_body: I am an estate planning attorney. When I noticed some clients had not done so, I asked them why.  Their excuse? \\"I didn't have a 3 hole punch handy.\\"  So I bought some 3 hole punches from Office Depot and started putting them in the Organizer. Unfortunately, the ones I bought at the office supply stores broke right away, always in the same place, for the same reason--the holder was made of plastic and would break whenever the notebook was closed--in many cases the very first time it was used. I found a place in Ohio that made rubberized punches, but they went out of business. Finally, I stumbled across X-Acto, the same company that I remembered from my second grade art class when they had those real sharp X-Acto blades.  That was 50 years ago, mind you.  When I read that the X-Acto Model 1520 3 ring punches had metal tabs, I knew that someone at X-Acto had actually listened to their customers and had figured out that Americans will still pay for quality. So I ordered 200 of them. I am now running out and will order another 200.  Way to Go, X-Acto!!! Paul N. Heckt, Attorney, Minneapolis, MN.

product_title: Safco Products Value Sorter Literature Organizer, 72 Compartment
review_headline: If I could put 0 Stars, I would!
review_body: We bought 2 of these sorters for our sales office to organize all of our literature from the different supply companies we use. It wasn't the cheapest option we found but we decided to go with this product due to all of the space it offered and the design. We would be able to secure it against the wall and it would be a convenient way for our salesmen to find what they need quickly. Upon ordering, it stated we'd have to wait several weeks for it to be shipped. Although we were hoping to have it right away, we decided it would be okay to wait. It took about 3 weeks for the first sorter to arrive and another week for the 2nd to arrive although they were ordered together. The tracking for these packages were both off. I got an email prior to delivery of both packages to inform me that they tried to make the delivery but because no one was in the office, they would have to try again although when I checked, they were in different states and had inaccurate information about expected delivery dates. Upon getting the first sorter, we opened everything up to begin and ALL of the hardware was missing. I looked through the entire box and inside all of the metal shelves because many of the pieces were stored within them, I suppose for safe keeping. I called Safco immediately and although she was very nice, the woman I spoke to urged me to look again and call her back if the pieces were indeed missing. I called again once I double checked and spoke to someone else. She ordered me the screws and fasteners at no charge to our company.We received the 2nd sorter the following week and decided to inspect to make sure the hardware was included in this packaging. Once we found the pieces, we decided to put the sorter together so we could have atleast one up and operable. That's when we discovered that the plastic trim strips that go on the front of the sorter to hide the cardboard weren't all there. Extremely frustrated after spending over $500 on these products, I again called Safco.I expressed my frustration to the customer service representative and after asking to have the additional pieces that were missing shipped overnight to our office, he informed me that the reason those pieces were missing was because they were on BACK ORDER! I couldn't understand why the would ship a product without all the pieces knowing that they didn't have everything they need. We would have been more than understanding if they would've contacted us to let us know about the back order and that there would be a delay but the only contact we had with them was when I called them. He told me that they don't have any control over what goes into the box because they get boxed up in Thailand. I asked to speak to a manager after going back and forth about what could be done. At first he refused and after pushing and pushing, he put me on hold and came back on the line a moment later to let me know that the supervisor was away from her desk. Finally we came to the conclusion that they would ship us overnight a whole new sorter so that we could get the parts we needed and toss out everything additional. After wasting enough of my time, I finally decided that if they would send out the new sorter and have it to us by the next day, I would just let it go. I couldn't talk to him any longer. Although the package came the next day as promised, it was the wrong sorter. We decided to cut our losses and not contact these morons again. I hope you will think twice before purchasing this product!

review_body: So, so.  Installation was not a easy as it could have been.  Software is not particularly user friendly.  Still trying to get it to work reliably from a Mac.

product_title: Cool Toner 4 Pack TN360 Compatible Brother TN-360 TN360 Black Toner Cartridges For Brother MFC-7340 MFC-7480W HL-2140 HL-2170W Printer
review_body: I was looking for a new cartridge for my Brother laser printer last August. Staples was charging $70+. An Amazon retailer was charging about $50, and this vendor's price was only $14 (with shipping, just over $20). Being leery of such a low price, I bought one cartridge from each of the two Amazon vendors. My $14 laser cartridge from this vendor is still going strong 9 months later. Print quality is identical to $70 cartriges. Further, although I signed up for standard shipping, the cartridge arrives within just a few days. I run a small business and this vendor is  getting all of mine from now on!

product_title: Canon CLI-226 4550B001 Gray Ink Tank
review_headline: Great ink, just wish it was a little less expensive
review_body: I purchased a generic refill kit for my Canon MG6120, and the only ink it didn't contain was the gray.  Amazon has a better price than I can find anywhere locally for this cartridge, and I'm going to lay in a supply of another one or two just so I don't get stuck in the middle of a project.  According to others, the gray is sometimes difficult to find elsewhere.  Free Prime shipping is another reason I order from Amazon.  As always, Amazon comes through.

product_title: Epson Artisan 725 Color Inkjet All-In-One (C11CA74201)
review_body: Met and exceeded my expectation from the shipper to use in our home. Wireless setup was a breeze both on Mac and Windows. Good job guys!

product_title: Fellowes Memory Foam Mouse Pad/Wrist Rest, Black (9176501)
review_body: This product does what it claims. It is comfortable and supports where it needs to. It has reduced, almost eliminated after 1 months of use, the strain caused to my wrist by using other products. The memory foam appears to do it's job well. I would recommend this product to anyone who has a strain in their wrist from mouse use.

product_title: Child 7" Short Stretch Gloves,14248,multi-colored,One-Size
review_body: These gloves were for my daughter's dance recital. They served their purpose for that. She did say they were a bit snug, so I would not recommend these for a child older than about 8 or 9. There wasn't a lot of stretch in them. Otherwise, they were perfect!

product_title: C-Line 13-Pocket Coupon Size Expanding File, Color
review_body: This product is made with quality material. It holds plenty of coupons and has pre-printed tabs for organizing alphabetically or by expiration date. It will hold a variety of sizes of coupons (though it just fits a smart source coupon) but you will have to fold the larger ones. It is very secure when closed and is lightweight.

product_title: RCA 25055RE1 1-Handset 2-Line Landline Telephone
review_body: Everything is good expect for the sound. I wish they would make the thing a little more louder to hear.  Other from that, the product came on time and in excellent condition. I strongly recommend buying from this seller.  In Christ's holy name,  Luong Do

product_title: Noodler's Ink Standard Nib Piston Fill Turquoise Fountain Pen
review_body: This pen is everything as described. I am very pleased with the Noodlers Pen. It writes beautifully...smooth and with no skips. I have very expensive pens...but know that Noodlers will be a favorite. Planning on purchasing another Noodlers pen to use with black ink for sketching. This is a good buy.

product_title: State of the Art Dual-Sided Aluminum Stylus Pen for Apple Ipad
review_body: First of all I got this product about 2 weeks later then when it said on the website. It comes in a plastic bag with no box. The construction looks cheap. I thought that both ends of it will work on my ipad but only the circle one does, the pen like side does not.

product_title: Texas Instruments TI-83 Plus Graphing Calculator
review_headline: Did not Refund when the Item was Returned.
review_body: The package was not opened after I received it.  The item was sent immediately back, because I found the object was no longer needed.  And for three months I was continuously told the item was not received and was not told whether or not I would get my money back.

product_title: Texas Instruments TI-83 Plus Graphing Calculator
review_headline: grandkids love it and how easy it is to use for school
review_body: This was bought for my granddaughters in high school.   One in middle school was having trouble understanding algebra and this is helping her alot.    They used it in her classroom last year and she liked it.  The high school 'lent' students these last year and my granddaughter used it all year and said it was easy to understand.

product_title: Printronic Remanufactured Ink Cartridge Replacement for HP C8765WN (Black,2-Pack)
review_body: This is the second time this year I've purchased these ink cartridges & they work great. My printer, a HP PSC 1610 all in one, did not have any problems recognizing them and worked as if they were the regular HP brand. I used to pay approx $45 for a set of blk & color (94 & 95)from wal-mart but not anymore... I wish I would of given these a try earlier:)

product_title: CableWholesales RG6 Cable Clip, Black (100 pieces per bag)
review_headline: they are nail clips... what more can they be?
review_body: used these to clip up the CAT6 gigabit network i made... they were a little big, but they do the trick, these are meant for use on CATV coax cables, but they are very similar is diameter and it got the job done.

product_title: Ace Label Full Sheet Shipping Labels for Laser and Inkjet Printer, Pressure-Sensitive Labels
review_headline: Great alternative to Avery 5126 labels (two per page), but...
review_body:
Update 6/13/14: Just ordered another batch of these labels and noticed that they're thinner than they used to be. They don't cover previous markings on packages as well. They're still a better bargain than the Avery labels, but wanted to warn folks about the change. I reduced my rating to 4 stars instead of 5.

Update 7/16/14: I purchased ACE regular address labels for the first time recently (previously only purchased the half-sheet labels for shipping packages) and wanted to share my thoughts about them. It's difficult to see where the labels separate from the backing, which makes them more difficult to peel off than the Avery or other name-brand labels. I've also had a problem with some of the labels sticking to the backing. If you can get regular address labels for a reasonable from somewhere else, give these a pass (try 3M - they're usually cheaper than Avery, but better quality than these). The half-sheet 8.5 x 5.5 ACE labels are still decent quality and a good buy... but they're thinner than they used to be. (See note above.)

Original review:

This is a great alternative to the much more expensive Avery brand labels. There are 100 sheets, with two labels per sheet (200 labels total). I use them to print my USPS Click and Ship postage labels. They run through my laser printer perfectly, with no jamming. (They're also suitable for inkjet printers.) They come in a shrink-wrapped box (not loose like some the reviews I've been reading of other off-name or no-name brands). The corners are square, while I prefer rounded, but that's a minor quibble. They're made in the USA, and are certified as a WBENC Women's Business Enterprise, if that matters to you. In the past, I printed my labels on paper, then taped them to the box or priority envelope due to the cost of the Avery labels. Never again when the cost of these labels is so reasonable. Great product!

Edited to add: If you use USPS Click-N-Ship software to create your label, check the \\"separate receipt\\" box in the \\"Options\\" area. This will cause only the label (Media Mail or whatever) to print on your sheet, while the receipt will print on the next page on regular paper that you you've loaded under your label paper. (That way you won't waste the 2nd label on the sheet.) Hope this makes sense!, check the \\"separate receipt\\" box in the \\"Options\\" area. This will cause only the label (Media Mail or whatever) to print on your sheet, while the receipt will print on the next page on regular paper that you you've loaded under your label paper.
