product_title: Swingline 74031 Light Touch Desktop 20-Sheet Hole Punch, 9/32 Diameter Holes
review_headline: Worked for a bit, failed after 6 months
review_body: This hole puncher worked for about 6 months and then failed. The outer puncher's spring popped out, leaving the punch to be ineffective (would not go back up after a punch due to the spring being out and jammed in). I suggest trying the Carl or Sparco brands of hole punchers if you are looking for increased guarantee of durability over the long run. I am sure this defect is not 100% prevalent but this problem does not seem to be uncommon so I would stay away from these.

product_title: 200 Label Outfitters Brand CD-DVD Labels, 100 Sheets
review_headline: 200 Label Outfitters® Brand Avery 5931, 8931 Format CD-DVD Labels (100 Sheets)
review_body: This product works as well as Avery for half of the cost. One must remember to keep the Avery product number so you can type it in to get it to line up correctly.

product_title: Panasonic DECT 6.0 Link-to-Cell via Bluetooth Cordless Phone with Answering System
review_body:
After much review here at Amazon I ordered the associated phone system. It has worked as promised with Bluetooth synching, range, etc. It seems to be a perfectly serviceable system EXCEPT one of the handheld units has an issue since new. One of the handhelds has no sound when talking. If I go to speakerphone then the sound is fine but when it's set to normal volume there is no audio. The person on the other end of the line can hear you just fine, just no audio to hear your caller. I've adjusted the volume levels, done the troubleshooting, etc. Nothing.

Since this is a four unit system and we had a cable issue with our telephone line so we had no service for a while, unfortunately the unit with the issue wasn't noticed until recently. Normally I'd contact Amazon but it's been about 60 days now. Contacting Panasonic appears to be a labyrinth of websites, RMAs, and BS. It just hasn't been worth the hours of time it would take to wade through all that so this unit sits idle while the other three work perfectly. Shame on me for not testing them better when they were new. Shame on you if you don't do the same when your's arrive.

product_title: Generic PGI-5BK and CLI-8 Set Variation-
review_body: I got a remanufactured canon 210 cart.  Inside the box, there was a note telling the user to run the paper feed if the trouble light comes on.  There's your first clue.  The trouble lights wouldn't stop, I couldn't print anything or  even feed paper through the printer.  Totally non-functional product.

product_title: Canon CLI-221 Ink Tank
review_body: Best price every time for original CANON

product_title: HP Officejet Pro 8500 Premier Wireless All-in-One Printer
review_body: After being overjoyed with an HP6500 we eagerly awaited our 8500. Mistake. Slow to warm up. Slow to print. Slow to scan. Holds lots of paper but is constantly re checking itself. Slow. Now the wireless is out. I really could not be more disappointed.

product_title: Microvision ShowWX Extra Battery
review_body: I use my SHOWWX+ once and a while, but when I do it's for hours at a time i.e. parties, cookouts, etc. I have owned this battery for over a year now. I was impressed to find out that the battery still worked after I neglected to charge them for over six or 7 months.

product_title: Sharpie Permanent Markers, Fine Point, Pink, "City of Hope" Edition
review_body: I been relying on Sharpie products for ages as I go to ball games and similar events for celebrities to sign my items.  I have silver and black ones already and figured this would be a unique item and a conversation starter for any female signers out there.  However, these are not as \\"juicy\\" as the pink and black version.  It is a little too light for my liking and very pastel-color looking.  These are only suitable for white paper autograph opportunities.  If they sign something dark, you will barely be able to see it.

product_title: Brother P-Touch Tc Tape Cartridges For P-Touch Labelers, 1/2W, 2/Pack
review_body: GREAT ITEM AT A GREAT PRICE

product_title: rooCASE Apple iPad 4 / 3 / 2 Leather Folio Case Cover
review_body: I ordered the  Roocase for iPad2 in black leather. It is a very attractive case carrying case and it is a perfect fit for the iPad2. You can adjust the case to stand at different heights to allow for typing or reading.

product_title: Navigator Premium Copy/Laser/Inkjet Paper, 99 Brightness, 24 lb, Letter Size (8.5 x 11), White, 5000 Sheets per Carton (NMP1124)
review_headline: Great item, but depends who you order from...
review_body: This is the second time I order 24 lb Navigator Paper except the last time I ordered straight from Amazon (when they offered it) and the paper arrived in perfect condition. The paper itself is excellent in quality, in my opinion. It's very white and has the expected thick feel to it. This order, however, arrived in atrocious conditions. The packaging was absolutely shredded and most of the paper is stained blue and folded. Not what I expect. The only thing that went well was the speedy shipping. I'm not saying all sellers of this paper are guilty here. I'm sure there are some 3rd party sellers that package the paper well (or better yet send it directly in the blue box it comes with from the manufacturer). Too bad Amazon doesn't sell this paper anymore. They packaged it very well. In my case, the seller I bought from was Shoplet, so if you want well packaged paper, do NOT order it from them.    If Shoplet contacts me in regards to this review and offers a refund or a reshipment or whatever they have in mind that sounds fair, I will inform you all to let you know of their courtesy, but in the meantime the item did not arrive in good condition at all.    Summary  24 lb Navigator Paper is fantastic paper. Great product.  Watch who you order it from. If you happen to stumble into it when Amazon offers it directly, TAKE IT. They always package extremely well.    The paper gets 5 stars.  The 3rd party seller (Shoplet) I ordered from gets 2 stars. The 2 stars were earned because of the fast shipping. But poorly packaged.  Averages to 3 and a 1/2 stars so I'll round to 4. But the PRODUCT itself is a solid 5 STARS. Keep that in mind.

product_title: Top Flight Legal Pad, 5 x 8 Inches, .375 Inch Rule, Canary, 50 Sheets per Pad (4620614)
review_body:
I originally purchased these legal pads for two reasons. One: To pay a few cents extra on my order so that I could have super saver shipping, and two so that I could have something to write on in my briefcase that was easy to access.

This product did just that. It is very affordable and durable and fits right into a briefcase or portfolio. The upper lining works well to hold the papers in place and they can be ripped out easily.

The only notable things that I would want to point out to the potential shopper, is that they are quite small. Make sure to get out a ruler and look how small a 5 x 8 really is. If you are looking for a full sized legal pad, don't buy this product.

product_title: Canon PIXMA MP495 Wireless Inkjet Photo All-In-One (4499B026)
review_body:
Long ago I had a Canon printer. The little printer could and could. It used little ink. It lasted 11 years.

Why, oh why, did I decide to replace it with an HP all-in-one printer? That's another story.

Point is, I'm back and happier than ever with this Canon. Installation was simple. Paper feed works well and doesn't drop paper all over my floor with big jobs. Two simple ink cartridges that seem to last (I've been printing a lot). Quality is good (caveat: I mostly print black and white and don't do color photos). Copying is easy.

All around a super printer for a low price.

product_title: 1/2" x 125ft x 24" ROLL (Large Bubbles)
review_body: Having moved a lot, I was always frustrated with the price of bubble wrap.  The cheapest we could find was at U-Haul, which costs $20 for a roll 100 ft long and 12 inches wide.  This is 4 1/2 times as much bubble wrap for less money!!!

product_title: Rolodex Mesh Workspace Laptop Stand, Black/Silver (82410)
review_body: I have two of these for two macbook book pros and you simply can't beat the price.  It has adjustable heights, feels sturdy once its locked into place, and does exactly what its meant to do.  There are obviously nicer options out there, but they also come at a higher premium, so if you're wanting to save a little money this will perform its job perfectly.

product_title: Monteverde Artista Candy Strip Ballpoint Pen (MV26833)
review_body: This is a very unique looking pen but the barrel is big and thick like a child's crayon. I came very close to returning.

product_title: STEELMASTER Steel Card File Box, Fits 3 x 5 Index Cards, 800 Card Capacity
review_body: This would have been a nice card file box if the lid would have closed properly.  I don't think it was damaged from shipping because the outer and inner boxes were not damaged at all.  I had to return the product!

product_title: HP Deskjet F4480 CB745A Color Inkjet Printer
review_body: Bought this machine a year ago ... Worked fine till a recent HP software update.  Now it doesn't recognize the non HP ink cartridges.  Do not buy.

product_title: Acco Brands 51-659312 Rewriteables Dry Erase Markers, 6-Pk.
review_body: The magnets and the erasers are very convenient. The mark is erased easily. But the ink run out quickly, or else I will give it a 5 stars.

product_title: Fellowes 32177 Powershred PS-77Cs Shredder
review_body: Credit cards and thicker sheets of paper are also no problem for this shredder. We have been able to go for about 30 minutes before the shredder overheated and shut down. It usually takes about 15 minutes before you are able to use it again, but after the first overload protection shut-off, the use time is significantly reduced. After the first time, I would say you are good for only 10 minutes or so before it shuts down again. My advice would be to give it at least an hour to completely cool down or you'll become annoyed very quickly.

product_title: Humanscale Keyboard Systems: 2G Standard Mechanism - Standard 21.625" Track
review_body: This was fairly easy to install.  It arrived quickly.  It puts the keyboard and mouse in a comfortable position.  I purchased one for a co-worker and it worked so well, I purchased another for another co-worker.

product_title: Hitech-Replacement HHR-P107 Battery for Panasonic Cordless Phone KX-TG6021M / KX-TG6022B
review_body: In the past, I've been burned by 3rd party batteries. However, the price disparity between this Hitech replacement battery and a 'recommended' replacement battery was so large ($20+), that I just had to give the Hitech a try. I bought two batteries-- one for each of my handsets one month ago. They charged right up. I had a handset off the charge station for about a week and have had long conversations, so they hold a charge well. Great deal!  Update:  The batteries are still fully functional after over 6 months of constant usage. Fantastic deal!

product_title: HP DESK JET F2210 PRINTER, SCANNER, AND COPIER ALL IN ONE
review_body: Should have come with a power cord but did not.  Seller insisted it was sent and that I had somehow lost it.  Anyone who has seen the size of the power cord for this printer/scanner/copier knows that it would be impossible to throw out without noticing.  When I purchased a power cord from another seller (at my expense) on Amazon.com, and hooked it up, the machine worked fine, and does everything I expected.  Print quality is fine.

product_title: Zebra's Eco Jimnie Clip Mechanical Pencil, 0.5mm, Black, 12-Pack (52510)
review_headline: I LOVE LOVE LOVE these pencils!
review_body: Such a steal for the price and love that they are eco-friendly. But they do not feel cheap at all and actually seem as if they are going to last a long time. The lead in the individual pencil itself doesn't last too long so I'd recommend buying lead as well. BUT I definitely recommend these pencils to all students alike. I'm a college student so this is right up my alley for the excessive amount of writing I do.

product_title: Educational Insights Fluorescent Light Filters (Tranquil Blue), Set of 4
review_headline: Great for diffusing intense office florescent lights
review_body:
We recently moved to a new office building where there are WAY too many bright florescent lights, directly above our workspaces. After attempting to work for 3 days, I started looking for a product to diffuse the light so that it is not so blinding, as I had a headache all day every day.

After finding these, and installing them in less than 30 seconds, my workspace is a nice diffused shade of blue. \\"Tranquil\\" definitely is a good way of describing them! My co-workers all loved it as well and plan on buying some for above their desks.

Before purchasing, I would make sure that your light fixtures are metal so the magnets to install these with will work. Not sure if all of them are metal, but I was worried that ours were not once I realized how these install (luckily they were).

product_title: Aurora AS890C 8-Sheet Cross-Cut Paper/Credit Card Shredder with Basket
review_body: This is a good home shredder and the second one of this model that I've owned. I accidentally broke my first one when I knocked it over on a hard tile floor and the shredder mechanism came apart. Because of that, I would not say it's the most durable unit, but that is more because of the small waste bin (and user error, a major factor) than anything else. So just make sure you put it in a secure place since it's small enough that one might trip over it if not paying attention. The shredder part itself is very durable and shredded away for a good year. Don't try to overload it, though, or it will jam. My husband did that once with a folded piece of junk mail and we had to fish out all the bits that caused it to stop working. I would say that it does 6 pages at a time happily.

product_title: Brother PT-80 P-touch Electronic Labeling System
review_body: Bought one from CSV Drugs for $24.00 which was cheaper than Amazon. Tapes at CSV were 9.99 which is too high. Works great. I'd use with small print so you use less tape. Should be a way to shorten margins on tape. Seems durable and well designed.

product_title: HP Officejet 6500 All-in-One Printer
review_body:
I orginally really liked this HP all-in-one printer but quickly found the printer cartidges don't last long. Color cartidges are used up even when only printing using the black ink so you'll have to spend more on ink than you want. You should also do a check and see exactly how much the ink will cost because it's running about half the cost of the printer. HP is making more money on the ink than they are on the printer I think.

Now for the next problem. I've had this printer for about 2 years now and while I like the features I've had more than my share of printing problems with it. As I'm writing this I've had to take the printer apart to see why it won't print using the black ink in from an HP cartridge that is brand new! Just do a Google search against this printer and you'll see how many other people are having problems getting black ink to print. Some of them had the problem from day one so I feel lucky I didn't experience this till now.

I would not buy another one of these printers and since this was also my first HP printer, I'm now not so inclined to purchase another HP printer. If you're not going to listen to all the dissatisfied reviews, at least buy this doorstop on a really big sale to save money for cartidges and shipping the printer back to HP under warranty.

product_title: HP Envy 100 e-All-in-One D410a Printer (CN517A#B1H)
review_body: UPDATE: The printer works pretty well, although I've not yet tried printing from my other devices. But be warned: it drinks up ink! I've used the XL cartridges, and they don't last very long at all. I finally figured out that I had to set it for \\"fast draft\\", which is indeed very fast, and which I hope will slow down ink consumption. I'm thinking very fondly of my old HP which I gave to a friend's son who is off to college this fall . . .    UPDATE #2: This is a very temperamental machine. It tells me I've got a paper jam long after I've cleared it. I've had to shut it down twice because it kept flashing and belling. It's kind of an annoying machine. Maybe after a few months I'll have it better figured out, but I wanted it to be easy and intuitive, and it definitely is not. I can hardly wait to try scanning (NOT!)    Original Review: I checked the price several times, and it changed based on the perceived level of my interest. FIrst it was $179. I returned to Amazon, and the price was $159. Great! I checked around and came back a day or so later and it was $179 again. Several hours later, when I checked, it was $199. So beware of \\"click for product details\\" when a price isn't shown. If they think you MIGHT be a buyer, the price goes down. If they think you're REAllY interested, it goes up. Not nice, and it makes me think twice about buying on Amazon.    PS: I got a lot of grief from other reviewers for giving a poor initial review based on the price bait and switch and not the product. While it didn't reflect the product, it did reflect the buying experience both with Amazon and HP, and I believe it's valid. If someone wants to tell me how to convey these very real issues in another way, please let me know.

product_title: Slappa SL-SB-102 Ballistix Aura Shoulder Bag (Black/Black)
review_headline: Slappa SL-SB-102 Ballistix Aura Sholder Bag Black
review_body: On the delivery side:  Reseller is top notch!  Received the brand new item as it should be in its proper packaging and delivered very promptly.  On the product side:  The main attributes are already listed above.  I've had the pleasure of carrying 2 laptops in this bag, one is a Gaming PC Malibal 17-inch laptop and the other one is a 17-inch Macbook Pro.  Both fit nicely in the bag, though it can be quite heavy.  Nonetheless, it's exactly the type of ballistic nylon material that I was looking for.  Still enough space for all other portable electronic junks you can think of, though your shoulder will give up first before the bag does.  I wouldn't advise to carry this bag with the contents above on a bike though, since there's enough force to strain the ballistic nylon strap to its limit.  I'm not saying that it will break, but you'll feel that it may break.  On a side note, airlines will give you the hassle of a lifetime if you carry two laptops in this thing, even international flights, but that's the airline's issue, not the bag.  I've used this bag several times now and so far it's living all the hype that it's known for.  A little on the pricey side, but as an Apple enthusiast would say, you're getting the full bang for the buck.  Lastly, this bag is also excellent for short term vacations.  It will have enough space to put in 3-4 days worth of stuff and it will fit in the overhead compartment in an airplane.  So far so good, so I'm giving all the thumbs up that I have...plus I'll need to borrow some thumbs from my friends.

product_title: Officemate Silver Binder Clips, Assorted Sizes, 30/Tub (31021)
review_body: I'd never heard of the Officemate brand, so was a bit apprehensive about getting these binder clips, but I was in a bind (no pun intended). Now that I've had a chance to use them, I must say I'm impressed. The clips are sturdy and stiff. I appreciate the stiffness of the clips because it means my documents stay more secure. The largest size clip, which I believe is Medium, is currently holding about 40 sheets of printer quality paper together; I can flip to any one of the sheets without worry of the clip sliding off. The downside to the stiffer clips, however, is that the top/bottom papers will have a pronounced indentation on them, and the clips can be difficult to squeeze open.

product_title: BAZIC Alphabet Wood Beads, Wood
review_headline: Good price for children's bead crafts
review_body: I have mixed emotions about these beads.  I had a few that were chipped on the corners, but they were painted and put in the bag anyway. A few of them had double stamped letters on them, and one was completely unusable because the letters weren't printed on all sides of it. Since this one was a V, I went and painted a red heart on each side and used it that way. The price is great, and the ones that were perfect are very nice looking. They served the purpose that they were bought for, and like I said the price was right, so I really don't have anything bad to say about them.

product_title: Epson Stylus NX625 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer, Copier, Scanner (C11CA70271)
review_body: It took a while for the fire wall to recognize the printer but now all seems to be working fine. Speed is not great but speed is not necessary for me.

product_title: Generic Dell 1100 Black Variation-
review_body: I've always considered this item to be overpriced, and it's refreshing to find a company that is reasonably priced with an excellent product!

product_title: HP 11 C4836A, C4837A, C4838A Compatible Remanufactured Combo Pack - 1 Cyan, 1 Magenta, 1 Yellow Ink Cartridges
review_headline: Great Replacement At A Great Price!
review_body: Bought an older wide format printer because I couldn't afford a new one, which means there was no way I could afford HP inks. This works just like the original and prints great. The printer recognizes it without any problems. I would give it five stars but the plastic seal over the ink outlet was a bit difficult to deal with. I think you are supposed to just let the printer puncture it, [there are no directions], but it took a lot of effort to do that, and I was afraid I might break something. Worked out fine though.

product_title: Remanufactured Ink Cartridge Replacement for HP 60 CC640WN CC643WN (2 Black 2 Color) 4 Pack
review_body: So far everything seems to be working okay and the price is great. At first there was a bit of a problem with my printer accepting it and I do get the wrong error messages about the ink being low, but you can just ignore them and print away. I am anxious to see how long this will last me , but so far so good.

product_title: HP 124A (Q6002A)  Original LaserJet Toner Cartridge
review_body:
For my second set of toner cartridges, I purchased 3rd party refills from a large auction site at half the cost of HP OEM toner cartridges. Boy was that a mistake. The yellow and cyan cartridges immediately started printing white streaks. I did search on the internet looking for streaking issues and people reported when they when back to HP OEM cartridges the print quality returned. I had purchased these back in 9/2010, but decided to use up the bad toner rather than junk them. I just installed the whole set of HP OEM cartridges today, including black.

To my relief, the original print quality returned! Lesson learned..

product_title: X-ACTO Work Pro Electric Pencil Sharpener, Black (19208)
review_body:
Please see the edit at the end of this review.

My family owns a retail art supply store ([...]), and we sell this sharpener in our store. My younger sister ([...]) went nuts when I got this for review. Apparently it's one of the only sharpeners good for Prismacolor pencils. Here's what she said about it:

\\"If you have Prismacolor pencils you can't sharpen them with a normal pencil sharpener, because they crack into pieces all the way down. You have to sharpen them with an electric one. People complain that their electric sharpeners wear out... very quickly. The X-Acto is an especially durable brand, and you can purchase replaceable blades. It's great for colored pencil artists.\\"

Of course, it's also great for the average pencil. Again, the blades are replaceable, so it'll last for a very long time. I found that it sharpens very fast and very cleanly.

8/10 EDIT:
We've been using this sharpener at our store for a while, using it for artists who come in to sharpen pencils, and also to sharpen regular pencils. product_title: Paper Mate Clickster 0.5mm Mechanical Pencils, 6 Assorted Pencils (65165PP)
review_headline: Ten years later, and I still use these mechanical pencils.
review_body: Of all the mechanical pencils I have used over the years, this is the only one that remains actively used by me. I've used Zebra and various other mechanical pencils, but none of them seem to match my experience with these Paper Mate Clicksters. It's a great mechanical pencil to use.    The Clickster was the first mechanical pencil that I used that instead of feeding lead using a button on the end, instead used one on the side. However, to the surprise of many, this button does not get in the way when writing. I really don't even notice it until I'm going to advance some lead which is done without a break in writing such as to push a button on the end. The amount advanced is a decent amount; not too much, but not too little. Unfortunately, some of my older ones that have seen constant writing over the years have been worn down somewhat. On the occasion they advance too much lead, but they're nearing five-six years of age.    The actual design of the pencil is also very nice. The length is just right and the circumference of the pencil makes it a nice fit in my hands. Most other mechanical pencils I have used just seem to be too large on the circumference for a comfortable fit. Especially the ones that try to add in a rubber grip which I find annoying in all cases like the new Clickster models. This design is simplistic and works perfectly. You also get a feeling that the whole pencil is very sturdy and mine have taken quite the beating over the years from middle school, high school, and now college. The only part that seems to fail in this area is the clip. Do not lend these to people and expect that piece to still be there. It breaks very easily from a little abuse.    Another area that seems to see some complaints is the button itself being on the side, and how it's attached to the body of the pencil. This pencil does take some getting used to from what I can tell. I've lent enough of them to see people stumble about trying to advance the lead before realizing it's done on the side. However, once you get used to that, it's very smooth sailing there on out. The other complaint about the button easily coming out is also exaggerated. Of all of my Clicksters (which is upwards 60), none of them have lost the button that advances the lead. Now, I do play with the button by pulling it out, but it takes both effort and nails to do so. If the button has come out, it's because you pulled at it with enough force to remove a button on any mechanical pencil.     A giant benefit of the button being on the side is that when erasing, you don't continuously advance lead. The eraser is stationary as you erase. On the eraser itself, it's a standard one from as far as I can tell. It's decent at its job, but it will be inadequate for erasing an entire page. Replacing them is pretty simple as with most mechanical pencils (unless it's a Zebra), and I found that buying Clic Erasers are pretty adequate for replacements. They fit snugly into the eraser hole and you just snip it off where you feel the length is right. Standard orthodox replacements also work just as well.    This particular model uses .5 mm lead which was another thing I liked with this mechanical pencil. It's easy to make distinguishable lines and the smearing is almost nonexistent. However, advancing too much lead and writing extremely hard will make the lead break, but then again, it would be the same with any lead. I break just as much .7 mm lead as I do .5 mm lead. Replacing the lead is as simple as removing the eraser and dropping in a few pieces (like any mechanical pencil).    All in all, I've been greatly impressed by this mechanical pencil and will continue to use them for as long as possible. This is what made me so sad that Paper Mate discontinued this model (or at least they don't list it anymore), and that all of my local stores stopped carrying them a few years back. I'm glad I stumbled upon them here and at $2 for six, it was like a steal with free shipping. I would definitely recommend giving this mechanical pencil a shot if you're willing to try something new.

product_title: Canon Photo Paper Pro Platinum, 8.5 x 11 Inches, 20 Sheets (2768B022)
review_headline: Platinum Pro vs. Photo Pro II
review_body:
I am not a professional, but I have been into photography for about 25 years. I now print through Lightroom 3 or PS5 using a calibrated IPS monitor with a Canon 9000 MkII and use only Canon ink. What I don't print myself I print through Bay Photo, who usually do a fantastic job, so I tend to compare my prints to those from Bay Photo.

I was not happy with Canon's Glossy II or the Photo Pro II because I felt colors were a bit washed out and the blacks were unimpressive, so I tried the Platinum Pro. To compare the Platinum Pro to the Photo Pro II, I printed a series of 10 photos at 4x6 that ranged in color content from starry night skies, sunrises, reef fish, amusement park rides, wedding shots, macro bug shots, landscapes, and B&W covering many of the color matching problems I've ran into. YMMV, but here's my observations:

First off these two papers are very different. Physically, The Platinum Pro paper achieves final color after only a few hours while the Photo Paper Pro II takes about 48 hours to fully set. Also, the Platinum Pro paper feels stiffer, but this may be due to a resin coating on the paper, and it definitely lies flatter after it is dried. Color wise, the difference in \\"most\\" of the photos is amazing and very evident - the Platinum Pro is nothing less than impressive. As Canon claims, the Platinum Pro displays a noticeably expanded red gamut and much deeper blacks. The difference is significant and can be amazing with some prints (e.g. sunrise over Mt. Haleakala - simply spectacular on the Platinum Pro, nice but unimpressive on the Photo Pro II). All pics with blacks or dark shadows, such as tuxedos in wedding shots, were noticeably darker and more saturated in these areas. Shots with lots of red are where the color differences are most noticeable, as Canon would have one expect, but blue skies (e.g. a carousel shot against a bright sky with the saturation bumped up in PS5), also were noticeably more saturated.

For some photos, the increased red gamut and saturation and the deeper blacks makes the shots \\"pop\\" in a way I have not seen with other Canon papers, and usually only see on metallic or other commercial prints. The concern I have with the Platinum Pro is the expanded red ends up being a bit over saturated on people shots, particularly with pale skinned people with a hint of red tone. Some wedding prints were clearly over saturated in this area. Also, the deep blacks do seem to cause some loss of detail (those tuxedos again), though IMO this is offset by the richness of the blacks. The overall reservation I have with the Platinum Pro paper, and the reason I give it only 4 stars, is the overall affect on a lot of shots is over saturation. Some people argue that Canon favors the \\"Disney\\" look in colors and there is a bit of this with the Platinum Pro paper. This is definitely not the case with the Photo Paper Pro II, but that paper has a slight under saturation problem in my hands. I like the \\"pop\\" on many of the shots and know, now, what to expect, so it is an easy task to tone down the red (or blue) saturation, particularly in flesh toned shots if I need to.

Where the Platinum completely fell apart in my tests was with B&W prints. The good part is the paper produced B&Ws with an amazingly neutral bright white, whereas the Photo Pro II looks much closer to the Glossy II paper, and both have a noticeable tint. Unfortunately, there is a noticeable loss of detail in the Platinum Pro paper with B&W. The loss of detail was, for me, very unexpected and completely unacceptable. I did not see this loss of detail in the color shots. I've only printed two B&W on this paper and will print more to further test this, but detail was clearly lost in both prints. The Photo Pro II and the Glossy II produced much better B&W prints.

Overall, the types of photos I print look better on the Platinum Pro, so it will be my new [Canon] paper of choice for color prints, but I will have to adjust the saturation for flesh toned prints. For B&W? Well, so far, I have not tried any Canon product that impresses me, at least not on this printer. There are lots of other choices out there that are favored for B&W printing, and the PIXMA 9000 MKII is not noted for it's B&W capabilities anyway, so for this review I was more interested in color prints, and the Platinum Pro is without a doubt an impressive paper.

review_headline: Great solution for mobile or low-volume scanning
review_body: This is a great solution for mobile scanning, or low-volume scanning needs. If you are scanning 20-50 pages or so a day, this scanner will probably be a good choice. The auto-feed works reliably well for up to 10 pages at a time, and the scanning speed is very good for a scanner of this size (around 5-8 seconds per page).  Setup and installation is quick and easy on both Mac OS X and Windows.     Couple of things to note:    Be sure you don't lose the CD that comes with the scanner. Fujitsu makes it very difficult to get the drivers for the scanner if you lose the CD. (You can NOT download them online without contacting Fujitsu first.)    As with the larger S1500, there is no TWAIN driver for this scanner. That means no scanning directly into Photoshop or whatever your favorite app is. (For me, this is not an issue.)    If you scan more than a few pages at a time, or more than 50 pages a day, the larger S1500 model is probably a better choice; that model completes a full color, double-sided scan of a page in about 2-3 seconds. It costs about twice what the S1300 costs, but is worth it if you scan a lot of documents at a time.    I give it 4 stars instead of 5 because of the hassle with the drivers if you lose the CD, and because the scanning speed is good, but not great.

product_title: Lexmark Prevail Pro705 Small Office Wireless Multifunction Inkjet Printer
review_headline: Run, don't walk away from this printer!
review_body: I really wanted to like this printer.  After replacing my less than stellar HP all-in-one with the Prevail Pro705, I couldn't have been happier...for the first three weeks, then the problems started.  I received an error message on the display indicating a problem with the printer head.  A call to Lexmark and a new one was in my mailbox in two days.  I was impressed.  The tech help also updated my software online while I was on the phone, even more impressed.  For two months all was fine, until I made a copy (something I obviously don't do very often).  Down the left side edge was a printed black band a quarter inch wide.  A few tests of the scanner and I determined something was wrong with the scanner, not a printing error.  Another call to Lexmark and a week later I had a refurbished printer in hand.  The manufacturing date was only a month earlier and it had only printed about 300 pages according to the status sheet I printed out, so I felt like it was a fair exchange.  Lexmark didn't send a new print head or ink cartridges, but since the ones I had were essentially brand new I figured I was good to go.  Oddly enough, I had to update the firmware to the latest version, but it was easy enough...much easier than getting the new printer to correctly align the print head and getting it reconnected to the network.  I had to completely uninstall the software from three computers and reinstall in order for it to forget the old printer and recognized the new one.  Anyway, all was well for 90 pages of printing then the color problems and black streaks started for a few pages. Then the black and yellow stopped printing all together despite half full XL cartridges.  Another call to Lexmark and a new print head and cartridges are suppose to be here in two days.      Lexmark is pretty good at sending out parts, but needing replacements every other month is beyond acceptable.  I'll continue using the printer for as long as the parts keep coming, which is 5 years under warranty.  How much do you think Lexmark will loose on this $100 printer before they just upgrade me with something that works?  The shipping alone on the replacement probably ate a good bit of their profit margin.

product_title: EXPO Original Dry Erase Markers, Chisel Tip, Assorted Colors, 16-Count
review_headline: PLEASE READ THIS REVIEW: Erases Easily? Not Really!
review_body: I purchased these markers at a local store (instead of ordering them). The reviews that I read prior to purchasing them stated that these markers erased more easily than the low odor EXPO markers. I opened up my package, and took one out.   What I found was that they wrote very well (the ink line you get is solid), BUT when I went to ERASE what I had written, a very bold ghost remained (allowing me to clearly see what I had written), so I pushed harder on the eraser and tried again, and the only thing that it did was take the ghost away and leave me with smeared ink that looked like VERY distinct \\"ink cloud\\" - at that point the \\"ink cloud\\" remained no matter how much I erased the area. After having this occur once, I tested different erasers to find out if it was the eraser that was causing the problem instead of the ink. The same thing happened with all of the erasers - I was left with an \\"ink cloud\\" [I erased with the black magnetic OfficeMax eraser, the EXPO Precision Point eraser (the felt layer was clean due to recent removal of a layer), and with the EXPO XL eraser (the felt layer was clean due to it being recently purchased)].  I tested at least 4 or 5 markers, and the same exact thing happened with all of them (when I tested them I made sure the whiteboard area was clean. ALSO, I tested these markers and erasers on both an EXPO 2' x 3' magnetic whiteboard, and a homemade whiteboard using a sheet of melamine for the dry erase surface - the results were identical on both boards.)    On the health side, the odor from the ink is very noticeable [and I would assume that it could pose health hazards (an obvious symptom would be a headache) as a result of prolonged inhalation of the fumes/odors]. Personally, after this experience, I WOULD HIGHLY RECOMMEND PURCHASING LOW ODOR MARKERS (you can take my word on this - no joke). Low odor markers erase better, and if ghosts remain, they can be taken care of by erasing harder. Most importantly, low odor markers leave no \\"ink clouds!\\"  (I have used them ever since I began to use whiteboards - I just bought the originals to see how they performed while under the impression that they erased better).

review_body: Easy to peel from the sheet and with strong adhesive, these little gems are great for color-coded organizing among other things. The assorted colors help my co-worker and myself see at a glance which customer folders are high priority, lower priority, researched, or completed. Another use that immediately came to mind would be their usefulness at a garage sale.  At a neighborhood sale, use the different colors to identify who that item belongs to or perhaps devise your own code.      Put them on moving boxes, storage boxes.....the possibilities are endless.    My only complaint was that, although they can be run through a laser or inkjet printer, I could not find a cross to Avery system which is standard on most Windows-based PC's.  The free downloadable template provided on the Post-it website was not user-friendly and it was faster to just mark each dot by hand when needed.  Given the size of the dots there is little room for alpha-numeric text anyway.  It would be handy to be able to print garage sale prices on them in multiples (100@$1, 250@$1.50, etc) but I was unable to easily accomplish that using the template. product_title: Epson Stylus CX8400 Color All-in-One Printer
review_body: Please ignore all the reviews complaining about ink and ink priming. Some people never do read the info included with the gadgets they buy... This takes a significant amount of ink... But once the printer hoses are primed, they never have to be again... The printer will ask for new cartridges when the cartridge is empty... But when the hose to that cartridge is still full...this way the print head does not dry out.  Users will find the second set of cartridges offering considerably more service life than the cartridges that come with the printer... And Epson does offer higher capacity cartridges for many of their printers.  In the final analysis... Epsons print quality and print durability is the best I have seen, and that is what I am after.

product_title: Canon Pixma MX882 Wireless Office All-in-One Inkjet Printer (4894B002)
review_headline: Like it so far... with addendum about lower cost
review_body:
I purchased this printer to replace a 12-year-old HP DeskJet 930 (I'm pretty easy on my stuff, so it tends to last a long time). I did quite a bit of research before buying, and am very happy so far with the printer. It prints well, scanning is a snap, and it's very handy now having a fax at home, since I have a number of document recipients who prefer fax to email.

I really like being able to fax without actually printing a document out -- the fax function shows up as an available printer, so to send a document, whether pdf or Word or Excel or PowerPoint, all you have to do is click the print button and select the Canon fax as the destination printer. A window pops up asking for the phone number. Enter the phone number from the computer keyboard, hit \\"enter\\" and ZIP -- the printer dials and faxes the document directly from the computer file with no intervening paper copy. Paperless faxing is VERY handy!

The automatic duplex is also handy but very slow -- it prints one side, then sucks the page back in to print the other side.

It appears to be a bit more frugal with ink than the old DeskJet it replaced; I've not yet put in new cartridges but the ink indicator says I've used about a quarter of the pigment black and negligible amounts of the dye tanks. With the older printer, I'd have used about half the black and a quarter of the color tank after the same amount of time -- and with this printer, I can change out individual color tanks instead of the entire cartridge when I run out of one color. Ink cartridge costs, both for the black and for the color set, are comparable to OEM for the HP and a little lower for non-OEM. As a rough estimate, it looks like my per-page costs will be about 75% or so of what they were with the DesdJet.

I'd read several comments about the footprint, but although the printer is much more massive and bulkier than the DeskJet, the two-dimensional footprint on the desk is virtually the same. The DeskJet had a large base with a fairly small upper body, while the Canon is much more cubic. It therefore seems much bigger and more in the way. Though it doesn't take many more square inches of the desk surface, it consumes many more cubic inches of volume and is easier to bump into.

All in all, I'm very happy with the print quality, ease of use, and functionality. I can't address photo printing since I've not done any yet. I don't know if it will last 12 years or even 12 months, but no regrets on the purchase as yet.

-----------------------------------

ADDENDUM after five months of use: I've now run about 400-500 pages through the printer of Office Depot recycled paper. I've seen some complaints about jamming with inexpensive paper, but the only feed problem I've had is the ONE time the printer took two sheets of paper at once. I had let the supply tray get down to near-empty, and the printer grabbed the last two sheets at the same time. I also now have a handle on ink costs, and I'm VERY happy. My HP InkJet used HP 45 black and 78 cartridges; a set of both ran about $70 OEM and about $50 for off-brands and refills -- and the off-brands and refills had about an 20% failure rate, so they weren't any cheaper than HP name brand cartridges.

I just now changed out the black pigment tank and two of the color dye tanks -- using off-brand cartridges I ordered from an online discounter for just over $7 each (about $36 for a full set vs $50 for the HP). They work perfectly with no streaking, spotting, or missed spots. After three weeks of use, I'm using the off-brand no more quickly than I used the Canon brand -- and I got about 50% more pages using the Canon \\"fast\\" setting than I did with the HP \\"draft\\" setting.

Cheaper ink cartridges that print more pages -- I LOVE saving money on ink. It looks so far like my ink costs could be about half what they used to be for the same print volume. It will be nice not to spend as much on ink every year as I did for the printer.

My only annoyance is caused by my fairly low print volume. I print 20-30 page jobs about 5 or 6 times per month, with one or two page jobs about twice a week. That means the printer may be in use daily for a few days, but it also means it might sit idle for four or five days at a time. After an extended idle time, the first print job may not start until the machine takes about 3 or 4 minutes to clean the cartridges and do other \\"internal maintenance.\\" I guess the cure would be to print more often, but it's a very minor and occasional annoyance.

So, after six months of use, I'm still very happy with the printer and would definitely purchase again.My only annoyance is caused by my fairly low print volume. review_body: I had been searching for an all-in-one type of thing, but I knew I was really only wanting to scan pictures to make them digital & organize them. I finally searched for picture scanner instead of printers and I come across this one. I read numerous reviews and always make my final decision based on customer reviews, & this one had really good detailed ones. It arrived in two days like it said it would, and I liked the fact that you could follow the shipping online and know exactly where it was & when it arrives. When I took it out of the box to set it up, I noticed it was very minimal... scanner, cord, film tray, and installation cd, which made for extremely easy set-up. Whole thing took about 5 minutes from box to when I scanned my first picture. There are only 4 buttons on the whole thing and after reading the tutorial and included instructions it only get easier to use. I played with the settings and DPI's to see what the differences were... I finally realized that the only time you notice any difference is when you go to enlarge them! HA HA! I'm not very picture smart, but I figured it out. The only thing is, is that if you do a higher DPI, it does take longer per picture, but then again it's trying to scan a better quality. It is a little on the noisy side, but something you can't just tone out after a while of scanning. I've scanned tons of pictures so far and I'm just loving, that I can now jump on my computer, type in whatever I'm looking for, and BAM! there's my picture... (I did label every picture I scanned though, so it's not just a number for the original file, which allows me to organize and put pictures into folders of year, group, people, places, that sort of thing.) All in All, if you want to organize those boxes and boxes of photos you have, this is the ideal machine for the job. I also love the color restoration and auto fix buttons, again this does a better job if you scan it in the larger DPI numbers. I hope this review helped and I know you will be pleased with it. It's cheaper than some scanners, more expensive than others, but this is perfect for the quality and ease of operation.  It also does negative and slides. IT DOES NOT DO 110 FILM THOUGH! I found it fascinating when I went to do the negatives... Once you put in a negative it scans one per scan & it is time consuming, but its wonderful if you don't have a copy of the picture somewhere and well worth it. (As in there are usually 4-5 pictures per negative... It would scan 4-5 times to get all the pictures, not just once)

product_title: Lexmark Impact Wireless Multi-function Inkjet Printer (S305)
review_headline: Complete garbage - worst printer you could buy
review_body: After suffering with this thing for 6 months, I finally have to vent and write a review.  I'll start with the good... when it eventually does print, the printout looks reasonable (if it didn't run out of ink first).  But, so what?  Every other printer out there also looks reasonable.  Now, the bad...    The worst feature is that this printer, amazingly, eats ink rapidly even when not in use.  I maybe made less than 10 color printouts of web pages that only had text on them over a period of a few months, since I normally only need to print anything in black.  And, this was with replacement cartridges that I bought, not the nearly empty ones that they ship it with.  Somehow, that was enough to consume the color ink completely.  I mentioned this to the guy who works in the store that I bought it from, and he said \\"Oh you need the extra capacity ink cartridges\\".  Now, he was wrong, but that brings up the next problem.... Lexmark does a very sleazy thing by selling you mostly empty cartridges for a high price, and expecting you to pay even more than that already high price if you actually want them to fill the cartridges completely.  $80 to replace the black and color ink???  It is just a few ml's of ink... how much could that possibly cost them?  Sleazy tactics make businesses lose customers.  This is enough for me to NEVER buy another Lexmark anything again.    Now, whenever I print, the thing sits there for 5 minutes with a little message \\"Preparing printer\\" and making noises.  I have never had another printer do that.  What exactly does it think it is \\"preparing\\"?  Print already!    I'm more often using this thing to make a photocopy than a printout.  When making a copy, it defaults to a color copy.  There is a button to switch between color and black.  Pressing the button to make it a black copy only remembers the setting for a few minutes, then it automatically switches back to color copy.  There is no way to make it remember my setting, or force a black copy everytime.  These sleazy people did this on purpose so that you would accidentally use up the more expensive color ink quickly.    Whenever I power down my computer, background apps from Lexmark GPF on me, even if I didn't print during that session.  I then have to click to make the error go away before I can finish powering down.  Very annoying.    The initial setup was more complex than it should have been.  They do not need to require a USB cable in order to do the setup; it should be possible to do without if they put some thought into it.  The device feels cheap and flimsy, especially when replacing the ink cartridges... it feels like it is about to break apart from normal ink cartridge maintenance.  It hasn't broken yet, but it sure feels that way.      I replaced my router with a different SSID, which required reconfiguring the printer.  There was no way to do it from the computer or from the printer without getting out that USB cable thing again and remembering which part of the UI lets me do that.  It took me 15 minutes to find it, and was easy enough once I found it, but I'm still annoyed.    I plugged this into a Kill-A-Watts meter, and it uses 8 watts of power when not in use.  I realize that since it has wifi it may need to use more electricity than a hardwired printer so that it can detect when an incoming printout is happening, but a well behaved device that is in standby should never use more than 4 watts, and preferably only 2 watts.    Once I use up my current ink cartridges (shouldn't be long), I'm tossing this in the trash and buying another brand.  The money wasted on ink alone makes this thing a money loser to keep it even if it is still functioning.

review_body: I really like this product.  For the price, it's a steal.  I do wish it had a bit more features to it, but, again, it's not $300. One of my classes it rather large for my school, and other students are a little loud.  Even though it's a quiet room, when you have that many people in a single room, they just tend to not be silent.  I tried using one of its helpful functions; this function (can't remember what it's called) has a bar set, and if the surrounding noise (an air conditioner or other constant rumble) is apparent, it does not record this (provided you have the bar set just above this).  My professor, however, gets kind of quiet.  I just wish this setting had more preset bar settings, or just let you set it where ever you wanted.  That's pretty much my only complaint.  I really like all the folders it has, too.  I thought when I read that online, \\"Hey, I'm probably not going to use them for organization or anything.. It'll be an extra feature I'm not going to gain or lose anything from.\\"  I was wrong.  I do really like it for the days I don't have time to put the files onto my computer.  I can use a new one each day I can't get them on my computer.  Anyway, a great buy if you're looking for a cheap, and (so far seemingly) good quality, audio recorder!  I'm not regretting, what-so-ever, this buy, even though, at first, I thought it was a rather impulsive buy.  My money was well spent in my opinion.

product_title: Aprilaire 5000 Air Cleaner
review_headline: Great air cleaner (don't call it a filter!)
review_body:
ha... I suppose you can call it an air filter... but they say Air Cleaner...

I ordered this to add to my old furnace, but then decided to upgrade the furnace too. So I had the HVAC guy put it in when they installed the new furnace.

Then we had the ducts cleaned too.

All the HVAC guys and the duct cleaner guy made comments about this being a great air cleaner.

We've been using it for a few weeks now and it seems to work just fine. Our new furnace has the variable speed blower so we just leave the blower on 24-7 (it runs at very low speed till the furnace or AC kicks on)

Because of this, we aren't using the fancy air cleaner control right now... so I can't comment on that.

I also can't comment yet about filter life.

But one interesting thing... the filter comes in a little box... its not in a cardboard frame like you might be used to seeing with standard filters (when I first opened the air cleaner I thought they forgot to include the filter!)

The filter is all collapsed (like an accordion) and you have to install it into the plastic frame. This is pretty easy to do - you just snap on the top and bottom and then insert a bunch (6 maybe?) of plastic combs between the filter pleats to hold them in the proper position. The filter is about 4\\" or 5\\" thick... which creates a lot of surface area for collecting dust and whatnot. (standard filters are only 1\\" thick)

Once you have it in place, you snap the ends of the plastic box shut... they have foam or something on them so they seal up tight against the ends of the filter medium to prevent any air from \\"bypassing\\" the filter.

I mainly mention this for those that might wonder why replacement filters are only like $25 (last I checked)... I think the low cost is because the filter isn't in a cardboard frame which would require more assembly and shipping costs.

Anyway, this is rather expensive - but it seems to be one of the more affordable options for a better air cleaner. Plus if these filters really do last a year then there is some savings on buying filters... I probably replaced my old style filter 3-4 times a year at 12-15 bucks per filter. If you want to upgrade your current filter then this seems to be a good way to go.

*** UPDATE 19 July 2012 ***
I replaced the air filter last night (for the first time). It was definitely time to replace it. After about 9-10 months of use it was rather dirty and perhaps starting to limit air flow. They say it should be good for 12 months, but I have a variable speed furnace blower so I leave it on all the time (it runs slowly except when calling for heat or AC) which I assume probably reduces the life of the filter.

But of course I get constant air filtration (and better temperature regulation) by keeping the blower on so I'm OK with this.

While changing the filter I washed the metal screen and wiped down the wires. There was some dust buildup on these. Other than that, I just swept out the nooks/crannies on the filter box (the upstream side had some dust accumulation) and put the new filter in.

It really isn't that hard to install the filter... it takes a few seconds to get the first spreader bar in, but then the rest pop right in if you start right next to the first one and then slide them into place.

I checked the blower box on the furnace while I was re-installing it - I ran my fingers across the bottom and it was perfectly clean. This tells me that this filter is doing a great job.

So - I would still recommend that people buy this. It works great!

product_title: AT&T CL80109 DECT 6.0 Cordless Phone Accessory Handset, Silver/Black (Accessory handset only)
review_headline: Good addition to other AT&T phones.
review_body:
After installing the AT&T U-verse system, I discovered I needed to switch to cordless phones. U-verse hates the old copper lines in my house.

After reading Consumer Reports and these Amazon reviews, I bought the AT&T DECT 6.0 Digital 4-Handset, plus this fifth identical AT&T DECT 6.0 Accessory Handset from Amazon. Oddly, my local major AT&T store does not stock these phones. These phones work great with U-verse VoIP (or normal copper lines).

Good:

1. The phones are compact and light, though I find the silver finish rather cheesy-looking.

2. Sound quality is excellent, handsets were ready to go (after a lengthy charging), and instructions are fairly readable.

3. The AT&T DECT 6.0 Accessory Handset requires one additional step so it would \\"link\\" to the rest of the system, but it isn't too confusing and it is good to go.

Minor gripes:

1. These handset bases are nice and small, but they cannot be mounted to the wall. This would have been an easy design option, but the designers did not bother. All these lightweight units are just sitting around cluttering tables and waiting to be knocked off instead of being safely mounted on vertical surfaces.

2. Batteries arrived about 98 percent drained and take about 16 hours to charge.

3. Handsets cause an annoying \\"buzz\\" whenever it is near my computer's sound system. In all fairness, it is probably a grounding issue with my computer's speakers.

Overall good, inexpensive units slightly flawed by AT&T's sloppy corporate mentality.

NOW, FOR ALL YOU WINDOWS 7, 64-BIT PEOPLE:  THE CD DOES NOT SUPPLY THE 64-BIT DRIVERS.  A negative against canon to do that, but it can be resolved quickly and easily.  Go to their website and download the 64-bit drivers first to your desktop.  Unpack the file onto your desktop by double-clicking the file you downloaded (it will unpack the drivers into a new folder on your desktop...look for it before proceeding and remember the name of the folder), then plug the USB cord into the printer.  When the computer finds the printer, it will want to find drivers for it.  Instead of letting the computer go looking on the internet for the drivers, go searching for that file you put on the desktop and select it for the place the computer will look for drivers.  Bingo!.....you now have the printer working on a 64-bit Windows 7 OS.  Canon did screw up by not putting 64-bit drivers on the CD, and Windows 7 will lead you astray if you let it go looking for new ones online.  But, if you have ANY technical know-how, you should be able to get your computer up and running on your own.  If not, take it to someone who knows what they are doing.  The printer IS of good quality. Don't blame it for Canon's shortcomings.

review_headline: Well-Thought Product that Makes Organization Easier
review_body: I received 7 blue, 7 red and 6 yellow folders.   This is great for color-coding different material in different files.      I like that with each folder you get five different positioned tabs to pick from for the label and literally all you have to do is pull up one of the five label tabs between your fingers and you have an instant label that you can either write on directly or add a sticker label.  This is great since you don't have to worry about inserting those annoying plastic tabs used on other folders, or worse yet risk one of them falling out and having an unlabeled folder.  In essence with the system used by these folders one could simply push down one tab, reposition a folder, and then pop-up one of the other four tabs with a fresh label.  While I love having five multi-positioned and built-in labels for each folder, I think having all of the labels white is one area where an improvement can be made.  Having multi-colored folders is great; however, having multi-colored labels would have been a nice feature to include with this particular product.  My only other concern is the durability of the label tabs.  Time will tell; however, since they are not plastic they might wear or get bent when flipping through folders in a cabinet loaded with files.      I like that the tops of each folder near the label tabs is reinforced with an additional layer of approximately 1.4\\" clear material to keep the slots from tearing.  There is also a little 0.75\\" clear colored reinforcement strip on the outer edges of the bottom and the top of the folders as well.  The folders seem durable enough and don't have the rough feeling surface as many of the recycled folders on the market even though these are made in part (10%) of recycled material.    If you don't like handwritten labels, you can print your own custom tab labels with the included template sheet.  It is not quite as easy as just selecting the model number of the label like can be done with Avery labels with the Microsoft Office Suite; however, it is still doable with a little work and by following the included instructions.  You get 40 labels for the 20 folders so a little margin of error is built-in for trial-and-error, or later on changing the name of your labels.      I also like the easy-to-access box.  There are slits that can be cut to slide out one folder at a time instead of having to lift up the entire box.

As for the pad not being wide enough, my keyboard is almost exactly as wide as the foam pad, so I have found it to work marvelously. However, if other reviewers' keyboards are greatly wider, I can see how it may cause some discomfort. Comparing your keyboard's width to the foam pad's may be something you would like to do prior to ordering.

There are two features that I enjoy about this product. The first being that the foam feels durable. I am not worried about having to replace it in a few short months due to the foam breaking down from normal wear and tear. The second is the non skid backing. This makes it much easier to avoid having to make adjustments while typing.

There is only one con I have about the pad. If your desk has a pullout keyboard shelf, it can be difficult to fit both the keyboard and the pad on the shelf without one or the other hanging over a bit. It does not interfere with the quality of my typing, but it can be a small annoyance. Granted, this is not a fault of the manufacturer, simply something to keep in mind.

Overall, I am highly pleased with the 3M Foam Wrist Rest, and would recommend it to a friend.

product_title: Panasonic DECT 6.0 Link-to-Cell via Bluetooth Cordless Phone with Answering System
review_headline: Integrating cellphone, Google voice and skype + bluetooth speaker
review_body: Let me first talk about my phone setup.  1. I use google voice + Obihai 110 (highly recommend) as a free land-line, google voice will forward calls to both my cellphone and panasonic 7644M.  2. I have one cellphone paired directly with 7644M with link-to-cell.  3. Finally, I use link-to-cell to pair my computer with 7644M, so as to make computer calls with skype, etc.  Below are the results for this setup, I numbered them corresponding to the above 3 different ways of using the phone.  1. There is no problem using GV this way, I read from one previous review that if GV forwards calls to both a landline and a mobile-phone, there will be a glitch that the other side cannot hear your voice. But in my case, GV forwards calls to google chat (which is converted by ohihai 110 to voip signal), and mobile phone. And there isn't any glitch at all. When receiving a call, usually 7644M would ring first, then after 2-3 seconds, my cellphone rings, I can pick-up either phone to answer the call.  2. Basic feature of link-to-cell phones, works like a charm, really easy to setup. One thing worth mentioning is its ability to transfer contacts from mobile phone to landline. However, to copy all contacts together as a whole to 7644M, your phone need to support PBAP (phone book access profile), which seems not existing in my cellphone. So I have to transfer contacts individually. Another good thing is you can make multiple calls using different handset at the same time. For example, if one handset is making calls using cellphone signal, another handset can still use the land-line to call someone else. I believe there can be 3 simultaneous calls (1 land line, 2 link-to-cell) at maximum.  3. This is like using it as a bluetooth headset paired to computer. The manual doesn't mention anything about it, but it turns out working well. Here are the steps to achieve this. First, use link-to-cell to pair the phone with your computer. After pairing is successful, your computer will automaticallyinstall the drivers for this blue-tooth handset. Then in the sound and recording devices, you should be able to see one new device named blue-tooth hands free audio. Now, if you want to chat on skype with this handset, dial a random number (I dialed 1) using the handset via the computer link-to-cell, since this is an empty number, you will not be connected to anyone. But after a few beeps, the handset will establish a voice connection to your computer. You can now chat via skype or any other chatting software with your handset, assuming you have properly setup the sound devices within these softwares.  One major problem using it with skype is that the handset would hang up either when skype finishes a call or when there is no call and no sound from computer for like 10 seconds. This means after you dialing 1 with the handset, you need to dial the person you need to call immediately on computer, and the connection only last one call, after which you need to repeat again to establish connection. The numberpad on handset works with some lag in skype. I guess there is some workaround for skype to maintain a constant or automatic connection, but didn't figure out how.  I also tried to set my default audio device as 7644 on computer, and played mp3 via the handset speakerphone. It's mono sound obviously, but acceptable for some audio books. I tested for about 10 mins without seeing any problem, and handset automatically hang up after I stopped music for 15-20 seconds.  As you can see, this phone integrates all of my phone services. Whenever I receive calls from cellphone, GV, skype, I can answer them with it. I can also make calls with it using all the above services.  A few comments for the difference between 7641 series and 7621 series if someone wonders. They are basically the same except for  1. handset on 7641 have headphone jacks.  2. You can dial and speak via the base unit with 7641, while 7621 only have the answering machine function on the base unit.  3. For thesame reason, 7621 doesn't have base unit display, and there is no intercom between base unit and handset.  4. 7641 have power back-up mode during power failure, which means you can still make calls even there is a power outage less than 13 hours.  5. I didn't see on 7621 description page it has range-boost, while 7641 clearly says it has range-boost, which allow 20% more distance between base unit and handset.  So if you only use your handset to make calls, and your area doesn't have power outage once in a year. Then probably 7621 could also meet your needs.  I just played with it for half a day, so cannot comment on its reliability. But for its versatility and good sound quality, I would vote it for more than 5 stars!  *******************************************  Update: 2/21/2012  a few small glitches of the phone.  1. product_title: Excelmark Identity Theft Guard Stamp, Large (42050-SEC)
review_body:
It seems like a great idea as an alternative to ripping addresses out of catalogs and form letters. I've had it about a week and I've tested it out on many types of mailings. What it seems to handle well: Obliterating name/address printed on regular porous paper. Things like credit card offers and whatnot.

It does not work flawlessly on glossier surfaces. I've tried it on several different glossy surfaces. I let the ink dry for at least 24 hours and in some cases, several days. Then I wiped at it with a damp paper towel and a little dish detergent. As an example, the glossy sticker label that UPS had affixed to a package immediately wiped clean enough to view the address beneath. On my issue of The Week magazine (a sort of intermediate glossy), wiping produced a smear that initially obliterated everything. But I happened to look at the magazine the next day when the liquid had dried and--once again--you could easily make out the name and address.

So, depending on how secure you want things--if you're just trying to prevent someone at the recycle center from glancing at a magazine and seeing your name and address--this is fine. But if you're at all fearful of someone finding your name appearing on an issue of Naked Transvestite Midgets Monthly, it's still best to shred the glossy stuff.

Re the size issue that a few people have mentioned: For any computer-generated address, the \\"large\\" size is fine. The problem is that the stamp housing has outer dimensions significantly larger than the stamp so it does take a little practice to be able to obliterate the address in one shot.

product_title: Epson WorkForce 633 All-in-One Printer (C11CB06211)
review_headline: Very good AIO for the price!
review_body: Great value for the money spent. Small footprint, comparable to other consumer AIO inkjets. Quite light in weight too. Refills look affordable. Great print quality, even in colour. I love Epson's proprietary ink - no more smudging when I highlight!    Very easy to set up, anyone should be able to do it without breaking a sweat. Attractive, sleek design. Haven't had any problems so far with dropped network connectivity or print jobs. Haven't tested the scan function yet though, so can't comment on scan quality. Might be okay if you only need to install on one computer, but if you have to do it for a home/small business network, it gets annoying fast.    Minor additional features I would have liked to see (often found in other AIOs):   1) Something equivalent to an \\"econo mode\\" in the printing preferences - almost every printer out there these days offers an option to use less ink for non-presentation print jobs (\\"draft\\" isn't the same).   2) A built-in blacklist for the fax to block specific numbers. Another AIO I bought several years ago that was nowhere near top of the line even had this feature.    The 633 is the 2nd highest model of the 630 series. The biggest difference between the top model - the 635 - and this model is the 635 has the ability to do double sided copies. If you don't need that function, save your money and get the 633!

I am writing my memoirs and need to look up words fast and nothing beats Sharp for speed. For example, if you want to go from thesaurus to dictionary using the Franklin, you have to first go to the library function and then click on dictionary; with the Sharp, there's no need to do this. You just push the dictionary key and you're there. You can transfer from one to the other instantly.

What I've ended up doing is using the Franklin as an addendum for the Sharp so I have access to a larger choice of words. Also, you can have more fun with the Franklin because there are more functions to play with. I'm just not into playing with electronic gadgets.

Either the Sharp or the Franklin would be extremely useful for students, writers, or just people who love words. Either one of them beats a clunky paper book by a whole lot. I've given the Sharp as gifts to my grandson and my son.

One more thing, there's a huge price difference between the two instruments. The Sharp costs under $100; the Franklin is over $250.

Enjoy!

review_headline: Extra Fine Point is the Way to Go!
review_body:
The Pilot G2 Extra Fine Point is definitely one of the best pens I've ever used. They never jam, leak, or break ... and the outer plastic shell is so durable, I usually just get replacement inserts. However, at this price it's easier just to use the Pilot G2 as a disposable pen.

There's a definite visual difference between a Pilot Fine Point and an Extra Fine Point. I never found that Fine Points to draw a thin enough line for my liking, especially if you're writing on a pad that doesn't have a super hard surface beneath it. You can distinguish an Extra Fine Point because it has the number \\"05\\" written on the pen where as the Fine Points has a \\"07\\". The \\"05\\" Extra Fine Point produces a thinnest in the line similar to a ball point pen but with the smoothness of a gel pen.

The G2 Extra Fine Point is a great pen!

product_title: Monteverde Ballpoint Refill to Fit Montblanc Ballpoint Pens, Medium Point, Soft Roll, 2 Per Pack
review_body: First of all, this alternative Mont Blanc ballpoint refill is a perfect fit for the pen. Second, it is a blue-black or really a dark blue color. At one time Mont Blanc made a dark blue ballpoint refill but currently the blue ballpoint is a pale blue that I don't like at all. This is a nice dark blue and the only choice out there if that is your preference. It is an expensive pen, after all, and I should have choices of ballpoint colors. Otherwise I might as well write with a cheap pen. Third, the ink flow is very smooth. This is a low viscosity ballpoint ink, meaning that it writes like a ballpoint - not like a gel or liquid ink - but with much less pressure and effort than an old fashioned ballpoint, which is all that Mont Blanc makes. This is a much, much nicer writing experience. And fourth, these refills are cheaper than the Mont Blancs. I guess if you spend what a Mont Blanc costs the price of a refill is not crucial, but hey, cheaper is better anyway. I have had no problems - certainly no leaking, globbing or skipping, and I am very picky about my pens and writing. This refill is sure to please. The black Monteverde refill is just as good, I've used them too, if black ink is your thing. I just really like the blue-black. It is classy.

product_title: Collections Etc - 3 In 1 Hand Crank Paper Shredder
review_body: The shredder has 3 slots: one for paper, one for CDs, and one for cards. It does not need AC power to operate: you'll just crank it up to get it to shred your stuff. For shredding papers, I can only get it to do at most 2 sheets at a time (I think the recommended max limit is 3 sheets, I forgot). For single sheets, it turns smoothly; for 2 sheets, it's a bit harder to turn, but still manageable. Thus, it's definitely not for shredding lots of papers, but more for just the occasional stuff you need to shred. Besides, the bin it stands on is not that large, so I'm pretty sure after shredding about 10 sheets, you'll need to empty it.     My only gripe is that there's no easy way to grip the unit when you're cranking the lever. I manage by just holding the side and carefully turning it and not processing more than 2 sheets at a time (so that it won't be too difficult to turn). You'll need to set it on a flat, stable surface to operate. Also, the shredding unit doesn't really \\"lock\\" onto the bin, so you have to be careful about turning the lever so that it won't tip over.     I have not tried the CD shredder nor the card shredder. Note though, that when shredding the card, you'll have to put it in, short side first. I'm doubtful about its effectivity, because it looks like if you don't properly align the card so that the magnetic strips, name, and card number line up to the blades, then you'll end up with your personal info not getting shredded at all.     Overall, it's a good shredder for its price and I am satisfied with my purchase.
