product_title: Canon ImageCLASS MF4570dn Laser Multifunction Printer (4509B020AA)
review_body: We got this machine to replaced our Canon MF5770 that we had for about 4 years, and finally sucame to the dreaded \\"download standby\\" error. We use all functions of the machine, both this one and the MF5570 which it replaced.    We are a small medical research clinic, and the machines usually gets about 50 pages on average sent to them either from a print job or a fax. Many days it will be quite a bit more. We also fax jobs out a few times a day. The new machine is a definite upgrades in many ways, and a downgrade in one critical way (though how critical will very per person).    So what's great about this machine?  - Duplexing: Works great and is speedy. It also duplexes faxes and print jobs.  - Networking: Once set up correctly you can print to this printer from anywhere, and scan from the computer or from the machine to a computer on your network.  - Speed: Print jobs are fast.  - Paper tray: Holds plenty of paper and the translucent cover lets you see when you are running low.  - Size: Its about half the size of the printer it replaced, and yet its still faster, and does more.  - Scanning: The included software is a breeze to use, and the ability to initiate scanning from the machine or the computer is ideal. Before only the one computer attached to the machine could scan, but now all the computers in the clinic can scan. This is a huge time saver for us.  - Energy Saver Mode: Works great, and wakes up super fast from this mode so no waiting to print or fax or copy but you still save energy.    So whats not so great about this machine?  - Text quality: The text printed from the machine is just a bit not right. I mean, most people will not notice is, but the MF5770 had superb text rendering, and this machine just doesn't. Its completely passable, and like I mentioned most people would not even notice. Its too sharp, and not smooth, is the real way to describe it. Some people might even prefer the extra sharpness, but I sure didn't, and neither did the PCMag editors.  - Buttons: The buttons are like tictacs in shape and sort of hollow, and are not great on the fingers, and sort of small. The layout is also a little weird. The menu okay button is a big round circle and I keep hitting it instead of the button i actually mean to hit, the green ok button for initiating an actual activity.  - Noise: Its very quiet when not in use, but maybe a tad too loud when in use. However its fast so its not noisy for very long.    Some other things. I've seen it asked many places to let me just clear it up here. This machine will provide a confirmation page for faxes and include an image of the fax facesheet. It is not located under the fax settings but under the reports setting. You just need to go to reports-->fax tx-->print report with image after each transmission-->yes/on. If you set the machines up correctly, you can have it so that the machines scans a file and attaches it right to an email with the push of one button. Love this feature as we often have to email scanned documents.    This machine got the editor's choice award from PC mag, and rightly so. For the price you get an incredibly versatile, speedy, machine that doesn't take up much space and can handle the work load of a small office with ease. You just can't beat that.

product_title: Canon PIXMA MG6120 Wireless Inkjet Photo All-in-One Printer (4503B002)
review_headline: Excellent Photo Printer and Best Option for B&W Prints For Under $200
review_body: Like everyone else here, I too agree that this is an excellent AIO device. I bought the 6120 EXCLUSIVELY to print photos so I will only review it as such. I already have a Canon scanner and a Brother laser printer for monochrome prints. I am an amateur photographer and was printing exclusively on Epson printers for as long as I printed anything. I was most recently printing with a pigment ink based Epson R1800 which was great...if it didn't clog constantly! I had it decided to change brands instead to Canon. The 6120 is much faster and the pictures on glossy photo paper didn't supper from the \\"bronzing\\" effect that the Epsons were known for where part of the print without ink (the whites) were dull and had a bronze tinge to it if viewed from an angle. The only issue I have with the printer is that the 9ml ink cartridges are pricey. The Epsons used a 13ml cartridge. But I was also using a third of the ink to clean the R1800's heads so it all balances out. I simply order the inks from Amazon and recycle the empty cartridges at Staples to get $2 back per. The single cartridges are the same price on Amazon as they are at most Staples so you get 10% of your ink money back each quarter if you become a Rewards member along with the $2 recycle reward.     PROS:  1) Excellent Photo prints that cost about the same as pharmacy prints (25 cents each). I like Epson's Premium Gloss photo paper as it's thicker and has more gloss to them. Cost is about the same regardless of where you buy them.  2) Very good Black and White prints with the gray ink tank. You need to step up to pro printers like the Mark II 9500 to do better with their 2 black inks.  3) Very fast prints in about 20 seconds if you set print quality to STANDARD for 4x6 prints  4) Very easy WiFi setup process  5) No \\"bronzing\\" effect on glossy prints like the Epsons  6) Heads don't seem to clog...at least not yet. Only time will tell. I will try to print at least once a week to keep the heads from drying up.  7) Decentprint quantity on initial set of cartridges. I've made about 150 4x6s and the gray ink cart low ink and the magenta and yellow carts are down to 1 bar. I expect more prints when I replace the inks.  8) Touch sensitive controls that disappear gives the printer a very contemporary feel    CONS:  1) Ink cartridges are pricey for a measly 9ml of ink. You should get at least 13ml.  2) A lot of work and time needed to assemble the printer and align the heads. Although everything went smoothly so as long as your are careful and read the instructions. And you only do it once.  3) Piano black finish is a dust, scratch and fingerprint magnet. But boy does it look nice.    As you can see, I really don't have many bad things to say about the 6120. I get better prints out of this printer than my $500 Epson R1800 which clogged half the time. I really don't need the scanner but I guess it's a nice bonus. Overall, this printer is an excellent product with excellent value and I would recommend it to anyone interested in making home prints that rival photo labs.

product_title: Fujitsu ScanSnap S1500 Instant PDF Sheet-Fed Scanner for PC
review_body: I had a huge number of documents forwarded to me that needed to be scanned. Probably 2-3,000.  I was somewhat dreading the task because my printer combo doesn't scan at top speeds.  I decided to bite the bullet and get equipment to make it easier - which I also justified because I knew I could use it in my office for other occasions.  When I saw the price tags on this, I didn't want to bite a bullet that big.  I wanted to spend about half that price.  However, the reviews won out.  Better to spend more to get the job done than spend half and get half of it done.    It was easy (beyond belief) to set up and get going.  Scanning started well, but then I started getting a ridiculous number of double feeds.  I suspected it was the cheap paper and the fact that the paper had been freshly copied.  Just like a copier, those tend to jam the most.  I wasn't upset with the machine because even when I tried to copy on my good paper, my printer double fed it too.  Still, I had just spent a ton of money and it wasn't working for my project.    That's when I did some searching on the internet.  There were several comments on this.  The most helpful to me was to set the paper gently into the feeder.  I know that sounds weird because I wasn't slamming it in or anything.  But, if I had a large number I was trying to scan (which was common due to the size of the job and the short amount of time to do it), I would tap them on the table to get them straight and then put them in.  When I tried the \\"gently\\" approach, it made an incredible difference.  I hardly had the problem at all after that.  It was amazing.  So, I am writing this review for others who may be in the same boat.  Try the gently thing.  It works.    Also, \\"gently\\" forced me to take out ten or so papers if I needed to.  That helped, too.    I do have to say, the scanner is AMAZING at catching double feeds.  You don't have to sit and watch.  It will stop and tell you.  It's not like the copy machine that, if you don't watch, you're gonna find out later it missed some.    The one issue I did have was that the scanner is duplex - which I needed - but, because of the thin cheap paper used to copy these documents, the scanner recognized print on some of the pages \\"through\\" the page.  So, I would get one side with the correct print and another reverse side (as it also read the scan through the back).  I don't think I will have this problem as often because cheap paper always causes me problems in the printer, copier, etc.  So, I try to get good deals on the better quality.  It saves alot of headache in the end.    I echo the other reviewers on the other things.  The duplex is amazing.  This thing is amazingly fast.  I saved hours upon hours using it over my printer scanner.  I never would have shelled out the money if I hadn't been in a huge time crunch on a big project.  But, now, I don't think I could ever use another machine after seeing this powerhouse go through the scans so fast.    So, reading my review, please know that I agree with the others.  I just wanted to add the \\"gently\\" thing because, as ridiculous as it sounds, it made a ton of difference.      Happy Scanning!

product_title: HP LaserJet P2035 Monochrome Printer (CE461A#ABA)
review_body: This printer makes a hellacious noise every time the engine starts-which is every time it prints. The \\"quiet mode\\", a critical selling point for me, cannot be enabled on a Mac operating system, even though the advertising says the printer is Mac compatible. Which, if you don't mind the really unpleasant racket, it is.  Even worse, the User Guide that came in the installation documentation specifically sets out the method for enabling quiet mode in Mac. It doesn't work-and can't be made to work in the Mac environment as the printer is delivered. After hours of trying to find a solution through Apple and HP Support, I was informed (by HP) that I can enable quiet mode on this printer only through a Windows environment, and then when I reconnect to my Mac, the printer will be in quiet mode. What a wonderful fix. When you make a statement in your advertising that is knowingly untrue, and you compound the misrepresentation by including a second misrepresentation in the User Guide, it is to my mind nothing less that a fraud. HP will have to pay me to have another of their products. You'd be better off buying a printer from a sleazy used-car dealer.

product_title: 10P PGI-5 CLI-8 Ink with 2 PGI-5 for Canon MP520 MP510 Mx700 iP3300 iP3500 Printer
review_headline: Quality Ink and Quality Customer Service
review_body: I recently purchased this ink for my Canon Pixma MP520 after sifting through mounds of overpriced products. Because everything sold by E-Z Ink is so cheap, I assumed that the ink would be of low quality. Boy was I wrong! First, let me tell you about my experience with E-Z Ink's great customer service team. Upon receiving my package (which came in about 3 days), I immediately opened up one of the cartridges to install it. When I did, the ink leaked all over my hands. Annoyed, I tried it again with the same result. Now I was upset. I re-read the instructions on the box and tried it one more time. Still no luck. At this point, I decided to send an e-mail to the seller describing my experience. They responded in about 36 hours with this message:    Hi,    Thank you for your purchase and we regret the inconvenience you've experienced with the leaking cartridges. We pack our products tightly to avoid this issue but sometimes due to carrier mishandling or other factors, products can still get damaged during the shipping process. If possible, please send pictures of the leaking cartridges for record purposes to: (e-mail). Additionally, please confirm your mailing address so that we can send you replacement ink tanks.    They were going to replace the ink, no questions asked. I later found the ACTUAL directions for the product, still in the package. Apparently, some leakage is normal upon opening and you are supposed to let it sit on some newspaper until it dries. After doing this, I installed the cartridge with no problems and tested the new ink. The black color was sharp and deep and the printer had no problem recognizing the non-OEM ink. Not only does it work, but the customer service provided is top notch. I would highly recommend this particular ink and E-Z Ink as a whole to anyone looking for a cheap solution to replacement printer ink.

product_title: Canon PIXMA MP780 All-In-One Photo Printer
review_headline: Five to six years and still going
review_body: Five to six years and still going.  When we were PC, things were fine, all drivers worked, more or less.  Why does every printer have 3 or so scan programs and NONE work well.  Anyway, printer wakes up to first page really slow, printing is good, pretty quiet, pictures are GREAT.  Printer does EVERYTHING.  Duplex, fax, scan, ADF - NICE, rear feed, etc.      Switched to Mac laptop and wireless N.  Tough since the printer is only USB.  But that's not their fault.     Airport Extreme  has a USB connection that works with printers.  Started with lockups over network,  Half print jobs would stop, and I'd have to delete and rerun them.  Correct print drivers for MAC didn't exist, so I had to use \\"basic\\" drivers.  Oddly enough, the last couple years, print drivers keep getting updates and better.  Thanks, Apple?    Now things are pretty good.  Functionality is plenty adequate.  You do need to USB connect for some maintenance features and scanning.  I feel like I'd like to get a new printer with wireless and ethernet for better functionality.  But between the better drivers from Apple and the printer runs fine, so why bother?  Every time I find a printer I like, half the user reviews are terrible anyway.      Never had \\"won't turn on\\" problems.  But then you're NOT supposed to turn it off anyway.      I'm surprised how many people have had this printer for only a few years,  did they sell this printer THAT long?  Probably were better options YEARS ago.

product_title: HP Officejet Pro 8500A Plus Wireless e-All-in-One (CM756A#B1H)
review_body: I am somewhat perplexed by the large number of negative reviews for this HP All-In-One Printer. After having owned an older HP C7100 for nearly five years and giving me great reliability and service, when it came time to update I did not hesitate in purchasing another HP Printer. This Officejet model is a premium high end AIO Printer with perhaps only the Canon MG8120 having simlar features. Although the Canon has received excellent reviews, it is more of a photo printing unit than the HP. For home or small office users printing a large volume of text documents,the HP with its larger paper cartridge and automatic document feeder is more robust.     Setting up the 8500A Plus was a breeze with the initial loading of printheads and ink catridges taking only about 15 minutes out of the box. The Printer sprang to ife upon powering it up with test printing and alignment working flawlessly. Loading the Windows 7 drivers from the CD-ROM was again extremely easy and took about 5 minutes. I ran into one small problem with setting up the wireless network for my home office latops but that was quickly rectified by making a call to HP Support.       Thus far I am extremely happy with the 8500A Plus. Printing speeds in black and white and color are well above average for an inkjet although not as fast as a laser. Print quality seems very good with nice bold black texts. The copier/scanning functions also work very well with excellent speeds and print quality. Printing costs as advertised by HP for this Printer should be very low though I have not verified this as yet.     In summary , the HP Officejet Pro 8500A Plus seems to be an excellent AIO Printer that will handle all office tasks with ease while giving you some very nice features for the price.

product_title: AT&T 4-Line Expandable Corded Phone System with Speakerphone
review_body: Updated 4/23/11  Further to the comments below. In our own AT&T 1070 vs. the Panasonic KX-TS4200B bake-off, we ultimately went with the AT&T 1070.  But for intercom speaker/line quality issues, both phones have this problem, which since the intercom works using radio frequencies, is typically caused by outside interference. So in addition to my earlier comments below,  2 recommendations for isolating the cause:  1. Make sure your cell phone is typically not placed on your desk right beside the phone  2. Check out this link to track down interference problems - especially making sure your power adapter is plugged into the wall and not into a power board:  [...]  There have been several similar reviews on this phone, which I would echo, for intercom users only.  From our experience, having tested both AT&T and Panasonic 4 line phones, we have found that both phones have similar issues, with Panasonic being the better of the two.  Some contributors here reported the AT&T speakers failing after a few days, others two out of three were bad, etc.  Here is our experience    We first owned AT&T's older 974 phones for several years.  Eventually after several years, they failed, not on telephone calls but on intercom calls.  A loud, unacceptable screech developed.  So we purchased two 1070's and found that while the loud screech problem was gone, on one phone the speaker on intercom was unintelligible.  Swapped phone positions, the problem traveled with the phone.  Ordered a 3rd phone.  Same problem to a lesser degree.  Returned all three and purchased 2 Panasonic KX-TS4200's.      We purchased the Panasonics knowing from the AMZN review board that there was going to be delay in the phone recognizing key presses.  Some users couldn't stand it.  Others could.  We found same, although with a medium-paced, deliberate dial, it was fine.  However, in the end, we concluded we could live with it either.  But the speaker problem on intercom calls re-emerged, to a lesser, but still not good, level.      The AT&T and Panasonic techs won't help you on this.  They will just tell you to try doing a hard reset of the phone. But I think we may have fixed it, or at least alleviated it on the Panasonics.  The solution, we think, no matter which phone you buy, is to try configuring non-adjacent extension numbers, which are presumably working on just different frequencies and possibly interfering with each other.  For example, rather than setting up Ext 11, 12, 13 and 14, try 12, 16, 20 and 24.  Can't guarantee it will help, but try it.    Of course if you are not an intercom user, or even if you are and don't mind connecting by intercom with either the handset or the earphone, either the AT&T or Panasonic are great phones.  But I do believe, with AT&T, there is a higher risk of the intercom speaker system eventually failing - just based on our own 974/1070 experience, plus the reviews on this board.  AT&T needs more robust electronics here, and you may have to return a phone, or two, or three to get one that works.  Once you do get it right - great system.

The CardIris and ScanSnap software work very well. My problem is with the included Acrobat 8 Pro software - BEWARE this software does not work with Mac OS X 10.6 or higher. When I called Adobe they were no help telling me I had to purchase another, more up to date version. I was under a time constraint to get this scanning done so I paid up for the new Acrobat rather than jump through the hoops involved with tracking down the vendor. Point is, rather than getting a scanner for about $400, it actually cost closer to $600. There should be a disclaimer stating that not all software will work with newer Mac Operating Systems.

Lastly, I didn't mind this fact but you should know this is not a plug and play scanner. It is necessary to use the software included in the package - you cannot simply download fujitsu drivers from the internet.

If you are relying on being able to use Acrobat 8 Pro do not purchase this scanner. If that software is not important I would highly recommend the scanner and the non-Adobe products mentioned above.

product_title: Fujitsu ScanSnap S1500 Instant PDF Sheet-Fed Scanner for PC
review_body: I have had the ScanSnap S1500 for about a month, and am very impressed. I am using it in an effort to reduce the clutter on, in, and around my desk at home. It performs admirably in this function. I debated, and read reviews in several places, before settling on this scanner, without the more expensive software package. So far no regrets.    Best feature: Speed. Incredibly fast - scans both sides of a page in about 1.5 seconds. So that big stack of bills, statements, etc., disappears quickly. Paper handling overall, though not flawless, is excellent.    Second best feature: Automatically arranges scanned pages with correct orientation, seemingly every time! Impressive.    Third best feature: Compact. Takes up relatively little desk space.    Worst feature: The software takes a little while to learn, e.g., where things are in the menus, etc. Still haven't figured out exactly how to merge documents, though it apparently can be done within the full version of Acrobat. Seems like it should be easier. Still, for my purposes, the filing system is straightforward, and allows me to sort things into appropriate \\"filing cabinets.\\" I'm hopeful that over time, I'll have an easier time searching my hard drive than a real filing cabinet.    Second worst feature: The time it takes to convert pdf's to searchable pdf's. Considering that I'm doing this on a quad-core CPU with 8GB of RAM, it seems rather slow. Still, searchable files are a plus. Just have to leave the computer on at night to plug away at this task.    Overall, though it's bit pricey compared to my all-in-one printer/scanner HP, it's speed and convenience make it a winner.

product_title: HP Officejet 6000 Color Inkjet Printer (CB051A#B1H)
review_headline: A Great Buy for the money
review_body: Dear Folks,  Before I start to review this product, HP 6000 Officejet Printer, I better explain that I am a color photograph printing nut.  I use color management profiles and super duper Epson paper, and  Epson high quality Stylus printers.  So I can judge print quality!!  In this case I am judging quality vs. price.  The price of this printer belies the quality of the prints. Do not be afraid of the quality. I printed some 8 x 10 glossy prints, and although not in the Epson league, are acceptable, based on the price.    Now let's get to the bad side.  I am used to installing Epson printers so I didn't expect to need the GEICO psychiatrist with the tissues.  I like to have my printers running through a simple router (wired) network. This one has the absolute dumbest software I have ever seen.  I have W7 64 bit, and the wife's is W7 32bit. No problem. The second disk in the box had drivers for both systems.  Here's the problem I ran across. Maybe this will prevent you calling the GEICO psychiatrist.  I could not network the printer because the software (Downloaded latest from HP site version 14.0) offered me a choice: wireless network, or Ethernet network. Mine is a hard wired through the router network.  I did all the ADD printer, is this a network printer stuff. (Not my first time networking a simple printer.)    After many hours of detective work, I was sure the problem was the driver... it didn't fully install into my computer. My wife's computer was printing but that was USB wired to the printer.   I have at least 9 Epson drivers in my computer which I use to trouble shoot printing questions for people that use QIMAGE to make their quality prints. I never had problems installing drivers.... until now.  As a last resort, I hard wired my computer to the USB port on the printer, and the driver completed the installation into my computer.   I removed the USB cable, and now the printer will print through the network from my computer.    So what I learned is that HPdoes not allow a driver installation unless it \\"sees\\" the printer.    Part ll.    Again based on the price of the printer:  Text is excellent, Ink is reasonable. (I am a confirmed user of Factory Ink.)  Now just to test the photo print quality, I set up my prints in QIMAGE, set the HP driver to as much quality as possible, and made some glooy 8 x 10s.  For the price of the printer, quite acceptable.    Why did I buy HP instead of another Epson?  Good question.  My wife has the printer on a shelf with little head room. Only HP feeds the paper from a flat front feed. The rest, Canon Epson,,, stack the paper vertically, standing up and out of the top.    Don't be afraid of this product. You get more than your money's worth.  Thank you for reading my comments.    Oh yes, forgot. Amazon's service and timely shipping was excellent!  Sincerely,  Fred Auerbach

product_title: Pilot FriXion Light Erasable Highlighters, Chisel Point, Assorted Colors, Box of Six 3-Packs, 18 Pens total (FXLC3001)
review_body: I was so glad to have found these during my last semester of grad school!! I am a chronic highlighter (worksheets, readings, notes, etc) and usually found that I would highlight too much information for the marks to be valuable.  These highlighters saved me! I was able to remove the marks I didn't need- because a concept was illustrated in a better way later in the reading... because I highlighted to the end of a line when the statement ended partway through.  Only a few times did I notice that smudges remained, and those times I simply erased too soon and didn't give the ink time to dry.    I also work in a tutoring center and was able to astonish the students I work with as well as helping them with issues in math work or papers.  I highlight the areas they needed to review, they look for the mistake and correct it, then I erase the marks and leave their corrected work unaltered.      I will always keep one of these highlighters and one of the Frixion gel pens with my calendar planner.  I hate the way pencil looks and the smudges and the carbon-paper-like transfers, but the world changes way too much for the permanence of ink.  I look forward to seeing how the two work together- whether the highlighter will smudge the pen much, how the whole mess erases and so on.      I never thought about the marks disappearing in a hot car, but it is worth it to pass on this tip from another review... put it in the freezer and the marks will come back, just like magic!

product_title: Pentel Arts Aquash Water Brush Fine Point Tip
review_body: I've been using water brushes with pan watercolors as my travel kit, and I keep returning to this brush, it's my favorite. It's the easiest to fill with water, it doesn't leak in my bag, and the bristles are surprisingly durable and they maintain their point nicely despite the fact that I really grind this thing into the hard, dry watercolor paint. In fact, water brushes do a better job of softening up the dry paints and they're cheaper to replace than sable brushes. The previous reviewer was unhappy about how much water is released when you squeeze the brush, but all water brushes are like that and you quickly learn to mix your paints a little more concentrated to compensate for that. You can make a perfect little travel kit with a mechanical pencil (never needs sharpening), a water brush, a set of pan watercolors or water-soluble pencils, and a small sketchbook or 4x6\\" watercolor postcards, and just keep it in your bag!

product_title: Lapinator - Blocks the heat & keeps your notebook cooler!
review_body: I did a lot of research before buying this product and compared it to a lot of different brands.  I've had my lapinator for about a year now and really love it.      My mom bought a lapinator plus for her Dell laptop so she could use it in the car.  She raved about how comfortable it was and how easy to transport.  I decided to try one for my HP which vents on the bottom.  Because my battery is in the back and tilts my computer forward, I put the adhesive bumpers in the front to allow air to circulate underneath.      I like that the computer sits securely on my lap.  It doesn't slide when I'm working on the couch or in the car.  I use it on the table as well and it's nice that I can slide it without scratching my wood table, unlike the hard plastic models.  I've had no issue with feeling any heat through the lapinator and the surface under the computer always feels cool to the touch.  My computer is often on for over 12 hours at a time.    When my husband's cooling mat (a hard plastic product with a fan) stopped working, I suggested he try a lapinator plus.  He has a Toshiba that is a bit wider than mine and vents on the side.  It does put out quite a bit of heat.  He hasn't used the adhesive bumpers and the mat has worked perfectly for him as well.      Incidentally, when I ordered my lapinator last year, the bumpers were missing from the package.  Amazon wanted me to send the whole product back just to send out a new one that included a small bag with the adhesive bumpers.  I called the lapinator company directly expecting to speak with a customer service rep.  The gentleman who invented the product answered and was so nice.  He sent me a package of bumpers right away without hassle.    I've not used the additional mouse pad, so I can't comment on that.  But, I wouldn't hesitate to recommend the lapinator.  It's been well worth the $25 I paid!

product_title: HP 02 Magenta Original Ink Cartridge
review_body: First off - I swore off (and at!) HP printers back during the Windows 98 to Windows XP SP1 days.  Their print heads would fail early and they did not have multi-cartridge units like those today that take the Vivera 02 ink cartridges.  I gave them a 2nd chance with their HP Photosmart C6180 all-in-one unit.  It has been a great experience for the price.    The only ink cartridges I will use at this point are OEM since my experience with refurbs has shown that quality, yield and performance are poor with the replicas.  Check out the marketing videos that HP has put together with/for Amazon about ink cartridges - most if not all of it is very accurate.  The Vivera ink is awesome both for its visual quality, longevity and overall pricing.  However - the marketing for the Vivera 02 cartridges by HP is terrible - and the pricing for the higher volume XL cartridges is wrong.    It is very confusing to find a clear online store-front that explains the difference between the newer XL Vivera 02 cartridges and the original regular cartridges.  When I search for HP 02 ink cartridges I should get all results for both the original lower volume cartridge and the XL higher volume cartride - but the results are varied and you end up searching on HP 02XL, etc.    The XL packaging says that it yields 50% more pages.  If you search the HP website you can eventually discover the exact volume of each cartridge.  Printer manufacturers should be required to market both their cartridges yield and volume.  However the Amazon listings do not always show the details.  XL cartridges only come in black, magenta, cyan and yellow - there are no XL light cyan or light magenta cartridges mysteriously.  XL packaging only comes with a twin pack for the black and a single pack for each color.  Finally, unless I failed math the pricing for ANY XL cartridge is expensive.    As of today, April 8th, 2011 -  Unless I failed arithmetic you are getting a better value by not buying the XL cartridges unless youfind a better price than shown below:    Get a HP 02 black 'reg' cartridge 2pk for $30.98 with free shipping.  That equates to $15.49 per cartridge.  The XL black 2pk is $55.98 which is $27.64 each.  However using the 50% more for an XL cart yield, you would pay $23.24 for one and a half regular black cartridges.  So in effect you are paying over $4.50 more for the convenience of the XL cart!    Similarly, the 5pk combo color package of the regular volume cartridges is $40.57 which is about $8.11 for each cartridge.  The XL color 1pk (only packaging of XL color available now) is $14.99. Using the 50% more for an XL cart yield, you would pay $12.17 for a one and a half regular color cartridge.  So in effect you are paying over $2.70 more for the convenience of the XL cart!

product_title: Post-it Super Sticky Removable Label Roll, 1 X 700
review_headline: They're labels...that you use like tape. Good product.
review_body:
Think of the Post-it Super Sticky Removeable Label roll as one of those odd, middle-of-the-road kind of products that at first you're not sure how it's supposed to be used. That's actually a good thing, because once you start using it, you realize that there are a ton of uses. I've used them to label food in plastic containers in the fridge, on computers, to mark something in a book, to leave myself a note on the computer monitor, to leave someone else a note on a package, to put a quick note on a stack of papers, etc. Basically, if something needs to be labelled with a quick note or other blurb of information, you can use this to do it.

The labels themself come on a roll and you basically use it like a roll of tape. Pull the length of product you want to use, then rip it off on the serrated cutting edge. That's really about it. There are no set label lengths and using it is no harder than using a roll of tape. The labels are very sticky and stay on, but when it's time to remove them, doing so is very easy, without any kind of residue. They'll also stick to just about any clean surface. It's great for any quick, impromptu labelling instance that could come up.

If there is any con to this product, it's that the way the serrated egde cuts them leaves them looking jagged. While this isn't a big deal when it comes to the way this product is likely to be used, it does kind of limit it if you're wanting something clean or professional-looking (which isn't really happening here anyways since there's no way to print on it). That's a minor quibble (almost have to be looking for something to dislike to cite that). This is a product with a wide application of uses, and good to have around when a situation calls for it. You might initially think that it's a limited product, but once you start using it you realize just how flexible a product it is by how many different ways you'll actually make use of it. The Removeable Label Roll really is a nice product, once you give it a chance.a chance.

product_title: IntelliScanner Comic Edition
review_headline: A great deal of false advertising....
review_body: I bought this product with the assumption that the scanner would would allow me to scan my comics into their database software, creating an inventory of my collection. I could not be farther from the truth. Looking at their site, one would think that the scanner actually enters some information into the software: wrong. When you wish to enter a comic into the program, first you click the \\"add series\\" button, and type the name of the series. Not scan the barcode of the comic: manually type the name of the comic. Then you parse through a list of possible names (depending on title: x-men and star wars bringing up huge lists, for example) to find the one you wanted. Chose the target. The you click \\"add issues.\\" Manually type in a range of issues. 1-10, 15, 16-35 for example. Still, no scanning. You see, the scanner is ONLY USED when you create custom barcodes with the program and print them yourself. If you're like me and looking for software that can handle having barcodes scanned into it, then try the Comic edition over at Collectorz.com. Steer clear of this. And as for the excuse I've heard bantered about that comics aren't meant to be scanned, my personal Uncanny X-men collection which starts at issue 101 has unique bar codes. That's 36 years of unique barcodes (and it took some serious boredom to scan through a stack of them looking at those numbers and comparing, but oh well). I've found a few oddballs in my collection without barcodes, but out of 13 long boxes, I estimate well over 90% to have barcodes. As attractive a presentation as this product has, I really wish it had the functionality to claims to have as well.

The phone will start to ring, then the display will say \\"searching...\\" and the answering machine will kick in before it ever \\"finds\\" what it's looking for. Or for fun, sometimes it will drop a call for no reason and you'll find yourself staring at the \\"Handset 1\\" (or 2) screen. Proximity to the base has no apparent connection because it does this to me while I'm in the kitchen with the base a foot away.     It's so ridiculous, that when my friends call and it acts up, I just call them back and they'll say \\"your phone again?\\". Not a high recommendation.     I'm not a super temperamental person, but I've literally thrown this thing at the floor. I guess I can say that it withstands violence!     Oh and the battery life is sub-par. It will beep with increasing frequency and you're forced to find the other handset, which will do the same thing not too much later.     Do yourself a favor and buy a V-tech. product_title: HP Officejet Pro 8000 Wireless Printer
review_headline: Unreliable -- the last HP Printer I'll buy
review_body:
The features of the HP Officejet Pro 8000 are good and so is the print quality -- if and when the printer actually works, that is. This is the most unreliable piece of {bleep} I have ever had the displeasure of using as a printer. I have had HP printers since my first HP DeskJet 500 (purchased in 1995 or 1996 if I remember right) and have become less and less satisfied from printer to printer. Between home and work place I have owned/used more than a dozen different HP printers, both InkJet and Laser. The best one of them is the Color LaserJet 3800 PCL6, but the Officejet Pro 8000 is a new low point and my last HP printer. It is unreliable, jams often, uses too much ink and has a serious paper feed problem. Seemingly independent of the paper I use the printer fails to draw in the next sheet every five to ten pages. Pushing the \\"feed\\" button resolves the problem in 90% of the cases, but it means I have to sit next to the printer and baby it when printing. That results in a productivity problem, because I cannot submit a print job and do something else while the document is printing.

I give this printer two stars instead of only one because the print quality is good and the features are very nice, especially for the price. The reliability, however, is poor and I would neither recommend this printer to anybody nor would I buy it again.

I told the tech support guy that I'd take my chances on baking the formatter board in the oven as recommended on the internet.  What do I have to lose?  HP knows of the problem with this product and they fail to stand behind it.  This will probably be my last HP printer purchase. I would definitely stay clear of this model.

product_title: Epson Duet 80-Inch Dual Aspect Ratio Projection Screen
review_headline: Great value screen, but maybe not the best portability choice
review_body: We bought this screen in a hurry, choosing something inexpensive that we thought would fill our need for showing movies in the garage for my son's birthday party. We were pleasantly surprised by its execution. The screen makes a really nice package, if not a little heavy. It's easy to set up, and the components seem to be of good materials and workmanship. I expected something with basic metal legs (perhaps even with some sharp edges), loose and wobbly, but serviceable for our trivial purpose. What I got was a screen with a solid tripod base that opens easily and smoothly. The screen drops onto the tripod simply, and then you pull open the screen to the left and right--it opens like theater curtains--to the width you need. Operation is smooth, the screen area is large, and our images look bright and clear projected on it. Very happy, especially for the price. This screen is an excellent value. When collapsed for storage, the unit easily fits into a corner of any closet, or can even be slid under a bed. My only caution is that the unit is heavy, so if you are looking for something to carry around a lot, this may not be a perfect choice. But if you are looking for something that stores easily, sets up fast, and gives you a big screen that looks good, and you don't want to spend a ton of money, this screen is a great choice.

product_title: LG Mobile HBS-700 Stereo Bluetooth Headset (Neckband Style Headset)
review_headline: Very Good Sound Quality, Ease Of Use, And Comfort
review_body:
The LG HBS-700 is the third Bluetooth stereo headset that I have used (see my reviews of the [[ASIN:B004BN40AS Motorola S10-HD]] and [[ASIN:B0040X33SE Jabra CLIPPER]]). As in my other reviews I will focus on the music experience as I use my Motorola T305 for hands free calling. After pairing this unit with my Droid X, I evaluated it for sound quality, ease of use, and comfort.

Sound Quality: I don't have the strictest standards for music listening, but I haven't had many better listening experiences that I have with the 700. After changing out the earbuds for the larger set to get a good fit, I was ready to go. I can't emphasize enough the importance of getting a good seal between your ear and the earbud for sound quality. I have had this wrong on other earbuds in the past, and the difference in sound quality is night and day. For clarity of playback the only thing that I have gotten better sound from is my Creative Zen X-Fi with the EP-830 earbuds. While the 700 doesn't produce booming base, it is rare that earbuds do. By comparison I think that the 700 has better sound than either the Motorola or Jabra units that I have used.

Ease of Use: This is an area where I think LG has really scored. The 700 has a dedicated on/off switch, and each of its controls does exactly one thing. There are dedicated buttons for play/pause, skip, and reverse for controlling your music player. In addition there are dedicated volume and call buttons too. Once you learn which side the controls are on, it is very easy to control the 700 without being able to see the controls.

Comfort: If you have used earbuds with no issues in the past, you should have every reason to expect the 700 to be of similar comfort. I have listened for an hour and a half without giving any thought to the headset I was using. The unit itself rests like a necklace around your neck. The only potential issue I could see is that people with long hair may find that it gets tangled in the unit. If you are concerned about this, I would recommend checking out this unit in person. As of this writing you can do so at a Sprint store.

The one caution I would issue would be around active use. I don't think the unit is designed to hold up to bouncing around, and it also does seem to be sweat resistant either. I would recommend the Jabra Clipper for active use. However I use the 700 while sitting at my desk at work. It does fine with normal walking around and light activity. I would just refrain from using it during exercise.

Overall: The LG HBS-700 is a very strong offering. It hits the mark on sound quality, ease of use, and comfort. The only downside I see to it is that it was not designed for using during exercise. (Don't want a sore neck from pinning handset to my ear with my shoulder) Thankfully, I can use my cell phone's Bluetooth headset with this phone and the conversation is crystal clear from both the transmit and receive end. Moreover, I can still use my headset with my cell phone (Bluetooth headset feature), so I can operate pretty much \\"hands free\\" all day long. I also like that you can modify ring tones (or turn off) independently for each line AND independently for the base unit and the handset. This is a nice feature for the home office user as I can set it to only ring when my \\"business\\" line is used. I can easily hear the other phones in my home from my home office, but at least the ring is minimized in my home office if I am on a work call and someone calls the my home line. Just a couple of downsides. Working the menus can be a bit complicated; definitely keep the user manual nearby for reference. From the manual, it looks like you can make a conference call with the 2 lines, however it seems like a complicated process. I don't do this often, but I would like it if was an easier function. The main issue I have is the angle of the base unit. Sitting at my desk, it can be a bit challenging to see the base unit screen because of the low/flatter angle. Both the base unit and handset screens light up when a call comes in which helps. But I usually find myself looking at the handset screen to see who is calling. Wish they would have made the base unit screen adjustable or increased the angle/tilt of the base unit. All said, I am very happy with my selection.     Pros:- Excellent Bluetooth connectivity  - Decent handset  - You can modify ring tones independently for each line  - Good looking phone     Cons:    - Viewing angle of base unit screen  - Complicated menus

product_title: HP LaserJet Pro P1606dn Printer - Old Version, (CE749A)
review_headline: Don't Use HP Universal Print Driver (Post Script)
review_body: After a few hours of playing tittly-winks with HP Technical Support, having them go on and on about how I can't use this in a \\"business environment\\" and how \\"it doesn't support printing via ethernet\\" (I really wish I was joking about that one, but the technician actually said that), I was just about to throw my hands up in the air - Until I happened to try the PCL version of the HP Universal Print Driver - And then it started working like a champ!    I generally make a habbit of only using HP Universal Drivers and installing both PCL and PS versions on my Windows 2003 print server so I:      A) Don't have to worry about maintaining individual drivers for all of the HP C/LJ's around my office.    and    B) If someone needs to use PCL or Post Script, each of them are there as seperate printer instances so my users can connect to them any time they need either version.      My issue was when testing to make sure I could print to this device - before maping a user to this printer - I was only testing with the Post Script instance of the printer. I suppose I should also mention that when I told HP I had a print server handling jobs (good practice when you have an office full of printers and prefer keeping your hair on your head rather than between your fingers as you pull them out), and that I had established a DHCP reservation so the printer would obtain IP information dynamically, but always be given the same address - let's just say that drove HP technical support up a wall; almost to the point where they just about put the kibosh on the entire support call. I suppose the kind of training that goes into those that support these is different than those that support, say, LJ 8150s.      The end result was after being told:      A) I had a bad toner cartridge (at which point jumped through the proverbial hoop and went out to buy a spare)    B) There were \\"multiple\\" bad ports on my Extreme Networks Summit X450-48p switch (yeah right, pretty sure I would have noticed that)C) That ethernet printing was either \\"not supported entirely\\" or that at most it was \\"only supported being connected to a home Linksys router\\"    D) Not having enough paper loaded into the device (even when it was full)      We finally came to find that when a print job is sent via the Post Script driver this printer TANKS.    And when I say \\"tanks\\", I mean:    A) Web interface stops working  B) Ping requests time out  C) The NIC completly shuts down (link light drops offline)  D) The printer appears to restart / re-initialize (yellow lights flicker on the top)  E) You have to wait 15-20 seconds for it to come back up    Worse yet, after being sent a job via PS (and it subsequently goes into it's fit of rage), it usually requires a restart to remain stable. I found this out because while testing I had a continuous ping going throughout all of this, and it would randomly time out long after the restart / reinitializing sequence was complete - even when no job was being sent. The only way to get it to remain stable again was to completely shut it off and reboot. WOW - What a joke!      Moral of the story, I'm rating this a 4 because if you don't even think Post Script, it's actually a good light-duty (all I'm planning on using it for) printer that absolutly WILL work in a network environment (in a business or otherwise). Just make sure you don't try to use a Post Script driver, unless you enjoy making your brain hurt watching your printer act a fool for no apparent reason.      PS: I generally NEVER write reviews about things (even though, full disclosure, I read them all the time). That said, the wasted afternoon I spent troubleshooting this was SUCH A PAIN IN THE REAR that I couldn't resist the temptation to share my experiance with those of you wanting to pick this puppy up. Hope it's helpful for you!

Also, the manual is obviously written by someone who does not speak English as a native tongue.  That makes things even more fun.  The instructions are obtuse and unclear and worded quite oddly. product_title: Fujitsu ScanSnap S1500M Instant PDF Sheet-Fed Scanner for the Macintosh
review_body: I bought this scanner hoping that I could scan the thousands of deteriorating photos that my family has lying around. After I figured out how to save to JPG instead of PDF I was scanning ten or more photos per minute. The resulting images look good at scanned size, but definitely aren't able to be scaled to larger sizes. The scan is almost too good for pictures. You can see the texture of the underlying paper that the photo was printed on.    After all is said and done, I will have loads of memories preserved plus copies shared with family and friends, all for around $400 and a few enjoyable evenings flipping through the old albums :)    A few random comments about the scanner:    - It is small, which is nice. I was able to put it in a large backpack and get it on an airplane with me as a carry-on. I did have to take it out to get it under the seat in front of me though. Now, it sits on my desktop next to my monitor.    - If you are scanning photos, be prepared to clean the glass on both sides of the scanner regularly. You can get a $100+ custom kit for this scanner online. So far, I've been okay using a $10 camera lens cleaner that I had already. You'll notice you need to clean the glass when lines start showing up on the pictures you are scanning... check the scanned images regularly. Depending on the type (and dustiness) of the photos you are scanning, you'll get more-or-less photos through before you start to see the lines. I could get 500 or so through between cleanings in most cases. Also, when you do clean, be sure to let the scanner cool off for 15 minutes before cleaning. If you don't wait, you might break the glass and ruin your scanner!    - Of course, the scanner works fine for documents too. I'm experimenting with a paperless office now.    - The scanner has trouble with some types of photos getting jammed in the feeder or tripping up its sensors. Polaroids are so thick the scanner thinks more than one document was scanned and you end up doing a lot ofclicking to force the Polaroids through. Tiny (smaller than wallet) photos just won't feed sometimes. You have to use a feeder sheet for those. Sticky photos stick together of course. The scanner typically detects it and allows you to fix the issue. Still, clicking in software can be annoying. When I have sticky pictures, I tend to feed the photos one at a time instead of loading up the hopper with multiple photos. It requires more attention and a little bit of timing, but still moves quickly.

product_title: Swingline 747 Classic Stapler, 20 Sheets, Black (74701)
review_body: I bought this stapler because it looked to be of solid construction.  It costed more than most staplers, but I wanted a solid stapler that would work the first time every time, and I did not much care that it was uninspiring to look at.      This stapler worked for about 6 months and then broke.  It broke such that you could only staple once.  Then you had to open the staple compartment on top, close it gently so as to not disturb the staples, and then you could staple once more.  The problem, you see, is that the \\"staple guillotine\\" that comes down to separate a staple from its bundle and compress it through your paper and into a fold -- could not automatically position itself above another staple in the staple bundle once it had separated and stapled a first staple.  This constitutes exceptionally poor design, as the ability of the \\"staple guillotine\\" to reposition itself is one of the few key parameters in good stapler design.  In order to fix this stapler, I will need to remove the \\"staple guillotine\\", take it to the machine shop, pay a machinist $30/hr to shave 1 mm off the bottom of the guillotine, and then put it all back together.  The average office mate should not need a machine shop to get stapling potential!      Save your money and look elsewhere.

product_title: Uniden  DECT 6.0 Digital Cordless Phone with Digital Answering System with Two Extra Handsets (DECT2180-3)

product_title: Lexmark X6675 All-in-One Printer

product_title: Canon CLI-8 Ink Tank
review_body: Fine product.  Arrived on time.  I will continue to purchase through Amazon for this product

product_title: Brother MFC-295CN Color Inkjet Multifunction Center for Home/Office
review_body: Since I have 2 other printers; -a Brother Laser MFC 7820, and HP Photosmart Premium All In One Inkjet; both are network connected and am extremely satisfied with both. product_title: HP C1861A Designjet Bright White Inkjet Paper, 4 mil, 36" x 150 ft, White
review_headline: Perfect for color line drawings & throw-away banners
review_body: I use this HP Inkjet paper on my Epson 9900. I needed something that was lightweight but could still hold color without bleeding all over the place; this product filled these need perfectly. I use it primarily to print architectural & engineering line-drawings that require color lines. It's perfect for this because it is weight-wise similar to the 20# bond I use for B/W line drawings, but every line is crisp and clear. Its also very economical compared to some other wide-format media. I also use it for short-term 'throw-away' banners, such as \\"Happy 40th Birthday Bob\\", but it is not limited to just lettering, sometimes I put a photo on it and for the purposes of having the banner for a specific indoor event, the image looks just fine. Since this paper is not very expensive, it is perfect for one-use occasions, as you don't have to throw down a ton of money on a custom banner that you will only use for a few hours. This paper also lays very flat post-print (little to no curling).

product_title: Brother MFC-9840CDW Laser Multifunction Center
review_body: Only had new printer a week because my Canon MP830 AIO bit the dust and was also sick of having to deal with the expense of having to purchase new cartridges due to them drying up (not a problem with the laserjet's toner cartridges). product_title: Panasonic KX-TG6531B DECT 6.0 PLUS Expandable Digital Cordless Answering System
review_headline: Disappointing in comparison to older Panasonic system
review_body: I've been using a Panasonic KX-TG6051M 5.8 GHz answering machine for the last three years, and it has performed excellently.  It doesn't have call blocking, however, and I wanted a system which could block some annoying robo callers.  That's why I purchased a KX-TG6531B DECT system.    I found that the KX-TG6531B doesn't have firmware with the attention to detail that the older phone has, and that it wasn't as mechanically rugged either (lots more plastic and a wobbly base stand, for example).  The audio from the base unit's speaker was also noticeably inferior and was clipped at times, and the synthesized speech used English incorrectly in a couple of places.  In short, the attention to detail that I've come to associate with the Panasonic brand name was missing when this phone was designed.    Still, it'll do what it claims, even if it doesn't do it well.  That's why I gave it a three star rating and am not replacing my older phone with it.  Instead, this phone will be used to block calls only by operating as a wired extension that never answers calls.

product_title: Battery For Uniden BBTY0458001 [Item # CPB035]
review_body: This battery appeared to be exactly what I wanted. It arrived quickly and looked perfect. However, it's already stopped working after only a couple of weeks. So -- can't recommend it.

product_title: Avery Shipping Labels for Laser Printers
review_headline: Nice stickers, work well for my needs.
review_body:
These are nice shipping labels if you do a bunch of shipping from your computer. Each sheet has 10 stickers on it, generally one for \\"From\\", and one from \\"To\\", although you can configure however you want.

Avery's \\"True Block\\" tech is basically a sticker with a solid background, so you could put it on top of an old shipping label on a box you might be re-using, and you can't see the old label. product_title: Brother HL-5370DW Laser Printer
review_headline: Wireless does NOT work on the Mac
review_body: This printer is great in terms of its print quality and basic mechanical operation, if you connect it using USB.    However, it is totally false that this printer can be used wirelessly with a Macintosh.     First of all, the set-up wizard on the HL5300 disc (the install disc that comes with the printer) will not work with Mac OS 10.6. There is a CUPS driver for OS 10.6, but you need to use the install disc to set up the printer for wireless operation. So it is totally impossible to set it up wirelessly unless you have a computer with an older OS.    Even if you have OS 10.4 installed, as I do on another machine, the wireless set-up is excruciatingly painful and --- when all is said and done --- does not even work. There is discussion about this on the Apple boards, and the issue has never been resolved. It is possible that the printer is not compatible with some of the security protocols used by an Airport Extreme Base Station, as many users who experience these problems have that device. If you own a Mac and want a wireless printer, look elsewhere.

product_title: AT&T CL82209 DECT 6.0 Cordless Phone, Black/Silver, 2 Handsets
review_headline: Telephone does not allow automatic redialing & is complete garbage
review_body: I experienced failure with the battery recharging, which has been repeated with all three battery packs that I tried within a month, within a week of purchasing this telephone and AT&T's Philipines-based customer service refused to address the matter properly; further, the AT&T corporate office refused to do anything other than keep sending me back to the Philipines.     On top of this, the caller ID information for both stored and unstored numbers cannot place a \\"1\\" before the area code; this makes the redial feature completely useless. For example a call from \\"212-555-5555\\" will appear in that manner when that person calls you even if it is a stored number that you saved as \\"1-212-555-5555.\\" You will get a recorded message that you must first dial a \\"1\\" if you try to use the redial feature. This requires either writing down or memorizing the number before calling the person back.    I accidentally deleted my call log while trying to fix this and was dismayed that such an accident was incredibly easy to make and nearly impossible to undo once the process began.    \\"Bob,\\" who is a technical services manager in the Philipines, stated that this flaw exists in every AT&T phone but denied that it was a flaw. He kept repeating that that is how the telephone is made and that it works at intended.    I was very pleased with the Panasonic telephone that I used for five years and bought the AT&T one only because of its voice mail notification feature. I have pulled my Panasonic telephone out of the closet and am going to return the AT&T piece of garbage.

product_title: HP Officejet 6500 Wireless All-in-One Inkjet Printer
review_headline: Might be a Deal Breaker for Artists + Designers
review_body: This printer looked to be the answer to all my needs.    I am NOT a techy, but was willing to do a massive learning curve to get what I wanted.  I found it challenging to set up, can't use the fax cause my phone is 3 rooms away, and not thrilled with it's performance on everyday paper. The control thingy is complex, and I haven't tried wireless yet.  But the deal breaker for -me- is it's inability to print large image files on several sheets of paper.    I use my printer mainly to print large template for my artwork.  A typical image will take 12-20 pages, which I then cut and assemble by hand.  Instead, we must use their pre-generated templates, which only allow a maximum of 1 image per page.  According to HP support, they have -NO- printers that can do multi-page images. (I used to have an old hp printer that did this, but apparently they don't make then anymore)    This might be a deal breaker, if you plan to print patterns, designs or templates.  If I keep this printer, I'll have to bring all my images to a copy place, so they can print them out for me;  an expense and time waster I wasn't expecting from an HP product.

product_title: Pilot G-Knock BeGreen Retractable Gel Ink Pens, Fine Point, 3-Pack, Black Ink (31502)
review_headline: Great ecologically friendly alternative for the G-2
review_body: These pens are pretty much exactly the same as the G-2, with a few subtle differences. First off, it's made from over 81% recycled materials, which is great. Second, the grip is extended further than the one on the standard G-2 and doesn't have the texture on the grip. It extends further down to the tip, which I enjoy because I tend to hold my fingers very close to the tip. The clip seems pretty much the same as the standard G-2. It uses the same refills as the G-2 and it's actually less expensive just to buy a new pack of these than to buy refills, but that would defeat the purpose of buying a \\"BeGreen\\" product. :) That said, I would still definitely buy these again if I lose them and they're a great bargain at only $1/pen!    If you're familiar with the G-2 or Dr. Grip Gel, you know exactly what you're getting. Dark, crisp lines and an easy-to-maneuver pen. The only downside to these pens is they seem to run out of ink slightly faster than a standard rollerball pen, but it comes with the benefit of having a darker, juicier line. Highly recommended!

product_title: Sparco 86000 Staple Remover, Color May Vary

Gary Peterson

product_title: HP Photosmart C6380 All-in-One Printer
review_body: I am a college student, and I have to say that this printer caused me exponential amounts of stress.   I bought this printer for its fast print speeds, all the features, and the 5 ink cartridges (and the Office Max guy recommended it). Alright, so it does print fast, when it's awake. HP has integrated this power save thing, which is the worst thing EVER!!!!!!    Example: Printing a document from the computer  Just as a note, printer preparation is where it aligns the ink cartridges or something and makes a whole lot of noise. Oh, and if you try to hit \\"cancel\\" or any other button, the printer complains and tells you to stop pressing buttons during printer preparation.  I hit print from my computer --> printer turns on --> printer preparation --> still printer preparation --> continuing with the printer preparation --> prints document (really fast). Almost impossible to cancel the printing of a document from the printer before at least one whole page is printed (on fast draft, and believe me, I've tried).  Summary: Printing speed = fast. Printer preparation and time to get to the act of printing = painfully slow and aggravating.    Example: Scanning a document from the printer  Lets say I want to scan something. Press power button on printer --> printer preparation --> printer preparation --> --> printer preparation --> Press scan button --> warming up lamp --> warming up lamp --> place document on scanner, select scanning options, and press \\"okay\\" or \\"enter\\" or whatever button it is --> scans the document --> goes to sleep. If you want to scan more than one page, you'll be sitting in front of the printer for a while because the printer turns off after every page, or at least needs to go through printer preparation all over again. It is very frustrating and has resulted in me almost smashing my printer into smithereens.  Summary: Scanning one document = average to a little above average on the effort and headache meter. Scanning more than one page = a horrible and dreadful experience.    Then there's the sheer size of this thing. This is a MASSIVE printer! Especially since the tray that holds your just printed documents, does not fold up. So you have the mass that is the main part of the printer, then this awkward plastic bit hanging out the front.     I liked how you could customize different printing settings, like fast draft and black ink cartridge only (so you don't waste your color ink printing plain text) except you cannot set it as your default. This means you can't just hit the little \\"print\\" button and expect it to print the way you want it, you have to go through the printer settings every time. AWESOME!    The printer is also kinda loud. Everything it does it has to be done as loud as possible.     Ink is cheap and freakishly easy to replace/change though. That's about the only thing this printer has going for it.    I'm not just an HP hater. We have an HP at my house that we've had for almost 5 years now and I love it. It prints when I want it to, not 2 minutes later. It's quite. Scanning multiple pages is easy and not very time consuming. No headache or frustration required.    Basically, this power save thing is the worst thing ever, unless you only use your printer once every other month. Otherwise it's just a HUGE pain to deal with. I rather just turn my printer on and off manually or leave it on.

product_title: Vertical Dual/Two LCD Monitor Stand Free Standing Holds up to 24" Widescreen Displays New
review_headline: Super stable, versatile, easy to use and well priced
review_body: Most of the multi-monitor stands are more expensive, and I was wondering what I would have to sacrifice if I bought this model for $79.90 + shipping.  I called the retailer, [...] and talked to one of their staff.      She was quite knowledgeable, assured me that it's a solid, high-quality piece of equipment, and informed me that there is another mounting option: instead of the weighted base, you can also secure the vertical pole through a drill hole in the desktop, using included hardware.  As it turns out, I don't need that option, but it's good to know.    I unpacked and set up the monitor stand yesterday.  I had it set up in 5 minutes, and had my monitors mounted to it in another 10 minutes.  Very easy!  The adjustable holders are easy to work with, the stand overall is very heavy and stable, and the result is visually impressive.  For a dual-monitor setup with today's wide-screen LCDs, I think vertical mounting, rather than side-by-side, is really the way to go.    One caveat:  The range of positioning is limited as compared to other stands that have articulating arm mounts for each of the monitors.  So, for example, you can't position the two monitors at different depths.  Basically, the adjustments are tilt, swivel and rotation.  Look at the photos and do the math.  This limitation is easily apparent from looking at the description and photos, and the product is still a great bargain, so I'm not knocking a star off for that.  But it would be nice if the company sold an optional holder with an articulating arm.

product_title: AT&T CL82409 DECT 6.0 Cordless Phone, Black/Silver, 4 Handsets
review_body: I really like this phone system. For $77.54, it's a great buy, and I wouldn't hesitate to buy it again. It has everything that I could ask for on a phone -- keypad backlighting, good intercom, good recording system, a wide selection of ringtones, good volume control etc. You can individually select ringtone and volume for each handset.
