While there may be higher end phones on the market, this one meets all our needs and is a very good buy for the money. And yes, it did take a full 16 hours to initially charge up the phones for use, per the documentation.

product_title: Olympus Linear Recorder (LS-11)
review_body: Good-looking style. Easy to handle. Professional grade sound. I'm using it now only to record my own guitar, and harmonica playing. And it's living up to it's claims. Quick response buttons are a plus, as is the easy-to-read screen. Showed it to my guitar teacher, and he proceeded to tell me all this machine could do. More than I could take in at one lesson! Am satisfied with product, and would recommend it. Thank you, Wayne Lambeth.

product_title: 20pack(5k,3c,3m,3y,3lc,3lm) Replacement Epson T048 for Epson Stylus Photo R200 R220 R300 R300m R320 R340 Rx500 Rx600 Rx620 Rx640
review_body: My epson recognized the cartridges fine, but the magenta has never worked and the black has lines and shows up more grey. I can't print anything of importance with this, so it wasn't worth the discount.

product_title: Ampad Evidence Pastels Pads, Legal/Wide Rule, Ltr, 50-Sheet Pads/Pack, Dozen
review_body: This may seem like nothing, just blue pads of paper, but to keep your desk organized these are essential.  With all of the white paper that goes by my desk I needed something that would stand out.  Blue paper does the trick.  I keep this next to my laptop and use it all day long.  Having a pad of paper that isn't white helps me to keep track of it and stay organized.  If I need to rip out pages the blue paper doesn't get lost among the white paper.  Worth a try, right?

product_title: Brother HL-2170W 23ppm Laser Printer with Wireless and Wired Network Interfaces
review_body: We refuse to buy another HP because they will not support our trusty little HP1012 in the new Windows 7 operating environment. So we bought the Brother. My wife wants to wirelessly connect all the computers with this new printer but it's not so simple for the faint of heart (and computer illiterate). After one month, and numerous instruction manual reads, nobody's had the guts to try.  The printer is noisier than our old HP but much faster. It just spits out pages like no tomorrow.  Highly recommended.

product_title: Retractable 1.0mm Ballpoint Pen, Black Ink and Barrel (ZPC24211) Category: Ballpoints
review_body: I received a different pen than advertised.  I received a retractable Zebra pen but it is not the pen they advertise.  It's impossible to tell whether it was an innocent error or they knowingly shipped me the wrong pen hoping that I wouldn't go through the hassle of returning such an inexpensive item.  If the latter is true, then they were right.  I did not return it.  CAVEAT EMPTOR.

product_title: Logitech Wireless Presenter R800 with Laser Pointer Green
review_body: I had been using a notebook mouse with presenter capability and found it frustrating to use. Since receiving this presenter, I have found the freedom to move about my classroom and the green laser is clearly visible even when I am standing almost 30 feet away. I don't know why I did not buy one sooner. There is nothing about this quality product that is lacking.

product_title: Epson WorkForce 610 Wireless Color Inkjet All-in-One Printer (C11CA50201)
review_body: Vertical paper feeder only catches the paper about 60% of the time.  Other times printer gives me a load paper message when the feeder fails to catch it.  I have to move around the paper for the feeder to catch it and sometimes, when it does catch it, feeder just spits it out to the other side without printing.  Every other feature work fine but this particular design kills the deal.  Also, the price for replacement ink cartridges is outrageous, about $56 at the chain office supply store.  Some of the HP cartridges, for example, have less costly alternatives, such as generic brands from the chain office supply store itself.  Epson appears to have a monopoly on this after deal hunting at different stores.    Next time I'll consider the price of replacement ink cartridges and the feeder design to be important factors in getting a printer instead of just looking at the purchase price.

product_title: Clarity Dect 6.0 Cordless Amplified Phone With Clarity Power and Call Waiting Caller ID (50615)
review_headline: Nice big button phone with a few significant flaws
review_body: Got this set for my elderly parents. The setup was a little troublesome due to the lack of good included directions (and I consider myself a techie...) All that was included was a sort-of quick-start guide. A minus, but nothing major. Basic setup was no problem, but the more involved features slowed me down a bit.    The phones themselves feel fairly solid, but a little plastic-y for my taste. Not a big fan of the white coloring--they are a real magnet for dirt and women's makeup. I am forever wiping them down...    In use, I find the set to work pretty well. My mother however, is CONSTANTLY pressing the MENU & CLEAR/MUTE buttons with her cheek by accident, and interrupting her calls. It isn't a problem for me, but a MAJOR issue for her (so much so she wants to replace the phone...) She is also frequently pressing the volume up/down buttons accidentally while holding the phone normally--the volume buttons are located right where the average person grabs the phone. Again, not a problem for me, but a major nuisance for her. I have encouraged her to try using the handset speakerphone to avoid these problems, but she has trouble remembering how to use that feature (despite the relative simplicity for me).    There are also a couple of issues that we found with the answering machine. First, the clarity (ironically...) and volume are lacking (both during local playback and when calling-in to the machine). When the volume is turned up near max (which my mother needs to hear), the sound becomes more distorted and and difficult to hear. I know you can listen to messages via the handsets and employing the BOOST feature, but again, that's a little over my mom's head technologically ;-) Secondly, there is a strange quirk with the recorded machine voice. When you erase a message, the machine says what sounds like \\"Message Eraged\\"--not a dealbreaker, but hard to believe this wasn't caught in the production process.    Overall, this phone/answering machine combo is good, but in need of a bit of improvement. It has some great features, but did not turn out to be the perfect solution I had hoped for for my aging parents. I think more simplicity of use and \\"idiot-proofing\\" would make this a better product for its intended audience.

product_title: AT&T 993 2-Line Phone w/Caller ID Charcoal
review_body: Easy to set up and works very well.  Please read the directions so you can use it to it's full potential.

product_title: Ooma Telo Free Home Phone Service
review_body: Oooma Telo is a great device, works well, and past the initial cost, its practically free. The website for retrieving messages, and setting up calling options is pretty good, but slooow. The customer service (by email) is the slowest I have seen, takes about a month to respond to queries, but luckily my interaction has been minimal. All in all, well worth the money, pays itself in under 6 months. ...

product_title: 32 Oz. Cutter Bug Free Backyard Spray
review_body: The plastic connector kept popping off my hose - I was completely soaked in less that 10 minutes.  I had to keep crimping the hose and re-connecting, only for it to pop out of place again.  When I turned the white dial to the \\"on\\" position, IT kept popping off as well allowing water to jet out everywhere.  water with pesticide.  all over me.  not fun at all.      cheap plastic parts all the way around that fail.  I would never buy this product again

product_title: Avery Dennison Mark III Tagging Gun, 5000 2" Avery Dennison Barb/fasteners and 4 Avery Dennison Replacement Needles
review_body: This was an awesome deal for a tagging gun! I needed one for my clothing company and having the extra needles and barbs will really come in handy! Product works perfectly and shipper sent it out very quickly! Would definitely buy from this seller again!

product_title: VELCRO Brand - ONE-WRAP Cable Management, Thin Self-Gripping Cable Ties: Reusable, Light Duty - 8" x 1/2" Ties, 25 Ct. - Black
review_body: Not the toughest Velcro strips out there, but for light use they're perfect at that price.  Probably best if you're going to leave cords strapped in.

product_title: Replacement Stylus - Sony Clie T & NR Series (3-Pack)
review_headline: Great product for a great price
review_body: I had a difficult time locating these at retail outlets. When I saw these I thought the price was mismarked or else they wouldn't fit. Well, they arrived quickly with free shipping and they fit the silo perfectly. Couldn't ask for more.

product_title: HP 10B Financial Calculator
review_body:
I purchased my first HP 10B when I was in college in 1996 to work towards my degree in finance & economics. The only thing that I have had to do with this unit is to replace the batteries approximately 4-5 times. I use this calculator for everything...cash flows, deciding on mortages & daily household checkbook purposes and it handles everything flawlessly.
I absolutely love the layout of this calculator and especially the feel and position of the buttons. A few years ago I purchased one of the newer versions of the HP 10B and it was the worst $30 I have spent in a while. It felt of poor and cheap construction and it has set untouched,unused for 12 months. I wish HP would go back to the original construction for future customers but for me I hope my original lasts for another 15 years!

product_title: 50mW Green Laser Pointer w/ Silver Body
review_body: More than I expected for 19.99.  With Energizer Lithium AAA I can pop baloons wich I never expected from a laser at this price point.  This laser is no toy for children.  Can be extremely dangerous.

product_title: Alpha Nontoxic Low Dust Chalk, White, 12/Pack QRT314005
review_body: The chalk is adequate, but the shipping failed.  144 pieces of chalk; every single one broken.

product_title: Royal Sovereign Sort 'N Save Manual Coin Sorter, Clear (MS-1)
review_body: I chose this product because people gave it more stars over an electric one and it costs significantly less. I know someone who owns an electric one and he says it always jams up and sometimes has to be dismantled. Yes this one does jam up but not alot and all you have to do is back it up a little then try it again and it works fine, big whoopty do. I tell you one thing it's better than doing it by hand or dumping it in one of those machines that charge you like 10 to 15%. Yea it may have been cheaper to do it that way then buy this but in the long run this was the better deal.   Like somebody else said the nickles and quarters are shorted one coin but I guess I can insert one in the sleeve buy hand. This is a great product and I would recommend it to anyone.

product_title: Avery NoteTabs, 3 x 1.5 Inches, Pastel Blue and Yellow, 36 per pack (16300)
review_headline: Great Alternative to Dedicated Tab Pages
review_body: For my guitar music binder I just threw papers into it, but with some level of inherent grouping. Still, I had to flip through to find each grouping (i.e. genre of music), so these tabs helped a bunch. They stick very strong and aren't too obtrusive at all. I like that I don't have to waste pages in my binder for tabs, I can just use what's already there. I was able to write on them just fine with sharpie, but didn't experiment much with seeing if it removes ink under it if you were to remove them.

product_title: FM Transmitter with integrated Car Charger for the Apple Nano Video Gen 3 - uses Gomadic TipExchange Technology
review_body: I have tried several FM transmitters for the ipod and have until now been disappointed. This Gomatic transmitter works great!!! I have tried it in three different vehicles and it worked every time. I was unhappy at first because the perceived signal to noise was not great. The instructions direct you to set the ipod volume to 50%. At this level, not so good. By turning the ipod volume up to about 80% the improvement in the sound quality is amazing!!!! I am purchasing 2 more of these for my family.

product_title: Faux Giraffe Fur Mouse Pad - By Art Plates
review_body: I love the texture of this mouse pad - it's smoother than I expected.  I want another!  This one is at school, but I need one for at home too!  :o)

product_title: 1 X 3X Full Page Magnifier Fresnel Lens
review_headline: just what it says it is.. good product
review_body: Product arrived in a manila envelope and plastic bag, kinda thought being somewhat breakable it should have had a couple sheets of tage board around it for strength.  Anyway the lens came, was in brand new shap, no cracks, no scratches or dings.  I'm actually using this as a cheap lens for my homebuilt \\"strap it to your tv set\\" video projector.  Worked great and a great lens for the price.

product_title: Canon PIXMA MP560 Wireless Inkjet All-In-One Photo Printer (3747B002)
review_body: I had a HP office jet printer before this and was very unhappy with it. I decided to try this printer. I dont know if my expectations were low (I dont think so). This printer has exceeded all my expectations so far. Photo prints are great. SW is easy and friendly to use. Have had no issues setting it up or using it. I can print from computer, scan to computer, scan to USB, scan from computer, all using wireless.    Have nothing but good things to say about this printer.

product_title: Dome Weekly Bookkeeping Record Book, 11in. x 9in., Brown
review_body: I got the product quickly and for a very good price. I am very pleased with this service.

product_title: Generic Compatible Ink Cartridge Replacement for Brother LC-51 ( Black , 8-Pack )

product_title: Compatible Ink Cartridge Replacement for Kodak 10 (2 Black 2 Color) 4 Pack
review_body: I had purchased this ink because it is less expensive than the Kodak brand ink.  That is a mistake I won't make again.  This ink didn't work right from the start.  It printed like it is running low on ink on the first, second and third try.  There are also times that my EasyShare 5300 doesn't recognize that the ink is installed properly. I then re-installed it, and after that it still does not print a full document or picture with good quality. My printer worked perfectly before I tried it with this ink.

product_title: FDP35419 - Franklin Covey Classic Planner Refill
review_headline: Just like what I would find in the store only  cheaper
review_body: The product was just as described, I ultimately end up using Franklin Planner when I get frustrated with the electronics in my life.

review_body: I understand you cant get everything you want, so its a good enough set of labels.... has just about every spice you could think of in an average kitchen I guess and some blanks for you off the wall spice collectors out there ;)  Fit diagonally on the window of my 2\\" square see through lid tins

product_title: NeatReceipts Mobile Scanner and Digital Filing System
review_body: Works great.  Just what I need to organize my life.  Get rid of all the receipt clutter I tend to keep around the office.  Scan other documents for electronic filing.    Easy software install.  Just put in the CD install, reboot, fill out the serial numbers, and start scanning.    Just feed in the document and hit the button.  Allows for organization of the files via software.

product_title: 3M Adjustable Notebook Riser
review_body: This thing does the job. I was having neck pains, so I went ergonomic on all my laptop needs. I am tall, so I needed one that is adjustable, and this one is great. The one complaint I have is that my laptop is a toshiba, therefore the volume adjustment, headphone/mic input and SD card input are all in the front, which is blocked by the rubber grip. I deal with it by adjusting the volume digitally now, but it would be nice if I had a different type of laptop.

product_title: Pantech Impact P7000 Black Rubber Feel Hard Case Cover w/Belt Clip
review_body: When I got this item it was not as it seem to be. There was no belt clip that came with this item. I was very disappointed and it didn't hold up to its standard. The case broke within a matter of days. Not the greatest item out there.

product_title: Casio fx-115MS PLUS SR Scientific Calculator
review_body: Well I am a big Casio fan, having bought fx's for years, not to mention the 30 year old watch that continues to work perfectly to this day..... however, while it's a nice calculator, I bought it off Amazon because it had base conversions, something we use a lot in programing... imagine my surprise when I discovered that the binary conversion of 512 overflowed the registers. This is a very small number, not even 10 bits worth, which makes it useless  The limitation was in the instructions... but not on the package or Amazon ad. That said, it's a great, easy to use advanced calculator, but it doesn't do me any good in the area I specifically bought it for. Still looking for now. Bound to be a casio somewhere    If you need binary/hex/decimal conversion, look elsewhere.

product_title: Epson Stylus NX515 WiFi Color Inkjet All-in-One Printer (C11CA48231)
review_body: I shopped around for awhile before I purchased the Epson NX515. I bought it to replace a very cheap Lexmark printer. The cost of the ink replacements for the Lexmark was so expensive, almost as much as the printer itself, and the print quality was very poor. I was glad to get rid of it.   The NX515 does everything better than my old Lexmark. It prints amazingly fast, a little noisy, but nothing too bad. I am a grad student and primarily use it to print out my papers, but I was very impressed with the photo quality of this printer, much better than the cost would indicate. The ink colors are seperated which is a must have feature, I no longer have to replace my color inks just because I ran out of blue. Just replace the colors as they run out. The inks overall are about half the price of the Lexmark inks, and seem to last as long. There is even a very great price for replacement inks here at Amazon [[ASIN:B002IE14HY Epson DURABrite Ultra Ink Cartridges (68) - Dual Pack High-Capacity Black (T068120-D2)]].  One 68 Black Ink at my local Wal-mart cost almost the same as this dual pack, and the dual pack on Epson's site is about $10 more, so Amazon is the way to go for the ink.  I was able to get the printer recognized on my wi-fi and lan with out much of a problem. There is one con if you are going to hook up your printer over LAN. There are some functions of the printer that do not work over LAN, such as; can't print to both sides, also information such as ink levels are not displayed on your PC, but they are on the printer. I eventually hooked up by USB because I like those features.  I wish it would have had a better paper loader, at this price it was not expected. Also, the paper exit tray seems very flimsy, especially the little plactic lip, im afraid it will break off when I fold it out and push it in.   Overall a great printer for the price. The NX515 I bought at a tremendous price from Amazon. Even cheaper than it is now. But even at that price it's good. If youwant a decent printer for around 1 Benjamin the NX515 from Epson is definitly a good way to go    Pros  +Great Price  +Very good quality, both for papers and photos  +WI-FI, Ethernet, and USB hook-up  +very fast printing  +Decent ink cost    Cons   -Cheap paper tray  -some functions not included if hooked over a LAN

product_title: OEM BlackBerry Koskin Holster, Black HDW-18193-003
review_body: Just backing up everyone else, because their reviews are the reason I ordered this holster.  It is the original blackberry holster that came in the box with Bold.  Perfect.

product_title: Laptop Table
review_body:
After reading so many great reviews for this table, maybe my expectation were too high. The first table? Was in pieces by the time i received it, but i notified the seller and was sent a better packaged one.

I liked the light feature, though i rarely used it because i didn't use the table for reading or eating in the dark. The mouse area was really nice and i even liked the part where my netbook stood. I was able to stand my netbook as high as i wished, without having it fall on me. The legs height was really perfect for me. I recommend for those who use it on their beds to lower the legs whenever you get down from the bed or trying to find a comfortable position. Otherwise it will send your things flying to the bed or floor.

The novelty of course came to an end just weeks after i bought it. When i lifted the area where i was going to place my netbook cracked almost in half. As a girl, it would have been quite amusing, had i not needed the table at that moment to work on a paper. It was not like i did anything different or used too much force (I have never won any arm-wrestling against another girl).

In the end, if you do not mind that the material may come apart any day you use it, i say go for it. The price is very good and everything else works just fine. I was able to find a better one, so this one was thrown out.

product_title: 4-Pack Set Non-OEM Ink w/ Chip for PGI-5BK CLI-8 Canon Pixma iP3300 iP3500 MP510 MX700
review_body: Says they come with chip,,, not true. Bought all colors for my mx700, finally put two of them in today. No chips. Well guess what, they won't work AT ALL without a chip!!! They come with instructions to remove chip, but they don't say remove from where. I did pry the chip out of the canon cartridge, it works so so. Won't buy again. Amazon should remove these from their list of partners!!

product_title: Royal Sovereign Sort 'N Save Manual Coin Sorter, Clear (MS-1)
review_body: I've tried several inexpensive ($19.99) battery operated sorters available at Wal-Mart and Office Depot.  They do OK but often the coins somehow get routed to the outside of the coin sorter into the sorter mechanism and then a near disassembly is the only way to get the stray coins out.    The Royal Sovereign is hand operated.   As long as you don't turn the crank too fast, coins reliably find their way into the plastic cylinders.  Turning the crank too quickly results in some coins flying over the cylinders into the shield and then down to the table....still not a disaster, not even an inconvenience really.    Not just for home, but also good for a small business like a florist, bicycle shop, etc.    No motors to burn out, no batteries to leak/go dead.    Do suggest letting the coins sort into the naked plastic cylinders and then sliding paper coin tubes into the coin full cylinder rather than trying to use the more rigid heavier paper coin tubes (which are more expensive).   This scenario seems to work better for this machine.    You'll be glad you bought it.

product_title: 6 in 1 Multi-Function Executive Red Laser Pointer Pen LED Light Gift
review_body: I received the pen on time and in perfect condition. And it works as advertise, but  in the end I don't really like the pen. It's too complicated. There is some fumbling around to go from one function to another. It's one of those items that looks good and works in theory.

product_title: Zebra M-301 Stainless Steel Mechanical Pencil, 0.5mm, Black Barrel, 12-Pack (54010)
review_headline: Solidly constructed mechanical pencil, lasts for many years!
review_body: I first stumbled upon the Zebra M-301 mechanical pencil back in 2000, at my local college bookstore, after using and being disappointed by numerous BIC pencils.  I immediately noticed how much more precise my writing became, which was largely due to the extended metal tip of the lead holder.  The narrow width of the barrel was also a factor, as well as the sturdy embossed plastic grip.  I bought a second M-310 soon thereafter and used these pencils for about 4 years.  The only issues I had were that I would feel strained after using the pencil for my 3 hour electromagnetics exams, and how the erasers are tiny.  I have since been using M-301 Ultra pencils for the last 6 or so years (slightly wider, rubber grip), but the Zebra M-301 remains ingrained in my mind as one of the best mechanical pencils of all time.

product_title: Lexmark C540H1CG Return High Capacity Cyan Toner Cartridge
review_body: This Lexmark printer seems to work well.  I have not had to replace the laser cartridge yet which is a good thing

product_title: USB Remote Red Laser Wireless Pointer Media Control PowerPoint Presentation Pointer with with Mouse Function and Laser Pointer and Page Up/down Presentation Function - up to 20m
review_body: Couldn't get it to go back. Had to be too close to the computer for it to work. I liked another brand that I have much better!

product_title: AT&T SL82318 DECT 6.0 Cordless Phone, Silver/Gray, 3 Handsets
review_body: I was pleasantly surprised to see how simple it was to program the new phone - program one, program all.  The longest part was allowing the batteries to fully charge.  The meory feature has enough space to allow not only for family and friends but for businesses.  The speakerphone is amazingly clear for the size of the speaker and people at the other end don't think I'm talking in a barrel.  Best price I've seen for three phonesets although the shipping was a little pricey (14% of the total cost).

product_title: LD Dell Compatible black XG721 (PF030), cyan XG722 (PF029), magenta XG723 (RF013), and yellow XG724 (NF556) laser toner
review_body: Second Black toner purchased from LD for a 3110CN. Both have worked without a problem.  I have ordered color toner from them but have not installed yet.

product_title: MonMount Triple Monitor Articulating Desk Mount Supports Up to 20-Inch Screens
review_body: Fabulous is the word that comes to mind. This stand is much sturdier than it looks & has freed up desktop space for me. Easy to assemble. I had no problem getting my monitors installed.  If you're looking for a stand to handle 3 LCDs then this is the stand for you!  Other stands that I have tried would shake the displays when anything on the desk was disturbed (including typing). This one is solid as a rock!  Great Product!

product_title: Brother MFC-465CN Color Inkjet All-in-One Printer with Networking
review_headline: Good value for features and quality
review_body: I've had this printer for over a year. It works very well. The built-in networking is a big plus. Print speed is what you'd expect for an inkjet.  Print quality is very good. I like having separate color (3) and black cartridges. I've been using non-Brother inks and the quality is still good. The printer is quiet and fits well on the desk in our home office.    I use the copy feature once in a while and it works well. The automatic document feeder is a nice feature.    The scanner works well for documents and photographs. The colors aren't always EXACTLY as the original but that's easily corrected with software. I like the option of being able to set custom scan settings for jobs when I have to scan several similar documents to the same directory. Works great!    I don't have a land line so I don't use the Fax feature and can't say if that works well or not.    One thing that is a minor pain is printing photos. The regular paper has to be removed and then ONE piece of photo paper can be put in to print ONE photo. The photo quality is very good, but it's a pain to feed the paper. I usually opt to send to Walgreens and pay $.14 per print - on photo paper no less.    Overall this is a good printer. I think I paid less than $US 100 for it - a very good value.

product_title: Boise ASPEN Presentation Copy/Laser Paper, 96 Brightness, 24 lb, Letter Size (8.5 x 11), 500 Sheets (BPL-2411RC)
review_body:
Well, i bought two, one for me and one for my dorm mate, we both like how thick it is, really nice feel for when professors or others read it, gives a little something they can't put their finger on but overall better feeling from reading on it; well thats what i think LOL
I really liked it and the value is CRAZY good!
I would recommend a buy

product_title: Seventeen Fleur College Planner, Green (16077)
review_headline: Stylish way to keep super organized!
review_body: I love this product because it takes all the guess work out of keeping on track with the college entrance process.  It's a long journey with a lot to do and remember.  This planner makes it easy to keep all your information in one place from which colleges you are considering to your essays to submit.  The planner is so cute that once in college you will keep it for other needs.

product_title: Fujitsu ScanSnap S1500M Instant PDF Sheet-Fed Scanner for the Macintosh
review_body: Okay...I don't write many reviews, and I would never (usually) spend an obnoxious amount of money for a scanner for home use...but I am striving to be more OCD and track receipts and documents. I scoured the products available for the Mac, and decided I would try this one. I already own a Neat portable scanner that was worked well, but was way too slow. I figured that I'd buy this, and if it was mediocre, I'd return it. I have several Macs and run Snow Leopard.    This is amazing. It is wickedly fast, produces terrific scans (even photos), and has an ease of use that is intuitive. The software is really good (compares favorably to  Neat) and I am able to email, store, or print scans instantly. I am really impressed with this. Flawless on my MBP (2.5 GHz, Snow Leopard), but also terrific on an old Mac Mini running Panther, which I have dedicated to the scanner.     Bottom line: No fear with this baby. Still pangs of guilt over the price, but if I become better organized, it'll be worth it.

product_title: X-Acto The Mini Standup (Sculptura Series) Battery-Operated Pencil Sharpener, Black, 1 Unit (16765)
review_headline: The Sharpener Basically Eats Up My Pencils
review_body: I purchased this sharpener to have a portable sharpener. I liked X-Acto's other sharpener (the Mighty Mite that plugs into the wall here: [[ASIN:B000DT8CJ4 X-Acto 19500 Mighty Mite Electric Pencil Sharpener, Mineral Green, 1 Unit]]). Unfortunately, the Mini Standup sharpener performs the polar-opposite of the Mighty Mite. As others have said, it's basically a motorized $.50 sharpener, and I have horrible luck with those manual sharpeners, it's like every manual one that I've owned eats up my pencils (like this one). It doesn't shave the wood around the lead smoothly, and the lead gets so exposed and breaks if I use it for more than one or two seconds. If I had known this, I would have just brought my Mighty Mite around, even though I have to plug that one in.

product_title: Sophia Global Remanufactured Ink Cartridges for HP 96 and 97 (2 Black, 2 Color)
review_body: I am very pleased with the ink cartridges that I purchased and I will be a return customer!

product_title: Fellowes NEATO CD Labels (Matte, 40-Count)
review_body: I've used literally hundreds of these labels in inkjet printers, and I've never experienced a problem with them.  They are less expensive than the Avery labels, and they do the job just as well(if not better!).  These labels are money well spent!

product_title: Fellowes Microban Split Design Wired Keyboard, Dark Gray (98915)
review_headline: The perfect keyboard - Better than the Microsoft Natural Elite
review_body:
A couple years ago, I'd started to experience some bothersome wrist/lower arm discomfort and figured it was due to repetitive stress from nearly non-stop daily computer use at work, so I purchased this keyboard, along with the [[ASIN:B00004VUGJ Logitech Cordless TrackMan Wheel]] -- which, by the way, is also wonderful but knowing what I know now, I'd have saved the couple bucks & the wasteful batteries and just purchased the wired version [[ASIN:B00005NIMJ Logitech Trackman Wheel Optical (Silver)]] which I later bought for my home office.

This keyboard is absolutely wonderful. It took a few days getting used to the split design but within 1-2 days, my wrist & arm pain had completely vanished. (And now, a \\"normal\\" keyboard feels positively medieval. You don't realize how awkwardly your wrists are positioned on a normal keyboard until you've used one of these ergonomic ones.)

The keys on this 'board have a perfect feel - they're neither too soft/mushy nor too brittle & clackety. As for the extra task buttons along the top (mute, volume, internet, etc), I didn't start using those until maybe the last 6 months but now have been really enjoying their convenience.

Recently, I set up my home office more ergonomically, and couldn't remember exactly which keyboard I used at work. I mistakenly assumed it was the [[ASIN:B002VRFIL6 Microsoft Wired Natural Keyboard Elite Win PS2/USB English North America Black]], so I ordered that from Amazon. It's nice, but not as nice as the Fellowes. The keys don't have as confident a feel - they're too mushy -- and I'm missing those extra buttons that the Fellowes has. The few extra dollars for the Fellowes is very well worth it, if you do a lot of keyboarding.

product_title: Celestron StarHopper 8
review_headline: Great bargain but not a "dream scope"
review_body:
So, the other night I took the telescope out after a yearlong hiatus from stargazing. I saw the Northern Cross (Cygnus) overhead in my light-polluted skies and I thought, hey why not observe the Ring Nebula tonight. After meticulously lining up the 9x50 finderscope, I got the telescope FOV very close to that in the finderscope. Problems I noticed:

1) The mount is stable but the heavy optical tube is NOT. The law of inertia couldn't have applied better in my circumstance. Whenever I, say, moved the optical tube to the right, it would automatically swing back to the left a few inches no matter how gently I moved the tube. Very annoying. Especially considering how hard it is to get an object in the field of view in the first place since the view in the finderscope will never exactly correspond to the view in the telescope

2) Maybe this is just me, but the position I have to assume in order to look through the eyepiece is far from comfortable. I have to get very close to the tube, which is tall enough so that I have to stand up, but short enough to entail hunching my shoulders. Occasionally, I would accidentally bump into the tube and after combining the effects of problem 1), whatever object I'm looking at drifts out of the field of vision (FOV) as the tube moves in an arbitrary direction

3) [Combination of problem 1) ]
High power is near impossible to use effectively, and by high I mean anything over 120-150x. The object drifts out of the FOV in a dozen seconds so I have to continually adjust the telescope to keep the object in the center. However, the mount is recusant in all but the widest telescopic tube movements. It's very hard to gently \\"nudge\\" the tube one direction when the mount automatically adds to or subtracts from your movement.

I found the location of the Ring Nebula with my binoculars in about two seconds. In the 40 minutes I was out, wrestling with my telescope, I had the Ring Nebula in my FOV about 4 different times but was never able to make the change from magnification 50x to 160x. I pretended that I saw the nebula in my telescope under high power. What a view it was.

As for positives, there's too many to list among which are:

1) very cheap price, most aperture for the money
2) relatively portable
3) light bucket
4) 8 inch Dobsonian is the best combination of portability and light-gathering power
5) amazing optics, breathtaking views of large DSOs
6) good 9x50 finderscope, upgrade from stander 6x30
7) easy maintenance
8) stylish decoration in the living room
9) can't emphasize enough the benefit 1), with this scope you can see all the messier objects and many of the NGCs. Views of the planets are also outstanding. Aperture is the thing that makes this scope perhaps more desirable than even one of the uber-expensive apochromatic refractors by Televue. For me anyway.

I would still wholeheartedly recommend this scope to a friend or family member. There's just too many benefits. What else could you buy for this price? product_title: AT&T 32200 DECT 6.0 Cordless Phone, Black/Silver, 2 Handsets
review_headline: The AT&T TL32200 is an excellent phone: lots of features, very good ergonomics, excellent performance.
review_body:
Recently it became time to replace our aging Uniden cordless phone after years of good service, but for which batteries are increasingly hard to find and expensive. We looked at Uniden, AT&T, Panasonic, Motorola, and V-Tech models. We considered only DECT 6.0 units, which operate on a dedicated 1.9 GigaHertz band and offer generally superior performance.

Many units we looked at were eliminated by what we felt were poor handset ergonomics or one or more operating deficiencies. After much online research and reviews, and hands-on inspection, it came down to the Panasonic KX-TG4021N versus the AT&T TL32200, the latter being new on the market in September 2010. Both units are loaded with similar operating features.

Performance of the answering machine part of the system had a lot to do with our choice of the AT&T TL32200. The Panasonic unit has a very small speaker and low audio level making it sound tinny and hard to hear. It has no base display of how many calls have been received. The AT&T unit, on the other hand, has a bright 2-digit LED that blinks when there are messages waiting in queue and displays the number of messages. It can be easily read from across the room. The audio is crisp and at a comfortable level, making it easy to audibly screen incoming calls.

Pros: Handset is very comfortable, has a bright LCD display, and back-lighted key pad. Menus are easy to navigate, and audio level can be easily adjusted in multiple steps from low to almost painfully loud.

Speed dialing for up to 10 numbers. Pauses can be inserted for calls that involve two parts, such as the telephone number itself followed after answer by entry of a PIN number or ID code. In our case this reduced our toll phone card access from four keystrokes to merely one.

Excellent distance from base unit. We tested it at over 200 feet before any breakup at all occurred. Not quite as good on intercom, but still more than adequate.

Very good sound quality on both receive and transmit. Also has built in four-step audio equalizer to allow tailoring of frequency response to personal preference.

Ringers can be adjusted independently on each handset and the base unit in multiple steps from off to very loud. Visual ring indication on handsets as well.

Best-in-class manual. Very clear and complete, total of 84 pages including index. The usual syntax and translation problems are refreshingly absent.

Cons: These are mostly minor quibbles. The Panasonic unit uses two standard AAA NiMH batteries that simply plug in and can be recharged in a fast charger. Replacement is also simple. The AT&T phone also uses two batteries of the same type, but they are soldered together and plastic covered as a single unit with a pendant cable. Not as easy to replace and more expensive. The internal charger takes up to 16 hours to fully charge run-down batteries, although this limitation is shared with other makes of phones as well -- the chargers generally run at a trickle-charge rate to avoid overcharging.

If you use the speakerphone and then then turn it off to revert to the handset earpiece, the audio defaults to a low level rather than remembering where you had it set before. Although you can easily turn it back up, this is somewhat annoying.

Bottom Line: If we were in the equipment review business, which we are not, we would award the TL32200 a definite Editor's Choice. (Originally written Sept 2010.)

Update: May 2013. A few months ago the batteries in both phones began to fail with \\"low battery\\" indication. Not wanting to replace with more Chinese batteries, I looked around and found a 4-pack of Duracell AAA NiMH batteries made in Japan using low self-discharge technology. (These are model DX2400, and the package says \\"Stays recharged for up to one year\\") As a bonus, at 800 MaH they have twice the capacity of the originals, meaning that you can leave the phone off the base much longer. They also are only 1/3 the price of AT&T replacements. There is a catch, however: these are not plug-in replacements. Being a retired engineer and handy with electronics, I stripped off the plastic covering from the old batteries (also AAAs), carefully removed the wiring which is spot-welded to the originals, and soldered it to the new batteries (They are connected in series, and be sure to observe polarity.) I then wrapped the new battery packs with electrical tape and plugged them in. Voila, no more battery problems! They have performed superbly since; never less than full-charge indication, no matter how hard the usage.

Sorry to hear that some other purchasers have had problems. On the very rare occasions that we have had a glitch, unplugging the base for about 30 seconds and replugging has reset everything to normal. Two other households in our family are now using this system as well and have had excellent service.

review_body:
This product is an upgrade from an older OfficeJet all-in-one machine (5610v). It definitely has both pros and cons.

The folks at HP have thought of every detail, right down to the unpacking. The plastic the printer is wrapped in is actually a BAG with handles, so there is no wrestling to get it out of the box. Everything needed to get set up is included in the box, right down to the ink cartridges and telephone cable. Both ink cartridges are the same number (one is then labeled \\"color\\" and the other \\"black-and-white\\"), making it easier to remember which cartridge you need. The machine is fairly compact, the controls are very intuitive, and it was very easy to install (even with an uncooperative computer which, for reasons completely unrelated to the printer, shut down four times during the brief installation process). I was a bit thrown by the fact that there is only one paper tray, rather than separate trays for input and output. It will, apparently, also print \\"borderless,\\" for brochures and such. I have not yet tried this feature.

Unfortunately, not everything about the OfficeJet 4500 is this peachy. The biggest selling point of this machine, for me, was that it can be used wirelessly, which would make it much easier for us to print to it from our two separate computers. I was never able to successfully set up this feature. When the \\"wizard\\" fails to set up the wireless network, there is no other option or information given - no clue as to what went wrong, no alternate method for entering the information, etc. It just doesn't work. This is a bigger problem than one might think, as the included USB cable is rather short. At the moment, I can't print to this printer without putting the printer in my desk chair and hooking it up. (And then I have to unplug it between uses.)

Receiving a fax is unnecessarily difficult, as well, for users without a dedicated fax line. On my old OfficeJet, the fax and my telephone could easily share a line. When I answered the phone and heard fax signals, all I had to do was punch \\"1,2,3,\\" and hang up after I heard the fax machine click on. It never interfered with my regular phone usage, but I didn't have to fuss with controls on the machine to receive a fax, either. I'm not sure why HP couldn't do the same thing with this machine. Installation of the ink cartridges was not intuitive, in my opinion. And the plastic the printer is made of looks chintzy. (It may not be; it just has this look. A more matte plastic would have appeared sturdier.)

product_title: Canon PIXMA MP495 Wireless Inkjet Photo All-In-One (4499B026)
review_body:
The PIXMA MP495 is a fine printer with all-in-one features and WiFi capabilities. The driver and software installation, however, did not go so smoothly (Windows 7 x64). I can't imagine a layman going through the difficulty I went through getting WiFi working with this printer. But once it's configured, it works quite well.

Document Printing:
Funny enough, this is probably the least interesting part of the all-in-one. There's not much that can be said in this category. The MP495 is a very competent document printer with all the features you'd find in any inkjet printer. Paper loads from the back, so it's a bit more intuitive which side of the paper will be printed on, but it also means you need more space heightwise.

Photo Printing:
As a photo printer, the MP495 is both fast and high quality. I found that the supplied 'Photo Paper Plus Glossy II' sample paper outperformed some HP photo paper I had. And the MP495 outperformed another HP photosmart 385 printer I have in both speed and quality. So I am quite pleased with the performance here as I find this to be one of the major draws of this device. Canon claims about 86 photos from one Color ink cartridge. I have not owned the printer long enough to verify the accuracy of their claim.

Scanning:
I don't scan very often, but it's a very useful feature to have when you need it. In a scanner I look for speed, image quality and usable software. I'm quite pleased with the MP495's scanner capabilities. My test involved a sheet from a notepad that had a light gray watermark-like background. The scanner picked it up no problem. From initialization to scan completion took approx. 20 seconds, which I find adequate. There's a scan button on the printer, but pressing it doesn't do anything if the printer is hooked up via WiFi.

WiFi:
One of the main draws of this printer is its wifi capabilities. But since the printer has no controls on the device itself for configuring the connection to your likely secured WiFi access point, it must be configured through software installed on one of the computers on the network. Configuring the WiFi was a bit tricky. After repeated failed attempts, I figured out that the trick is to plug the USB cable (which they call a WiFi configuration cable) in at precicely the right point during setup -- during the detection phase. Plugging it in too soon seems to cause it to fail -- and I waited the first few times too. Regardless, this will no doubt be a hurdle for novices trying to configure this printer. I suggest having a competent computer person around while configuring the WiFi connection on this printer. With that being said, not having to have the printer close enough to my computer for the USB cable to reach is fantastic.

Software:
The software is not very impressive but adequate. There's a utility for managing your scans and OCR text conversion and all that good stuff. Canon boasts an automatic scanning feature that automatically detects the type of document being scanned. I tested it out and it seems to work well as far as being convenient. The software however lacks ability to open the file location in Explorer or even open the file using the default application. So that's quite annoying.
Included with the software is \\"MyPrinter\\" utility that allows you to connect to the printer and configure various options. It seems like nothing more than a shortcut to the printer properties utility included with windows. There's no options for configuring the WiFi connection in this utility. You must use the Setup program to do that -- something I find rather annoying since this is something you should easily be able to access without having to pop in the driver disc or dig up the setup utility.
If you decide to go with the Easy install instead of the custom install, the setup utility will dump some annoying shortcut toolbar application called Menu something or other. I removed it right quick.
There's also something Canon calls \\"Web Print Ex\\" which allows you to change the layout of web pages to print them out better. I didn't test this software out.

Cost:
At around $80, half the cost of this printer is in the ink. On Amazon, the ink for this printer seems to run around $17 for Black and $18 for Color. Canon reveals the following for ink life:
Black Ink Tank Life Black: 220 pages (PG-510), 401 pages (optional PG-512)¹
Black: 2955 photos* (PG-510), 7275 photos* (optional PG-512)²
* Estimated supplemental yield
Colour Ink Tank Life Colour: 244 pages (CL-511), 349 pages (optional CL-513)¹
Colour: 83 photos (CL-511), 122 photos (optional CL-513)²
Note that I found this info on Canon's European site. The actual cartridge models are PG-210 and CL-211.

So even with those numbers, which are probably the upper bound, you're looking at around 19 cents per photo plus cost of paper. While the photo quality is excellent, I've ordered prints online for around 5 cents per photo. So the ink here is certainly expensive.

Conclusion:
Pros
- Wifi
- Quiet and fast scanner
- High quality and fast printing
- Reasonable purchase price
Cons
- Expensive ink
- Clunky software
- Lack of LCD for independent configuration

Rating the device itself on its merits alone, I give it 4 stars. Whether that ink cost is a major deterrent to you is really up to you.g Canon calls \\"Web Print Ex\\" which allows you to change the layout of web pages to print them out better. product_title: Samsung ML-2525W Wireless Mono Laser Printer
review_headline: Easy Wireless hookup on a Mac, and with a PC, but sleeps too often!
review_body:
On any printer, I always download the latest driver from the internet. I don't even bother with the install disk. Although the driver was version 1.0, I had it set up in 5 min with my MacBook Pro, and with my wife's PC laptop, both printing wirelessly. I don't know why people are having such an issue. I had a Samsung ML-2510, which was going to be $70 for a new toner cartridge, and it was $59 for this printer at a local retailer, so the decision was easy. Yes, it comes with a 1000 copy starter cartridge, so if you figure the cartridge is worth about $30, I paid about $30 for the printer, but got a new one with wireless capability.

UPDATE: Downgraded my review because of the famous \\"Wi-Fi sleeping problem\\". Printer works wonderfully except now if it is on for more than 15 minutes the Wi-Fi goes to sleep, and won't \\"wake up\\" unless I turn off the printer, turn it on again, and wait a minute or two until it resets with the Wi-Fi. VERY irritating. I have called Samsung about this, and they act like they have never heard of this problem.
I will say that I am using it on a Mac, and the problem surfaced after an Apple software update on Snow Leopard. Samsung seems to indicate it is Apple's problem, but there have been multiple software updates from Apple since, and I have upgraded to the latest version of Lion, and the problem persists. Samsung, meanwhile, still has the same software version, so the problem is with Samsung. Apple is too good about software fixes, especially considering that their printer drivers are IN their software. I would give this one star, but since it works perfectly with USB, and I love the small footprint and the fact that paper is stored IN the machine, and lots of it, I'll give it 3 stars. I would bump it back to 5 if Samsung would fix the Wi-Fi issue.

Also, my wife has a PC laptop, and the problem with the sleeping affects both Macs and PCs, so the issue is definitely with Samsung.

product_title: HP Officejet 6500 Wireless All-in-One Inkjet Printer
review_headline: Everything I need, for the best price EVER
review_body: I love this printer!  I spent 4-6 weeks shopping around and this specific printer was it!  I didn't want a preppy photo printer that mom's typically use.  You know, the ones with 2 buttons, and come with the glossy special paper.  I wanted an all inclusive office printer that could do everything, something that would be good for a small business.  This is it!    Some of the features I needed:  wireless, good paper capacity, color, cheap ink, scanner, and the multiple page scanner at the top.    When I got the printer, I was surprised by the easy set up.  I thought I needed help from a network genius to have it set up for our wireless network.  It turns out that my basic computer knowledge was just enough.  All I did was plug it in, and install the disk.  The wireless configuration all happened on it's own.  Amazing how two electronics can communicate with each other when they are in separate rooms.    Con:  When I turn off the printer (don't do) you have to re-establish the network.  It was really frustrating to press 1 button and ruin the whole thing for 2 days.  I now know how to re-establish the network, and I always keep the printer on.    Next was the price.  I looked at all the features I needed and went to tiger direct, HP, and newegg to find the right features for the right price.  The result was this office jet 6500.  The printer is normally priced at $200.  Tiger direct will give it to you for $150.  When I called all the places in town for a quote, they told me $200.  Tiger Direct ALMOST won my business until I went to Amazon.com, and found it for $132 with free shipping.  Amazing deal!!!  Big savings!! Should be illegal!! Probably is!!!    Con:  My only problem with the printer has to do with it's speed.  At my work, the printer (a full sized one) sucks in the papers super fast.  A stack of 50 pages will be sucked through in less than a minute.  I was kinda expecting something similar...but my expectations fell quite short.  The printer takes a couple seconds to prepare itself...then it slowly feeds in the paper and carefully scans each detail (scans in color BTW).  The printer thinks for a couple more seconds...and a page slowly prints out with precision.  It is slow as heck compared to the full sized printer at work =\  But, everything else is an A+!  You probably can't find a small printer that sucks in papers at amazing speeds.  Maybe I'm living in a dream world to have expected this.    If you are a small business starting up, this is the PERFECT printer for you.

product_title: Vtech Expandable 4-Handset Cordless Phone with Digital Answering System
review_headline: Pretty Good, Contact Management a little weak.
review_body: Have had these units for a couple of months now and for the most part they work great. They are priced very well for what you get.    Here are the things I like:   1) Sound quality is excellent, no WiFi/Microwave/Keyboard/Mouse interference Yay!   2) Pairs up with 2 iPhones most of the time (95%) without any fiddling. I walk in the house and see my Blue light on as I put my phone in charging station. Once in a while you have to fiddle with iPhone settings to force connect.  3) The convenience of answering my wife's phone, my phone or the house Vonage line anywhere in the house is great. Sometimes there is a lag on answering cell you must get used to. Count to 5 and then say \\"hello\\" after hitting the Cell button to answer a call.  4) You can have two independent calls going at once from two handsets. i.e. Wife can talk to sisters, I can talk to my folks using the Vtech handsets at the same time.  5) Speakerphone works well, sounds good both ways.  6) The Bluetooth contact transfer worked like a charm. To avoid transferring all of your iPhone contacts, setup a contact folder hold the subset of contacts you want to transfer to the phone. You may have to do this from MobileMe, Outlook or the Mac Contact manager. Go into the iPhone Bluetooth setup screen for the VTech device and check off that folder. When you transfer the contacts to the Vtech, you will get only that subset. BTW, you can dial \\"landline\\" calls using this list to avoid having to setup the main directory. It wasn't clear from the manual if you could do that. Search for the contact and hit \\"Home\\" to dial.  7) The caller ID log shows calls missed from either Cell or Landline, a nice touch if you were in the yard and missed hearing the ring.    The only things that prevent this phone system from being perfect:  1) The contacts names are clipped at one line of the display. The display should allow for two lines or have sideways scrolling.  It is hard to distinguish contact \\"David ReallyLongName(mobile)\\" and \\"David ReallyLongName(home)\\". The display will show these as \\"David ReallyLon\\" for both numbers. There are lots of wasted pixels that could have been used to fix this.  2) The Caller ID log does not try to match names to directory numbers. Most cell caller IDs are phone number only so you had to know the name of the number that called you. My 10+ year old Siemens Gigaset did this perfectly. If you had a contact directory entry it would replace \\"Cellular Caller, NY\\" with their directory name. A minor point but I find I miss this feature.  3) It would be great to name the handsets like my old GigaSet. Remembering \\"Handset 4\\" is the basement requires a cheat sheet taped to the phone as someone else remarked.

product_title: HP Officejet Pro 8000 Wireless Printer
review_headline: When it comes to printing...you do not want HP...
review_body: i bought this printer to replace another hp photosmart all-in-one that i owned about a year ago.  the photosmart stopped printing correctly so i replaced it with this one because i could get it on sale.  NEVER again will i go with HP.      i've had problems intermittently with wireless connectivity and \\"paper jams/out of paper\\" (it really isn't jamming or out of paper) errors. both errors were happening a few months after i got it, but seemed to right themselves for a while.    the connectivity seems to be doing fine now, but for a while, every time i would try to print, it would tell me \\"printer busy\\" or \\"error: connection timed out...attempting to reconnect in 30 seconds\\"...it never reconnected on its own. i finally decided to reinstall some drivers and it works fine now....at least the wireless connection.    The reason i am finally done putting up with this thing is because a few weeks ago i was trying to print a report from my mac onto this printer and a few things went wrong:    -the paper's lower margin was continually being cut off, and until i read the reviews (which i should've done before buying) is something i wasn't aware of. it is something HP, and only HP has a problem with.  it will not let you print anything with a margin shorter than nearly a half-inch without cutting off some of it.  that becomes really frustrating, especially when trying to print school reports that require a very low margin.    -(this is THE reason i am done with it.) after printing a few more reports (and just resigning to the fact that the bottom will be cut off) the printer told me there was a paper jam, or it was out of paper. i checked the paper tray and it still had paper. so i took the duplexer off to see where the paper was jammed, and lo and behold, there was no paper jam. i pushed the button to resume printing, the printer made some really weird noises, and the printer gave the same error, only this time it was only saying there was no paper. so i went on hp's websitefor support. it told me to clean the rollers with a damp rag...so i did, still nothing. i downloaded new drivers again and that did nothing. from what ive heard, HP's phone support is no help so i didnt even waste my time. ive tried everything on the website and it still doesnt work even though i have good paper in the tray, still have ink in the cartridges and no jams...it just will not print...it won't even pick up any paper.    There were some pros to this printer:    -when wireless worked, it worked well and did the job    -print quality was average, nothing to write home about, at least when it would print    -print speed was pretty good, when printing wirelessly i could print my document from down the hall, and set my computer down and save the document, by the time i got to the printer, the document was usually just finishing or sitting on the tray completely done.      Other than the major problems i had with the printer as stated above, there were a few other cons:    -extremely loud...the first time i printed wirelessly, i was in another room, and i heard something down the hall and thought someone was breaking into my house through my window....ya, thats how loud it was    -looks like it's hurting itself when it prints, shakes vigorously, probably goes hand-in-hand with the noise.    -it is a huge printer, from front of paper tray to back of attached duplexer, it measures about 19 inches (with the paper tray collapsed). side to side is about 19 inches also. that wouldnt be a big deal if you could put things next to or on top of it. since it shakes so badly, anything will be knocked down.      i am a college student and cant afford to keep throwing my money down on brand new printers just because HP has poor quality control. i will definitely go with another brand, even if that means spending slightly more on ink every once in a while.  at least i won't be feeding money into HP's belly. thank God for the free-market economy.    all that to say, this printer has given me nothing but headaches, and i can say the same about the last one i had. when there is something that needs to be printed for the next day, you do not want to rely on HP.     P.S. -i got my first report printed using my fiance's printer at her house (ironically, she has the same printer as my old one, maybe i got a lemon), and my second using my dad's canon (which worked beautifully).

product_title: HP Officejet Pro 8500 All-in-one Printer
review_body: Bought for a single print user in an office (Windows XP Pro, SP3, wired connection) w/ additional fax/copy volume from other users. Based on other reviews, before installing, I deleted the previous HP Officejet printer, then uninstalled the programs for the previous printer, then removed the folders on the C: drive. I didn't edit the registry. Two minor annoyances: the print cartridges take about 20 minutes (no lie) to install the first time-- it goes through an elaborate alignment process, for each of 4 ink cartridges. To add to that, the initial display that comes on when powered up is in a number of languages other than English, and you can't readily tell what it is wanting you to do. After trial and error, if I hit the arrow key to the right of the \\"ok\\" button on the panel, it then told me to hit \\"11\\" for English. Then I got the instructions on the display in English and everything went fine from there. I reviewed the programs to install (did not take the defaults) as I didn't want a \\"yahoo toolbar\\" or some of the other extras, just a basic install for a basic user. The machine works well, the user loves it. The resolution of the print in \\"draft\\" mode is very good for general business use, using cheap generic copy paper. Quieter and less vibration than all previous Officejets. Pretty big footprint, but not unreasonable for a printer that can handle 15,000 copies a month. We did not get the extra paper tray, but I would if it was networked with multiple print users. Nice PC-screen fax software. Because of my steps to remove the previous printer and the alignment, it took over an hour to do the entire \\"remove/install\\" process. Overall, our best Officejet yet.

With the HP I replaced the cartridges maybe twice a year, with the Artisan I've replaced all the cartridges at least twice and the black at least 4-5 times in the few months I've had it. product_title: uni-ball Vision Rollerball Pens, Fine Point (0.7mm)
review_headline: Best utilitarian ballpoint on the planet...
review_body:
I am a senior in college and take notes a lot! I have been using these pens since junior high and have tried many other pens (from Bic disposables to Cross fountain pens) and these are my personal favorite. The ballpoint is very fine, and the ink will outlast the paper you write it on. As evidence to this, in 6th grade I accidently poked my hand with this pen and it left a black dot underneath the skin in my palm still visible to this day!(my first tattoo...) Since then this pen has LITERALLY become a part of me; this pen really is amazing. I love the look, feel, weight, style, and everything about it.

Some other reviewers mentioned they run out of ink quickly. True the uni-ball vision may seem to run out of ink faster than a cheapo disposable, but this is because the output of ink in this pen is much thicker and consistent than those throwaway barrel pens. For example with a Bic roundstic you can draw a line, then go over that line again and it will get darker. You could even do this a third and maybe fourth time and the line will become increasingly darker (as well as carve a dent into your paper.) Not with this pen. It is as dark as it gets the first time, with a non-forceful contact on the page. Because of its copious flow of ink, there is some occasional smudging, but this does not happen very often and the ink dries very fast.

The pen is well under the $5 range on a per pen basis, but performs comparably to many pens which cost in the $20 and up range, so the price makes a lot of sense in relation to its quality. Plus, if you are doing large amounts of writing or administration work during the day, the small perfections of the uni-ball vision really start to make a HUGE difference. I don't want to keep rambling on about a PEN, but this is a great pen and I highly recommend you try it for yourself; they are delightful to write with.

review_body: We purchased this unit in April, after our previous HP wireless printer had a problem which HP couldn't resolve. It would go 'off line' whenever it wanted.  Curiously, the laptop's relationship with it seemed, mostly, fine.  After a month of trying to figure the thing out, I gave up and contacted HP via phone.  I spent a total of 4 hours, over two days, on the phone with HP while they played with our computers trying to get things to work.  The high-light?  \\"Uh-oh.\\"  That was the indication that the HP-8500 software would have to be removed (which I'd already done in a vain attempt to get the damn thing to work.    Along the way the laptop suddenly 'lost' the HP software.  I don't know what really happened, but there was no little printer icon on the display, but for a second when I tried to print something that, in the end, didn't print.  I reloaded the software and it seemed 'OK'.  Well that's happened, again (makes three times, total).  HP's response?  \\"We request you do xyz.\\"  At this point I've done xyz to the umpteenth power, and I told HP if they want that done they can do it themselves.      Their response,\\"Thank you for your reply. I am glad to assist you.    I appreciate your efforts that you have performed to troubleshoot the issue. I regret to note that the issue remains unresolved even after the recommended steps are performed. I apologize for the inconvenience caused.    Let us reinstall the software which should resolve the issue.    Step 1: Uninstall the software...\\"    We've used HP printers for a long time but, based upon the problems with this piece of junk, and their totally unsatisfactory support, I'll be surprised if our next printer bears the 'HP' logo.

product_title: Brother HL-5370DW Laser Printer
review_headline: Comes with standard toner IN-BOX, not "starter" toner -- Indispensable for Graduate Students; Replaced HL-5140
review_body: I used my Brother HL-5140 all through undergrad and the first year of grad school, and it held up for over five years. It still works, but sometimes has problems with paper jams and the like.    Not only does the 5370DW have wireless capability, it also prints front-to-back duplex, which is a major cost saver if you happen to be a grad student. Before I purchased this through Amazon, I went to Office Depot and looked at the box itself, to make sure the toner was not a \\"starter\\" toner. It's not. The great thing about the Amazon price (around $200 a few weeks ago) is that you are getting a great laser printer AND it comes with the standard (3,000) sheets toner, versus a starter toner. At Office Depot, the 3,000 toner was priced at $67, and the 8,000 at $119. So, really, you are paying +/- $125 for the printer, with free shipping via Amazon. I believe average yield on this printer is a max of 10,000 a month.    Even if you're not a student, Brother makes great printers. I had Lexmark and HP die repeatedly in the past; once I purchased my first Brother, I never looked back.

product_title: HP Photosmart Plus Wireless e-All-in-One Printer (CN216A#B1H)
review_body:
I purchased this printer after looking on the HP website and looking at the numerous applications which were available for the HP e-series printers. What is not being stated is that this printer can only run a small fraction of the total applications available. No maps, no boarding passes, limited news etc.

What makes this worse is that there does not appear to be any easy way to determine if the applications that you want are compatible with the printer you purchased until after you register the printer on HP's web site. In order to do this you must unpack and use the printer - this makes it almost impossible to return if not satisfied.

I fail to see any reason that HP could not make easily available an list of which applications will run on which of their products before purchase. It appears to me that HP is deliberately hiding the poor functionality of their product so that the customer cannot make an informed decision.

To be fair, I did find the setup of this printer (MAC) to be extremely easy even though the manual leaves a lot to be desired. The print quality and speed is acceptable although nothing spectacular. I have tried to use the e-print function and it worked well on the email attachment although the cover page of the email was printed too small to be acceptable. Processing of the email took less than five minutes.

In summary, I would suggest that anyone considering this printer for the applications be very, very careful prior to purchase. Given the situation, I can find very little justification for replacing my previous printer with this model.

product_title: Sharpie Accent Retractable Highlighters, Chisel Tip, Assorted Colors, 8-Count
review_headline: Very Nice New Take On Highlighters
review_body:
I may just have never seen them before, but these are a whole new type of highlighter to me! These highlighters are \\"clicky\\", like BIC pens. The ones I got come in a package of 8 colors, and the package is a plastic pouch, a very nice place to keep them.

These highlighters have fairly small tips, but they do have chisel tips like traditional markers. The chisel tips are just a bit smaller, which has both an up and a down side. Since the tips are smaller, they do a marvelous job of underlining, which a bigger highlighter doesn't do so well. As for highlighting, the line is a bit small (narrow).

These highlighters have something called \\"smear guard\\", and in testing it seemed to work well. I made a note with an ink pen, like a flowing ink pen, not the BIC type, and highlighted it about an hour later. Maybe I waited too long, YMMV, but the ink did not smear at all.

I was concerned when I got these about the highlighter drying out with no traditional cap on it to keep it moist. Like everyone else I suppose, I've picked up a highlighter I haven't used for a while, even with a cap, and found it dried out. Also, my granddaughter is not the best at keeping track of caps and putting them back after she's done. These do have an internal cap. Clicking the highlighter pushes the internal cap out of the way and the chisel tip comes out. Quite ingenious! Looks like they about thought of everything.

These highlighters are a fun new product that you might want to try.

They contain a traditional manuscript alphabet across the top, a left and right hand, and a ruler and a number line across the bottom. product_title: Mustek Scan Express A3 1200 Pro USB Large Format Scanner
review_body: I bought this for archiving magazines and similar items.  For that, the scanner works really well and this is easily the cheapest way to get an A3 scanner.  The next cheapest is ~$500 and then they start at $1000 and go up from there.  So, your choices are basically this one, spend $500 or spend $1000+.    The scan quality is pretty good.  Blacks get a little grayed out but scanning reflective/shiny paper makes capturing blacks difficult.  Colors aren't quite as vibrant on the computer monitor as in the original either.    It also isn't the fastest scanner.  For me, scanning an A3 sized page took about 50 seconds from the time I hit \\"scan\\" to having an image on my computer, so I wouldn't consider this a high throughput machine.    It is also important to remember that this isn't an industrial scanner for a library.  I've beaten the hell out of mine.  It has probably done ~6000 scans and while it still works, there are lots of squeaks and rattles and groans.  But....you don't expect industrial quality items for the price of this scanner.    So....I say this is incredible bang for the buck.  But, it isn't industrial equipment either.  Although at this price you could perhaps just treat it as a disposable since replacing this item might be cheaper than maintaining a more expensive unit.

product_title: Brother Printer HL2270DW Wireless Monochrome Printer
review_body: I bought this from the local Staples because it was in stock and the same price.  But it's a royal pain in the butt to set up for wireless (I highly recommend the USB option) and once it was set up, the duplexer mangled 4 out of every 5 sheets.  The main reason I got this printer was because of the built in duplexer, and so this was really disappointing.  I am going to return it to Staples and perhaps get another one to see if the duplexer was a one-time issue.  But now I'm worried that the duplexer will crap out after my return period ends, which would annoy me no end.

product_title: Canon PIXMA MX860 Wireless All-In-One office Printer
review_body: I have had the MX860  3 months now and used the site to get feedback on it before purchase. It is an improvement from the 530 machine of a few years ago which had a constant \\"ginding\\" sound before each print session which I could never completely resolve. The MX860 set up went easily, although you need to follow the instructions carefully which can be a bit tedious. I did use customer support to figure out a way to use the fax functionality away from a answer phone and found them to be excellent. Printing does not begin instantaneously as other reviewers mentioned, but once the machine is underway it is plenty fast for small/home office needs. I control ink consumption by printing most things on draft, but like all ink-jets the ink seems to run out quickly. The wireless printing functionality has been excellent not only for my notebook, but an away a college kid who showed up needing to print. My only complaint is I wish there was a printed manual provided with the machine in addition to the on line manual. Almost no one it seems provides printed manuals, but I am always impressed when one it there, particularly when a machine is new. Overall I am quite happy with the purchase and would recommend it to others who may find it available much less expensively now that a newer model is available.

product_title: Epson NX300 All-In-One Printer Print/Copy/Scan/Fax (Black)
review_body: I wish they had made clear, before I bought it, that it can't Print To Fax.  Every printer I've ever had has a choice, when you want to print a document, to choose which printer to print to, and the fax is one of the choices.  Windows then pops up with a fax header form that asks you what number to dial.    This doesn't have that.    If you want to send a Word document, you first have to print it out, and then place it on the platen, and manually dial the phone number.    The directions are very complicated to do that, as well.  I hate it.    I even tried to Print to File, which is a way of sending the document to your hard drive, and then trying to use some built-in Windows utilities to fax it, but the Print to File doesn't work, either.  Every printer I've had since 1983 has been able to print to file, but I guess Epson is just convinced that their way to fortune is to make everyone buy their ink and cut down trees!    I wish I had never bought it.    The print quality is OK, but not any better than other printers I've used.    And you CAN use non-Epson ink cartridges
