product_title: HP DesignJet 130nr - printer - color - ink-jet ( C7791D#A2L )
review_body: I bought this printer (used) and even though it was very poorly strapped to a wood pallet for shipping and i feared that its delicate alignments and parts would suffer badly, it actually survived the cross-country trip remarkably well.  A surprisingly robust printer, to be sure.    After using the Designjet 130nr for over a year, here are my observations:    PROS:  - For a printer that gives prints up to 24\\" wide, it's surprisingly compact.  Believe me, there are 24\\" printers out there that are HUGE.  This one I guess you could call a desktop printer, because it will take up an entire desk.  But I have a rolling stand for mine and the printer doesn't seem too big at all.  And although not light, I have picked it up and moved it by myself, but I wouldn't recommend that if you can help it...    - The color, just as I had read in other reviews, is outstanding.  On HP paper, the blacks are deep and solid, which is really necessary to achieve clean contrasts.  Colors are pure and solid as well.  Some say that good color calibration is necessary to get good color, and that may be true generally, but I haven't had to do much of anything to mine.  Maybe lighten or darken the print overall slightly, but that's about it.  No fuss.    - The roll feed is excellent, and a necessity.  As I had read, this printer is indeed a bit cranky about the feeding of single sheets, as they often get pulled in at and angle and jam.  I sometimes print on standard 8 x 10\\" paper and it usually works fine, but not always.  Roll feed has to be done properly, but you get the hang of it and works well +98% of the time.  Also, rolls of paper are MUCH cheaper than an equal amount of single sheets.  Use rolls.    - No real issues here insofar as setting up, getting good color, networking, or troubleshooting.  This printer has given me very few problems that weren't easily taken care of.  Just standard replacement of consumables (inks and printheads, both easily performed).    - Ink seems to last a VERYlong time!  I am still shocked at how long a cartridge of ink lasts, even though most of my prints are 20 - 24\\" wide and usually 30-40\\" long!  Having used Epson printers for many years, I feared how much it would cost to keep feeding this thing ink to make big prints, but it is amazingly frugal with ink, even with high coverage.  I don't know how it does it, but it does!  Because of this, you will not be so afraid to print large and print often, as it won't be as expensive as you thought.    - The printer can sit unused for months, and then still make an excellent print first try without resorting to head/nozzle cleanings, unlike my Epsons.  Epson printheads would clog within a week of non-use and I'd waste buckets of ink just performing lots of cleaning cycles to clear them, but this HP never seems to need cleaning cycles!  It's amazing.  That alone sold me.    - Here is the cool part.  The software/print driver that comes with this printer will enlarge (scale up) prints and artwork to make large prints, and it does an incredible job of enlargement!  I've taken pictures with a 'cheap' 4MP point-and-shoot camera, then produced a large 20x30 print from the digital file, without any other software, and made unbelievable prints!  That's not supposed to be possible with only a 4MP camera to make a good print this size, but the pictures produced by the 130nr printer driver are outstanding!    CONS:  - Paper feeding, as noted, can be a bit of a pain, especially single sheets.  But don't let that scare you off, it is manageable.  Read the instructions, and use care.  Stick with the much cheaper rolls of paper; they load more easily, and will keep your costs down.    - There are small wheels inside the printer that hold the paper as it is fed through, and they sometimes leave slight indentations along photo paper as it feeds through.  This is really not acceptable for a decent printer, but it doesn't always happen (I don't know why), and when it does, the 'tracks' will sometimes disappear over time, or with a bit of work with a small hand roller.  But it is annoying, and shouldn't be necessary.  (My Epson printers made these marks on photo paper as well.)    - The front panel LCD display tells you, roughly, the amount of remaining inks, and the status (good/replace) of the printheads.  However, the display is not always accurate, and I have run out of inks and had an occasional printhead reach the end of its useful life when the panel says everthing is good, so it's a good ideal to keep extras inks and printheads on-hand.  You can have a printout of all the consumables, and it seems best to go by that than rely on the front panel display.    Overall, this is an excellent printer, does what it is supposed to do and does it very, very well, with the exception of the wheel tracks.  This printer is highly recommended.    ---Alex

review_headline: Looking for a document  scanner - get the Fujitsu S300
review_body: Since I didn't want to spend a fortune on a scanner I was debating for months whether to buy this Canon or one of the other models under $100.  But as I mainly wanted it for documents, none of them seemed right. I recently stumbled on the Fujitsu Scansnap S300 - for $260 (there's also a model just for the Mac). Installiion is a snap.  It is not a flatbed, but you can scan up to 12 docs at once, it scans both sides, and takes seconds.  The included Organizer software is really easy to use.  It's well worth the extra $.

product_title: ScanSnap S510M Instant PDF Sheet-Fed Scanner
review_headline: stacks of papers gone in an instant
review_body: I bought this item back in May 08 and have been continuously pleased these last few months.  I've been able to completely digitize all my paperwork within two days (I had alot of paperwork).  After scanning, the document is automatically saved as a PDF file.  I've been able to scan all my magazines and put them in the recycling bin where they belong.

product_title: Moleskine Small Sketch Notebook
review_body: I like the size, hate the price, and love the paper in this sketchbook. I've bought several and really like the small size for it's portability.

product_title: GE - DECT 6.0 - Stainless Steel Finish
review_body: This is a very good phone. It can only do one thing at a time, it CAN\\"T MULTI TASK... So just to say it simply, It can't multi task.

product_title: Rhinolin Writing Surface, 38"x24", Black/Burgundy
review_body: This desk pad is perfect.  I have used the Rhinolin pads for a decade and they are tough, self-healing, promote better handwriting, ease fatigue from extensive hand-writing, and look great.  They are padded lightly on the back to protect the desk surface.  I use a non-toxic cleaner to keep it looking nice (such as Method non-toxic all surface cleaner).  Definitely 5 stars.

product_title: HP LaserJet 1022 Printer (Q5912A#ABA)
review_headline: Very quick and good value - dont' bother with networking tho
review_body: So far I'm loving this printer.  It is very quick and seems great quality.  I've always like the HP brand anyway, and this little printer doesn't disappoint.  I'm waiting on a new print server and hopefully will have it up and running shortly on a wireless connection.  However, in the meantime, printing USB couldn't be any better.    **Well, I'm on the third print server now.  It will NOT work with any of them, despite hours on the phone and hours researching.  Linksys, DLink, and NetGear.  All see the printer as offline or not connected.  HP of course recommends an expensive JetDirect.  I refuse to dump any more money into this and am very disappointed with HP.  I have always been a big cheerleader for them, but this has truly put me off of them for quite awhile.

product_title: Krystal Urinal Screens with Non-Para Cleaner Block, Green Apple Fragrance, 12 Screens/bx
review_body: The cakes do not have the typical bathroom cleaner smell. I did not want that smell for the urinal in our home. The green apple is not supposed to be that fragrant anyway. It does its job of neutralizing urine smell. Good enough for me.

product_title: 4ft Micro Pda Hot Sync Cable for Palm M100/ M105
review_body: If you buy this without having any syncing program, your a fool.  Didnt even fit the darn pda.  Who uses these anyways?

product_title: Cricut Cartridge Paper Doll Dress Up
review_headline: Best Cartridge I've Used Thus Far!
review_body: I LOVE this cartridge!!!!  You can do so, so, so much with it!  My friend actually owns it, but she loaned it to me this past week.  My kids wouldn't let me get my own scrapping done.  One had me print out a princess scene plus a ballerina and the other child made \\"Super Flower Man\\" complete with a super-hero-mobile and an entire dinosaur set complete with a volcano.  I was able (after they went to bed at night) to get a set of pirate motif pieces ready for a layout of their birthday party last year . . . ship, girl & boy pirates, jolly rogers, treasure chests . . . totally awesome!    The one thing that I will say about it is that you must use the manual with this cartridge and follow it very closely or you'll end up cutting out the wrong piece.  It's not difficult, it's just that you have to be very sure which buttons are pushed to get the piece you want.  This cartridge uses a layering technique to create the different characters. product_title: Pucker Up Design VERTICAL CAMERA Original Pearl 8110/ Pearl 8100 Cell Phone Protective Skin Decal Sticker
review_body: I thought this was a hard plastic faceplate. it is just a skin and a poorly done one at that. it doesnt line up perfect and im anal so it didnt work for me

product_title: Brother TN580 High Yield Toner Cartridge - Retail Packaging - Black
review_body: Biggest bang for your buck on the market. I have tried refills before but with awful results. Now I will only purchase original manufacturer, new cartridges. The only 'catch' is that on all the Brother printers I have owned, which is several, they all prematurely signal 'low toner' at somewhere around the halfway point. So, when the printer finally stops printing, I remove the cartridge and rock it back and forth a few times, re-insert it into the printer and it works great for a few more thousand sheets. I use this initial 'low toner' signal as the point to re-order another cartridge and, unless you print over a ream of paper per day, this should be plenty of lead-time. If not for this slightly annoying feature I would have rated this 5 stars.

product_title: HP Deskjet 6940 Color Printer (C8970A#B1H)
review_body: After I leave the 6940 on for a few days all the displays start flickering and the printer locks. What I then have to do is unplug its power cord and plug it back in. It works fine then. What I have done to eliminate this problem is to leave it turned off. If and when I decide to print something it seems to turn on automatically. After I've printed what I want to print I turn it off again. Pretty stupid. I've never had to do this with any other HP printers I've owned. When it prints it does so very nicely. Obviously since all HP printers are essentially throw aways if they don't work properly I'll live with the problem as long as it prints when I need it to.

product_title: Panasonic DECT 6.0-Series 3-Handset Cordless Phone System with Answering System (KX-TG1033S)
review_headline: It's a great phone to have
review_body: I brought this 3 handsets cordless phone around last Christmas.  It work great for all these months and I could walk outside the house during a call still have clear communication.  The weight is light and AAA battery make it flexible to looking for replacement.  Easy menu setup that I still keep the menu booklet with the boxes untouched. product_title: United Facility Supply 1300015 40-Lb. mediumweight 9 dia. brown kraft wrapping paper roll, 18w x 900-ft.

product_title: Page-Up Crystal Pageup ( Translucent Blue )
review_body: I got this because i really need a document holder for when i'm typing this at work and home.  I wanted the holder to be small and not occupy too much space on my desk.  This holder was just perfect.  it can hold atleast 5 sheets of paper.

product_title: Canon Pixma MP210 Photo All-In-One Inkjet Printer (2175B002)
review_headline: HORRIBLE!!  Paper jams and must manually feed!
review_body: We got this printer in a package deal.  We didn't really need it, as we already had a HP printer that worked well.  But for a little extra this was part of the package so we went for it.      The first few printings were ok, but after that I paper started to jam.  I read through the instruction book, looked at online help and still have issues.  They suggest using high quality, 20lb paper to avoid paper jams.  That in itself is kind of frustrating. Sometimes you want to use cheap paper when you're printing something in draft mode.      Even when I use the high quality paper I have to insert each sheet individually or it will jam.  The mechanism that feeds the sheet of paper in is very aggressive and it \\"grabs\\" the paper too quickly.  I have even tried 90lb cardstock and it still does the same thing.    The error codes are frustrating also.  As for the printer cartridges, when the machine says one is empty, it will STOP printing.  We all know that its possible to get a little extra life out of an ink cartridge - even when the printer says it is empty.  But with this printer you can't do that.  Its very frustrating when you have the last page of a draft doc left to print and the machine won't print it until you put in a new cartridge!    The scanner does function well.  I've only had to use it a few times.    Photo quality is poor.

product_title: HP Advanced Photo Paper, Glossy (60 Sheets, 5 x 7 Inch)
review_body: HP advanced photo paper is the paper recommended for my HP B9180 printer. The printer prints beautiful pictures, but I wish the advanced paper was thicker and did not scratch so easy. product_title: Franklin Electronics Holman Bible Dictionary (HBD-1450)
review_body: I found the unit to be not as user friendly as I expected. It's extremely hard to read the screen, even with largest print settings. product_title: Fellowes P-57Cs, 8 Sheet Cross-Cut Shredder 3205701
review_body: I've only the had the shredder for about a month, but so far, it's seems great.  Feels real powerful and sturdy.  I like the fact that it is a regular trash can and shredder in one.

product_title: Plantronics M214C Headset with Adjustable Volume
review_body:
I have been using this headset for almost a year. The first one I bought worked really well, then about 8 months of constant use, the wire broke, right underneath the volume control.

product_title: Post-it Flag Highlighter with 50 Red Flags per Pen PLUS 2 Refills
review_headline: Good in theory, bad in practice
review_body: I am graduate student and do a lot of reading on a daily basis.  I find myself using highlighters and Post-it flags frequently while reading.  So, when I saw this product, I got excited about it and bought a few of them - I needed one in every color, of course :)    Well, I used them for a little more than a month before going back to the \\"old fashioned\\" highliters and flags. Mainly, this was because the highlighter would dry out when I still had plenty of flags leftover.  And, as someone else mentioned already, it is very difficult to replace the flags.  So, I found it irritating to constantly have to yank the flags out and add them to a new highlighter.      Plus, the highlighter tip gets \\"blunt\\" very quickly.  After a few uses, the tip would no longer make sharp highlights and would, instead, make thick highlights.  I'd end up highlighting two lines of an article instead of just the one that I intended to highlight.    For me, this product turned out to be pretty impractical.  Again, I tend to do a lot of highlighting, so that is probably why.  Otherwise, I am sure that it would be great.      All in all, this product is great in theory and pretty cool, too.  But, for me, it is much more practical to just carry around a little case where I keep only my highlighters, pens, and posit-its.    I think that the pen version of this product might be good though...as long as you can replace the ink in the pen, as well as the flags.  Otherwise, the same problems would arise.

product_title: Sony ICDUX70 Digital Voice Recorder MP3 Stereo Recording and Playback
review_body: Downloading the recording files (that already are in MP3 format) is as easy as plugging the device into a usb port and copying them to the c: drive.  They present no difficulty when importing them into iTunes and copying them to an iPod.  I use it to record the lectures of certain professors and the sound quality is top notch.  This recorder WORKS like a charm. If you are looking for a recorder with seamless computer integration...LOOK NO FURTHER, BUY THIS MODEL.

product_title: HP Deskjet F4280 All-in-One Printer (CB656A)
review_body: Easy to use...accurate scanning and minimal driver updates.

product_title: Vtech gz5838 - 5.8 GHz V Mix Cordless Phone w/ Changeable Handset & Base Plates
review_headline: I LOVE THIS PHONE SO MUCH!!!
review_body:
I've had the pleasure of using this phone for a few years now and my husband and I both appreciate it. Because of my clumsiness, we had to replace it about 6 months or so ago (which I loved it so much that we bought another of the same model) and I must say that it went through a lot of abuse before the old one crapped out.

It has 33 ringers to choose from and the polyphonic melody ringtones are the best of any cordless phone I've ever came across. I am especially fond of the polyphonic melody ringers \\"Cannon\\" and \\"Warrior\\", and enjoy changing it to \\"Monster\\" for Halloween and \\"Deck the Halls\\" for Christmas. I absolutely adore polyphonic melody ringers because you don't have the annoyance of the basic ringtones or the hesitation between rings as it continuously plays the music the entire time it's ringing. Everything (Caller ID, Voice Mail, etc.) all work very well on the phone. You can even add numbers to the directory on the phone and set them to have their own distinctive ringtone so you know who's calling when the phone rings.

My only complaint with Vtech as of right now is that this phone isn't being sold in stores as often anymore and it seems they haven't bothered to bring out a newer version of this phone with all the wonderful polyphonic melody ringtones this phone features. My husband and I recently decided to get another phone to use along with this one and we've had an extremely difficult time trying to find one we like the ringtones on as much as this one and have had no luck thus far.

I'd highly recommend this phone to anyone looking for a phone that works great and has WONDERFUL polyphonic melody ringtones. The sound of the phone ringing definitely is not annoying with this phone. I just wish other phones had really good ringers like this does.

product_title: Panasonic TH-50PZ850U 50-inch Viera 1080p Plasma HDTV
review_body:
We spent quite a bit of time doing our research on the 50-inch Plasmas. I looked at almost every brand (Pioneer, Panasonic, Samsung, LG, Sony, etc) The performance and quality of the Pioneer Elites was hard to deny...but the price dictated our decision. Many reviewers (Cnet, independents, etc.) all had a hard time justifying the money as well and recommended this unit. We had a TH-50PZ800U that we lost due to a lightning strike. And when I went out to replace that unit, the 800U and 850U were the same price on Amazon. So it was a no-brainer....

The image quality is the same as the 800U, however the sound is so much better (we do not have any surround system, so this was a plus). The upgraded remote is a plus as well (lighted and runs our DirecTV DVR flawlessly). We currently have HD DirecTV DVR, Sony BD-S550 Blu-Ray, and a Nintendo Wii system hooked up to this TV. No doubt the Blu-Ray player really makes this unit dance and shine! And, the added Viera-cast features are nice also.

There is only one feature of this TV that annoys me and that is when it senses a signal come in on an HDMI port, the TV selects that port as the active input (ie: turn on the Blu-Ray player and it switches to that input). But, given the performance of this TV...we can live with it!

product_title: Panasonic KX-TGA820B DECT 6.0 Cordless Handset for KX-TG8231/8232 Series Telephone Systems
review_headline: Nice looking phone but generic ring tones and screen savers!
review_body: We were very unhappy with this phone. Though the sound was good and we did not get any interference, we did not like the ring tones and felt that the screen savers were generic. For the price - we thought we would have better choices for this. We ended up sending these phones back and purchased phones from Uniden for half the cost. The Uniden phones have better ring tones but no screen saver. I gave it two stars since the sound quality was really good.

product_title: Canon Pixma iP4500 Photo Inkjet Printer (2171B002)
review_body: I bought this printer a little over a month ago to replace an 9 year old HP Deskjet printer. I was really sad to see it go, and wondered if the new, less expensive printers could match up to the performance of the older one. After much research I decided to give the Canon Pixma a try.    Esthetic: The printer is a sleek black and gray design. It is a lot larger than I thought, but my desk is very long, so it doesn't look out of place next to my Sony Vaio LT Desktop. But, if you have a small workspace, this printer may take up too much space.     Ease of Set Up: I ran into a few problems with Vista recognizing this printer at first and had to run set-up a few times before the driver was completely installed.     Performance: This printer is very fast! So fast you would almost think you were giving up performance for efficiency, but that is not the case with this printer. I have used it for basic black text and Internet printing, as well as graphic-heavy school projects and pictures, and it has worked great in both cases.     Overall, I am very happy with my purchase. It is a great machine for home printing projects like basic text, presentations and pictures.

product_title: Moleskine 2009 X-Large Black Soft Cover Weekly Planner + Notebook + Pilot G-2 Retractable Black Gel Ink Rolling Ball Pen

product_title: Max HD-50DFGY Max Flat-Clinch Standard Stapler, 30 Sheet Capacity, Gray
review_body:
I bought this to staple shut cardboard/Mylar coin holders. The flat cinch is essential to allow the coins to stack neatly for storage. A regular stapler will leave the crimped ends of the staple in little humps. These humps 1) take up space and 2) run the risk of rubbing against another coin and damaging it.

A nice bonus is that whatever you staple has a more finished/professional look to it. You don't need to use special or hard-to-find staples either. Any standard staple brand will do. The flat cinch is a function of the stapler, not the staples you put in it.

And, it takes a full strip of staples. I've had other staplers where you have to break the strip in half before putting it in the stapler, not so with this model.

I recommend this stapler to anyone whether you need the flat cinch or not.

product_title: Philips ID9371B/37 Enhanced High DefVoice Digital Cordless Phone with Single Handset
review_body: I just purchased this phone, and it chimes every 30 seconds. product_title: Franklin German - English Dictionary Bookman Cartridge
review_headline: So far, best electronic German-English dictionary
review_body: Whatever the faults of Franklin's German-English pro dictionary, none can be ascribed to the dictionary per se, but rather arise from a few awkward circumstances in the Franklin hardware.  The plug-in dictionary is far superior to the LingvoSoft dictionary, and even to the no-longer available electronic Collins product.  Synonyms are rich, as are numerous useage examples.  The supporting hardware could be improved in a few minor ways, as screen-to-screen navigation can be cumbersome, I personally would like to store more than 40 new words in the learning list, and sometimes a back light would be nice.  Unlike other reviewers, I've had no problems with durability, and I've had to swap out the AAA batteries only once in four months of rather heavy use.  I use rechargeables to reduce costs and environmental impact, and as I prepared myself to move quickly, I did not have a problem with memory loss.  Ironically, the Spanish-English dictionary that is hard wired in the unit is not nearly as complete or satisfying; the German version closely mimics the hardbound collegiate dictionary that might sit on one's bookshelf, whereas the Spanish one comes closer to the lightweight flexibly bound reference you should more sensibly pack for that Barcelona trip.  It's not bad, it just fails to take advantage of the tremendous potential of the electonic format.

product_title: Texas Instruments TI-89 Titanium Graphing Calculator
review_headline: ti89 is an outstanding  piece of geare.But TI-nspire CAS is where education is going.
review_body: The [[ASIN:B000QSX9EK Ti-nspire Cas Graphing Calc]] is the calculator for any serious high school or college student. I will be the only calculator through grad school. I have taught at the High School level for 31 yr. Several system developments have converged on this piece of equipment that have to be understood before you can see the length,depth and breadth of this technology. Ti has put together an integrated class learning environment that projects the learning experience at the individual level while the whole class shares on that level. Geometric shapes can be manipulated on screen while the class views the changes that occur in the related formulas from which they come.Plans can be written, implemented on the calculator and projected onto a screen for all to see. The document concept is so flexible that I can not pursue its potential in this venue. Finally, at the graduate level you can bring a level of accuracy to your work in several number systems,not experienced at the calculator level. You can then handshake with your computer to bring presentation objects into and through your work for clarity. This is especially useful when presenting work that is highly abstract where models and examples can make the research values come alive. At the High School level tests for core subjects IE. Geometry, Algebra , Trig and pre calculus.The sophistication of this training at the High School Level is not lost in the transition to college level work, no matter what the major you pick. The document format system lends itself to open ended applications which can be stored on your computer.  Fred C Wendell

product_title: Royal Cash Register (115CX)
review_body: We are a small family run farm and we go to farmer's markets every weekend plus we open up our farm for visitors and such. We have food items which are a totally different price than our non-food items and now I don't have to go a bunch of extra steps at the end of the day.  I also know what products are selling and making us money and which I can almost cut out or cut back on.  Yeah - pushing the cash drawer to make it pop out can sometimes be a hassle, but one I'm willing to deal with - I found it prints faster with new batteries (which by the way seem to last forever!).  I replace the C batteries 2-3 times PER YEAR and we use the machine every weekend almost.  The smaller batteries which hold the information of the PLU's and such I don't change very often (maybe 1x per year). product_title: Brother HL-2170W 23ppm Laser Printer with Wireless and Wired Network Interfaces
review_body:
Not for old wiring.

I have this printer set up in an apartment that has all lights and all standard electrical outlets on two 15-amp circuit breakers. Running at the same time as a Mac Pro and a 19-inch LCD monitor, the printer makes the lights flicker and briefly trips the UPS battery backup when it first warms up and when it prepares to print. (The printer is not hooked to the UPS, and it's not on the same outlet.)

Obviously, Brother took no consideration of older wiring systems when it designed this laser printer, even though it's supposed to be entry-level. In order to deliver \\"instant-on\\" printing and 23 pages per minute, Brother engineered far too high a power draw for this model. (The Brother HL-5280, which I tried before this, was even worse.) My old HP Laserjet NEVER makes the lights flicker.

I might also mention that the Mac USB printer driver for this model seems to be deficient. A week before I bought this, Apple updated its Leopard operating system to 10.5.5, and apparently the security improvements broke the Brother driver. After hours of frustration, I was able to locate a partial and complicated fix online that at least got it printing. Brother will probably get it fixed entirely before long -- but I don't think it should have happened in the first place.

Other than that, the printer seems OK, though it should come with a printed manual -- not just a printed booklet for quick setup -- and it looks like it will need more maintenance than my old HP.

product_title: HP OfficeJet Pro L7590 All In One Printer
review_headline: L7590, like the printer, hate the install
review_body: I was very excited to get such a good deal on the HP Officeject Pro L7590, $199 at OfficeMax.  I had looked at more than enough reviews to realize that this printer may not be the easiest thing to install.  But, I figured I was up for the challenge.  After all, in my life as an office manager, I've installed at least 10 printers on different computers!    Ugh!  Was I wrong.    Day one:  First, I did exactly what all the reviews said to do.... Ignore the installation CD and go straight to the updated drivers on the HP website.  Well, after installing and reinstalling at least 5 times because it wouldn't recognize my printer (even though it said it was installed!), I thought I would give those wonderful HP technicians a try.  Several times, I told the first tech I spoke with that the printer didn't connect unless I unplugged the USB from the computer and then reconnected.  THEN, and only then, would the installation recognize the device.  Of course, at one point, the technician gave me a long list of things to do and said, \\"You will have to restart your computer and you will lose connection with me.  If you have any other additional problems, here is your trouble ticket number and you can call back.\\"  Famous last words.    So, I did the 4 different things the instructions told me to do and they didn't work.  Surprise.  So, I tried using the installation CD.  This time it worked (though it still did not recognize the device until I unplugged the USB cable from computer).  However, I could not get anything to print.  Now, when I first purchased the printer, the salesperson asked if I had a printer that used a USB cable.  I said `yes' and he said, \\"Okay, then you won't need a new one.\\"  But, because of the way it was acting with connection during installation, I decided to try a new USB anyway.  Voile!  Now I could print... but, I couldn't scan!    Day two: After speaking with 3 more technicians (who, at the end of the conversation said, \\"You will have to restart your computer and you will lose connection with me.  If you have any other additional problems, here is your trouble ticket number and you can call back.\\") who gave me no solution at all, the 4th technician said, \\"Let's try installing the updated driver from the HP website, again.  But, first let's make sure you aren't already currently updated.\\"  So, he asks me to click on a link he provided and then click on the \\"Check if you are up to date\\" link on the page.  I tell him I don't see the link.  He says, \\"It is there.\\"  Well, after 30 minutes of trying to get me to see the link, *I* realize that I am not using Internet Explorer but Mozilla and I cannot view these links with Mozilla.  Hmmmmm, shouldn't the tech have asked, at some time, what browser I was using?  I'm not the tech, he is.  Also, I told the tech I had HP folders/files on both my C and D drive.  He kept trying to delete them in a multitude of ways with no success.  After I disconnected from HP for the last time (\\"You will have to restart your computer and you will lose connection with me.  If you have any other additional problems, here is your trouble ticket number and you can call back.\\") I decided to right click on all the folders/files and delete.    To make a long story even longer, I installed the driver from the HP site and now the printer works perfectly.  All in all, it took 16 hours to install this `puppy' (more than 6 of those hours were wasted talking to HP techs)... which translates to an additional $280 this printer cost me!    The printer is loud and `jerky' but fast.  The print and copy jobs, even in the draft mode, come out looking great.  It seems the ink *is* lasting longer, too.  Blank paper capacity is three times the amount of the 6110xi I previously owned.  Note:  Print heads and ink are separate.  Don't know how long the print heads will last.    Summary: Like the printer, hate the install (which, btw, the actual installation, without problems, takes a loooong time).  Get a new USB anddownload driver from website.  HP techs good for only helping you eliminate the obvious.

product_title: HP Officejet 6310 All-in-One Printer
review_headline: This Time, It's Slick Success.  Maybe Next Time, It'll be Protocol Prime.
review_body:
I can't think of how I could be more pleased with my HP Deskjet J4580. When I bought mine (10/7/08), Amazon was offering it at an awesome special price (with one of those \\"click to see price\\" links) with Super Saver Shipping... Even on the SSS the printer was delivered only 3 days after I ordered it (10/10/08)!

When I clicked to see the price markdown, I was so flabbergasted my first thought was that maybe the low price was because this printer is not \\"wired\\" for wireless, and and/or because it didn't come with the USB cable included (a packing lack which quite a few buyers noted not being pleased with). I decided I didn't need a wireless printer anyway, thinking I might have trouble with installation since I know nothing about wireless protocol (I barely know the word protocol).

(I did buy a wireless mouse and love it! [[ASIN:B0002CPBWI Microsoft Wireless Notebook Optical Mouse 3000 - Slate]])

It appears my instincts were right, at least for me, because I just read some of the reviews for another HP printer, a model number up from mine (J6480 instead of J4580), and it sounds like quite a few people have had trouble getting the drivers to work with wireless protocol. And most of these reviewers were tech savvy ethers beyond me, a person who always thought protocol arrived into reality with my beloved nephew Lonnie, an ex marine who described what protocol means in that branch of the military. They know how to apply that word to its Nth degree. As a clumsy dyslectic, I admire anyone who can shine in any branch of the military.

With my J4580, I easily, quickly, and successfully followed the instructions which came in the box, all the while thanking the other reviewers of that model who reminded purchasers to buy a separate USB cable. I bought the [[ASIN:B00004Z5M1 Belkin Pro Series USB 2.0 Device Cable (USB A/USB B, 10 Feet)]] which I'm absolutely pleased with, and was again helped by the reviews posted on Amazon's buying page.

Everything on the printer works with a slick ease which has me feeling like a sort of semi-pro myself. This is the first time I've had a simple FAX machine which works either separately from or with my PC. With my previous HP (which I also loved and it still works but I wanted to upgrade for speed, capacity, and general purposes), I had tried repeatedly, unsuccessfully (phone bills to prove it), to use FAX programs within my PC, so this new setup is a joy!

Of course wouldn't you know it that I would wait to get this FAX setup about the time I might consider changing to cell phones only, without a land line, which would make this FAX non functional...

OH! So that's why the wireless FAX capacity is becoming the thing now!

Oh well, by the time I get rid of my land line, if I do, maybe the wireless FAX All-in-One machines will have fixed the driver snarls. And maybe I'll know more about wireless protocol by then... if I'm still alive.

For now, I have just what I want, and am thankful for that link on the buying page from the printer I had been looking at to this one I bought. The link said that a newer model was now available. And that newer model (due to the Amazon special price then) was $40 cheaper and several ways better than the older one!

Even at the current discounts available on this printer, which (at the time of my review post) weren't as good as the discount I got, I would purchase this printer again.

Another similar printer, non-wireless, which I would also consider, is the [[ASIN:B000F2KRGK HP Officejet 6310 All-in-One Printer/Fax/Scanner/Copier (Q8061A#ABA)]]

NOTE: I've posted my review on the 6310 model's buying page, as well as on the buying page for the J4580. All things considered, at the time I posted this review I would buy the 6310, since it is now (11/13/08) offered by Amazon on a similar special to the one I got on 10/7/08 on the J4580.

I enjoy shopping on Amazon, cruising for those specials offered regularly. That research takes a bit of time, including reading reviews, but I enjoy that type of browsing, so I'm a satisfied customer every-which-way.

A writer without protocol (living in a town with pity),

review_body:
Updated 12 Aug 08 - I used this scanner for 14 hours one day and it didn't flinch; I was more tired than my scanner. But a few tips since beginning to use this particular scanner:
1. Invest in flatbed scanner cleaning supplies. This is crucial to keeping excessive noise from being added to your scanned image. Use a dust remover air bulb or compressed air. Plus clean the bed frequently. Another tip; if you are scanning a large number of photographs, or in my case old (1900's type) wash hands frequently. Keep finger tips clean or as I state below, invest in nylon gloves to handle photos.
2. I'm scanning film negatives and color positives that are very fragile and one broke (brittle) while moving it to the scanner. My only suggestion is to use archive quality gloves for old negatives and glass mounted photos
3. Buy and use a film cleaning solution and handle each one carefully. I know that goes without saying, but I've found a lot of BW shots have fingerprints on their face and they add more noise to end item.
4. I'm not promoting anything but I'm using a Photoshop plug-in Noise Ninja to control excessive noise gained through scanning and Kodak ROC for color restoration processes. This saves me hours of color matching and testing swatches. I still need to adjust for some, but this saves me hours of computer time.
5. I've surpassed 2K scanned photos so far and it's still working like a charm. I have another 1/2 million to go.
5. 120 film negatives have become a problem; perhaps it's due to age but I'm running into difficulty getting the scanner to recognize them. It's been hit and miss. I suspect the top side scanning lamp may not be wide enough or bright enough to sense the negative.
After 919 scans of various kinds of media, I have a mixed bag of reviews. Beginning with 35mm slides and negatives - works great. Black and white 120 size came out great. It took me a while to make 120 work work though. The carrier was too small for large format, 4x6, so I had to improvise and that took a lot of time. Once I learned to use large format, then I tested it with 110 negatives. No luck with those. These are too small for the scanner to sense and I pushed the capabilities of this scanner. Overall it worked as designed, quick and fast.
I also used the advanced, simple and multiscan settings and they worked perfect.
Scanned documents looked like the originals after scanning and printing.
In summary I used each setting and they worked flawlessly. My request to Canon is to add a carrier for larger format film, it would make it easier to scan.
I used this with a Mac, new version, and it works really great. If I really get technical and want professional grade reproductions, that's when I go to photo labs, but those visits are rare. This is a great scanner for the price and it did everything I asked without failing or crashing.

product_title: Bialetti Mukka Express Cappuccino Maker
review_body: I received this cappuccino maker in the brushed alumnimum color almost two years ago as a birthday present.  I had specifically requested it because I love cappuccinos, but do not have room in my kitchen for a large cappucino maker.  Overall, I have been impressed with how well this meets my needs.  It only takes a few minutes to make a flavorful, foamy cappuccino.  Because it is small and portable I also find that I use it a lot more than I probably would a full-sized machine.  This I think is a true testiment to it's value because it doesn't matter how well something is made or works if you don't feel compelled to use it frequently instead of running to starbucks.  I often switch up what I use for the milk (using Egg Nog around the holidays and flavored soy milks more often) to make a variety of drinks that compare to my Starbucks favorites.  It's worth noting though that as other reviewers said, this won't really make 2 cups by American standards.  I've found using the measurement lines on the maker that it's more comparable to a single drink I would get at Starbucks.    So with all those compliments why do I give it 4 stars?  The biggest reason, as I have stated in my title is that it can be a bit tempremental.  You have to be careful when screwing the bottom base (which holds the water and coffee filter) in because if it doesn't catch just right it can be prone to leaks.  You also have to make sure that the frothing attachment isn't plugged or that will also create leaking problems.  As other reviewers have mentioned.  Soaking it in hot water immediately after using it as well as running a thin needle through it every once and awhile seem to help.  Thankfully the rest of the maker is pretty easy to clean, although I have found that it starts to accumulate tarnished spots on it after awhile no matter how diligent you are about cleaning it.  These don't detract from the attractiveness of the appliance, but are worth noting.    Overall I enjoy this appliance.  Overall I wish I didn't have to be quite so watchful that I maintain the frother and screw the bottom on correctly, but when I do it works like a charm.  Bottom line, it's great for people with little kitchen space and a big love for cappuccino.

product_title: Panasonic Dect 6.0 Expandable Digital Cordless Answering System - Dual Handset System (KX-TG9372B)
review_body: This review is being updated after about a month of use and I would change the rating to only 2 or 3 stars if I could.      First, we purchased this phone because we were having so much interference from our wireless modem and, while it's better with this phone, we're still experiencing too much interference and are returning this phone to the store.     Second, the \\"Block Calls\\" feature does not send the call directly to a busy signal as advertised, instead, it sends the caller directly to the answering machine! If I wanted to receive messages from the blocked callers, I'd just let the phone ring when caller-ID shows who it is! Instead, it helps the nuisance caller because they don't have to sit through the regular number of rings before the answering machine picks up.  The \\"block calls\\" feature is WORTHLESS.     Another reviewer commented on the fact that while the numbers on the handset are backlighted, the \\"talk\\" and \\"off\\" buttons are not. This makes it difficult to answer or hang up a call when you're in a darkened room and cannot get to the light quickly.      A considerable problem is the fact that if the ringer has been turned off (for various reasons) & the handset is lying face down, there is absolutely nothing that alerts me a call is coming in.  Our other panasonic phones had a little ring around the antenna that would light up when a call came in and the light was visible from any angle. But this phone does not.  There is only a teeny, tiny, tiny, tiny light on the very tip-top of the phone that flashes when a call comes in or a message is waiting. Unfortunately, that light is invisible unless the top of the phone happens to be pointed at you-- and most of us put it down with the top facing away.    Another problem is that, although the ringer can be turned off at the handset, it is darn near impossible to figure out how to turn off the ringer in the base unit.  The 'manual' does tell you how -- but good luck finding it in the manual because it's not inthe index and this particular instruction is buried.  Also, what good is turning off the ringer if you can still hear the caller leaving a message?  Our other panasonic phone had an LCD display that displayed the volume of incoming messages -- and that volume could easily be set to zero so we didn't have to listen to callers leaving messages.  It's not so easy to turn off the volume of incoming messages on this phone.  I guess panasonic (incorrectly) believes everyone wants to hear the message as it is being left by the caller - which defeats the purpose of turning off the ringer in order to get work done.      And finally, you can't see it in the photos but the back of this phone is bordello RED.  It's black on the front and red on the back. YUK !  Very gaudy, unattractive color combination.     We are taking this phone back to the store for a refund!

review_headline: Never worked, out of the box, no real tech support
review_body: I bought this printer over a year ago. My dad was dying so I didn't set it up immediately. When I finally tried to set it up, it wouldn't work. It claimed the ink cartridges weren't HP. I called tech support in India which told me that I had no support because it was no longer under warranty. I wrote to hp and was told by some local tech support that the inks had dried out and I needed to buy new ones. I bought new ones. Now the printer says it wants the introductory cartridges reinstalled. I did that, it doesn't recognize them. What happened is that HP wanted to lock people into using only their cartridges and to prevent their refilling the cartridges. So, they've put a chip on each cartridge. The printer will not work if it can't recognize the chip. And you can imagine how many ways a printer can fail to recognize a chip. The chip is modified by the software of the printer and the printer can zero out the chip. Technical users have noticed the printer will zero out the chip, following some kind of algorithm by which the printer \\"imagines\\" it can detect that you are not using a fresh cartridge.   Anyway, there went $250+ down the drain. And I will never forget, as a corporate customer, the company that HP has become.

product_title: Kensington Wireless Presenter (K33373US)
review_headline: How to disable your F5 key.
review_body: Overall, this is a great presentation remote.  It fits nicely into your hand, takes AAA batteries, includes a laser pointer, has only four buttons, and is plug and play.  I would have given it 5 stars except for one glaring fault: pressing the button for the laser pointer also sends the signal for the F5 key to the computer.  In some presentation programs this is fine, since it corresponds to the full-screen button.  In others and in most other programs, it produces effects that vary from mildly distracting to intolerable.    I knew this when I bought the remote.  I'd hoped to rewire it, but I failed.  If you too bought this remote or are planning on it, here's my suggested hack: disable your F5 key.    In Windows XP, this can be accomplished by setting F5 as a global keyboard shortcut...  EDIT: My previous hack stopped working suddenly.  I was forced to remap the keyboard instead.  The following two webpages include details on how to do this.  [...]  [...]    In KDE on linux, you can set a keyboard shortcut for F5 with no associated command.  To do this, go to Control Center -> Regional & Accessibility -> Input Actions, click the New Action Button and choose Keyboard Shortcut -> Activate Window, switch to the Keyboard Shortcut tab and input F5 as your desired shortcut.    Of course, the down side to this approach is that it disables the functionality of your F5 key.  I re-enable the F5 key after each presentation.

product_title: Brother HL-4070CDW Color Laser Printer with Built-In Duplex Printing and Wireless Interface
review_body: I bought this printer, not expecting that it would really be that good, because it was the only one that would fit in my cabinet.  It is very good at printing photo images, where there is a lot of detail.  Also, it hasn't jammed on me yet.  However, it has its drawbacks.  I put out this kind of money, knowing up front that it has higher operating costs, because I needed it most of all to print drawings that have plain solid color backgrounds.  Unfortunately, the toner imaging strips of this printer are apparently inferior when it comes to maintaining their electronic charges long enough for wide plain fields of color, and so it always prints wide plain color fields with major blotch defects!  Still it is better than having expensive ink jet cartridges, which always dried up and clogged before I could ever print much on them.  Furthermore, the color toner cartridges that came with this printer didn't last that long, although they appear to be advertised as long use everywhere.    It does not let you print with the fading cartridges at all.  You get an all or nothing toner experience.  It stops working completely and demands that you replace all the color cartridges, before it will start working again, even though it never once printed a faded copy yet.  Additionally, the replacement toner cartridges exceeded the cost of the printer by a fair bit!  This printer also often has a strong, eye burning, ozone emission that is quite noticeable.  I found that by keeping it in its closed cabinet that this helped mitigate this quite a bit.  I wouldn't use this printer too much in an unventilated room for that reason.  Worst of all, the black toner cartridge that it came with spewed black toner powder all over the place when changing the color toners!  Forewarned, I was quite ready to take the needed precautions upon finally needing to change the black toner cartridge, by spreading blank papers all over the floor first.  Quite the good idea that I did too, by the way!  None ofthe color cartridges leaked any toner out at all, however.  I pretty much knew ahead of time, that the first generation of affordable color laser printers like this would be kind of trouble prone.  However, I don't think I will buy another Brother color laser when the second generation color lasers are finally out, given its horrible ability to simply print a solid field of color.  If all you print are photos, you won't even notice this defect at all, however.  The duplexing works great so I save money on paper while worrying a little bit about what to do about my bad drawing print outs.  Now I just printed a good color background finally, so maybe I just got scammed on the color cartridges that came with it at first!

product_title: Gyration Motion Sensing Remote Control
review_body: I've had this product for about 1 month.  Here's the run down of pros and cons:     Pros:  1) MCE functions are integrated flawlessly and work very.  2) MCE functions are not directional because it has been integrated to Gyration's RF technology.  You can control MCE from a very good distance and without the need to point the remote to the receiver like IR remotes.  3) The Gyration mouse function really shines on this product.  It took a little bit to get use to but after a while I got the hang of it.  Note you can click the mouse button twice and it will lock the movement of the mouse to allow drag-n-drop.      Cons:  Uuuggg, IR functions.  As noted from one of the earlier comments, this is where this thing is really flawed.  1) Programming codes for equipment: 1a) Process to program it is extremely cumbersome using code entry method so you'll have to experiment with various codes.  This is bothersome and time consuming to juggle the remote & the instruction book at the same time.  1b) There is a feature which automatically scrolls through the codes which helps a bit, but still the process is cumbersome and time consuming.  1c) Does not support equipment with discrete on and off, I have this problem with my A/V receiver (Onkyo).  Be prepared to remove those batteries because it get lock in the programing process...SEVERAL times on my part.  2) Programming learned functions:  2a) None of the buttons dedicated for MCE mode are programmable.  Why in the heck did they lock this!!!  In my opinion, at least the volume button should've been opened to avoid an extra button sequence to change the volume to the A/V receiver / TV.  2b) Here's another annoying thing.  I can have one button learn an IR command but when transferring that same IR command to another button, the remote will NOT accept it.  What the heck????  I was almost ready to give up on this thing, but I hung on.  What a PAINFUL experience compared to programming my Onkyo learning remote!  And this is coming from someone who likes to tweak things.  Ok, now that it is all programmed to my liking, 3) the remote response for the IR aspect is very lacking.  This is probably due to the auto power reserve feature which puts the remote to \\"sleep\\" after some interval.  Even so, I had to press the function button several times before it kicks in (lights up).  4) The IR transmission is weak and directional.  For me the remote was not responsive beyond 8ft and you'll have to be almost direct center of the equipment.      In summary, MCE functions great; but on the IR aspect, this needs to be majorly OVERHAULED.  I've been using the Gyration mouse & keyboard for almost two years and was really anticipating this remote.  I'm very disappointed with this product.  Just beware.  I'm currently considering another remote from Logitech.  I can live with the Gyration mouse being separate from the remote unit.

They won't replace it, saying I have to buy a new one.  Just order the same product at the same price from someone with integrity and save yourself the hassle.    As the icing to this proverbial cake, the black toner (the one with the problems) is now saying it's empty, meaning they sold me a toner that was already nearly 3/4 empty.  I think it's pretty telling of their company that they will not replace this disgraceful toner for me.

product_title: Canon Pixma MP530 Office All-In-One Inkjet Photo Printer
review_body: This printer is terrible! The first one I bought showed an error message that was not only incorrect (it said there was a missing ink cartridge when all were properly installed) but could not be cleared. Canon had me send it to them and in return they sent me a refurbished unit. The refurbished unit does not scan properly. The scanner gets \\"stuck\\" after about 2/3 of the page and the unit must be turned off and turned back on to resume printing. The result is a copy (or scan) that is muddled and blurry on one side.     The really terrible thing about the \\"new\\" unit is the noise it makes when the cartridges return to the original position after printing. It sound like the buzzing of a child's wind-up toy, only 100 times louder, and lasts 15 seconds. I cannot make a phone call or carry on a conversation while printing for this reason.    The only good point: it did print well for about a week before breaking!

product_title: Prismacolor Premier Double-Ended Art Markers
review_body: I'm always satisfied at Amazon with whatever the product I buy.  Where else can you go to get the variety of products and the satisfaction guarantee.

product_title: HP iPAQ hx2495b Pocket PC (FA674B#ABA)
review_body: Brilliant. What can i say? This is my first PDA and i am very happy with it. Does as it says on the tin!!!

product_title: Dell Axim X50v - Handheld - Windows Mobile 2003 SE - 3.7" color TFT ( 480 x 640 )
review_body: I bought this used and cannot figure out how to download apps on it!! other than that it is pretty good. It connects to the internet fast, and the programs all run well. I just wish i knew how to put more programs on it!!!

product_title: Olympus WS-311M Digital Voice Recorder and WMA Music Player
review_body: We bought this recorder for our son's music class, which requires very good recording quality. This recorder is definitly living up (and exceeding) our expectations. It is easy to record, play, move files to computer and into our iTunes library. We love it. Only minor gripe is that the product did not come with a strap and a carrying case. It costs a fortune to buy those separately.

product_title: HP Deskjet F4280 All-in-One Printer (CB656A)
review_body: This printer is quiet easy to setup and all of its functions are very intuitive. I have used its scanning function and also edited my scans using the OCR software provided. My prints are crisp and great looking. Overall the HP Deskjet F4280 is ideal for a SOHO. I plan to buy two more for the my school's IT lab to complement the laser printer (HP) and for the secretary's office.

product_title: HP Officejet 6310 All-in-One Printer
review_body: This printer replaced an old Canon because I thought I wanted to be able to scan and copy. I didn't buy another Canon because the print heads wore out rather quickly.    At least the Canon worked. I've had this for 3 months and the scanning virtually never worked properly. Not the hardware, but the software. HP seems to think that it's perfectly reasonable to ship a 300 MB cluster of buggy software apps that are not needed just to shove their products onto our computers. After hours of troubleshooting with their friendly agents I still cant' scan without either 1)Windows error messages or 2)having absolutely NOTHING happen. I'm running this on the exotic and seldom-encountered Windows XP SP2 on a Dell laptop. I'm an IT manager, and this absolutely fails the \\"Dad\\" test in that my father could not possibly set this up himself. (He was able to set up the Canon that I bought him for Christmas).     Plus: Print quality is decent, both black & white and color, as well as photos.    Minus: Copying is as slow as refrigerated molasses. Scanning doesn't work. Rather than letting you install a little bit of software that works they practically ship you a new operating system that's slow and buggy.    HP, you fooled me once and you will not fool me again.     UPDATE: I bought a new Vista computer and had exactly the same problmes. HP blamed it on compatibility issues with Vista and I had to remind them that I previously had the same problems on XP. After a year, and many hours of doing worthless things with their customer support team (they might as well have had me chant and sprinkle water around the house because it was so ineffective), HP finally replaced the printer with a different model. It installed easily and has caused no problems since. It's clear from my experience that the 6310 software was defective, but HP prefers to blame the operating system (no matter which one you have). While they eventually did come through I feel that they were trying to cover up a defective product by trying to place the blame everywhere else (their customer, Microsoft, my router, etc.)

product_title: The Wilderness 2009 Vertical Wall Calendar
review_body: This is a beautiful calendar and I would have given it a 5 star rating for the photographs as well as size. The one thing I felt that it lacked was that there was no full sized calendar sheet for December 2008 which for me would have been worth another star. Also I did not see an actual measurement on the website so I had to hope that it would fit well in an area where I wanted it to hang. If you are having a problem with this I will provide the actual measurements which are 22\\" high X 9\\" wide overall. The Photographs are 16\\" high X 9\\" wide. The bottom calendar portion is 6\\" high X 9\\" wide with a possible writing area in each block of just under 1 and 1/2 inches.

product_title: Vtech ia5847 - 5.8 GHz Two Handset Coredless Phone Sytem w/ Caller ID
review_body: This phone serves its purpose as a basic analog 5.8GHz cordless phone and is worth what you pay for it. The caller ID works as it should. The phone holds a charge for about a day and a half (not seven like stated in the manual) on standby. I don't remain on the phone long to measure continuous talk time. You should not expect stellar performance and features from a $35 cordless telephone set.      I didn't expect this phone to have rock solid reception. The phones suffer from static for no apparent reason, no matter what the distance from the base is. I wanted to write this \\"review\\" because I've experienced something I didn't expect to occur on a phone that uses the 5.8GHz frequency - crosstalk. It picked up a conversation between two individuals crystal clearly. I guess this is because it is ANALOG and doesn't have advanced signal encryption... None at all I guess.     I suggest anyone looking for a basic phone to pass on this one. The static becomes a bit of a nuisance and conversations may not be safe from signal eavesdropping. Vtech makes decent phones, but when they make CHEAP phones... they sure are cheap.

product_title: AT&T 2116 2.4 GHz Telephone with Caller ID (Silver Grey)
review_body: This is good basic phone but just ensure you don't pay more than $25.    1.) Good Looks.  2.) Fine Voice Clarity.  3.) Very Useful headset speaker phone, allows you to take the phone anywhere and use it as a speaker phone.  4.) Basic features are fine, showing you if there is a voice mail.  5.) Value for money < $25.

product_title: 4in X 6in Photo Paper
review_headline: Very Nice Pictures, particularly for a 300 dpi dye sub
review_body: Very nice photo appearing output.     Direct comparison with HP Photo printer, the Panasonic is much more photo-like.     The box does arrive with limited instructions on roughly how many prints you can get per ribbon set, but the printer manual has that info.       This may be a fairly new printer model, as none of the local electronics/office supply stores have the paper/ribbon kits for the Panasonic photo dye sub printers yet.

product_title: Clearsounds Amplified Phone with 50dB of Amplification (CLS-CSC600)
review_body: the is the worst phone I've ever purchased. the speaker phone does not work how it should. i have to yell for you to hear me. the bright blue lcd goes no/off sporadically. very annoying phone.i will not recommend.

product_title: Geargrip Lite CPU Holder
review_body: Works as expected. I spend a long time trying to find one of these online and this was not only the cheapest, but in my opinion, the best.

product_title: Floortex Ultimat Polycarbonate Chair Mat for Hard Floors, 53" x 48", Rectangular, Clear (FR1213419ER)
review_body: I had looked and looked for a high quality chairmat to protect my hardwood floors from the office chair wheels for a long time.  I had ordered a couple other chairmats from a different company and sent them back right away because they were flimsy and I could tell they would not be able to stand up to much abuse.  This chairmat from Floortex is a thick, firm, high quality mat.  It was wrapped/packaged really well for shipping (my other two from another company came unwrapped and had marks and scratches all over them).  I have now had this mat on my maple floor at my desk for a month. It gets daily abuse from my rolling office chair and does not show any marks.  It is very sturdy and it feels like the chair is just on the wood floor.  Although it is \\"clear\\", it does have a textured appearance, which I didn't like at first.  However, I really love it now.  I think if it were perfectly clear, it would show marks more easily so I prefer it this way.  It is not very noticeable on the floor.  I am extremely happy with this product!

product_title: Panasonic KX-TG6052B 5.8 GHz FHSS Expandable Digital Cordless Phone System with 2 Handsets
review_body: Bought this as a gift to my parents. They love it.  I would have given it five stars, but they have not had it very long so not sure of any quirks it may have. It gives you an option of announcing who is calling if you have caller ID.  Great option so you do not have to race to find the phone!  Well lit caller ID and good answering machine.

product_title: HP Photosmart A526 Compact Photo Printer
review_body: This printer is ok if you are printing photos with light backgrounds, but if the background in the photo is dark the printer makes it darker.  Seems to darken everything up, and there is no way to adjust the brightness that I can see.  The instructions that it comes with are not great, and I found little support for it online.  I do like that it's compact and easy to use, just wish the photo quality was a little bit better.

product_title: HP Photosmart C7280 All-in-One Printer
review_headline: waste of paper and my time
review_body: great printer with these exceptions:  always printing a spacer sheet in between each print (waste of time and paper) and so easily goes OFF LINE and having to set it up ALL OVER AGAIN!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

product_title: HP LaserJet P1006 Printer
review_body: The pages and print are nice and sharp .   there are still bugs with Vista spent some time with HP support and they gave me a fix and said hopefully any updates will fix the bugs A couple of ideals for HP provide some kind of manual along with the CD and why ship a short toner cartridge (700 pages)instead of the full 1500 page cartridge. Also if it matters to you Made in Vietnam.

product_title: Meade Rb-70 / 20230 70Mm A-Series Altazimuth Refractor Telescope
review_body: Ok. I have withdrawn my previous review in light of a number of items which have turned up.  I still say this is a good beginning scope for the amature and I have certainly had any number of good viewings.  However, be aware, this is NOT a product that Meade will repair, replace or even talk to you about. They save that for the higher end high quality scopes.  So, you break something, you buy new scope. Period. End of story.  Additionally, the fine adjustment controls are cheap Chinese crap.  Broke from day one (on both brand new scopes I bought).  Shipping back to Meade for replacement costs more than scope worth.  So the upshot is this.  If you buy this scope, buy another tripod arraingment if you can find one to fit.  Other wise, go ahead and pony up the extra bucks and get a really good scope.  You'll save money and time in the long run, be much happier and probably extend your life expectancy with the lower stress levels!

product_title: HP iPAQ RX1950 Pocket PC

Then, it will decide to constantly jam when it does take from the manual try.  Awful, awful, awful.

product_title: Uniden DCX200 DECT 6.0 Accessory Handset and Charging Cradle for the DECT2000/DECT 3000 Series Phones - Silver
review_body: The reviews which say this phone lacks an \\"add 1\\" format feature for returning long distance phone calls are either mistaken or outdated. I almost returned my just-purchased phone based on these reviews, but page 30 of the manual reveals that the \\"*/tone\\" button will add or remove a \\"1\\" to/from any caller ID number. I tried it and it indeed works as advertised. I have not had this phone long enough yet to contribute more, but so far it seems fine. It has every feature I want in a multiple-handset cordless system

product_title: X1270 All In One with usb Inkjet Printer
review_headline: Does the Job, no hassle for 2 years
review_body: In my 2 years of usage of this printer, I did not face any significant issue. The only thing is that sometimes you have to insert paper carefully and the cartridges are costly as with any other printer.

product_title: Panasonic KX-TS108W Corded Phone with Clock, White
review_body: Works well; speakerphone is loud and clear, and unit is easy to program. Only wish the display was brighter, but this seems to be a problem with most speaker phones. You would think manufacturers would be sensitive to this issue, and offer a bright green or red readout such as one finds on DVD players, stereos, etc. After all, the unit is hooked up to an AC adaptor so there is plenty of juice.

product_title: AT&T SL82318 DECT 6.0 Cordless Phone, Silver/Gray, 3 Handsets
review_body: I love the features on these phones.  Each handset includes a speakerphone with great volume and very clear audio quality.  The person you are calling will not know they are on a speakerphone.  The phones have an intercom system that allows any handset to call any other handset.  The audio quality is excellent.  The answering machine is easy to use.  The phones are light but not too small.

product_title: HP Officejet 6310 All-in-One Printer
review_body: I previously had the HP 6110 and liked it fairly well but it died and they sent me a refurbished one. The 1st and that 2nd one had some problems with the carriage hanging up, so I decided to upgrade. I do like this better, including the document feeder and the paper input tray. Also, the software allows you to control what you're doing from the computer, not just the unit panel.    Nonna scrapbooker

product_title: HP Officejet 6310 All-in-One Printer
review_body: This is not a top-of-the-line photo printer and the scanner cover won't stand up to serious abuse, but this printer model has repeatedly done a good job with printing, scanning, faxing, etc through a number of purchases I've done for/with friends. Its hard to beat the price for a decent workhorse printer that doesn't drink ink.

product_title: Clarity 5.8 GHz Professional Amplified Cordless Phone with DCP and Digital Answering Machine (C4230)
review_body: We bought this phone for my mother-in-law who is to phones the exact opposite of Will Rogers to people.  She never met one she liked. product_title: Aurora 8 sheets paper shredders
review_body: Before ordering this item, I had read some other purchasers' opinions and felt this shredder would be as satisfactory as my Fellowes [Model DM3].    Had I the Aurora shredder first, I might have been content with its function.  However, after having a Fellowes shredder for better than 15 years, that worked effortlessly [until I inadvertently shred a document with a thick binding and it jammed the mechanism and ultimately botched the sensor], the Aurora is a huge disappointment.    When feeding papers into the sensor it takes some coaxing to activate; if the paper slides 'out of the sensor's range' it will hang there until another sheet is fed to activate.  The cost was nominal.    I guess the saying, you get what you pay for is applicable here.    I'd look into a Fellowes before getting this one.

product_title: ace 05024 ace Aceliner Full Strip Executive Stapler, 20 Sheet Cap, Chrome/Marbled Walnut
review_body: The Aceliner, with it's smooth and typically flawless operation plus retro look, would be at the top of my favorite stapler list (if I had a favorite stapler list).  However, the 'marbled walnut' color looks more like mud - I definitely prefer black.

review_body: I was looking for a food journal. I found this notebook and absolutely love it. Perfect size. The cover feels very upscale. Wipes right off with damp cloth. Pocket in front and back and a pen strap. Magnetic closure. I highly recommend!

product_title: AT&T 2230 2.4 GHz Dual-Handset Cordless Phone with Caller ID (Champagne)
review_headline: Think twice or more before buying
review_body:
At first it worked fine, although battery life was low. When the original Nicads gave out I bought NMIH batteries. Note: No one should use Nicads anymore.

product_title: Canon BU-10 Bluetooth Adapter for i80 Printer
review_body: I am very satisfied with this adapter. Works great. A little slow at a distance, but that is understandable.

product_title: Panasonic KX-TG6702B 2-Line 5.8 GHz FHSS GigaRange Expandable Cordless Phone System with 2 Handsets
review_body:
I recently purchased and deployed the Panasonic KX-TG6702B 2-Line phone to my home office, and so far it has worked like a champ!

In the past, I've used a few other Panasonic phones and been less than satisfied with the overall quality of the phone, but NOT in this case. I find the base unit to be well constructed and of high quality.

I was initially concerned that the vertically mounted handset would get routinely knocked out of the cradle (annoying), but it is actually well seated and difficult to bump out of place.

Integrating with additional handsets is simple and doesn't involve any manual intervention. Just plug in the additional handsets and they configure themselves with the base unit.

Multi-line functionality (e.g. call transferring, 3-way calling, etc.) is rich and easy to use.

I'm using the phone (both lines) over a digital (i.e. cable) service which seems to be working great. In other words, the phone works over both digital (VOIP) and analog (POTS) carriers.

I don't use the answering machine functions, so I can't comment on their qualities.

The sound quality is impressive, and I haven't had a single person say \\"Am I on speaker phone?\\" thus I conclude that the quality of the microphone is such that people can't tell I'm using the hands-free features.

In summary, I think this is a great unit for any home office setup.

product_title: Olympus WS-300M 256 MB Digital Voice Recorder and Music Player
review_headline: DVR-could come with more logical instructions
review_body:
This is a great product. I use it to tape lectures at school and it records very well.
My only complaint, as with all tech products, is that the instructions arent easy to follow if they even include instructions for the product purchased. How many times have you read the instructions to find out that they pertain to various models, not just the one that you are trying to figure out?
Took me a while to figure it out, and I am still trying to figure out why the recording sometimes stays on the recorder, after I copy it to my computer, and sometimes it just completely goes over to the computer without keeping a copy on the unit.

product_title: HP PSC 1610 All-in-One Printer, Scanner, Copier
review_body: This printer has been nothing but trouble.  This is the second 1610 that I have owned.  The first one worked fine for five minutes, then started up with the \\"Remove and check color cartidge\\" error.  After I was unable to fix the problem, I returned it to the store for a new 1610, the same error occurred.  The patch from HP for this specific error did nothing to correct the problem.  I always heard that HP made good printers.  This frustrating piece of garbage proves that wrong.  Consider yourself warned.

product_title: Canon 0307B001 CanoScan LiDE 25 Color Image Scanner
review_headline: Affordable, fast and easy to use. A must have.
review_body:
You already have a printer, you have the fax machine, you just need a scanner. Of course there are these new all in one packages you can buy these days but they are costly and bulky.

Here you have a simple flat bed scanner that is affordable, and has the features to copy, scan, email, even edit what you scan as well. It's powered through the USB cable so no need to worry about plugs. The scans come out great and so do the copies. The speed couldn't be any faster which is of course a plus. The scanner fits nicely just about anywhere, or can be easily stored if not used frequently.

Total quality, and a great buy especially for the price as well. Worth picking up.

product_title: AT&T 1855 Corded Telephone with Digital Answering System and Speakerphone
review_body: Does the job well. Had I thought about it a little more, I would have purchased a phone with Caller ID exhibited.

product_title: HP OfficeJet 7310 All-in-One Printer
review_body: Primarily, I wanted a network printer that I could hit from any computer around the house that happened to be turned on.  As a much lower priority, I thought that it would be nice to have a fax (from paper, to paper) and photocopy machine.  I have no interest in the gadgety memory cards, etc.  Reliability was very important to me because I am the only one in the household willing to fix a paper jam or install a patch, which gets old after a while.  The sales dude told me that this HP printer would be perfect for me.    The scanner was OK for three weeks, but then \\"scanner failure, turn power off then on\\" message was displayed, and I had to exchange the unit.    The printer installation is bizarre - the printer is visible in WinXP's \\"My Network Places\\" as if it is another computer, but seems as if it does not have any shared devices.  Instead, you have to install a ton of HP software from the CD which gives you 100% access to the all-in-one features, such as the memory card, lots of fax functionality that I will never use, HP Director and HP Image Zone that I find annoying.      I can't find any hits on Google, to make this printer work with Linux, which I had assumed would be trivial.      When I take my laptop to work, WinXP seems to be very concerned that it can not access the memory card that I don't own that isn't in my printer at home!  I believe that this is slowing the boot procedure.

review_body: After searching four stores in my area for white cardstock without success, I finally logged onto trusty Amazon and found what I needed.  This cardstock is bright, works great with my printer, works great with my stamps, and is a good deal price-wise.  I'll be back for seconds.

This printer is large, bulky, and not as intutive as HP printers BUT it performs all tasks far better than most.

product_title: Star Wars Dual Compartment Lunchbox Kit
review_body: It was nice to go on-line and get this product before school started.  None of our local retailers had it in stock.

product_title: Panasonic KX-TG5439P 5.8 GHz Cordless Phone with Digital Answering System

product_title: GE 28110EE1 DECT 6.0 Expansion Handset with Caller ID
review_body: This is a very inexpensive phone that has all the options you could ever want with the ease of cordless functionality.

product_title: Epson Stylus Photo R380 Color Inkjet Printer (C11C658011)
review_headline: It's drinks ink like an alcoholic in a vat of beer!

It lasts a long time if your printing pages off the internet or for a term paper, but it's main use is supposed to be as a photo printer!@#  I ignored the other posts thinking they were exaggerating about the ink usage.  DON'T IGNORE THIS POST!  I'm not sure how other printers use ink but at best you get about a dozen pictures before you need to replace one or more of the ink cartridges.
